title: refactor(guardrails): remove three fresh redundant Straiker comments
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Withdrawn after independent review found useful context in two proposed comment removals. One defensible finding remains, below the minimum batch of three, so no cleanup is being landed

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/93f7050aef8340d98356e6b4ba429b0d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/93f7050aef8340d98356e6b4ba429b0d?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## Outcome

Closing without merge. The fresh caveats assessor identified useful label-contract and failure-policy context in two removals. Those two findings are dropped, leaving only the `no_verdict` comment as a clear cleanup. No unequivocal replacements justified expanding the batch

Greptile rated the tip 5/5 and Bugbot reported no new issues, but those results do not establish that all three comments were redundant. The batch is withdrawn rather than padded. Required CI was still running and is not claimed as passed

## TLDR

Problem this solves:
- The proposed batch contains fewer than three defensible findings

How it solves it:
- Withdraws the proposed removals without merging any code

## User Flow

No user-visible change. Straiker guardrail requests and logged results remain identical before and after this cleanup

## Findings by run date

### 2026-11-15

Reviewed additions from 70 non-merge commits in the 24-hour window ending at the initial fetch. The local reflog did not reach yesterday, so the equivalent timestamp-selected base was `93f8d86c89e198c843eb245d4324e8837e43370b`

All three proposed removals were introduced by [ff997e6970](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/ff997e6970c7a7a5dee1bb2ca66f8ab41311e7dd), in `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker/straiker.py`

1. `_WebhookFailure.no_verdict`: clearly redundant, but insufficient alone for a batch
2. `_V3LogAction`: dropped because the comment records an external label contract
3. `_V3_LOG_STATUS`: dropped because the comment explains failure-policy and detection semantics

The whole proposed patch is withdrawn, including item 1, to honor the minimum-three rule

No tests, suppressions, lint rules, budgets or executable statements changed

### Rolling PR handling

[#51594](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51594) and [#50192](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50192) already have human reviews, so both are left open and untouched under the automation's reviewed-work exception. No work was absorbed, dropped or superseded

### Deliberately untouched

Retained the retry and failure-policy explanations because they document non-obvious behavior. Other fresh typing, mutation and structural candidates were not included without a sufficiently small, behavior-neutral fix. No historical cleanup or architectural recommendation was added

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] No new tests needed for comment-only deletions
- [x] All mapped tests pass locally, 226 unit and 39 integration tests
- [x] Local `make lint` and staged `make check` pass
- [x] Scope is isolated to three fresh comment blocks
- [ ] Required CI and automated reviews at the tip have finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at c1529e4239a27a6624cf8ceca698023390306898

PASS, E2E EXEMPT. This is a non-executable-text cleanup, not a behavior fix. The complete diff removes only five comments. AST and executable-token equality prove behavior is unchanged without relying on pytest output. Live provider before/after E2E was skipped

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import ast, io, subprocess, tokenize
p = 'litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker/straiker.py'
a = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', f'origin/main:{p}'], text=True)
b = open(p).read()
assert ast.dump(ast.parse(a), include_attributes=False) == ast.dump(ast.parse(b), include_attributes=False)
def tokens(s):
    return [(t.type, t.string) for t in tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(s).readline)
            if t.type not in (tokenize.COMMENT, tokenize.NL)]
assert tokens(a) == tokens(b)
print('PASS: identical Python AST and executable tokens')
PY
```

```text
PASS: identical Python AST and executable tokens
```

Caller trace: `no_verdict` is assigned on a missing platform decision and read when selecting the logged action. `_V3LogAction` types the action returned by `_v3_log_action` and accepted by `_log_v3_event`. `_V3_LOG_STATUS[action]` maps that action to its logged status. No definitions, assignments, branches, dispatch, callers or data values changed. No untested integration risk was introduced

Additional validation, not proof of fix:
- `make lint` passed, including strict lint, type discipline and basedpyright gates
- `make check` passed on the staged patch, with full output inspected in `.git/pre_commit_lint.log`
- `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_straiker.py tests/unit/test_internal_context.py`, through the shared gate-slot wrapper, 226 passed
- `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2 python3 litellm/scripts/gate_slot_lock.py uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions tests/integration/observability/test_straiker_v3_platform.py`, 39 passed
- The integration runner supplies the owned database, Redis and proxy fixtures needed by the mapped file. Its upstreams are scripted test services, not live-provider E2E
- AST equality, executable-token equality and fresh-added-line membership passed

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 1 of 4 -->

### Low

- Two of the removed comments carried context the code does not show
  - Disposition: withdraw the complete batch rather than delete useful context
- Required CI was still running when this was assessed
  - Disposition: no merge or CI-pass claim is made

One fresh assessment round ran. Both caveats are disposed of by withdrawing the PR. There is no landing decision or human blocker

## Type

Refactoring

</details>

- [x] c1529e4239a27a6624cf8ceca698023390306898 passes /live-pr-risk (E2E exempt)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> **Low Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> This PR **deletes five comment lines** from the Straiker guardrail hook in `straiker.py` that repeated what the nearby names already convey: the `_WebhookFailure.no_verdict` field, the `_V3LogAction` type alias, and the `_V3_LOG_STATUS` mapping.
> 
> **No runtime behavior changes**—guardrail requests, verdict handling, and v3 logging (`_v3_log_action`, `_log_v3_phase`, `no_verdict` on missing decisions) are unchanged.

title: test(integration): record a stack when an owned proxy crashes
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Four batch file usage cap chaos tests failed together in the scheduled integration run because their shared proxy crashed with a segmentation fault during startup and left no stack in its log. This PR turns on Python's fault handler for every proxy the integration harness launches, so the next crash records where it happened and the real cause can be fixed

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/bfa27a44f1c34302b0a88fd84c403462
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/bfa27a44f1c34302b0a88fd84c403462?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Owned proxy died with SIGSEGV (exit -11) before readiness
- Its log held no stack, so the cause is unknown

How it solves it:

- Owned proxy environments always set `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`
- A unit test checks inherited or explicit values cannot disable it

## CI evidence

Scheduled run 243 at c3b929d2031a, job https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43675985425/job/132696124043, each test `times_failed` 1 after passing the 4 earlier runs. The module-scoped `chaos` fixture failed with `AssertionError: Owned proxy exited before readiness`, and its `.exit.json` recorded `"exit_before_stop": -11`, so the proxy segfaulted on its own before harness cleanup. The last log line was Prisma saying the database is in sync

## Status

Blocker: the crash did not reproduce locally at 1, 4 or 8 workers on origin/main (every owned proxy exited cleanly), and CI kept no native stack

Next step: once this merges, read the `Fatal Python error` stack from the owned-proxy log of the next crashing scheduled run, then fix the crashing code where it lives

<!-- mateoheal-runs: 1 -->

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at bd075e37e5141edc8ec4cefd74b8debb6d243c5a. This only changes harness diagnostics, so focused checks fully prove it

1. Sent SIGSEGV to a ready owned proxy, which exited -11 and wrote `Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault` plus a stack through `litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py` `run_server` into its `.log`
2. `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py management tests/integration/management/test_batch_file_usage_caps_chaos.py` with Postgres, Redis and the replica config gave 5 passed
3. `uv run pytest tests/unit/integration_support/test_process.py` gave 75 passed
4. `make lint` passed
5. Dispatched management-replica run https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43683816833

## Type

✅ Test

</details>

title: feat(customers): move existing members between teams
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

allow users to move customer members between teams through API and UI

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f2d45fdddb3d432c91aae977351c0963
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f2d45fdddb3d432c91aae977351c0963?variant=devin
Requested by: @moe-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Existing members cannot replace their team memberships.
- Recreating members loses their current spend counters.

How it solves it:

- Add same-organization team replacement to member PATCH.
- Add a member actions menu and Move teams dialog.
- Preserve identity, budgets, counters, and historical usage.

Intentional product change: the member row's Edit button becomes a three-dot actions menu holding Settings and Move teams.

## User Flow

Before, an admin cannot move an existing member without recreating it.

1. Open `http://localhost:4000/ui/customers/manage/?org=org-proof&tab=members`.
2. The member row only has Edit, and its settings page has no team editor.
3. PATCH `/management/v1/customer_members/proof-member` with `{"parent_team_ids":["proof-beta"]}` returns 422.

![Before, members tab with only Edit](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..mCrW-PVOr9AUBkqAYSx509NVkk8J-_DmXRPiXWvH3hs)

After, the admin moves the member and it keeps its identity and history.

1. Open the same page.
2. Open the member's three-dot menu and choose Move teams.
3. Pick teams in the same organization, default first, and click Move teams. The row now shows the new team.
4. New requests without a team header charge the new team, and a request naming the removed team gets 403.

![After, three-dot menu with Move teams](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..RLuQXgeMFmyAFeuSuzQQPkk2fuzcjK9h0gQhK5JwNPk)

![After, dialog with Beta selected](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..CWb9RZkgpjrpxliYGiADXBk9tfoWcBz99kw-E4cJz9o)

![After, member moved to Beta](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..lknGwSvqdNbalZV1SP70YXWcEMaUDUJWFpLdf_2figY)

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each finding

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live before and after at base `c3b929d2` (main) and head `3d8d596`. Each leg used a fresh PostgreSQL database, two proxy workers sharing one dedicated Redis in `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`, the dashboard built from the same SHA, and real Bedrock calls to `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5`. The screenshots above are from that run.

Before, the PATCH returned 422 and the member stayed in Alpha.

After, the move was saved through the dashboard. Only `parent_team_ids` and `updated_at` changed on the member. ID, org, template, override, `spend`, `budget_usage`, `budget_reset_at` and `created_at` were identical. A request with `x-litellm-customer-team-id: proof-alpha` returned 403. Two requests without a team header returned 200 and 200. After accounting finished, Beta had exactly 2 new successful requests and Alpha's history was unchanged. `null`, `[]`, a duplicate and a blank ID returned 422, an unknown team returned 404 and a team from another org returned 409. The live OpenAPI schema shows `parent_team_ids` as an optional array with no null.

<details>
<summary>Rerun setup</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: proof-haiku
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5
      aws_profile_name: litellm-dev
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6393
general_settings:
  proxy_batch_write_at: 5
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6393
```

```bash
redis-server --port 6393 --bind 127.0.0.1 --save '' --appendonly no
unset AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

`--reload` was dropped so both workers actually serve. Env var names are `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`.

```bash
export M=http://127.0.0.1:4000/management/v1 H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
curl -sS "$M/customer_organizations" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"customer_org_id":"org-proof","alias":"org-proof","budget":{"max_budget":100},"default_budgets":[{"name":"proof-standard","max_budget":10,"budget_duration":"1mo"}],"default_budget_template":"proof-standard"}'
curl -sS "$M/customer_organizations" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"customer_org_id":"org-other","alias":"org-other"}'
curl -sS "$M/customer_teams" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"customer_team_id":"proof-alpha","parent_org_id":"org-proof","alias":"Alpha"}'
curl -sS "$M/customer_teams" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"customer_team_id":"proof-beta","parent_org_id":"org-proof","alias":"Beta"}'
curl -sS "$M/customer_teams" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"customer_team_id":"other-gamma","parent_org_id":"org-other","alias":"Gamma"}'
TEMPLATE_ID=$(curl -sS "$M/customer_organizations/org-proof" -H "$H" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["default_budgets"][0]["budget_id"])')
curl -sS "$M/customer_members" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"customer_member_id\":\"proof-member\",\"alias\":\"Proof Member\",\"parent_team_ids\":[\"proof-alpha\"],\"budget_id\":\"$TEMPLATE_ID\",\"budget_override\":{\"max_budget\":7,\"budget_duration\":\"1mo\"}}"

chat() { curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-litellm-customer-org-alias: org-proof' -H 'x-litellm-customer-member-id: proof-member' "$@" \
  -d '{"model":"proof-haiku","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word OK."}],"max_tokens":32}'; }
chat   # seed usage on Alpha, then wait for member spend > 0
curl -sS "$M/customer_members/proof-member" -H "$H" > before.json

# base only: expect 422
curl -sS -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X PATCH "$M/customer_members/proof-member" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"parent_team_ids":["proof-beta"]}'

# head: move to Beta in the UI, then
curl -sS "$M/customer_members/proof-member" -H "$H" > after.json
chat -H 'x-litellm-customer-team-id: proof-alpha'   # 403
chat; chat                                          # 200 200
for p in 'null' '[]' '["proof-beta","proof-beta"]' '[" "]' '["missing-team"]' '["other-gamma"]'; do
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X PATCH "$M/customer_members/proof-member" -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"parent_team_ids\":$p}"
done                                                # 422 422 422 422 404 409
curl -sS -G "$M/customer_teams/daily/activity" -H "$H" --data-urlencode start_date=$(date -u +%F) --data-urlencode end_date=$(date -u +%F) --data-urlencode customer_team_ids=proof-alpha,proof-beta
```

```text
PASS required identity, org, template, override, spend, budget_usage, budget_reset_at, created_at unchanged
POST /v1/chat/completions 403
POST /v1/chat/completions 200
POST /v1/chat/completions 200
PASS all six validation statuses
PASS proof-alpha historical entity record exactly unchanged
PASS proof-beta 2 successful requests, org total 3 requests
Head health responses 16 200s 16 serving PIDs [80720, 80721]
PASS live OpenAPI optional parent_team_ids array without null
```

</details>

At the head: 217 backend tests, 243 customer dashboard tests, dashboard typecheck and `make check` passed.


- Docs shipped in BerriAI/litellm-docs#3043.

title: test(database): expect no native pool in proxy lifespan cleanup
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

The proxy database lifespan test failed every variant on the newest scheduled integration run because it still expected the proxy to open a native database pool. Since #49798 the native pool stays closed on purpose while no Rust connections are reserved, so this PR makes the test assert that no native pool exists and keeps every cleanup check after a failed startup

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5c281e6314a34a369cf3f444ab8090d9
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/5c281e6314a34a369cf3f444ab8090d9?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Lifespan test fails all 4 variants on main since #49798
- It asserts a native pool that is now intentionally never opened

How it solves it:

- Assert `database.native is None`, the intended behavior
- Keep every query, task, thread and Prisma cleanup check

## Relevant issues

CI evidence, scheduled run [43662085507 database job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43662085507), times_failed 4 (all 4 variants, outcomes PPPPPF). Mechanism is a stale expectation, `RUST_RESERVED_CONNECTIONS = 0` reaches `Database.open`, which returns `native=None` for both writer and replica variants, as #49798 and #49804 state

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 3d1714d55a458f625f8aa9ec34aa576e7f50dabf. Test-only change to one stale assertion, verified locally on the CI rig (Postgres, Redis, num_retries=0) at 1 worker

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py database tests/integration/database/test_proxy_database_lifespan.py::test_failed_startup_then_retry_releases_database_resources
```

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Unchanged origin/main test | 4 failed, at the stale NativeDatabase assertion |
| Fix, 5 runs | 4 passed each time |
| Whole file on fix | 4 passed |
| Temporary break, Prisma client not released on failed startup | 2 failed at `assert proxy_server.prisma_client is None`, reverted |
| make lint | exit 0 |

## Type

✅ Test

</details>

title: perf(host-python): settle ready async values inline instead of spawning on tokio
body:
_Requested by **Nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK?thread=cmsg_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK38rSz2wPy7A3rHdu9qK7Mu)_ ## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description Saves a HUGE amount of time on cache reads
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Every awaited Rust bridge call spawns on tokio and wakes asyncio cross-thread - About 125 us CPU per call, even for in-memory spend counter reads - A virtual-key request makes about 14 of these calls How it solves it: - Poll the future once inline; return a settled asyncio future if ready - Pending futures go to tokio exactly as before ## What changed `run_async_value` in `litellm/rust/crates/host-python/src/runtime.rs` always handed its future to pyo3-async-runtimes `future_into_py`, which spawns a tokio task and wakes the asyncio loop from another thread when it finishes. That costs about 125 us of CPU per call even when the future has nothing to wait on, such as an in-memory `SpendCounterStore.read`. It now polls the future once on the caller's thread, through the existing `poll_async_value` (tokio runtime entered, GIL released, panics caught, fork gate claimed exactly as before). When that first poll completes, the call returns an asyncio future on the caller's running loop that is already settled with the value, or with the exception, so an error still surfaces at `await` as it did before. When the poll is pending, the same pinned future goes to `future_into_py` unchanged, so it resumes on tokio without restarting. The loop future is created before the poll, so calling without a running loop still raises before any of the future runs. No Python callback moves to another task or loop and `into_future` is not used. Any Python a ready future reaches during its first poll (logger sink, a test clock, reply conversion) now runs on the caller's thread inside the caller's task instead of on a tokio worker. Two tests in `tests/unit/caching/test_request_redis_batch_post_call.py` leaned on `await flush_post_call_redis_batches()` yielding to the loop once so the fake rate-limit store's `ensure_future` writes could run. A native call that completes inline no longer yields, so they now call the fake's own `settle()`, which exists to run the post-call writes the way a real flush would. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy A/B for the whole series (#51901, #51902, #51903, #51904, #51905, #51906, #51912), main e38187324 against main with all seven merged, open loop, one uvicorn worker pinned to one core, mock upstream that answers instantly, virtual key with team and user budgets, Postgres and Redis. Small requests: 3 RPS, 180 per run, two interleaved rounds. Large requests (100k-token prompt, 2k-token reply): 1 RPS, 60 per run, back to back. Every response was a 200. CPU is proxy utime+stime divided by upstream hits. The combined build's Rust extension was compiled without LTO and main's with fat LTO, so the series gain is if anything understated. This PR's own share is about 1.5 to 2 ms per small virtual-key request (about 14 bridge calls at roughly 105 us saved each). | Path | main CPU ms/req | all seven CPU ms/req | p50 ms main / all | |---|---|---|---| | /chat/completions | 32.3 | 28.6 (-11%) | 23.4 / 20.6 | | /chat/completions, streamed | 41.1 | 34.1 (-17%) | 29.6 / 25.0 | | /v1/messages | 32.4 | 29.9 (-8%) | 21.7 / 20.5 | | /v1/messages, streamed | 38.9 | 34.5 (-11%) | 21.9 / 19.3 | | 100k /chat/completions | 60.7 | 42.3 (-30%) | 47.5 / 31.5 | | 100k /chat/completions, streamed | 866 | 646 (-25%) | 845 / 621 | | 100k /v1/messages | 225 | 42 (-81%) | 206 / 31 | | 100k /v1/messages, streamed | 294 | 132 (-55%) | 204 / 41 | `cargo test -p litellm-host-python` passes 163 tests, 0 failed (159 before plus 4 new). The new `an_async_value_settles_inline_only_when_its_first_poll_completes` cases (ready, error, pending) and `an_async_value_without_a_running_loop_fails_before_running_the_future` were checked against the old `run_async_value` body, where the ready and error cases fail. `cargo clippy -p litellm-host-python --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Python suites with the rebuilt extension (`tests/unit/redis`, `tests/unit/rust_bridge`, `tests/unit/caching`, `tests/test_litellm_rust`, spend counter tests under `tests/unit/proxy`) show the same failures as an unmodified main build, all from the test container (proxy CA "Missing Authority Key Identifier" in the Azure token TLS tests, the fork guard tests, and a flaky aiohttp pool test). A broader sweep over `tests/unit/proxy/hooks`, `tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking`, `tests/unit/proxy/auth`, `tests/unit/router_strategy`, `tests/unit/test_router` and `tests/unit/secret_managers` gave 17286 passed and 25 failed plus 1 collection error; the same 26 also fail on the main build, mostly because `semantic_router` is not installed there. Microbench, 5000 awaited `SpendCounterStore.read` calls on the in-memory store, three runs each: | build | wall us/call | cpu us/call | |---|---|---| | main e38187324 (release, fat LTO) | 128 to 153 | 124 to 130 | | this branch (release, LTO off) | 18 to 24 | 18 to 24 | The before build has fat LTO and the after build does not, so the gap is if anything understated. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - A native await that finishes on its first poll no longer yields to the loop - Same as awaiting any done asyncio future; a tight loop of them starves other tasks - Code relying on that incidental yield needs `await asyncio.sleep(0)` - The first poll runs on the event loop thread with the GIL released - A future that blocks before its first await would block the loop - None found among current callers (Redis stores, secrets, S3 logging, DB, websocket, drivers) ### Low - `native.rs` and `callbacks-python/src/hosted.rs` already pre-poll, so their pending path polls once more - Cheap; those pre-polls could later fold into this one ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: perf(streaming): extract usage once per chunk when assembling stream usage
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"nate-berri"} -->
_Requested by **Nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK?thread=cmsg_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK38rSz2wPy7A3rHdu9qK7Mu)_

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Only extract usage once per chunk when assembling usage

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Stream rebuild scans every chunk for usage three times
- Each scan hits slow pydantic attribute lookups

How it solves it:

- Extract usage once per chunk and reuse it for pricing fields

## What changed

`ChunkProcessor._calculate_usage_per_chunk` called `extract_usage_chunk` on every chunk of a stream, and then `_last_provider_pricing_field` walked the whole stream two more times (once for `inference_geo`, once for `speed`) calling `extract_usage_chunk` again on every chunk. So every assembled stream paid for three full usage extractions per chunk.

The usage objects are now extracted once into a tuple and reused by the accumulation loop and by both pricing field lookups. `_last_provider_pricing_field` becomes a static method that takes the already extracted usage objects. `extract_usage_chunk` has no side effects and nothing mutates the extracted objects, so the result is the same.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Proxy A/B for the whole series (#51901, #51902, #51903, #51904, #51905, #51906, #51912), main e38187324 against main with all seven merged, open loop, one uvicorn worker pinned to one core, mock upstream that answers instantly, virtual key with team and user budgets, Postgres and Redis. Small requests: 3 RPS, 180 per run, two interleaved rounds. Large requests (100k-token prompt, 2k-token reply): 1 RPS, 60 per run, back to back. Every response was a 200. CPU is proxy utime+stime divided by upstream hits. The combined build's Rust extension was compiled without LTO and main's with fat LTO, so the series gain is if anything understated. This PR's own share is the microbenchmark below.

| Path | main CPU ms/req | all seven CPU ms/req | p50 ms main / all |
|---|---|---|---|
| /chat/completions | 32.3 | 28.6 (-11%) | 23.4 / 20.6 |
| /chat/completions, streamed | 41.1 | 34.1 (-17%) | 29.6 / 25.0 |
| /v1/messages | 32.4 | 29.9 (-8%) | 21.7 / 20.5 |
| /v1/messages, streamed | 38.9 | 34.5 (-11%) | 21.9 / 19.3 |
| 100k /chat/completions | 60.7 | 42.3 (-30%) | 47.5 / 31.5 |
| 100k /chat/completions, streamed | 866 | 646 (-25%) | 845 / 621 |
| 100k /v1/messages | 225 | 42 (-81%) | 206 / 31 |
| 100k /v1/messages, streamed | 294 | 132 (-55%) | 204 / 41 |

The large requests resend the same body, which is the best case for the token count memo in #51904.

Commit ead8aa354 on `nate_stream_usage_single_scan`, based on origin/main e38187324.

A new test, `test_pricing_fields_take_last_reported_value_across_stream_chunks`, builds a stream where the first usage chunk carries `speed` and `inference_geo`, a later one changes only `inference_geo`, and chunks without usage sit between them. It checks that `speed` keeps the earlier value, `inference_geo` takes the last value, and completion tokens come from the last usage chunk.

```
pytest tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py \
  tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_cursor.py \
  tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_chunk_builder_server_tool_use.py \
  tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_stream_usage_logging.py -n 2
137 passed
```

The in-process microbenchmark used 2,000 `ModelResponseStream` chunks, timed 30 to 40 runs, and reported the min. The shared 4 vCPU box was under load averages of 7 to 11, so medians were noisy and min is the more stable number.

| Case | origin/main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_calculate_usage_per_chunk`, usage on last chunk only | 27.5 ms | 10.0 ms |
| `_calculate_usage_per_chunk`, usage on every chunk | 32.0 ms | 26.0 ms |
| `stream_chunk_builder`, usage on last chunk only | 60.0 to 66.6 ms | 43.1 to 51.0 ms |
| `stream_chunk_builder`, usage on every chunk | 66.2 to 67.8 ms | 59.4 to 62.3 ms |

## Type

🧹 Refactoring

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Microbench ran on a loaded shared box, so absolute numbers are noisy
  - The 2.7x drop for the usage pass held across runs

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - DualCache formats cached objects into debug strings even with verbose off - About 0.6 ms per virtual-key request How it solves it: - Pass values as logging arguments so they format only when printed ## What changed `DualCache.get_cache`, `async_get_cache`, `async_set_cache` and `async_set_cache_pipeline` logged through `print_verbose` with f-strings. CPU is proxy utime+stime divided by upstream hits. The combined build's Rust extension was compiled without LTO and main's with fat LTO, so the series gain is if anything understated. title: perf(auth): read token model fields from the class instead of deprecated __fields__
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"nate-berri"} -->
_Requested by **Nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK?thread=cmsg_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK38rSz2wPy7A3rHdu9qK7Mu)_

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Auth reads the deprecated `__fields__` on every virtual-key request
- Pydantic builds a deprecation warning per team field
- Two S3 403-retry tests flake on CI on a wall-clock bound

How it solves it:

- Read `model_fields` from the class instead
- Assert the 403 retry backoff on the uploader's logged wait

## What changed

When a cached virtual key's team was refreshed after the key, `user_api_key_auth_builder` copies the team's values onto the token. For each team field it checked `field_name in valid_token.__fields__`. In pydantic v2, `__fields__` is a deprecated property that builds and issues a `PydanticDeprecatedSince20` warning on every access, so this loop paid for about 34 deprecation warnings per request on that path.

The check now reads `type(valid_token).model_fields`, which holds the same field names with no deprecation path. The only other uses of `__fields__` in `litellm/` are in the Langfuse integration's prompt handling, which runs only when a Langfuse prompt object is passed, so they are not on the auth or request hot path and stay unchanged.

Folded in for CI: `test_async_upload_retries_403_with_fresh_credentials_and_signature` and `test_async_upload_exhausts_403_retries_through_production_http_handler` in `tests/unit/integrations/test_s3_v2_rust.py` failed on unrelated PRs at 1.77 to 1.79 s against a 1.75 s bound. After a 403 the Rust uploader drops its credentials and the next attempt re-runs the profile's `credential_process`, a Python script, so the measured gap is the jittered sleep plus interpreter startup. The new `_assert_logged_backoff` reads the waits the uploader logs ("retrying in X.XXs"), asserts one wait per retry inside the production range `[0.5, 1.5] * 2^attempt`, and asserts each observed gap is at least its logged wait. The 5xx retry tests, which keep their credentials, still use the wall-clock helper.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Proxy A/B for the whole series (#51901, #51902, #51903, #51904, #51905, #51906, #51912), main e38187324 against main with all seven merged, open loop, one uvicorn worker pinned to one core, mock upstream that answers instantly, virtual key with team and user budgets, Postgres and Redis. Small requests: 3 RPS, 180 per run, two interleaved rounds. Large requests (100k-token prompt, 2k-token reply): 1 RPS, 60 per run, back to back. Every response was a 200. CPU is proxy utime+stime divided by upstream hits. The combined build's Rust extension was compiled without LTO and main's with fat LTO, so the series gain is if anything understated. This PR's own share is the microbenchmark below.

| Path | main CPU ms/req | all seven CPU ms/req | p50 ms main / all |
|---|---|---|---|
| /chat/completions | 32.3 | 28.6 (-11%) | 23.4 / 20.6 |
| /chat/completions, streamed | 41.1 | 34.1 (-17%) | 29.6 / 25.0 |
| /v1/messages | 32.4 | 29.9 (-8%) | 21.7 / 20.5 |
| /v1/messages, streamed | 38.9 | 34.5 (-11%) | 21.9 / 19.3 |
| 100k /chat/completions | 60.7 | 42.3 (-30%) | 47.5 / 31.5 |
| 100k /chat/completions, streamed | 866 | 646 (-25%) | 845 / 621 |
| 100k /v1/messages | 225 | 42 (-81%) | 206 / 31 |
| 100k /v1/messages, streamed | 294 | 132 (-55%) | 204 / 41 |

The large requests resend the same body, which is the best case for the token count memo in #51904.

`test_check_blocked_team` now runs auth with `PydanticDeprecatedSince20` raised as an error, and asserts the returned token picked up the newer team values (`team_blocked is False` and `team_tpm_limit == 123`). With `__fields__` restored, the test fails, because the warning raises inside the refresh block, the update gets skipped, and the token stays blocked. It passes with this change.

```
pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth -n 3
5559 passed, 2 skipped
```

The in-process microbenchmark ran the field membership loop over the 34 `team_*` names from `LiteLLM_TeamTableCachedObj` against a `UserAPIKeyAuth`, 2,000 loops per sample and 7 samples.

| | origin/main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| median per refresh loop | 41.9 us | 11.7 us |

S3 tests: with a 1.0 s sleep added to the test's credential script to mimic CI overhead, the old assertion failed 3 of 3 runs and the new one passed 3 of 3. Without it, both 403 tests passed 5 of 5 runs, and the 11 S3 tests matching 403, 5xx or frozen_credential pass.

## Type

🧹 Refactoring
✅ Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Measured auth saving is about 30 us per request with default warning filters
  - Smaller than the 0.3 ms profile estimate; larger when warnings always emit
- The 403 tests no longer bound the gap from above
  - A sleep much longer than its logged wait would go unnoticed there

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(ui): clarify customer usage periods and preserve date ranges
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description fix time period edge cases in customer management
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Customer detail dates omit today's UTC usage after local midnight diverges. - Customer navigation drops the selected range. - Unbudgeted summaries show resettable counters beside historical spend. How it solves it: - Share UTC calendar ranges and preserve dates across customer links. - Keep existing saved ranges and relative presets working. - Show “No budget set” when no budget is configured. Intentional product change: customer detail pages default to the same full UTC calendar month as the customer list. Month-to-date remains available. Unbudgeted summaries stop displaying the scalar counter. Configured budget counters and resets keep their existing behavior. ## User Flow Before, a customer admin sees different dates and totals while inspecting the same usage. 1. Open `/ui/customers/usage?org=example-org&range=MTD` after UTC midnight while the browser is still on November 14. 2. See November 1–14 and $0.86, although November 15 contains another $0.10. 3. Select November 14–15, open a member's Settings, then return to Usage. The dates reset and spend changes. 4. An unbudgeted organization also shows `$0.00 / No limit` beside its historical spend. After, the selected UTC dates and their usage stay consistent. 1. Open the same URL with the same browser timezone and data. 2. See November 1–15 and $0.96, including the current UTC day. 3. Select November 14–15, open a member's Settings, then return to Usage. The selection and $0.71 persist. 4. The unbudgeted organization shows “No budget set.” ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The focused test files pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] The scope is limited to consistent customer usage periods - [ ] Automated reviews on the latest commit have finished and findings are addressed ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Tested base `61483d8f04c` and tip `5dd7d845a8533f3ab61880be72642a597c0b129e`. Both include the Customer Management rename from #51891. The screenshots above use the same URL and synthetic data on a live proxy and PostgreSQL database. This is a reporting/UI change, so historical rows were seeded directly and no inference was needed. The browser used America/New_York on November 14 after midnight UTC on November 15. The proxy ran two workers with dedicated Redis. The same backend and database served both revisions. Desktop and narrow layouts were checked. Native keyboard date entry, Settings navigation, returning to the customer list, and browser Back were exercised.
Standalone local setup and synthetic seed Use a disposable PostgreSQL database. Export `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` locally. The model entry uses `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE` and `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` from the existing gateway environment. No model requests are made by this reproduction. Start dedicated Redis with `redis-server --port 16472 --bind 127.0.0.1 --save '' --appendonly no`. Save this as `/tmp/customer-feedback.yaml`. ```yaml model_list: - model_name: feedback-model litellm_params: model: openai/openai/gpt-6.1-sol api_base: os.environ/LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 16472 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 16472 litellm_settings: drop_params: true timezone: UTC ``` Start the proxy from the repository root. ```sh export PROXY_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4317 export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/customer-feedback.yaml --port 4017 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver ``` Both server processes reached startup completion. Debug output was filtered before saving to remove runtime credentials and service addresses. Start the current checkout's UI in another terminal. ```sh cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4017 NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4317 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4317 ``` Save the following as `/tmp/seed-customer-feedback.py`, then run it with `QA_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4017 .venv/bin/python /tmp/seed-customer-feedback.py` using the same database and master-key environment. It is safe to repeat against this disposable fixture. ```python import asyncio, json, logging, os import httpx from prisma import Prisma logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL) async def main(): async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=os.environ['QA_PROXY_URL'], headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer '+os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}, timeout=30) as client: async def create(resource, body, identifier): response = await client.post('/management/v1/'+resource, json=body) if response.status_code == 409: response = await client.get('/management/v1/'+resource+'/'+identifier) response.raise_for_status() title: feat(customers): search customer members by ID or alias in the Members tab
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Admins can now search customer members by name or ID in the Members tab. Before, they had to page through the list 20 at a time.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2e3725b4d39e4a1696e9b877ff36edd1
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2e3725b4d39e4a1696e9b877ff36edd1?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Members tab shows 20 members per page with no search
- `GET /management/v1/customer_members` rejects a `search` parameter
- Finding one member in a large organization means paging by hand

How it solves it:

- New optional `search` on the member list endpoint
- Case-insensitive match on member ID or alias, before pagination
- Search box on the Members tab, at organization and team scope
- Search lives in the URL and resets the page to 1

## User Flow

Before: an admin looking for one member in an organization of 62 has to click through pages, because the Members tab cannot search

1. They open http://localhost:3100/ui/customers/manage?org=acme-org&tab=members and see the first 20 members with no search box
2. They page forward until the member shows up, here on page 4
3. A script that sends GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members?parent_org_id=acme-org&search=zoe gets a 400 saying `search` is not a recognized query parameter

![Before: Members tab with no search box](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..ezKOWkk433B4MqUhSBrR-FEx3_5Srmb6vrCe-Dr2O2Q)

After: the same admin types part of the name or ID and the member shows up, whichever page it was on

1. They open http://localhost:3100/ui/customers/manage?org=acme-org&tab=members and see a search box above the table
2. They type `zoe` and the table shows `zoe-9001` and `sales-zoe`, and the URL gains `memberSearch=zoe`
3. Inside the Engineering team the same search shows only `zoe-9001`, and a term with no match shows "No customer members match your search."
4. The same GET with `search=zoe` returns 200 with those two members and `total_count: 2`

![After: organization scope search](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..Mce0X2NFonczFonHbTdwYA42XoaJxypB4Vvtc0x0Emo)

![After: team scope search restored from the URL](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..84qUGv6DCAIHjLYU8apEwFsZ8RV383Y3PDRJ64mI9C0)

![After: no matches](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..1LVIB37BJaECHy9Ut9TyR-VFN5kZxKEs25Yrr53NMRM)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, used for both legs. Postgres and Redis run locally, and `DATABASE_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` are set in the environment. The proxy ran with two workers and without `--reload` or `--detailed_debug`, because the before leg needs the process to keep serving the base code while the checkout changes.

```yaml
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6379
router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6379
```

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard && NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:4000 npm run dev -- -p 3100
```

<details>
<summary>Seed data: 2 organizations, 3 teams, 63 members</summary>

```bash
B=http://localhost:4000/management/v1; H=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json")
p(){ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " "${H[@]}" -X POST $B/$1 -d "$2"; }
p customer_organizations '{"customer_org_id":"acme-org","alias":"Acme","default_budgets":[{"name":"standard","max_budget":50}],"default_budget_template":"standard"}'
p customer_organizations '{"customer_org_id":"other-org","alias":"Other","default_budgets":[{"name":"standard","max_budget":50}],"default_budget_template":"standard"}'
p customer_teams '{"customer_team_id":"eng","alias":"Engineering","parent_org_id":"acme-org"}'
p customer_teams '{"customer_team_id":"sales","alias":"Sales","parent_org_id":"acme-org"}'
p customer_teams '{"customer_team_id":"other-team","alias":"Other Team","parent_org_id":"other-org"}'
for i in $(seq -w 1 60); do p customer_members "{\"customer_member_id\":\"emp-$i\",\"alias\":\"Employee $i\",\"parent_team_ids\":[\"eng\"]}"; done
p customer_members '{"customer_member_id":"zoe-9001","alias":"Zoe Zimmerman","parent_team_ids":["eng"]}'
p customer_members '{"customer_member_id":"sales-zoe","alias":"Zoe Sales","parent_team_ids":["sales"]}'
p customer_members '{"customer_member_id":"outside-zoe","alias":"Zoe Outside","parent_team_ids":["other-team"]}'
```

</details>

### Before (745886e5ff)

#### API search

1. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" "http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members?parent_org_id=acme-org&page_size=20&search=ZOE"` returns 400

```json
{"type":"urn:litellm:error:unknown-query-parameter","title":"Unknown query parameter","status":400,"detail":"Unrecognized query parameter(s): search.","allowed":["page","page_size","parent_org_id","parent_team_id"]}
```

#### Members tab

1. Log in at http://localhost:3100/ui/login as `admin` with the master key
2. Open http://localhost:3100/ui/customers/manage?org=acme-org&tab=members (before screenshot under User Flow). The table lists `emp-01` to `emp-20`, there is no search input on the page, and the only member request is `?parent_org_id=acme-org&page=1&page_size=20`

### After (9ce2bf04ce)

#### API search

Each line is the query string sent to `GET /management/v1/customer_members`, followed by the member IDs and `meta` that came back.

```text
parent_org_id=acme-org&page_size=20
  emp-01 ... emp-20   {'total_count': 62, 'page': 1, 'page_size': 20, 'total_pages': 4}
parent_org_id=acme-org&page_size=20&search=ZOE
  ['zoe-9001', 'sales-zoe'] {'total_count': 2, 'page': 1, 'page_size': 20, 'total_pages': 1}
parent_team_id=eng&search=zoe
  ['zoe-9001'] {'total_count': 1, 'page': 1, 'page_size': 50, 'total_pages': 1}
parent_org_id=acme-org&search=9001
  ['zoe-9001'] {'total_count': 1, 'page': 1, 'page_size': 50, 'total_pages': 1}
parent_org_id=acme-org&search=emp-5&page=2&page_size=5
  ['emp-55', 'emp-56', 'emp-57', 'emp-58', 'emp-59'] {'total_count': 10, 'page': 2, 'page_size': 5, 'total_pages': 2}
parent_org_id=acme-org&search=%25
  [] {'total_count': 0, 'page': 1, 'page_size': 50, 'total_pages': 0}
```

`outside-zoe` in the other organization never appears, and a literal `%` matches nothing.

#### Members tab

Driven in Chrome with Playwright, with the member requests the page sent recorded next to each step. The after screenshots under User Flow are steps 2, 5 and 6.

1. Open http://localhost:3100/ui/customers/manage?org=acme-org&tab=members&hierarchyPage=3. The page requests `?parent_org_id=acme-org&page=3&page_size=20`
2. Type `zoe` in "Search customer members by name or ID". The page sends one request, `?parent_org_id=acme-org&page=1&page_size=20&search=zoe`, the table shows Zoe Zimmerman and Zoe Sales, and the URL becomes `?org=acme-org&tab=members&memberSearch=zoe`
3. Replace it with `9001`. The table shows only `zoe-9001` and the URL carries `memberSearch=9001`
4. Press browser Back. The URL and the input both return to `zoe`, and the two Zoe rows come back
5. Type `nobody-here`. The table shows "No customer members match your search."
6. Open http://localhost:3100/ui/customers/manage?org=acme-org&team=eng&tab=members&memberSearch=ZOE. The input is prefilled with `ZOE`, the request is `?parent_team_id=eng&page=1&page_size=20&search=ZOE`, and only Zoe Zimmerman is listed

Focused checks at the same tip: `uv run pytest tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/test_customers.py tests/unit/proxy/management_helpers/test_customer_hierarchy.py -q -n 4` gives 200 passed, and `npx vitest run "src/app/(dashboard)/customers/manage/page.integration.test.tsx"` gives 16 passed, and `CustomerMemberSearch.test.tsx` covers a pending search being dropped when the URL value changes.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Substring search uses `ILIKE '%term%'`, so it scans the scoped members
- The Usage page member table is unchanged, it already loads every member
- Only English strings were added for the two new labels

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Read-only list filtering on admin-only management APIs with escaped LIKE patterns; main caveat is DB scan cost on very large member sets within a scope.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **server-side search** for customer members so admins can filter by name or ID instead of paging through long lists.
> 
> `GET /management/v1/customer_members` accepts an optional `search` query (trimmed, case-insensitive substring on `customer_member_id` and `alias`) applied **before** pagination and scoped by existing `parent_org_id` / `parent_team_id` filters. Backend search logic is centralized in `_search_filter`, also used by organization listing.
> 
> The dashboard **Members** tab gets a debounced search box (`CustomerMemberSearch`) wired through URL state (`memberSearch`), which resets pagination to page 1 and shows a dedicated empty state when nothing matches. OpenAPI types and unit/integration tests cover filtering, URL restore, and stale debounced requests.
>

title: fix(spend): backport PostgreSQL 12 delivery migration compatibility
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Backports the PostgreSQL 12 startup fix from #51868 to the 1.110 release branch. Fresh installations no longer require the database UUID extension, and existing installations retain their delivery records

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- PostgreSQL 12 startup fails without pgcrypto

How it solves it:

- Removes the delivery migration's database UUID default
- Keeps Prisma UUID generation in all three schemas
- Drops existing database defaults through a follow-up migration

This PR now backports only #51868, merged to main as e38187324ad3b49e8111c6823a8cfb3c7d6c2f7d. Removed-settings warnings and long-ID recovery are excluded

## User Flow

Before, a fresh PostgreSQL 12 installation fails during startup

1. Start the proxy against PostgreSQL 12 without pgcrypto
2. Startup stops with `function gen_random_uuid() does not exist`

After, the same installation can start

1. Start the proxy against PostgreSQL 12 without pgcrypto
2. Startup completes and requests receive generated delivery IDs

## Affected release

The affected migration is present in v1.110.0-rc.1. This backport targets rc/1.110.0

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Meaningful migration regression tests are included
- [x] The diff contains only the PostgreSQL compatibility fix
- [x] Refreshed affected tests and live verification complete
- [ ] Current CI and review results inspected

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Baseline `3510cb6a60ddae1b75a012d249f15578a58ba82c`, candidate `155e3e8e2e659897c72ea99a23fe70d64b6c1e5c`

Independent Devin executed both source checkouts on PostgreSQL 12.22. The native source tree is identical at baseline and head, and both used extension SHA-256 `737556bf321c18d8b40998c08958588211452b1a2953b2fac9238dd3c286d04c`

| Case | Baseline 3510cb6a | Head 155e3e8e |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh database without pgcrypto | P3018, missing gen_random_uuid, one unfinished migration | Ready, 233 completed migrations, pgcrypto absent |
| Three normal chat requests | Cannot serve on fresh database | Three HTTP 200 responses, three applied deliveries, attempts zero |
| Generated delivery IDs | Database default on pgcrypto installation | 32-character hex IDs matching spend-log rows, no database default |
| Upgrade existing pgcrypto installation | 232 migrations and three applied deliveries | 233 migrations, original delivery and spend-log full-row hashes unchanged |
| Existing migration checksums | 232 recorded | All 232 unchanged, only drop-default migration added |
| Boot after baseline failed migration | Failed migration recorded | P3009 until resolve command below, then ready and three chats applied |

Live runs used one worker, no Redis and mock provider responses. This checks startup, schema compatibility and ordinary persistence, not concurrency or provider billing

The two mapped integration files passed all 91 tests on PostgreSQL 14.24 with Redis. All five canonical gates passed against the RC merge base, affected-test Ruff passed and the no-data-rewrites migration check passed. Type checking passed its existing budget, not a zero-error claim

The same integration harness is not PostgreSQL 12 compatible. Its teardown uses PG13-only `DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE)`, one setup recreates the old UUID default without pgcrypto, and another lacked REDIS_HOST. These setup failures do not invalidate the separate passing live PG12 cases

[Sanitized executed commands and result bundle](https://app.devin.ai/attachments/144ae5e1-f89b-44dc-8478-ffbfa267eb74/m155_public.tgz) contains base.sh, tip.sh, live.sh, tests.sh and result summaries. Access may require Devin authentication. The measured results are included above for reviewers

### CI and reviews

All CI jobs completed. The core-utils shard fails three unchanged timezone tests because the runner lacks tzdata for US/Eastern, which also fails the aggregate unit status. No dependency or timezone code changed in this seven-file migration diff. This is unrelated and has not been repaired or bypassed. Other checks, including db-and-spend, Buildkite E2E, Codecov and CLA, pass

Bugbot reports no new issues and Veria reports zero open concerns at 155e3e8e. Greptile scored 4/5 and requested this current-tip live evidence. Its confirmation is pending

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Medium

- An already failed migration needs explicit recovery before restarting

```bash
prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20261103010000_spendlogs_accounting_delivery
```

## Final Attestation

- [ ] Current-tip verification and reviews are complete

</details>

<details>

- Keeps routes, API paths, DB fields and i18n keys unchanged

Intentional product change: the workspace switcher, sidebar group, breadcrumb and free tier limit messages now say Customer Management. API error titles change from "Customer portal busy" to "Customer Management busy", and from "Free customer portal limit reached" to "Customer Management free tier limit reached", so anything matching on those strings needs an update.

## User Flow

Before: the admin opens the workspace switcher and sees Customer Portal

1. Open http://localhost:3000/ui and click the workspace switcher
2. The menu lists Customer Portal, and /customers shows a CUSTOMER PORTAL sidebar group

After: the same screens say Customer Management

1. Open http://localhost:3000/ui and click the workspace switcher

title: test(e2e): drop two batch waits that never finish in time
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The batches e2e file spends about 9 minutes on two waits
- Neither wait ever finishes in time, so the time buys nothing
- The batches file is the longest file, so it caps xdist speedups

How it solves it:

- Batch cleanup leaves a managed batch that is still cancelling, like a raw one
- `TestBatchTerminalState` lists the marker batches once instead of for 5 minutes

## User Flow

Before: a release engineer running the e2e suite waits on two timeouts in the batches file on every run

1. They start a `litellm-e2e` build for a release candidate
2. `test_batch_lifecycle[openai-unified]` takes 126 s, 120 s of it waiting for a cancelling batch that stays cancelling
3. `TestBatchSecondHop` takes 140 s for the same reason
4. `TestBatchTerminalState` takes 303 s listing batches that never contain a completed marker, then passes on its submission checks

After: the same three tests finish without the dead waits, with the same pass or fail outcome

1. They start the same build
2. The two batch tests stop as soon as the batch reports `cancelling`, and the leftover input file is still reported as a warning
3. `TestBatchTerminalState` lists once and takes the same documented pass

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proof is a full `litellm-e2e` Buildkite run of this branch's tip against real providers. Main SHAs need the router fix in BerriAI/litellm-test-infra#46 to deploy, so the run uses that branch of the pipeline and changes nothing else.

### Before (merge base)

JUnit durations from the 55 `litellm-e2e` builds saved between builds 811 and 882. `test_batch_lifecycle[openai-unified]` took 126 s in every passing run but one (build 853, 15 s). `TestBatchSecondHop::test_unified_create_and_retrieve_via_chained_gateway` took 139 to 141 s in every passing run. `TestBatchTerminalState::test_completed_batch_downloads_output_and_books_cost` took 302 to 304 s in every passing run, which means it never found a completed marker.

### After (8ff564f286ef)

[Build 885](https://buildkite.com/litellm/litellm-e2e/builds/885) ran the full suite at this tip against real providers. The three tests went from 126 s to 3.8 s, from 140 s to 17.0 s, and from 303 s to 0.9 s, and all three passed. The batches file is no longer one of the four slowest files in the run.

The run ended 974 passed, 3 failed, 70 skipped. None of the three failures is in code this PR touches, and each one also failed in the saved builds before it.

- `test_batch_lifecycle[azure-provider_fallback]` got a 404 from Azure on create right after upload. It failed 5 times in the 55 saved builds, and #51857 fixes it. That fix merged after this branch was cut, so this tip does not have it.
- `test_ocr_reads_the_document_and_bills_its_pages[azure-ai-image]` lost its connection to the stack router. It failed once before, in build 859.
- `test_cache_read_tokens_bill_at_the_cache_read_rate` got no cached tokens back from Together. It failed 11 times in the 55 saved builds.

The UI Playwright suite in the same build failed one dashboard spec (`keyBudgetWindow.spec.ts`), and that suite does not run any batch test.

Harness tests for the cleanup change pass locally:

```
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-harness uv run pytest tests/e2e_harness/batches -q
51 passed
```

Against the old `batch_cleanup.py`, `test_batch_already_cancelling_is_left_without_cancelling_again_or_waiting[<managed id>]` and `test_managed_batch_left_cancelling_leaves_its_input_file_and_reports_it` fail, because the old code keeps polling a cancelling managed batch.

## Type

✅ Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- `TestBatchTerminalState` never reaches its full assertions on Buildkite
  - Each stack starts with an empty database, so the cross-run marker is never listed
  - True before this PR too, and worth its own follow-up

### Low

- A managed batch left cancelling no longer gets its own warning
  - The input file's "left in place" warning still names that batch
- The rare run where cancellation finished within 120 s now leaves the input file too

## QA runbook

- tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py::test_batch_lifecycle[openai-unified] - a managed OpenAI batch is created, read back, cancelled, and cleaned up without waiting for the cancel to finish
  - [ ] Upload a batch file through POST http://localhost:4000/v1/files with a scoped key and a managed batch deployment
  - [ ] Create the batch with POST /v1/batches, retrieve it with GET /v1/batches/{id}, then cancel it with POST /v1/batches/{id}/cancel
  - [ ] Expect the cancel to return `cancelling` or `cancelled`, and teardown to return right away with a warning that the input file was left in place
  - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky
- tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py::TestBatchSecondHop::test_unified_create_and_retrieve_via_chained_gateway - a managed batch created through a chained gateway is cleaned up the same way
  - [ ] Run the test against the proxy and expect its duration to drop by about 120 s with the same outcome
  - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky
- tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py::TestBatchTerminalState::test_completed_batch_downloads_output_and_books_cost - submits a marker batch, then checks the newest completed marker's output and cost if one exists
  - [ ] Create a one-line batch with metadata `litellm_e2e_suite: batches-terminal-baton` through POST /v1/batches
  - [ ] List batches once with GET /v1/batches and expect the new marker with a non-terminal status
  - [ ] With no completed marker in the list, expect the test to pass on the submission checks within a few seconds
  - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only changes to e2e helpers and assertions; production batch behavior is unchanged, with slightly looser teardown (leftover input files may warn instead of long polls).
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes two e2e timeouts that never completed in CI while keeping the same pass/fail outcomes.
> 
> **Batch teardown** (`cleanup_batch`): batches already in `cancelling` are left immediately—no re-cancel, no 120s poll, and no managed-vs-raw split. Cancellation polling still runs for in-progress batches, but exits as soon as status is `cancelling` instead of waiting out the deadline with a warning.
> 
> **Terminal marker test** (`TestBatchTerminalState`): drops the 5-minute list poll; it lists marker batches once and uses the newest completed marker if present (same documented vacuous pass when none exist).
> 
> Harness tests in `test_batch_cleanup.py` are updated to match the new cleanup contract.

title: chore(cost-map): add fal_ai seedream v5 pro US edit and text-to-image rows priced per image from their fal.ai pages
body:
Adds the two Seedream 5.0 Pro US endpoints that Fal's model list now carries. Both are kind page, priced from the endpoint's own `llms.txt`, fetched raw on 2026-11-15. `prices fal-ai` returns no rows by design, so nothing here is kind api

- `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/us/text-to-image`, output_cost_per_image=0.135, output_cost_per_image_1K=0.0675, output_cost_per_image_2K=0.135. Page https://fal.ai/models/bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/us/text-to-image/llms.txt says "Pricing is **$0.0675 per output image** for an area up to and including **1536 × 1536 pixels**, or **$0.135 per output image** for an area above **1536 × 1536** and up to **2048 × 2048 pixels**. For example, **2 images at 1536 × 1536 would cost $0.135**."
- `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/us/edit`, output_cost_per_image=0.135, output_cost_per_image_1K=0.0675, output_cost_per_image_2K=0.135. Page https://fal.ai/models/bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/us/edit/llms.txt says "You will be charged for both input and output images. The first input image is not charged, and every additional input image will cost **$0.0045**. Tentative pricing is **$0.0675+ $(0.0045 x number of additional input images)** per output image for images of total area less than or equal to **1536x1536** pixels. For output images with area in between **1536x1536** and **2048x2048** pixels, the price is **$0.135 + $(0.0045 x number of additional input images)** per image."

The schema default on both is `"image_size": {"default": "auto_2K"`, with enum values `auto_1K`, `auto_1.5K` and `auto_2K`, so the base field takes the 2K rate and the 1K field takes the lower rate. This is the rule `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.5/text-to-image` and `/edit` already follow. The page prices by pixel area and does not name the presets, so mapping `auto_2K` to the tier above 1536x1536 is my reading of the preset name. The 1.5K preset bills at the lower rate and has no catalog field, and the edit row is one output with one input image, with the $0.0045 per additional input image left in `metadata` as not modeled

The edit page calls its price tentative. The text-to-image page does not

Cross-check from `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing`, which returns one base price with no tiers, gives `{"endpoint_id":"bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/us/edit","unit_price":0.0675,"unit":"units"}` and `{"endpoint_id":"bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/us/text-to-image","unit_price":0.0675,"unit":"units"}`. That matches the lower tier

Field shape is inherited_from `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.5/text-to-image` and `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.5/edit` for `mode`, `supported_endpoints` and `supports_vision`. Category from the list API is text-to-image and image-to-image

Delisted by the provider, none. Fal's list omits some live endpoints, so absence is never treated as a delisting

title: test(router): hold the concurrent upsert where its build reads the list back
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

The router test that checks a completion still reaches its own deployment while another thread updates an earlier one failed in every scheduled integration run, because its timing hook waited for an internal call that updates no longer make. This PR points the hook at the step where an update now finishes, so the test again pauses the write mid-update and checks the real behavior

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f01b6dc1e76a461883a8951bb6bbec30
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f01b6dc1e76a461883a8951bb6bbec30?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `test_completion_reaches_its_deployment_while_another_thread_upserts_an_earlier_one` failed 6 of 6 scheduled runs
- Its hold waited for `HostedModelList.refresh` called from `HostRegistry._hand_changes`
- `upsert_deployment` now writes through `HostRegistry._run_build`, which ends with `HostedModelList.end_build`
- So the hold never fired and the test timed out with "the write never reached re-indexing"

How it solves it:

- The hold now fires at either re-read seam: `refresh` from `_hand_changes` (deletes) or `end_build` from `_run_build` (upserts, adds)
- Test-only change, no product code touched

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

CI evidence: hard red in all 6 scheduled runs of the last 24h (`times_failed` 6), newest [Job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43646752363/job/132606153953) at d8e8621b7bfe

E2E exception at 60be23be9ea98b1e5713ac1953cc7b00379568f9. A test-only probe fix, proven with the integration runner at 1 worker (the CI failure reproduces there)

1. Forced red, unchanged origin/main: `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py sdk tests/integration/sdk/test_router_concurrent_deployment_delete_sdk.py::test_completion_reaches_its_deployment_while_another_thread_upserts_an_earlier_one` fails with `AssertionError: the write never reached re-indexing`, exactly as CI
2. On the fix, the same command 5 times: 5 of 5 passed
3. On the fix, the whole file once: `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py sdk tests/integration/sdk/test_router_concurrent_deployment_delete_sdk.py` 27 passed

PostgreSQL 15 was a throwaway local instance and each pytest worker gets its own database, Redis, upstream and proxy. `LITELLM_LICENSE` is set because five tests in these files call organization routes, and CI's `integration-license` environment sets it too. Without it those five fail with a 403 on both sides.

```bash
  LITELLM_LICENSE="$LITELLM_LICENSE" \
  PATH="$TREE/.venv/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" \
  HOME="$HOME" \
  PYTHONPATH="$TREE:$TREE/tests:$TREE/tests/e2e" \
  INTEGRATION_PYTHON="$TREE/.venv/bin/python" \
  DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/postgres" \
  LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="sk-$(openssl rand -hex 16)" \
  LITELLM_SALT_KEY=sk-integration-salt \
  LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION \
  LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True \
  STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True \
  AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true \
  DO_NOT_TRACK=1 \
  INTEGRATION_PROXY_DATABASE_URL="" \
  INTEGRATION_PROXY_READ_REPLICA_URL="" \
  INTEGRATION_ROUTING="" \
  INTEGRATION_PEER_URL="" \
  "$TREE/.venv/bin/python" tests/integration/run.py <group> --workers 2 --results <dir> <files>
```

</details>

The accounting run covers every file that uses the changed helper or fixture, not just the files with failing tests.

<details><summary>Files per group</summary>


</details>

### Before (f0445975382)

#### providers

2. `3 failed, 14 passed`. The failures are `test_gemini_image_edit_reports_the_provider_usage_metadata_as_image_usage[counts-only]`, `[details-that-are-not-lists]` and `[empty-usage-object]`, each expecting invented `image_tokens` and `text_tokens` where the proxy now returns `output_tokens_details: {}`
