title: feat(guardrails): make the straiker prompt-block reply opt-in with on_flagged_action
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- #51401 turned every Straiker prompt block into an HTTP 200 reply
- Existing Straiker users silently lose their HTTP 400 on upgrade
- Every other guardrail makes the 200 reply opt-in

How it solves it:

- New Straiker setting `on_flagged_action`: `block` (default) or `passthrough`
- `block` answers a blocked prompt with HTTP 400, as before #51401
- `passthrough` keeps #51401's HTTP 200 reply with `finish_reason: content_filter`
- Blocked answers (post_call) are unchanged in both modes

Intentional product change: on current `main`, a blocked prompt gets an HTTP 200 reply; after this PR it gets HTTP 400 again unless the guardrail sets `on_flagged_action: passthrough`. #51401 merged today, so no release has shipped the 200 yet.

## User Flow

Before (current `main`): an app that treats a Straiker block as an error never sees one

1. The admin has a Straiker guardrail with `mode: pre_call` and no other settings
2. The app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt that leaks AWS keys
3. It gets HTTP 200 with the block message as the assistant reply and `finish_reason: content_filter`
4. The app's error handling never fires, so it shows the block message as if the model said it

After: the same app gets the same HTTP 400 it got before #51401

1. The admin has the same Straiker guardrail with `mode: pre_call` and no other settings
2. The app sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions
3. It gets HTTP 400 with the block message in `error.message`
4. An admin who wants the 200 reply adds `on_flagged_action: passthrough` to the guardrail and gets it

## Behavior changes

### Removed / renamed

- None

### Silent regressions to watch

- A Straiker prompt block is HTTP 400 again by default on `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`. Migration for anyone who wants #51401's 200 reply: set `on_flagged_action: passthrough` on the guardrail
- Guardrails saved through the API store other vendors' defaults as if they were set, `monitor` at the top level and `block` inside `optional_params`. So `passthrough` at either level opts in, `monitor` reads as "not set", and a reloaded guardrail keeps its setting
- Any other value (a typo such as `reply`) blocks with 400 and logs a warning; the constructor itself rejects anything but `block` or `passthrough`
- A policy pipeline step with `on_fail: block` over a Straiker guardrail without `passthrough` now returns Straiker's own block message, as before #51401, instead of main's `Content blocked by guardrail pipeline '<name>'`. Status (400) and error type are unchanged
- A streamed chat prompt block with the default setting writes one failure spend row, as before #51401, instead of main's two
- Dashboard: the edit form of a Straiker guardrail saved with no setting shows `on_flagged_action: monitor`, because the save stores the shared top-level default. `monitor` reads as not set, so the guardrail blocks with 400. Cisco shows the same on main

### Tests pinning the contract

- `test_v3_a_blocked_prompt_is_a_400_by_default_even_where_a_reply_could_be_sent` (all 7 reply-capable call types)
- `test_v3_a_resend_of_a_blocked_prompt_is_a_400_from_memory_by_default`
- `test_v3_a_blocked_answer_is_a_reply_whatever_on_flagged_action_says`
- `test_initializer_reads_on_flagged_action` (flattened, nested, unset, `block`, `monitor`, typo)
- `test_a_guardrail_saved_and_reloaded_keeps_its_on_flagged_action` (real `LitellmParams`, saved with `model_dump()` like the DB write, then reparsed)
- `test_init_rejects_invalid_on_flagged_action`
- Integration: `test_v3_block_verdict_without_on_flagged_action_is_a_400` on chat, messages and responses; the existing reply tests now opt in with `on_flagged_action: passthrough`

## Relevant issues

Follows #51401 (by `srik-straiker`); found during a live audit of that PR.

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live audit at the tip `cea080f09b5`, against the real Straiker v3 API (`sk_agt_` key), OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini`, Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5` and Gemini `gemini-2.5-flash`, no mocks. Four proxies ran side by side, two workers each, `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, each with its own Postgres database, with a logging forwarder in front of Straiker, OpenAI and Anthropic so every outbound request was captured and compared:

- **pre-#51401** (`52d1c4cd801`): what released versions do today
- **main** (`d8e8621b7bf`)
- **this PR** (`cea080f09b5`)
- **merged** (`refs/pull/51870/merge` at `18a80ed9b02`, a subset of the cells)

pre-#51401 and main ran the PR's tree with only the three Straiker product files swapped, so everything else is byte-identical. 340 cells per proxy; each cell compares status, body, `x-litellm-*` header names, outbound request count per destination, spend rows by tag and logging callbacks by call id.

![Logs and dashboard flow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51870/evidence/flow_cea080f09b5.webp)

| Logs: default guardrail, HTTP 400 | Logs: `passthrough`, HTTP 200 reply |
|---|---|
| ![default](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51870/evidence/H-50-detail-922ba40b_cea080f09b5.png) | ![passthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51870/evidence/H-50-detail-2063ad1a_cea080f09b5.png) |

| Create form: new `on_flagged_action` field | Edit form of a guardrail saved with no setting (this PR) | Same edit form for Cisco on main |
|---|---|---|
| ![create](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51870/evidence/H-29-on-flagged-action-step2_cea080f09b5.png) | ![edit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51870/evidence/H-33-edit-ofa-st-default_cea080f09b5.png) | ![cisco](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51870/evidence/M-33-edit-ofa-ui-cisco-base_cea080f09b5.png) |

Status code for the blocked prompt (cells per row in brackets):

| Scenario | pre-#51401 | main | this PR | merged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| YAML with no setting, `block`, `monitor`, a typo (`reply`) or `PASSTHROUGH`: chat, messages, responses, text completions, each streamed and not (39) | 400 | 200 | **400** | 400 |
| YAML with `passthrough` at the top level or in `optional_params` (14) | 400 | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| Embeddings and `/guardrails/apply_guardrail`, any setting (15) | 400 | 400 | 400 | 400 |
| OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, sync, async and streamed, plus the Responses SDK: default (7) / `passthrough` (7) | 400 / 400 | 200 / 200 | **400** / 200 | 400 / 200 |
| Guardrail attached to a virtual key, and a key with `max_parallel_requests: 1`: default / `passthrough` | 400 / 400 | 200 / 200 | **400** / 200 | 400 / 200 (key only) |
| Same blocked prompt sent again (Straiker answers from memory): default / `passthrough` | 400 / 400 | 200 / 200 | **400** / 200 | not run |
| `run_in_parallel: true`: default / `passthrough` | 400 / 400 | 200 / 200 | **400** / 200 | 400 / 200 |
| Policy pipeline step with `on_fail: block` (8) | 400 | 400 | 400 | 400 |
| Saved with POST /guardrails: no setting, `block`, `optional_params` `block`, and `""`, `null`, `" "`, a 5 KB string, `PASSTHROUGH`, a nested typo (33) | 400 | 200 | **400** | 400 |
| Saved with POST /guardrails: `passthrough` top level, nested, or alongside `optional_params` (12) | 400 | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| PUT or PATCH to `passthrough` / PUT to `block` (9) | 400 / 400 | 200 / 200 | 200 / **400** | not run |
| Every saved guardrail again after a restart on the same database, both workers up (45) | 400 | 200 | same as before the restart | same as before the restart |
| Blocked answers (post_call), streamed and not (16) | 200 | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| `/guardrails/apply_guardrail` on an answer while Straiker rejects the call (2) | 500 | 400 | 400 | 400 |
| Straiker 500, 400, no answer, connection refused, `fail_open`, `fail_on_error: false` (14) | | same as main | same as main | not run |

Every 400 for a verdict carries `"message": "This command violates Straiker Inc's policies on Coding Tools usage. Please contact your administrator if you believe this is an error."`, and every 200 carries the same text as the reply. Clean prompts returned 200 on all four proxies in every group. No blocked prompt reached a provider on this PR: every 400 sent 0 requests to OpenAI and Anthropic. Straiker got 0 or 1 requests per cell on every proxy, because the integration answers a resend of a blocked prompt from that worker's memory.

Concurrency and outage leg (48 concurrent requests across chat, messages and responses, streamed and not, half default and half `passthrough`; Straiker taken down 0.8 s in for 3 s; then one worker SIGKILLed and 12 more requests):

| | pre-#51401 | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Straiker down: "detection unavailable" | 38 x 400 | 38 x 400 | 38 x 400 |
| Verdict, default | 400 | 200 | **400** |
| Verdict, `passthrough` | 400 | 200 | 200 |
| After the worker kill, the other worker served | 12 of 12 | 12 of 12 | 12 of 12 |

<details>
<summary>Config, start command and requests</summary>

Env var names: `STRAIKER_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_LICENSE`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`.


```bash
python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 2
```

```bash
curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4000/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
```

Notes on this run:

- The first pass ran while the VM was overloaded by another job, so main and merged booted with one live worker; the restart and concurrency legs were then rerun one proxy at a time with both workers up

🐛 Bug Fix

> Adds a Straiker **`on_flagged_action`** setting (`block` default, `passthrough` opt-in) so blocked **prompts** again return **HTTP 400** with the block message unless the operator explicitly opts into the HTTP 200 assistant-reply path introduced in #51401.

title: fix(spend): support PostgreSQL 12 delivery migrations
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Fix fresh PostgreSQL 12 startup by removing the delivery ID’s database default, which requires gen_random_uuid()
- Keep UUID generation in Prisma with @default(uuid()) and retain the migration that drops the default on existing databases
- Verify fresh installation and upgrades preserve existing delivery rows

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Proxy boot fails on PostgreSQL 12 without pgcrypto
- The SpendLogs delivery migration needs `gen_random_uuid()`, which PG12 lacks

How it solves it:

- Delivery table is created without a database-generated id default
- A follow-up migration drops that default where it already exists
- Prisma schemas use `@default(uuid())`, the proxy always sends the id

## User Flow

Before: an admin running LiteLLM on PostgreSQL 12 cannot start the proxy after upgrading

1. They upgrade LiteLLM and start the proxy against their PostgreSQL 12 database
2. The database migration step stops with `function gen_random_uuid() does not exist`
3. The proxy exits before it serves any request

After: the same admin starts the proxy and spend is tracked as before

1. They upgrade LiteLLM and start the proxy against their PostgreSQL 12 database
2. All migrations apply and the proxy reports ready
3. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions and get 200, and the request's spend shows up on its key

## Affected release

The affected delivery migration is present in v1.110.0-rc.1 and v1.111.0-dev.1

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

All runs below were done on Devin against a PostgreSQL 12.22 container without pgcrypto. The proxy runs from source with a mock provider, since the bug is in the boot migration and needs no real provider call. One worker and no Redis are used because the change only touches migrations and the delivery table, and neither depends on shared router or rate-limit state.

The fresh PostgreSQL 12 boot cases, before and after, were rerun with a native extension rebuilt from the Rust sources these commits share (`litellm/rust_bridge/_native.abi3.so` sha256 `e06fbeb136f3091740e3218b375d75064f212f6f6af8cca3d223e9969e00e3bd`, `uvx maturin@1.15.0 develop`) and gave the same results. The rest ran on an earlier build of the extension from an older commit, whose Rust changes since then touch only the messages and router code.

<details>
<summary>Shared setup: container, config, proxy command, client and SQL</summary>

```bash
docker run -d --name pg12 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<PG_PASSWORD> -p 127.0.0.1:55412:5432 \
  postgres@sha256:2f2a8c2a7d10862e7fba2602e304523554f9df8244c632dafe2628ccb398fb5c
psql ... -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_extension WHERE extname='pgcrypto'"   # 0
psql ... -c "CREATE DATABASE fresh"
```

config.yaml

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mock-gpt
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5-mini
      api_key: dummy
      mock_response: "mock reply"
general_settings:
  master_key: <MASTER_KEY>
  use_spend_logs_ledger: true
  proxy_batch_write_at: 5
```

Env var names: `DATABASE_URL`, `PYTHONPATH`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP`. `DIRECT_URL` unset.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/litellm/enterprise:$PWD/litellm/proxy-extras"
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres:<PG_PASSWORD>@127.0.0.1:55412/fresh"
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4711 --num_workers 1

KEY=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4711/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <MASTER_KEY>" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"user_id":"qa-user"}' | jq -r .key)
for i in 1 2 3; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "http=%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:4711/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"mock-gpt","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
done
```

```sql
SELECT delivery_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{32}$', state, attempts FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogDelivery";
SELECT spend FROM "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" WHERE user_id = 'qa-user';
SELECT coalesce(column_default, 'NONE') FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'LiteLLM_SpendLogDelivery' AND column_name = 'delivery_id';
```

</details>

### Before (36edf9c4b90b2c369ca6269303122ed16aaf86d1)

#### Fresh PostgreSQL 12 boot

1. Start the proxy with the command above
2. It exits with code 2 before it is ready. The migration step reports P3018 on `20261103010000_spendlogs_accounting_delivery` with `ERROR 42883 function gen_random_uuid() does not exist`
3. `_prisma_migrations` shows 226 applied and 1 failed, and `LiteLLM_SpendLogDelivery` does not exist

#### Existing delivery table (PostgreSQL 12 with pgcrypto, and PostgreSQL 14)

1. Boot on this commit, send 3 chats, all HTTP 200, 3 deliveries `applied`, key spend 0.0001275
2. The `delivery_id` default is `(gen_random_uuid())::text`

### After (c3c06b7369876210f0b01fcc1a7f8baa27c82548)

#### Fresh PostgreSQL 12 boot

1. Start the proxy with the same command
2. Ready in about 36s, `_prisma_migrations` shows 250 applied, 0 failed, and `prisma migrate status` prints "Database schema is up to date!"
3. 3 chats return HTTP 200, 3 deliveries with app-supplied 32-hex ids reach `applied` with 0 attempts, SpendLogs has 3 rows, key spend is 0.0001275
4. The `delivery_id` default is NONE and pgcrypto is still not installed

#### Existing delivery table upgraded (PostgreSQL 12 with pgcrypto, and PostgreSQL 14, 5 rows including database-generated ids)

1. `prisma migrate status` before deploy lists only `20261104020000_spendlogs_delivery_id_drop_default` as pending
2. Deploy succeeds through the v2 and legacy resolvers and `migrate status` then says the schema is up to date
3. Row count, row md5, `(ctid, xmin, delivery_id)` md5 and relfilenode are identical before and after, so no row was rewritten
4. The only change is the `delivery_id` default going from `(gen_random_uuid())::text` to NONE

#### Tests and gates on Devin at c3c06b7

1. The two new tests in `tests/integration/database/migrations/test_drop_accounting_event_tables.py` pass on the head and fail on the baseline (`DID NOT RAISE NotNullViolation`, and the drop-default migration file missing)
2. `tests/integration/database/test_spendlogs_delivery.py` 47 passed, `litellm/proxy-extras/tests` 22 passed, `tests/integration/database/test_spendlogs_ledger_parity.py` 101 passed with Redis set
3. `check_migrations_no_data_rewrites.py` and `check_migrations_lock_timeout.py` pass
4. ruff strict, type discipline, test quality, OpenAPI docs and type check gates pass against the merge base

5. `tests/integration/database/migrations/` 86 passed, 2 failed. Both fail the same way on the baseline, so neither comes from this change: `test_schema_migration_in_sync` reports the same pre-existing drift on both commits, none of it on the delivery table, and `test_a_valid_partitioned_parent_index_under_another_name_is_renamed_with_its_children_kept` fails the same `Building index` assertion on both

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A PostgreSQL 12 database whose earlier boot failed on this migration still stops at startup
  - Prisma recorded the failed attempt, so the v2 resolver asks for `prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20261103010000_spendlogs_accounting_delivery`
  - After that one command the next boot applies both migrations
- The edited `20261103010000` migration keeps its old checksum in databases that already applied it
  - Measured: `migrate deploy` and `migrate status` accept it without a warning

### Low

- A PostgreSQL 12 database where the legacy v1 resolver wrongly marked `20261103010000` applied without creating the table fails the v2 boot on the new drop-default migration
  - The legacy v1 resolver on this commit recovers that database and creates the table


Current-tip CI has 105 successful checks and two unrelated image-verification failures in unchanged admin MCP tool discovery. The [backend job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43649425544/job/132617711015) and [migrations job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43649425544/job/132617711076) both fail the same admin MCP test after successful startup. Migration checks passed. These failures are outside this PR and remain unfixed

Greptile scored the current tip 5/5. Cursor Bugbot and Veria found no new issues, and there are no inline findings

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Schema/migration changes affect proxy startup and the spend delivery ledger; mis-migration could block boot or break inserts without an app-supplied id.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes proxy boot on **PostgreSQL 12** (without `pgcrypto`) by stopping migrations from using `gen_random_uuid()` for `LiteLLM_SpendLogDelivery.delivery_id`.
> 
> The spend-log delivery table is created with **no DB default** on `delivery_id`, and a follow-up migration **drops** that default on already-upgraded databases. Prisma schemas switch from `dbgenerated(gen_random_uuid())` to `@default(uuid())` while the proxy continues to supply IDs via `accounting_delivery_id` (`uuid.uuid4().hex`).
> 
> Integration tests now **require explicit `delivery_id`** on inserts and add coverage for app-provided IDs and the drop-default migration path.
>

title: ci(unit): cut unit check time with cheaper per-test resets and fewer non-unit tests
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Fixture setup is 67% of unit test time
- Proxy tests deep-copy the price map before every test
- Enterprise and MCP tests reload litellm before every test
- Unit shards run tests that spawn processes and servers
- Six tests fail on main with no code change

How it solves it:

- The per-test reset copies back only what changed
- 99 process and socket tests move to `tests/integration`
- Four heavy unit shards run on 16-core runners
- The six flaky tests are removed
- Two smoke jobs stop running on pull requests

## User Flow

Before: a contributor waits about 14 minutes for required checks, and 35 of 116 recent green commits waited more than 15

1. They push a commit to a pull request against `main`
2. `unit` starts 44 shards and the slowest one, `proxy-feature-endpoints`, takes 13.7 minutes
3. `smoke` waits about 9 minutes on `windows-sdk`, which runs three tests
4. `unit passed` turns green after about 14 minutes

After: the same push no longer waits on fixture setup, so its slowest unit shard finishes in under 10 minutes

1. They push a commit to a pull request against `main`
2. `unit` starts the same 44 shards and `proxy-feature-endpoints` takes 5.6 minutes
3. `smoke` skips `windows-sdk` and `proxy-build-from-pip`, which still run on every push to `main` and no longer feed `smoke passed`
4. `unit passed` turns green 10.5 minutes after the push in the run below, with a slowest shard of 8.4 minutes

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [ ] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

This PR changes only tests and CI, so the proof is the `unit` workflow running before and after on the same commit of `main`. Both runs were started with `gh workflow run test-unit.yml --ref <branch>`.

### Before (`580203cce6b`)

[Unit run 43633726540](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43633726540) is `main` with `--durations=0` added so every test reports its time.

1. 130,732 test cases took 21,494 s of test time summed over workers. Fixture setup was 14,477 s of that and the test bodies were 6,398 s
2. The median setup per test was 0.12 s for the 56,031 tests under `tests/unit/proxy`, 3.27 s under `tests/unit/enterprise`, 0.21 s under `tests/unit/proxy/mcp_server` and 0.00 s under `tests/unit/llms`
3. The 109 tests this PR set out to move took 921 s, 396 s of it in the MCP client transport tests that wait on a real TCP connection. Ten of them went away when `main` deleted the Python s3_v2 logger in #51539, so 99 move
4. The slowest shard took 13.7 minutes and the 44 shards used 256 runner minutes

### After (`59664597b8a`)

In [unit run 43646150147](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43646150147), the pull request's own run on the tip, every job passed and no test was rerun. The slowest shard took 8.4 minutes, the 44 shards used 188 runner minutes and the whole workflow finished 10.5 minutes after the push.

| Shard | Before, minutes | After, minutes |
|---|---|---|
| proxy-feature-endpoints | 13.7 | 5.6 |
| proxy-endpoints | 11.4 | 5.3 |
| enterprise-routing | 10.8 | 7.0 |
| mcp-elicitation | 10.6 | 4.4 |
| llms-openai-meta | 9.7 | 6.8 |
| enterprise-package | 9.6 | 2.8 |
| root | 9.4 | 3.8 |
| llms-providers | 8.9 | 4.8 |
| router | 8.6 | 8.4 |
| core-utils | 8.3 | 7.0 |
| proxy-auth | 7.0 | 4.6 |

`proxy-auth` was slower than `main` in the first run of this branch, at 9.5 minutes. A test module in its directory registers four models at import, so `litellm.model_cost` differed from the snapshot before every test and the whole price map was still copied each time. `f592beebcb2` copies back only the entries that differ, and the shard's pytest time is now 169 s against 530 s on `main` at `fd6e4fb6a`.

### Unit on the merged tip

[Unit run 43651752067](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43651752067) on `5f28751954e`, after `main` was merged in, passed every job with no failed test and took 18.7 minutes. `main`'s s3 rewrite in #51539 changed the Rust inputs, so `rust-bridge` missed its cache and compiled for 8.2 minutes before any shard started. `main`'s own run on that commit, [43651326250](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43651326250), compiled for 8.3 minutes and took 23.8. The slowest shard was `integrations` at 9.7 minutes, against 9.4 in that `main` run.

### Four unit runs, no new failure or rerun

1. [Run 43641423840](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43641423840) on `0312b94a1fe`, [run 43645252345](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43645252345) on `9900336813e`, run 43646150147 on `59664597b8a` and run 43651752067 on `5f28751954e` all passed every job with no failed test
2. Two tests were rerun, once each. `test_an_active_read_declared_on_the_pre_call_batch_and_never_awaited_leaves_no_coroutine` is rerun in 5 of the last 24 `unit` runs on `main` and `test_custom_content_adapter_accounts_for_one_success[False]` in 6 of them
3. 8 of those 24 `main` runs are red. The two that were checked, [43643588226](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43643588226) and [43641925426](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43641925426), fail on `test_reported_list_cost_is_billed_instead_of_rows`, one of the six tests removed here

### The moved tests inside the integration groups

`integration` ran three times through the `run-ci` label, in [run 43644770195](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43644770195) on `9900336813e`, [run 43648296537](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43648296537) on `59664597b8a` and [run 43651755392](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43651755392) on `5f28751954e`.

1. Every moved file was collected and every one of its cases passed in all three runs, in the `sdk`, `mcp`, `management`, `management-replica`, `accounting` and `extensions` jobs. That was 30 files and 318 cases before `main` was merged in, and 29 files and 307 cases after
2. Each run is red, as every scheduled run on `main` has been for two days, and no failure is in a file this PR adds
3. Most failures also fail on `main`. Ten fail in each of six scheduled `main` runs from the last two days, and `test_cold_workers_fetch_the_beta_map_only_for_filtered_safeguards_requests_off_the_shared_threads` fails in the newest one
4. Four tests failed in one of the three runs, passed in the other two and did not fail in recent `main` runs
   - `test_free_allowance_is_atomic_and_enterprise_resumes_the_unfinished_page` in `database-replica`
   - `test_repeated_hub_reads_return_the_same_rows` in `management-replica`
   - `test_h5_stored_scope_survives_owned_postgres_outage_and_recovers_once` in `extensions`
   - `test_cache_hit_reject_after_ttl_expiry_is_a_miss` in `extensions`

### The moved and remaining tests behave the same

The 30 split files were run before and after on a laptop, before `main` was merged in, with `pytest <files> -n 8 --junitxml=...` and the two reports were compared case by case.

1. All moved cases are collected in their new files and none is left behind
2. All 5,206 cases that stayed in the unit files report the same outcome as before, 5,152 passed, 20 failed and 34 skipped in both runs. The 20 fail on `main` on the same laptop
3. Of the moved cases, 259 passed before and the same 259 pass after. The other 59 fail in both runs because the laptop environment has no installed `litellm` package for a child interpreter to import
4. `pytest tests/unit/enterprise tests/unit/proxy/mcp_server -n 5 --dist=loadscope` fails the same 72 node ids on `main` and on this branch, passes 8,374 on both, and takes 385 s on `main` against 75 s here

### Checks that guard the test layout

1. `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` reports that all 4,410 test files are still selected by a job
2. `python litellm/scripts/test_quality_gate.py` reports that no rule grew past its merge-base count
3. `ruff check --config .github/linters/ruff-tests.toml tests` passes
4. `pytest tests/code_coverage_tests/test_unit_passed_gate.py` passes. The first push of this branch failed `lint passed` on it because the smoke gate accepted a skipped job, and `59664597b8a` takes the two skipped jobs out of the gate instead

## Type

🚄 Infrastructure
✅ Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- `integration` is red on `main` and on this pull request
  - Four tests failed once each here and not on recent `main`, none in a moved file
- `main` deleted the Python s3_v2 logger in #51539
  - The ten s3_v2 tests this PR had moved are gone with it
- The moved tests no longer run on every pull request
- 37 files with process or socket tests stay in `tests/unit`
  - 7 would break the integration lint rules for signals, ports and elapsed time
  - 8 depend on fixtures in unit conftest files
  - 22 take 6.5 s in total
- Six tests are removed, so nothing covers these behaviours until they are rewritten
  - `test_hook_falls_back_to_the_sdk_when_the_runtime_has_no_router`
  - `test_concurrent_user_config_requests_each_count_once_against_the_tpm_limit`
  - `test_start_metrics_server_process_returns_only_once_child_serves`
  - `test_start_metrics_server_process_fails_when_port_is_taken`
  - `test_start_metrics_server_process_rejects_metrics_from_another_service_on_the_port`
  - `test_reported_list_cost_is_billed_instead_of_rows`

### Low

- `windows-sdk` and `proxy-build-from-pip` only run on `main` and manual runs
  - `smoke passed` no longer waits on them
- 16-core runners cost more per minute than the default
- Unchanged module state is no longer replaced with a fresh copy per test

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(vertex_ai): backport #40376 versioned Claude max_tokens to lts/1.108.x
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description On the 1.108 LTS line, a Vertex AI Claude chat on a versioned id like `claude-haiku-4-5@20251001` with no `max_tokens` goes out with `max_tokens` 4096, so long replies stop mid-sentence. This brings #40376's fix to the line, so those requests get the model's mapped output cap instead
Original ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex `claude-*@` chats with no `max_tokens` get 4096 on this line - Long replies stop at 4096 tokens with `finish_reason: length` - Main fixes it in #40376, which the line lacks How it solves it: - Ports #40376's lookup: own row, unversioned row, provider row, then the default - Adapted to the line, which lacks two things main's diff touches - Ids with no cost-map row keep the line's 4096 default ## User Flow Before: a LibreChat user on a versioned Vertex Claude Haiku 4.5 gets a long story cut off 1. The proxy admin adds `vertex_ai/claude-haiku-4-5@20251001` to the config with no `max_tokens` 2. A LibreChat user adds a custom endpoint with `baseURL: https://litellm-domain/v1` and picks that model 3. They ask for a 6000-word story, and LibreChat sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with no `max_tokens` 4. The reply stops mid-sentence after about 3000 words After: the same chat gets the whole story 1. The proxy admin adds `vertex_ai/claude-haiku-4-5@20251001` to the config with no `max_tokens` 2. A LibreChat user adds a custom endpoint with `baseURL: https://litellm-domain/v1` and picks that model 3. They ask for a 6000-word story, and LibreChat sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with no `max_tokens` 4. The reply runs to the end of the story ## Relevant issues Backport of #40376 (issue #40363) to lts/1.108.x. The one LTS commit applies #40376's net diff, so each of its commits maps to it. 53d146bb9f and 8fdc9062c1 cancel out, and 054e585218 is empty, so the pair block lists them as main-only | #40376 commit | LTS commit | | --- | --- | | `73b0c54bcc` | `b8b71a79cb` | | `6c3884c6c9` | `b8b71a79cb` | | `c88718915f` | `b8b71a79cb` | | `757f7991bf` | `b8b71a79cb` | | `6046f5bc9c` | `b8b71a79cb` | | `3570922b36` | `b8b71a79cb` | ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live Vertex AI calls, no mocks. Two proxies with 2 workers each and no database, one booted from the line tip b6fbe1f882 and one from this branch at b8b71a79cb, same config, `DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_CHAT_MAX_TOKENS` unset on both. The reporter's client, LibreChat v0.8.8, talks to both through one custom endpoint per proxy and sends no `max_tokens`, set up as in #40376's proof | Case | Before (b6fbe1f882) | After (b8b71a79cb) | | --- | --- | --- | | LibreChat long reply, Haiku 4.5 versioned | cut mid-sentence, 3077 words | whole story, 6472 words | | curl long reply, Haiku 4.5 versioned | `length` at 4096 tokens | `stop` at 6368 tokens | | Sonnet 4.6 `@default`, short reply | 200, `stop` | 200, `stop` | | Sonnet 4.5 versioned, short reply | 200, `stop` | 200, `stop` | | Azure AI Opus 5.5 fast, long reply, live on Foundry | `length` at 4096 tokens | `stop` at 14729 tokens, THE END |
Proxy config, the same file on both proxies ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vertex-claude-haiku-4-5-versioned litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/claude-haiku-4-5@20251001 vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT vertex_location: us-east5 - model_name: vertex-claude-opus-4-5-versioned litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/claude-opus-4-5@20251101 vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT vertex_location: us-east5 - model_name: vertex-claude-sonnet-4-6 litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6 vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT vertex_location: us-east5 - model_name: vertex-claude-sonnet-4-6-default litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6@default vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT vertex_location: us-east5 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY ``` Each proxy runs `python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config qa-config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port --num_workers 2` from its tree. title: fix(openai): backport #49176 to lts/1.108.x
body:
On lts/1.108.x, async codestral chat requests with a `file` part answer 400, because a flag every OpenAI-compatible provider shares makes async chat transform its messages twice. Streamed chat requests with PDF URLs also download the PDF on the event loop, so parallel streams wait for each other

This backports #49176, which removes the shared flag, downloads PDF URLs with the async client and then runs the sync transform once on a thread. On this line only PDF URLs in user messages download up front, since the line already sends PDF URLs in tool messages upstream as they are

## TLDR

Backport of #49176 to `lts/1.108.x`, so the next LTS patch matches main

Problem this solves:

- Async codestral chat with a `file` part answers 400
- A streamed PDF URL request blocks its worker's event loop

How it solves it:

- Cherry-picks #49176's squash commit, original author kept
- Downloads only user-message PDF URLs up front, as this line's transform does

## User Flow

Before: a codestral request with an uploaded file fails, and parallel PDF streams queue up

1. Their 2-worker proxy serves `codestral` and `gpt-4.1`, and their PDF host takes 4 s per GET
2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` to `codestral` with a `file` part naming an uploaded Mistral file
3. It answers 400 `Content block has type='file' but is missing the required 'file' field`
4. They send 8 streamed requests to `gpt-4.1` at once, each with one PDF URL `file` part, and all 8 finish after about 21 s

After: the same steps work. The codestral request answers 200 with the file's code word, and all 8 streams finish after about 5 s

  - The tool-result case of the async download test is dropped, since this line has no tool-message PDF download for it to check
  - Main's Mistral hunk is not needed, since the line's Mistral config never set the flag
  - The o-series transform on this line stops rewriting the caller's system messages in place, as main does, and a new test in `tests/unit/llms/openai/test_o_series_transformation.py` covers it. The request body is unchanged, and only the sync logged `input` moves (Caveats)
- [x] Added on the line, a6d0113879 tests an async codestral `file` request after an OpenAI call in `tests/unit/llms/mistral/test_mistral_chat_transformation.py`. It fails on the line's tip with the 400 above
- [x] No version bump (LTS line): neither `enterprise/` nor `litellm-proxy-extras/` changed
- [x] Importer scan: no name the pick dropped is still imported on the line
- [x] Picked tests: 3511 passed in `tests/unit/llms/openai`, the chat tests of every provider reusing the OpenAI config, and the prompt template and image handling tests, with no new failure against the line's tip
- [x] CVE sweep: no lock-only dependency bump clears a shipped finding that main already clears, so the lock is unchanged

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core message transformation and streaming request assembly for all OpenAI-GPT–based providers, including async PDF URL fetching and sync/async parity; regressions could affect file parts, PDF inlining, and provider-specific content flattening.
> 
> **Overview**
> This backport fixes async OpenAI-compatible chat where **messages were transformed twice** (breaking `file` parts on providers like Codestral) and **streamed requests downloaded PDF URLs on the event loop**, serializing parallel streams.
> 
> **Async request shaping** now detects `file_id` URL parts, optionally **prefetches PDFs with the async HTTP client** (user-role messages only on this branch), stores results in a **context variable**, and runs the existing **`transform_request` once on a worker thread**—skipping prefetch for configs that **flatten content lists** (DeepSeek, Heroku, Docker Model Runner, SambaNova, JSON dynamic providers). Shared **`image_handling`** helpers download URLs **one-at-a-time until the first failure** so bad links don’t trigger extra GETs.
> 
> The **`_is_base_class` split** in async transform is removed. **O-series** maps `system` → `user` via **`_with_provider_roles`** without mutating the caller’s message list. **Streaming** chat builds the body with **`async_transform_request`**. title: test(anthropic): expect adaptive thinking temperature dropping under drop_params
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

A scheduled integration test expected Claude Code requests on Claude Opus 4.6 with adaptive thinking to keep a temperature of 0, but #51834 deliberately started dropping a temperature other than 1 whenever thinking is on and drop params is set, which Claude Code requests get automatically. This PR updates that one test case to expect the temperature to be dropped while the thinking and effort settings pass through unchanged, and renames the test to say so

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c4790c508dec4aeb9cf157436141ff33
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/c4790c508dec4aeb9cf157436141ff33?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Scheduled integration run failed the `opus-4.6-adaptive-keeps-temperature` case
- The test still expected the behavior from before #51834

How it solves it:

- The case now expects `temperature` dropped, thinking and effort unchanged
- Test and case names describe the new behavior

Intentional product change: none in this PR, it follows the change #51834 made on purpose

## CI evidence

- Failed 1 time (`times_failed` 1) in scheduled run 223 at `8fc67892951c`: [Job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43630579098/job/132556053007)
- Passed in the run before, at `9d827093c5cd`, which predates #51834
- Failure: the forwarded body was `{"thinking": {"type": "adaptive", "display": "omitted"}, "output_config": {"effort": "high"}}` where the test expected `"temperature": 0` too

## Mechanism

- Claude Code's user agent turns on `drop_params` for the request
- #51834 changed `drop_incompatible_temperature_for_thinking` in `litellm/rust/crates/llms/src/anthropic/messages/thinking.rs` so adaptive capable models drop a non-1 temperature when thinking is on under `drop_params`
- #51834 states this as intended ("under `drop_params` it now drops a conflicting `temperature`") and adds its own test for adaptive models, with Anthropic's 400 "temperature may only be set to 1 when thinking is enabled or in adaptive mode" as the reason
- The integration test still asserted the old keep-temperature behavior

## Fix

- Only `tests/integration/messages_endpoint/providers/anthropic/reasoning/test_anthropic_reasoning_request_translation_wire.py` changes
- The case still sends `temperature: 0` and checks the exact forwarded body, so thinking and effort must still pass through unchanged
- The other five cases are untouched

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at b2a902373b97d96236e5487e3d2b8a5c6275c8fb: test-only expectation update, proven on the CI-equivalent integration rig (local Postgres, Redis, scripted upstream, `num_retries` 0, `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1`, group `providers`)

1. Unchanged origin/main, `uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "<file>::test_temperature_is_dropped_only_when_a_non_adaptive_model_thinks[opus-4.6-adaptive-keeps-temperature]"`: 1 failed, `Right contains 1 more item: {'temperature': 0}`, same as CI
2. Fixed test, `run.py providers "<file>::test_temperature_is_dropped_when_thinking_requires_it_under_drop_params"` five times: 6 passed each time
3. Whole file, `run.py providers <file>`: 53 passed
4. Temporarily restored the old early return for adaptive models in `thinking.rs` and rebuilt the native extension: the healed case failed with `Left contains 1 more item: {'temperature': 0}`. Reverted, rebuilt, case passed
5. `make lint`: passed

## Type

✅ Test

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix: backport #51451, #51449 and #51715 to rc/1.110.0
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description [insert handwritten description here]
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Three provider bugs reported against v1.110.0-rc.2 are fixed on main only - Hugging Face chat crashes when the endpoint comes from `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` - Unmapped Fireworks models sized like `1p5b` are billed at double the rate - OpenCode Go Messages-protocol models return HTTP 500 when streamed through chat completions How it solves it: - Cherry-picks #51451, #51449 and #51715 onto `rc/1.110.0` unchanged - No version bump, no dependency change, no workflow change Intentional product change: reported spend for unmapped Fireworks models sized like `0p6b` or `1p5b` drops to the up-to-4B rate, which is half of what the proxy reported before. ## User Flow ### Hugging Face endpoint from the environment Before: a team that points Hugging Face chat at its own endpoint through an environment variable gets an error on every request 1. The proxy admin sets `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` to their endpoint's chat completions URL and lists `huggingface/tgi` with no `api_base` 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for that model 3. The proxy answers HTTP 500 with `not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)` and the endpoint never receives the request After: the same request reaches the endpoint and returns its reply 1. The proxy admin sets `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` to their endpoint's chat completions URL and lists `huggingface/tgi` with no `api_base` 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for that model 3. The proxy answers HTTP 200 with the endpoint's reply ### Fireworks models with a fractional size Before: a team calling a Fireworks model that is missing from the price map, with a size like `1p5b` in its name, sees double the expected spend 1. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `fireworks_ai/accounts//models/-1p5b` through a `fireworks_ai/*` route 2. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` shows the 4.1B to 16B rate, twice what the same call costs for a `1b` model After: the same call is priced at the up-to-4B rate 1. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `fireworks_ai/accounts//models/-1p5b` through a `fireworks_ai/*` route 2. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` matches the cost of the same call for a `1b` model ### OpenCode Go streaming Before: a developer streaming chat completions from an OpenCode Go model served over the Messages protocol gets an error after the upstream has already been called 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` for `opencode_go/minimax-m3` 2. The proxy calls the upstream, retries, and answers HTTP 500 with `'NoneType' object is not an iterator` After: the same request streams the reply 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` for `opencode_go/minimax-m3` 2. The proxy answers HTTP 200 with SSE chunks carrying the text, a `stop` finish reason and `data: [DONE]` ## Relevant issues Backports the fixes for #51448, #51450 and #51666 to the `rc/1.110.0` line. All three are already merged on main ## Backport The three commits are `git cherry-pick -x` picks in their original merge order, and each one is patch-identical to its source commit on main. - #51451 fix(fireworks_ai): read fractional sizes like 1p5b in the size bucket fallback - #51449 fix(huggingface): honor HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE and env endpoints for chat - #51715 fix(opencode): stream Go Messages-protocol models through chat completions Every file the picks touch was byte-identical on `rc/1.110.0` to the version each fix was written against, and none of those files has a later follow-up on main. The mapped unit tests (`tests/unit/llms/fireworks_ai`, `huggingface`, `opencode`, `anthropic/chat` and `custom_httpx`) pass on both trees with no failures, 2244 on the rc tip and 2279 with the picks. ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two proxies ran side by side on one machine, Before on the rc tip `5ca1e3f797b` and After on this branch at `750ba60ba51`. Each ran two workers with its own Redis and its own Postgres database, and the two config files differ only in the Redis port. No provider keys were available for a Hugging Face endpoint, Fireworks or OpenCode Go, so each upstream is a local stub that answers in that provider's wire format and logs every request it receives. The proxy code under test is real. An adversarial review of the three commits, with findings executed on both trees, confirmed one behaviour change outside the stated scope of #51449. It is listed under Caveats. The reviewers found nothing against #51451 or #51715. Proxy start command, run once per tree. The env var names are `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` and `LITELLM_MODE`. Output went to a log file instead of `tee`. ```bash env -i PATH="$TREE/.venv/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" HOME="$HOME" LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 \ LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="$(cat master_key)" \ DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:54332/$DB" \ HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE="http://127.0.0.1:4611/hf/v1/chat/completions" \ "$TREE/.venv/bin/python" litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port "$PORT" \ --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver ```
config.yaml (After; Before uses Redis port 63793) ```yaml model_list: - model_name: fireworks_ai/* litellm_params: model: fireworks_ai/* api_key: stub-key api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4611/fw/inference/v1 - model_name: hf-tgi-env litellm_params: model: huggingface/tgi api_key: stub-key - model_name: hf-tgi-explicit litellm_params: model: huggingface/tgi api_key: stub-key api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4611/hf - model_name: oc-minimax-m3 litellm_params: model: opencode_go/minimax-m3 api_key: stub-key api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4611/oc/v1 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 63794 litellm_settings: drop_params: true router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 63794 ```
Stub upstream, started with python3 provider_stub.py 4611 ```python import json import sys import time import uuid from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer def chat_completion(model: str) -> dict: return { "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}", "object": "chat.completion", "created": int(time.time()), "model": model, "choices": [ {"index": 0, "message": "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": "stub "}}, ), ( "content_block_delta", {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": "streamed reply"}}, ), ("content_block_stop", {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0}), ( "message_delta", { "type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn", "stop_sequence": None}, "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}, }, ), ("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"}), ] class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def send_json(self, payload: dict) -> None: body = json.dumps(payload).encode() self.send_response(200) self.send_header("content-type", "application/json") self.send_header("content-length", str(len(body))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(body) def do_POST(self) -> None: length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0")) body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}") model = str(body.get("model", "?")) stream = bool(body.get("stream")) print(f"UPSTREAM_HIT path={self.path} model={model} stream={stream}", flush=True) if self.path.endswith("/v1/messages") and stream: self.send_response(200) self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream") self.end_headers() for name, data in messages_events(model): self.wfile.write(f"event: {name}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode()) self.wfile.flush() return if self.path.endswith("/v1/messages"): self.send_json(messages_reply(model)) return if self.path.endswith("/chat/completions"): self.send_json(chat_completion(model)) return self.send_response(404) self.end_headers() def log_message(self, *args: object) -> None: return ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever() ```
Client, run as python replay.py http://127.0.0.1:$PORT master_key stub.log ```python import json import subprocess import sys import httpx base_url, master_key_path, stub_log = sys.argv[1:4] master_key = open(master_key_path).read().strip() headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {master_key}"} QUESTION = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}] def upstream_hits() -> int: return int(subprocess.run(["grep", "-c", "UPSTREAM_HIT", stub_log], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout or 0) def plain(name: str, model: str) -> None: before = upstream_hits() response = httpx.post( f"{base_url}/v1/chat/completions", headers=headers, timeout=120, json={"model": model, "messages": QUESTION} ) cost = response.headers.get("x-litellm-response-cost") print( f"{name}: HTTP {response.status_code} | reached upstream: {upstream_hits() - title: test(e2e): run the batch lifecycle with a key that only reaches its own deployment
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `test_batch_lifecycle[azure-provider_fallback]` fails in most scheduled e2e runs
- Batch create returns an Azure 404 right after a successful upload
- It started when the suite went from 8 to 12 xdist workers

How it solves it:

- The lifecycle key now sits in a team limited to its batch deployment
- Provider-only calls resolve that deployment in any registration order
- Test and suite docs only, no product change

## User Flow

Before: the engineer watching the scheduled e2e run sees one Azure batch case go red in about a second

1. The run starts 12 workers, and the batches file and the realtime file both begin in the first second
2. Each registers its own Azure deployment with POST /model/new, `azure-batch-<run>` on `api_version` 2025-04-01-preview and `azure-realtime` on 2025-08-28
3. The test uploads a file with POST /azure/v1/files using an all-models key and gets a 200
4. It sends POST /azure/v1/batches with that file id and gets 404 `Resource not found` whenever `azure-realtime` registered first

After: the same run passes whichever deployment registered first

1. The run starts 12 workers, and the batches file and the realtime file both begin in the first second
2. Each registers its own Azure deployment with POST /model/new, `azure-batch-<run>` on `api_version` 2025-04-01-preview and `azure-realtime` on 2025-08-28
3. The test creates a team that may only use `azure-batch-<run>`, makes a key in it, and uploads with POST /azure/v1/files, 200
4. POST /azure/v1/batches returns 200 with a `batch_...` id, and retrieve, cancel and the file delete on cleanup succeed

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [ ] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### What the scheduled runs show

The failing case is in the `e2e-attempt-0` job log of the scheduled `litellm-e2e` builds. Build 864 ran 8 workers and passed. The batches file starts at log row 52 and the realtime file at row 476, 127 seconds later, so `azure-batch` is always the first Azure deployment on the proxy. Builds 865, 872 and 874 ran 12 workers and failed. There the two files start 2 to 4 ms apart (rows 61 and 56, 53 and 59, 57 and 64), and the case fails in under a second with `upstream call failed (status 404)` and the body `Error code: 404 - {'error': {'code': '404', 'message': 'Resource not found'}}`. Build 873 also ran 12 workers with the same 4 ms gap (rows 54 and 64) and passed in 6 seconds, which is what a race between the two registrations looks like.

### Local reproduction

No Azure credentials exist on the dev machine, so Azure is a stand-in HTTP server that records each request and answers 404 `Resource not found` for `api-version=2025-08-28`. That rule mirrors what the scheduled runs returned and is the one assumption in this proof. OpenAI calls are live. The proxy ran as one worker with no Redis and without `--reload` or `--detailed_debug`, because the behavior under proof is which credentials one request resolves and it shares no state across workers.

Shared setup, with `$S` a scratch directory and `$WT` this checkout:

```bash
initdb -D $S/pgdata -U postgres --auth=trust
LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 postgres -D $S/pgdata -p 55471 -k '' -h 127.0.0.1 -c max_connections=200
python azure_standin.py 18471 $S/azure_requests.log
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config $S/proof/proxy_config.yaml --port 14471 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Proxy env var names: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB`, `LITELLM_MODE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AZURE_API_BASE` (the stand-in's URL), `AZURE_API_KEY`, `VERTEXAI_PROJECT`, `VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS`, `GCS_BUCKET_NAME`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_BATCH_S3_BUCKET`, `AWS_BATCH_ROLE_ARN`. The Vertex and AWS ones hold placeholders so the suite's session fixture can register its deployments.

```yaml
model_list: []

files_settings:
  - custom_llm_provider: openai
    api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - custom_llm_provider: azure
    api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE
    api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY
    api_version: 2025-04-01-preview

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  store_model_in_db: true
```

<details>
<summary>azure_standin.py</summary>

```python
import json
import sys
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

REJECTED_API_VERSIONS = {"2025-08-28"}
FILE_EXPIRY_SECONDS = 14 * 24 * 60 * 60
LOG_PATH = sys.argv[2]
BATCHES: dict[str, dict] = {}


def log(line: str) -> None:
    with open(LOG_PATH, "a") as handle:
        handle.write(line + "\n")


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        return

    def _reply(self, status: int, body: dict) -> None:
        raw = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(raw)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(raw)

    def _handle(self) -> None:
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0"))
        body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
        url = urlsplit(self.path)
        api_version = parse_qs(url.query).get("api-version", [""])[0]
        if api_version in REJECTED_API_VERSIONS:
            log(f"{self.command} {url.path} api-version={api_version} -> 404")
            self._reply(404, {"error": {"code": "404", "message": "Resource not found"}})
            return
        log(f"{self.command} {url.path} api-version={api_version} -> 200")
        now = int(time.time())
        parts = url.path.strip("/").split("/")
        if self.command == "POST" and url.path == "/openai/files":
            self._reply(
                200,
                {
                    "id": f"file-{now}{len(body)}",
                    "object": "file",
                    "bytes": len(body),
                    "created_at": now,
                    "expires_at": now + FILE_EXPIRY_SECONDS,
                    "filename": "batch_input.jsonl",
                    "purpose": "batch",
                    "status": "processed",
                },
            )
        elif self.command == "DELETE" and parts[:2] == ["openai", "files"]:
            self._reply(200, {"id": parts[2], "object": "file", "deleted": True})
        elif self.command == "POST" and url.path == "/openai/batches":
            request = json.loads(body)
            batch = {
                "id": f"batch_{now}{len(BATCHES)}",
                "object": "batch",
                "endpoint": request["endpoint"],
                "input_file_id": request["input_file_id"],
                "completion_window": request["completion_window"],
                "status": "validating",
                "created_at": now,
            }
            BATCHES[batch["id"]] = batch
            self._reply(200, batch)
        elif self.command == "POST" and parts[:2] == ["openai", "batches"] and parts[-1] == "cancel":
            BATCHES[parts[2]]["status"] = "cancelling"
            self._reply(200, BATCHES[parts[2]])
        elif self.command == "GET" and url.path == "/openai/batches":
            self._reply(200, {"object": "list", "data": list(BATCHES.values()), "has_more": False})
        elif self.command == "GET" and parts[:2] == ["openai", "batches"]:
            self._reply(200, BATCHES[parts[2]])
        else:
            self._reply(404, {"error": {"code": "404", "message": "Resource not found"}})

    do_GET = do_POST = do_DELETE = _handle


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()
```

</details>

Then register the realtime suite's Azure deployment first, with the same params that suite uses, so it sits ahead of `azure-batch-<run>` on the proxy for both runs:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:14471/model/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model_name":"azure-realtime","litellm_params":{"model":"azure/gpt-realtime-1.5","api_key":"os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY","api_version":"2025-08-28","realtime_protocol":"GA"}}'
```

Both runs use this command from `tests/e2e`, with `LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:14471` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` set:

```bash
python -m pytest "batches/test_batches_e2e.py::test_batch_lifecycle" -k "azure or openai" -v -p no:cacheprovider --reruns 0
```

### Before (580203cce6b)

1. The pytest command above ends `1 failed, 7 passed, 5 deselected`. The one failure is `test_batch_lifecycle[azure-provider_fallback]`, with the same message as the scheduled runs:

```
E       Failed: upstream call failed (status 404); body={"error":{"message":"Error code: 404 - {'error': {'code': '404', 'message': 'Resource not found'}}","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"404"}}
```

2. The stand-in's log for the `azure-model_param` and `azure-provider_fallback` cases shows the proxy sending the realtime deployment's `api_version` on the batch create and on both file deletes. The `azure-model_param` case still passes because its cleanup reads the delete's 404 as already deleted. GET lines are left out:

```
POST /openai/files api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches/batch_17946882822/cancel api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
DELETE /openai/files/file-1794688282693 api-version=2025-08-28 -> 404
POST /openai/files api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches api-version=2025-08-28 -> 404
DELETE /openai/files/file-1794688284693 api-version=2025-08-28 -> 404
```

### After (5ad377214a9)

1. The same pytest command ends `8 passed, 5 deselected`, with `azure-realtime` still registered first.

2. The stand-in's log for the same two cases shows every call on the batch deployment's `api_version`, including the deletes. GET lines are left out:

```
POST /openai/files api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches/batch_17946890038/cancel api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
DELETE /openai/files/file-1794689003693 api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/files api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
POST /openai/batches/batch_17946890079/cancel api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
DELETE /openai/files/file-1794689007693 api-version=2025-04-01-preview -> 200
```

## Type

✅ Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Azure's 404 for `api-version=2025-08-28` on the batch path is inferred
  - no Azure credentials locally, so the stand-in encodes it
  - if wrong, the cause is something else and this change would not fix it
- Vertex and Bedrock lifecycle cases were not run locally
  - they need real credentials, the scheduled run is their first proof
- Product gap, not fixed here
  - a batch or file call with a provider and no model uses the first deployment of that provider the key can reach
  - with an all-models key the result depends on registration order

### Low

- Other tests in this file still use an all-models key on `/openai/v1/files`
  - safe only while every OpenAI deployment on the proxy shares one key and base URL

## QA runbook

- tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py::test_batch_lifecycle (13 cases, one per provider and routing scenario) - a key in a team that may only use the batch deployment uploads a file, creates a batch, retrieves it, cancels it and finds it in the list, and the provider-only cases stay on that deployment whatever else is registered
  - [ ] Prerequisites: `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, a `files_settings` entry for azure on `api_version` 2025-04-01-preview, and Azure credentials on the proxy
  - [ ] Register a second Azure deployment first: POST /model/new with `{"model_name":"azure-realtime","litellm_params":{"model":"azure/gpt-realtime-1.5","api_key":"os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY","api_version":"2025-08-28"}}`
  - [ ] Register the batch deployment: POST /model/new with `{"model_name":"azure-batch","litellm_params":{"model":"azure/gpt-5.4-mini-batch","api_base":"os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE","api_key":"os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY","api_version":"2025-04-01-preview"},"model_info":{"mode":"batch"}}`
  - [ ] Create a team limited to it: POST /team/new with `{"team_alias":"batch-qa","models":["azure-batch"]}`, then POST /key/generate with `{"team_id":"<team_id>","user_id":"e2e-test-user"}`
  - [ ] Upload with that key: POST /azure/v1/files, multipart `purpose=batch`, `expires_after[anchor]=created_at`, `expires_after[seconds]=1209600` and a one-line JSONL whose `body.model` is `gpt-5.4-mini-batch`. Expect 200 and a raw `file-...` id
  - [ ] Create: POST /azure/v1/batches with `{"input_file_id":"<file id>","endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","completion_window":"24h"}`. Expect 200, a raw `batch_...` id and status `validating`, `in_progress` or `finalizing`
  - [ ] GET /azure/v1/batches/<batch id> returns the same id and input file, POST /azure/v1/batches/<batch id>/cancel returns `cancelling` or `cancelled`, DELETE /azure/v1/files/<file id> returns `deleted: true`
  - [ ] Repeat the upload and create with an all-models key to see the old failure: the create returns 404 `Resource not found`
  - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
