> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Data-only additions to the model pricing JSON with no changes to runtime logic, auth, or billing code paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Registers **Inkling 2 Small** in LiteLLM’s model cost map for **Cloudflare Workers AI** (`cloudflare/@cf/thinkingmachines/inkling-2-small`) and **Nebius** (`nebius/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small`), with the same entries mirrored in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`.
> 
> Each row adds per-token input/output (and cached-input where applicable), a 1M-token context window, chat mode, and capability flags (function calling, reasoning, vision) sourced from each host’s public model listings. **Before** this change, `litellm.completion_cost` could fail with “model isn’t mapped yet” for those model IDs; **after**, spend can be calculated from usage for the Cloudflare path (and Nebius once the row is used).

title: fix(responses): backport cache_control breakpoints on the chat-to-Responses bridge to lts/1.108.x
body:
This brings #51783 to lts/1.108.x. Chat completions requests with a function tool on GPT models that LiteLLM serves through the Responses API (gpt-6 on Foundry, gpt-6.1 on OpenAI) lost the client's Anthropic-style cache marks on the way out, so explicit prompt caching never wrote or read anything on this line either. Bedrock Mantle caches the growing prefix on its own, so it stays as it was

Now those marks reach the provider as OpenAI cache breakpoints whenever the deployment reads them, as this line's plain chat path already does. Three more commits carry #51783's follow-ups, so leading system messages keep client order when a mark moves one to `input`, and Mantle and unmarked chats send what they sent before

-->

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Function tools plus reasoning send chat requests over the Responses API
- On this line that bridge dropped `cache_control`, so explicit mode on Foundry and OpenAI cached nothing

How it solves it:

- Four cherry-picks from #51783, adapted to this line's breakpoint check
- The bridge renames `cache_control` to `prompt_cache_breakpoint` before converting
- Only for deployments that read breakpoints, except Bedrock Mantle, which caches on its own
- Leading system messages keep client order when a mark moves a string one to input

| Main commit | LTS commit |
|---|---|
| 1c3dd2d8bc | d3e02ad9b3 |
| 0db932802e | 27c828d3bc |
| 74cb624fa7 | 916da413ac |
| 6419de8a90 | a67c5f0c9d |

## User Flow

Before: a developer on explicit prompt caching sends function tools with a cache-marked system prompt and gets no cache at all

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Foundry gpt-6-astra deployment with a 7.4k-token system part marked `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}`, `prompt_cache_options: {"mode": "explicit"}`, and one function tool
2. The answer comes back with `cache_write_tokens: 0`
3. They send the same request again and get `cached_tokens: 0`, the same on OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol

After: the same request writes the cache on the first call and reads it on the second

1. They send the same request
2. The answer comes back with `cache_write_tokens: 7449`
3. The same request again comes back with `cached_tokens: 7449`, the same on OpenAI and a message-level mark

## Relevant issues

Backport of #51783

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Last updated: a67c5f0c9d. QA ran on 916da413ac. Changes since QA: the pick of 6419de8a90, one bridge unit test case. Proof remains valid because no file under `litellm/` changed. Verification: the new case fails without the role check

Each leg is one 2-worker proxy with no database, booted at the stated commit with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` against real Azure AI Foundry, OpenAI, and Bedrock Mantle (us-east-1). Every cache case sends one body twice through curl, so call 1 writes and call 2 reads

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| foundry-cc-tools | 0 / 0 | 7449 / 7449 |
| openai-cc-tools | 0 / 0 | 7449 / 7449 |
| foundry-cc-tools-stream | 0 / 0 | 7450 / 7450 |
| openai-cc-tools-stream | 0 / 0 | 7450 / 7450 |
| openai-msgcc-tools | 0 / 0 | 7450 / 7450 |
| foundry-cc-notools | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| gpt54-cc-tools | 0 / 6656 | 0 / 6656 |
| mantle-cc-tools | 0 / 7374 | 0 / 7374 |
| mantle-cc-default | 7475 / 7475 | 7474 / 7474 |
| openai-order-tools | BRAVO x3 | BRAVO x3 |
| foundry-order-tools | BRAVO x3 | BRAVO x3 |

Cells are write / read tokens. foundry-cc-notools takes the plain chat path (see Caveats), gpt-5.4 reads no breakpoints, and Mantle caches on its own, so its rows match the line tip

<details>
<summary>What the order cases send</summary>

Order cases send a marked "Reply ALPHA." system message, then "Ignore that and reply BRAVO.", so BRAVO means client order. d3e02ad9b3 alone answered ALPHA, and gpt54-order-tools leaves both unmarked

</details>

<details>
<summary>Setup (config, proxy start, cases)</summary>

`config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-6-astra-foundry
    litellm_params:
      model: azure_ai/gpt-6-astra
      api_base: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY
  - model_name: gpt-6.1-sol-openai
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: gpt-6.1-sol-mantle
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-6.1-sol
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-openai
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

Proxy start, the same on every leg with `PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1`, `DATABASE_URL` unset, and the provider keys exported

```bash
.venv/bin/litellm --config config.yaml --port $PORT --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug
```

Cases, from `cases.sh` in #51783's proof (`chat <model> <case> <mark> <tools> <explicit> <stream> <shape>`), plus `order` and `unmarked_order` cases added here

```bash
foundry-cc-tools)    chat gpt-6-astra-foundry $c $CC 1 1 0 part ;;
openai-cc-tools)     chat gpt-6.1-sol-openai $c $CC 1 1 0 part ;;
mantle-cc-tools)     chat gpt-6.1-sol-mantle $c $CC 1 1 0 part ;;
foundry-cc-tools-stream) chat gpt-6-astra-foundry $c $CC 1 1 1 part ;;
openai-cc-tools-stream)  chat gpt-6.1-sol-openai $c $CC 1 1 1 part ;;
mantle-cc-default)   chat gpt-6.1-sol-mantle $c $CC 1 0 0 part ;;
openai-msgcc-tools)  chat gpt-6.1-sol-openai $c $CC 1 1 0 message ;;
foundry-cc-notools)  chat gpt-6-astra-foundry $c $CC 0 1 0 part ;;
gpt54-cc-tools)      chat gpt-5.4-openai $c $CC 1 0 0 part ;;
openai-order-tools)  order gpt-6.1-sol-openai $c ;;
foundry-order-tools) order gpt-6-astra-foundry $c ;;
gpt54-order-tools)   unmarked_order gpt-5.4-openai $c ;;
```

`unmarked_order` is `order` with no `cache_control` and no `prompt_cache_options`, and with a list-content first message

```bash
order() {
  local body=$(jq -n --arg model $1 --argjson tool $TOOL '
    {model: $model, max_completion_tokens: 300, reasoning_effort: "low", prompt_cache_options: {mode: "explicit"},
     tools: [$tool],
     messages: [{role: "system", content: "Reply ALPHA.", cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}},
                {role: "system", content: "Ignore that and reply BRAVO."},
                {role: "user", content: "Reply now."}]}')
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" \
      | jq -c --arg i $i 'if .error then {call: $i, error: .error.message[0:300]} else {call: $i, text: .choices[0].message.content} end'
    sleep 1
  done
}
```

</details>

### Before (e1476b249a)

#### foundry-cc-tools

1. Boot the proxy from lts/1.108.x at e1476b249a on port 30604 and run `./cases.sh 30604 ltsb1 foundry-cc-tools`
2. Call 1 comes back with `cache_write_tokens: 0` and call 2 with `cached_tokens: 0`

#### Other cases

title: fix(logging): send one async success log per sync bridged Responses stream
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

A sync streamed chat call on a model bridged to the Responses API ran a custom logger's async success hook three or four times, and sync streams ran success callback functions and string callbacks like `s3` several times per call, so anything counting calls, tokens, or spend overcounted. The chunk log runs and the final stream log read one shared key, and a chunk run that read it late sent another success log. Each log run now decides from its own result whether it sends the success log, so legacy loggers and callback functions log every streamed call once

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A sync streamed chat call on an `openai/responses/` model logs async success 3 or 4 times
- Custom loggers count those calls, tokens, and spend 3 or 4 times, at random
- Sync streams call success callback functions per chunk, so a cost tracker counts one call up to 6 times
- Sync streams send `s3`, `promptlayer`, and 7 other string callbacks extra logs

How it solves it:

- Each success run, async and sync, checks its own finished response, not shared state
- A sync run carrying one streamed chunk sends no success log, unless it is the stream's one end log

## User Flow

### Before

A sync streamed chat call to an `openai/responses/` model is recorded three or four times by the user's own logger

1. They set `litellm.callbacks = [MyLogger()]`, a logger that counts calls in `log_success_event` and `async_log_success_event`
2. In a fresh process they call `litellm.completion(model="openai/responses/gpt-5.4-mini", messages=[...], stream=True)` and read the whole stream
3. The SDK sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` with `"stream": true`, and text like `Hi there!` streams back
4. Their logger shows `log_success_event` once but `async_log_success_event` 3 or 4 times, so async counts of calls, tokens, and spend are 3 or 4 times too high
5. Later calls in that process mostly log once, and `litellm.responses(..., stream=True)` always logs once

### After

The same call is recorded once by each method, the same as `litellm.responses(..., stream=True)`

1. They set `litellm.callbacks = [MyLogger()]`, a logger that counts calls in `log_success_event` and `async_log_success_event`
2. In a fresh process they call `litellm.completion(model="openai/responses/gpt-5.4-mini", messages=[...], stream=True)` and read the whole stream
3. The SDK sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` with `"stream": true`, and text like `Hi there!` streams back
4. Their logger shows `log_success_event` once and `async_log_success_event` once, with the finished response
5. Every later call in that process also logs once, and `litellm.responses(..., stream=True)` still logs once

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg ran its own tree's `.venv` with real OpenAI and Anthropic calls. The proxy booted with `--num_workers 2` on a fresh Postgres database. The `s3` case wrote to a local SeaweedFS 3.99 bucket with versioning on, so each extra write adds an object version

| Case | Before (c6aa2a3b2a) | After (26200f626c) |
|---|---|---|
| SDK bridged sync stream, async logs | 3 | 1 |
| Same, first call of 5 fresh processes | 3, 3, 3, 3, 3 | 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 |
| SDK `responses(stream=True)`, async logs | 1 | 1 |
| SDK plain sync chat stream, async logs | 0 | 0 |
| Proxy, 5 streamed routes, spend rows | 5 | 5 |
| Proxy, key spend equals row sum | yes | yes |
| SDK bridged sync stream, `s3` log writes | 3, 3 | 1, 1 |
| SDK plain sync stream, `s3` log writes | 6, 6 | 1, 1 |
| SDK plain sync stream, cost callback calls | 6 | 1 |
| SDK bridged sync stream, cost callback calls | 3 | 1 |
| Both cost cases, message logging off | 6, 3 | 1, 1 |
| SDK `file_content(stream=True)`, callback calls | 1 | 1 |
| Response builder fails, without and with usage chunk | 8, 7 | 1, 1 |

<details>
<summary>The SDK scripts, the proxy config, and the proxy case script</summary>

`s3_log_writes.py`

```python
import sys
import time
import uuid

import boto3
import litellm

ENDPOINT, MODEL = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
CREDENTIALS = {"aws_access_key_id": "qaaccess", "aws_secret_access_key": "qasecretkey123", "region_name": "us-east-1"}
BUCKET = f"litellm-logs-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"

s3 = boto3.client("s3", endpoint_url=ENDPOINT, **CREDENTIALS)
s3.create_bucket(Bucket=BUCKET)
s3.put_bucket_versioning(Bucket=BUCKET, VersioningConfiguration={"Status": "Enabled"})

litellm.s3_callback_params = {
    "s3_bucket_name": BUCKET,
    "s3_endpoint_url": ENDPOINT,
    "s3_aws_access_key_id": CREDENTIALS["aws_access_key_id"],
    "s3_aws_secret_access_key": CREDENTIALS["aws_secret_access_key"],
    "s3_region_name": CREDENTIALS["region_name"],
}
litellm.success_callback = ["s3"]

stream = litellm.completion(model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in two words"}], stream=True)
text = "".join(chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "" for chunk in stream)
time.sleep(8)

versions = s3.list_object_versions(Bucket=BUCKET).get("Versions", [])
print(f"completion({MODEL}, stream=True): text={text!r}")
print(f"  log objects: {len({v['Key'] for v in versions})}, writes to them (object versions): {len(versions)}")
```

`track_cost.py`, the docs' cost tracking callback

```python
import sys
import time

import litellm
from litellm import completion

MODEL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "gpt-5.4-mini"
costs = []


def track_cost_callback(kwargs, completion_response, start_time, end_time):
    cost = kwargs.get("response_cost")
    costs.append(cost)
    print(f"Request cost: ${cost}")


litellm.success_callback = [track_cost_callback]
litellm.turn_off_message_logging = "--turn-off-message-logging" in sys.argv

for model in (f"openai/{MODEL}", f"openai/responses/{MODEL}"):
    response = completion(model=model, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in two words"}], stream=True)
    for chunk in response:
        continue
    time.sleep(3)
    print(f"completion({model}, stream=True): track_cost_callback calls={len(costs)} summed=${sum(c or 0 for c in costs):.8f}")
    costs.clear()
```

`track_file_download.py`

```python
    print(f"file_content(stream=True): bytes={len(downloaded)} matches upload={downloaded == line}")
    print(f"file_content(stream=True): track_download calls={calls}")
finally:
```

```python

import litellm

MODEL = sys.argv[1]
stream_options = {"include_usage": True} if "--include-usage" in sys.argv else None
costs = []


def track_cost_callback(kwargs, completion_response, start_time, end_time):
    costs.append(kwargs.get("response_cost"))


def stream_chunk_builder_that_fails(*args, **kwargs):

litellm.success_callback = [track_cost_callback]

response = completion(
    model=f"openai/{MODEL}",
```

`count_callbacks.py`

```python
import sys
import threading
import time

import litellm
from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger

MODEL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "gpt-5.4-mini"
events = []
lock = threading.Lock()


class CountingLogger(CustomLogger):
    def log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        with lock:
            events.append(("sync_success", type(response_obj).__name__))

    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        with lock:
            events.append(("async_success", type(response_obj).__name__))


litellm.callbacks = [CountingLogger()]


def drain(label, stream):
    text = "".join(
        (getattr(c.choices[0].delta, "content", None) or "") if hasattr(c, "choices") else ""
        for c in stream
    )
    time.sleep(3)
    print(f"{label}: text={text!r}")
    print(f"{label}: events={events}")
    print(f"{label}: async_log_success_event calls={sum(1 for e in events if e[0] == 'async_success')}")
    events.clear()


drain(
    "completion(openai/responses/" + MODEL + ", stream=True)",
    litellm.completion(
        model=f"openai/responses/{MODEL}",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in two words"}],
        stream=True,
    ),
)

resp_stream = litellm.responses(model=f"openai/{MODEL}", input="Say hi in two words", stream=True)
for _ in resp_stream:
    pass
time.sleep(3)
print(f"responses(openai/{MODEL}, stream=True): events={events}")
print(f"responses(openai/{MODEL}, stream=True): async_log_success_event calls={sum(1 for e in events if e[0] == 'async_success')}")
```

```python
import sys
import time

import litellm
from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger

events = []


class L(CustomLogger):
    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
```

## Type

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Medium

- v2 loggers with an awaited `attempt_ended` still receive it twice
  - It happens on sync bridged chat and `responses(stream=True)` streams at both commits
  - It is filed separately, so "logs once" here covers legacy loggers only

### Low

- No test fails if the v2 hook gate change is reverted
  - A non-awaited v2 `attempt_ended` counted 1 at both commits, so no run shows the change
  - See Decisions item 3

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

1. Target one async and one sync log per call, matching sync `litellm.responses(stream=True)`. Zero async logs, like a plain sync chat stream, was the other option, but a logger that only implements the async method would then lose the call
2. Each run of the async success handler decides from its own finished response whether it sends the final stream log. A lock around the shared call details would serialize every chunk log, and a shared "already logged" flag is the same read-then-write race
3. The v2 hook gate uses the same per-run flag. Sync stream chunk logs run on executor threads, so a chunk run can read the shared call details after the final run fills them. That window has no await to hold open in a test, so the race tests cover the legacy deliveries
4. Both handlers read pass-through through `_is_pass_through_call()`, spelled `self.call_type in (CallTypes.pass_through.value,)` because `==` on the str enum adds two unknown-type errors to the type gate
5. The openmeter, dynamodb, and sync string-callback tests patch the module-level logger globals, since that is the only way those integrations get their logger
6. The sync string callbacks keep their `complete_streaming_response` key check next to the per-run flag, since a pass-through stream has no assembled response and they read the key its handler set
7. Sync callback functions and the `promptlayer`, `wandb`, `athina`, and `traceloop` callbacks skip a run whose result is one streamed chunk, checked before message redaction turns the chunk into a dict, so they get only the finished response, as async callback functions already did. Calling them per chunk with a per-run copy of kwargs was the other option, but the docs treat a success callback as one call per request. A gate on the assembled response alone, like the async handler's, would also drop the one log of a sync `file_content(stream=True)`, whose result is a dict. The stream wrapper marks its end log and sends it once, so a stream whose response builder fails still calls them once with best-effort usage
8. Built from scratch. #36434 and #46608 touch other bridge logging symptoms, so neither covers this

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

> **Overview**

title: feat(vertex_ai): backport caller identity labels on Vertex requests to lts/1.108.x
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

This brings the opt-in Vertex identity labels from #50732 to the 1.108 LTS, so proxy admins on the LTS can split Vertex spend per key, team, org, and project in Cloud Billing. It also brings #48753, which those commits build on, so Claude on Vertex sends its labels in the labels header like it does on main

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- LTS Vertex calls carry no key, team, org, or project labels
- Any caller can send `user_api_key_*` labels itself

How it solves it:

- Cherry-picks all 12 commits of #50732 with `-x`, authors kept
- Also picks #48753, the Claude labels header change they build on
- Same opt-in `vertex_request_label_fields` setting as main
- No version bump, since neither `enterprise/` nor `litellm-proxy-extras/` changed

Intentional product change: with the setting off, Claude on Vertex chat now sends caller labels in the `X-Vertex-AI-Labels` header instead of the body, which is #48753's behavior on main

## User Flow

Before: Cloud Billing can't split LTS Vertex spend per team, because no team labels reach Vertex

1. The proxy admin creates org `ml-org`, team `ai-platform`, project `support-bot`, and key `chargeback-key`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with that key to a Vertex Gemini model
3. The call returns 200, but Vertex receives no `labels`
4. Any developer can send a forged `user_api_key_team_alias` label, and Vertex takes it

After: the same calls reach Vertex labeled with the caller's key, team, org, and project

1. The proxy admin lists the alias fields and `spend_logs_metadata` under `litellm_settings.vertex_request_label_fields` and restarts
2. The developer sends the same request with the same key
3. Vertex receives the key, team, org, and project aliases and `cost-center: cc-1234` as labels
4. A forged `user_api_key_team_alias` is dropped wherever it is sent

## Relevant issues

LTS twin of #50732, which merges to main first. Also carries #48753, already merged on main

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10161

## Picks

Every pick keeps its original author and an `-x` line naming its source

Seven picks applied clean. #48753 went in first, from its squash `db5b9401437` on main, because the first #50732 commit edits code it added. The other six were resolved the way main has them, keeping only what each pick adds

1. `c84e2e731c` puts the Claude Messages label change in `vertex_ai_partner_models/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/transformation.py`, where that config lives on the line, and leaves out `map_vertex_image_size`, which the line doesn't have
2. `dd2eb2764a` adds the `Mapping` and `Final` test imports the line was missing
3. `24ba38af06` is the one real adaptation. The line's `/vertex_ai` pass-through has no upstream headers filter, so the pick adds an `upstream_request_filter` parameter to `pass_through_request` and `create_pass_through_route` and runs the labels filter on the outgoing headers and JSON body before the request goes out. The non-streaming handler now takes that filtered body. The line keeps logging the outgoing headers as it did before. The pass-through tests bring main's `vertex_proxy` fixture and path constants without main's beta-route tests. It also adds a missing `Mapping` import in the base Interactions config and `TypeAdapter` in the image edit test
4. `8072769539` keeps only the PR's new Veo test, since main's neighbouring tests don't exist on the line
5. `b510e84be8` keeps only the PR's new rerank test, without main's `clear_vertex_rerank_cache` fixture, since the line builds a new rerank config per call and has no cache to clear. Main's credential-cache test stays out

6. `c84e2e731c` also builds the Claude Messages headers it returns as a new dict, instead of deleting from and writing into the `headers` argument, so the line's LIT011 count doesn't grow
7. `24ba38af06`'s Codestral FIM test seeds a chat template for `codestral-2` in `litellm.known_tokenizer_config` instead of passing `roles`. On this line the Codestral handler needs every custom prompt key once any is set, and main's change that relaxed that isn't here
8. `1a4c6ca36a` keeps the source's `TypeAlias` import, which `VertexLabelPlacement` needs

The step-4 importer scan found one name the picks drop, the rerank module's import of `vertex_request_labels_from_litellm_params`, and no other file on the line imports it from there

```python
import base64
import json
import os

from mitmproxy import http

POINTER = os.environ["MITM_OUT_POINTER"]


def response(flow: http.HTTPFlow) -> None:
    if not flow.request.pretty_host.endswith("aiplatform.googleapis.com"):
        return
    try:
        body = json.loads(flow.request.get_text() or "{}")
    except ValueError:
        body = {}
    header = flow.request.headers.get("X-Vertex-AI-Labels")
    record = {
        "vertex_method": flow.request.path.split("?")[0].rsplit("/", 1)[-1],
        "status": flow.response.status_code,
        "labels": body.get("labels", "<absent>"),
    }
    if header is not None:
        record["X-Vertex-AI-Labels header, decoded"] = json.loads(base64.b64decode(header))
    with open(open(POINTER).read().strip(), "a") as handle:
        handle.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
```

title: fix(router)!: keep a deployment's own litellm_params over router default_litellm_params
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

If you set a router-wide default region, it used to override the region a deployment set for itself, so a deployment pinned to the EU quietly got served from global. Now a deployment's own settings win, and router defaults only fill in what a deployment leaves unset

[/stupid: What the PR adds](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mateo-berri/b4c8090c890bffe6afe0f9ea2335a3db/raw/BerriAI-litellm-51785-stupid-purpose.html)

[/stupid: What breaks](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mateo-berri/88fb02adb131d4b780910fe880da5eba/raw/BerriAI-litellm-51785-stupid.html)

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `router_settings.default_litellm_params` overwrote a deployment's own `litellm_params`
- A Vertex deployment pinned to `vertex_location: eu` was served from `global`

How it solves it:

- The request wins, then the deployment, then the router default
- Router defaults only fill keys a deployment leaves unset
- `metadata` defaults still merge key by key like before
- Token counting and drop-params checks use the same order as inference
- A key the deployment's `litellm_credential_name` credential sets counts as the deployment's own
- Router-wide `headers` and `extra_headers` merge under a deployment's own by header name, and a header the deployment sets under either key wins
- `router.chat.completions.create` no longer sends router defaults as request params, so it follows the same order
- Sync `text_completion` sends the deployment's model like async does, where it used to send the group name

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin pins one Vertex deployment to the EU, but its traffic still goes to the global endpoint

1. The admin sets `default_litellm_params: {vertex_location: global}` under `router_settings` and gives the `vtx-eu` deployment `vertex_location: eu`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vtx-eu"` (same for /v1/responses and /v1/messages)
3. The response is 200, but the `x-litellm-model-api-base` header shows `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/.../locations/global/...`

After: the same request goes to the EU endpoint the deployment asked for

1. The admin sets `default_litellm_params: {vertex_location: global}` under `router_settings` and gives the `vtx-eu` deployment `vertex_location: eu`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vtx-eu"` (same for /v1/responses and /v1/messages)
3. The response is 200 and the `x-litellm-model-api-base` header shows `https://aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com/.../locations/eu/...`
4. A deployment with no `vertex_location` of its own still gets `global` from the router default

recorder.py, started with `python recorder.py 23417 recorder.jsonl` before the proxy

```python
import json
import re
import sys
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import httpx

PORT = int(sys.argv[1])
LOG = sys.argv[2]
HOP = {"host", "content-length", "connection", "accept-encoding", "transfer-encoding"}


def upstream_host(path: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r"/locations/([^/]+)/", path)
    location = match.group(1) if match else "global"
    if location == "global":
        return "aiplatform.googleapis.com"
    if location in ("eu", "us"):
        return f"aiplatform.{location}.rep.googleapis.com"
    return f"{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com"


class Recorder(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0")))
        host = upstream_host(self.path)
        reply = httpx.post(
            f"https://{host}{self.path}",
            content=body,
            headers={k: v for k, v in self.headers.items() if k.lower() not in HOP},
            timeout=60,
        )
        location = re.search(r"/locations/([^/]+)/", self.path)
        record = {
            "time": time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"),
            "location": location.group(1) if location else None,
            "endpoint": self.path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1],
            "upstream": host,
            "status": reply.status_code,
            "x_qa_headers": {k: v for k, v in self.headers.items() if k.lower().startswith("x-qa-")},
        }
        with open(LOG, "a") as out:
            out.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
        self.send_response(reply.status_code)
        self.send_header("content-type", reply.headers.get("content-type", "application/json"))
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(reply.content)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(reply.content)

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:
        pass


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Recorder).serve_forever()
```

2. `vtx-counted` gets a count

3. The recorder shows `vtx-headed` chat sent the router `X-Qa-Team` next to its own `X-Qa-Region`, and its own `x-qa-owner` and `X-Qa-Cross` beat the router's values for both names. The `vtx-counted` count went to the router default `global`, and Vertex answered it with a 200

<details>
<summary>SDK router.chat.completions.create and router.text_completion, Before and After</summary>

</details>

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Severe

- A key set under `router_settings.default_litellm_params` no longer overrides the same key on a deployment or its credential
  - Before, `default_litellm_params: {vertex_location: global}` sent a deployment with `vertex_location: eu` to global. Now it goes to eu, with that region's price and quota. The same goes for `api_base`, `api_key`, and a header the deployment sets under `headers` or `extra_headers`
  - A deployment with its own `drop_params: false` under a router default `drop_params: true` now answers 400 on a param the router default used to drop
  - Before upgrading, remove the key from each deployment or credential, DB-saved ones included, that should follow the router default. The release note has to say this

### Medium

- The litellm-docs count_tokens, decisions, and two config pages describe the old order until a docs update merges right after this PR

### Low

- `extra_body` and list params like `additional_drop_params` are replaced whole, not merged
- A deployment value equal to the field's built-in default counts as unset
- Sync `text_completion` now sends the deployment's model, not the group name
- `router.chat.completions.create` now uses a deployment's own `timeout` over `Router(timeout=...)`, as `router.completion` already did
- Entra caller-credential cooldown now reads the deployment's secret before the router default
- The Vertex token counter now counts a deployment with no region of its own in the router default region, where main used `us-east5`. `vertex_count_tokens_location` on the deployment brings the old region back
- An unknown `litellm_credential_name` now logs its warning up to 3 times per request, not once. Left as is, since it only shows on a broken config

<details>
<summary>Decisions and their alternatives</summary>

A deployment value counts as unset when it is None or equals the `LiteLLM_Params` field default. Deployments reach the router as dicts with some defaults already filled in, so a bare "key is present" check would let a filled-in default block the router default. The cost is that a deployment cannot force a field back to its built-in default against a router default. The alternative, pydantic's `model_fields_set`, is lost once params are dumped to dicts on the way in

`headers` and `extra_headers` merge by header name, compared without case, and a header the deployment sets under either key drops the router's header of that name from both, since `extra_headers` override `headers` when the request is built. Main let the router's dict win whole, which dropped the deployment's own headers. Letting the deployment's dict win whole was the alternative, but the litellm-docs Helicone recipe puts `Helicone-Auth` under router-wide `headers`, and that header would vanish from every deployment that sets a header of its own. A request's own `headers` still replace both whole, as on main

`extra_body` follows the top-level order, so the deployment's dict wins whole. Its keys are provider body fields that a deployment sets on purpose, so a merge would push router-wide fields into a body the deployment shaped itself. The public report this came from asked for `extra_body` to merge. This PR does not, but the deployment's `extra_body` now wins whole, so that report's deployment keeps its own provider routing

List-valued params such as `additional_drop_params` follow the same order, so a deployment's own list replaces the router default's list. Taking the union was the alternative, but main never merged them either (the router list replaced the deployment's), and a union would stop a deployment from sending a param the router drops for everyone else

Sync `text_completion` used to send the request's group name as the model, so a group named apart from its model failed with `LLM Provider NOT provided` before any precedence applied. It now sends the deployment's model, as async `atext_completion` already did. Leaving it out would keep this fix out of reach for those groups

`max_retries` stays router-owned, so the router's pin of 0 still beats a deployment's own value. The router runs its own retry loop through `num_retries`, and letting a deployment's `max_retries` through would multiply the two loops into extra upstream calls per request, which the routing docs already describe. The alternative, treating it like every other key, sent 4 upstream calls where main sends 3 for an embedding deployment with `max_retries: 3`

A key the deployment's `litellm_credential_name` credential sets counts as the deployment's own, so the order is the request, the deployment, its credential, then the router default. Main put the router default above the credential, so a region or `drop_params` kept in a reusable credential lost to the router default on inference, while the proxy token counters, which merge the credential first, used it. Keeping the credential below the router default was the alternative, but the counters and inference would disagree again

`router.chat.completions.create` used to pass the router defaults, `Router(timeout=...)` included, as request params, so they beat a deployment's own `timeout`. It now goes through `router.completion`, which already used the deployment's `timeout` first (a 1 s deployment timeout against `Router(timeout=6)` gave up after 1.6 s, where `router.chat.completions.create` on main waited 6.0 s). Keeping the old order for this one path was the alternative, but the two chat entry points would disagree

One helper now builds the params a deployment is sent, and the router, the proxy token counters, the drop-params checks, and the Entra cooldown check all call it, so counting and policy checks see what inference sends. The provider token counters now get those full params too, where main gave them only the drop settings, so a Vertex count uses the region inference uses. The old per-call merges each put router defaults last, which is the bug

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
- [x] 2f3298ecb6 passes /live-pr-risk

</details>

title: fix(scim): clear every group or member on a PATCH remove with no value or filter
body:
An IdP that sends a SCIM PATCH `remove` on `groups` (for a user) or on `members` (for a group) with no value and no filter got a 200 back, but nothing changed. The user kept every team and its team keys kept working, so a deprovision the IdP thought was done never happened

RFC 7644 section 3.5.2.2 says a remove on a multi-valued attribute with no filter removes all of its values. Now that request takes the user out of every team, or empties the group, which matches how `remove roles` and `remove entitlements` already work

<details><summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A bare `remove` on user `groups` answers 200 and removes nothing
- A bare `remove` on group `members` answers 200 and removes nothing
- The user's team keys keep serving after the IdP thinks they left

How it solves it:

- A remove on the bare path with no value now clears it
- Filtered removes and removes with a value list work as before

## User Flow

Before: the IdP sends a bare remove and gets 200, but the user stays in every team

1. The admin's IdP creates a user in two groups with POST https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Users
2. The IdP sends PATCH https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Users/{id} with `[{"op":"remove","path":"groups"}]` and gets 200
3. GET https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Users/{id} still lists both groups, and GET /team/info still lists the user on each team
4. The user's team key still gets 200 on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions
5. The same thing happens with PATCH https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Groups/{id} and `[{"op":"remove","path":"members"}]`, the group keeps every member

After: the same bare remove takes the user out of every team

1. The admin's IdP creates a user in two groups with POST https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Users
2. The IdP sends PATCH https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Users/{id} with `[{"op":"remove","path":"groups"}]` and gets 200 with `"groups": []`
3. GET https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Users/{id} lists no groups, and GET /team/info no longer lists the user on either team
4. The user's team key now gets 401 on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions
5. PATCH https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Groups/{id} with `[{"op":"remove","path":"members"}]` now empties the group

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

QA at 454f235ad4 is running now. The before and after runs go here once both finish

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix
✅ Test

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

<details><summary>Decisions</summary>

1. Only the bare path counts (`groups` or `members`, any case) with no `value`. A filter the proxy cannot parse, like `groups[display eq "x"]`, still removes nothing rather than everything, since reading an unknown filter as "remove all" would wipe teams by accident. That filter case is tracked separately
2. `"value": []` still removes nothing, since an explicit empty list names no group. Treating it as remove-all was the alternative
3. On /Groups the clear is a change against the roster read at request time, like every other add or remove, not an absolute "the roster is now empty". So a member another request adds at the same moment survives, which is the less destructive of the two
4. /Groups `members` is fixed along with /Users `groups`, since the same RFC rule covers both and IdPs drive most membership through /Groups
5. Ops that follow a groups `replace` in the same user PATCH are still ignored. That is an older, separate bug with its own fix pending, and this PR does not change it

</details>

</details>

title: fix(responses): send cache_control as a prompt_cache_breakpoint on the chat-to-Responses bridge
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Chat completions requests with function tools on GPT models that LiteLLM serves through the Responses API (gpt-6 on Foundry, gpt-6.1 on OpenAI) lost the client's Anthropic-style cache marks on the way out, so explicit prompt caching never wrote or read anything and every call paid full input price. Bedrock Mantle drops them too but caches the growing prefix on its own, so it stays as it was

Now those marks reach the provider as OpenAI cache breakpoints whenever the deployment reads them, the same way the plain chat path already handles them, so the same request caches with or without tools

<!-- litellm-pair:v1
{"changes":[{"id":"responses-bridge-cache-control-breakpoints","scope":"translation","owner":"@mateo-berri","driver":"https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51783","driver_state":"active","main":[51783],"lts":[51796],"source_commits":["1c3dd2d8bca3c1f355d6d9e9f212ca00e2415139","0db932802ea3ebbc4e409ace7583c93d454dc91b","74cb624fa79aa3a84577f68d7d65d164435055dc","6419de8a90e3d24fd21d4b6162fec9643656a548"],"coverage_verified":true,"evidence":["https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51783","https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/1c3dd2d8bca3c1f355d6d9e9f212ca00e2415139","https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/0db932802ea3ebbc4e409ace7583c93d454dc91b","https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/74cb624fa79aa3a84577f68d7d65d164435055dc","https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/6419de8a90e3d24fd21d4b6162fec9643656a548"]}]}
-->

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Function tools plus reasoning send chat requests over the Responses API
- That bridge dropped `cache_control`, so explicit cache mode on Foundry and OpenAI cached nothing
- Same request without tools cached fine, so tools silently cost cache

How it solves it:

- The bridge renames `cache_control` to `prompt_cache_breakpoint` before converting
- Only for deployments that read breakpoints, except Bedrock Mantle, which caches on its own
- Unmarked content parts are left exactly as the client sent them
- Leading system messages keep client order when a mark moves a string one to input

## User Flow

Before: a developer on explicit prompt caching sends function tools with a cache-marked system prompt and gets no cache at all

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to a Foundry gpt-6-astra deployment with a 7.4k-token system part marked `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}`, `prompt_cache_options: {"mode": "explicit"}`, and one function tool
2. The answer comes back with `cache_write_tokens: 0`
3. They send the same request again and get `cached_tokens: 0`, the same on OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, while the request without the tool caches all of it

After: the same request writes the cache on the first call and reads it on the second

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the marked system part, explicit mode, and the function tool
2. The answer comes back with `cache_write_tokens: 7450`
3. The same request again comes back with `cached_tokens: 7450`, the same on OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, streaming, and a mark on a tool result

- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Last updated: 6419de8a90. QA ran on 74cb624fa7. Changes since QA: one bridge unit test case. Proof remains valid because no file under `litellm/` changed. Verification: 1773 unit tests pass, the new case fails without the role check, and a title alias test fails after a `proxy_server` reload, as on the merge base

Each leg is one proxy process with 2 uvicorn workers and no database, booted at the stated commit with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` against real Foundry, OpenAI, and Bedrock Mantle (us-east-1). The change holds no per-process state. Each case sends one body twice with a fresh run tag, so the table shows call 1's cache write and call 2's cache read

<details>
<summary>Setup (config, proxy start, case script)</summary>

`config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-6-astra-foundry
    litellm_params:
      model: azure_ai/gpt-6-astra
      api_base: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY
  - model_name: gpt-6-astra-foundry-explicit
    litellm_params:
      model: azure_ai/gpt-6-astra
      api_base: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY
      prompt_cache_options: {mode: explicit}
  - model_name: gpt-6.1-sol-openai
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: gpt-6.1-sol-openai-explicit
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
      prompt_cache_options: {mode: explicit}
  - model_name: gpt-6.1-sol-mantle
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-6.1-sol
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-openai
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

Proxy start, the same on both legs with `PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1`, `DATABASE_URL` unset, and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_BASE`, `AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` exported

```bash
.venv/bin/litellm --config config.yaml --port $PORT --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug
```

Write is call 1's `cache_write_tokens` (`cache_creation_input_tokens` on `/v1/messages`) and read is call 2's `cached_tokens` (`cache_read_input_tokens`)

`cases.sh`, run as `./cases.sh <port> <run tag> <case>...`

```bash
#!/bin/zsh
# usage: cases.sh <port> <run tag> <case>...
PORT=$1 TAG=$2; shift 2
URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
KEY="$(cat ${0:A:h}/master_key)"
RULES=$(for i in {0..299}; do printf 'Rule %d: when asked about route %d, answer with the fare class code %s. ' $i $i $(printf %s $i | sha256sum | cut -c1-10); done)
ASK='What is the fare class code for route 7? Reply with the code only, no tool call.'
TOOL='{"type":"function","function":{"name":"lookup_route","description":"Look up a route by number","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"route":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["route"]}}}'
CC='{"cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}'
BP='{"prompt_cache_breakpoint":{"mode":"explicit"}}'

chat_body() {  # model case mark tools(0|1) explicit(0|1) stream(0|1) shape(part|message|tool_output)
  jq -n --arg model $1 --arg sys "Run $TAG $2. $RULES" --arg ask "$ASK" --arg key "qa-$TAG-$2" \
    --argjson mark $3 --argjson tools $4 --argjson explicit $5 --argjson stream $6 --arg shape $7 --argjson tool $TOOL '
    {model: $model, max_completion_tokens: 300, reasoning_effort: "low", prompt_cache_key: $key,
     messages: (
       if $shape == "part" then
         [{role: "system", content: [{type: "text", text: $sys} + $mark]}, {role: "user", content: $ask}]
       elif $shape == "message" then
         [{role: "system", content: $sys} + $mark, {role: "user", content: $ask}]
       else
         [{role: "user", content: "Look up route 7, then tell me its fare class code only."},
          {role: "assistant", content: null, tool_calls: [{id: "call_route_7", type: "function",
            function: {name: "lookup_route", arguments: "{\"route\": 7}"}}]},
          {role: "tool", tool_call_id: "call_route_7", content: $sys} + $mark]
       end)}
    + (if $tools == 1 then {tools: [$tool]} else {} end)
    + (if $explicit == 1 then {prompt_cache_options: {mode: "explicit"}} else {} end)
    + (if $stream == 1 then {stream: true, stream_options: {include_usage: true}} else {} end)'
}

chat() {  # same args as chat_body; sends it twice to /v1/chat/completions
  local body=$(chat_body "$@")
  for i in 1 2; do
    if [ $6 = 1 ]; then
      curl -sN $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" \
        | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | grep -v '^\[DONE\]' \
        | jq -sc --arg i $i '{call: $i, text: (map(.choices[0].delta.content // "") | join("")), usage: (map(select(.usage)) | last | .usage | {prompt_tokens, details: .prompt_tokens_details})}'
    else
      curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" \
        | jq -c --arg i $i 'if .error then {call: $i, error: .error.message[0:300]} else {call: $i, text: .choices[0].message.content, usage: {prompt_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens, details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details}} end'
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
}

messages() {  # model case: Anthropic /v1/messages with a cache_control system block and one tool, sent twice
  local body=$(jq -n --arg model $1 --arg sys "Run $TAG $2. $RULES" --arg ask "$ASK" '
    {model: $model, max_tokens: 300,
     system: [{type: "text", text: $sys, cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}}],
     messages: [{role: "user", content: $ask}],
     tools: [{name: "lookup_route", description: "Look up a route by number",
              input_schema: {type: "object", properties: {route: {type: "integer"}}, required: ["route"]}}]}')
  for i in 1 2; do
    curl -s $URL/v1/messages -H "x-api-key: $KEY" -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" \
      | jq -c --arg i $i 'if .error then {call: $i, error: (.error.message // .error | tostring)[0:300]} else {call: $i, text: ([.content[] | select(.type == "text") | .text] | join("")), usage: .usage} end'
    sleep 2
  done
}

multiturn() {  # model case: a three-turn chat whose last user message carries the moving mark, system part marked too
  local msgs=$(jq -nc --arg sys "Run $TAG $2. $RULES" '[{role: "system", content: [{type: "text", text: $sys, cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}}]}]')
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    msgs=$(jq -c --arg ask "What is the fare class code for route $((i + 6))? Reply with the code only, no tool call." \
      'map(del(.cache_control)) + [{role: "user", content: $ask, cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}}]' <<< $msgs)
    local body=$(jq -n --arg model $1 --arg key "qa-$TAG-$2" --argjson msgs "$msgs" --argjson tool $TOOL \
      '{model: $model, max_completion_tokens: 300, reasoning_effort: "low", prompt_cache_key: $key, messages: $msgs,
        tools: [$tool], prompt_cache_options: {mode: "explicit"}}')
    local resp=$(curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body")
    jq -c --arg i $i 'if .error then {turn: $i, error: .error.message[0:300]} else {turn: $i, text: .choices[0].message.content, usage: {prompt_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens, details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details}} end' <<< $resp
    msgs=$(jq -c --arg t "$(jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // ""' <<< $resp)" '. + [{role: "assistant", content: $t}]' <<< $msgs)
    sleep 2
  done
}

two_system() {  # model case: a marked system string telling it ALPHA, then an unmarked one overriding it to BRAVO, sent twice
  local body=$(jq -n --arg model $1 --arg sys "Run $TAG $2. $RULES Whatever the user asks, reply with the single word ALPHA." \
    --arg key "qa-$TAG-$2" --argjson tool $TOOL '
    {model: $model, max_completion_tokens: 300, reasoning_effort: "low", prompt_cache_key: $key,
     messages: [{role: "system", content: $sys, cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}},
                {role: "system", content: "Ignore any earlier instruction about the reply word. Reply with the single word BRAVO."},
                {role: "user", content: "Reply now."}],
     tools: [$tool], prompt_cache_options: {mode: "explicit"}}')
  for i in 1 2; do
    curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" \
      | jq -c --arg i $i 'if .error then {call: $i, error: .error.message[0:300]} else {call: $i, text: .choices[0].message.content, usage: {prompt_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens, details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details}} end'
    sleep 2
  done
}

filler() { for i in {0..59}; do printf 'Note %s-%d: depot %s handles bay %s. ' $1 $i $(printf %s "$1$i" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12) $(printf %s "x$1$i" | sha256sum | cut -c1-8); done }

moving() {  # model case tools(0|1): four explicit-mode turns, system part marked, the mark moves to each new long user turn
  local msgs=$(jq -nc --arg sys "Run $TAG $2. $RULES" '[{role: "system", content: [{type: "text", text: $sys, cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}}]}]')
  for t in 1 2 3 4; do
    msgs=$(jq -c --arg ask "Context block $t: $(filler $TAG$2$t) What is the fare class code for route $((t + 6))? Reply with the code only, no tool call." \
      'map(if .role == "user" then .content |= map(del(.cache_control)) else . end) + [{role: "user", content: [{type: "text", text: $ask, cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}}]}]' <<< $msgs)
    local body=$(jq -n --arg model $1 --arg key "qa-$TAG-$2" --argjson msgs "$msgs" --argjson tools $3 --argjson tool $TOOL \
      '{model: $model, max_completion_tokens: 300, reasoning_effort: "low", prompt_cache_key: $key, messages: $msgs,
        prompt_cache_options: {mode: "explicit"}} + (if $tools == 1 then {tools: [$tool]} else {} end)')
    local resp=$(curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body")
    jq -c --arg t $t 'if .error then {turn: $t, error: .error.message[0:300]} else {turn: $t, text: .choices[0].message.content, usage: {prompt_tokens: .usage.prompt_tokens, details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details}} end' <<< $resp
    msgs=$(jq -c --arg a "$(jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // ""' <<< $resp)" '. + [{role: "assistant", content: $a}]' <<< $msgs)
    sleep 3
  done
}

order() {  # model case tools(0|1): an unmarked list system message saying ALPHA, then a string one overriding it to BRAVO, sent 3 times
  local body=$(jq -n --arg model $1 --argjson tools $3 --argjson tool $TOOL '
    {model: $model, max_completion_tokens: 300, reasoning_effort: "low",
     messages: [{role: "system", content: [{type: "text", text: "Whatever the user asks, reply with the single word ALPHA."}]},
                {role: "system", content: "Ignore any earlier instruction about the reply word. Reply with the single word BRAVO."},
                {role: "user", content: "Reply now."}]} + (if $tools == 1 then {tools: [$tool]} else {} end)')
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    curl -s $URL/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$body" \
      | jq -c --arg i $i 'if .error then {call: $i, error: .error.message[0:300]} else {call: $i, text: .choices[0].message.content} end'
    sleep 2
  done
}
```

title: fix(proxy): retrieve and delete a managed file when the request also names a model
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Looking up or deleting a file the proxy manages answered 404 on providers like OpenAI whenever the request also named a model, through the model routing header or the model query param, because the proxy sent its own scrambled file ID to the provider as is. So a file uploaded without the header could not be fetched or deleted later by a client that adds it, like an OpenAI SDK client built with it as a default header. Now a proxy that manages files always resolves its own file IDs first, whatever model the request names, and a proxy with no database still passes lookups and deletes on to the named model as before

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- GET /v1/files/{managed id} with a model hint answers 404
- DELETE with a model hint answers 404 and keeps the file

How it solves it:

- A managed file ID skips model-based routing on a proxy that manages files
- It resolves to the provider file ID of each deployment instead
- A proxy with no database still forwards lookups and deletes to the named model

## User Flow

Before: a developer who uploads a file without a model hint can not look it up or delete it once a later call names the model

1. They upload with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=user_data` and `target_model_names=gpt-files-global`, and get back a long scrambled file ID
2. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{that id} with no model hint answers 200 with the file object
3. The same GET with the `x-litellm-model: gpt-files-global` header (or `?model=gpt-files-global`) answers 404 `No such File object: <the scrambled id>`
4. DELETE https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{that id} with the same header also answers 404, and step 2 still finds the file afterwards

After: the same calls with the header find the file and delete it

1. They upload with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=user_data` and `target_model_names=gpt-files-global`, and get back a long scrambled file ID
2. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{that id} with no model hint answers 200 with the file object
3. The same GET with the `x-litellm-model: gpt-files-global` header (or `?model=gpt-files-global`) answers 200 with the same file object
4. DELETE https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{that id} with the same header answers 200 `"deleted": true`, and step 2 now answers 404

<details>
<summary>sdk_flow.py, the case 1 client</summary>

```python
import os, sys
import openai
from openai import OpenAI

base, path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
key = os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]
uploader = OpenAI(base_url=base, api_key=key)
routed = OpenAI(base_url=base, api_key=key, default_headers={"x-litellm-model": "gpt-files-global"})
print("openai", openai.__version__)
with open(path, "rb") as fh:
    created = uploader.files.create(file=fh, purpose="user_data", extra_body={"target_model_names": "gpt-files-global"})
print("uploader.files.create ->", created.id[:40] + "...", created.filename)
print("uploader.files.retrieve ->", uploader.files.retrieve(created.id).filename)
for name, call in (
    ("routed.files.retrieve", lambda: routed.files.retrieve(created.id)),
    ("routed.files.delete", lambda: routed.files.delete(created.id)),
    ("uploader.files.retrieve after routed delete", lambda: uploader.files.retrieve(created.id)),
):
    try:
        result = call()
        print(f"{name} -> OK", type(result).__name__, getattr(result, "filename", None) or getattr(result, "deleted", None))
    except openai.APIStatusError as error:
        print(f"{name} -> {type(error).__name__} {error.status_code}: {str(error.message)[:160]}")
```

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Low

- File content through a proxy with no database still answers 500
  - Not caused here, follow-up filed

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

On a proxy that loads the managed files hook (one with a database), a managed file ID now ignores the model hint on retrieve, content, and delete, the same way the content route already treated it. Ignoring the hint uses none of the named model's credentials, so it opens up nothing the caller could not already reach without the hint

A proxy with no database loads no managed files hook, so it cannot resolve a managed ID itself. There the hint still forwards the ID to the named model as before, since that model may be another LiteLLM proxy that owns the file. Skipping the hint there too broke retrieve and delete through such a chained proxy with a 500

Bedrock reads the S3 location out of a managed ID, so before this change a lookup there with the hint answered with the S3 object's details instead of 404, and a delete with the hint removed only the S3 object. It kept the stored record, so the file still showed up afterwards, and it skipped the check that refuses to delete a file a batch still uses when batch cost tracking is on. Both calls now go through the managed files hook like a call without the hint, so a lookup answers with the stored record and a delete removes every copy and the record. Keeping that Bedrock path was turned down because it leaves a record that points at a deleted object and gives one ID two different answers

Three alternatives were turned down. Letting the hint pick one deployment's copy of the file would be wrong for DELETE, which has to remove every copy and the stored record, and it would add a second lookup path for retrieve. Answering 400 when the hint names a model the file does not live on would be a new restriction nobody asked for, and it would break clients that send the header on every call. Looking the ID up in this proxy's own table and falling back to the hint when it is missing would add a query for nothing, since a proxy with a database already answers 404 for a managed ID it does not own before any routing runs

A provider file ID (one the proxy does not manage) keeps routing by the hint exactly as before

</details>

title: fix(cohere)!: bill Embed V5 image tokens at their own rate on Foundry and direct Cohere
body:
Foundry's Cohere Embed V5 relay was billing images at the text rate. Foundry folds each image into `input_tokens` at embed v4's image to text ratio, and we priced that folded count at V5's text price, so V5-Pro image calls logged about 17% over Azure's bill and V5-Fast ones about 22% under

For V5, Foundry also sends `text_tokens` and `image_tokens`, so now when those are there we bill each at its own cost map price. embed-v-4-0 and the v3 models don't send `text_tokens` and keep billing the folded count, which already matches Azure

Direct Cohere V5 also billed images at the text rate, because its cost map entries had no image price. Both entries now carry Cohere's $0.40 per 1M image tokens

[/stupid: What the PR adds](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mateo-berri/a647c17c38dff1c1c960ee8fe3d8773a/raw/BerriAI-litellm-51779-stupid-purpose.html)

[/stupid: What breaks](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mateo-berri/99d3cf4f5e05318ff061064b785073e6/raw/BerriAI-litellm-51779-stupid.html)

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Cohere Embed V5 calls with images log the wrong spend
- On Foundry, V5-Pro logs about 17% high and V5-Fast about 22% low
- On direct Cohere, both log 70 to 80% low

How it solves it:

- Bill itemized `text_tokens` and `image_tokens` at their own rates
- Models without `text_tokens` (embed v4, v3) bill as before
- Add Cohere's image price to both direct V5 cost map entries

## User Flow

Before: a team embedding text plus images through Foundry's Cohere Embed V5 sees key spend that does not match their Azure bill

1. The admin adds `azure_ai/Cohere-Embed-V5-Pro` pointing at their Foundry resource
2. A developer POSTs a text and an image to https://litellm-domain/azure_ai/Cohere-Embed-V5-Pro/providers/cohere/v2/embed
3. `meta.billed_units` comes back as 1017 input, 6 text and 258 image tokens
4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows $0.00012204, all 1017 tokens at the text rate, 17% over Azure (V5-Fast is 22% under)

After: the same call logs what Azure's text and image meters charge

1. Steps 1 to 3 are the same as before
2. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows $0.00010392, the 6 text and 258 image tokens each at their own rate

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

- When Foundry sends `text_tokens`, the logged prompt token count is `text_tokens + image_tokens`, not Foundry's folded `input_tokens`
  - The folded count is in embed v4 image units, so it is not a real token count for V5
  - Keeping `input_tokens` as the prompt count would bill an image-only call's leftover (input minus image) at the text rate
  - The same count feeds spend log token totals and key and team TPM limits, so a V5 image call on a cost map priced deployment now counts about 4x fewer tokens there, the same way direct Cohere calls already count them
- The switch keys on whether `text_tokens` is present in the response, not on the model name
  - Alternative was a list of V5 model names, which goes stale with the next Foundry model
  - Foundry sends `text_tokens` only for models it itemizes, and embed-v-4-0 and both v3 models never send it (checked live)
- A future model that itemizes but has no `input_cost_per_image_token` in the cost map bills its images at the text rate
  - Alternative was falling back to the folded count for that case, but the parser never sees prices, and the fix for a missing price is the cost map entry
  - Both V5 models have an image price today
- Direct Cohere V5 gets `input_cost_per_image_token` of 4e-07 in the cost map, from [Cohere's Embed 5 post](https://cohere.com/blog/embed-5)
  - Its parser already itemizes `image_tokens`, so the missing price was the only gap
- A deployment that sets its own prices but no `input_cost_per_image_token` keeps Foundry's folded count, so it bills and counts tokens as before
  - Itemizing it would bill its image tokens at its text rate, since custom-priced deployments on every provider fall back to the text rate for a modality price they don't set. That billed V5-Pro images about 70% under Azure
  - Alternative was inheriting the cost map's image price for custom-priced deployments, which changes billing for custom-priced deployments of 121 cost map entries on 11 providers
  - Setting `input_cost_per_image_token` under the deployment's `model_info` switches it to the itemized count at that image rate
- This goes to main only, with no LTS twin
  - lts/1.108.x has no `CohereImageTokenBilling`, and its Foundry relay costs only rerank and FLUX calls, so the relay change never runs there
  - Its Cohere parser takes image tokens only from `billed_units.images`, which Cohere's v2 embed no longer sends, so image tokens stay empty and the V5 image price has nothing to price there. That gap comes from #48978 never reaching LTS (see Caveats)

</details>

### /live-pr-risk at f785b8e0bd

<details>
<summary>Breaking, backward incompatible, regression risk, dependency graph, and the cells</summary>

The verdict is no breaking change. f785b8e0bd does what it says for every custom-priced deployment shape I could build. A V5-Pro deployment priced in `model_info`, in config `litellm_params`, or in `litellm_params` through `/model/new`, with no image price, bills Foundry's folded 1017 tokens on head exactly as on main. Rerank, FLUX, OCR, image generation, the v3 and embed-v-4-0 relays and the V5 v1 404 answer and bill the same on both sides. The 4eda0c210d Severe caveat (custom-priced V5 billing about 70% low) no longer holds at this commit

The rig ran base main dcba0cf6f0 and head f785b8e0bd, one proxy per tree with 2 uvicorn workers, its own Postgres 16 and Redis 7.4, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, real Foundry behind a mitmdump forward proxy that logs each request and forwards it. The top cells ran again on the PR merged into current main (e63b2cc69ac) with the same results. Every cell used a fresh key and read `/key/info` spend and the `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row

#### Breaking

None found. Every outbound request body appeared on both sides with the same header key set and the same attempt count (wire_diff.txt). Status, body, spend and spend row matched in every cell apart from the changes listed next

#### Backward incompatible

One change, and it narrows the 4eda0c210d Medium caveat. The relay's logged token count now depends on how the deployment is priced. A custom-priced deployment with no image price logs Foundry's folded count (1017 for the text plus 512px image call), the same as main. A cost-map deployment or one with `input_cost_per_image_token` logs 264. Spend rows and the key TPM counter read this count. On base all three log 1017 (cells/*/c11-tpm-*, tpm_probe.txt). Before f785b8e0bd every V5 relay logged 264 on head, so this commit puts custom-priced deployments back on main's count. The cost-map spend change ($0.00012204 to $0.00010392) is the PR's intended change and is unchanged from the last pass

#### Regression risk

These were not driven:

- A deployment whose `model_info.id` matches a cost map key. The router seeds that deployment's price entry from the cost map row, which has the image price, so the folded branch would not fire and images would bill at the cost map image rate. This comes from reading `registration_base`, not from a run
- `/model/update` that removes an image price. Price entries merge into the existing one under the same id, so the old image price would stay until the cost map reloads and the call keeps itemizing. Read from code, not run
- `/vllm`, `/nvidia_nim` and the other generic passthrough routes when they name an azure_ai model group. They reach the same `logging_non_streaming_response`, so the relay cells cover the code but not those entrypoints
- Router deployment TPM and the Prometheus token counters, which read the same usage. Carried from the last pass
- A metadata, `litellm_metadata` or `model_info` value that is not a mapping would now raise inside logging for every Foundry relay, rerank and FLUX included, and drop that call's log. A caller cannot get there through the relay because the body goes to Foundry verbatim and Foundry answers 422 to the extra field on both sides (c15, c16)

title: fix(router): unregister vertex pass-through credentials on deployment delete/update (#51627)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #51627.

When a pass-through deployment for Vertex AI is deleted or replaced via upsert on the router, its credentials previously remained registered in `passthrough_endpoint_router.deployment_key_to_vertex_credentials` until process restart.

This adds credential cleanup:
- `passthrough_endpoint_router.remove_vertex_credentials(project_id, location)` to pop cached credentials for that deployment key.
- `remove_vertex_pass_through_credentials` exposed on `ProxyRouterHost`.
- `_remove_vertex_pass_through_credentials` invoked in `registry.py` during deployment deletion (`_core_delete_deployment`) and deployment upsert/replacement (`_core_upsert_deployment`).

## Tests

- Added `test_vertex_deployment_credentials_removed_on_delete` in `tests/unit/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_passthrough_endpoint_router.py`.
- Verified python syntax with `py_compile`.

## AI assistance disclosure

I used AI assistance to investigate the lifecycle of vertex credentials in `passthrough_endpoint_router`, trace registration in `registry.py`, and draft the removal logic and unit test.

title: fix(gateway): return Claude thinking blocks on chat completions instead of a 500
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

When Claude thinks before it answers, the Rust gateway's chat completions answered 500 after Anthropic had already answered and billed the call, while the Python proxy answers 200. Haiku 5.5 thinks on its own once a prompt is hard enough, so normal requests hit this

Now the gateway returns Claude's thinking on the message the way the Python proxy does and answers 200. A client that sends that reply back on its next turn, to Claude or an OpenAI-compatible model, also gets 200 now, where the gateway used to refuse it with 501

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Gateway chat answers 500 whenever Claude returns a thinking block
- Sending a thinking reply back next turn answers 501
- The Python proxy answers both 200

How it solves it:

- Thinking blocks map to the two message fields Python sets
- A thinking reply sent back is replayed to Claude like Python
- OpenAI-compatible models get that reply as sent, like Python

## User Flow

Before: a developer whose prompt makes Claude think gets a 500 and no answer, though Anthropic billed the call

1. The admin adds `model_name: claude-haiku-5-5` with `model: anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` and starts the Rust gateway
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "claude-haiku-5-5"`, `"max_tokens": 2048`, and a short math question
3. They get HTTP 500 `invalid response: non-text response content block is not handled by the rust path`
4. A thinking reply from elsewhere, sent back with a follow-up question, gets HTTP 501 `declined by the rust path: unrecognized message field`

After: the same request answers 200 with the answer and Claude's thinking block

1. The admin sets up the gateway as in Before step 1
2. The developer sends the same request as in Before step 2
3. They get HTTP 200 with the answer in `content`, plus `reasoning_content` and a `thinking_blocks` entry with its signature, like the Python proxy
4. With `"max_tokens": 16`, Claude runs out mid-thought and they get 200 with `finish_reason: "length"` and `content: null`
5. They send the step 3 reply back with a follow-up question and get 200 with Claude's next answer
6. Sending the step 4 cut-off reply back also gets 200
7. Sending the step 3 reply to `openai_like/gpt-5.4-mini` instead also gets 200

## Decisions

<details>
<summary>Decisions and alternatives</summary>

1. The message gains the top-level `reasoning_content` and `thinking_blocks` fields the Python proxy sets, and nothing else
    - Python also sets `provider_specific_fields.thinking_blocks` and `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, but the gateway's chat response has never carried either field for any response, so adding them is a separate change
    - Cost does not move, since Anthropic already counts thinking tokens in `output_tokens`, which the gateway reports as `completion_tokens`
2. `reasoning_content` is the thinking text of every `thinking` block joined in order, and `""` when the only blocks are empty or redacted, which is what Python returns (every default thinking block Haiku 5.5 sent in my runs had empty text, so `""` is the common case)
    - Leaving it out when it would be empty would make the gateway's body differ from Python's for the same request
3. A text-only answer carries neither field, as before, so existing clients see the same body
4. Blocks the chat route still cannot map, like `tool_use`, keep the existing error, since the gateway still declines `tools` with 501 before calling Anthropic, so Claude has nothing to call
5. Requests that set `thinking` or `reasoning_effort` still get the gateway's 501 decline before any call to Anthropic, which this PR does not change
6. A thinking reply sent back on a later turn goes to Anthropic with each message's thinking blocks ahead of its text, which is what Python sends
    - Like Python, blocks Anthropic could not have signed are dropped (no signature, or another provider's encrypted reasoning), `index` is removed, and redacted data Bedrock wrapped in extra base64 is unwrapped
    - A sent-back `reasoning_content` is accepted and ignored, since Python never reads it for Anthropic
    - A reply cut off mid-thought, sent back with `content: null`, no content, or an empty content list, goes to Anthropic as its thinking blocks alone, like Python. With no block Anthropic can replay it keeps the 501 `message without content`
    - A thinking block that several consecutive assistant messages carry is sent once, where it first appears, found in one pass over the blocks like Python
    - Blocks carrying `cache_control`, or redacted blocks with blank data, keep the 501, because Python changes them only under `drop_params`, which the gateway cannot see
    - OpenAI-compatible models get the reply as sent, with `thinking_blocks` and `reasoning_content`, since Python passes messages on verbatim. Like Python, `null` fields are dropped first
    - Bedrock keeps the 501 for a sent-back thinking reply, since this PR does not translate one for it
7. Bedrock Converse still answers 500 when Claude thinks there, which LIT-6436 tracks separately

</details>

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg built its tree's gateway with `cd litellm/rust && cargo build -p litellm-gateway --bin litellm-gateway`, ran one process on a random port, and called real Anthropic and OpenAI with curl, the client in the original repro

```yaml
  - model_name: claude-haiku-5-5

      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai_like/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_base: https://api.openai.com/v1
      api_key: <OPENAI_API_KEY value>

  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

```
LITELLM_CONFIG=config.yaml HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=$PORT <target dir>/debug/litellm-gateway
```

| Thinks, then answers | 500, 500, 500 | 200, 200, 200 |
| Cut off mid-thought | 500, 500 | 200, 200 |
| `/chat/completions` | 500 | 200 |
| Reply sent back next turn | 501, 501 | 200, 200 |
| Cut-off reply sent back | 501, 501 | 200, 200 |
| Reply sent to OpenAI-compatible | 501, 501 | 200, 200 |
