title: feat(cli): backport per-user GitHub Copilot credential connect to rc/1.107.0 (#50863)
body:
Backport of #50863 onto `rc/1.107.0`, so developers on the 1.107.0 release candidate can link their own GitHub Copilot account from the terminal

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3f19b79ee1a84292a5ca901803f6eb4e
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3f19b79ee1a84292a5ca901803f6eb4e?variant=devin
Requested by: @jesus-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `lite credentials connect` is on main but missing from `rc/1.107.0`
- Developers without Admin UI access cannot link GitHub Copilot there

How it solves it:

- Cherry-picks the squash commit of #50863 onto the line
- Adds the one JSON adapter the pick reads and the line lacked
- Bumps ten shipped dependencies in `uv.lock` to versions main already runs

## User Flow

Before: a developer with their own LiteLLM key can't link their GitHub Copilot account without the admin UI

1. The admin sets up a per-user GitHub Copilot credential and hands the developer a key
2. The developer runs `lite credentials connect copilot-per-user` and gets `Error: No such command 'connect'`, so the UI is the only way in

After: the same developer links their GitHub account from the terminal

1. The admin sets up a per-user GitHub Copilot credential and hands the developer a key
2. The developer runs `lite credentials connect copilot-per-user`, which prints a code and the https://github.com/login/device link
3. They enter the code on GitHub and approve, and the command prints `Connected as <their GitHub login>`

## What is in this backport

- [x] #50863 `feat(cli): connect a per-user GitHub Copilot credential from the command line`, picked from `e95bf288f3` as `b955673c11`. It applied clean with no conflicts and keeps its original author
- [x] Prerequisite, `27491063f2`. The pick calls `_DECODED_JSON` in `litellm/proxy/client/credentials.py`, which main got from an earlier typing refactor that is not on this line. Only that one adapter (`_DECODED_JSON: Final = TypeAdapter(object)`) is ported, the same definition main has
- [x] No version bump. An rc line keeps litellm at `1.107.0`, and the picks touch neither `enterprise/` nor `litellm-proxy-extras/`

Dependency bumps, lock only, one commit each, `pyproject.toml` untouched:

- aiohttp 3.14.3 -> 3.14.4 (also moves yarl 1.23.0 -> 1.25.1)
- certifi 2026.4.22 -> 2026.10.18
- ddtrace 4.11.0 -> 4.15.6 (adds its new required package ddtrace-internal 0.1.0)
- gitpython 3.1.62 -> 3.2.1
- graphql-core 3.2.8 -> 3.2.12
- mlflow 3.17.0 -> 3.17.2 (with mlflow-skinny and mlflow-tracing)
- oauthlib 4.0.0 -> 4.0.1
- pyasn1 0.6.4 -> 0.6.5
- pypdf 6.19.0 -> 6.21.4
- setuptools 83.0.0 -> 84.1.0

## Checks on the line

- `tests/unit/proxy/client` passes on this branch with 1220 tests, against 1210 on the line's tip. The 10 new ones are the tests #50863 added
- `BASE_REF=origin/rc/1.107.0 make check` passes
- The suites covering the code that imports the bumped packages (`tests/unit/llms/custom_httpx`, `tests/unit/integrations/test_mlflow.py`, `tests/unit/integrations/datadog`, `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_dd_tracing.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/roi_calculator`, `tests/unit/rag`) pass on the bumped lock, apart from the one baseline-red test under Caveats
- `uv lock --check` passes

Gauntlet-mini: SURVIVED, 5/5 lenses, 0 confirmed, run f83af6b74a97, reviewed d78ff73e225702c49bb90a80d7d8841fd1cf8d00. The session had no subagent tool, so the five lenses ran one after another in the main thread, which is the skill's weaker degraded mode

- Rejected: an error response with a body that is not JSON would crash the command. Executed with 502 and 401 HTML bodies, and the command prints the status and body and exits 1
- Strongest dissent: a 200 response with a body that is not JSON is reported as "could not reach the proxy". Rejected as a backport finding because main behaves the same and no sub-claim depends on it
- Baseline-red test carried as a caveat: see Caveats

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The change is only in the `lite` CLI and its Python client, so both sides ran against the same live proxy, started from this branch on port 4471 with real Postgres and Redis, and only the CLI changed. `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` held the proxy's master key. The device code is masked

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: copilot-gpt-4.1
    litellm_params:
      model: github_copilot/gpt-4.1
      litellm_credential_name: copilot-per-user

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

credential_list:
  - credential_name: copilot-per-user
    credential_values:
      github_copilot_auth_type: per_user_oauth
    credential_info:
      custom_llm_provider: github_copilot
```

### Before (f9778e945d)

1. Run the CLI from the line's tip

   ```
   $ lite --base-url http://localhost:4471 credentials connect copilot-per-user
   Error: No such command 'connect'.
   exit 2
   ```

### After (d78ff73e22)

1. Run the same command from this branch. It reaches GitHub through the proxy, prints a real device code and waits. It was stopped after 25 seconds because nobody approved the code

   ```
   $ timeout 25 lite --base-url http://localhost:4471 credentials connect copilot-per-user
   Go to https://github.com/login/device and enter code XXXX-XXXX
   Waiting for approval...
   exit 124
   ```

2. Run it for a credential that does not exist. It prints the proxy's 404 error body and aborts

   ```
   $ lite --base-url http://localhost:4471 credentials connect nope
       "code": "404"
   Aborted!
   exit 1
   ```

3. Run it with a wrong key. It prints the proxy's 401 error body and aborts

   ```
   $ LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY=sk-wrong lite --base-url http://localhost:4471 credentials connect copilot-per-user
       "code": "401"
   Aborted!
   exit 1
   ```

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- The GitHub approval step was not run live on this line
  - It needs a person with a Copilot seat to enter the code in a browser
  - #50863 ran it end to end on main, and the proxy endpoints it calls are unchanged here

### Low

- Copied from #50863
  - The command waits in the foreground until GitHub answers or the code expires
  - A dropped connection while waiting ends the command with a message asking the user to rerun it
  - On the source PR's account, Copilot only accepted gpt-4.1, not the other models tried
- `test_finalizer_on_live_loop_disposes_foreign_loop_session_without_scheduling` fails in one multi-directory test ordering
  - It fails the same way on the line's tip with the old lock, and passes when its own directory runs alone
- Some findings stay on the line because they could not be cleared with a lock-only bump
  - The resolver refused the target version, the package is dev-only, or no fixed version exists

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: perf(logging): scan opt-in spend-log tokens natively
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

use native scanning for PII removal in logs for performance

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves

- Opt-in token redaction spends most large-prompt CPU in Python regexes.
- Malformed JWT headers also need efficient scanning without hiding keys.

How it solves it

- Finds credential prefixes in Rust and validates matching candidates.
- Scans failed JWT headers once, preserving embedded-key redaction.
- Keeps redaction opt-in and preserves existing matching rules.

## User Flow

Before, enabling spend-log redaction reduces throughput for large prompts.

1. An admin enables prompt storage and token redaction.
2. A client sends concurrent POST requests to `http://localhost:18489/v1/chat/completions` with a 1 MB prompt.
3. The client receives successful replies, but sustained throughput drops while spend logs are scrubbed.

After, the same requests use substantially less CPU for redaction.

1. An admin enables prompt storage and token redaction.
2. A client sends concurrent POST requests to `http://localhost:18489/v1/chat/completions` with a 1 MB prompt.
3. The client receives successful replies faster, with the same masked content saved in spend logs.

## Relevant issues

Follow-up to #48968 and the opt-in mitigation in #51729.

## Implementation

The measured bottleneck is the Python token matcher. Profiling attributed about 91% of the 1 MB payload-building time to regex substitution. Moving that work to a thread still consumes Python CPU and the GIL.

The native scanner searches known prefixes with Aho-Corasick, then validates only candidates. It releases the GIL and returns the original Python string when no replacement is needed. Failed JWT headers are scanned once, while bounded credentials inside them remain eligible for masking. Python supplies its Unicode word ranges so token boundaries match the running interpreter. The existing Python matcher handles replacement backslashes and lone surrogates.

`redact_tokens_in_spend_logs` remains false by default. This PR does not change callback dispatch, prompt storage limits, or provider and caller payloads.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The focused tests covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR only solves one specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on the latest commit has finished and its findings are addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The comparison uses base `f5ef14308bf7582af365aabae1ea0ff1b0c626df` and tip `68707fa3170bf1e8309bb7559c40845ea4bf6e8e`. Both use the same dependencies, schema, native build settings, workload, and isolated services. The native extension was rebuilt from each checkout and the generated Prisma schema was checked against both sources. Before publication, main was refreshed to `cd2e4b6b60e0f6e0d106a955234f269f81b50b77` and the tested commit merged cleanly without conflicts.

The upstream is a local scripted OpenAI-compatible server, so these measurements isolate proxy overhead and spend persistence. No external inference is included. All authentication, routing, spend-log writes, and budget accounting use the real proxy, Postgres, and Redis.

The load test uses four workers, balanced persistent connections, 50 or 200 concurrent clients, two 20-second repetitions, and 1 KB or 1 MB prompts. The 80 measured runs cover storage on/off and redaction on/off, plus malformed JWT text with storage on. At 50 clients, worker connection counts are 13, 13, 12, 12. At 200, each worker gets 50. Every measured response is checked against its assigned worker PID. Warm-up spend rows and accounting settle before measurement. Persistence and accounting are checked after each run.

Reload and detailed debug logging are disabled for the four-worker load test. The separate endpoint preservation checks use two workers on both revisions. The default 2,048-character storage truncation remains enabled, and redaction happens before truncation.

### Balanced load results

All 80 valid balanced matrix runs completed. There were 685,223 successful requests, 0 HTTP errors, and 0 missing spend rows after the drain window. All four workers served measured traffic with zero connection moves. Accounting completed in every run.

Throughput is total successful requests divided by total elapsed time across the two repetitions. Accounted throughput also includes the time waiting for spend persistence and budget accounting to settle.

```python
        try:

                payload = await response.json()
                if response.status != 200:

                pid = int(response.headers['x-benchmark-worker'])

        except BaseException:
            await client.close()

                raise RuntimeError('Could not establish balanced worker connections')
            await asyncio.gather(*(open_connection() for _ in range(32)))
        while not warmup_complete(warm_ids):
            if time.monotonic()-prepare_started > 180:
                raise RuntimeError('Balanced connection warmup did not settle')
            await asyncio.sleep(.5)
        latencies = []
        ids = []
        errors = Counter()
        error_details = Counter()
        served_by = Counter()
        moved_connections = 0
        wall_started = time.time()
        started = time.monotonic()
        deadline = started+options.seconds
        cpu = time.process_time()

        async def worker(expected_pid, client):
            nonlocal moved_connections
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                before = time.monotonic()
                try:
                    async with client.post(route, data=body) as response:
                        result = await response.json()
                        if response.status == 200 and result.get('choices', [{}])[0].get('message', {}).get('content') == 'OK':
```

```python
                now = time.monotonic()
```

```python
    database(dbname,'CREATE')
    redis.Redis(host='127.0.0.1',port=16389).flushdb()
    repo=REPOS[options.revision]
    settings=dict(master_key='os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY',database_url='os.environ/DATABASE_URL',store_prompts_in_spend_logs=bool(options.store),proxy_batch_write_at=5,proxy_batch_polling_interval=1,coordination_redis=dict(host='127.0.0.1',port=16389))
    if options.redact!='unset':settings['redact_tokens_in_spend_logs']=options.redact=='true'
    config=dict(model_list=[dict(model_name='load-model',litellm_params=dict(model='openai/synthetic-redaction-model',api_key='os.environ/BENCH_UPSTREAM_KEY',api_base='os.environ/BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL',input_cost_per_token=.001,output_cost_per_token=.002))],general_settings=settings,router_settings=dict(redis_host='127.0.0.1',redis_port=16389),litellm_settings=dict(callbacks=['load_observer.observer']))
    config_path=out/'config.json'
    config_path.write_text(json.dumps(config,indent=2))
    environment={k:os.environ[k] for k in ('HOME','PATH','TMPDIR','LANG') if k in os.environ}
    environment.update(PATH=str(Path(PYTHON).parent)+os.pathsep+environment.get('PATH',''),PYTHONPATH=os.pathsep.join((str(ROOT/'python-client'),str(repo),str(repo/'litellm/enterprise'),str(repo/'litellm/proxy-extras'),str(repo/'litellm/packaging/litellm-proxy'),str(ROOT))),PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED='1',LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP='True',LITELLM_MODE='PRODUCTION',PYTHONWARNINGS='ignore',DATABASE_URL=f'postgresql://redaction_load@127.0.0.1:15489/{dbname}',LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=MASTER,BENCH_UPSTREAM_KEY='synthetic-upstream-key',BENCH_UPSTREAM_URL='http://127.0.0.1:18089/v1',BENCH_OBSERVER_DIR=str(observations))

    assert resolved['prisma'].startswith(str(ROOT/'python-client'))
    process=subprocess.Popen(command,cwd=repo,env=environment,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,text=True,start_new_session=True,bufsize=1)

            for line in process.stdout:f.write(sanitize(line));f.flush()
    logger=threading.Thread(target=logs,daemon=True);logger.start()
    summary=dict(tag=tag,database_setup='migrations from pinned checkout proxy-extras',command=command,head=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',str(repo),'rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip(),runs=[])
    try:
        with httpx.Client(base_url=PROXY,headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+MASTER},timeout=30,trust_env=False) as client:
            deadline=time.monotonic()+300
            while True:
                if process.poll() is not None:raise RuntimeError('Proxy exited before readiness, see sanitized proxy.log')
                try:
                    ready=client.get('/health/readiness',timeout=2)
                    if ready.status_code==200:break
                except httpx.TransportError:pass
                if time.monotonic()>deadline:raise RuntimeError('Proxy readiness timeout, see sanitized proxy.log')
                time.sleep(1)
            with psycopg.connect(**DB,dbname=dbname) as conn:
                assert conn.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE (table_name,column_name) IN (('LiteLLM_BudgetTable','name'),('LiteLLM_DailyTagSpend','guardrail_spend'))").fetchone()[0]==2
            start=time.monotonic()
            response=client.post('/v1/chat/completions',json=dict(model='load-model',messages=[dict(role='user',content='cold first request')]))
            summary['cold_request_ms']=(time.monotonic()-start)*1000
            if response.status_code!=200:raise RuntimeError('Cold request HTTP '+str(response.status_code)+' '+sanitize(response.text)[:1000])
            key_response=client.post('/key/generate',json=dict(models=['load-model']))
            if key_response.status_code!=200:raise RuntimeError('Virtual-key creation HTTP '+str(key_response.status_code))

            assert accounted(dbname,key,accepted_for_key)['complete'], 'Warmup accounting did not settle'
            summary['serving_worker_pids']=[int(p.stem.split('-')[-1]) for p in observed]
            environment['BENCH_WORKER_PIDS']=','.join(str(pid) for pid in summary['serving_worker_pids'])
            print(json.dumps(dict(tag=tag,smoke_passed=True,workers=4,cold_request_ms=summary['cold_request_ms'])),flush=True)
            if options.smoke_only:return
            cases=[(size,concurrency,'plain') for size in (1000000,1000) for concurrency in (50,200)]
            if options.malformed:cases=[(1000000,concurrency,'jwt') for concurrency in (50,200)]
            for repeat in range(options.repetitions):
                for size,concurrency,shape in cases:
                    file=out/f'{shape}-{size}-c{concurrency}-r{repeat}.json'
                    client_command=[PYTHON,str(ROOT/'load_client.py'),'--size',str(size),'--concurrency',str(concurrency),'--shape',shape,'--seconds',str(options.seconds),'--output',str(file)]
                    run=subprocess.run(client_command,env=environment,capture_output=True,text=True)
                    if run.returncode:raise RuntimeError('Load generator failed '+sanitize(run.stderr)[-1000:])
                    result=json.loads(file.read_text())
                    if result['wall_elapsed_s']-result['elapsed_s']>5:raise RuntimeError('Machine suspended during measured run')
                    persistence=drain(dbname,result['ids'])
                    result['persistence']=persistence
                    accepted_for_key+=persistence['persisted']+result['warmup_count']
                    accounting=accounted(dbname,key,accepted_for_key)
                    result['accounting']=accounting
                    result['accounted_per_second']=persistence['persisted']/(result['elapsed_s']+persistence['drain_s']+accounting['drain_s'])
                    result['persisted_per_second']=persistence['persisted']/(result['elapsed_s']+persistence['drain_s'])
                    samples=[json.loads(line) for p in observations.glob('*.jsonl') for line in p.read_text().splitlines()]
                    relevant=[s for s in samples if result['start']<=s['time']<=result['end']]
                    result['worker_loop_max_ms']=max((s['loop_max_ms'] for s in relevant),default=None)
                    result['workers_observed']=len({s['pid'] for s in relevant})
                    result['worker_cpu_s']=sum(max(s['cpu_s'] for s in relevant if s['pid']==pid)-min(s['cpu_s'] for s in relevant if s['pid']==pid) for pid in {s['pid'] for s in relevant})
                    file.write_text(json.dumps(result))
                    compact={k:v for k,v in result.items() if k not in ('ids','warmup_ids')}
                    if result['moved_connections']:
                        print(json.dumps(dict(tag=tag, invalid_worker_distribution=True, **compact)),flush=True)
                        raise RuntimeError('A measured connection moved between proxy workers')
                    summary['runs'].append(compact)
                    (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))
                    print(json.dumps(dict(tag=tag,repeat=repeat,**compact)),flush=True)
                    if not accounting['complete']:print(json.dumps(dict(tag=tag,warning='Accounting did not settle within the observation window')),flush=True)
                    if not persistence['complete']:print(json.dumps(dict(tag=tag,warning='Missing spend logs after the observation window',missing=persistence['expected']-persistence['persisted'])),flush=True)
    finally:
        (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))
        if process.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(process.pid,signal.SIGTERM)
            try:process.wait(timeout=90)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

        logger.join(timeout=5)
        if len(summary['runs']) == (0 if options.smoke_only else (2 if options.malformed else 4)*options.repetitions) and all(r['persistence']['complete'] for r in summary['runs']):
            database(dbname,'DROP')
```

title: fix(azure): backport Foundry project and resource /openai/v1 Responses bases to lts/1.108.x
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

On the 1.108 LTS line, Azure deployments pointed at a Foundry project's /openai/v1 URL fail every Responses and chat call, and resource-level /openai/v1 bases get a doubled path that Azure answers with a 404. This brings every fix from #51767 to the line, so those deployments work on 1.108.x without an upgrade, a gateway deployment can set `api_version: none`, and an `azure/model-router` call bills the model it picked

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `azure/` Responses and chat on a Foundry project `/openai/v1` base always 400
- Resource `/openai/v1` Responses bases get a doubled path and 404
- A gateway URL that hides the project path cannot drop `api-version`
- WebSocket Responses on `/openai/v1` bases dials a doubled path
- `azure/model-router` bills only its fee for models priced under `azure_ai/`

How it solves it:

- Hand-ports 96abce842b, main's `/openai/v1` base fix for #48072
- Picks every commit of #51767, whose Decisions hold on the line as written
- Every other Azure URL and call type keeps what it sends today

| main | lts/1.108.x | How it applied |

| 96abce842b9 | f087f7dfda6 | Hand-ported, explicit `/openai/v1` branch only |

title: fix(azure): send no api-version on Foundry project /openai/v1 Responses bases
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description Azure deployments pointed at a Foundry project's /openai/v1 URL failed every Responses and chat call, because LiteLLM always added an api-version query param and Azure rejects any api-version on that path. This drops it on that path only, and a deployment behind a gateway URL that hides the project path can set `api_version: none` to send none. It also bills an `azure/model-router` call for the model the router picked when that model is only priced under `azure_ai/`
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `azure/` Responses and chat on a Foundry project `/openai/v1` base always 400, since LiteLLM always adds `api-version` - A gateway URL that hides the project path has no per-deployment way to drop it - WebSocket Responses on any `/openai/v1` base dials a doubled `/openai/v1/openai/v1/responses` - `azure/model-router` bills only its router fee when it routes to a model priced only under `azure_ai/` How it solves it: - Drop `api-version` only on project `/openai/v1/responses` URLs - Retrieve, delete, input items and the chat bridge inherit it - Chat on a project `/openai/v1` base uses the v1 OpenAI client, with no `api-version` - `api_version: none` sends no `api-version` on Responses, chat and embeddings, on any base - The WebSocket URL no longer doubles `/openai/v1` - A routed model priced only under `azure_ai/` is billed from there, plus the router fee - Every other Azure URL and call type keeps its `api-version` as before ## User Flow Before: an admin who points an `azure/model-router` deployment at a Foundry project's `/openai/v1` URL gets a 400 on every Responses and chat call 1. The admin sets `api_base: https://.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects//openai/v1` on an `azure/model-router` deployment, with or without `api_version` 2. The app calls `client.responses.create(model="model-router", ...)` through the proxy, or POST /v1/chat/completions 3. The app gets HTTP 400 "api-version query parameter is not allowed when using /v1 path" 4. Retrieve, delete, and the chat and messages bridges fail the same way 5. A gateway base such as `https://apim.example.com/my-foundry/openai/v1` gets the same 400, and no setting removes it 6. A WebSocket client on ws://localhost:4000/v1/responses gets an error, since LiteLLM dials a doubled path 7. On a working base, a call routed to a model priced only under `azure_ai/` bills only the router fee After: the same calls succeed and are billed for the routed model plus the router fee 1. The admin and the app change nothing 2. The app gets HTTP 200 with the routed model's answer 3. The `x-litellm-response-cost` header is the routed model's token cost plus the router fee 4. Retrieve, delete, and the chat and messages bridges answer 200 5. The gateway admin adds `api_version: none`, and the same calls answer 200 6. The WebSocket client gets `response.completed` ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10663
Decisions 1. An explicit `api_version` on the deployment, or an `api-version` already in `api_base`, is dropped too on a project `/openai/v1` URL. Azure answered 400 for every value tried there (`preview`, `v1`, `2025-04-01-preview`) and 200 with none, so keeping it can only fail. The alternatives were honoring an explicit value, which is a guaranteed 400, or dropping it only under `drop_params`, but the path takes no version at all, so there is nothing to keep 2. The match is on the final URL path `/api/projects/

/openai/v1/responses`, so a gateway prefix in front of it still matches and other query params like `tenant` stay. Resource-level `/openai/v1` bases keep `api-version`, since Azure accepts `preview` there 3. A project root base (`/api/projects/

`) with a dated project version such as `2025-11-15-preview` keeps `/openai/responses?api-version=...`, which Azure accepts 4. Built from scratch. #51116 changed the same function for a different bug, and this branch keeps both changes 5. This is an LLM translation fix, so a paired lts/1.108.x PR carries it along with the `/openai/v1` base handling from 96abce842b (the fix for #48072), which that line lacks 6. Only chat completions, o-series models included, on a project `/openai/v1` base switch to the v1 OpenAI client, which sends no `api-version` even with a dated `api_version` set, for the same reason as decision 1. Its auth header is decision 10. Embeddings, text completion, transcription, speech, files, batches, fine-tuning, images, vector stores and assistants keep the Azure client, so on a project `/openai/v1` base they still get Azure's own 400, the same as before this PR. Moving them all at 7770bbceb2 made transcription and `azure_text` fail with a 500, since their handlers expect the Azure client, so each is a follow-up. Resource-level `/openai/v1` bases keep today's client and version 7. Only an `azure/` model-router request whose routed model has no `azure/` price but has an `azure_ai/` price is billed from `azure_ai/`. The alternatives were a general `azure/` to `azure_ai/` price fallback for every deployment, which would silently price custom deployment names, leaving the fee-only bill, or relying on the per-deployment `model_info.pricing_provider: azure_ai` setting from #47620, which still works and still wins. A routed model with its own `azure/` price keeps it. The billed total matches the [model-router docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/azure_ai/azure_model_router#cost-tracking), `Total = Model Cost + Router Flat Cost`, which `azure_ai/` model-router already follows 8. `api_version: none`, in any case, means send no `api-version`. Responses and its retrieve, delete and input items calls go to `/openai/v1/responses` with no version, after dropping a trailing `/openai/responses` from the base, and chat completions and embeddings use the v1 OpenAI client. It is for a gateway URL that hides the project path, which decision 2's path match cannot see. A set `responses_api_version` still wins for Responses. Image, speech, transcription and text completion calls do not read the value, so they send what they send today. The alternatives were an empty `api_version`, which a blank UI field or an unset env var also produces, so it would silently change those deployments, a new flag, which is one more param to carry through the router and document, and the proxy-wide `AZURE_DEFAULT_RESPONSES_API_VERSION=""`, which changes every deployment 9. A query in the v1 client's `api_base`, such as `?tenant=example`, moves to the client's `default_query` with any `api-version` removed, and the route goes on the path. Before, the route was glued on after the query, which built a broken URL. Dropping the whole query was the alternative, but it would lose a gateway's own params. A v1 client base ending in `/openai` gets `/openai/v1` once, and a percent-encoded gateway path stays as typed, which fixes `api_version: v1` chat on that base too 10. With `api_version: none`, each call keeps the auth header its v1 path already sends. Chat and embeddings go through the v1 OpenAI client, which sends the key only as `Authorization: Bearer`, the same as LiteLLM's existing `api_version: v1` chat, and Responses keeps `api-key`. So a gateway that reads only `api-key` rejects chat and embeddings with `none`, as it already rejects `api_version: v1` chat. Sending `api-key` from the v1 client too was the alternative, but it adds a header to every existing `api_version: v1`, `latest` and `preview` deployment, so it needs its own change and proof

title: fix(responses): mark only the item a cut response ended on as incomplete
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

When a Claude or Gemini response streamed through the gateway's Responses API got cut off by a refusal or by `max_output_tokens`, the event that closes the answer message said `completed` and the final event said `incomplete`. A tool call cut off mid-arguments said `completed` everywhere, and reasoning that finished before a capped answer said `incomplete`

This PR marks only the item the cut landed on as `incomplete`, as OpenAI does for messages and tool calls, and every item that finished before it says `completed`. Every event reads one helper, so they can't disagree anymore

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Streamed `/v1/responses` called a cut-off message `completed`, then `incomplete` in the final event
- A tool call cut off by `max_output_tokens` said `completed` in both events
- Reasoning that finished before the cut said `incomplete`

How it solves it:

- One helper picks the item the cut landed on and gives only it `incomplete`
- Message and tool call done events, the final event and the non-streamed response read it

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

1. Only the item the response was cut on says `incomplete`, and every item before it says `completed`. OpenAI's Responses API does the same for messages and function calls, so for one short sentence and then a tool call cut by `max_output_tokens` it sends the message `completed` and the function_call `incomplete`. The first version of this PR gave every item the response's status, and I dropped that because it marks a message that finished before the cut as unfinished and leaves a cut tool call `completed`
2. The cut item is the last client tool call when the turn has one, else the message when it has text or a refusal, else the reasoning. A turn's client tool calls come after its text, so a cut that reaches a tool call lands on the last one. In a stream, a last call whose arguments are already a whole, non-empty JSON object finished before the cut and says `completed`, because Gemini drops the call it could not finish and its non-streamed response says `completed` too. Claude streams a cut call's arguments as unfinished JSON, or as `{}` when the cut comes before the first argument, so `{}` counts as cut. The other choice was to treat `{}` as whole, which would call a cut Claude call `completed`. A non-streamed response keeps the last call as the cut one, since Claude returns a cut call's input already parsed into a partial object like `{"path": "numbers.txt"}`
3. When the cut lands on a pending server-side web search, that search keeps its `in_progress` status and every bridged item before it says `completed`. Other server tool items (web search with results, tool search, code execution) and image generation items keep the statuses they already had, so a cut that ends on an image after reasoning still marks the reasoning `incomplete` too, as main does
4. Anthropic's `pause_turn` still reads as `completed` for every item, from main's paused-turn rule, and a missing finish_reason still means `incomplete`, now on the cut item only
5. A status the provider put on a tool call's function still wins over the computed one, as it did before
6. Reasoning that finished before the cut says `completed` in the final event and the non-streamed response, the status main already gives reasoning on every normal finish. OpenAI leaves `status` null on reasoning items, and I didn't switch to that because it would change the reasoning item on every response, not only cut ones
7. The reasoning item's done event still has no `status`, since OpenAI's reasoning done item carries none and it often goes out before the finish reason is known. #47271 covers that item
8. `_web_search_calls_by_call_id` now reads each choice through a new per-choice helper, so the cut rule and the output builder parse web search calls the same way

</details>

## User Flow

Before: a developer streaming Claude through the gateway's Responses API is told that a cut-off answer or tool call finished, then told otherwise in the final event

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with a Claude model, `"stream": true`, and a small `max_output_tokens` or a prompt Claude refuses
2. The cut message's `response.output_item.done` event says `"status": "completed"`, and so does a tool call cut off mid-arguments
3. The final `response.incomplete` event calls that message `incomplete`, the reasoning before it `incomplete`, and the cut tool call `completed`

After: only the item the cut landed on says `incomplete`, the same way in both events

1. They send the same request
2. The cut item's `response.output_item.done` event says `"status": "incomplete"`, and items that finished before it say `"completed"`
3. The final `response.incomplete` event matches the done events, and reasoning that finished before the cut says `completed`

title: feat(proxy): accept nested paths in spend_logs_metadata_fields.exclude
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `spend_logs_metadata_fields.exclude` only accepts top-level metadata keys
- Some upstreams add a large `attribution` block inside `usage`
- Dropping it today means dropping all of `usage_object`, token counts included

How it solves it:

- An exclude entry can now be a dotted path like `usage_object.attribution`
- The stored log drops only that key and keeps its siblings
- Startup still checks the first segment against known metadata keys
- Paths under keys the proxy always keeps or rewrites are refused
- `include` still takes top-level names only

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin who wants stored logs without the `attribution` block can't get the proxy to start

1. The admin adds `usage_object.attribution` to `general_settings.spend_logs_metadata_fields.exclude` in config.yaml
2. They start the proxy and it exits with `'usage_object.attribution' is not a LiteLLM_SpendLogs.metadata field`
3. They fall back to excluding `usage_object`, and every stored log loses its token counts too

After: the same config starts, and stored logs keep token counts without the `attribution` block

1. The admin adds `usage_object.attribution` to `general_settings.spend_logs_metadata_fields.exclude` in config.yaml
2. They start the proxy and it becomes ready
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses or /v1/messages, streaming or not, and get 200
4. Each request's stored spend log keeps `usage_object` with `prompt_tokens` and has no `attribution` key

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both versions ran against the same local setup. Postgres 17 listens on 127.0.0.1, and a small fake OpenAI-compatible upstream answers chat completions and responses, streaming or not, with a fixed `usage` that carries an `attribution` block. The block's keys and nesting copy what a real upstream returns to us, but that upstream isn't one a reviewer can call, so this proof has no real provider call. In our traffic the block only shows up on Responses calls. The fake adds it to chat completions too, so the chat cases run the filter on a synthetic payload. The model is `openai/gpt-4o-mini` pointed at the fake, and /v1/messages reaches the fake's /v1/responses through the proxy's own translation.

The proxy starts with the AGENTS.md QA command. I left Redis out because this change only filters one log row as it is written and doesn't touch any state shared between workers. Both versions started two worker processes, and for the same reason I didn't check which worker served each request.

Shared setup, run from the litellm checkout with its `.venv/bin` and the Postgres 17 binaries on `PATH`. Env var names are `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `PG_PORT`, `PROXY_PORT` and `OUT_DIR`, and `DATABASE_URL` is set by the runner.

```shell
initdb -D "$OUT_DIR/pg-data" -U e2e --auth=trust -E UTF8
pg_ctl -D "$OUT_DIR/pg-data" -o "-p $PG_PORT -c unix_socket_directories= -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1" -l "$OUT_DIR/pg.log" -w start
createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PG_PORT" -U e2e litellm
python3 fake_upstream.py 46293 &
```

`config.yaml` is below. `config-control.yaml` is the same file without the last line, so the control run shows what the fake returns when nothing nested is excluded.

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: e2e-gpt
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:46293/v1
      api_key: synthetic-upstream-key
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  proxy_batch_write_at: 1
  spend_logs_metadata_fields:
    exclude:
      - model_map_information
      - additional_usage_values
      - usage_object.attribution
```

The runner starts the proxy with the QA command, sends one request per path below, tags each one so its stored row can be found, waits for five stored rows and reads their metadata back from Postgres.

<details>
<summary>run_paths.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage, from the litellm checkout: run_paths.sh <label> <config.yaml>
# env: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, PG_PORT (local Postgres, user e2e, database litellm), PROXY_PORT, OUT_DIR
set -euo pipefail

label="$1"
config="$2"
log="$OUT_DIR/proxy-paths-$label.log"
out="$OUT_DIR/paths-$label.txt"
psql_e2e=(psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p "$PG_PORT" -U e2e -d litellm -At)
run_id="$label-$(date +%s)"
excluded="$(grep -A4 'exclude:' "$config" | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ' | paste -sd' ')"

DATABASE_URL="postgresql://e2e@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/litellm" \
  setsid python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config "$config" --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PROXY_PORT" \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver > "$log" 2>&1 &
proxy_pid=$!
trap 'kill -- "-$proxy_pid" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

ready=no
for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
  curl -sf -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$PROXY_PORT/health/readiness" && { ready=yes; break; }
  kill -0 "$proxy_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
  sleep 2
done
if [ "$ready" = no ]; then
  {
    echo "case=$label commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) dirty_proxy_files=$(git status --short litellm/proxy | wc -l)"
    echo "config exclude: $excluded"
    echo "proxy did not become ready"
    grep -E 'ValidationError|spend_logs_metadata_fields\.exclude|Value error|Application startup failed' "$log" | head -4
  } | tee "$out"
  exit 1
fi

send() {
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:$PROXY_PORT$1" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -d "$2"
}
tags() { printf '"metadata":{"tags":["%s-%s"]}' "$run_id" "$1"; }

declare -A status
status[chat]=$(send /v1/chat/completions \
  "{\"model\":\"e2e-gpt\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],$(tags chat)}")
status[chat_stream]=$(send /v1/chat/completions \
  "{\"model\":\"e2e-gpt\",\"stream\":true,\"stream_options\":{\"include_usage\":true},\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],$(tags chat_stream)}")
status[responses]=$(send /v1/responses "{\"model\":\"e2e-gpt\",\"input\":\"hi\",$(tags responses)}")
status[responses_stream]=$(send /v1/responses "{\"model\":\"e2e-gpt\",\"input\":\"hi\",\"stream\":true,$(tags responses_stream)}")
status[messages]=$(send /v1/messages \
  "{\"model\":\"e2e-gpt\",\"max_tokens\":16,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],$(tags messages)}")

found=0
for _ in $(seq 1 45); do
  found="$("${psql_e2e[@]}" -c "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where request_tags::text like '%$run_id-%'")"
  [ "$found" -ge 5 ] && break
  sleep 2
done

{
  echo "case=$label commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) dirty_proxy_files=$(git status --short litellm/proxy | wc -l)"
  echo "config exclude: $excluded"
  for path in chat chat_stream responses responses_stream messages; do echo "http $path: ${status[$path]}"; done
  echo "server processes: $(grep -c 'Started server process' "$log")"
  echo "stored rows: $found of 5"
  echo "path | call_type | usage_object present | usage_object.attribution present | usage_object.prompt_tokens"
  "${psql_e2e[@]}" -F ' | ' -c "select regexp_replace(request_tags::text, '.*$run_id-([a-z_]+).*', '\\1'), call_type,
      metadata::jsonb ? 'usage_object', metadata::jsonb->'usage_object' ? 'attribution',
      metadata::jsonb->'usage_object'->>'prompt_tokens'
    from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where request_tags::text like '%$run_id-%' order by \"startTime\""
} | tee "$out"
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>fake_upstream.py</summary>

```python
import json
import sys
import uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

TOKENS = {"input_tokens": 7, "output_tokens": 1, "cached_tokens": 4, "cache_write_tokens": 0}
ATTRIBUTION = {
    "items": {"msg_e2e": TOKENS, "fc_e2e": TOKENS, "rs_e2e": TOKENS},
    "request_fields": {"instructions": TOKENS},
}
CHAT_USAGE = {
    "prompt_tokens": 10,
    "completion_tokens": 2,
    "total_tokens": 12,
    "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 4},
    "attribution": ATTRIBUTION,
}
RESPONSES_USAGE = {
    "input_tokens": 10,
    "output_tokens": 2,
    "total_tokens": 12,
    "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 4},
    "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0},
    "attribution": ATTRIBUTION,
}


def chat_completion(model: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
        "object": "chat.completion",
        "created": 1,
        "model": model,
        "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok"}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
        "usage": CHAT_USAGE,
    }


def chat_chunks(model: str) -> list[dict]:
    base = {"id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1, "model": model}
    return [
        {**base, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "ok"}, "finish_reason": None}]},
        {**base, "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]},
        {**base, "choices": [], "usage": CHAT_USAGE},
    ]


def response_object(model: str, status: str) -> dict:
    message = {
        "type": "message",
        "id": "msg_e2e",
        "status": "completed",
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "ok", "annotations": []}],
    }
    return {
        "id": f"resp_{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
        "object": "response",
        "created_at": 1,
        "status": status,
        "model": model,
        "output": [message] if status == "completed" else [],
        "usage": RESPONSES_USAGE if status == "completed" else None,
    }


def response_events(model: str) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    created = response_object(model, "in_progress")
    done = {**response_object(model, "completed"), "id": created["id"]}
    return [
        ("response.created", {"type": "response.created", "sequence_number": 0, "response": created}),
        (
            "response.output_text.delta",
            {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "sequence_number": 1, "item_id": "msg_e2e", "output_index": 0, "content_index": 0, "delta": "ok"},
        ),
        ("response.completed", {"type": "response.completed", "sequence_number": 2, "response": done}),
    ]


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def send_json(self, body: dict) -> None:
        payload = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(payload)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(payload)

    def send_sse(self, frames: list[bytes]) -> None:
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
        self.end_headers()
        for frame in frames:
            self.wfile.write(frame)
            self.wfile.flush()

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        length = int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0"))
        request = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
        model = request.get("model", "gpt-4o-mini")
        stream = bool(request.get("stream"))
        if self.path.endswith("/responses"):
            if stream:
                self.send_sse([f"event: {name}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode() for name, data in response_events(model)])
            else:
                self.send_json(response_object(model, "completed"))
            return
        if stream:
            self.send_sse([f"data: {json.dumps(chunk)}\n\n".encode() for chunk in chat_chunks(model)] + [b"data: [DONE]\n\n"])
        else:
            self.send_json(chat_completion(model))

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        self.send_json({"object": "list", "data": []})


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), Handler).serve_forever()
```

title: feat(proxy): support budget_limits windows on internal users
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Internal users can now carry several budget windows at once, like a monthly cap plus a tight hourly cap, the same way keys and teams already can. Whichever window runs out first blocks that user's requests on their personal keys and JWT calls, and each window resets on its own schedule

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `budget_limits` windows only worked on keys and teams
- A user could only have one `max_budget` and `budget_duration`
- `/user/new` accepted `budget_limits` but never stored it

How it solves it:

- Stores `budget_limits` on the user row (schema-only migration)
- `/user/new`, `/user/update` and `/user/bulk_update` validate, set and clear user windows
- Auth checks every user window, for virtual keys and JWT users
- User windows get their own Redis counters
- Post-call spend, reservation, reseed and the reset job cover user windows
- `default_internal_user_params` windows reach users made by `/user/new`, JWT upsert and member add
- An all-users bulk `spend` reset also clears each user's Redis spend counter

## User Flow

Before: an admin caps a user at $100 a month and a tiny amount an hour, but the user keeps spending

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/user/new with `"budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": 0.000001}, {"budget_duration": "1mo", "max_budget": 100}]`
2. GET https://litellm-domain/user/info shows `"budget_limits": null`
3. The user's key or JWT keeps calling POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and every call returns 200

After: the windows are stored and the first one to fill blocks the user

1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/user/new
2. GET https://litellm-domain/user/info returns both windows with their `reset_at`
3. The first call returns 200, the second returns 422 `ExceededBudget: User=<id> over 1h budget`, on any proxy instance, with a key or a JWT
4. POST https://litellm-domain/user/update with `"budget_limits": null` clears them and the next call returns 200

## Relevant issues

Part of LIT-6961, API only with no Admin UI editor. Replaces #51695 and supersedes #41722, #34500 and #29404

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Before ran at merge base `01de1a686d` and After at `8f4bdbae76`, each with proxies A and B on one Postgres, one Redis and real OpenAI `gpt-5.4-nano`, started as in Config. The client in Client script alternates OpenAI and Anthropic SDK calls between A and B, up to 8, and stops at the first non-200. JWT first-call and member add rows used a third proxy per leg, as in Default windows setup

Since `8f4bdbae76`, the head `bdf6f9cea3` changes only tests and the all-users bulk update, so the bulk row ran again at the head and the rest carry. /live-pr-risk raced bulk updates there to hit its failure path. The changed test files pass 1995 tests, and 10 sqlite cases from main fail only on Python 3.14

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1h cap fills, chat completions | 8 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| 1h cap fills, responses | 8 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| 1h cap fills, Anthropic messages | 8 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| 1mo cap fills | 8 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| Admin raises the 1h cap | Edit returns 400 | Still 422 on 1mo |
| `proxy_admin` user | 8 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| `/user/new` auto key | Key blocked after clear | 200 after clear |
| Lookalike user id spends | 8 calls, all 200 | Own call 2 gets 422 |
| JWT user, no key | 8 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| JWT user made on first call | Call 1 gets 401 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| Bulk update adds windows | Bulk returns 500 | Call 3 gets 422 |
| Team or org member add, default windows | 3 calls, all 200 | Call 2 gets 422 |
| Migration on a migrated DB | No `budget_limits` column | Column added, user row kept |

Clearing windows, a user with no windows, and `/user/new` with a team are unchanged ([output](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/7afbe6da9e5d2756e78882afc19566df))

<details>
<summary>Config</summary>

`python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config user-windows.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port> --num_workers 2 --timeout_worker_healthcheck 60 --telemetry False --use_prisma_db_push` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_LICENSE`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_HOST`, `REDIS_PORT` and `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL` (a local JWKS with the test public key)

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-nano
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-nano
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST
  redis_port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST
    port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT
  enable_jwt_auth: true
  litellm_jwtauth:
    user_id_jwt_field: sub
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Client script</summary>

```python
import json
import pathlib
import re
import secrets
import sys
import time

import anthropic
import httpx
import jwt
import openai

MODEL = "gpt-5.4-nano"
PROMPT = "Say hi"

leg, port_a, port_b, key_file, jwt_key_file = sys.argv[1:6]
proxies = {"A": f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_a}", "B": f"http://127.0.0.1:{port_b}"}
admin_headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {pathlib.Path(key_file).read_text().strip()}"}
tag = f"{leg}-{secrets.token_hex(3)}"


def redact(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: redact(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [redact(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("sk-"):
        return "sk-<redacted>"
    return value


def admin(method, proxy, path, body=None, fields=None, source=lambda payload: payload):
    shown_path = re.sub(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "sk-<redacted>", path)
    print(f"$ curl -X {method} {proxies[proxy]}{shown_path}" + (f" -d '{json.dumps(body)}'" if body is not None else ""))
    response = httpx.request(method, proxies[proxy] + path, headers=admin_headers, json=body, timeout=120)
    payload = response.json()
    picked = source(payload) if response.status_code == 200 else payload
    shown = {k: picked.get(k) for k in fields} if fields and response.status_code == 200 else picked
    print(f"HTTP {response.status_code} {json.dumps(redact(shown))}")
    return payload


def user_info(proxy, user_id):
    return admin(
        "GET", proxy, f"/user/info?user_id={user_id}", fields=("budget_limits", "spend"), source=lambda p: p["user_info"]
    )


def new_key(proxy, user_id):
    payload = admin("POST", proxy, "/key/generate", {"user_id": user_id}, fields=("key", "user_id"))
    return payload["key"]


def call(surface, proxy, key):
    base = proxies[proxy]
    if surface == "chat":
        print(f">>> OpenAI(base_url='{base}').chat.completions.create(model='{MODEL}', messages=[user: '{PROMPT}'])")
        run = lambda: openai.OpenAI(base_url=base, api_key=key, max_retries=0).chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}]
        ).choices[0].message.content
    elif surface == "responses":
        print(f">>> OpenAI(base_url='{base}').responses.create(model='{MODEL}', input='{PROMPT}')")
        run = lambda: openai.OpenAI(base_url=base, api_key=key, max_retries=0).responses.create(
            model=MODEL, input=PROMPT
        ).output_text
    else:
        print(f">>> Anthropic(base_url='{base}').messages.create(model='{MODEL}', max_tokens=64, messages=[user: '{PROMPT}'])")
        run = lambda: anthropic.Anthropic(base_url=base, api_key=key, max_retries=0).messages.create(
            model=MODEL, max_tokens=64, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT}]
        ).content[0].text
    try:
        print(f"200 {json.dumps(run())}")
        return 200
    except (openai.APIStatusError, anthropic.APIStatusError) as error:
        print(f"{error.status_code} {json.dumps(error.body)}")
        return error.status_code


def call_until_blocked(surface, key, limit=8):
    for attempt in range(limit):
        if call(surface, "A" if attempt % 2 == 0 else "B", key) != 200:
            return
        time.sleep(3)


def windows(hour, month):
    return [{"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": hour}, {"budget_duration": "1mo", "max_budget": month}]


def key_info(proxy, key):
    return admin("GET", proxy, f"/key/info?key={key}", fields=("budget_limits",), source=lambda p: p["info"])


def mint_jwt(user_id):
    now = int(time.time())
    private_key = pathlib.Path(jwt_key_file).read_text()
    return jwt.encode({"sub": user_id, "iat": now, "exp": now + 3600}, private_key, algorithm="RS256", headers={"kid": "qa"})


for surface in ("chat", "responses", "messages"):
    print(f"\n## case hourly_{surface}: 1h $0.000001 + 1mo $100, calls on {surface}")
    user = f"hourly-{surface}-{tag}"
    admin("POST", "A", "/user/new", {"user_id": user, "auto_create_key": False, "budget_limits": windows(0.000001, 100)}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
    user_info("B", user)
    call_until_blocked(surface, new_key("A", user))

print("\n## case monthly_first: 1h $100 + 1mo $0.000001")
monthly = f"monthly-{tag}"
admin("POST", "B", "/user/new", {"user_id": monthly, "auto_create_key": False, "budget_limits": windows(100, 0.000001)}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
monthly_key = new_key("B", monthly)
call_until_blocked("chat", monthly_key)

print("\n## case edit_keeps_block: admin raises the 1h cap on the blocked user, the 1mo window keeps its spend")
admin("POST", "A", "/user/update", {"user_id": monthly, "budget_limits": windows(200, 0.000001)}, fields=("budget_limits",), source=lambda p: p["data"])
call("chat", "B", monthly_key)

print("\n## case clear_windows: admin clears the windows, the user calls through both proxies")
cleared = f"hourly-chat-{tag}"
admin("POST", "A", "/user/update", {"user_id": cleared, "budget_limits": None}, fields=("budget_limits",), source=lambda p: p["data"])
cleared_key = new_key("A", cleared)
call("chat", "B", cleared_key)
call("chat", "A", cleared_key)

print("\n## case no_windows: /user/new without budget_limits")
plain = f"plain-{tag}"
admin("POST", "A", "/user/new", {"user_id": plain, "auto_create_key": False}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
plain_key = new_key("A", plain)
call("chat", "B", plain_key)
call("chat", "A", plain_key)

print("\n## case admin_windows: a proxy_admin user with 1h $0.000001")
admin_user = f"admin-{tag}"
admin("POST", "A", "/user/new", {"user_id": admin_user, "auto_create_key": False, "user_role": "proxy_admin", "budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": 0.000001}]}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
call_until_blocked("chat", new_key("A", admin_user))

print("\n## case default_auto_key: /user/new with the default auto_create_key, then the admin clears the user's windows")
auto = f"auto-{tag}"
auto_key = admin("POST", "A", "/user/new", {"user_id": auto, "budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": 0.000001}]}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))["key"]
key_info("B", auto_key)
call_until_blocked("chat", auto_key)
admin("POST", "A", "/user/update", {"user_id": auto, "budget_limits": None}, fields=("budget_limits",), source=lambda p: p["data"])
call("chat", "B", auto_key)
call("chat", "A", auto_key)

print("\n## case lookalike_user: user <id>:window:1h spends, then user <id> with a 1h window calls")
victim = f"victim-{tag}"
lookalike = f"{victim}:window:1h"
admin("POST", "A", "/user/new", {"user_id": lookalike, "auto_create_key": False}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
call("chat", "A", new_key("A", lookalike))
time.sleep(3)
admin("POST", "B", "/user/new", {"user_id": victim, "auto_create_key": False, "budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": 0.000001}]}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
call_until_blocked("chat", new_key("B", victim))

print("\n## case jwt_user: a JWT user with no virtual key, 1h $0.000001 + 1mo $100")
jwt_user = f"jwt-{tag}"
admin("POST", "A", "/user/new", {"user_id": jwt_user, "auto_create_key": False, "budget_limits": windows(0.000001, 100)}, fields=("user_id", "budget_limits"))
```

```python
import json
```

```python
import secrets
import sys
import time

import httpx
import openai

leg, port, key_file = sys.argv[1:4]
base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {pathlib.Path(key_file).read_text().strip()}"}


def post(path, body):
    print(f"$ curl -X POST {base}{path} -d '{json.dumps(body)}'")
    response = httpx.post(f"{base}{path}", json=body, headers=headers, timeout=60)
    print(f"HTTP {response.status_code}")
    return response.json()


for kind in ("team", "organization"):
    user_id = f"{kind}-member-{leg}-{secrets.token_hex(3)}"
    print(f"\n## case {kind}_member_add: default_internal_user_params windows 1h $0.000001 + 1mo $100")
    if kind == "team":
        team_id = post("/team/new", {})["team_id"]
        post("/team/member_add", {"team_id": team_id, "member": {"role": "user", "user_id": user_id}})
    else:
        org_id = post("/organization/new", {"organization_alias": user_id})["organization_id"]
        post("/organization/member_add", {"organization_id": org_id, "member": [{"role": "internal_user", "user_id": user_id}]})
    info = httpx.get(f"{base}/user/info", params={"user_id": user_id}, headers=headers, timeout=60).json()["user_info"]
    print(f"$ curl {base}/user/info?user_id={user_id}\nbudget_limits {json.dumps(info.get('budget_limits'))}")
    client = openai.OpenAI(base_url=base, api_key=post("/key/generate", {"user_id": user_id})["key"], max_retries=0)
    for call in range(1, 4):
        try:
            client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-5.4-nano", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}])
            print(f"chat call {call} with the user's key: 200")
        except openai.APIStatusError as error:
            print(f"chat call {call} with the user's key: {error.status_code} {error.body['message']}")
            break
        time.sleep(3)
```

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Medium

- `/user/new` windows cap the user, not its personal auto key, so clearing the user unblocks it
  - Only keys show window usage, so a user's window spend has no read endpoint, same as teams
  - Older keys keep their own windows. A personal key moved into a team skips user windows, same as user `max_budget`
- Team keys and team JWTs skip user windows unless `apply_user_budget_to_team_keys` is on, same as user `max_budget`
- Team-key spend counts toward the user's windows and can block the user's personal keys, same as user `max_budget`
- A pre-existing gap in user `max_budget` also applies to user windows, and it went to security engineering
- No Admin UI editor for user windows yet

### Low

- SpendLogs reseed for a user scans by `user` with no index
- Windows added seconds after a call can miss that call's spend until it is written, and LIT-10468 tracks it
- No alert when a user window runs out, same as keys and teams
- A deleted user's window counters stay, so re-creating that id starts blocked until each window resets
- A bad default window duration like `banana` is stored, not rejected, like the scalar default `budget_duration`
- Racing all-users bulk updates queue on one lock, and one past the 5s transaction limit answers 500 and changes nobody

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

- `/user/new` windows go on the user, like its `max_budget`, and on the auto-created key only when it is a team key
  - Rejected: copying them to a personal key, which double-counts and survives a clear
  - Rejected: leaving a team key without them, since team keys skip user windows and the caps would never apply
- Clearing windows stores null
  - Rejected: storing `[]`, which reads differently from never set
- Editing windows keeps each stored `reset_at`
  - Rejected: recomputing resets on edit, which can skip a reset that is already due and keep the user blocked
- An all-users bulk update reads the users after it takes the users lock, keeps each user's own `reset_at`, writes every user in one transaction, and evicts and reports the users it read
  - Rejected: one shared value for all users, which restarts windows other users already used
  - Rejected: reading windows before the lock, which can write back resets another edit just changed
- Default windows from `default_internal_user_params` go on every new user row, from `/user/new`, JWT upsert, and team or org member add, each with its own `reset_at`
  - Rejected: only `/user/new` and JWT upsert, which left member-add users with no windows
- An all-users bulk `spend` reset clears each user's spend counter, like a single-user spend edit
  - Rejected: leaving the counters, which keeps reset users blocked by spend that was reset
- The all-users bulk reply returns each user's windows as parsed JSON, like `/user/info`
  - Rejected: the stored JSON string, which no other user endpoint returns
- The all-users window writes go through chunked `in` lists inside the one transaction
  - Rejected: one `in` list per window value, which Postgres rejects past 32,767 users
- A failed all-users bulk transaction answers 500 and changes no user
  - Rejected: the old per-user fallback, which wrote the newest user and then failed on every input
  - Rejected: a longer transaction limit, which keeps every user row locked longer and delays spend writes
- User windows use their own `spend:user_window:<id>:<duration>` counters
  - Rejected: `spend:user:<id>:window:<duration>`, which collides with a user named `<id>:window:<duration>`
- Team keys skip user windows the way they skip user `max_budget`
  - Rejected: enforcing them on team keys, which would differ from every other user budget

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

- [x] bdf6f9cea3 passes /live-pr-risk

<details><summary>Bugbot summary</summary>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches auth budget enforcement, Redis spend accounting, and DB migrations across the proxy spend path; incorrect counter keying or reset logic could block users incorrectly or allow budget bypass.
> 
> **Overview**
> Users can now carry **multiple concurrent budget windows** (`budget_duration` + `max_budget`) on their row, matching keys and teams. The schema adds a `budget_limits` JSONB column on `LiteLLM_UserTable`, wired through user models, repositories, and API types.
> 
> **Management**: `/user/new`, `/user/update`, and all-users bulk update validate windows, persist JSON with per-window `reset_at`, clear with `null`, and treat `budget_limits` as a protected field for non-admin self-updates. Personal auto-keys no longer inherit user windows (team auto-keys still get key windows when applicable). Defaults from `default_internal_user_params` apply on JWT upsert and member creation.
> 
> **Enforcement & spend**: Auth runs `_user_multi_budget_check` before the legacy single `max_budget` check; reservation and post-call accounting use dedicated Redis keys (`user_window_counter`). Window spend is seeded from spend logs by `user`, reseeded, reset by the budget job, and blocked when any window is exhausted (team-key behavior still gated by `apply_user_budget_to_team_keys`).
>

title: fix(azure): drop the traceback from stream-cut errors sent to clients and alerts
body:
When an Azure stream dropped mid-response, the client got a full Python traceback with server file paths, and the llm_exceptions Slack alert printed it 3 to 6 times

This PR makes the Azure connection error carry the error line alone, like OpenAI's. The client error, stream frame, and alert all come from that message, so none carry the traceback now

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- An Azure stream cut leaks a server traceback to API clients
- The same traceback floods the llm_exceptions alert

How it solves it:

- Azure's no-status connection error no longer appends the traceback

## User Flow

Before: a developer streaming from an Azure deployment through the proxy sees the server's traceback when Azure's stream drops

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` to an Azure OpenAI model
2. Azure's connection drops after the first chunks
3. The last SSE event is an error whose message holds `Traceback (most recent call last)` and the proxy's file paths, like `.../site-packages/aiohttp/client_proto.py`
4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions cut before its first chunk answers HTTP 500 with that traceback in the JSON body, and the admin's llm_exceptions alert prints it several times

After: the same cut gives the client and the alert the error line alone

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` to an Azure OpenAI model
2. Azure's connection drops after the first chunks
3. The last SSE event's message is just `litellm.APIConnectionError: AzureException APIConnectionError - Response payload is not completed: <TransferEncodingError: 400, message='Not enough data to satisfy transfer length header.'>`
4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/completions cut before its first chunk answers HTTP 500 with that line behind a `litellm.MidStreamFallbackError:` prefix, and neither it nor the alert has a traceback

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both legs boot `litellm --config config.yaml --port 29150 --num_workers 2` from their own tree and venv with no database, against a real Azure OpenAI `gpt-5.4-nano`. A small relay passes Azure's real stream through and closes the socket after the first text chunk (`azure-stream-cut-chat`) or right after the headers (`azure-stream-cut-first`). The `llm_exceptions` Slack alert posts to a local webhook so its text can be read. The config, relay, case script, and every raw response and alert are in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/b42e37c7e5a457437cdb0c057c6c7b7f)

The before leg ran at the PR's merge base fa79311dfc and the after leg at 9bfa38e56e

Last updated: 5b5b79ecd4. QA ran on 9bfa38e56e. Changes since QA: the Azure no-status branch names the exception type when the error message is empty (a47f63c456), then two test-only commits drop a fixture docstring and stop the /v1/completions route test from pinning the MidStreamFallbackError prefix. Proof remains valid because every case in the table carries a non-empty message, so its line is unchanged, and the last two commits touch tests only. Verification: the httpx reset case below ran fresh at fa79311dfc and a47f63c456, and the mapping and route tests pass

Tracebacks per case, counted from [the gist's files](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/b42e37c7e5a457437cdb0c057c6c7b7f)

| Case | Client before | Alert before | Client after | Alert after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chat, cut after first chunk | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| Chat, cut before first chunk | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| /v1/completions, cut after first chunk | 3 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| /v1/completions, cut before first chunk | 3 | 6 | 0 | 0 |
| /v1/messages, cut after first chunk | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| /v1/responses, cut before first chunk | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| OpenAI Python SDK chat, cut after first chunk | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| Chat, no cut (control) | 0 | no alert | 0 | no alert |

### Before (fa79311dfc)

1. `curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:29150/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"azure-stream-cut-chat","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 40, one number per line."}]}'`

## Tests

Mapping tests cover `azure` and `azure_text` on a cut stream's `httpx.ReadError`, one with an empty message. Two route tests stream Azure chat and text through respx, cut after the first chunk, and check the error frame holds the line alone. Each fails with its fix reverted

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

- Azure's connection error drops the traceback instead of redacting it
  - `redact_string` only masks secrets, so the frames and paths still went out
  - Moving it to `litellm_debug_info` would still print it in the alert
  - OpenAI's matching branch already carries no traceback
  - SDK callers still get the original traceback through exception chaining (`__context__`)
  - It covers every Azure error with no status code, internal bugs like a `KeyError` in stream parsing included, the same as OpenAI's branch
  - An error with an empty message shows its type name instead, as the Timeout branch already does
- The generic fallback for unmapped exceptions keeps its traceback
  - SDK callers rely on it for debugging (#4201), so providers that reach it, like Cohere and Vertex AI partner models, need their own fix
- Client error messages are not passed through the shared redactor at the route level
  - It also rewrites valid guardrail and hook messages ("Basic authentication", URLs) and drops hostnames and router notes, so it garbled real 400s on moderations and audio

</details>

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Medium

- The generic fallback keeps its traceback on purpose, so Cohere and Vertex AI partner stream cuts and other providers' internal errors still carry it. A follow-up is tracked

### Low

- /v1/completions still wraps a cut before the first chunk in MidStreamFallbackError, and its alert repeats the line, as on main. A follow-up is tracked
- Only Azure names the error type on a reset with no message. Other providers end the line in an empty cause. A follow-up is tracked
- The route tests run on httpx since respx cannot intercept aiohttp. The live run covers aiohttp
- Live /v1/completions cases ran on an Azure chat deployment, as the QA resource has no text model. Tests cover azure_text

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

The message is now **only** the upstream error text, or the exception type name when that text is empty—matching the lean OpenAI connection-error shape and keeping server paths out of SSE error frames, JSON errors, and `llm_exceptions` alerts.

title: test(otel): keep proxy startup out of the per-test timeout in the excluded services matrix
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

The OTEL excluded services matrix tests failed all at once in one scheduled run because the shared proxy took longer than each test's 120 second limit to start on a slow CI runner. This PR keeps proxy startup out of that limit, so each test body still gets its full 120 seconds and a proxy that never comes up still fails with a clear readiness error

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/328ac248b84245278aadd47842962355
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/328ac248b84245278aadd47842962355?variant=devin
Requested by: @yucheng-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- 85 matrix cases failed setup in scheduled run 215
- Proxy startup counted toward every test's 120s timeout
- Green runs already took about 80s to boot

How it solves it:

- Adds `func_only=True` to the file's 15 timeout marks
- Startup stays bounded by the harness readiness deadline

## CI evidence

- Failing job: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43517292776/job/132202376927 (85 cases, 15 test functions, setup Timeout >120s)
- The whole job ran slow. The median proxy boot went from 56s in green run 43489815036 to 81s in the red run, and 58 proxies in other files also took more than 120s to boot
- Slack triage thread: https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0C9S11M0NQ/p1794612358465899

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 54e3c416033f56768ebbd5fffa3c21f411580c7a. This is a test-only timeout scope change with no product code touched, so it is proven by forced red and green runs at 1 worker

Forced slow startup, a temporary 130s readiness gate with a 145s startup deadline, removed after the run

1. origin/main: `E   Failed: Timeout (>120.0s) from pytest-timeout.` 1 error in 126.58s
2. Fix: 1 passed in 144.45s
3. Fix with a proxy that never becomes ready: `AssertionError: Owned proxy readiness deadline exceeded` 1 error in 152.31s

Normal runs on the fix, `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions <file>`

1. Whole file: 96 passed in 868.28s
2. `test_unconfigured_tenant_trace_keeps_datastore_spans` 5 times: 36 passed each run
3. `make lint`: All checks passed

## Type

✅ Test
