title: fix(bedrock): stop naming typed tools on Bedrock invoke /v1/messages so toolset entries reach Claude
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Computer use and browser use with Claude on Bedrock Invoke failed on every request, because the gateway gave those tools a placeholder name that Bedrock refuses. Now only custom tools sent without a name get one, so the same request that works against Anthropic works against Bedrock Invoke too

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Computer and browser toolsets on Bedrock `/v1/messages` answer 400
- LiteLLM adds a placeholder name that Bedrock refuses on toolsets

How it solves it:

- Only nameless custom tools get the placeholder name
- Typed tools pass through untouched, toolsets included

## User Flow

Before: a developer running a computer-use agent on Claude through Bedrock gets a 400 on the first request

1. They POST http://litellm-domain/v1/messages for a `bedrock/invoke/` Claude model with `"tools": [{"type": "computer_toolset_20260801"}]` (or the browser toolset), streaming or not
2. LiteLLM answers 400 `name is not accepted on a toolset entry`, and the agent never starts

After: the same request reaches Claude, and the agent loop runs

1. They send the same POST http://litellm-domain/v1/messages
2. They get 200 with a `tool_use` block named `screenshot` carrying `toolset_name: computer` (or `browser`)
3. They send back the screenshot as a `tool_result` and get 200 with Claude's answer about the screen

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Last updated: dce672ad23. /live-pr-risk ran on f59780e753 and still applies, since the merge of main leaves the changed function's callers the same and every case below ran again at dce672ad23

Setup shared by both legs. Each leg is a proxy with 2 workers and no database, started with `litellm --config config.yaml --port $PORT --num_workers 2`, using AWS credentials for a Bedrock account in us-east-1 and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`. Before runs the merge base and After runs this branch's tip. Case 4 sends a 64x40 solid blue PNG as `$IMG`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: bedrock-claude-sonnet-5-5
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/invoke/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
```

The SDK loop case runs the computer toolset helper from the Anthropic TypeScript SDK, `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 1.8.0 (the latest release), on Node 24.19.0. The SDK's tool runner runs the turns on its own and sends back the real `tool_use` id. The `screenshot` member returns the same blue PNG, and the runner keeps its default settings. Install the SDK in an empty directory

```bash
npm init -y && npm install @anthropic-ai/sdk@1.8.0
```

Then save the PNG's base64 as `blue_screen.b64` and this program as `loop.mjs` in the same directory

<details>
<summary>loop.mjs</summary>

```js
import Anthropic from '@anthropic-ai/sdk';
import { BetaAbstractComputerToolset20260801 } from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/beta/toolsets/computer';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const blueScreen = readFileSync(process.env.SCREENSHOT_B64, 'utf8').trim();

class BlueDesktop extends BetaAbstractComputerToolset20260801 {
  screenshot() {
    return { data: blueScreen };
  }
}

const loggingFetch = async (url, init) => {
  const sent = JSON.parse(init.body);
  const toolResultIds = sent.messages.flatMap((m) => [m.content].flat()).filter((b) => b.type === 'tool_result');
  const res = await fetch(url, init);
  console.log(`POST ${new URL(url).pathname} tool_result ids ${JSON.stringify(toolResultIds.map((b) => b.tool_use_id))} -> HTTP ${res.status}`);
  return res;
};

const client = new Anthropic({ baseURL: process.env.LITELLM_URL, apiKey: process.env.LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, fetch: loggingFetch });
const desktop = new BlueDesktop();
console.log(`tools[0] ${JSON.stringify(desktop.toJSON())}`);

const runner = client.beta.messages.toolRunner({
  model: 'bedrock-claude-sonnet-5-5',
  max_tokens: 1024,
  tools: [desktop],
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Take a screenshot, then tell me in one sentence what color the screen is.' }],
});

try {
  for await (const message of runner) {
    for (const block of message.content) {
      console.log(block.type === 'text' ? `text: ${block.text}` : `${block.type} ${block.name} id ${block.id}`);
    }
  }
} catch (err) {
  console.log(`error: ${err.status} ${err.message}`);
}
```

</details>

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SDK computer toolset loop | 400, 400 | 400, 200, 200, "solid, bright blue" |
| Computer toolset | 400 | 200, `screenshot` |
| Browser toolset | 400 | 200, `screenshot` |
| Computer toolset, streaming | 400 | 200, `screenshot` |
| Second turn with screenshot | 400 | 200, "solid, bright blue" |
| Custom tool without a name | 200 | 200 |

### Before (5849906ddb)

#### Anthropic SDK computer toolset loop

1. Run the program

```bash
LITELLM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:26040 SCREENSHOT_B64=blue_screen.b64 node loop.mjs
```

2. Output


Notes from the QA run

- A toolset `tool_result` needs `toolset_name`, else Bedrock answers 400
  - That is Bedrock's rule, and this PR leaves it alone
- Responses keep `toolset_name` on `tool_use`, streaming included
- The SDK's first call asks for a thread and gets 400
  - Main answers that on Bedrock, and the SDK resends without one
- A nameless dated tool like `bash_20250124` still answers 400
  - The message is now Bedrock's `Field required`, the same as Anthropic

title: fix(proxy): list key and team aliases on /model_group/info and apply listing callbacks to them
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

When a key or team maps a model alias, pi, OpenCode and Codex launched through lite showed that alias with no context window or reasoning levels, because the proxy's model info route skipped the aliases its model list shows. Now the model info route lists every alias the model list shows, each with its target model's limits and reasoning levels. An alias to a paused, hidden or other-team model still gets no row, same as the model list

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `/model_group/info` skipped key aliases and team model aliases
- lite pi, OpenCode and Codex showed no limits or reasoning for them

How it solves it:

- `/model_group/info` now lists every alias `/v1/models` lists
- Each alias row carries its target model's info under the alias name
- A name a listing callback hides stays hidden even when it is also an alias, now on `/v1/models` and `/v1/models/{model_id}` too, where main still listed it
- Listing callbacks also judge an alias's unlisted target, and the alias gets its info only if kept. Main gave it none under a legacy callback

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

1. The fix is on the server. The clients only see the alias name, never its target, so they can't resolve it themselves, and any other client reading `/model_group/info` would still miss aliases
2. An alias row is a copy of its target's row with `model_group` set to the alias. `is_public_model_group` is worked out from the alias name, so an alias is public only when an admin made that name public
3. Listing callbacks, legacy or V2, judge the caller's own listed names once, agents included, plus each unlisted model that a listed name's key alias, team alias or `litellm.model_alias_map` entry sends requests to, and that model's router alias target. These targets skip the caller's access check. A listed name a callback hid never comes back as an alias row on `/v1/models`, `/v1/models/{model_id}` or `/model_group/info`, and an alias only resolves to a target the callback kept. A target the callback hid hides no listed name. Alias names the caller doesn't list are not offered to callbacks, same as main, so an allow-list callback never starts hiding an alias `/v1/models` shows, and the callback docstring now says so. A router alias whose target a callback hid stays hidden, but a key or team alias with the same name is listed by its own target, since that alias is what a request to the name uses
4. An alias to a paused, undiscoverable or other-team model gets no row, matching `/v1/models`, even when the key lists the paused model. A paused model stays listed, and when its name is also a key alias its row describes the alias target, matching `/v1/models` and where a request to that name goes
5. `GET /model_group/info?model_group=<alias>` returns the alias row, and offers listing callbacks only that name, the model the caller's aliases send it to, and its router alias target
6. Agent rows are unchanged and still come last
7. An alias target matches a team model by the name in the team's models list or by the model's public name, so a key that lists the internal routing key still gets the alias row. The team model's own row keeps the internal name, as on main

</details>

## User Flow

Before: a developer whose key maps the alias `my-sol` to `gpt-6.1-sol` gets a 128k window and no thinking in lite pi

1. They run `lite pi` with that key against https://litellm-domain
2. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/models lists `my-sol`, but GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info has no `my-sol` row
3. They type `/model my-sol` and press Shift+Tab to turn on thinking
4. pi shows `0.0%/128k` and "Current model does not support thinking"

After: the same alias gets its target's 922k window and reasoning levels

1. They run `lite pi` with that key against https://litellm-domain
2. GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info now has a `my-sol` row with `max_input_tokens` 922000 and five reasoning efforts
3. They type `/model my-sol` and press Shift+Tab to turn on thinking
4. pi shows `0.0%/922k` and "Thinking level: high", and a prompt gets a reply

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg booted one proxy with `--num_workers 2` from its own tree, on its own Postgres database with the same config and setup, and called the real OpenAI API. The clients were pi 1.5.2, Codex 0.169.0 and OpenCode 1.19.5, each launched through the same `lite` install and driven in its interactive TUI under tmux, with `LITELLM_PROXY_URL` set to the leg's proxy and `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` set to the key below. Only the proxy commit differs between the legs, since this PR does not touch `lite`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-6.1-sol
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
```

Setup used the master key on each proxy. `POST /key/generate` with `{"models":["gpt-6.1-sol"],"aliases":{"my-sol":"gpt-6.1-sol"}}` made the key alias key. `POST /team/new` with `{"models":["gpt-6.1-sol"],"model_aliases":{"team-sol":"gpt-6.1-sol"}}` and with `{"models":["gpt-6.1-sol","team-sol2"],"model_aliases":{"team-sol2":"gpt-6.1-sol"}}` made two teams, and `POST /key/generate` with `{"team_id":...}` made one key for each

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| pi on key alias | 128k, no thinking | 922k, thinking high |
| pi on team alias | 128k, no thinking | 922k, thinking high |
| pi on team alias to a team model | 128k, no thinking | 922k, thinking high |
| Codex on key alias | no effort picker | effort picker |
| OpenCode on key alias | no variants | variant picker |
| API, key alias | no `my-sol` row | `my-sol` row |
| API, team alias | no `team-sol` row | `team-sol` row |
| API, team-listed alias | `team-sol2` all null | `team-sol2` filled |
| API, one alias | empty | `my-sol` row |
| Chat through alias | `ok` | `ok` |
| Callback hides `secret-b`, alias `secret-b` | listed | hidden |
| Alias over a hidden router alias | no row | row |
| Callback on, team alias to unlisted model | no info, 404 | 272k, 200 |

title: fix(proxy): run baggage tag mappings and budget checks on /queue/chat/completions
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Queued chat calls skipped the baggage tag rules and auth checks that `/v1/chat/completions` runs. Now `/queue/chat/completions` runs the same checks and budget reservation, tags its spend row like chat, and bills a dropped stream for what it sent. Pre-call hooks, model group aliases, and `DISABLE_LLM_API_ENDPOINTS` still skip it

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `/queue/chat/completions` skipped `request_tag_mappings`, every budget check, and the request checks chat runs, and its spend got no mapped, key, or team tags
- A dropped queued stream was never billed, and a rejected queued call wrote no failure row

How it solves it:

- One route check, chat routes plus the queued route, gates those checks and budget reservation
- The queue handler copies the tags, and its stream uses chat's first-chunk step, so a dropped stream bills what it sent

Intentional product change: queued calls that break these rules are now rejected, as on `/v1/chat/completions`

## User Flow

Before: queued chat calls skip the baggage rules, budgets, and request checks an admin sets

1. The admin sets `request_tag_mappings` with a required `entrypoint` rule, `enforce_user_param`, and a proxy `max_budget`
2. A caller sends POST https://litellm-domain/queue/chat/completions with no `baggage` header, or no `user`, and gets a 200
3. A call with `baggage: entrypoint=queue_chat` gets a 200, but its spend log row has no `usecase:queue_chat` tag
4. With a $0.00001 budget on the tag, key, key tag, team, user, end user, or proxy, queued calls keep getting a 200
5. A streamed queued call the client drops adds nothing to the key's spend

After: queued chat calls follow the same rules as `/v1/chat/completions`

1. The admin sets the same settings
2. No `baggage` gets a 400 "Missing, invalid or unmapped baggage value for entrypoint", and no `user` a 401
3. The spend log row carries `usecase:queue_chat` plus the key and team tags
4. Once a budget is spent, the next queued call gets a 422 "Budget has been exceeded!", and `/spend/logs/ui` shows a failure row
5. The dropped stream's partial reply shows up in the key's spend, and the key's next call still gets a 200

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

- The queued route is not added to the LLM API route set
  - That set also decides which routes every virtual key may call by default, which is out of scope here, so keys still need `/queue/chat/completions` in `allowed_routes`
  - A new route check, chat routes plus `/queue/chat/completions`, feeds the inference checks instead
  - The checks it feeds are the baggage mapper, every budget check (proxy, key, team, user, end user, tag), `enforce_user_param`, `reject_clientside_metadata_tags`, the unpriced model block (also on a team member's model budget fallback), budget reservation, a team's `require_trace_id`, a JWT admin's `x-litellm-team-id`, and the failure logging for rejected calls
  - Key and team `model_group_alias` and the enterprise `DISABLE_LLM_API_ENDPOINTS` check stay on the old set. Switching the alias check alone would authorize the alias target while the queue handler routes the model the client sent, and the enterprise check ships in its own package
  - OAuth2 token introspection and the early key rejection that reads only headers stay on the old set too. Moving introspection would change which credentials the queued route accepts, so an OAuth2 token still gets a 401 there, and a blocked key on the queued route is still refused, only after its body is read
- Budget reservation is on for the queued route
  - The queue handler puts the key's reservation in its metadata, the same field chat uses, so the cost callback settles it
  - The hold is taken at auth, before the queue wait, and renewed while the call waits. Taking it when the scheduler picks the call was rejected, because the scheduler waits and calls the model in one step, and the hold at auth is what keeps a burst of parallel queued calls from overshooting a budget. The cost is that a burst can get 422s while earlier calls still wait
  - When the client leaves a queued stream, the partial reply is billed through the logging object, as chat does. A stream left before the first model chunk releases its reservation down to the input cost
  - The release runs after partial billing and only when no bill fired. A guardrail that buffers the stream can hold model chunks the client never saw, and the partial bill already settles those. Checking for buffered chunks before the release was rejected, because only the bill knows whether it fired, for chat chunks, Responses events, or a bill that failed
  - That release lives in `async_data_generator`, which chat and Responses API streams share too, so on those routes a stream the client leaves after a keepalive ping and before the first model chunk also gives its reservation back. Releasing only on the queued route was rejected, because a dropped chat or Responses stream that keeps its hold until the counter expires is the same bug, and the release still keeps the input cost
  - A call sent the instant a stream is dropped can still meet that stream's hold and get a 422, as on chat, since the hold is settled when the proxy notices the hang-up
  - A queued call cancelled while it waits for a worker gets its whole hold back, since no model call was made. One cancelled after the model call claimed the hold keeps the input cost, the same settlement as a stream dropped before its first chunk. Leaving it to the request-end release was rejected, because that release skips a hold the model call has already claimed
- The queue handler builds its stream with `create_response`, like chat
  - It reads the first chunk while watching for a hang-up, so a client that leaves before the first chunk cancels the provider call, and the response closes the stream as soon as the client leaves mid-stream. A bare `StreamingResponse` left that cleanup to garbage collection, so the partial bill came late, and a stream dropped before its first chunk kept its hold until the counter expired
  - A queued stream whose first chunk is an error now answers with that error's status and a JSON body, as chat does, where it used to send an SSE error frame under a 200. Keeping the 200 on the queued route alone was rejected, because a client would then need two error paths for the same model call
- The queue handler reads the trace headers and sets the call ID, as chat does
  - The spend row keeps the `x-litellm-trace-id` that a team's `require_trace_id` asks for, and a queued response carries `x-litellm-call-id`, also in an error body when `include_call_id_in_error_body` is on
  - A queued call takes the caller's `x-litellm-call-id` as its call ID, as chat does. Ignoring the header was rejected, because one call traced across both routes would then get two IDs
- The queue handler merges tags the way chat does
  - Request `metadata.tags`, then key and team tags, then the caller's body `tags` or `x-litellm-tags` header, without duplicates
  - It also sets `inherited_tags`, so tag-based routing treats key and team tags as the admin's, not the caller's
  - With tag filtering on, key and team tags now narrow which deployments serve a queued call, as on chat. Merging them for budgets only and leaving routing alone was rejected, because chat puts them in `metadata.tags` where tag routing reads them, so the two routes would pick deployments differently
  - The caller's `litellm_metadata` is folded into `metadata` and dropped, as on chat, after proxy-owned fields (`user_api_key_*` and internal control fields) are stripped from both. That stops a caller from setting the queued spend row's org ID. Leaving the bucket in place was rejected, because routing reads `litellm_metadata` when it exists, so an empty one hid the key and team tags
- Pre-call hooks (guardrails, rate limits) still do not run on the queued route
  - The queue handler never ran them before this PR either, and wiring them in changes much more than the auth checks

</details>

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg ran two proxy processes with 2 uvicorn workers each, sharing one Postgres and one Redis, against real OpenAI, OpenRouter, and Gemini, alternating calls

<details>
<summary>Config, command, and case setup</summary>

Before ran on ports 25590 and 30108, After on 20827 and 20313. Env vars `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_HOST` and `REDIS_PORT` are set

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port> --num_workers 2 --timeout_worker_healthcheck 60 --telemetry False --use_prisma_db_push
```

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: litellm-qa-baggage-nano
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-nano
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: litellm-qa-unpriced
    litellm_params:
      model: openrouter/mistralai/mistral-nemo
      api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY

litellm_settings:
  block_requests_for_models_without_pricing: true

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  enforce_user_param: true
  reject_clientside_metadata_tags: true
  request_tag_mappings:
    - key: entrypoint
      tag_prefix: "usecase:"
      required: true
    - key: budgeted
      tag_prefix: "budgeted:"
      require_budgeted_tag: true
```

Both legs restarted with the OpenRouter alias before the unpriced and key tag cases. The proxy budget case ran on a second pair of legs (Before 25699 and 28806, After 24135 and 21617) that also set these

```yaml
litellm_settings:
  block_requests_for_models_without_pricing: true
  max_budget: 0.00001
  budget_duration: 30d
```

Calls send `"priority": 0` and `"user"` unless the case drops it. A minted key goes into `$QA_KEY` with the route in `allowed_routes`, and budget calls run 4 seconds apart

The tag routing, provider error, and admin JWT cases ran on a third pair of legs (Before 21311 and 28858, After 30846 and 28680) with no Redis, `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL` also set, and this config. The admin JWT carries the `litellm_proxy_admin` scope and goes into `$QA_JWT`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: litellm-qa-tagged
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-nano
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
      tags: ["qa-route-nano"]
  - model_name: litellm-qa-tagged
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
      tags: ["default"]
```

title: fix(responses): accept a string or tuple allowed_openai_params on Responses models instead of answering 500
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Since #47432, a chat or /v1/messages request to a Responses API model whose `allowed_openai_params` is a string or a tuple answers 500 "can only concatenate list" instead of the reply. This makes those requests answer 200 again, and a string like `"presence_penalty"` or `"seed, presence_penalty"` now allowlists every param it names everywhere, the router included, while a dict keeps allowlisting its keys. It also gives the unsupported-param 400 a real `response`, so SDK code reading `error.response` no longer crashes

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A string or tuple allowlist on a Responses-mode model answers 500
- A string allowlisted nothing, so a param that needs it still got a 400
- Sync SDK code reading `error.response` on an unsupported param crashes

How it solves it:

- One shared reader turns the allowlist into param names on every path, the router included. A string is read for every name in it and a dict for its keys
- `UnsupportedParamsError` now builds its response like every other 400

## User Flow

Before: a team whose deployments list `allowed_openai_params` as a string gets a 500 on Responses-mode models and a 400 on Mistral

1. The proxy admin's config has an `openai/responses/gpt-5.6-luna` deployment with `allowed_openai_params: "prompt_cache_key"` and a `mistral/mistral-large-latest` deployment with `allowed_openai_params: "presence_penalty"`
2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to the OpenAI one with `prompt_cache_key`, streaming or not, or the same request to /v1/messages
3. The proxy answers 500 "can only concatenate list (not "str") to list"
4. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions to the Mistral one with `presence_penalty: 0.5`
5. The proxy answers 400 "mistral does not support parameters: ['presence_penalty']", even though the config allowlists it

After: the same requests come back 200 with the model's reply

1. The proxy admin's config has the same two deployments
2. A developer sends the same requests to the OpenAI one
3. The proxy answers 200 with the reply
4. The developer sends the same request to the Mistral one with `presence_penalty: 0.5`
5. The proxy answers 200 with Mistral's reply

## Affected release

The 500 on chat and /v1/messages is a regression since v1.109.0-rc.1, the first release with #47432. A direct /v1/responses call with a string allowlist has answered 500 since 1.76.0

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-9350

- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg booted one proxy from the merge base `35b9df1f40` (Before) and from `20be987746` (After), with the same config and the same requests. The OpenAI cases are real calls to `gpt-5.6-luna`, the Mistral cases to `mistral-large-latest` on api.mistral.ai, and the embeddings cases to `gemini-embedding-2` on Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint

Each proxy ran `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <port> --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver` from its tree, with `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` set. The timeout case sends a `timeout: 2` deployment to a local socket that never answers, then falls back to a real `gpt-5.6-luna`. Each leg had its own Redis behind `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`. Neither proxy printed the "workers flag is ignored" warning or reloaded, and 24 open keep-alive connections showed both worker PIDs serving on each leg. No database was attached

| Case | What it sends | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| chat-string | string in request, chat | 500 | 200 |
| chat-string-stream | same, streaming | 500 | 200 |
| chat-deployment-string | string in config, chat | 500 | 200 |
| responses-string | string in request, /v1/responses | 500 | 200 |
| messages-deployment-string | string in config, /v1/messages | 500 | 200 |
| mistral-request-string | string in request, Mistral | 400 | 200 |
| mistral-deployment-string | string in config, Mistral | 400 | 200 |
| mistral-responses-string | string, Mistral /v1/responses | 400 | 200 |
| mistral-forwarding-probe | string, `presence_penalty: 5` | 400 LiteLLM | 422 Mistral |
| mistral-no-allowlist-control | no allowlist (control) | 400 | 400 |
| mistral-comma-allowlist | `"seed, presence_penalty"` | 400 | 200 |
| mistral-dict-allowlist | dict allowlist (control) | 200 | 200 |
| tier-param-request-string | tier pins `presence_penalty: 5`, string in request | 200, dropped | 422 Mistral |
| tier-param-deployment-string | same, string in config | 200, dropped | 422 Mistral |
| mistral-space-allowlist | `"seed presence_penalty"` | 400 | 200 |
| mistral-letter-n | `n: 2` with `"reasoning_effort"` | 200 | 400, as decided |
| chat-bridge-unsupported-string | string, chat to a Responses model | 400 | 200 |
| embeddings-space-string | `"dimensions encoding_format"` | 200 | 200 |
| embeddings-json-list-string | `'["dimensions"]'` | 200 | 200 |
| embeddings-no-allowlist-control | no allowlist (control) | 400 | 400 |
| fallback-errors-header | header `type` (control) | `UnsupportedParamsError` | `UnsupportedParamsError` |
| fallback-timeout-header | timeout, then fallback (control) | `None` | `None` |
| sdk-tuple | SDK tuple allowlist | APIConnectionError | reply |
| sdk-sync-error-response | SDK reads `error.response` | AttributeError | 400 response |

<details>
<summary>Config, case script, SDK scripts, and worker check</summary>

The codestral case runs the SDK against a real Azure-hosted Mistral endpoint, which LiteLLM rejects with a 400 before sending, and reads `QA_AZURE_MISTRAL_BASE` and `QA_AZURE_MISTRAL_KEY`. `hang_server.py` accepts connections and never answers. The config skips `dev_config.yaml`, whose `drop_params: true` hides this 400

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A string or dict allowlist now changes traffic on router paths that ignored it. A tier param that was dropped is now sent, so `tier-param-*` went from 200 to Mistral's 422, and the pre-call filters keep a deployment whose allowlist names the param. Each change makes the allowlist do what it says, as Design decisions records

### Low

- Pickling `UnsupportedParamsError` now works but doubles the prefix in `args[0]`, while `.message` and `str()` stay correct. Every other LiteLLM exception still fails to unpickle, as it did before

<details>
<summary>Design decisions</summary>

A string allowlist is read for every param name in it on every path, so `"presence_penalty"`, `"seed, presence_penalty"`, `"seed presence_penalty"`, and a list written as a string, `'["dimensions"]'`, all allowlist the names they hold. Reading it letter by letter was rejected because it silently allowlists nothing, which is what chat and the Responses API did before, and the router ignored a string outright. That letter reading did let any string with an `n` in it, like `"reasoning_effort"`, allowlist `n`. Keeping that was rejected because it allowlists a param nobody named, so such a request with `n: 2` now gets the same 400 as one with no allowlist. Embeddings used to accept `dimensions` anywhere inside the string, and it now needs `dimensions` as a whole name. Answering 400 for a string or dict was rejected because configs that hold one already work on chat or embeddings and would start failing. A dict is read for its keys, the way chat and embeddings read one before. The router now reads the allowlist the same way, so a tier param or a deployment filter that a string or dict allowlist names is kept, where the router used to drop the param or filter the deployment out. Keeping the router on lists only was rejected because the same config would then allow a param on chat and drop it in routing. A list, tuple, set, or frozenset is read for its string entries, and a list entry is not split because no path split it before. Anything else, such as a number, allowlists nothing

`UnsupportedParamsError` now calls the `BadRequestError` constructor, so it gets `response`, `body`, `request`, and `request_id` like every other 400 LiteLLM raises. Setting only `response` was rejected because callers of the OpenAI error types also read the other fields. The message keeps its `litellm.UnsupportedParamsError:` prefix, `status_code` stays 400, and `args` holds that same message. The fallback errors header names `UnsupportedParamsError` by its class, as before, even though that error now inherits `type = None`, and every other error keeps the `type` it carries, so a timeout still shows "None". Using the class name for every error with an empty `type` was rejected because it changed the header for errors this PR does not touch. Setting `type` on `UnsupportedParamsError` was rejected because `type` carries the provider error body's type, and the proxy's 400 body would then say `UnsupportedParamsError` instead of `invalid_request_error`

`BadRequestError` now types `message` as `str` and `model` and `llm_provider` as `str | None`, which the type gate needed once the subclass called its constructor. Two callers passed a value read from an untyped dict, so the router's multi-team 400 and the deployment hook's malformed-field 400 now pass `None` for `model` when that value is not a string. Passing the raw value through was rejected because the error's `model` is a string everywhere else, and both values are strings on every real request

</details>

title: fix(gemini): stream TTS audio in delta.audio on chat completions
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Streaming a Gemini text-to-speech model through chat completions returned no audio, because the proxy dropped every audio slice Google sent and only the final empty stop chunk reached the client. Now each slice reaches the client in the same streamed audio field OpenAI's own audio models use, on both the AI Studio and Vertex routes. With message logging turned off, the response object handed to logging callbacks now drops that audio too, which it did not before

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Streamed Gemini TTS on chat completions returns zero audio
- Only an empty `{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}` chunk arrives
- With message logging off, callback response objects still carry the clip

How it solves it:

- Each streamed audio slice goes out as `delta.audio = {"data": ...}`
- Matches OpenAI's streamed audio chunk shape, so SDKs read it as is
- Callback response objects drop `audio` when message logging is off

## User Flow

Before: a developer streaming Gemini text-to-speech through the proxy gets an empty stream, so their player has nothing to play

1. They point the OpenAI Python SDK at `https://litellm-domain/v1` and call `chat.completions.create` with a Gemini TTS model (AI Studio or Vertex), `modalities=["audio"]`, `audio={"voice": "Kore", "format": "pcm16"}`, `stream=True`
2. The SSE stream from `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` holds one chunk, `{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}`
3. No chunk ever has `delta.audio`, so they collect 0 bytes of audio, though the same call without `stream` returns `message.audio.data`

After: the same streamed call delivers the speech slice by slice

1. They point the OpenAI Python SDK at `https://litellm-domain/v1` and call `chat.completions.create` with a Gemini TTS model (AI Studio or Vertex), `modalities=["audio"]`, `audio={"voice": "Kore", "format": "pcm16"}`, `stream=True`
2. The stream carries dozens of chunks, each audio one with `delta.audio.data` holding a base64 slice of 24 kHz PCM16, then `finish_reason: "stop"`
3. Joining the slices gives about 3 s of non-silent 24 kHz PCM16 audio for a one-line prompt, which saves as a WAV

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10182

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both legs run the same 2-worker proxy (`--num_workers 2`, no DB), differing only in the commit it booted from, and the same client scripts on the OpenAI Python SDK 3.41.0. Env vars are `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `VERTEXAI_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`

```yaml
  - model_name: gemini-tts
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-3.8-flash-tts
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
  - model_name: vertex-tts
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash-tts
      vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT
      vertex_location: global
      vertex_credentials: os.environ/GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

<details>
<summary>tts_stream_client.py</summary>

```python
import base64
import os
import sys
import wave

import openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url=os.environ["PROXY_URL"], api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"])
model = sys.argv[1]
out_path = sys.argv[2]
print(f"openai SDK {openai.__version__}, model {model}")
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=model,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say cheerfully: Have a wonderful day!"}],
    modalities=["audio"],
    audio={"voice": "Kore", "format": "pcm16"},
    stream=True,
)
chunks = 0
pcm = b""
finish_reasons = []
for chunk in stream:
    chunks += 1
    for choice in chunk.choices:
        if choice.finish_reason:
            finish_reasons.append(choice.finish_reason)
        audio = choice.delta.audio
        if audio is not None and audio.data:
            pcm += base64.b64decode(audio.data)
with wave.open(out_path, "wb") as wav:
    wav.setnchannels(1)
    wav.setsampwidth(2)
    wav.setframerate(24000)
    wav.writeframes(pcm)
print(f"stream: {chunks} chunks, finish_reason={finish_reasons}, {len(pcm)} PCM bytes = {len(pcm) / 48000:.2f} s of 24 kHz mono audio")
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Ticket curl setup, config and stream reader</summary>

```yaml

  - model_name: gemini-2.5-pro-tts
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-pro-tts
      vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT
      vertex_location: us-central1
      vertex_credentials: os.environ/GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

```bash
  "model": "gemini-2.5-pro-tts",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "Read the dialogue verbatim. Two speakers: Alex uses Leda, Sam uses Charon."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Alex: Does streaming return audio?\nSam: Let'"'"'s find out.\n"}
  ],
  "modalities": ["audio"],
  "speechConfig": {"multiSpeakerVoiceConfig": {"speakerVoiceConfigs": [
    {"speaker": "Alex", "voiceConfig": {"prebuiltVoiceConfig": {"voiceName": "Leda"}}},
    {"speaker": "Sam", "voiceConfig": {"prebuiltVoiceConfig": {"voiceName": "Charon"}}}
  ]}},
  "stream": true
}' > stream.sse
```

```python
import base64
import json
import sys

events = [line[len("data: "):] for line in sys.stdin.read().splitlines() if line.startswith("data: ")]
chunks = [json.loads(e) for e in events if e != "[DONE]"]
deltas = [choice["delta"] for chunk in chunks for choice in chunk["choices"]]
audio = [d["audio"]["data"] for d in deltas if (d.get("audio") or {}).get("data")]
pcm = b"".join(base64.b64decode(a) for a in audio)
finish = [c["finish_reason"] for chunk in chunks for c in chunk["choices"] if c.get("finish_reason")]
print(f"first chunk: {json.dumps(chunks[0])[:200]}")
print(f"{len(chunks)} chunks, {len(audio)} with delta.audio.data, finish_reason={finish}, done={events[-1] == '[DONE]'}")
print(f"{len(pcm)} PCM bytes = {len(pcm) / 48000:.2f} s of 24 kHz mono audio")
```

</details>

```python
response = client.chat.completions.create(**request)
audio = response.choices[0].message.audio
print(f"non-stream: client got {len(base64.b64decode(audio.data)) if audio else 0} PCM bytes")
pcm = b""
for chunk in client.chat.completions.create(**request, stream=True):
    for choice in chunk.choices:
        if choice.delta.audio is not None and choice.delta.audio.data:
            pcm += base64.b64decode(choice.delta.audio.data)
print(f"stream: client got {len(pcm)} PCM bytes")
```

```python
import json
import os

from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger


def _audio_chars(response):
    choices = getattr(response, "choices", None) or []
    message = getattr(choices[0], "message", None) if choices else None
    audio = getattr(message, "audio", None)
    if audio is None:
        return 0
    data = audio.get("data") if isinstance(audio, dict) else getattr(audio, "data", None)
    return len(data or "")


class AudioSeenByCallback(CustomLogger):
    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        streamed = kwargs.get("async_complete_streaming_response")
        choices = getattr(response_obj, "choices", None) or []
        message = getattr(choices[0], "message", None) if choices else None
        line = {
            "model": kwargs.get("model"),
            "stream": bool(kwargs.get("stream")),
            "response_obj_content": getattr(message, "content", None),
            "response_obj_audio_b64_chars": _audio_chars(response_obj),
            "complete_streaming_response_audio_b64_chars": None if streamed is None else _audio_chars(streamed),
        }
        with open(os.environ["AUDIO_SEEN_LOG"], "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(line) + "\n")


proxy_handler_instance = AudioSeenByCallback()
```

</details>

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 3 of 4 -->

### Medium

- With message logging off, callbacks still get the raw clip in `original_response`
  - Non-streamed calls only. The raw Google body keeps the audio there
  - Predates this PR, leaks reply text the same way, and is tracked separately
  - The proof's callback rows check only the response object

### Low

- Logged streamed clips get a 1-hour `expires_at`, non-streamed ones 24 hours
- With message logging on, streamed TTS logs now carry the whole base64 clip
  - Non-streamed calls already did, about 200 KB of base64 per 3 s clip
- The logging-off audio drop covers every provider, not only Gemini
  - The standard logging payload already dropped audio

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

- Streamed `delta.audio` carries only `data`
  - Matches OpenAI's streamed chunks, where `id` appears once and `expires_at` on the last chunk
  - Rejected a fresh id and expiry per chunk, since one clip would carry many ids
  - Rejected a per-stream id kept on the iterator. Gemini has no audio id to reference, so it would be made up
  - `stream_chunk_builder` already fills `id` and `expires_at` when it rebuilds `message.audio`
- The delta is a plain dict, not the `ChatCompletionAudioResponse` object
  - The chunk builder reads streamed audio as a dict, and the object made it raise
- One audio part per streamed event, same as the non-streaming path
  - Live Gemini streams sent exactly one audio part per event on both models tested
- Message logging off drops `audio` from logged message and delta objects
  - The dict path already dropped it, so the object path now matches
  - Applies to every provider's audio, OpenAI and Azure audio models included
  - This also stops the non-streamed clip reaching callbacks, a leak that predates this PR
  - Rejected keeping audio in logs, since a spoken clip is message content like text
  - Reuses the existing `_drop_field_when_present` helper, so the client response is untouched
- With message logging on, logged streamed responses keep the rebuilt clip
  - Same as non-streamed calls and OpenAI's streamed audio
  - Rejected always stripping audio from logs, since operators who want no content turn message logging off
- `original_response` is left as is here
  - The Responses bridge reads it from the live logging data after the provider call, so redacting it there breaks that bridge with logging off
  - A safe fix needs a redacted copy for each callback, a change to every provider's logging that belongs in its own PR
- The `expires_at` gap above stays as is
  - Gemini stores no audio, so neither expiry points at anything a client can fetch
  - Aligning them means a made-up expiry per chunk or a new chunk builder default for every provider

</details>

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Kimi K3 on Azure AI Foundry forgot its own thinking after each tool call in Claude Code, and the gateway refused or dropped its reasoning effort. Now the effort and Kimi's earlier reasoning both reach Foundry

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Kimi's `reasoning_content` was stripped from replayed history, so Kimi forgot its own reasoning after each tool call
- `reasoning_effort` answered 400 for every non-GPT `azure_ai` model. Claude Code never saw it, since this line keeps `drop_params` on for it and drops the effort silently

How it solves it:

- A Foundry model whose cost map row lists levels takes `reasoning_effort`, and a deployment under its own name is matched through `base_model`
- On chat the level goes out as the caller wrote it, and `"default"` leaves it to the model
- Any other value answers 400, or is dropped with a warning under `drop_params`
- Fireworks-hosted `FW-` models and Foundry's `kimi-` models, named directly or through `base_model`, keep `reasoning_content` in history
- This is the `lts/1.108.x` copy of #51747, which merges first

<details>
<summary>Decisions made on purpose, with what was rejected</summary>

- The gate reads the cost map as loaded, not the live model map. A router copies one deployment's `model_info` onto the shared `azure_ai/<model>` row, so the live map would let one deployment's levels open `reasoning_effort` for an undeclared sibling. Gating on every `FW-` model with `supports_reasoning` was also rejected, since it would send the param to models nobody checked
- The level goes out unchanged. Foundry Kimi K3 answers 200 for `auto`, `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`, though its cost map row lists only `low`, `high` and `max`. Rounding onto the row was rejected, since it sent `medium` as `high` and spent more reasoning than the caller asked for. On /v1/messages the Anthropic adapter still moves `xhigh` down to `high` and `minimal` up to `low`, the nearest levels the row lists, before this code runs, as it does for every provider, and this PR leaves that step alone
- `"default"` sends no level, so the model picks its own. Any other string, such as `"High"`, answers 400 naming the eight levels, or is dropped with a warning under `drop_params`, because Foundry rejects it with "did not match any variant of untagged enum ReasoningEffort"
- An effort object such as `{"effort": "low", "summary": "detailed"}` sends its level and logs a warning naming the other fields it dropped. A 400 for `summary` was rejected, since the Anthropic adapter adds `summary` itself when `reasoning_auto_summary` is on, so it would break Claude Code on those proxies
- The cost map lookup matches `azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3` in any case and with or without the `azure_ai/` prefix, since Foundry deployment names are case-insensitive
- A deployment under its own name is read through its `base_model`, for both the effort gate and the `FW-` replay check, the way the proxy prices it. Ignoring `base_model` was rejected, since it quietly dropped the effort for a renamed Kimi deployment under `drop_params`
- `reasoning_content` is kept only for models whose name or `base_model` starts with `FW-` or `kimi-` (any case). Fireworks documents replaying it for its reasoning models (https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/reasoning), and native `fireworks_ai` has replayed it since #40682. Foundry's MoonshotAI-format Kimi models read it back too. Other Foundry backends can reject it with "Extra inputs are not permitted". Keeping it for Kimi only was rejected. Every `FW-` model Foundry still deploys on a standard SKU, six cost map rows besides Kimi K3 plus `FW-Kimi-K3.1-Pro`, answered 200 with the replayed field before and after this change, and four of the seven used it. The other 13 `FW-` cost map rows are deprecated or provisioned-only on Foundry and cannot be newly deployed to check. The effort gate stays narrower, since a level a model does not take answers 400, while a model that ignores replayed reasoning still answers 200
- Levels a deployment declares in `model_info.reasoning_effort_levels` are not read on this line, since that path from #46601 is only on main. A Kimi deployment under another name gets its levels through `base_model`
- Moonshot's `fill_reasoning_content` placeholder and its fixed `temperature` and `top_p` were not copied, since Foundry Kimi K3 answers 200 without replayed reasoning and with `temperature` 0.2 and `top_p` 0.5
- This replaces #36919, which shaped Kimi by model name across chat and the Messages to Responses bridge and has been idle since September
- On `lts/1.108.x` the helpers live in `litellm/router_utils/reasoning_effort_capability.py`. The tests seed the loaded cost map through `get_model_cost_map` with a mock client and reload the bundled map afterwards, since this line has no `install_model_cost_map`
- `make check` against `lts/1.108.x` reports one ruff I001 in `litellm/main.py`, a file this PR leaves as the base has it, and the base fails the same way
- On the line, `test_azure_ai_claude_messages_filters_auto_injected_betas_by_azure_support` fails at the base too, because the line fetches main's beta-header map, which now forwards `compact-2026-01-12` for azure_ai. This PR does not touch that path

</details>

## User Flow

Before: in Claude Code on Kimi K3 through the proxy, Kimi forgets its own reasoning across tool calls, and no reasoning effort reaches it

1. They point Claude Code at the proxy with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and run `claude --model FW-Kimi-K3`
2. They ask Kimi to decide a secret code in its thinking, read NOTES.md, then reveal the code
3. After the file read, Kimi reveals a different code than the one its thinking picked
4. A curl or SDK client that sends `reasoning_effort` gets 400 "azure_ai does not support parameters: ['reasoning_effort']". Claude Code's effort is dropped without a word

After: Kimi remembers what it decided, and the effort level reaches Foundry

1. They start Claude Code and send the same prompt as before
2. After the file read, Kimi reveals the exact code its thinking picked
3. The same requests with `reasoning_effort` low, medium, max or "default", and /v1/messages with thinking, return 200


Claude Code v2.1.299 ran interactively in tmux in a folder holding only NOTES.md ("The deploy target for this project is eu-west-3 and the owner is the payments team.")

```shell

```

The `kimi-renamed` run starts it with `claude --model kimi-renamed` instead

The prompt, typed into the TUI, was "Before you do anything, silently invent a random 8-character code made of uppercase letters and digits, decide on it once, and keep it only in your thinking, never in your visible reply. Then read NOTES.md. After reading it, tell me the deploy region and reveal the exact code you invented before reading the file." Ctrl+O opened the transcript view that shows the thinking. The `drop_params: false` runs add this to config.yaml, because the proxy otherwise turns `drop_params` on for Claude Code

```yaml
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: false
```

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Kimi K3 on Azure AI Foundry forgot its own thinking after each tool call in Claude Code, and the gateway refused or dropped its reasoning effort. Now the effort and Kimi's earlier reasoning both reach Foundry

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Kimi's `reasoning_content` was stripped from replayed history, so Kimi forgot its own reasoning after each tool call
- `reasoning_effort` answered 400 for every non-GPT `azure_ai` model. Claude Code hid it because the proxy turns on `drop_params` for it, which dropped the effort silently

How it solves it:

- A Foundry model whose cost map row lists levels takes `reasoning_effort`, and a deployment under its own name is matched through `base_model`
- On chat the level goes out as the caller wrote it, and `"default"` leaves it to the model
- Any other value answers 400, or is dropped with a warning under `drop_params`
- Fireworks-hosted `FW-` models and Foundry's `kimi-` models, named directly or through `base_model`, keep `reasoning_content` in history
- The same fix for `lts/1.108.x` is #51748, which merges right after this one

<details>
<summary>Decisions made on purpose, with what was rejected</summary>

- The gate reads the cost map as loaded, not the live model map. A router copies one deployment's `model_info` onto the shared `azure_ai/<model>` row, so the live map would let one deployment's levels open `reasoning_effort` for an undeclared sibling. Gating on every `FW-` model with `supports_reasoning` was also rejected, since it would send the param to models nobody checked
- The level goes out unchanged. Foundry Kimi K3 answers 200 for `auto`, `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`, though its cost map row lists only `low`, `high` and `max`. Rounding onto the row was rejected, since it sent `medium` as `high` and spent more reasoning than the caller asked for. On /v1/messages the Anthropic adapter still moves `xhigh` down to `high` and `minimal` up to `low`, the nearest levels the row lists, before this code runs, as it does for every provider, and this PR leaves that step alone
- `"default"` sends no level, so the model picks its own. Any other string, such as `"High"`, answers 400 naming the eight levels, or is dropped with a warning under `drop_params`, because Foundry rejects it with "did not match any variant of untagged enum ReasoningEffort"
- An effort object such as `{"effort": "low", "summary": "detailed"}` sends its level and logs a warning naming the other fields it dropped. A 400 for `summary` was rejected, since the Anthropic adapter adds `summary` itself when `reasoning_auto_summary` is on, so it would break Claude Code on those proxies
- The cost map lookup matches `azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3` in any case and with or without the `azure_ai/` prefix, since Foundry deployment names are case-insensitive
- A deployment under its own name is read through its `base_model`, for both the effort gate and the `FW-` replay check, the way the proxy prices it. Ignoring `base_model` was rejected, since it quietly dropped the effort for a renamed Kimi deployment under `drop_params`
- `reasoning_content` is kept only for models whose name or `base_model` starts with `FW-` or `kimi-` (any case). Fireworks documents replaying it for its reasoning models (https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/reasoning), and native `fireworks_ai` has replayed it since #40682. Foundry's MoonshotAI-format Kimi models read it back too. Other Foundry backends can reject it with "Extra inputs are not permitted". Keeping it for Kimi only was rejected. Every `FW-` model Foundry still deploys on a standard SKU, six cost map rows besides Kimi K3 plus `FW-Kimi-K3.1-Pro`, answered 200 with the replayed field before and after this change, and three of the seven used it. The other 13 `FW-` cost map rows are deprecated or provisioned-only on Foundry and cannot be newly deployed to check. The effort gate stays narrower, since a level a model does not take answers 400, while a model that ignores replayed reasoning still answers 200
- A deployment's own `model_info.reasoning_effort_levels` stays with the shared router path from #46601. That path now sees `reasoning_effort` as supported for Kimi K3, so the #46601 test in `tests/unit/test_main.py` now expects the level forwarded unchanged instead of dropped
- Moonshot's `fill_reasoning_content` placeholder and its fixed `temperature` and `top_p` were not copied, since Foundry Kimi K3 answers 200 without replayed reasoning and with `temperature` 0.2 and `top_p` 0.5
- This replaces #36919, which shaped Kimi by model name across chat and the Messages to Responses bridge and has been idle since September

</details>

## User Flow

Before: in Claude Code on Kimi K3 through the proxy, Kimi forgets its own reasoning across tool calls, and no reasoning effort reaches it

1. They point Claude Code at the proxy with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and run `claude --model FW-Kimi-K3`
2. They ask Kimi to decide a secret code in its thinking, read NOTES.md, then reveal the code
3. After the file read, Kimi reveals a different code than the one its thinking picked
4. With `drop_params: false` in the proxy config, the first prompt fails with "API Error: 400 ... azure_ai does not support parameters: ['reasoning_effort']". Curl and SDK clients get it by default

After: Kimi remembers what it decided, and the effort level reaches Foundry

1. They start Claude Code and send the same prompt as before
2. After the file read, Kimi reveals the exact code its thinking picked
3. With `drop_params: false`, the same prompt succeeds, and chat `reasoning_effort` low, medium, max or "default" returns 200

Claude Code v2.1.299 ran interactively in tmux in a folder holding only NOTES.md ("The deploy target for this project is eu-west-3 and the owner is the payments team.")

```shell
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY claude --model FW-Kimi-K3
```

The `kimi-renamed` run starts it with `claude --model kimi-renamed` instead

The prompt, typed into the TUI, was "Before you do anything, silently invent a random 8-character code made of uppercase letters and digits, decide on it once, and keep it only in your thinking, never in your visible reply. Then read NOTES.md. After reading it, tell me the deploy region and reveal the exact code you invented before reading the file." Ctrl+O opened the transcript view that shows the thinking. The `drop_params: false` runs add this to config.yaml, because the proxy otherwise turns `drop_params` on for Claude Code

```yaml
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: false
```

title: fix(proxy): preserve caller metadata on auth failures
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Preserves x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata when requests fail authentication, including invalid keys and exceeded budgets
- Makes that metadata available in failure spend logs and callbacks across Chat Completions, Responses, and Messages
- Keeps existing error responses and successful-request behavior unchanged
- Adds regression tests using the real spend writer, covering header precedence, missing or malformed headers, and cleanup

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Auth rejections drop caller request markers from spend logs

How it solves it:

- Read the metadata header before logging an auth failure
- Preserve metadata for the logger and route callbacks
- Test the resulting failure row and unchanged authentication errors

## User Flow

Before, the budget rejection loses the caller's request marker

1. Create a key with a small budget and send POST http://localhost:4391/v1/chat/completions with a metadata header
2. The call returns 200 and its spend log retains the marker
3. Send another marked request after the key exceeds its budget and receive HTTP 422
4. GET http://localhost:4391/spend/logs/v2 shows a failure row without the marker

After, the budget rejection retains the caller's request marker

1. Create a key with a small budget and send POST http://localhost:4391/v1/chat/completions with a metadata header
2. The call returns 200 and its spend log retains the marker
3. Send another marked request after the key exceeds its budget and receive HTTP 422
4. GET http://localhost:4391/spend/logs/v2 shows the failure row with the submitted marker

## Relevant issues

Fixes #37260

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Added meaningful tests that assert the built failure-row payload
- [ ] Affected tests pass on Devin at the final commit under the requested remote verification workflow
- [ ] Required CI checks have completed without in-scope failures
- [x] The change only fixes caller header metadata on auth failures
- [ ] Required automated reviews have finished on the latest commit and actionable findings are resolved

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Baseline `c7747002e570e512ed02e6bb18caa5536a5b2426`, candidate `9ff26c7b7cfa1f6446858ae56080e038dd264008`

Devin ran the source proxy with PostgreSQL and dedicated Redis on port 6391, with two worker processes at each revision. Each live run used its own empty task database. The original issue uses a mock model to exhaust a key budget, so no real provider call is required

<details>
<summary>Executed configuration and client script</summary>

The same config was used at both revisions

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mock
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/mock
      api_key: mock
      mock_response: "ok"
      input_cost_per_token: 1.0
      output_cost_per_token: 1.0
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6391
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6391
```

Set `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `LITELLM_SALT_KEY` to disposable test secrets and `DATABASE_URL` to the fresh database for that revision. From its source checkout, run the proxy with the configuration above. The verifier waited for `/health/liveliness` to return 200 and checked two worker PIDs before running the client

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4391 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver > proxy.log 2>&1
```

The following is the actual executed `drive2.py`. It uses `httpx` and `psycopg`, waits for observed spend and log persistence, and reads the resulting rows through `/spend/logs/v2`. Use an isolated empty database, since the script identifies newly written rows by comparing request IDs. Credentials stay in environment variables

```python
"""Issue 37260 live driver. Usage: drive2.py <label> <base_url> <out_dir>. Env: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, DATABASE_URL."""
import json, os, sys, time, uuid
import httpx, psycopg

LABEL, BASE, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
ADMIN = {"authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}"}
RUN = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
c = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=60)
db = psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], autocommit=True)
CHAT = {"model": "mock", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}
RESP = {"model": "mock", "input": "hi"}
MSGS = {"model": "mock", "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}
AV = {"anthropic-version": "2023-06-01"}
BODY_SLM = {"spend_logs_metadata": {"my_request_id": "body"}}
results = []


def keygen(**extra):
    r = c.post("/key/generate", headers=ADMIN, json=extra)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["key"]


def row_ids():
    return {r[0] for r in db.execute('select request_id from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"').fetchall()}


def wait(pred, timeout, every=0.5):
    start = time.monotonic()
    while time.monotonic() - start < timeout:
        v = pred()
        if v:
            return v
        time.sleep(every)
    return None


def v2_rows(request_id):
    r = c.get("/spend/logs/v2", headers=ADMIN, params={
        "start_date": "2026-01-01 00:00:00", "end_date": "2027-01-01 00:00:00",
        "request_id": request_id, "page": 1, "page_size": 10})
    return r.json().get("data", []) if r.status_code == 200 else []


def M(tag):
    return json.dumps({"my_request_id": f"{tag}_{RUN}"})


def call(case, key, hdr, body=CHAT, path="/v1/chat/completions", extra_headers=None):
    before = row_ids()
    h = {"content-type": "application/json", **(extra_headers or {})}
    if key is not None:
        h["authorization"] = f"Bearer {key}"
    if hdr is not None:
        h["x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata"] = hdr
    r = c.post(path, headers=h, json=body)
    new = wait(lambda: sorted(row_ids() - before), 60) or []
    rows = [row for rid in new for row in (wait(lambda: v2_rows(rid), 20) or [])]
    rec = {"case": case, "path": path, "http": r.status_code, "sent_header": hdr,
           "error": r.json().get("error") if r.status_code != 200 else None,
           "rows": [{"status": row["status"], "spend": row["spend"], "call_type": row["call_type"],
                     "spend_logs_metadata": (row.get("metadata") or {}).get("spend_logs_metadata")} for row in rows]}
    results.append(rec)
    print(json.dumps(rec), flush=True)


def key_spend(key):
    r = c.get("/key/info", headers=ADMIN, params={"key": key})
    return (r.json().get("info") or {}).get("spend") or 0.0


free = keygen()
call("M1_messages_success_header", free, M("msg_ok"), MSGS, "/v1/messages", AV)
k = keygen(max_budget=0.01, models=["mock"])
call("A1_chat_success_header", k, M("req_success_1"))
print(json.dumps({"key_spend_persisted": bool(wait(lambda: key_spend(k) >= 0.01, 90)), "spend": key_spend(k)}), flush=True)
call("A2_chat_budget_reject_header", k, M("req_rejected_2"))
call("B1_chat_budget_reject_missing_header", k, None)
call("B2_chat_budget_reject_malformed_header", k, '{"x":')
call("F1_chat_budget_reject_body_litellm_metadata_plus_header", k, M("hdr_over_lm_body"), {**CHAT, "litellm_metadata": BODY_SLM})
call("F2_chat_budget_reject_body_litellm_metadata_no_header", k, None, {**CHAT, "litellm_metadata": BODY_SLM})
call("F3_chat_budget_reject_body_metadata_plus_header", k, M("hdr_over_body"), {**CHAT, "metadata": BODY_SLM})
call("F4_chat_budget_reject_body_both_buckets_plus_header", k, M("hdr_both"), {**CHAT, "metadata": BODY_SLM, "litellm_metadata": {"x": "y"}})
call("G1_responses_budget_reject_header", k, M("resp_rejected"), RESP, "/v1/responses")
call("G2_responses_budget_reject_native_metadata_header", k, M("resp_native"), {**RESP, "metadata": {"native": "keep-me"}}, "/v1/responses")
call("G3_responses_budget_reject_malformed_header", k, '{"x":', RESP, "/v1/responses")
call("G4_messages_budget_reject_header", k, M("msg_rejected"), MSGS, "/v1/messages", AV)
call("G5_messages_budget_reject_native_metadata_header", k, M("msg_native"), {**MSGS, "metadata": {"user_id": "keep-me"}}, "/v1/messages", AV)
call("G6_messages_budget_reject_missing_header", k, None, MSGS, "/v1/messages", AV)
bogus = f"sk-bogus-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
call("E1_chat_invalid_key_header", bogus, M("chat_invalid_key"))
call("E2_responses_invalid_key_header", bogus, M("resp_invalid_key"), RESP, "/v1/responses")
call("E3_messages_invalid_key_header", bogus, M("msg_invalid_key"), MSGS, "/v1/messages", AV)
call("P1_chat_postauth_unknown_model_header", free, M("chat_badmodel"), {**CHAT, "model": "nope"})
call("P2_responses_postauth_unknown_model_header", free, M("resp_badmodel"), {**RESP, "model": "nope"}, "/v1/responses")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
json.dump({"label": LABEL, "run": RUN, "results": results}, open(f"{OUT}/results.json", "w"), indent=1)
```

Run once against each revision's proxy with its matching `DATABASE_URL`

```bash
python drive2.py base_c7747002_r2 http://127.0.0.1:4391 evidence/c437/live_base_c7747002_r2
python drive2.py cand_9ff26c7b http://127.0.0.1:4391 evidence/9ff2/live_cand_9ff26c7b
```

</details>

### Before (c7747002e570e512ed02e6bb18caa5536a5b2426)

#### Chat Completions

1. Run the baseline driver above, cases A1/A2 and F1/F3/F4
2. A1 returns 200 and records its header marker. The key spend reaches 28.0
3. A2 and F1 return 422 with `budget_exceeded` and record `spend_logs_metadata=null`. F3/F4 retain the body value instead of the header
4. Invalid-key case E1 returns 401 with `token_not_found_in_db` and records no header marker

#### Responses

1. The same driver sends cases G1/G2 and E2 to `/v1/responses`
2. Budget cases return 422 and the invalid-key case returns 401
3. Each persisted failure row has `spend_logs_metadata=null`

#### Messages

1. The same driver sends cases M1, G4/G5 and E3 to `/v1/messages`
2. M1 returns 200 and records its marker. Budget cases return 422 and the invalid-key case returns 401
3. Each persisted auth failure row has `spend_logs_metadata=null`

### After (9ff26c7b7cfa1f6446858ae56080e038dd264008)

#### Chat Completions

1. Run the candidate driver above, cases A1/A2 and F1/F3/F4
2. A1 returns 200 and records its header marker. The key spend reaches 28.0
3. A2 and F1/F3/F4 return the same 422 error and record the header's `my_request_id`, including requests with both body metadata fields
4. E1 returns the same 401 error and now records its header marker

#### Responses

1. The same driver sends cases G1/G2 and E2 to `/v1/responses`
2. Budget cases return the same 422 and the invalid-key case returns the same 401
3. Each persisted auth failure row contains the submitted header marker, including native body metadata cases

#### Messages

1. The same driver sends cases M1, G4/G5 and E3 to `/v1/messages`
2. M1 returns 200 and records its marker. Budget cases return the same 422 and the invalid-key case returns the same 401
3. Each persisted auth failure row contains the submitted header marker, including native body metadata cases

All 20 paired cases have identical HTTP status and error bodies. Missing and malformed headers retain baseline behavior. The post-auth controls also remain unchanged, including the pre-existing missing header on the Responses unknown-model failure. Both driver runs exit 0 and observe `key_spend_persisted=true` before the rejection


## Validation

Independent verification is complete at `9ff26c7b7cfa1f6446858ae56080e038dd264008`, including the read-only field and real-writer test repairs

At `9ff26c7b7cfa1f6446858ae56080e038dd264008`, the auth handler suite passes 94 tests, spend callback suite passes 191, and pre-call utility suite passes 712. A separate success-header compatibility check passes 14 cases, including non-object JSON. Eight regression cases fail on unchanged baseline source and pass on this tip, while the five unchanged-behavior cases pass on both

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_auth_exception_handler.py -p no:cacheprovider -q --no-header
python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_proxy_track_cost_callback.py -p no:cacheprovider -q --no-header
python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/test_litellm_pre_call_utils.py -p no:cacheprovider -q --no-header
python -m coverage run --rcfile=/dev/null --branch \
  --include='*/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_exception_handler.py,*/litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py' \
  -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_auth_exception_handler.py tests/unit/proxy/test_litellm_pre_call_utils.py -p no:cacheprovider -q --no-header
python -m coverage report --rcfile=/dev/null -m
```

Changed executable lines are covered 14/14 in the auth handler, 3/3 in pre-call utilities, and 1/1 in the TypedDict declaration. Branches originating on changed handler lines are covered 4/4. The handler overall has 101/102 statements and 29/30 branches covered, with the single missing statement outside the diff. Coverage.py does not record arcs for the TypedDict conditional expression, but both arms passed header-present and header-absent unit and live cases

The auth suite also passes a repeat run and a four-worker xdist run. A disposable plugin measured the shared spend queue byte counter before and after every test in both serial runs, with 0 before and 0 after throughout

The baseline and candidate use the same Rust source tree `a75bdb621b3f489678aa4d6ab94cf586508d11bf`. Their compiled bridge binaries differ, with SHA-256 prefixes `8304cc993df13747` and `6ef6b993141cd4d7` respectively

title: test(s3_v2): give the slow-sink ramp test a callback limit that outlasts its burst
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

`test_s3_v2_slow_sink_ramps_concurrency_and_drains_the_backlog` fails on slow CI runners because the proxy cancels success callbacks that wait more than 20 seconds, so some of the 400 requests never reach the S3 logger and no wait can recover them. This gives the test's proxy a 600 second callback limit so the test measures the S3 upload ramp it was written for

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The test pushes 400 requests through a single-worker proxy and expects 400 stored objects within 180 seconds
- On a loaded runner the proxy's logging worker cancels `Logging.async_success_handler` after `LOGGING_WORKER_MAX_TIME_PER_COROUTINE` (20 seconds by default), before those callbacks reach the S3 logger
- The cancelled callbacks never queue an upload, so the test ends at 340 to 370 objects however long it waits
- It failed in 6 of 28 scheduled runs on main from 11-06 to 11-13

How it solves it:

- The test's proxy sets `LOGGING_WORKER_MAX_TIME_PER_COROUTINE=600`
- The 180 second wait and every assertion stay as they are

None. This changes one integration test's proxy environment and no product code

### Migration for existing customers

title: fix(model-prices): drop Flex prices from Vertex AI Gemini 4 Argon and Hydrogen
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3630926dbe3542aba669439de443a74d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3630926dbe3542aba669439de443a74d?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Three Vertex AI Gemini 4 rows carried Flex prices
- Google says Flex PayGo is not supported on Gemini 4

How it solves it:

- Removes the three `_flex` price fields from each row
- Leaves every other field on those rows unchanged

## Rows changed

All three rows are kind `page`, under ruling `vertex-ai-gemini-4-argon-hydrogen-drop-flex`. The fields removed from each row are `cache_read_input_token_cost_flex`, `input_cost_per_token_flex` and `output_cost_per_token_flex`.

| Key | Flex input / cache read / output removed (per 1M tokens) |
| --- | --- |
| `vertex_ai/gemini-4-argon` | $1.00 / $0.05 / $5.00 |
| `vertex_ai/gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive` | $2.00 / $0.10 / $10.00 |
| `vertex_ai/gemini-4-hydrogen` | $0.75 / $0.0375 / $3.75 |

The catalog and `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` get the same change and stay byte-identical.

## Evidence

Fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-13.

https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/flex-paygo says "Notice: Flex PayGo is supported only in select Gemini 3.8 Flash and earlier models. It is not supported in newer Gemini models such as Gemini 4 Argon." Its "Supported models and locations" list runs from `gemini-3.8-flash-cyber` to `gemini-3-flash-preview` and has no `gemini-4` id.

https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing shows the Gemini 4 tabs as "Standard Model", "Priority" and "Batch" with no Flex tab, while the Gemini 3 and 2.5 sections read "Standard", "Priority" and "Flex/Batch".

The Gemini 4 Argon, Hydrogen and Carbon model pages list "Pay-as-you-go: Standard PayGo with Usage Tiers, Priority PayGo" and "Batch inference: Supported", and do not mention Flex. The two `vertex_ai/gemini-4-carbon` rows already had no Flex fields.

The removed values were equal to each row's batch prices, which stay in place.

## Caveats

A request sent to these models with the Flex service tier is now costed at the standard rate. Google states it does not serve Flex on these models, so no real traffic should take that path.

No tests are added because this is a data-only change to vendor prices. One existing test is edited. `test_vertex_gemini_4_argon_matches_gemini_api_global_pricing` compared thirteen price keys between `vertex_ai/gemini-4-argon` and `gemini/gemini-4-argon`, three of them Flex, and failed with `KeyError: 'input_cost_per_token_flex'` once the Vertex row lost them. The three Flex keys are dropped from `GEMINI_4_ARGON_TOKEN_PRICE_KEYS`, so the test still checks the ten standard, batch, priority and cache-read prices the two rows share.

The `gemini/gemini-4-argon` row keeps its Flex prices. https://aistudio.google.com/docs/flex-inference lists Gemini 4 Carbon, Argon and Hydrogen as supporting Flex inference and https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing has a Flex tab for each, so the two providers now differ on Flex on purpose.

</details>
