title: fix(deps): require uvloop 0.23.0 so a cancelled connect cannot close another connection
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

When a client leaves a streaming request while the proxy is still opening an outbound connection, uvloop 0.22.1 can later close a different, unrelated connection and leave the worker failing new outbound calls with `File descriptor N is used by transport`. uvloop 0.23.0 fixes this, so this raises the floor to 0.23.0 and relocks

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- uvloop before 0.23.0 does not detach the Python socket when `loop.create_connection(sock=sock)` is cancelled (MagicStack/uvloop#738)
- When that socket is collected it closes whichever connection now owns the same fd number, so another client's request is dropped
- uvloop still holds a transport for that fd number, so later outbound calls on the worker return 500

How it solves it:

- `pyproject.toml` requires `uvloop>=0.23.0,<1.0`
- `uv.lock` moves uvloop from 0.22.1 to 0.23.0, and nothing else in the lock changes

## User Flow

Before: a client disconnect can break other requests on the same worker

1. A client starts a streaming request that runs a guardrail scan and disconnects while the scan's connection is opening
2. Another client's in-flight request on that worker is dropped with no response
3. Later requests on that worker that open an outbound connection return 500 with `File descriptor N is used by transport`

After: the disconnect affects only the client that left

1. A client starts a streaming request and disconnects while the scan's connection is opening
2. Other requests on that worker finish normally
3. Later requests on that worker keep working

## Relevant issues

Fixes #44623. Same two-file change as #44618, which was closed because fork PRs cannot change `uv.lock`

Seen in the scheduled integration run https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43153655627/job/130968458497 in `tests/integration/observability/test_bedrock_converse_stream_post_call_guardrail.py`, tests `test_concurrent_streams_each_get_their_own_verdict_and_spend_rows` and `test_guardrail_vendor_outage_during_a_burst_fails_closed_then_recovers`

## Behavior changes

### What changes for existing callers

- Installs with the `proxy` extra now need uvloop 0.23.0 or newer. An environment pinned to uvloop 0.22.x no longer satisfies the requirement
- On Python 3.13, uvloop 0.23.0 passes `eager_start=` to a custom task factory. `loop.set_task_factory(asyncio.eager_task_factory)` or a factory with a fixed signature now raises `TypeError` on `create_task`, where 0.22.1 accepted it. litellm and its locked dependencies set no task factory, so this reaches only operator code such as custom callbacks, guardrails or auth
- `Transport.write` now writes at once instead of batching per loop turn, so unawaited write bursts make more syscalls and a write to a reset peer fails one call earlier. Read boundaries on 18 real streams through the proxy were the same on both versions
- Python 3.14 macOS wheels of uvloop need macOS 10.15, up from 10.13. Default executor threads are named `uvloop_N`. The bundled libuv moves from 1.48 to 1.52.1, and `UV_USE_IO_URING=0` no longer disables io_uring
- No litellm code changes

### Migration for existing customers

None required when installing from the lock or the published image. Anyone pinning uvloop below 0.23.0 by hand needs to lift that pin

### Regression tests

- No new test. The two integration tests above are the regression, and they fail on 0.22.1 only when a cancelled connect lands in the right window

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The failing CI run's proxy log shows the bug directly: eight lines of `File descriptor 45 is used by transport <TCPTransport closed=False reading=True ...>`, three `converse-stream` 500s, and 15 of the 16 burst responses logged

Reproduction of the two tests at `a3c52e69d30c` (the failing commit) on Python 3.12.3, with CI's test order, a fresh proxy per run and 12 runs in parallel. The uvloop 0.23.0 runs installed 0.23.0 into the same environment, before this lock change existed

| uvloop | Runs | Failed | Cancelled connects seen | `File descriptor N is used by transport` in the proxy log |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.22.1 | 36 | 6 | not traced | 6 runs |
| 0.22.1, connect tracing on | 12 | 5 | 7, socket left attached | 5 runs |
| 0.23.0, connect tracing on | 24 | 0 | 13, socket detached every time | 0 runs |

The 0.22.1 failures match CI: `httpx.RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected without sending a response` in the first test, and in the second a 500 JSON body `{"error":{"message":"File descriptor 43 is used by transport ...` that the test then fails to decode as an event stream

With this PR's lock at `a208bfe9081` the environment installs uvloop 0.23.0, and the whole Bedrock guardrail test file passed in three runs out of three, 30 tests each

The same behaviour reproduces without litellm: on uvloop 0.22.1 a cancelled `create_connection(sock=sock)` leaves the socket holding its fd number and collecting it closes an unrelated connection, and on 0.23.0 the socket reports `fileno() == -1`

### Live before and after on a real proxy

```
  - model_name: claude

Results (before | after)
loop in the worker (custom logger)          uvloop.Loop 0.22.1 | uvloop.Loop 0.23.0
48 request cells x3 (3 endpoints, stream/non-stream, raw + OpenAI/Anthropic SDK sync/async, guardrails, errors)
                                            identical status, body shape, headers, spend row
outbound requests to OpenAI / Anthropic / guardrail vendor   16 / 8 / 36 | 16 / 8 / 36, identical
```

<details>
<summary>Rig files as run: env.sh, launch.sh, config.tmpl.yaml</summary>

Env var names: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `PROXY_BATCH_WRITE_AT`, `LITELLM_LOG`, `RIG_CB_LOG`. Each side has its own Postgres and Redis, and both run `launch.sh <base|head> main --num_workers 2`. `--reload` is dropped because the comparison needs two serving workers per side. `rigcb.inst` is a logging-only callback that records the running loop class and uvloop version

```bash
export H=$HOME/w/litellm_uvloop_0_23-ce5ede2a      # head tree  a208bfe9081 (uvloop 0.23.0)
export B=$HOME/w/pr51734-base-dd939b06             # base tree  db75214bdc3 (uvloop 0.22.1)

export OUT=$RIG/out
export NS=pr51734

export PX_A=27340 PX_B=27341

export VEND_A=27360 VEND_B=27361 STALL=27362 DEAD=27363 FAKEUP=27364
export MASTER=sk-rig-51734
mkdir -p "$OUT" "$RIG/logs" "$RIG/pids"
side_tree () { [ "$1" = base ] && echo "$B" || echo "$H"; }
side_port () { [ "$1" = base ] && echo "$PX_A" || echo "$PX_B"; }

```

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# launch.sh <base|head> <leg-tag> [extra litellm flags...]   start one proxy; stop.sh <side> frees its port.
. "$(dirname "$0")/env.sh"
side=$1; tag=$2; shift 2
tree=$(side_tree $side); port=$(side_port $side)
[ $side = base ] && { REC_OA=$REC_OA_A; REC_AN=$REC_AN_A; VEND=$VEND_A; } || { REC_OA=$REC_OA_B; REC_AN=$REC_AN_B; VEND=$VEND_B; }
mkdir -p "$RIG/cfg-$side"
sed -e "s/@REC_OA@/$REC_OA/; s/@REC_AN@/$REC_AN/; s/@VEND@/$VEND/g; s/@REDIS@/$(side_rd $side)/; s/@DEAD@/$DEAD/; s/@STALL@/$STALL/g; s/@FAKEUP@/$FAKEUP/" \
  "$RIG/config.tmpl.yaml" > "$RIG/cfg-$side/config.yaml"
cp "$RIG/rigcb.py" "$RIG/cfg-$side/rigcb.py"
ss -ltn | awk '{print $4}' | grep -q ":$port\$" && { echo "launch $side: port $port still busy"; exit 1; }
cd "$tree" || exit 1
export PATH="$tree/${RIG_VENV:-.venv}/bin:$PATH" PYTHONPATH="$tree" VIRTUAL_ENV="$tree/${RIG_VENV:-.venv}"
export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://llmproxy:dbpassword9090@127.0.0.1:$(side_pg $side)/litellm"
export LITELLM_ENABLE_MCP_STDIO=true LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=$MASTER PROXY_BATCH_WRITE_AT=3 RIG_CB_LOG="$OUT/cb-$side.jsonl" LITELLM_LOG=INFO
"$tree/${RIG_VENV:-.venv}/bin/python" - <<PY || exit 1
import litellm, uvloop, os, sys
ok = litellm.__file__.startswith(os.getcwd())
print("$side tree:", litellm.__file__, "uvloop", uvloop.__version__, uvloop.__file__, "python", sys.version.split()[0], "OK" if ok else "WRONG TREE")
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
PY
log="$RIG/logs/proxy-$side-$tag.log"
setsid nohup "$tree/${RIG_VENV:-.venv}/bin/litellm" --config "$RIG/cfg-$side/config.yaml" --host 127.0.0.1 --port $port "$@" > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
echo $! > "$RIG/pids/proxy-$side.pid.keep"
scheme=http; case " $* " in *ssl_keyfile_path*) scheme=https;; esac
for i in $(seq 1 150); do
  curl -sk -o /dev/null -m 3 "$scheme://127.0.0.1:$port/health/liveliness" && break
  kill -0 "$(cat "$RIG/pids/proxy-$side.pid.keep")" 2>/dev/null || { echo "launch $side: proxy died"; tail -30 "$log"; exit 1; }
  sleep 2
done
curl -sk -o /dev/null -m 3 "$scheme://127.0.0.1:$port/health/liveliness" || { echo "launch $side: never became live"; tail -30 "$log"; exit 1; }
echo "launch $side ok port=$port pid=$(cat "$RIG/pids/proxy-$side.pid.keep") workers_started=$(grep -c 'Started server process' "$log") log=$log"
```

### Worker recycle under a burst

`--num_workers 2 --max_requests_before_restart 15`, 80 concurrent chat requests to OpenAI, six rounds, same tree at `a208bfe9081` with only uvloop swapped, sides alternating which bursts first

| uvloop | Runs | Runs with 500s | Bursting first | Bursting second |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.22.1 | 6 | 3 | 3 runs, 80 x 200 each | 3 runs, 32, 3 and 32 x 500 |
| 0.23.0 | 6 | 3 | 3 runs, 80 x 200 each | 3 runs, 32, 4 and 32 x 500 |

The 500s are `CancelledError: Task cancelled, timeout graceful shutdown exceeded` and follow burst order, not the uvloop version. Every cancelled request was waiting on an outbound TCP connect to OpenAI, and a plain TCP probe from the same machine with no proxy connected 80 of 80 in a first storm and 48 of 80 in a second one 7 seconds later. Same behaviour on both versions

<details>
<summary>recycle_burst.py</summary>

```python
"""recycle_burst.py <side> <tag> <n>: n concurrent OpenAI-only chat requests (alternating non-stream / stream, PONG prompt)
against one side, then spend rows for this run's key. Reuses driver.py helpers. Writes $OUT/<tag>-<side>.json."""
import asyncio, collections, json, os, sys, time
import driver as d

side, tag, n = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
LOG = f"{os.environ['RIG']}/logs/proxy-{side}-{tag}.log"


def logcount(needle: str) -> int:
    with open(LOG, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        return sum(needle in line for line in f)


async def one(c, i: int) -> dict:
    stream = i % 2 == 1
    body = d.chat_body("gpt", stream)
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        async with c.stream("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", json=body) as r:
            raw = b""
            async for part in r.aiter_raw():
                raw += part
            txt = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            return {"i": i, "stream": stream, "status": r.status_code, "t0": t0, "t": time.time() - t0, "bytes": len(raw),
                    "cancelled": r.status_code == 500 and ("CancelledError" in txt or "graceful shutdown" in txt),
                    "done_marker": ("[DONE]" in txt) if stream else None,
                    "body": None if r.status_code == 200 else txt[:300]}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"i": i, "stream": stream, "status": -1, "t0": t0, "t": time.time() - t0, "bytes": 0, "cancelled": False,
                "done_marker": None, "body": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}"}


async def go(key: str) -> list:
    async with d.aclient(side, key) as c:
        return list(await asyncio.gather(*[one(c, i) for i in range(n)]))

alias = f"{tag}.burst"
key = d.mk_key(side, alias)
pre = {"maxlimit": logcount("Maximum request limit"), "started": logcount("Started server process")}
t0 = time.time()
rs = asyncio.run(go(key))
wall = time.time() - t0
post = {"maxlimit": logcount("Maximum request limit"), "started": logcount("Started server process")}
sp = d.spend(side, alias, want=n, wait=float(os.environ.get("SPEND_WAIT", "60")))
st = collections.Counter(f"{'stream' if r['stream'] else 'nonstream'}.{r['status']}" for r in rs)
res = {"side": side, "tag": tag, "n": n, "burst_start_epoch": t0, "wall": round(wall, 2),
       "status": dict(sorted(collections.Counter(str(r["status"]) for r in rs).items())), "tally": dict(sorted(st.items())),
       "cancelled_500": sum(r["cancelled"] for r in rs),
       "other_non200": [r["body"] for r in rs if r["status"] != 200 and not r["cancelled"]][:10],
       "streams_without_done": sum(1 for r in rs if r["stream"] and r["status"] == 200 and not r["done_marker"]),
       "spend_n": sp["n"], "spend_statuses": dict(collections.Counter(r["status"] for r in sp["rows"])),
       "lat_p50": round(sorted(r["t"] for r in rs)[len(rs) // 2], 2), "lat_max": round(max(r["t"] for r in rs), 2),
       "slow_over_10s": sum(r["t"] > 10 for r in rs),
       "recycles_before_burst": pre["maxlimit"], "recycles_triggered_during_burst": post["maxlimit"] - pre["maxlimit"],
       "sample_500": next((r["body"] for r in rs if r["cancelled"]), None)}
print(json.dumps(res), flush=True)
with open(f"{d.OUT}/{tag}-{side}.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump({"summary": res, "requests": rs}, f, indent=1)
```

title: fix(types): build chat, text and embedding response schemas eagerly so parallel first requests cannot race
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

A burst of parallel requests hitting a freshly started proxy worker could fail some of them with an internal schema error while building the response object. #51591 fixed this for the usage types, and this does the same for the chat, text completion and embedding response types, so concurrent first requests can no longer race on them

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Parallel first requests on a fresh worker sometimes fail with `AttributeError: type object 'ModelResponse' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'`
- The response models build their pydantic schema lazily on first use, and concurrent rebuilds race
- #51591 covered `Usage` only, so the same race stayed open on the models around it

How it solves it:

- The chat, text completion and embedding response models set `defer_build=False`, the same one-line setting `Usage` and `ChoiceLogprobs` already use
- The regression test in `tests/unit/types/test_types_utils.py` now forces the race on each of these models in a fresh subprocess

## User Flow

Before: some requests in a burst against a freshly booted proxy worker fail

1. The admin starts or restarts the proxy
2. A client fires many POST /v1/chat/completions requests at once
3. A few come back as 500 errors mentioning `type object 'ModelResponse' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'`

After: the same burst succeeds for every request

1. The admin starts or restarts the proxy
2. A client fires many POST /v1/chat/completions requests at once
3. Every request returns 200

## Relevant issues

Seen in the scheduled integration run https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43056354526/job/130646740944 in `tests/integration/observability/test_azure_content_safety_dispatch_resilience.py::test_x1_azure_server_stop_restart_during_mixed_burst`. Follow-up to #51591

## Behavior changes

### What changes for existing callers

- These models now build their schema when `litellm.types.utils` is imported instead of on first use: `ModelResponse`, `ModelResponseStream` (through `ModelResponseBase`), `Message`, `Delta`, `Choices`, `StreamingChoices`, `EmbeddingResponse`, `Embedding`, `TextCompletionResponse`, `TextChoices`, `Logprobs`, `TopLogprob`, `ChatCompletionTokenLogprob`, `Function`, `FunctionCall`, `ChatCompletionMessageToolCall`, `ChatCompletionDeltaToolCall` and the four custom tool call models (through `_CustomToolCallAccess`)
- `DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD` no longer changes build timing for these models, and their `model_config["defer_build"]` reads `False`
- Subclasses of these models inherit the eager build
- Import does the schema build up front. Over 30 alternating runs per side, `litellm.types.utils` self time goes from 38.3 ms to 48.9 ms, first use of the response models goes from 10.1 ms to 0.76 ms, the `import litellm` paired median moves by +0.06 s with a standard deviation of 0.23 s, and resident memory is unchanged
- Field values, validation, serialization and `extra` handling are unchanged

### Migration for existing customers

None required

### Regression tests

- `test_types_utils.py::test_parallel_first_response_model_construction_does_not_race_schema_build` constructs each model from eight threads in its own forked child of a fresh interpreter, holding them at the line where pydantic deletes the half built schema

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Before and after, base `db75214bdc3` against head

```
Checked base db75214bdc3 against 1bf794e0328 (bd88293f7a3 only changes the test), Python 3.12.3, pydantic 2.13.4

Red/green without a trace hook: 240 fresh interpreters per side, each starting 32 threads that construct
the response models for the first time (natural_probe.py below, mode ctor, default switch interval)

  $ seq 1 240 | xargs -P 12 -I{} python -I natural_probe.py <tree> 32 ctor
  base: 8 of 240 interpreters failed   TypeError: 'MockValSer' object is not an instance of 'SchemaSerializer'
  head: 0 of 240

Same through litellm.acompletion(mock_response=...) x 32 with sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6):

  $ seq 1 240 | xargs -P 12 -I{} python -I natural_probe.py <tree> 32 acomp 0.000001
  base: 6 of 240 failed   type object 'ModelResponse' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'
  head: 0 of 240

Live proxy, real OpenAI and Anthropic, real Postgres, fresh boot each time, no warm-up:

  $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21738 --num_workers 2
  # config.yaml: gpt-4o-mini, text-embedding-3-small (openai), claude-haiku (anthropic), master_key set
  # client: 32 simultaneous first requests across /v1/chat/completions (plain, tools, stream),
  #         /v1/messages, /v1/responses, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings
  base: 14 boots, 448 requests, 448 x 200, 0 schema errors
  head: 14 boots, 448 requests, 448 x 200, 0 schema errors

The base proxy did not reproduce the failure in these boots, so the live run shows the change is safe
and the probes above show it works

Base vs head on a 4-worker proxy: 182 live requests across the five endpoints (streaming and not,
tool calls, logprobs, bad keys, timeouts, client disconnects) returned the same status, body shape,
headers, spend rows and callback payloads
```

<details>
<summary>natural_probe.py</summary>

```python
"""Natural race probe: no settrace. One fresh interpreter = one fresh worker.
usage: python -I natural_probe.py <tree> <threads> <mode: ctor|acomp|atext|aembed|mixed> [switchinterval]
ctor  : N threads each construct the response models directly (ModelResponse() first, as litellm/main.py does).
acomp : N concurrent litellm.acompletion(mock_response=...) calls: the product's own run_in_executor path, no network.
prints one JSON line {complete_before, errors, kinds}."""
import asyncio, json, sys, threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
n, mode = int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
if len(sys.argv) > 4:
    sys.setswitchinterval(float(sys.argv[4]))
import litellm
from litellm.types.utils import ModelResponse, ModelResponseStream, TextCompletionResponse, EmbeddingResponse, Message, Choices
assert litellm.__file__.startswith(sys.argv[1] + "/")
pre = bool(ModelResponse.__pydantic_complete__)
TC = {"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}
def err(e): return f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:140]}"
if mode == "ctor":
    start = threading.Barrier(n, timeout=10)
    def construct(i):
        start.wait()
        try:
            ModelResponse()
            r = ModelResponse(id="x", created=1, model="m", choices=[{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "tool_calls", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [TC]},
                              "logprobs": {"content": [{"token": "a", "logprob": -0.1, "top_logprobs": [{"token": "a", "logprob": -0.1}]}]}}], usage={"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2})
            r.model_dump(); r.model_dump_json()
            ModelResponseStream(id="x", created=1, choices=[{"index": 0, "delta": {"content": "a", "tool_calls": [{**TC, "index": 0}]}}]).model_dump()
            TextCompletionResponse(id="x", created=1, model="m", choices=[{"text": "a", "index": 0, "logprobs": {"text_offset": [0], "token_logprobs": [-0.1], "tokens": ["a"], "top_logprobs": [{"a": -0.1}]}}]).model_dump()
            EmbeddingResponse(model="m", data=[{"embedding": [0.1], "index": 0, "object": "embedding"}]).model_dump()
            return None
        except Exception as e:
            return err(e)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n) as pool:
        res = list(pool.map(construct, range(n)))
else:
    M = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
    async def one(i, gate):
        await gate.wait()
        try:
            kind = mode if mode != "mixed" else ("acomp", "astream", "atext", "aembed")[i % 4]
            if kind == "acomp":
                r = await litellm.acompletion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=M, mock_response="hello there"); r.model_dump_json()
            elif kind == "astream":
                r = await litellm.acompletion(model="gpt-4o-mini", messages=M, mock_response="hello there friend", stream=True)
                async for c in r: c.model_dump_json()
            elif kind == "atext":
                r = await litellm.atext_completion(model="gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct", prompt="hi", mock_response="hello"); r.model_dump_json()
            else:
                r = await litellm.aembedding(model="text-embedding-3-small", input=["hi"], mock_response=[0.1, 0.2]); r.model_dump_json()
            return None
        except Exception as e:
            return err(e)
    async def main():
        gate = asyncio.Event()
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(one(i, gate)) for i in range(n)]
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05); gate.set()
        return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    res = asyncio.run(main())
errs = [r for r in res if r]
print(json.dumps({"mode": mode, "complete_before": pre, "errors": len(errs), "schema_race": sum("__pydantic_" in e for e in errs), "kinds": sorted(set(errs))[:4]}))
```

```python
"""Fresh-boot burst leg. usage: burst.py <label> <boots> <workers> <requests> [ENV=VAL ...]
Each boot: start one proxy from the tree (base or head, alternating order), wait for every worker's startup line, fire
<requests> simultaneous FIRST requests, then stop the proxy. Provider keys come from this process's environment."""
import asyncio, collections, json, os, re, signal, subprocess, sys, time
import httpx

LABEL, BOOTS, WORKERS, NREQ = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
EXTRA = dict(a.split("=", 1) for a in sys.argv[5:])
HOME = os.environ["HOME"]; R = f"{HOME}/rig51733"; OUT = f"{R}/burst/{LABEL}"; os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
TREES = {"base": f"{HOME}/w/pr51733-base-8c961bf7", "head": f"{HOME}/w/litellm_response_schema_build_race-43d05fb6"}
PORTS = {"base": 21738, "head": 21739}; PG = {"base": 21731, "head": 21732}; REC = {"base": 21735, "head": 21736}
KEY = "sk-rig-51733"; NEEDLE = "__pydantic_"
CFG = EXTRA.pop("CFG", "config.yaml")

def plan(n):
    kinds = (["cc-oai", "cc-oai-stream", "cc-ant", "cc-oai-tools", "cc-oai", "tc", "cc-ant-stream", "emb", "cc-oai", "msg", "cc-oai-stream", "resp", "cc-ant", "tc", "emb", "cc-oai-tools"])
    return [kinds[i % len(kinds)] for i in range(n)]

async def one(client, kind, gate, port):
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"; h = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "x-litellm-tags": f"c51733-burst-{LABEL}"}
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK"}]
    tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}]
    spec = {"cc-oai": ("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 16}),
            "cc-oai-tools": ("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Weather in Paris? Use the tool."}], "tools": tools, "tool_choice": "required", "max_tokens": 64, "logprobs": True}),
            "cc-ant-stream": ("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "claude-haiku", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 16, "stream": True}),
            "tc": ("/v1/completions", {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "prompt": "Say OK", "max_tokens": 8}),
            "cc-ant": ("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "claude-haiku", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 16}),
            "cc-oai-stream": ("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 16, "stream": True, "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}}),
            "msg": ("/v1/messages", {"model": "claude-haiku", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 16}),
            "msg-stream": ("/v1/messages", {"model": "claude-haiku", "messages": msgs, "max_tokens": 16, "stream": True}),
            "resp": ("/v1/responses", {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Reply with OK", "max_output_tokens": 32}),
            "resp-stream": ("/v1/responses", {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Reply with OK", "max_output_tokens": 32, "stream": True}),
            "emb": ("/v1/embeddings", {"model": "embed-small", "input": "hello"})}[kind]
    await gate.wait()
    try:
        r = await client.post(base + spec[0], headers=h, json=spec[1])
        text = r.text
        usage_seen = '"usage"' in text
        return {"kind": kind, "status": r.status_code, "schema_error": NEEDLE in text, "usage_seen": usage_seen,
                "error": text[:400] if r.status_code != 200 else None}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"kind": kind, "status": "exception", "schema_error": NEEDLE in str(e), "usage_seen": False, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}"}

async def burst(port):
    gate = asyncio.Event()
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120, limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=NREQ, max_keepalive_connections=NREQ)) as client:
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(one(client, k, gate, port)) for k in plan(NREQ)]
        await asyncio.sleep(0.2); gate.set()
        return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

def free(port):
    out = subprocess.run(["ss", "-tlnpH", f"sport = :{port}"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    for pid in set(re.findall(r"pid=(\d+)", out)):
        try: os.kill(int(pid), signal.SIGKILL)
        except ProcessLookupError: pass
    for _ in range(60):
        if not subprocess.run(["ss", "-tlnH", f"sport = :{port}"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip(): return
        time.sleep(0.5)
    raise RuntimeError(f"port {port} busy")

def kill_engines(pgport):
    for pid in subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-u", str(os.getuid()), "-f", "[q]uery-engine"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split():
        try:
            if f"localhost:{pgport}/litellm".encode() in open(f"/proc/{pid}/environ", "rb").read(): os.kill(int(pid), signal.SIGKILL)
        except (OSError, ValueError): pass

def boot(side, number):
    tree, port = TREES[side], PORTS[side]; free(port)
    log = f"{OUT}/{side}-{number}.log"
    env = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": f"{tree}:{R}/cfg", "DATABASE_URL": f"postgresql://llmproxy:dbpassword9090@localhost:{PG[side]}/litellm",
           "REC_OPENAI": f"http://127.0.0.1:{REC[side]}/openai/v1", "REC_ANTHROPIC": f"http://127.0.0.1:{REC[side]}/anthropic",
           "CAP51733_OUT": f"{OUT}/cap-{side}-{number}",
           "LITELLM_DISABLE_NO_REDIS_WARNING": "true", "LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP": "True", **EXTRA}
    for k in ("GEMINI_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS", "OPENAI_BASE_URL", "AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK"): env.pop(k, None)
    with open(log, "w") as stream:
        proc = subprocess.Popen([f"{tree}/.venv/bin/python", "litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py", "--config", f"{R}/cfg/{CFG}", "--host", "127.0.0.1",
                                 "--port", str(port), "--num_workers", str(WORKERS)], cwd=tree, env=env, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 300
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            text = open(log).read()
            if text.count("Application startup complete") >= WORKERS: break
            if proc.poll() is not None: raise RuntimeError(f"{side} boot {number} exited {proc.returncode}")
            time.sleep(0.05)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{side} boot {number} startup timed out")
        died_before = text.count("Child process")
        results = asyncio.run(burst(port))
        time.sleep(4)
        text = open(log).read()
        caps = "".join(open(f"{OUT}/{f}").read() for f in os.listdir(OUT) if f.startswith(f"cap-{side}-{number}.") and f.endswith(".jsonl") and ".trace." not in f)
        flips = sorted({fl["cls"] for line in caps.splitlines() if '"flips"' in line for fl in json.loads(line).get("flips", []) if fl["at_boot"] == "deferred"})
        summary = {"label": LABEL, "side": side, "boot": number, "tree": os.readlink(f"/proc/{proc.pid}/cwd"), "requests": len(results),
                   "status_counts": dict(collections.Counter(str(r["status"]) for r in results)),
                   "non_200": sum(r["status"] != 200 for r in results),
                   "schema_error_responses": sum(r["schema_error"] for r in results),
                   "schema_error_log_lines": sum(NEEDLE in line for line in text.splitlines()),
                   "schema_error_in_callback_capture": caps.count(NEEDLE),
                   "workers_started": len(set(re.findall(r"Started server process \[(\d+)\]", text))),
                   "worker_deaths_before_burst": died_before, "loadavg": os.getloadavg()[0],
                   "callback_events": caps.count('"kind"'), "callback_pids": len(set(re.findall(r'"pid": (\d+)', caps))),
                   "lazily_built_litellm_models": [f for f in flips if f.startswith("litellm.")], "lazily_built_other": len([f for f in flips if not f.startswith("litellm.")]),
                   "tracebacks_in_log": text.count("Traceback (most recent call last)"), "by_kind_non_200": dict(collections.Counter(r["kind"] for r in results if r["status"] != 200)),
                   "errors": [r["error"] for r in results if r["status"] != 200][:6]}
        json.dump({"summary": summary, "responses": results}, open(f"{OUT}/{side}-{number}.json", "w"), indent=1)
        print(json.dumps(summary), flush=True)
        return summary
    finally:
        try: os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
        except ProcessLookupError: pass
        try: proc.wait(timeout=20)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL); proc.wait()
        free(port); kill_engines(PG[side])

totals = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.Counter())
for number in range(1, BOOTS + 1):
    for side in (("base", "head") if number % 2 else ("head", "base")):
        try:
            s = boot(side, number)
            for k in ("requests", "non_200", "schema_error_responses", "schema_error_log_lines", "schema_error_in_callback_capture"): totals[side][k] += s[k]
            totals[side]["boots"] += 1
        except Exception as e:
            print(json.dumps({"label": LABEL, "side": side, "boot": number, "boot_error": str(e)}), flush=True); totals[side]["boot_errors"] += 1
print("TOTALS", json.dumps({k: dict(v) for k, v in totals.items()}), flush=True)
json.dump({k: dict(v) for k, v in totals.items()}, open(f"{OUT}/totals.json", "w"), indent=1)
```

</details>

### Regression test

The regression test forces the race on every model, run at `bd88293f7a3` on Python 3.12.3 with pydantic 2.13.4. Each model is raced in its own forked child, so every case sees that model's first use

With the change:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/types/test_types_utils.py -q
82 passed in 13.10s
```

With the new `defer_build=False` lines removed and the test left as is, the three usage models from #51591 pass and every newly covered model fails:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/types/test_types_utils.py -q -k parallel_first
E         AssertionError: ['ModelResponse', 'ModelResponseStream', 'Message', 'Delta', 'Choices', 'StreamingChoices', 'EmbeddingResponse', 'Embedding', 'TextCompletionResponse', 'TextChoices', 'Logprobs', 'TopLogprob', 'ChatCompletionTokenLogprob', 'FunctionCall', 'Function', 'ChatCompletionMessageToolCall', 'ChatCompletionDeltaToolCall', 'ChatCompletionMessageCustomToolCall']
1 failed, 81 deselected in 22.11s
```

After import, every model listed under Behavior changes reports `__pydantic_complete__` as true

Not covered here: models outside the chat, text completion and embedding responses still build lazily, including `ImageResponse`, `TranscriptionResponse`, `ChatCompletionAudioResponse` and `StreamingChatCompletionChunk`. `TranscriptionResponse()` in `litellm/main.py` is constructed in the executor the same way `ModelResponse()` was, so the same race stays open there

</details>

title: fix(mcp): backport #41197 to stable/1.106.x
body:
Backports #41197 to `stable/1.106.x`. Upstream MCP OAuth authorize redirects to Google (`accounts.google.com`) now request offline access (`access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`), so Google issues a refresh token and 1.106 users stop having to re-authenticate their Google MCP servers when the access token expires. Authorize URLs for other providers are unchanged, and values an admin sets in the configured authorization URL still win.

## Picks

- [x] #41197 fix(mcp): request offline access from Google upstream OAuth providers (`8007773ec59a` → `f1e1ab9ac80`)
  - Conflict in `oauth_utils.py` imports only. The line keeps its own import set and adds `collections.abc.Mapping`, which the new helper needs. `re` and `dataclass` come from unrelated main changes the line doesn't use.

No version bump in this PR. This line's release owner bumps the version in a separate release PR. No dependency bumps: the only finding main clears (soupsieve) is in the `ci` dev group and does not ship.

## Gates

- Picked tests: `tests/unit/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/` on the line: 6442 passed, 1 skipped. That includes the new `test_authorize_preserves_contract_with_provider_defaults` (15 cases).
- Lint: ruff is clean on changed product files. The test file's format drift was already on the line before the pick.
- Gauntlet-mini: SURVIVED, 5/5 lenses, 0 confirmed, reviewed f1e1ab9ac80. Not recorded in the ledger (no ledger tool in this session).
  - Rejected: a trailing-dot host (`accounts.google.com.`) gets no defaults. Same exact-match check as main, and not a regression.
  - Rejected: client-supplied `prompt`/`access_type` are not forwarded by `/authorize`. The route never accepted them, before or after, and it matches main.
  - Strongest dissent: Google users now always see a consent screen (`prompt=consent`). This is the intended behavior of #41197, and setting `prompt` in the configured authorization URL overrides it.

## Proof (live proxy, line tip vs pick)

A real proxy ran on each tree with two `oauth2` (`authorization_code`) MCP servers. Each test sent `GET /<server>/authorize` and read the redirect `Location`.

| Case | Before (`36742a02ea3`) | After (`f1e1ab9ac80`) |
|---|---|---|
| Google (`accounts.google.com`) | no `access_type` / `prompt` | `access_type=offline&prompt=consent`, other params unchanged |
| Other IdP | no extra params | identical to before |

<details><summary>Raw output</summary>

```
before google_drive -> https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=configured-google-client&redirect_uri=...&state=...&response_type=code&scope=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fdrive.readonly&code_challenge=abc&code_challenge_method=S256
before other_idp    -> https://idp.example.invalid/oauth/authorize?client_id=configured-other-client&redirect_uri=...&state=...&response_type=code&code_challenge=abc&code_challenge_method=S256
after  google_drive -> https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?access_type=offline&prompt=consent&client_id=configured-google-client&redirect_uri=...&state=...&response_type=code&scope=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.googleapis.com%2Fauth%2Fdrive.readonly&code_challenge=abc&code_challenge_method=S256
after  other_idp    -> https://idp.example.invalid/oauth/authorize?client_id=configured-other-client&redirect_uri=...&state=...&response_type=code&code_challenge=abc&code_challenge_method=S256
```
</details>

## Caveats (copied from #41197)

### Low

- Durable vault storage and reconnect after expiry were not exercised
- Real Google refresh was immediate, without waiting for token expiry
- An explicit operator override can disable offline access or change the consent prompt
- This PR does not establish that pod-restart authentication loss has the same cause

title: fix(spend-logs): make token redaction opt-in
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

make token redaction opt-in

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Default-on token scanning adds CPU overhead to spend logging
- Requests without prompt storage still pay for thread offloading

How it solves it:

- Default `redact_tokens_in_spend_logs` to `false`
- Require explicit `true` for scanning and thread offloading
- Keep explicit opt-in behavior and credential-field masking

Intentional product change: Stored free-form text is no longer scanned for token-shaped secrets by default. Administrators who want that protection must set `general_settings.redact_tokens_in_spend_logs: true`

## User Flow

Before, enabling prompt storage also enables token scanning implicitly

1. Enable `general_settings.store_prompts_in_spend_logs` and leave token redaction unset
2. Send a request containing a tool result
3. Stored text is scanned for token-shaped secrets automatically

After, administrators choose whether to enable token scanning

1. Enable `general_settings.store_prompts_in_spend_logs` and leave token redaction unset
2. Send the same request containing a tool result
3. Stored text keeps its token-shaped content unless redaction is explicitly enabled

To opt in:

```yaml
general_settings:
  store_prompts_in_spend_logs: true
  redact_tokens_in_spend_logs: true
```

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The focused test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is isolated to the opt-in mitigation
- [ ] Every automated review on the latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Tested commit `708ca9cc4c309c40a9a4a09481789fcc4fa67949` against base `db75214bdc312607c18b1a874f02266107e64e7b`

This is a draft mitigation for #48968 while the full HTTP load comparison remains unfinished. No live end-to-end performance claim is made

The regression tests cover unset, false and true with prompt storage both enabled and disabled. They check stored content and whether the injected thread runner executes. Restoring the base implementation produces three failures and four passes: the configuration default and both unset-setting thread-offload cases fail

On the mitigation, the spend-tracking tests, secret-redaction tests and CI-coverage check all pass, 715 tests total. The dashboard API types were regenerated from the backend schema. The existing integration test now opts into redaction explicitly; it has not been rerun locally

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_utils.py tests/unit/test_secret_redaction.py tests/unit/test_assert_ci_coverage.py -q
```

The standard local check command could not rebuild its dependencies because the disk filled. A second run against the prepared environment passed Ruff formatting, test-quality checks and generated TypeScript formatting, but could not provision the separate type-check environment or complete the OpenAPI baseline checkout because of disk space. Dashboard lint also lacks eslint-plugin-i18next in the local dependency cache. Full lint and the integration test remain for CI; these are not reported as passes

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Severe

- Free-form credential masking now requires explicit administrator opt-in

### Medium

- Full HTTP load testing and live before/after QA remain pending

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world use cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Default behavior now stores unredacted token-shaped strings in spend logs unless configured, which increases accidental secret retention risk but reduces logging CPU overhead.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`redact_tokens_in_spend_logs` is now off by default** instead of masking token-shaped secrets in stored spend-log request/response content unless admins set `general_settings.redact_tokens_in_spend_logs: true`.
> 
> Spend logging only runs the heavier **thread offload path** when that flag is explicitly `true`; unset or `false` skips token scanning and keeps stored free-form text as-is (credential-field masking elsewhere is unchanged). Config types, dashboard OpenAPI schema defaults, and tests/integration fixtures were updated so redaction-related tests and the Anthropic tool-payload integration scenario **opt in** to redaction explicitly.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 708ca9cc4c309c40a9a4a09481789fcc4fa67949. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(otel v2): proxy-level default langfuse_span_scope for key and team destinations
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2a10736c25d3431397d8be1c20564133
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2a10736c25d3431397d8be1c20564133?variant=devin
Requested by: @shivamrawat1

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Key and team Langfuse destinations always default to the full span tree
- Operators must set `llm_only` on every key, easy to forget

How it solves it:

- New proxy setting `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_DESTINATION_SPAN_SCOPE` sets the destination default
- Environment lookup ignores the unprefixed `langfuse_destination_span_scope` alias
- Also settable as `callback_settings.otel.langfuse_destination_span_scope`
- Explicit `langfuse_span_scope` on a key or team still wins
- Unset keeps today's `full` behavior, an invalid value warns and falls back to `full`

## User Flow

Before: an operator who gives each key its own Langfuse project gets auth, route, postgres and redis spans in every project unless each key sets `llm_only`

1. The operator starts the proxy with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true` and `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_SPAN_SCOPE=llm_only`
2. They create a key with POST /key/generate whose `metadata.logging` has a `langfuse_otel` entry with only public key, secret key and host
3. A developer sends POST /v1/chat/completions with that key
4. The key's Langfuse project receives 6 spans, `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `auth`, `route`, `postgres.select`, `redis.pipeline` and `chat <model>`

After: one proxy setting gives every key and team project only the model-call span

1. The operator starts the proxy with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true` and `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_DESTINATION_SPAN_SCOPE=llm_only`
2. They create the same key with POST /key/generate
3. A developer sends the same POST /v1/chat/completions
4. The key's Langfuse project receives only `chat <model>`, and a key that sets `langfuse_span_scope: "full"` still gets all 6

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10702

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live A/B on two proxies at the same time, Before at merge base 49ea54ee7a and After at 914a850c07. Each proxy ran 2 workers with real Postgres and a dedicated Redis shared by `router_settings` and `coordination_redis`, real Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` calls, `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, no global Langfuse keys and no global callbacks. The key's `langfuse_host` pointed at a local OTLP protobuf sink that records every exported span, so Langfuse Cloud itself was not used. Each case sent one non-streaming and one streaming chat call, all 32 returned 200, and the proxy was restarted between cases.

<details>
<summary>Proxy command, config.yaml, key and request</summary>

```bash
LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_DESTINATION_SPAN_SCOPE=llm_only \
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

```yaml
model_list:
- model_name: live-sonnet
  litellm_params:
    model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
    api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379
litellm_settings:
  callbacks: []
  provider_url_destination_allowed_hosts:
  - 127.0.0.1:4318
```

```bash
curl -sS localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "models": ["live-sonnet"],
  "metadata": {"logging": [{"callback_name": "langfuse_otel", "callback_type": "success",
    "callback_vars": {"langfuse_public_key": "pk-local", "langfuse_secret_key": "sk-local", "langfuse_host": "http://127.0.0.1:4318"}}]}}'

curl -sS localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "live-sonnet", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply only OK."}], "max_tokens": 16, "stream": false}'
```

Case B puts the same `logging` entry on a team via /team/new and makes the key on that team. Case C adds `"langfuse_span_scope": "full"` to `callback_vars`. Case E sets `callback_settings.otel.langfuse_destination_span_scope: llm_only` in the yaml with the env var unset. Case H uses an `arize` destination instead.

</details>

Full tree means `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `auth /v1/chat/completions`, `route live-sonnet`, `postgres.select LiteLLM_ModelAccessGroupBudgetTable`, `redis.pipeline router_cooldowns` and `chat live-sonnet`. Model-call only means `chat live-sonnet` alone, as a root span.

| Case | Before (49ea54ee7a) | After (914a850c07) |
|---|---|---|
| A. key entry, no scope, new env `llm_only` | full tree, 6 spans | `chat live-sonnet` only |
| B. team entry, no scope, new env `llm_only` | full tree, 6 spans | `chat live-sonnet` only |
| C. key entry `"full"`, new env `llm_only` | full tree | full tree |
| D. new env unset | full tree | full tree |
| E. yaml `callback_settings.otel` `llm_only` | full tree | `chat live-sonnet` only |
| F. new env `garbage` | full tree | full tree, 200, one warning per worker |
| G. old `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_SPAN_SCOPE=llm_only` only | full tree | full tree |
| H. arize destination, new env `llm_only` | full tree | full tree |

The new integration test `tests/integration/observability/test_langfuse_destination_span_scope.py` failed on the merge base for the key and team cases (`AssertionError: [('postgres.select LiteLLM_ModelAccessGroupBudgetTable', 3), ('auth /v1/chat/completions', 1), ...]`) and passes all 6 cases at the tip. `make lint` and the mapped OTel unit tests pass, and reverting the fallback fails the new unit tests. Later commits regenerate `schema.d.ts`, treat a null or non-mapping `callback_settings.otel` block as empty so tenant destinations still attach, and add integration cases for an explicit `llm_only` under env `full` and for an Arize destination. The integration file passes 15 of 15 at fc2fb5e with 2 workers, Postgres and Redis.

Follow-up at `f2e93c1755` restricts destination-default environment lookup to `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_DESTINATION_SPAN_SCOPE`. The unprefixed `langfuse_destination_span_scope` environment variable is ignored, while the configured value under `callback_settings.otel` still takes precedence. The new behavioral regression was red before the fix with 2 failed and 2 passed, and the complete OTel unit directory is green with 1303 passed. The original gauntlet alias reproducer no longer reproduces, and a local OTLP export probe confirms both corrected cases for keys and teams. Ruff and the strict-ruff and type-check gates pass. This follow-up did not rerun the full HTTP live A/B above.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Invalid value warns once per worker process, not once per proxy
- The setting is read once per process, so changing it needs a restart
- Docs for the new setting go in a separate litellm-docs PR

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which spans are exported to tenant Langfuse projects; behavior is gated by explicit overrides and safe fallbacks, but misconfiguration could hide infrastructure spans tenants previously saw by default.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **proxy-level default** for how much of each trace is sent to per-key and per-team **Langfuse OTel destinations**. Operators can set `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_DESTINATION_SPAN_SCOPE` (or `callback_settings.otel.langfuse_destination_span_scope`) to `llm_only` so tenants that only configure Langfuse credentials—without `langfuse_span_scope` on each key/team—receive **model-call spans only** instead of the full tree (auth, routing, Postgres, Redis, etc.). Explicit `langfuse_span_scope` on a destination still overrides; the existing `LITELLM_OTEL_LANGFUSE_SPAN_SCOPE` continues to scope only the **operator’s** Langfuse exporter, not tenant destinations.
> 
> Resolution is centralized via cached `langfuse_destination_span_scope()` with validation and a `full` fallback on invalid values. The dashboard logging UI and API docs now explain that leaving span scope empty follows the new proxy default.

title: feat(ui): reuse usage spend design for customer teams and members
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

use new customer management UI in all customer management tables

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session https://app.devin.ai/sessions/422007587178469292052a6a6cb39426

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Management tables lack the Usage page's detailed spend columns.
- Total-only reads download the organization's complete activity history.

How it solves it:

- Shares budget, spend, token and status cells across tables.
- Loads organization totals with one existing aggregate request.
- Uses main's exact singular organization filter.
- Keeps editing, scoped usage links and server pagination.

Intentional product change: Customer teams and Customer members replace simple recorded-spend and budget columns with monthly/yearly limits, spend share, tokens and status. Configured budget windows remain separate from calendar-month analytics.

The final commit is `c02cd2a40984aca7eb1034802da987c442ba861f`. After merging main at `03f14051`, the net diff is eight UI files. Main provides the singular `customer_org_id` API. This PR changes no backend code or schema.

## User Flow

Before, an admin must open Usage for detailed spend and caps.

1. Open `/ui/customers/manage?org=proof-51724-customer-01` and choose Customer teams.
2. See recorded spend and “No budget” for the concurrent-cap fixture.
3. Choose Customer members and see the same limited columns.
4. Use Next or Edit to reach the second page or settings.

![Before customer teams](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/911acb5e-a3af-4337-a206-0a3cf33956bc)

![Before customer members](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca195589-cb97-4e62-9e01-db29747a61ae)

After, the same rows expose spend and both configured caps.

1. Open `/ui/customers/manage?org=proof-51724-customer-01` and choose Customer teams.
2. See monthly/yearly budget progress, organization spend share, tokens and status.
3. Choose Customer members and see the matching details and customer teams.
4. Use Next or Edit to reach the same second-page row and settings.

![After customer teams](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b97b00fe-d9a2-4a6c-a4c1-f3bf351ba43d)

![After customer members](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddadbc2c-b15c-40d5-baa2-4740174bbf3e)

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Meaningful UI regression tests added and checked against prior code.
- [x] All 53 focused UI tests pass locally.
- [x] Dashboard typecheck and `make check` pass locally.
- [ ] Required CI checks on the latest commit have finished.
- [x] Changes are limited to the customer spend-table workflow.
- [ ] Automated reviews on the latest commit have finished.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The uploaded screenshots compare historical baseline `219c54ee1d073fbc6f288e8549358aa7d350424f` with `ae69b26ffd1e2283ebeb95187f0d715fdadecf90`. The 14-second recording below also comes from `ae69b26f`. It shows the real member table, page two, and the correct member settings entry with its inherited monthly/yearly profile. No settings save was exercised.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f25eabab-398b-4cf0-8455-7ef076aaa5fd

Both revisions used the same isolated PostgreSQL fixture and dedicated Redis, with two serving workers per proxy. No browser requests were intercepted. The table rendering remained equivalent after the main merge and affected paths were rechecked. The current browser check with frontend and backend both at `c02cd2a40984aca7eb1034802da987c442ba861f` confirmed member 01's $1.25/$10 monthly, $7.50/$100 yearly and 1.2K tokens. Its fresh reload recorded exactly three activity requests, all HTTP 200, including one organization aggregate request with singular `customer_org_id` and zero raw organization-history requests. Other application requests are outside that count.

The final proxy is now serving `c02cd2a40984aca7eb1034802da987c442ba861f` and passed all seven API/setup checks. The earlier comma-ID table capture used frontend `c02cd2a4` with the byte-identical backend from `5ec32f85`. All three exact-ID requests have now also passed against the final `c02cd2a4` proxy. The standalone recipe pins both frontend and backend to that final commit. The final helper applies the existing CSV validation only to child IDs and requires the exact organization ID to be nonempty. The comma-ID regression fails on `5ec32f85` and passes in the final 53-test run.

### Before (219c54ee1d073fbc6f288e8549358aa7d350424f)

1. Start the baseline proxy on 4194 and dashboard on 3123 using the recipe below. Log in with the local UI credentials.
2. Open customer 01, then Customer teams and Customer members. Both show recorded spend and “No budget” for multi-window caps, as captured above.
3. Click Next in Customer teams. Sample team 21 appears with $6.25 recorded spend. Edit opens that team's settings.

### After (c02cd2a40984aca7eb1034802da987c442ba861f)

1. Start the final proxy on 4195 and dashboard on 3124 against the same fixture database and Redis.
2. Open customer 01, then Customer teams and Customer members. Member 01 shows $1.25/$10 monthly, $7.50/$100 yearly and 1.2K tokens. Teams show $50/$500 caps.
3. Click Next in each table. The 21st row appears. Edit on member 21 opens the correct member and inherited profile. The recorded settings flow is shown in the video above.
4. Open member 21's Usage link. The recorded scoped flow retained organization, team and member selections and showed $6.25/$10 monthly, $37.50/$100 yearly and 25.2K tokens.
5. Open `/ui/customers/manage?org=exact-id-proof-51724%2Corg` after the optional seed. On final `c02cd2a4`, both Customer teams and Customer members show $47, 517 tokens and 100% organization share.

The final singular-ID API proof at `c02cd2a4` returned $11 for `exact-id-proof-51724-org`, $29 for ` exact-id-proof-51724-org ` with surrounding spaces preserved, and $47 for `exact-id-proof-51724,org`. All three requests passed. It exercises main's existing exact filter through the real proxy. The portable fixture and final requests appear below. No provider calls were needed for the exact-ID or comma-ID checks.

The original 21 customer fixtures remain intact. Two plain/whitespace-ID organizations brought the API list to 23, and the later comma-ID organization brings it to 24. The final API verification passed with organization pages of 20+4 and team/member pages of 20+1 within customer 01. The historical baseline organization screenshot has 21 customers.

The completed final validation passed 53 focused UI tests, dashboard typecheck and `make check`. The two large-history UI regressions fail on the original PR implementation, and the comma-ID regression fails on `5ec32f85`. `make check` ran dashboard formatting, ESLint and lint budgets. Python and generated API-type gates were skipped because no relevant files changed in the final net diff. This is not a claim that Python gates ran.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation commands</summary>

Run from the final checkout root.

```sh
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npx vitest run 'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/manage/page.integration.test.tsx' 'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/usage/page.integration.test.tsx' 'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/customerUsageApi.test.ts' 'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/useCustomerHierarchy.test.ts'
npm run typecheck
cd ../../..
make check
```

The initial recording used the supported Webpack development command. Scoped Usage used standard `npm run dev` after Webpack rejected an existing unrelated SVG import. No source workaround was applied. The recipe uses baseline `npm run dev:webpack` on 3123 and final `npm run dev` on 3124, with explicit API base and rewrite settings.

</details>

### Standalone local QA recipe

This recipe contains the helper, seed, verifier, and actual proxy configuration. It does not depend on the author's scratch files. Use it in an empty local directory with Git, Docker, Python 3.13, uv, Node/npm, and the Rust toolchain specified by the repository. Supply an authorized OpenAI-compatible upstream through environment variables. No credential values are included.

The baseline is `219c54ee1d073fbc6f288e8549358aa7d350424f`. The final revision is `c02cd2a40984aca7eb1034802da987c442ba861f`. The uploaded after screenshots and video were captured at `ae69b26ffd1e2283ebeb95187f0d715fdadecf90`. The current member-page reload and all three singular-ID API checks were verified with both frontend and backend at `c02cd2a4`. The earlier comma-ID table capture used frontend `c02cd2a4` with the byte-identical backend from `5ec32f85`. The older uploaded captures retain their original SHA, and rendering equivalence was checked on the current member table. This recipe starts the final proxy from the final pinned commit.

Both revisions use one dedicated local PostgreSQL database and Redis, with two workers each. The configuration points both router state and coordination counters at that Redis. Baseline serves on loopback port 4194 and final on 4195. Ports 59174 and 59175 are reserved for the database and Redis. Use free ports or stop only your previous reproduction before starting.

The initial fixture has 21 generic customers. Customer `proof-51724-customer-01` has 21 teams and 21 members. The other 20 customers have one team/member each. Management APIs create five customers, nine teams and nine members within free-tier limits. Additional pagination rows and readable historical spend are imported into the isolated database. No licensing source or limits are changed. This demonstrates table behavior over existing records, not licensed bulk creation or real billed historical spend. The optional exact-ID check adds three separate organizations, two plain/whitespace fixtures and one comma-ID fixture, making 24 in total while leaving the original 21 intact. The recorded team and member lists each contain 20+1 rows within the focused customer. The final `c02cd2a4` API check verified all 24 organizations in pages of 20+4. The baseline screenshot has the original 21 organizations. All seven final API/setup checks passed, including exact fixture membership, monthly/yearly member caps, dated aggregate usage, login and two serving workers.

Every member in the original fixture has a $10 monthly and $100 yearly policy, with separate nonzero window usage. Teams have $50/$500 caps and organizations have $500/$5,000 caps. The seed uses the local calendar day for visible daily history and the previous month for earlier history. Select the `date` in `fixtures.json` in both dashboards. Within the year, the original 21 customers' synthetic selected-day totals are $156.25, 871 requests and 553,200 tokens. The focused customer has $78.75 monthly history and $472.50 annual window usage. The three exact-ID organizations are outside those totals. The January prior-month row falls in the previous year, so the fixture is intended for reproducing the recorded November layout, not validating calendar reset logic.

The recorded setup made two separate real provider calls on November 14 UTC, both HTTP 200, totaling 29 tokens and $0.000065. The displayed historical day was November 13. Historical fixture totals are not provider billing. The optional verifier makes at most two small calls per revision with 32 output tokens, no retry and a local service key capped at $0.15 for 12 hours. Re-running it retains the saved smoke evidence instead of repeating inference.

Main merged at `03f14051` and supplies the exact singular `customer_org_id` aggregate filter. This PR's net diff contains eight UI files and no backend or schema changes. Compared with the older screenshot baseline, main adds exactly four schema fields, `LiteLLM_BudgetTable.budget_reset_count Int @default(0)` and nullable `spend_reset_window String?` on `LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable`, `LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable`, and `LiteLLM_EndUserTable`. The recipe validates the complete schema delta before applying it.

The recorded local proof reused a checksum-recorded native extension and an isolated copy of an existing Python runtime. The fresh-install commands below build dependencies for the selected revisions. This document was checked offline; a second fresh environment was not started merely to publish it.

<details>
<summary>Checkout, dependency installation, configuration and commands</summary>

Start in a new empty directory using the pinned final commit below. Load `LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY` from your approved secret manager and set `PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE` to its authorized compatible endpoint. The configured upstream model name is `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`, forwarded through LiteLLM's OpenAI adapter. If your endpoint uses a different identifier, record that change to the configuration and cost rates.

```sh
set -eu
umask 077
export FINAL_SHA=c02cd2a40984aca7eb1034802da987c442ba861f
python3 -c 'import os,re; assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", os.environ["FINAL_SHA"]), "FINAL_SHA must be a full reviewed commit"'
: "${LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY:?Load an authorized upstream credential}"
: "${PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE:?Set the authorized compatible endpoint base URL}"
export LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE
export PROOF_ROOT="$PWD/proof-51724-reproduction"
mkdir "$PROOF_ROOT"
git clone https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm.git "$PROOF_ROOT/repository"
git -C "$PROOF_ROOT/repository" fetch origin "$FINAL_SHA"
git -C "$PROOF_ROOT/repository" worktree add --detach "$PROOF_ROOT/before" 219c54ee1d073fbc6f288e8549358aa7d350424f
git -C "$PROOF_ROOT/repository" worktree add --detach "$PROOF_ROOT/after" "$FINAL_SHA"
uv sync --project "$PROOF_ROOT/before" --python 3.13 --frozen --no-dev --extra proxy --extra proxy-runtime --group proxy-dev
uv sync --project "$PROOF_ROOT/after" --python 3.13 --frozen --no-dev --extra proxy --extra proxy-runtime --group proxy-dev
cd "$PROOF_ROOT"
```

Save the complete Python blocks below as `ops.py`, `seed.py`, and `verify.py` in this directory. Save this YAML as `proxy-config.yaml`, then copy it to `final-proxy-config.yaml`. `ops.py validate_schema` checks both committed schema files and rejects every difference except the four additions named above. Each `prepare` repeats that check before touching the database. There is no schema bypass.

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: proof-gpt-6.1-terra
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/openai/gpt-6.1-terra
      api_base: os.environ/PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY
      max_retries: 0
    model_info:
      input_cost_per_token: 0.000001
      output_cost_per_token: 0.000005
router_settings:
  redis_host: os.environ/PROOF_REDIS_HOST
  redis_port: os.environ/PROOF_REDIS_PORT
  num_retries: 0
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: os.environ/PROOF_REDIS_HOST
    port: os.environ/PROOF_REDIS_PORT
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
  set_verbose: false
  success_callback: []
  failure_callback: []
```

The launcher generates `credentials.json` with mode 0600, containing fresh local login and database credentials. It never prints their values. Login uses its `ui_username` and `ui_password` fields. The upstream key stays in the environment.

Use the recorded sequential setup below. Apply the baseline schema to an empty dedicated database, generate its client in `before/.venv`, and seed the original fixture. Then `prepare --variant final` generates a separate client in `after/.venv` and applies the four reviewed additions to the same database. This is the recorded incremental setup. The schema push never uses `--accept-data-loss` and any unexpected change stops the recipe. Do not apply the baseline schema again after this step. This setup does not validate a production migration.

```sh
cp proxy-config.yaml final-proxy-config.yaml
docker pull postgres@sha256:0cefaabd882e42bcb2a2f3dc56d3ce4770560ba62fd7f197f1a2e008fd5731ab
docker pull redis@sha256:6ba19c50b56777f5c11c58eff8ddb69d0d5f27ba131cffb63f180ccfd43c66af
python3 ops.py prepare
python3 ops.py start
python3 ops.py wait_ready
python3 ops.py status
python3 ops.py login
before/.venv/bin/python seed.py
python3 verify.py --smoke
python3 ops.py prepare --variant final
python3 ops.py start --variant final
python3 ops.py wait_ready --variant final
python3 ops.py status --variant final
python3 verify.py --variant final
```

`wait_ready` fails after a bounded wait if startup does not finish. Inspect the `two worker processes` result in each verification JSON. The observed baseline supports two workers with reload enabled. If another checkout prints that reload ignores the worker count, follow that checkout's AGENTS instructions and disclose the serving difference.

The actual serving command is run in each revision's source root using its Python environment. The final command changes the config to `final-proxy-config.yaml` and port to 4195.

```sh
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config "$PROOF_ROOT/proxy-config.yaml" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4194 --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

The helper supplies `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`, `PROOF_REDIS_HOST`, `PROOF_REDIS_PORT`, `PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP`, `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE`, `PYTHONPATH`, and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`. The required upstream key variable is `LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY`. Do not put credentials in source, URLs, localStorage or a PR body.

For dashboard proof, open separate terminals in the reproduction directory and run the corresponding block. Baseline uses Webpack on 3123 and final uses the standard development server on 3124. The explicit API base and rewrite target both point at that revision's actual proxy.

```sh
export PROOF_ROOT="$PWD"
test -f "$PROOF_ROOT/ops.py"
cd "$PROOF_ROOT/before/litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard"
npm ci
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4194 \
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4194 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true \
npm run dev:webpack -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3123
```

```sh
export PROOF_ROOT="$PWD"
test -f "$PROOF_ROOT/ops.py"
cd "$PROOF_ROOT/after/litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard"
npm ci
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4195 \
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4195 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true \
npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3124
```

Use the normal login pages at `http://127.0.0.1:3123/ui/login` and `http://127.0.0.1:3124/ui/login`. Read `ui_username` and `ui_password` from the local credential file without publishing them. Open `/ui/customers/manage?org=proof-51724-customer-01`, select Customer teams and Customer members, and paginate each to row 21. Open Edit to check the settings entry and the member's Usage link to check the retained organization/team/member scope. For Usage, select the saved fixture date. Settings saves were not exercised. Record both Git SHAs alongside the captures.

With frontend and backend both at `c02cd2a4`, a fresh member-page reload recorded exactly three activity requests, all HTTP 200. Two were scoped child-period reads and one was `/management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity/aggregated` with singular `customer_org_id=proof-51724-customer-01`. There were no raw organization-history requests. Inspect those activity requests in browser Network after reloading the same route. This success count concerns activity requests, not every application request. At `c02cd2a4`, the separate comma-ID customer showed $47, 517 tokens and 100% organization share in both management tables. The 53 focused UI tests, typecheck and `make check` passed. The comma-ID regression fails on `5ec32f85`.

The optional final-only exact-ID recipe below reproduces the plain, whitespace-surrounded and comma-ID fixtures. It uses main's singular field. The final management helper accepts nonempty organization IDs without applying the child filter's CSV restrictions. Detailed Usage still has a legacy CSV limitation for comma-containing organization IDs.

To stop only the owned reproduction, stop the dashboards in their terminals, then run the following from the reproduction directory. Database state is retained.

```sh
python3 ops.py stop --variant final
python3 ops.py stop
docker stop pr-51724-reproduction-db pr-51724-reproduction-redis
```

Raw detailed logs are restricted and may contain secrets. Share only sanitized logs and credential-scanned evidence.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Complete ops.py</summary>

```python
import argparse
import base64
import json
import os
import re
import secrets
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SOURCE = ROOT / "before"
PYTHON = ROOT / "before/.venv/bin/python"
API = "http://127.0.0.1:4194"
FILE_PREFIX = ""
OWNER = "pr-51724-reproduction"
DB = OWNER + "-db"
REDIS = OWNER + "-redis"
CREDENTIALS = ROOT / "credentials.json"
os.umask(0o077)


def configure(variant):
    global SOURCE, API, FILE_PREFIX, PYTHON
    if variant == "final":
        SOURCE = ROOT / "after"
        PYTHON = SOURCE / ".venv/bin/python"
        API = "http://127.0.0.1:4195"
        FILE_PREFIX = "final-"


def save(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n")
    path.chmod(0o600)


def credentials():
    if not CREDENTIALS.exists():
        save(CREDENTIALS, {
            "ui_username": "review-admin",
            "ui_password": secrets.token_urlsafe(24),
            "master_key": "sk-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(32),
            "database_password": secrets.token_urlsafe(24),
        })
    return json.loads(CREDENTIALS.read_text())


def environment():
    c = credentials()
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k in (
        "PATH", "HOME", "TMPDIR", "LANG", "LC_ALL", "SSL_CERT_FILE", "SSL_CERT_DIR",
        "LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY", "PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE", "HTTPS_PROXY", "HTTP_PROXY", "NO_PROXY",
    )}
    env.update({
        "PATH": str(PYTHON.parent) + os.pathsep + env.get("PATH", ""),
        "PYTHONPATH": str(SOURCE),
        "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
        "DATABASE_URL": f"postgresql://proof51724:{c['database_password']}@127.0.0.1:59174/proof51724",
        "LITELLM_MASTER_KEY": c["master_key"],
        "UI_USERNAME": c["ui_username"],
        "UI_PASSWORD": c["ui_password"],
        "STORE_MODEL_IN_DB": "False",
        "DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE": "true",
        "LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP": "True",
        "LITELLM_SKIP_INTRO": "true",
        "PROOF_REDIS_HOST": "127.0.0.1",
        "PROOF_REDIS_PORT": "59175",
        "PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE": os.environ["PROOF_UPSTREAM_BASE"],
    })
    return env


def redact(text):
    values = list(credentials().values())
    values.extend(v for k, v in environment().items() if any(s in k for s in ("KEY", "PASSWORD", "DATABASE_URL")))
    for value in sorted(values, key=len, reverse=True):
        if isinstance(value, str) and len(value) >= 6:
            text = text.replace(value, "[REDACTED]")
    text = re.sub(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}", "[REDACTED_KEY]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", "[REDACTED_TOKEN]", text)

def command(args, *, env=None, cwd=ROOT, log=None):

        "after": os.environ.get("FINAL_SHA", ""),
    }
    schemas = {}
    for variant, revision in revisions.items():
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", revision):
            raise SystemExit("Set FINAL_SHA to the reviewed full commit SHA")
        source = ROOT / variant
        head = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(source), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
        if head != revision:
            raise SystemExit(f"{variant} checkout does not match its pinned revision")
        committed = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "-C", str(source), "show", revision + ":litellm/schema.prisma"])
        actual = (source / "litellm/schema.prisma").read_bytes()
        if actual != committed:
            raise SystemExit(f"{variant} schema differs from committed source")
        schemas[variant] = actual.decode()
    allowed = {
        "LiteLLM_BudgetTable": "  budget_reset_count Int @default(0)\n",
        "LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable": "  spend_reset_window String?\n",
        "LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable": "  spend_reset_window String?\n",
        "LiteLLM_EndUserTable": "  spend_reset_window String?\n",
    }
    model = None
    seen = set()
    retained = []
    for line in schemas["after"].splitlines(keepends=True):
        if line.startswith("model "):
            model = line.split()[1]
        if model in allowed and line == allowed[model]:
            if model in seen:
                raise SystemExit("Duplicate allowed schema field")
            seen.add(model)
            continue
        retained.append(line)
        if line.strip() == "}":
            model = None
    if seen != set(allowed) or "".join(retained) != schemas["before"]:
        raise SystemExit("Unexpected schema delta. Stop and review, do not bypass this check")

                                          "validate_schema", "wait_ready"])
    parser.add_argument("--variant", choices=["baseline", "final"], default="baseline")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    configure(args.variant)
```
