```python
"""Local Langfuse prompt fixture: serves GET /api/public/v2/prompts/<name> to the real Langfuse SDK."""
import json, sys, threading
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, unquote, parse_qs

PORT = int(sys.argv[1]); LOG = sys.argv[2]
TIERS = {"langfuse-quick": ("quick", 0.42, 31), "langfuse-deep": ("deep", 0.82, 63)}
lock = threading.Lock()

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def _send(self, code, obj):
        data = json.dumps(obj).encode()
        self.send_response(code); self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(data)
    def _log(self, method, status):
        u = urlparse(self.path)
        with lock, open(LOG, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"method": method, "path": u.path, "query": parse_qs(u.query), "status": status}) + "\n")
    def do_GET(self):
        u = urlparse(self.path); prefix = "/api/public/v2/prompts/"
        name = unquote(u.path[len(prefix):]) if u.path.startswith(prefix) else None
        if name not in TIERS:
            self._log("GET", 404); return self._send(404, {"message": "not found", "error": "NotFound"})
        tier, temperature, limit = TIERS[name]
        self._log("GET", 200)
        self._send(200, {"id": "fixture-" + name, "name": name, "version": 1, "type": "chat",
            "prompt": [{"role": "system", "content": f"Langfuse {tier}."}],
            "config": {"temperature": temperature, "max_tokens": limit},
            "labels": ["production", "latest"], "tags": [], "commitMessage": None, "resolutionGraph": None,
            "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "updatedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
            "createdBy": "fixture", "projectId": "fixture"})
    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
        self._log("POST", 207); self._send(207, {"successes": [], "errors": []})

ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), H).serve_forever()
```

```python
from litellm.integrations.dotprompt.dotprompt_manager import DotpromptManager
UP = sys.argv[1]; BASE = f"http://127.0.0.1:{UP}/v1"; DEAD = "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1"
MSG = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]
GEN = ("model", "temperature", "max_tokens", "top_p", "top_k")
def caps(): return httpx.get(f"http://127.0.0.1:{UP}/__captures").json()
async def case(name, **kw):
    before = len(caps())
    try:
        await litellm.acompletion(messages=MSG, api_key="k", num_retries=0, **kw); err = None
    except Exception as e:
        err = f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:160]}"
    new = caps()[before:]
    print("CASE", json.dumps({"case": name, "error": err, "upstream_calls": len(new),
          "sent": [{k: c["body"].get(k, "absent") for k in GEN} | {"system_msgs": sum(m["role"] == "system" for m in c["body"]["messages"])} for c in new]}))
async def main():
    litellm.callbacks = [DotpromptManager(prompt_data={"pinned": {"content": "System: Pinned prompt.", "metadata": {"temperature": 0.42, "max_tokens": 31, "top_k": 5}}})]
    C = dict(temperature=0, top_p=0)
    await case("no-hook", model="openai/plain", api_base=BASE, **C)
    await case("no-hook+extra-kwargs", model="openai/plain", api_base=BASE, top_k=3, max_tokens=7, **C)
    await case("prompt", model="openai/plain", api_base=BASE, prompt_id="pinned", **C)
    await case("prompt+extra-kwargs", model="openai/plain", api_base=BASE, prompt_id="pinned", top_k=3, max_tokens=7, **C)
    await case("prompt+ignore-request-flag", model="openai/plain", api_base=BASE, prompt_id="pinned", ignore_prompt_manager_optional_params=True, top_k=3, **C)
    await case("fallback-dict,no-hook", model="openai/primary", api_base=DEAD, fallbacks=[{"model": "openai/backup", "api_base": BASE}], **C)
    await case("fallback-dict,prompt", model="openai/primary", api_base=DEAD, prompt_id="pinned", fallbacks=[{"model": "openai/backup", "api_base": BASE}], top_k=3, **C)
    await case("fallback-dict,prompt,primary-ok", model="openai/plain", api_base=BASE, prompt_id="pinned", fallbacks=[{"model": "openai/backup", "api_base": BASE}], **C)
asyncio.run(main())
```

Run from the source checkout with `.venv/bin/python <rig>/kit/sdk_controls.py 18082` against the fixture capture on each revision

</details>

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Low

- Duplicate prompt text and version pinning remain tracked in #41735
- Langfuse prompts use an HTTP fixture, not Langfuse cloud

## Final Attestation

- [x] Tests and live verification cover the changed behavior and its relevant edge cases

</details>

title: fix(bedrock): log and bill Titan embedding replies on the invoke passthrough
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description Titan embedding calls sent through the Bedrock `/invoke` passthrough returned their vector but crashed success logging, so they were never billed or written to spend logs, and this logs them as embeddings with the provider's token count and image charge.
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/43459a5a05eb45cc9236739953196546 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/43459a5a05eb45cc9236739953196546?variant=devin Requested by: @kenneth-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Titan embedding calls on Bedrock `/invoke` passthrough are never billed - Success logging crashes, so no spend log row is written How it solves it: - Recognize a Titan embedding reply before the chat reader runs - Log it as an embedding with the provider's input token count - Accept Titan v2 replies that only carry `embeddingsByType` - Count the request's `inputImage` so the per-image price applies - Every other `/invoke` reply keeps the existing chat path ## User Flow Before: a developer calling Titan embeddings through the Bedrock passthrough gets their vector, but the call is never billed or logged 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/bedrock/model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0/invoke with `{"inputText": "..."}` 2. They get 200 with the 1024-number `embedding` and `inputTextTokenCount` 3. The `x-litellm-response-cost-original` response header reads `0.0` 4. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id= returns an empty list After: the same call is billed and logged with the provider's token count 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/bedrock/model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0/invoke 2. They get the same 200 with the `embedding` and `inputTextTokenCount` 3. The `x-litellm-response-cost-original` header carries the real cost 4. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id= returns one row with matching prompt tokens and spend ## Relevant issues Fixes #51455 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxies with Postgres and real Bedrock calls in `us-east-1`, no mocks. Both sides ran two workers with `--reload` against one shared local Redis, and two worker PIDs were serving on each port. Env var names used are `DATABASE_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (the value set as `master_key` below), and AWS credentials come from the `litellm-dev` profile. Four calls were made on each side, a Titan v2 text call, a Titan v2 call with `embeddingTypes: ["binary"]`, an image-only Titan multimodal call, and a Titan multimodal call with an image and text. `config.yaml` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 litellm_params: model: bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 aws_profile_name: litellm-dev aws_region_name: us-east-1 - model_name: amazon.titan-embed-image-v1 litellm_params: model: bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-image-v1 aws_profile_name: litellm-dev aws_region_name: us-east-1 router_settings: redis_host: localhost redis_port: 6379 general_settings: master_key: coordination_redis: host: localhost port: 6379 ``` Proxy start ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4155 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver > proxy.log 2>&1 ```
Client script, run as ./run_cases.sh 4155 proxy.log `image_body.json` is `{"inputImage": ""}`, and `image_text_body.json` adds `"inputText": "a red square"` to it. ```bash #!/bin/bash PORT=$1; LOG=$2 call() { curl -s -D hdr_$1.txt -o body_$1.json -X POST localhost:$PORT/bedrock/model/$2/invoke \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @$3 echo "== $1"; grep -i -E "^HTTP|cost-original" hdr_$1.txt | tr -d '\r' python3 -c " import json;b=json.load(open('body_$1.json')) v=b.get('embedding') or b['embeddingsByType']['binary'] print('keys',sorted(b),'vector_len',len(v),'inputTextTokenCount',b['inputTextTokenCount'])" } echo '{"inputText":"hello from the litellm passthrough"}' > req_float.json echo '{"inputText":"hello from the litellm passthrough","embeddingTypes":["binary"]}' > req_binary.json call float amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 req_float.json call binary amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 req_binary.json call image amazon.titan-embed-image-v1 image_body.json call image_text amazon.titan-embed-image-v1 image_text_body.json sleep 20 echo "crash lines in proxy log: $(grep -c "object is not subscriptable" $LOG)" for c in float binary image image_text; do CID=$(grep -i x-litellm-call-id hdr_$c.txt | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\r') echo "== spend log $c" curl -s "localhost:$PORT/spend/logs?request_id=$CID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" | python3 -c " import json,sys d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d),'row(s)') for r in d: print({k:r.get(k) for k in ['model','spend','prompt_tokens','total_tokens','status']})" done ```
### Before (bad8b1dae8) Every call returns its vector, the cost header is zero, the log has the crash, and no spend row is written ``` == float HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 keys ['embedding', 'embeddingsByType', 'inputTextTokenCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 9 == binary HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 keys ['embeddingsByType', 'inputTextTokenCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 9 == image HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 keys ['embedding', 'failureCount', 'inputTextTokenCount', 'message', 'results', 'successCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 0 == image_text HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 keys ['embedding', 'failureCount', 'inputTextTokenCount', 'message', 'results', 'successCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 5 crash lines in proxy log: 28 == spend log float 0 row(s) == spend log binary 0 row(s) == spend log image 0 row(s) == spend log image_text 0 row(s) ``` ### After (bdb3ea3c26) The same calls return the same shapes. The text and binary calls cost 9 tokens at the Titan v2 input price, the image call costs one image at the Titan multimodal image price, the image plus text call costs one image plus 5 tokens, and each has a spend row ``` == float HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 1.8e-07 keys ['embedding', 'embeddingsByType', 'inputTextTokenCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 9 == binary HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 1.8e-07 keys ['embeddingsByType', 'inputTextTokenCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 9 == image HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 6e-05 keys ['embedding', 'failureCount', 'inputTextTokenCount', 'message', 'results', 'successCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 0 == image_text HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 6.4e-05 keys ['embedding', 'failureCount', 'inputTextTokenCount', 'message', 'results', 'successCount'] vector_len 1024 inputTextTokenCount 5 crash lines in proxy log: 0 == spend log float 1 row(s) {'model': 'bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0', 'spend': 1.8e-07, 'prompt_tokens': 9, 'total_tokens': 9, 'status': 'success'} == spend log binary 1 row(s) {'model': 'bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0', 'spend': 1.8e-07, 'prompt_tokens': 9, 'total_tokens': 9, 'status': 'success'} == spend log image 1 row(s) {'model': 'bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-image-v1', 'spend': 6e-05, 'prompt_tokens': 0, 'total_tokens': 0, 'status': 'success'} == spend log image_text 1 row(s) {'model': 'bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-image-v1', 'spend': 6.4e-05, 'prompt_tokens': 5, 'total_tokens': 5, 'status': 'success'} ``` Regression test: `uv run pytest tests/unit/llms/bedrock/passthrough/test_bedrock_passthrough_transformation.py -k titan` gives 8 failed and 1 passed with the fix reverted (the Titan chat control passes) and 9 passed at bdb3ea3c26. `make check` passes at bdb3ea3c26. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - Cohere embed replies on `/invoke` still take the chat path - Titan text v1 and G1 are unit tested only, not called live - The spend row keeps `call_type` `allm_passthrough_route`, like other passthrough rows ### Low - The Llama streaming token count failure in the issue's script is a separate bug, not fixed here ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: fix(logging): keep a content-block system prompt in logged messages
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

system prompt block lists now go in standard logging payload instead of being thrown away 
<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

- When you send a system prompt as a list of blocks to `/v1/messages`, your logs never showed it
- Claude Code sends it that way, so its instructions were missing from every logger
- Now the logs show it as the first message, the same place plain text already goes
- Plain-text system prompts on direct Anthropic look exactly like before
- On Claude through Vertex, even plain text was missing before, and now it shows up

## User Flow

Before: a team logs every Claude Code call through the proxy to S3, and the system prompt is missing from each saved record

1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with `"system": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are a code reviewer.", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}]`
2. The model answers with a 200 as usual
3. The saved log record's `messages` holds only the user turn, so there is no trace of the instructions the model got

After: the same call is logged with its system prompt

1. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with the same list of blocks
2. The model answers with a 200 as usual
3. The saved log record's `messages` starts with a `system` entry holding those blocks, followed by the user turn

## Relevant issues

Fixes #36402

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Two proxies ran side by side against real Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Vertex, each with 2 workers sharing one Redis on port 46402. No Anthropic API key was reachable on the test machine, so Vertex stands in for the provider. The logging step this PR changes runs after the provider call and is the same for both providers. Direct Anthropic is covered by the new unit test below, which fails on main for a list of blocks and passes for plain text.

`LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION` is set on both only so the proxy skips auto-loading a parent `.env` that points at a shared Postgres. It changes nothing else.

Proxy command, run from each checkout

```
LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=<service account json> \
  python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <44371 before, 44372 after> \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Both logs show two `Started server process` lines.

<details>
<summary>config.yaml and the logger it loads</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: sonnet
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-5-5
      vertex_project: <gcp project>
      vertex_location: global

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: record_messages.recorder

router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 46402

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-qa-36402-live
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 46402
```

`record_messages.py`, next to config.yaml

```python
import json
import os

from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger

OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "logged.jsonl")


class RecordMessages(CustomLogger):
    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        record = {"pid": os.getpid(), "messages": kwargs["standard_logging_object"]["messages"]}
        with open(OUT, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")


recorder = RecordMessages()
```

</details>

Request, with `SYS` set per case

```bash
curl -s "http://localhost:$PORT/v1/messages" \
  -H "x-api-key: sk-qa-36402-live" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"sonnet\",\"max_tokens\":64,\"system\":$SYS,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Say hi in 3 words\"}]}"
```

### Before (143b4b7)

#### System prompt as a list of blocks

1. `SYS='[{"type":"text","text":"You are a code reviewer. BLOCK-SHAPE-MARKER","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]'` and send it, response `HTTP 200` with `"text":"Hello, nice day!"`
2. Logged record, the system prompt is gone

```
{"pid": 2889, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in 3 words"}]}
```

#### System prompt as plain text

1. `SYS='"You are a code reviewer. TEXT-SHAPE-MARKER"'` and send it, response `HTTP 200` with `"text":"Hello, nice meeting you!"`
2. Logged record, the system prompt is also gone, because the proxy turns it into blocks for Vertex before logging

```
{"pid": 2889, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in 3 words"}]}
```

### After (02aa8f8)

#### System prompt as a list of blocks

1. Same request, response `HTTP 200` with `"text":"Hello, hi there!"`
2. Logged record starts with the system prompt, blocks as sent

```
{"pid": 2893, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are a code reviewer. BLOCK-SHAPE-MARKER", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in 3 words"}]}
```

#### System prompt as plain text

1. Same request, response `HTTP 200` with `"text":"Hello, kind reviewer!"`
2. Logged record starts with the system prompt

```
{"pid": 2893, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are a code reviewer. TEXT-SHAPE-MARKER"}]}, {"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in 3 words"}]}
```

Neither proxy log has a traceback or a logging error.

#### Tests

`test_anthropic_messages_system_prompt_reaches_logged_messages` sends a real `/v1/messages` call through the SDK to a fake Anthropic HTTP server and checks what a logger gets. With main's logging code swapped in, the list-of-blocks case fails (`At index 0 diff: {'role': 'user', ...} != {'role': 'system', 'content': [{'type': 'text', ...}]}`) and plain text passes. On this branch both pass.

Mutations of the fix, each one restored after the run

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Stop accepting a list of blocks | 1 failed |
| Accept an empty list | 1 failed |
| Drop the check that skips a system prompt already in first place | 2 failed |

`tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_litellm_logging.py`, `tests/unit/router_utils/pre_call_checks/test_prompt_caching_deployment_check.py` and `tests/unit/router_utils/test_prompt_caching_cache.py` give 976 passed. The prompt caching files matter because prompt cache routing reads these logged messages and adds the system prompt itself, skipping it when it is already first, so the block list is not counted twice.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- On Vertex, a plain-text system prompt is logged as blocks, not a string
  - That's the shape the proxy actually sent, and before it wasn't logged at all
- Not run live against direct Anthropic, the unit test covers that route

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(customer-portal): keep existing memberships and scope free tier capacity locks
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

fix bot findings from enterprise gate on customer portal

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9981b693bc354726b4779f72dc737082
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/9981b693bc354726b4779f72dc737082?variant=devin
Requested by: @moe-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Existing members got 403 on retry or alias update at 5 teams
- One global lock serialized every free tier create

How it solves it:

- Member upsert without a team keeps current memberships, skips default team
- Team and member locks are scoped to their parent org or team
- Lock waits time out after one second
- Management API returns 503 retryable on contention, requests still run untracked

Follow-up to #51687 for Greptile findings 4567751618 and 4567416845.

## User Flow

Before: an existing member in an org with 5 non-default teams cannot be retried or renamed

1. Admin upserts member `m1` (already in `team-0`) with no `parent_team_id`
2. Proxy tries to create the org's `default` team, hits the 5 team cap, returns 403

After: the same upsert keeps the member where they are

1. Admin upserts member `m1` (already in `team-0`) with no `parent_team_id`
2. Proxy returns 200 and memberships stay `['team-0']`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both proxies ran `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config customer_portal_dev_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver`, base on port 4003 and head on 4000, sharing a dedicated Redis on 6381, with no license so `limits_apply` was true on both. Env vars are `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL`. The client script calls the `/management/v1` customer endpoints and holds advisory locks from a separate Postgres connection

### Before (1a682f9dbf)

1. Existing member retry and alias update in an org with 5 non-default teams

```text
Before existing member retry HTTP 403 memberships None
Before existing member alias update HTTP 403 memberships None
```

2. A create in an unrelated org while the global capacity lock is held

```text
Before create still waits after eight seconds while global capacity lock is held
```

### After (84158d704a)

1. Same retry and alias update

```text
After existing member retry HTTP 200 memberships ['qa-followup-team-0']
After existing member alias update HTTP 200 memberships ['qa-followup-team-0']
```

2. Same unrelated create, then a create while its own parent lock is held

```text
After independent organization create while global capacity lock is held HTTP 201
(503, {'type': 'urn:litellm:error:customer-hierarchy-capacity-busy', 'title': 'Customer portal busy', 'status': 503, 'detail': 'Customer portal capacity is being updated. Retry the request.'})
```

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- `lock_timeout` is set for the whole transaction, so any lock wait over 1s maps to 503
- On the request path, a busy lock means the new customer stays untracked for that request
- Overflow members still skip default team policies, see Veria 4567350654 on #51687

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes advisory locking, lock timeouts, and member upsert team resolution on the free-tier enforcement path; mis-handling could allow limit bypass or spurious 503s under load.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes free-tier customer portal behavior when orgs hit team caps and under advisory lock contention.
> 
> **Member upsert** no longer forces default-team resolution when `parent_team_id` is omitted on an existing member; memberships stay unchanged on retry/alias updates instead of failing the org’s five-team cap.
> 
> **Capacity locking** is narrowed: team limits lock per org (`teams:{org_id}`), member limits per team (`members:{team_id}`), with a 1s Postgres `lock_timeout`. Lock timeout (`55P03`) maps to new **`CAPACITY_BUSY`** → **503** “Customer portal busy” (retryable); other DB errors still propagate.
> 
> Tests cover upsert retention, scoped lock isolation, and 503 vs non-retryable errors.
>

## Summary Runway's pricing page and changelog now list a 4K output rate for Seedance 2.5, and `runwayml/seedance2_5` had no 4K price, so a 4K generation was costed at the 720p base rate. This adds `output_cost_per_second_4k` to the row, in the same field `runwayml/seedance2` already uses for its 4K rate. No other runwayml row differs from the pricing page ## Rows | Key | Field | Old | New | Kind | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `runwayml/seedance2_5` | `output_cost_per_second_4k` | absent | 1.1 | page | | `runwayml/seedance2_5` | `metadata.comment` | 480p/720p/1080p rates only | adds the 4K rate and the 57 credits per input second that is not modeled | page | ## Evidence Source https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing.md, fetched raw on 2026-11-13. The Video Generation Pricing table has this row > | `seedance2_5` (4K) | 110 credits per second of output, plus 57 credits per second of input and reference video (combined video capped at 30 seconds); reference images and audio are free (80 credit minimum per generation) | The same page states the dollar value of a credit in its worked example, "At 4K, a 5-second Seedance 2.5 generation without video references costs 550 credits ($5.50)", so 110 credits per second is $1.10 per second The changelog at https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/api-details/api_changelog.md agrees in its November 11th, 2026 entry "Seedance 2.5 4K" > Billed at 110 credits per second of output, plus 57 credits per second of input and reference video, with the same 80 credit minimum The 480p, 720p and 1080p rates on the row (20, 30 and 68 credits per second) still match the page and are unchanged. Input and reference video charges and the 80 credit minimum stay unmodeled, as they already were for the other resolutions ## Test change `test_aaamodel_prices_and_context_window_json_is_valid` rejected this row because `validate_model_cost_values` in `tests/unit/test_utils.py` capped every price field at 1, and a 4K second costs 1.1. The cap is now 1000 for per-second, per-image, per-request and per-query fields, where prices above a dollar are real, and stays at 1 for per-token, per-character and per-pixel fields, so a per-token price typed as dollars per million still fails. The nine seedance model ids that were exempted from the check one by one are removed from `exceptions` and are checked again ## Open items `runwayml/hailuo3_highspeed` and `runwayml/hailuo3_lite` are in Runway's OpenAPI spec but have no row on the pricing page, no changelog entry and no entry in the models guide, so they are left out of this PR until Runway publishes a rate. Their resolutions (480p and 768p) differ from `hailuo3` (768P and 2K), so its rates were not copied onto them

title: chore(cost-map): add github_copilot/gemini-4-hydrogen from the Copilot changelog launch post
body:
## Summary

Adds the `github_copilot/gemini-4-hydrogen` row. GitHub announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Copilot on 2026-11-13 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-13-gemini-4-hydrogen-in-github-copilot) and the Copilot supported-models page already lists it as GA, but the models-and-pricing.yml table that `prices github-copilot` reads has not caught up yet, so the price comes from the post's billing statement and Google's own list price. This is the same path `github_copilot/gemini-4-carbon` took in #51012. The 29 priced rows the table shares with the catalog match to the digit, so nothing else changes.

## github_copilot/gemini-4-hydrogen (kind page)

The changelog post says "Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Google's latest Flash model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot" and "This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details". The Copilot supported-models page (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models) lists "Gemini 4 Hydrogen Google GA", and the model-hosting page lists it among the Gemini models hosted on Google Cloud Platform.

Provider list pricing is Google's Gemini API pricing page (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing#gemini-4-hydrogen, Standard tab, Paid Tier per 1M tokens in USD), which states "Input price ... $1.50", "Output price (including thinking tokens) ... $7.50" and "Context caching price ... $0.075". So `input_cost_per_token` is 0.0000015, `output_cost_per_token` is 0.0000075 and `cache_read_input_token_cost` is 0.000000075, the same values as the first-party `gemini/gemini-4-hydrogen` row. The Copilot table does not list Hydrogen yet, so the Copilot-side numbers should be re-checked against models-and-pricing.yml once GitHub adds the row.

`max_input_tokens` 200000, `max_output_tokens` 65536, `supported_endpoints` and every `supports_*` flag are `inherited_from: github_copilot/gemini-4-carbon`. Copilot publishes no token limits for the model, and the Carbon row is the nearest Copilot sibling (same family and generation, added the same way three days ago). `supports_sampling_params: false` from `github_copilot/gemini-3.8-flash` is not copied because the first-party `gemini/gemini-4-hydrogen` row does not carry it, while `gemini/gemini-3.8-flash` does.

Release status is GA on the supported-models page and model-deprecation-history.yml has no entry for it, so the row gets no `deprecation_date`.

## Rulings applied

github-copilot-claude-sonnet-4-leave-out keeps `github_copilot/claude-sonnet-4` out of the catalog although the table still prices it. The table's `claude-opus-4.8-(fast-mode)-(preview)` id is the catalog's `github_copilot/claude-opus-4.8-fast` (naming mismatch, not a missing row).

## Pages checked without a pricing difference

https://github.blog/changelog/label/copilot/feed/ (the Hydrogen launch is the only new model entry since the last sync, the Gemini 4 Carbon and Claude Fable 5.2 posts are already in the catalog, the rest are product updates), models-and-pricing.yml (no difference on shared rows), model-release-status.yml (no Hydrogen entry yet) and model-deprecation-history.yml (every dated retirement already in the catalog or covered by a ruling).

title: feat(proxy): support budget_limits windows on internal users
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description Internal users can now carry several budget windows at once, like a monthly cap plus a tight hourly cap, the same way keys and teams already can. Whichever window runs out first blocks that user's requests across all of their keys, and the windows reset on their own schedule
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b5fabf071d4043c8ae51088564007cfe Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/b5fabf071d4043c8ae51088564007cfe?variant=devin Requested by: @mateo-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `budget_limits` windows only worked on keys and teams - A user could only have one `max_budget` and `budget_duration` - `/user/new` accepted `budget_limits` but never stored it on the user How it solves it: - Stores `budget_limits` on the user row (schema-only migration) - `/user/new` and `/user/update` validate, initialize and clear user windows - Auth checks every user window under the same skip rules as user `max_budget` - Post-call spend, reservation, reseed and the reset job cover user windows ## User Flow Before: an admin caps a user at $100 a month and a few cents an hour, but the user keeps spending 1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/user/new with `"budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": 0.000001}, {"budget_duration": "30d", "max_budget": 100}]` 2. GET https://litellm-domain/user/info shows `"budget_limits": null` 3. The user's key calls POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions twice and both return 200 After: the windows are stored and the first one to fill blocks the user 1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/user/new 2. GET https://litellm-domain/user/info returns both windows with their `reset_at` 3. The first chat completion returns 200, the second returns 422 saying the user is over the 1h budget 4. POST https://litellm-domain/user/update with `"budget_limits": null` clears them and the next call returns 200 ## Relevant issues Part of LIT-6961 (API and enforcement only, the Admin UI editor is not in this PR). Supersedes the closed #41722 and the stale external #34500 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup. Local Postgres, a dedicated Redis on port 6397 shared by both workers, real OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` calls. Env vars `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`. Each checkout ran `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config user-budget-live.yaml --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver` and the client script below with `python user-budget-live.py `
user-budget-live.yaml ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 6397 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL disable_prisma_schema_update: true coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6397 ```
user-budget-live.py ```python import json import os import sys import time import uuid import httpx import redis port = int(sys.argv[1]) label = sys.argv[2] client = httpx.Client(base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", timeout=90) admin = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}"} user_id = f"window-proof-{label}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}" windows = [ {"budget_duration": "1h", "max_budget": 0.000001}, {"budget_duration": "30d", "max_budget": 100.0}, ] def request(method, path, body=None, headers=admin): response = client.request(method, path, json=body, headers=headers) print(method, path, response.status_code, flush=True) assert response.is_success, response.text return response.json() request("POST", "/user/new", {"user_id": user_id, "auto_create_key": False, "budget_limits": windows}) info = request("GET", f"/user/info?user_id={user_id}") print("stored windows", json.dumps(info.get("user_info", {}).get("budget_limits")), flush=True) key = request("POST", "/key/generate", {"user_id": user_id})["key"] headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"} body = {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}], "max_tokens": 5} first = client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers) print("first completion", first.status_code, "cost", first.headers.get("x-litellm-response-cost"), flush=True) assert first.status_code == 200, first.text store = redis.Redis(host="127.0.0.1", port=6397, decode_responses=True) counter_names = [f"spend:user:{user_id}:window:{w['budget_duration']}" for w in windows] for attempt in range(40): counters = store.mget(counter_names) if all(c is not None and float(c) > 0 for c in counters) or label == "main": break time.sleep(0.25) print("user window counters", counters, flush=True) second = client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers) print("second completion", second.status_code, flush=True) if label == "main": assert second.status_code == 200, second.text print("MAIN reproduces missing user-window enforcement", flush=True) else: assert second.status_code == 422, second.text assert "over 1h budget" in second.text, second.text assert all(c is not None and float(c) > 0 for c in counters), counters request("POST", "/user/update", {"user_id": user_id, "budget_limits": None}) cleared = request("GET", f"/user/info?user_id={user_id}") assert not cleared["user_info"]["budget_limits"], cleared resumed = client.post("/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers) print("completion after clearing", resumed.status_code, flush=True) assert resumed.status_code == 200, resumed.text print("BRANCH enforces both windows, accounts spend and clears them", flush=True) ```
### Before (bad8b1dae8) ``` POST /user/new 200 GET /user/info?user_id=window-proof-main-024c26e5 200 stored windows null POST /key/generate 200 first completion 200 cost 4.35e-06 user window counters [None, None] second completion 200 MAIN reproduces missing user-window enforcement ``` ### After (6f5be79721) ``` POST /user/new 200 GET /user/info?user_id=window-proof-branch-15c4126f 200 stored windows [{"reset_at": "2026-11-13T20:00:00+00:00", "max_budget": 1e-06, "budget_duration": "1h"}, {"reset_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00+00:00", "max_budget": 100.0, "budget_duration": "30d"}] POST /key/generate 200 first completion 200 cost 4.35e-06 user window counters ['0.000001', '0.000001'] second completion 422 POST /user/update 200 GET /user/info?user_id=window-proof-branch-15c4126f 200 completion after clearing 200 BRANCH enforces both windows, accounts spend and clears them ``` Focused unit tests on the seven changed test files pass (639 passed), and the 11 new regression tests fail on `bad8b1dae8` (10 failed, 1 passed). `make lint` passes ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - No Admin UI editor for user windows yet, API only - Team-key requests skip user windows exactly like user `max_budget` does ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: fix(proxy): keep a customer budget reset from being undone by a stale hierarchy cache entry
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description fix race customer budget reset race condition
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d30680bc92b5484bafbd3738a4b67bf8 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d30680bc92b5484bafbd3738a4b67bf8?variant=devin Requested by: @kerry-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - After a customer budget reset, requests still get `ExceededBudget` - Database spend is already 0, the cached hierarchy is not - Alias-only requests: their cache entry was never evicted - Any request: a load in flight re-caches pre-reset spend How it solves it: - The reset job evicts `customer_org_alias:` entries on every worker - A cache miss takes a lease, any eviction of that key voids it - The cache refuses a write that carries a voided lease - With `enable_redis_auth_cache`, Redis checks the lease atomically Both findings are one seam (what the reset job leaves in the request-path cache), so they are fixed together. They were introduced by #51493 and #51546. ## User Flow Before: a customer whose organization budget window just reset keeps getting refused 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: ` until the budget is used up 2. The budget window ends and the reset job sets the organization's spend back to 0 3. They send the same request and get 422 `ExceededBudget: ... Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06` for up to 60 more seconds After: the first request after the reset goes through 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: ` until the budget is used up 2. The budget window ends and the reset job sets the organization's spend back to 0 3. They send the same request and get 200 ## How the lease works ``` miss on key K -> lease = cache.lease(K) # before the database read database read -> rows cache.async_set_leased(lease, value, ttl) refused when K was evicted since the lease was taken # the rows may predate that write ``` On one worker the lease is an object the cache drops on every eviction path (`async_delete_cache`, `async_delete_cache_keys`, `delete_cache`, `declare_delete`, `delete_local` from the eviction broadcast, `flush_cache`). With `enable_redis_auth_cache` the same rule holds across workers through a generation key in Redis, in the same cluster slot as the entry: ``` delete K -> one script: DEL K, then SET {K}:auth_cache_generation:K EX 600 lease(K) -> GET the generation set_leased(K) -> one script: SET K only if the generation is still the one the lease read ``` ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, the same for Before and After: Postgres, one Redis on port 6399, two workers, a real Anthropic call. Env vars: `DATABASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The two `PROXY_BUDGET_RESCHEDULER_*` values only make the reset job tick every 5 to 8 seconds so the run is short. `--reload` and `--detailed_debug` are dropped because the before and after builds are swapped by checkout between runs. ```bash PROXY_BUDGET_RESCHEDULER_MIN_TIME=5 PROXY_BUDGET_RESCHEDULER_MAX_TIME=8 \ LITELLM_DANGEROUSLY_PERMIT_WEAK_OR_UNSET_MASTER_KEY=true STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=False \ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --port 4455 ``` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6399 router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 6399 ``` The second case adds `litellm_settings: {enable_redis_auth_cache: true}` to that config.
repro.sh, run as `bash repro.sh ` ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # usage: repro.sh (proxy on :4455, master key sk-1234, DB kstack_a56) P=http://127.0.0.1:4455; H='Authorization: Bearer sk-1234'; A=$1 DB=$(echo $DATABASE_URL | sed -E 's#/[^/]*$##')/kstack_a56 curl -s -X POST $P/management/v1/customer_organizations -H "$H" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d "{\"customer_org_id\":\"$A\",\"alias\":\"$A\",\"budget\":{\"max_budget\":0.000001,\"budget_duration\":\"90s\"}}" | head -c 300; echo T0=$(date +%s) for i in $(seq 1 45); do code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/r.json -w '%{http_code}' $P/v1/chat/completions -H "$H" -H "x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $A" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":5,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}') row=$(psql "$DB" -Atc "select round(o.spend::numeric,6), to_char(b.budget_reset_at,'HH24:MI:SS') from \"LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable\" o join \"LiteLLM_BudgetTable\" b on b.budget_id=o.budget_id where customer_org_id='$A'") echo "t=$(( $(date +%s)-T0 ))s http=$code db_spend|reset_at=$row $( [ $code != 200 ] && head -c 110 /tmp/r.json)" sleep 3 done ```
It creates an organization with a budget one request uses up, then sends one alias-only request every 3 seconds and prints the status next to the organization's spend and `budget_reset_at` in the database. A 422 while `db_spend` is still above 0 is correct. A 422 after the reset set `db_spend=0.000000` and moved `budget_reset_at` is the bug. Stale 422s after a reset: default config 3 on main and 0 on this branch, with `enable_redis_auth_cache` 15 on main and 0 on this branch. ### Before (a166574ba4) #### Default config ``` t=54s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=19:50:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-mb2 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=57s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=19:50:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-mb2 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=60s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:51:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-mb2 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=63s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:51:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-mb2 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=66s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:51:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-mb2 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=70s http=200 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:51:30 t=73s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:51:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-mb2 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. ``` #### `enable_redis_auth_cache: true` ``` t=75s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=19:43:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=78s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=19:43:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=115s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:44:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=118s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:44:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=121s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:44:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=125s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:44:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=128s http=200 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:44:30 t=132s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=19:44:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-rb1 over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. ``` ### After (78d68d11b0) The tip `8639559f1d` (a merge of main onto `cde4d0f6c3`) differs from this tested commit in production code in two ways, the order of `DEL` and `SET` inside the delete script and refusing a leased write for a key with no slot-compatible generation key. `litellm/rust/crates/redis-store/tests/auth_cache.rs` covers both on a real Redis and a real Redis Cluster. #### Default config ``` t=56s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=20:19:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-t3a over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=59s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=20:19:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-t3a over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=63s http=200 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=20:20:30 t=66s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=20:20:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-t3a over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. ``` #### `enable_redis_auth_cache: true` ``` t=57s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=20:22:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-t3b over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=60s http=422 db_spend=0.000033 budget_reset_at=20:22:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-t3b over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. t=64s http=200 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=20:23:30 t=67s http=422 db_spend=0.000000 budget_reset_at=20:23:30 ExceededBudget: customer_org=org-t3b over budget. Spend=3.3e-05, Budget=1e-06. ``` After this run Redis holds `{customer_org_alias:org-t3b}:auth_cache_generation:customer_org_alias:org-t3b`. The in-flight load needs a database read to straddle the reset's commit, a window of milliseconds, so it is not hit by hand. It is reproduced by holding the read open: `test_customer_budget_reset_is_not_undone_by_a_hierarchy_load_in_flight` and its alias twin in `tests/integration/database/test_spendlogs_ledger_parity.py` fail on main with cached spend `5.0` where the database has `0.0`, and pass here. The cross-worker refusal runs against a real standalone Redis and a real Redis Cluster in `litellm/rust/crates/redis-store/tests/auth_cache.rs`. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - Every auth cache delete now also writes a generation key - A delete is one script per key instead of a multi-key `DEL` - Each generation key lives 600 seconds - A Redis error on the leased write still caches in memory - Same as a plain cache write today, the per-worker lease still applies - During a rolling upgrade, old pods delete without a new generation - A load on a new pod can still re-cache for up to 60 seconds, as today ### Low - With `enable_redis_auth_cache`, a hierarchy key hashed whole that holds a `}` is never cached - No hash tag can put its generation in the same cluster slot, so the leased write is refused and each request reads the database - When Redis is down the lease falls back to per-worker - Assumed, not tested: no load of one key runs longer than 600 seconds ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches auth cache invalidation and Redis Lua paths used on every delete and hierarchy load; incorrect lease logic could cause extra DB reads or transient budget false positives, but scope is limited to customer hierarchy keys and reset eviction. > > **Overview** > Fixes a race where customer budget resets could be undone by stale cached hierarchy spend (including alias-only org lookups that were not evicted). > > **Lease-guarded cache fills:** On miss, customer hierarchy loaders take a `lease` before the DB read and commit via `async_set_leased` instead of a plain set. Any eviction voids the lease so in-flight loads cannot re-cache pre-reset spend. > > **Cross-worker consistency:** With `enable_redis_auth_cache`, Redis uses per-key generation siblings and atomic scripts for leased `SET` and delete (DEL + bump generation). Local `UserApiKeyCache` tracks leases on every eviction path. > > **Reset job:** The budget cascade now broadcasts eviction of `customer_org_alias:` keys on every worker (alongside existing member hierarchy invalidation), via `_evict_on_every_worker`. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8639559f1dd2de8aebd5ae5ed4db807424161452. title: fix(mistral): declare low, medium and high reasoning effort for mistral-large-4
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Mistral Large 4 now gets the low or medium reasoning level you ask for. Before, both were sent to Mistral as high

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d8885d77eb8e46bd86469f4c01d055eb
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8885d77eb8e46bd86469f4c01d055eb?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `mistral/mistral-large-4` and `mistral/mistral-large-4-0` were declared as taking `none` and `high`
- Mistral actually takes `low`, `medium` and `high` for them
- So `low` and `medium` were sent upstream as `high`

How it solves it:

- Both cost map rows now declare `low`, `medium`, `high`
- The backup cost map carries the same rows

## User Flow

Before: a developer asking Mistral Large 4 for light reasoning silently gets, and pays for, the heaviest level

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "mistral-large-4"` and `"reasoning_effort": "low"` (or `"medium"`)
2. The call returns 200, but Mistral received `"reasoning_effort": "high"`

After: the level they asked for is the level Mistral receives

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"reasoning_effort": "low"` (or `"medium"`)
2. The call returns 200 and Mistral received `"reasoning_effort": "low"` (or `"medium"`)

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51691

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy against the real Mistral API, one worker, no database and no Redis, since the change is a cost map row that no shared state touches. The native extension was rebuilt at each SHA with `VIRTUAL_ENV=$PWD/.venv uv tool run --from maturin==1.15.0 maturin develop --profile dev`, because the cost map is bundled into it. Env vars: `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`

```
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4191 --num_workers 1 --detailed_debug > proxy.log 2>&1
```

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mistral-large-4
    litellm_params:
      model: mistral/mistral-large-4
      api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY
  - model_name: mistral-large-4-0
    litellm_params:
      model: mistral/mistral-large-4-0
      api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-qa-51691-<40 x characters>
```

For each model and each of `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`:

```
curl -s -o /tmp/out.json -w '%{http_code}' localhost:4191/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-large-4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":16,"reasoning_effort":"low"}'
grep "in place of" proxy.log
```

Independently of LiteLLM, a direct call to https://api.mistral.ai/v1/chat/completions on 2026-11-13 with each of `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` returned 200 only for `low`, `medium`, `high` on both ids, and for the rest `reasoning_effort none is not supported for this model, supported values: [<ReasoningEffort.high: 'high'>, <ReasoningEffort.low: 'low'>, <ReasoningEffort.medium: 'medium'>]`

### Before (bad8b1dae8)

1. Status per request

```
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=none -> HTTP 400
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=low -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=medium -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=high -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=none -> HTTP 400
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=low -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=medium -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=high -> HTTP 200
```

2. What the proxy log says it sent upstream

```
mistral: mistral-large-4 takes reasoning_effort ('none', 'high'), sending high in place of low
mistral: mistral-large-4 takes reasoning_effort ('none', 'high'), sending high in place of medium
mistral: mistral-large-4-0 takes reasoning_effort ('none', 'high'), sending high in place of low
mistral: mistral-large-4-0 takes reasoning_effort ('none', 'high'), sending high in place of medium
```

### After (11230c0410)

1. Status per request

```
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=none -> HTTP 400
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=low -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=medium -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4 reasoning_effort=high -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=none -> HTTP 400
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=low -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=medium -> HTTP 200
mistral-large-4-0 reasoning_effort=high -> HTTP 200
```

2. What the proxy log says it sent upstream

```
(no 'in place of' lines)
```

The `--detailed_debug` request body logged for `low` and `medium` carries `'reasoning_effort': 'low'` and `'reasoning_effort': 'medium'`

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- `none` still returns Mistral's 400 on these two models
  - LiteLLM never rounds `none` onto a level by design
  - The model cannot turn reasoning off

### Low

- Other Mistral rows were probed the same way and match their declarations
- `mistral/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` declares no levels, left for a follow-up

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Metadata and test-only changes for two Mistral model IDs; behavior improves for `reasoning_effort` passthrough with no auth or billing logic touched.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates **`reasoning_effort_levels`** for `mistral/mistral-large-4` and `mistral/mistral-large-4-0` in both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the backup from **`none` + `high`** to **`low`, `medium`, `high`**, matching what Mistral’s API accepts.
> 
> With the old metadata, LiteLLM treated `low` and `medium` as unsupported and **substituted `high` upstream**, so callers could over-pay and over-reason without knowing. After this change, those levels pass through unchanged.
> 
> Unit tests now assert the three accepted levels via `ACCEPTED_EFFORTS` and parametrize reasoning-effort and completion-contract cases over **`low`, `medium`, `high`** instead of `none` and `high`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 11230c04102b7a0f6a1be12381b041b491115ed2. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(proxy): reject slash customer hierarchy IDs
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3ec50e37352a4101bd91bba53899d2ff
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3ec50e37352a4101bd91bba53899d2ff?variant=devin
Requested by: @tin-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer org, team and member creates accept IDs containing `/`
- Item GET, PATCH and DELETE on those IDs always 404
- `%2F` is decoded before routing, so the ID splits into two segments

How it solves it:

- One shared `CustomerHierarchyId` type rejects `/` on create and upsert bodies with a 422
- Auto-registration skips slash IDs and the request runs untracked, like other unknown IDs
- Other punctuation such as `:` still works, generated UUIDs are unchanged

Intentional product change: an API caller sending a `/` in a customer org, team or member ID now gets a 422 instead of a 201 for an ID they could never read back.

## User Flow

Before: an admin creates a customer org with an ID containing `/` and can never open it again

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations with `{"customer_org_id": "acme/eu"}` and get 201
2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations/acme%2Feu
3. It returns 404 `{"detail":"Not Found"}`, and PATCH and DELETE fail the same way, same for teams and members

After: the bad ID is refused up front, so nothing unreachable gets stored

1. They send the same POST with `{"customer_org_id": "acme/eu"}`
2. It returns 422 `customer_org_id: Value error, Customer IDs must not contain '/'` and no org is created
3. An ID like `acme:eu` creates with 201 and GET returns 200

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more

- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy with real Postgres and a dedicated Redis, two workers serving at both base and head. No LLM provider is involved because these are management routes.

<details>
<summary>Shared setup</summary>

```bash
sudo service postgresql start
(cd litellm/proxy && uv run --no-sync prisma db push --skip-generate)
redis-server --port 6398 --save '' --appendonly no
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-slash-qa .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config slash-qa.yaml --port 4108 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
python slash-live-proof.py base   # or head
```

`slash-qa.yaml`

```yaml
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6398
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6398
```

`slash-live-proof.py` (env var `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` as above)

```python
import json, sys
from urllib.parse import quote
import httpx

phase = sys.argv[1]
client = httpx.Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:4108", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk-slash-qa"})

def call(method, path, body=None):
    response = client.request(method, path, json=body)
    print(method, path, json.dumps(body), response.status_code, response.text, flush=True)

prefix = "slash-proof-" + phase
org = prefix + "-org"
team = prefix + "-team"
call("POST", "/management/v1/customer_organizations", {"customer_org_id": org, "default_budgets": [{"name": "standard", "max_budget": 10}]})
call("POST", "/management/v1/customer_teams", {"customer_team_id": team, "parent_org_id": org})
for resource, field, extra in (
    ("customer_organizations", "customer_org_id", {}),
    ("customer_teams", "customer_team_id", {"parent_org_id": org}),
    ("customer_members", "customer_member_id", {"parent_team_ids": [team]}),
):
    for suffix in (["/bad"] if phase == "base" else ["/bad", "-normal", ":colon"]):
        identity = prefix + "-" + resource + suffix
        call("POST", "/management/v1/" + resource, {field: identity, **extra})
        call("GET", "/management/v1/" + resource + "/" + quote(identity, safe=""))
        if phase == "head" and suffix == "/bad":
            call("GET", "/management/v1/" + resource + "?q=" + quote(identity, safe=""))
```

</details>

### Before (0a78ce9cc5)

1. POST each resource with a `/bad` ID, then GET it by the encoded ID

```text
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id": "slash-proof-base-customer_organizations/bad"} 201 {...}
GET /management/v1/customer_organizations/slash-proof-base-customer_organizations%2Fbad 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}
POST /management/v1/customer_teams {"customer_team_id": "slash-proof-base-customer_teams/bad", ...} 201 {...}
GET /management/v1/customer_teams/slash-proof-base-customer_teams%2Fbad 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}
POST /management/v1/customer_members {"customer_member_id": "slash-proof-base-customer_members/bad", ...} 201 {...}
GET /management/v1/customer_members/slash-proof-base-customer_members%2Fbad 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}
```

### After (5a01cc1d1f)

1. The same POSTs are refused and nothing is stored

```text
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id": "slash-proof-head-customer_organizations/bad"} 422 {"type":"urn:litellm:error:invalid-request-body","title":"Invalid request body","status":422,"detail":"customer_org_id: Value error, Customer IDs must not contain '/'"}
GET /management/v1/customer_organizations?q=slash-proof-head-customer_organizations%2Fbad 200 {"data":[],"meta":{"total_count":0,...}}
POST /management/v1/customer_teams {"customer_team_id": "slash-proof-head-customer_teams/bad", ...} 422 {...,"detail":"customer_team_id: Value error, Customer IDs must not contain '/'"}
POST /management/v1/customer_members {"customer_member_id": "slash-proof-head-customer_members/bad", ...} 422 {...,"detail":"customer_member_id: Value error, Customer IDs must not contain '/'"}
```

Team and member lists don't take `q`, so `GET /management/v1/customer_teams?parent_org_id=slash-proof-head-org` and the members list were checked instead. Neither contains a `/bad` row.

2. Normal and colon IDs still create and read back

```text
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id": "slash-proof-head-customer_organizations-normal"} 201
GET /management/v1/customer_organizations/slash-proof-head-customer_organizations-normal 200
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id": "slash-proof-head-customer_organizations:colon"} 201
GET /management/v1/customer_organizations/slash-proof-head-customer_organizations%3Acolon 200
POST /management/v1/customer_teams ... -normal 201, GET 200, ... :colon 201, GET 200
POST /management/v1/customer_members ... -normal 201, GET 200, ... :colon 201, GET 200
```

Regression tests in `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/test_customers.py` and `tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_member_auto_create.py` (`-k slash`) went `9 failed` at base and `9 passed` at head. `tests/integration/management/test_customer_hierarchy_ids.py` passes against the head proxy. `make check` passes.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Slash IDs already stored stay unreachable through item routes
  - These routes shipped in #51459, so only QA data should be affected
- Auto-registration skipping slash IDs is covered by unit tests, not a live LLM call

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(proxy): /customer/new budgets reset on the same schedule as other budgets
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

budget reset bug fix

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/283f0b8ad95d41a7bef91df40584a53f
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/283f0b8ad95d41a7bef91df40584a53f?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `/customer/new` set the first budget reset to now plus duration
- `/budget/new`, `/key/generate`, `/team/new` and `/user/new` use the calendar schedule
- An annual customer budget made in November skipped the January 1 reset

How it solves it:

- `new_budget_request` now calls `get_budget_reset_time`, like the other four endpoints
- `litellm_settings.timezone` and `budget_reset_time` now apply to customer budgets too

Intentional product change: the first reset of a budget created inline by `/customer/new` now lands on the standard boundary for every duration (next midnight for `1d`, Monday for `7d`, the 1st of next month for `30d` and `1mo`, January 1 for `12mo`) and no longer on creation time plus the duration. The first window gets shorter for new customers. Later windows are unchanged because the reset job already used the standard schedule.

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin gives a customer a yearly budget in November and the customer gets no fresh budget on January 1

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `"max_budget": 1200, "budget_duration": "12mo"` on 2026-11-13
2. The response shows `litellm_budget_table.budget_reset_at` as `2027-11-13T18:18:44Z`
3. The same budget sent to POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new shows `budget_reset_at` as `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`
4. On January 1 the customer's spend is not reset, it first resets the next November

After: the same request gets the same January 1 reset as every other budget

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `"max_budget": 1200, "budget_duration": "12mo"` on 2026-11-13
2. The response shows `litellm_budget_table.budget_reset_at` as `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`
3. The same budget sent to POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new shows the same `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`
4. On January 1 the customer's spend resets

## Relevant issues

Follow-up to #51508, which added the January 1 reset for `12mo` budgets.

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, the same for Before and After. Two workers, Postgres and one Redis. `--reload` was dropped because this checkout failed to start its child process with two workers and `--reload`. No provider call is made, both endpoints are management routes.

Env vars set: `DATABASE_URL`, `A13_MASTER_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/A13_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4113 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

```bash
S=$(date +%s)
echo "now (UTC): $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
for d in 12mo 1mo 30d 7d 1d; do
  b=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:4113/budget/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $A13_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"budget_id\":\"a13-b-$d-$S\",\"max_budget\":1200,\"budget_duration\":\"$d\"}" \
    | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['budget_reset_at'])")
  c=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:4113/customer/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $A13_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"user_id\":\"a13-c-$d-$S\",\"max_budget\":1200,\"budget_duration\":\"$d\"}" \
    | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['litellm_budget_table']['budget_reset_at'])")
  echo "budget_duration=$d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=$b  /customer/new budget_reset_at=$c"
done
```

### Before (7a72c2b17a)

1. Run the loop above. `/customer/new` returns creation time plus the duration for every duration.

```
now (UTC): 2026-11-13T18:18:44Z
budget_duration=12mo  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2027-01-01T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2027-11-13T18:18:44.275000Z
budget_duration=1mo  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-13T18:18:44.548000Z
budget_duration=30d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-13T18:18:44.727000Z
budget_duration=7d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-16T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-20T18:18:44.957000Z
budget_duration=1d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-14T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-14T18:18:45.185000Z
```

2. Run the new integration test against the same proxy. It fails for all five durations.

```
$ python tests/integration/run.py management tests/integration/management/test_customer_budget_reset.py
E   assert datetime.datetime(2027, 11, 13, 18, 55, 7, 33000, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc) <= datetime.datetime(2027, 1, 1, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
============================== 5 failed in 0.94s ===============================
```

3. The wrong value comes from this frame, printed from a spy on the duration helper.

```
  File "litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/customer_endpoints.py", line 292, in new_budget_request
    seconds=duration_in_seconds(duration=budget_request.budget_duration)
2027-11-13 18:57:31.449750
```

### After (5b9b853353)

1. Run the same loop. Both endpoints return the same date for every duration.

```
now (UTC): 2026-11-13T18:56:06Z
budget_duration=12mo  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2027-01-01T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2027-01-01T00:00:00Z
budget_duration=1mo  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z
budget_duration=30d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z
budget_duration=7d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-16T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-16T00:00:00Z
budget_duration=1d  /budget/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-14T00:00:00Z  /customer/new budget_reset_at=2026-11-14T00:00:00Z
```

2. Run the same integration test. It passes.

```
============================== 5 passed in 0.85s ===============================
```

The unit regression `test_new_budget_request_resets_on_the_same_schedule_as_other_budgets` fails 5 of 5 on 7a72c2b17a and passes on the tip.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- First window is shorter for new non-annual customer budgets
- Existing rows keep their stored `budget_reset_at` until their next reset

### Low

- The new integration test first runs on main, the integration jobs do not run on every PR

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when customer spend resets (billing semantics) and shortens the first window for new customers, though logic is aligned with other budget endpoints.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Customer budgets created via `/customer/new`** now set the first `budget_reset_at` using **`get_budget_reset_time`**, matching `/budget/new`, `/key/generate`, `/team/new`, and `/user/new`. Previously inline customer budgets used creation time plus duration, so annual budgets could miss the January 1 boundary and `litellm_settings.timezone` / `budget_reset_time` did not apply.
> 
> **Behavior change:** the initial budget window for new customers may be shorter until the next standard reset (midnight, Monday, month start, or Jan 1 for `12mo`); existing stored `budget_reset_at` values are unchanged.
> 
> **Tests:** a new integration test asserts customer and budget endpoints return the same reset schedule across durations; the unit test for `new_budget_request` is parametrized to compare against `get_budget_reset_time`.
>
