title: feat(customer-portal): add free tier limits with Enterprise upgrade path
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add enterprise gate to customer portal

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9981b693bc354726b4779f72dc737082
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/9981b693bc354726b4779f72dc737082?variant=devin
Requested by: @moe-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer portal had no free tier boundary versus Enterprise
- Users could build on it without knowing it is Enterprise

How it solves it:

- Without a license, cap at 5 orgs, 5 teams each, 5 members per team
- Management creates past the cap return 403 with an upgrade link
- LLM requests keep working, new customers are just not tracked
- Dashboard shows a small free tier byline and a warning banner at the cap

Intentional product change: proxies without an Enterprise license can no longer create a 6th customer organization, a 6th team in an organization, or a 6th member in a team. Existing rows above the cap keep being tracked.

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin without a license can grow the customer portal without limit and never learns it is an Enterprise feature

1. They open http://localhost:3000/customers and see no free tier notice
2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations for a 6th organization and get 200
3. A chat request with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: sixth-org` auto-registers and tracks that org

After: the same admin sees the limits up front and a clear warning once they hit them

1. They open http://localhost:3000/customers and see "Free tier: up to 5 customers, 5 teams per customer, 5 members per team. LiteLLM Enterprise removes these limits."
2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations for a 6th organization and get 403 with an upgrade link
3. A chat request with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: sixth-org` still returns 200, the org is not created, and the proxy logs `CUSTOMER TRACKING OFF`
4. The Customers pages show a red "Free customer portal limit reached" banner with an Upgrade to Enterprise link

Below the limit, byline only:

![below limit](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..v7o60LGHTqWz_tMrWTFdgSK9eK767TLUfKQ9qK5zDok)

At 5 organizations, banner shown:

![at limit](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..Lr30ZPHSjHPw4B7sUfjA492uuvGjNiremhjJu80lNpo)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Proxy started with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config customer_portal_dev_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver`, where the config is a copy of `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` with `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis` pointed at a dedicated Redis on 6381. No `LITELLM_LICENSE` set, so `premium_user` is false. Two worker PIDs were serving. Env vars used are `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Dashboard ran with `npm run dev` on 3000.

### Before (df8b8d1b51)

Not captured live. On the merge base the hierarchy has no count checks, so organization, team and member creates always succeed and the dashboard has no limits notice

### After (ed648d4328)

1. Created five organizations with `POST /management/v1/customer_organizations`, then a sixth

```text
HTTP 403
{"type":"urn:litellm:error:customer-hierarchy-free-tier-limit","title":"Free customer portal limit reached","status":403,"detail":"Free customer portal limit reached: up to 5 customer organizations, 5 teams per organization and 5 members per team without a LiteLLM Enterprise license. Upgrade to Enterprise to remove the limits: https://www.litellm.ai/enterprise"}
```

2. Sent `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a virtual key, model `gpt-5.5` and header `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: sixth-org`

```text
HTTP 200  "content":"OK"
LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: customer_hierarchy_auth.py:555 - CUSTOMER TRACKING OFF for organization sixth-org because the free customer portal limit was reached. Upgrade to Enterprise to remove the limits: https://www.litellm.ai/enterprise
```

3. `GET /management/v1/customer_portal/limits` still reported `organization_count: 5` and `any_limit_reached: true`
4. Opened http://localhost:3000/customers and saw the screenshots in User Flow

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Severe

- Unlicensed proxies cannot create past 5/5/5 anymore
  - Existing rows above the cap keep working and tracking

### Medium

- The auto-created `default` team counts toward the 5 teams
- A member in several teams counts against each team
- Concurrency guard is a Postgres advisory lock, not tested under real parallel load
- Before state was not captured on a live proxy

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes product behavior for unlicensed deployments (hard create caps and silent loss of tracking for new customers at the limit) plus concurrency-sensitive capacity checks on the customer hierarchy store.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **free-tier caps** (5 customer organizations, 5 teams per organization, 5 members per team) for proxies without an Enterprise license (`premium_user`), enforced on management creates/upserts and request-path auto-registration.
> 
> **Backend:** `CustomerHierarchy` now takes `premium_user` and returns `ErrorCode.FREE_TIER_LIMIT` when a create would exceed capacity, guarded by a Postgres advisory lock. Management APIs map that to **403** with an Enterprise upgrade message; a new **`GET /management/v1/customer_portal/limits`** reports whether limits apply and if any cap is reached. When auto-registering orgs/members on LLM requests hits the cap, auth logs **CUSTOMER TRACKING OFF** and skips tracking instead of failing the request. Team selection is skipped when the resolved hierarchy has no member id.
> 
> **Dashboard:** A customers **layout** loads portal limits and shows a free-tier byline plus a destructive alert at capacity. Create/delete flows **invalidate** the limits query and surface 403 errors in toasts and form alerts.

title: fix(vertex_ai): send document_ocr, audio_track_extraction and auto_truncate on Gemini embeddings
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

The Gemini embedding options for OCR on scanned PDFs, video audio tracks and turning off truncation were silently ignored. They now take effect on both regular and batch embedding requests.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cba2a63e80044b8eb6033587c3067e09
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/cba2a63e80044b8eb6033587c3067e09?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `document_ocr`, `audio_track_extraction`, `auto_truncate` were dropped without an error
- Same three were dropped from Vertex batch embedding rows

How it solves it:

- Online requests carry them in `embedContentConfig` (Vertex and AI Studio)
- Batch rows carry them in `request.embed_content_config`

## User Flow

Before: a developer embedding a scanned PDF or a video with speech on Vertex `gemini-embedding-2` gets the same vector with or without the option

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with a PDF as `input` and `"document_ocr": true`
2. The response is 200 with the same embedding as without the option
3. They send a video with `"audio_track_extraction": true` and get the same embedding and the same 1650 tokens as without it
4. They send a 20k token text with `"auto_truncate": false` and get 200 with a truncated embedding instead of an error
5. The same three options in a POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches embeddings file are ignored for every row

After: the same requests reach Vertex with the options applied

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with a PDF as `input` and `"document_ocr": true`
2. The response is 200 with a different embedding than without the option
3. The video with `"audio_track_extraction": true` returns a different embedding and 2205 tokens, 355 of them audio
4. The 20k token text with `"auto_truncate": false` returns 400 saying the input exceeds 8192 tokens
5. The same three options in a POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches embeddings file are applied to each row

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10384

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy with two workers and one dedicated Redis, real Vertex AI calls to `gemini-embedding-2` in location `global`, no mocks. Before and After ran on the same proxy process. Before ran with the two source files at the merge base, and `--reload` restarted both workers when the fix was put back. Each cosine value compares the embedding with the option against the embedding of the same input without it, so 1.00000 means the option changed nothing.

Shared setup:

```bash
redis-server --port 6390
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=<random local key>
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=<path to a Vertex service account json>
export GCS_BUCKET_NAME=<bucket the service account can write to>
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/qa/lit10384/config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
python client.py
python batch_client.py
```

The log showed two `Started server process` lines for each boot. The fixtures are `scanned.pdf` (a two page image-only PDF of text), `speech.mp4` (a short video with a spoken audio track) and a 20k token string.

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
- model_name: gemini-embedding-2
  litellm_params:
    model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-2
    vertex_project: vertex-check-481318
    vertex_location: global
    vertex_credentials: os.environ/GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
    gcs_bucket_name: os.environ/GCS_BUCKET_NAME
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6390
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6390
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>client.py (online, POST /v1/embeddings)</summary>

```python
import base64
import os
import json
import math
import pathlib

import httpx

BASE = "http://localhost:4000"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}"}
HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent


def data_uri(name: str, mime: str) -> str:
    return f"data:{mime};base64,{base64.b64encode((HERE / name).read_bytes()).decode()}"


def embed(label: str, input_value: str, **params: object):
    response = httpx.post(
        f"{BASE}/v1/embeddings",
        headers=HEADERS,
        json={"model": "gemini-embedding-2", "input": [input_value], **params},
        timeout=180,
    )
    body = response.json()
    if response.status_code != 200:
        print(f"{label}: HTTP {response.status_code} {json.dumps(body)[:260]}")
        return None
    usage = {key: value for key, value in body["usage"].items() if value is not None}
    print(f"{label}: HTTP 200 cost={response.headers.get('x-litellm-response-cost')} usage={json.dumps(usage)}")
    return body["data"][0]["embedding"]


def cosine(a, b) -> float:
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b)) / (math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a)) * math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b)))


def compare(label: str, a, b) -> None:
    if a is not None and b is not None:
        print(f"  cosine({label}) = {cosine(a, b):.5f}")


pdf = data_uri("scanned.pdf", "application/pdf")
video = data_uri("speech.mp4", "video/mp4")
long_text = "bakery " * 20000

embed("pdf, warm-up call", pdf)
pdf_plain = embed("pdf, no option", pdf)
pdf_plain_again = embed("pdf, no option (repeat)", pdf)
compare("no option repeat vs no option", pdf_plain, pdf_plain_again)
pdf_ocr = embed("pdf, document_ocr=true", pdf, document_ocr=True)
compare("document_ocr=true vs no option", pdf_plain, pdf_ocr)

video_plain = embed("video, no option", video)
video_audio = embed("video, audio_track_extraction=true", video, audio_track_extraction=True)
compare("audio_track_extraction=true vs no option", video_plain, video_audio)

embed("20k-token text, no option", long_text)
embed("20k-token text, auto_truncate=false", long_text, auto_truncate=False)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>batch_client.py (POST /v1/files, POST /v1/batches, then the output file)</summary>

```python
import base64
import json
import math
import os
import pathlib
import time

import httpx

BASE = "http://localhost:4000"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}"}
HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
MODEL = "gemini-embedding-2"


def data_uri(name: str, mime: str) -> str:
    return f"data:{mime};base64,{base64.b64encode((HERE / name).read_bytes()).decode()}"


def line(custom_id: str, input_value: str, **params: object) -> str:
    body = {"model": MODEL, "input": input_value, **params}
    return json.dumps({"custom_id": custom_id, "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/embeddings", "body": body})


def cosine(a, b) -> float:
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b)) / (math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a)) * math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b)))


def file_lines(client: httpx.Client, file_id: str | None) -> list[dict]:
    if not file_id:
        return []
    content = client.get(f"{BASE}/v1/files/{file_id}/content", params={"model": MODEL})
    content.raise_for_status()
    return [json.loads(row) for row in content.text.splitlines() if row.strip()]


pdf = data_uri("scanned.pdf", "application/pdf")
video = data_uri("speech.mp4", "video/mp4")
long_text = "bakery " * 20000
jsonl = "\n".join(
    (
        line("pdf-no-option", pdf),
        line("pdf-document-ocr", pdf, document_ocr=True),
        line("video-no-option", video),
        line("video-audio-track-extraction", video, audio_track_extraction=True),
        line("long-text-no-option", long_text),
        line("long-text-auto-truncate-false", long_text, auto_truncate=False),
    )
)

with httpx.Client(headers=HEADERS, timeout=300) as client:
    uploaded = client.post(
        f"{BASE}/v1/files",
        params={"model": MODEL},
        data={"purpose": "batch"},
        files={"file": ("batch_input.jsonl", jsonl.encode(), "application/jsonl")},
    )
    print(f"POST /v1/files: HTTP {uploaded.status_code}")
    uploaded.raise_for_status()
    created = client.post(
        f"{BASE}/v1/batches",
        params={"model": MODEL},
        json={"input_file_id": uploaded.json()["id"], "endpoint": "/v1/embeddings", "completion_window": "24h"},
    )
    print(f"POST /v1/batches: HTTP {created.status_code}")
    created.raise_for_status()
    batch = created.json()
    while batch["status"] not in {"completed", "failed", "expired", "cancelled"}:
        time.sleep(20)
        batch = client.get(f"{BASE}/v1/batches/{batch['id']}", params={"model": MODEL}).json()
    print(f"batch status: {batch['status']} request_counts={json.dumps(batch.get('request_counts'))}")
    if batch.get("errors"):
        print(f"batch errors: {json.dumps(batch['errors'])[:600]}")
    rows = {row["custom_id"]: row for row in file_lines(client, batch.get("output_file_id"))}
    rows.update({row["custom_id"]: row for row in file_lines(client, batch.get("error_file_id"))})

embeddings = {}
for custom_id in sorted(rows):
    response = rows[custom_id].get("response") or {}
    body = response.get("body") or {}
    data = body.get("data") or []
    if data:
        embeddings[custom_id] = data[0]["embedding"]
        print(f"{custom_id}: status_code={response.get('status_code')} usage={json.dumps(body.get('usage'))}")
    else:
        print(f"{custom_id}: status_code={response.get('status_code')} error={json.dumps(rows[custom_id].get('error') or body)[:300]}")

for base, option in (("pdf-no-option", "pdf-document-ocr"), ("video-no-option", "video-audio-track-extraction")):
    if base in embeddings and option in embeddings:
        print(f"  cosine({option} vs {base}) = {cosine(embeddings[base], embeddings[option]):.5f}")
```

</details>

### Before

#### Online, POST /v1/embeddings (main at bad8b1dae8)

1. `python client.py`

```
pdf, warm-up call: HTTP 200 cost=0.00023219999999999998 usage={"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 516, "total_tokens": 516, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 0, "image_tokens": 516, "video_tokens": 0, "initial_prompt_tokens": null}}
pdf, no option: HTTP 200 cost=0.00023219999999999998 usage={"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 516, "total_tokens": 516, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 0, "image_tokens": 516, "video_tokens": 0, "initial_prompt_tokens": null}}
pdf, no option (repeat): HTTP 200 cost=0.00023219999999999998 usage={"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 516, "total_tokens": 516, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 0, "image_tokens": 516, "video_tokens": 0, "initial_prompt_tokens": null}}

  cosine(document_ocr=true vs no option) = 1.00000
video, no option: HTTP 200 cost=0.0198 usage={"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 1650, "total_tokens": 1650, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 0, "image_tokens": 0, "video_tokens": 1650, "initial_prompt_tokens": null}}

20k-token text, no option: HTTP 200 cost=0.0040002 usage={"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 20001, "total_tokens": 20001, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 20001, "image_tokens": 0, "video_tokens": 0, "initial_prompt_tokens": null}}

```

Both options leave the embedding identical, and `auto_truncate=false` still returns 200.

#### Batch, POST /v1/batches (a60e16b87d)

1. `python batch_client.py`

### After

```

#### Batch, POST /v1/batches (6d652ab05e)

```

batch status: completed request_counts=null

Actual token count:  ...
long-text-no-option: status_code=200 usage={"prompt_tokens": 20001, "total_tokens": 20001}

The option rows now differ from the plain rows, the audio row reports 2205 tokens, and the `auto_truncate=false` row comes back as a per-row error.

The two batch runs are from before main was merged into this branch at 5911436b2e. That merge brought in #51673, which already reports PDF tokens, so this PR no longer changes usage and the online runs above were redone on the merged tip. The merge did not change the batch row code, so the batch runs were not redone.

#### Where the fields go in a Vertex batch row

Four one-off batch jobs sent straight to the Vertex batch API settled the placement. `request.embed_content_config` with snake_case fields succeeded and applied all three options. The same three fields flat inside `request` failed the row with `no such field: 'audio_track_extraction'`. An `embed_content_config` sibling of `request` failed the whole job with an unsupported column type error.

#### AI Studio

The same named params were sent through `litellm.embedding(model="gemini/gemini-embedding-2", ...)`. `auto_truncate=False` on the 20k token text returned a 400 about the 8192 token limit, and a request with `document_ocr` and `audio_track_extraction` returned 200, so the nested `embedContentConfig` is accepted there too.

#### Tests

`pytest tests/unit/llms/vertex_ai/gemini_embeddings tests/unit/llms/vertex_ai/files/test_vertex_ai_files_transformation.py` gives 238 passed at the tip. With the two source files at main the five new tests fail and the other 221 in the two edited test files pass. `make lint` exits 0 at the tip.

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- A named param wins over the same field in `extra_body.embedContentConfig`
- Batch output rows still carry no per-modality token breakdown
- `document_ocr` cosine values move between runs because PDF embeddings are not fully deterministic

title: fix(sdk): stop requiring redis to import the Messages streaming path
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Streaming imported proxy modules that required Redis, even when Redis wasn’t used
- Without Redis installed, Anthropic and Bedrock streams completed but silently lost success callbacks, breaking cost tracking and logging
- Moved Redis imports inside the methods that need them
- Added regression tests and verified both providers deliver callbacks without Redis installed

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- SDK installs without redis lose every `/v1/messages` streaming success callback
- Two proxy modules on that import path import redis at load time

How it solves it:

- Import `RedisError` only where a Redis call can raise it
- Defer imports until the guarded Redis-related operation runs

## User Flow

Before: a Python SDK user who installed litellm with `fastapi orjson backoff soundfile` but not redis gets the streamed reply, but their cost and logging callbacks never fire

1. They register a `CustomLogger` in `litellm.callbacks`
2. They call `litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate(..., stream=True)` with an `anthropic/` or `bedrock/` Claude model and read the whole stream
3. The stream arrives in full, but stderr shows `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redis'` (Anthropic) or a WARNING `async_sse_wrapper billing failed after 6 chunks` (Bedrock)
4. Their success callback ran 0 times, so the request is missing from cost tracking and logs

After: the same call delivers the success callback without redis installed

1. They register the same `CustomLogger`
2. They make the same streaming call with either provider
3. The stream arrives in full with no redis error or billing warning
4. Their success callback ran once, same as with redis installed

## Relevant issues

Fixes #45380

## Affected release

Regression in v1.98.0. A second top-level redis import on the same path landed on main in c0114e55aa3

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] Affected tests passed on Devin against matching source commits, as required by this workflow
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both runs used real Anthropic and AWS Bedrock calls, Python 3.12.16, and a native extension built from source at the baseline. The `litellm/rust` tree is identical at both SHAs. Each case runs in a fresh process. The driver registers a `CustomLogger` and waits on an event set by the first success callback, failure callback, billing-failure log line or unraisable exception. The 60s timeout is only a safeguard and no run hit it.

Env var names are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AWS_PROFILE` and `AWS_REGION_NAME` (us-east-1).

<details>
<summary>Setup and run commands</summary>

```
# uv 0.13.8, CPython 3.12.16, run in the checkout
uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -o core-req.txt
uv venv --python 3.12 venv-noredis
uv pip install --python venv-noredis/bin/python -r core-req.txt backoff==2.2.1 fastapi==0.136.3 orjson==3.13.0 soundfile==0.12.1
uv venv --python 3.12 venv-redis
uv pip install --python venv-redis/bin/python -r core-req.txt backoff==2.2.1 fastapi==0.136.3 orjson==3.13.0 soundfile==0.12.1 redis==5.3.1
# native extension, built once
uv sync --inexact --frozen --extra proxy --group proxy-dev --group e2e-dev

PYTHONPATH=<checkout> LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True venv-noredis/bin/python driver.py anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
PYTHONPATH=<checkout> LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True venv-noredis/bin/python driver.py bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5
PYTHONPATH=<checkout> venv-noredis/bin/python -c "import litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.streaming_handler"
# controls: the same two driver lines with venv-redis
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>driver.py</summary>

```python
"""Issue #45380 repro. Usage: driver.py <model>"""
import asyncio, importlib.util, json, logging, sys, uuid

import litellm
from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger

model = sys.argv[1]
signals, state = [], {"done": None}


def signal(kind):
    signals.append(kind)
    if state["done"] is not None:
        state["done"].set()


class BillingFailureLog(logging.Handler):
    def emit(self, record):
        if "billing failed" in record.getMessage():
            signal("billing_failed_warning: " + record.getMessage())


def unraisable(u):
    signal(f"unraisable {type(u.exc_value).__name__}: {u.exc_value}")


class Counter(CustomLogger):
    success = failure = 0

    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        Counter.success += 1
        signal("success_callback")

    async def async_log_failure_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        Counter.failure += 1
        signal("failure_callback")


sys.unraisablehook = unraisable
logging.getLogger("LiteLLM Proxy").addHandler(BillingFailureLog(level=logging.WARNING))
litellm.callbacks = [Counter()]


async def main():
    state["done"] = asyncio.Event()
    response = await litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate(
        model=model,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Reply with the single word: pong. nonce {uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"}],
        max_tokens=16,
        stream=True,
    )
    raw = [c.decode() if isinstance(c, bytes) else str(c) async for c in response]
    events = sum(line.startswith("event:") for chunk in raw for line in chunk.splitlines())
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(state["done"].wait(), timeout=60)
        completion = "event"
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        completion = "TIMEOUT_60s_no_signal"
    return {"sse_events": events, "completion": completion}


result = asyncio.run(main())
print(json.dumps({"model": model, "redis_installed": importlib.util.find_spec("redis") is not None, **result,
                  "first_signal": signals[0] if signals else None, "success_callbacks": Counter.success,
                  "failure_callbacks": Counter.failure}, indent=1))
```

</details>

### Before (df8b8d1)

#### Anthropic, no redis

1. `driver.py anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` with venv-noredis
2. Stream completed with 7 SSE events. First signal was an unraisable `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redis'`. Success callbacks 0, failure callbacks 0

#### Bedrock, no redis

1. `driver.py bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` with venv-noredis
2. Stream completed with 6 SSE events. First signal was WARNING `async_sse_wrapper billing failed after 6 chunks: ModuleNotFoundError(No module named 'redis')`. Success callbacks 0, failure callbacks 0

#### Import, no redis

1. `python -c "import litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.streaming_handler"` with venv-noredis
2. Exit 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redis'`. An import tracer found 2 redis imports on this path, `redis_update_buffer.py:16` and `dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py:14`, and fixing either one alone still fails

#### Controls, redis 5.3.1

1. Both driver lines with venv-redis
2. Success callbacks 1 for each model

### After (ff4de66)

#### Anthropic, no redis

1. `driver.py anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` with venv-noredis
2. Stream completed with 7 SSE events. First signal was the success callback. Success callbacks 1, failure callbacks 0

#### Bedrock, no redis

1. `driver.py bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` with venv-noredis
2. Stream completed with 6 SSE events. First signal was the success callback. Success callbacks 1, failure callbacks 0

#### Import, no redis

1. `python -c "import litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.streaming_handler"` with venv-noredis
2. Exit 0. No redis module gets loaded, and the tracer records 0 redis imports

#### Controls, redis 5.3.1

1. Both driver lines with venv-redis
2. Success callbacks 1 for each model

#### Regression tests

The new tests were run against baseline source with the candidate tests applied. `test_buffer_without_redis_installed_skips_redis_work_when_no_cache_is_configured` and `test_the_limiter_loads_and_admits_requests_without_redis_installed` fail there with `ModuleNotFoundError` and pass at the tip. The Redis-error requeue case for tool discoveries passes on both, since it guards existing behavior. The affected test files (`tests/unit/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/`, `test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py`, `test_priority_class_share.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/`) gave 3309 passed and 8 skipped under xdist at badb44d, which differs from the tip by one blank line. Each new test also passed alone, and the files passed in random order with seeds 1 to 3. The ruff, strict-rule, type-discipline, test-quality, OpenAPI docs and type-check gates showed no rule growth against the merge base.

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

- `osv-scan` fails on `uv.lock` advisories this PR does not touch
  - The nightly scan on main failed the same way at 32cb45a3d

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: ci(mcp-deps): build unoptimized in the MCP dependency resolution workflow
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

The MCP dependency resolution check was timing out at 30 minutes on most PRs, because it compiled the Rust code with full release optimizations that it doesn't need. This makes it build without optimizations, so it finishes in about 11 minutes and stops showing up red.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- MCP Dependency Resolution hits its 30 minute timeout on most PRs
- 48 of its last 60 runs were cancelled
- It compiles the Rust workspace with fat LTO 18 times per run

How it solves it:

- Three Cargo env vars make the release profile build unoptimized
- Applies to this workflow only, release packaging is untouched

## User Flow

Before: a contributor whose PR touches Rust, `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` waits 30 minutes for a check that ends red

1. They push a commit to a pull request against `main`
2. `LiteLLM MCP Dependency Resolution` starts 12 jobs
3. The jobs run for 22 to 30 minutes and the run is cancelled by the timeout

After: the same push gets a green result in about 11 minutes

1. They push a commit to a pull request against `main`
2. `LiteLLM MCP Dependency Resolution` starts 12 jobs
3. All 12 jobs pass, the slowest in about 11 minutes

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [ ] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at a85ea9531d681e9b9444613d4b7b60423ac3e4bf. The change is three env vars in one CI workflow, so the proof is the workflow's own run time, measured on a fork with the same `ubuntu-latest` runners and one run per variant.

| Variant | Wall time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unchanged | 29.2 min | cancelled by the timeout |
| This PR | 10.8 min | 12 of 12 jobs passed |
| `MATURIN_PEP517_ARGS="--profile ci"` | 9.6 min | `resolve (3.15)` failed |
| LTO off only, as in #51069 | 19.4 min | 12 of 12 jobs passed |

Median job time went from 23.7 to 8.9 minutes for `core-distribution` and from 19.6 to 6.8 minutes for `resolve`. The build log reads `Finished release profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 3m 24s`.

`--profile ci` failed because `jiter` has no prebuilt wheel on Python 3.15, so uv builds it from source with maturin, which inherits the argument and stops on `profile ci is not defined`.

This PR's own run of the workflow is the proof on this repository.

## Type

🚄 Infrastructure

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- This workflow no longer builds the fat-LTO wheel
  - An LTO-only breakage would not be caught here
  - `rust-wheel` and CodSpeed still build the release profile on PRs
  - A full release build on `main` only is left as a follow-up

### Low

- The fork runs set the vars per job, this PR sets them once per workflow
- One run per variant, on a fork with an empty Actions cache
- The vars also reach third-party crates built from source, such as `jiter`
- Required checks do not get faster, this workflow is not required

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(router): prevent Responses fallback from replaying delivered tool calls
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- A Responses stream could deliver a tool call, then hit an error and replay it through a fallback, causing the action to run twice
- The fix checks whether a tool call has started before allowing fallback, even when no text was generated
- After a tool call, the original error now reaches the client. Fallback before output and text continuation still work


<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Responses fallback can replay a delivered tool call
- Codex can execute the same shell action twice

How it solves it:

- Check for delivered tool calls before permitting fallback
- Surface the primary error after a tool call
- Preserve fallback before output and existing text continuation

## User Flow

Before, a failed Responses stream can make Codex repeat a shell action

1. Configure a primary model and fallback, then start Codex through the proxy
2. Ask Codex to run a shell action
3. The primary completes the tool call and sends a retriable error
4. Codex runs the action twice and hides the primary error

After, the stream reports the failure after one shell action

1. Configure a primary model and fallback, then start Codex through the proxy
2. Ask Codex to run a shell action
3. The primary completes the tool call and sends a retriable error
4. Codex runs the action once and displays the primary error

## Relevant issues

Fixes #42955

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] Affected tests pass on the current tip, executed remotely under the requested jstack workflow
- [x] All six branch-required checks pass, with an unrelated OSV failure reported below
- [x] My PR only solves the delivered tool-call replay problem
- [x] Current-tip automated reviews are complete and actionable findings addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Independent Devin Ultra verification used source builds at the SHAs below, two proxy workers and dedicated Redis. The upstream deliberately injects the reported error, so this is controlled fault verification rather than paid-provider testing. Codex CLI 0.156.1 matches the original reproduction

The [public verification kit](https://gist.github.com/joshua-berri/7e940318f3ec8813cfd77f390e677197) contains the executed scripts, results and screenshots. The complete setup is also included below

<details>
<summary>Shared setup and client commands</summary>

Use a disposable verification directory and database. Run the upstream and proxy in separate terminals. Create the referenced kit, cfg, run and evidence directories first. The environment used an existing frozen proxy development environment, Redis, Postgres, tmux, Konsole, scrot and Codex CLI 0.156.1 installed under ~/verify-42955/codex-npm


Paths assume the kit sits in ~/verify-42955/kit and the checkout in ~/repos/litellm. codex_case.sh and gates.sh hardcode those paths.

```bash
redis-server --port 6399 --save "" --appendonly no --daemonize yes
python3 kit/upstream.py 18955 ~/verify-42955/run/upstream.jsonl
cd ~/repos/litellm && git checkout --detach <SHA>
.venv/bin/python ~/verify-42955/kit/make_config.py litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml ~/verify-42955/cfg/config.yaml http://127.0.0.1:18955/v1 6399
export DATABASE_URL=<disposable postgres database url>
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=<disposable local key, also written to ~/verify-42955/run/master.key>
export V42955_UPSTREAM_KEY=local-upstream-placeholder
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/verify-42955/cfg/config.yaml --port 4955 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

make_config.py copies dev_config.yaml and appends this (shown for one case, the other five are the same shape):

```yaml
model_list:
- model_name: trigger-tool-error
  litellm_params:
    model: openai/v-primary-tool-error
    api_base: http://127.0.0.1:18955/v1
    api_key: os.environ/V42955_UPSTREAM_KEY
- model_name: fallback
  litellm_params:
    model: openai/v-fallback
    api_base: http://127.0.0.1:18955/v1
    api_key: os.environ/V42955_UPSTREAM_KEY
general_settings:
  coordination_redis: {host: 127.0.0.1, port: 6399}
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6399
  num_retries: 0
  fallbacks:
  - trigger-tool-error: [fallback]
```

Model names and what the synthetic primary stream does:

| model_name | primary stream |
|---|---|
| trigger-tool-error | completed function_call item, then in-band `error` event |
| trigger-tool-failed | completed function_call item, then `response.failed` |
| control-no-fault | completed function_call, `response.completed` |
| control-prefail-error | `error` before any output item |
| control-prefail-failed | `response.failed` before any output item |
| ref-text-error | partial text "partial answer", then `error` |

## Client commands

Raw (prints public lifecycle counts and the upstream calls it caused):

```bash
.venv/bin/python kit/raw_case.py http://127.0.0.1:4955 <model_name> <outdir> <trials>
```

Interactive Codex (fresh HOME, CODEX_HOME and work dir per trial, TUI in a tmux pane shown in a terminal window, screenshots with scrot):

```bash
bash kit/codex_case.sh <evidence_dir> <model_name> <trial>
```

Codex config.toml written per trial:

```toml
model_provider = "v42955_litellm"
approval_policy = "never"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
web_search = "disabled"
[model_providers.v42955_litellm]
name = "LiteLLM proxy under test"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:4955/v1"
env_key = "V42955_LITELLM_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
request_max_retries = 0
stream_max_retries = 0
```

Launch: `codex -m <model_name> -C <work dir>`, then type `Append the line run to ledger.txt using the shell, once.` and press Enter. The side-effect count is `wc -l ledger.txt` in the work dir.


</details>

<details>
<summary>Executed upstream.py</summary>

```python
"""Synthetic deterministic OpenAI Responses upstream for issue 42955 verification.
Scenario is keyed only on the request body's `model`. Not a real provider."""
import hashlib, http.server, itertools, json, sys, threading, time

PORT = int(sys.argv[1]); LOG = sys.argv[2]
LOCK = threading.Lock(); COUNTER = itertools.count(1)
SERVER_ERROR = {"type": "server_error", "code": "server_error", "message": "upstream error"}

def sse(t, **f):
    return f"event: {t}\ndata: {json.dumps({'type': t, **f}, separators=(',', ':'))}\n\n".encode()

def robj(rid, model, status, output=None, error=None):
    usage = {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2,
             "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}}
    return {"id": rid, "object": "response", "created_at": 0, "status": status, "model": model,
            "output": output or [], "parallel_tool_calls": False, "tool_choice": "auto", "tools": [],
            "error": error, "usage": usage if status == "completed" else None}

def tool_call(req):
    names = [t.get("name") for t in req.get("tools", []) if isinstance(t, dict)]
    cmd = "echo run >> ledger.txt"
    if "append_ledger" in names: return "append_ledger", '{"line":"run"}'
    if "exec_command" in names: return "exec_command", json.dumps({"cmd": cmd})
    if "shell_command" in names: return "shell_command", json.dumps({"command": cmd})
    if "shell" in names: return "shell", json.dumps({"command": ["bash", "-lc", cmd]})
    raise ValueError(f"no known tool in {names}")

def has_tool_output(req):
    i = req.get("input")
    return isinstance(i, list) and any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "function_call_output" for x in i)

def fc(seq, name, args, call_id):
    item = {"id": f"fc_{call_id}", "type": "function_call", "status": "in_progress", "name": name,
            "call_id": call_id, "arguments": ""}
    done = dict(item, status="completed", arguments=args)
    return [sse("response.output_item.added", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, item=item),
            sse("response.function_call_arguments.delta", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, item_id=item["id"], delta=args),
            sse("response.function_call_arguments.done", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, item_id=item["id"], arguments=args),
            sse("response.output_item.done", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, item=done)], done

def text_events(seq, mid, text, finish):
    msg = {"id": mid, "type": "message", "status": "in_progress", "role": "assistant", "content": []}
    ev = [sse("response.output_item.added", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, item=msg),
          sse("response.content_part.added", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, content_index=0, item_id=mid,
              part={"type": "output_text", "text": "", "annotations": []}),
          sse("response.output_text.delta", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, content_index=0, item_id=mid, delta=text, logprobs=[])]
    done = dict(msg, status="completed", content=[{"type": "output_text", "text": text, "annotations": []}])
    if finish:
        ev += [sse("response.output_text.done", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, content_index=0, item_id=mid, text=text, logprobs=[]),
               sse("response.output_item.done", sequence_number=next(seq), output_index=0, item=done)]
    return ev, done

def err(seq): return sse("error", sequence_number=next(seq), error=SERVER_ERROR)
def failed(seq, rid, model):
    return sse("response.failed", sequence_number=next(seq),
               response=robj(rid, model, "failed", error={"code": "server_error", "message": "upstream error"}))

def stream(req, rid):
    model = req.get("model", ""); seq = itertools.count()
    out = [sse("response.created", sequence_number=next(seq), response=robj(rid, model, "in_progress"))]
    if has_tool_output(req) or not req.get("tools"):
        ev, done = text_events(seq, f"msg_{rid}", "done" if req.get("tools") else "ledger task", True)
        return b"".join(out + ev + [sse("response.completed", sequence_number=next(seq), response=robj(rid, model, "completed", [done]))])
    if model in ("v-primary-tool-error", "v-primary-tool-failed"):
        ev, _ = fc(seq, *tool_call(req), "call_primary")
        return b"".join(out + ev + [err(seq) if model.endswith("error") else failed(seq, rid, model)])
    if model == "v-primary-prefail-error": return b"".join(out + [err(seq)])
    if model == "v-primary-prefail-failed": return b"".join(out + [failed(seq, rid, model)])
    if model == "v-primary-text-error":
        ev, _ = text_events(seq, "msg_partial", "partial answer", False)
        return b"".join(out + ev + [err(seq)])
    if model in ("v-primary-nofault", "v-fallback"):
        cid = "call_primary" if model == "v-primary-nofault" else "call_fallback"
        ev, done = fc(seq, *tool_call(req), cid)
        return b"".join(out + ev + [sse("response.completed", sequence_number=next(seq), response=robj(rid, model, "completed", [done]))])
    raise ValueError(f"unknown scenario model {model!r}")

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self, *_): pass
    def do_GET(self):
        b = b'{"object":"list","data":[]}'
        self.send_response(200); self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b)
    def do_POST(self):
        raw = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", "0")))
        req = json.loads(raw); n = next(COUNTER)
        rid = f"resp_{req.get('model')}_{n}_{int(time.time()*1000)}"
        try:
            body = stream(req, rid); status = 200
        except ValueError as e:
            body = json.dumps({"error": {"message": str(e), "type": "invalid_request_error"}}).encode(); status = 400
        inp = req.get("input")
        rec = {"n": n, "ts": round(time.time(), 3), "path": self.path, "model": req.get("model"), "status": status,
               "stream": req.get("stream"), "response_id": rid, "has_tool_output": has_tool_output(req),
               "input_item_types": [x.get("type") or x.get("role") for x in inp if isinstance(x, dict)] if isinstance(inp, list) else type(inp).__name__,
               "input_sha256": hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(inp, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest(),
               "tool_names": [t.get("name") for t in req.get("tools", []) if isinstance(t, dict)][:12],
               "request_bytes": len(raw), "response_events": [l[7:].decode() for l in body.split(b"\n") if l.startswith(b"event: ")]}
        with LOCK:
            with open(LOG, "a") as f: f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream" if status == 200 else "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(body))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(body)

http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), H).serve_forever()
```

          "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"line": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["line"]}}]
os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
def uplines(): return open(up_log).read().splitlines() if os.path.exists(up_log) else []
rows = []

    body = json.dumps({"model": label, "input": "Append run to the ledger.", "tools": TOOLS, "stream": True}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + "/v1/responses", data=body, headers={"content-type": "application/json", "authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})
    events, status, t0 = [], None, time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:

    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        status = e.code; raw = e.read().decode()

title: feat(fal_ai): add per-clip prices for 23 Pixverse video endpoints
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Adds per-clip prices for the 23 fal.ai Pixverse video ids, so they stop billing $0 out of the box.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/8391f8983b8b4232be7ca1e1ab0e71c0
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/8391f8983b8b4232be7ca1e1ab0e71c0?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The Pixverse catalog rows carry no clip prices, so their videos record $0

How it solves it:

- Adds `output_cost_per_video_clip` tables for 23 Pixverse ids in both catalog copies, which stay identical
- Adds 8s prices for effects, transition and extend
- Five follow published 2x, three assume 8/5

The field and the billing landed in #51679, so this now targets main and only adds the catalog rows. It replaces #51336.

## User Flow

Before, a developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/videos for `fal_ai/fal-ai/pixverse/v5/text-to-video` with seconds "5" and size "360p", with no custom pricing on the deployment. They get a video id and the recorded spend is $0.

After, the same request records $0.15 of spend, the catalog price for a 5s 360p clip.

## Relevant issues

Follows #51679. Supersedes #51336.

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10648

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Real catalog-backed Pixverse proof

The promised catalog-backed rerun was completed after #51679 merged. Before is freshly fetched origin/main `316f9ef905ad845eb20fb2ba5236456ecf7ec9ff`, which has clip billing support but none of these 23 catalog rows. After is `6dd623de40851cdf20c63fa1ca928cf2422741b0`. Runtime code is identical. The diff is the 23 rows in both catalog JSONs and the existing catalog-aware fal tests. Native extensions were rebuilt independently for both legs.

Both legs use the repository's own bundled catalog with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. No catalog URL or copied catalog is used. The deployment config contains no price fields in either litellm_params or model_info. The transparent observer only forwards real fal traffic and captures its JSON. Its /catalog.json route refuses requests.

| Case | Before HTTP | Before header / persisted spend | After HTTP | After header / persisted spend | Actual fal payload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| /v1/videos, seconds 5, size 360p | 200 | absent / $0.00 | 200 | $0.15 / $0.15 | duration "5", resolution "360p" |
| /fal_ai native, duration "5", resolution "360p" | 400 | absent / no generation | 200 | $0.15 / $0.15 | duration "5", resolution "360p" after only |

Main's existing /fal_ai guard rejects the unpriced pass-through before dispatch. The PR changes neither that guard nor the proxy config. After bills the catalog's 5s/360p cell on both endpoints. All three submitted videos completed.

### Same rig and startup checks

Port 4018, two proxy workers, dedicated Redis 6407 for both router and coordination state, and PostgreSQL spend persistence match the earlier proof rig. Each startup terminated the prior proof proxy, verified no listener, and verified curl exit 7 before launching its own workers. The loopback observer listens on 4028 and forwards to https://queue.fal.run without mocking provider responses. The before and after configs are byte-identical.

import ast

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re

import socket
import subprocess

import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import httpx
import yaml

ROOT = Path(os.environ.get('QA_REVIEW_ROOT', '/home/ubuntu/pixverse-pricing/catalog-proof'))
CHECKOUT = Path('/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm')
PY = str(CHECKOUT / '.venv/bin/python')
ENDPOINT = 'fal-ai/pixverse/v5/text-to-video'
MODEL = 'fal_ai/' + ENDPOINT
BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:4018'
OBSERVER = 'http://127.0.0.1:4028'
LOCK = threading.Lock()


def save(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2))


def credentials(pid):
    if pid == 0:
        return {name: os.environ[name] for name in ('FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'DATABASE_URL')}
    own_qa_env = dict(part.split('=', 1) for part in Path(f'/proc/{pid}/environ').read_bytes().decode().split('\0') if '=' in part)
    return {name: own_qa_env[name] for name in ('FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'DATABASE_URL')}


def prepare():
    ROOT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for leg in ('before', 'after'):
        (ROOT / leg).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    config = yaml.safe_load((CHECKOUT / 'litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml').read_text())
    config['model_list'] = [{
        'model_name': 'pixverse-review',
        'litellm_params': {'model': MODEL, 'api_key': 'os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'api_base': OBSERVER, 'use_in_pass_through': True},
        'model_info': {'mode': 'video_generation'},
    }]
    config['router_settings'] = {'num_retries': 0, 'redis_host': '127.0.0.1', 'redis_port': 6407}
    config['general_settings'] = {
        **config.get('general_settings', {}), 'database_url': 'os.environ/DATABASE_URL',
        'master_key': 'os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'disable_spend_logs': False,
        'proxy_batch_write_at': 1, 'disable_model_info_refresh': True,
        'coordination_redis': {'host': '127.0.0.1', 'port': 6407},
    }
    config.pop('sandbox_tools', None)
    config['litellm_settings'] = {'drop_params': True, 'num_retries': 0, 'disable_aiohttp_transport': True}
    for leg in ('before', 'after'):
        (ROOT / leg / 'config.yaml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False))
        repo = Path('/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-clip-billing-main') if leg == 'before' else CHECKOUT
        catalog = json.loads((repo / 'model_prices_and_context_window.json').read_text())
        save(ROOT / leg / 'repo-catalog-row.json', catalog.get(MODEL))
        assert (repo / 'model_prices_and_context_window.json').read_bytes() == (repo / 'litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json').read_bytes()
        print(leg, 'catalog row', json.dumps(catalog.get(MODEL)))
        print(leg, 'catalog SHA256', hashlib.sha256((repo / 'model_prices_and_context_window.json').read_bytes()).hexdigest())
    print('Deployment prices absent, config copies identical')


def serve():
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *_):
            pass

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path == '/catalog.json':
                self.send_error(403, 'No catalog served, use the repository bundled catalog')
                return
            self.forward()

        def do_POST(self):
            self.forward()

        def forward(self):
            body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0)))
            target = 'https://queue.fal.run' + self.path
            event = None
            if self.command == 'POST':
                with LOCK:
                    ledger = json.loads((ROOT / 'ledger.json').read_text()) if (ROOT / 'ledger.json').exists() else []
                    label = json.loads((ROOT / 'active-case.json').read_text())
                    data = json.loads(body)
                    seconds = float(data.get('duration', 5))
                    resolution = data.get('resolution', '720p')
                    cost = {'360p': 0.15}.get(resolution)
                    valid = self.path == '/' + ENDPOINT and seconds == 5 and cost is not None
                    valid = valid and not any(row['leg'] == label['leg'] and row['case'] == label['case'] for row in ledger)
                    valid = valid and len(ledger) < 4 and sum(row['estimated_cost'] for row in ledger) + (cost or 0) <= float(os.environ.get('QA_REVIEW_BUDGET', '0.80'))
                    if not valid:
                        (ROOT / 'STOP').write_text('Budget, request shape or duplicate-submission guard stopped a call')
                        self.send_error(409, 'Live proof guard stopped submission')
                        return
                    event = {**label, 'url': target, 'method': 'POST', 'body': data, 'effective_duration': seconds,
                             'effective_resolution': resolution, 'estimated_cost': cost, 'status': 'submitted'}
                    ledger.append(event)
                    save(ROOT / 'ledger.json', ledger)
                    print(json.dumps(event), flush=True)
            headers = {key: value for key, value in self.headers.items() if key.lower() in ('authorization', 'content-type', 'accept')}
            with httpx.Client(timeout=180, follow_redirects=False) as client:
                response = client.request(self.command, target, headers=headers, content=body)
            if event is not None:
                with LOCK:
                    ledger = json.loads((ROOT / 'ledger.json').read_text())
                    for entry in ledger:
                        if entry['leg'] == event['leg'] and entry['case'] == event['case']:
                            entry['status'] = response.status_code
                            entry['provider_request_id'] = response.json().get('request_id') if response.is_success else None
                    save(ROOT / 'ledger.json', ledger)
                print('Fal response', event['leg'], event['case'], response.status_code, flush=True)
            self.send_response(response.status_code)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', response.headers.get('Content-Type', 'application/json'))
            self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(response.content)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(response.content)

    print('Real-fal transparent observer listening on 127.0.0.1:4028, no catalog served', flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 4028), Handler).serve_forever()


def start(leg, repo, source_pid):
    env = {**os.environ, **credentials(source_pid), 'PYTHONPATH': f'{repo}:{repo}/enterprise',
           'LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP': 'True',
           'FAL_AI_QUEUE_API_BASE': OBSERVER}
    env.pop('LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL', None)
    active = ROOT / 'active-proxy.pid'
    if active.exists():
        try:
            os.killpg(int(active.read_text()), signal.SIGTERM)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pass
    for _ in range(120):
        with socket.socket() as probe:
            if probe.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1', 4018)) != 0:
                break
        time.sleep(0.25)
    listeners = subprocess.check_output(['ss', '-ltnp', '( sport = :4018 )'], text=True)
    assert len(listeners.strip().splitlines()) == 1, 'Proxy port still occupied'
    curl = subprocess.run(['curl', '--max-time', '2', '-fsS', BASE + '/health/liveliness'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert curl.returncode == 7
    proof = listeners + f'Pre-start curl exit {curl.returncode}\n' + curl.stderr
    print(proof, flush=True)
    (ROOT / leg / 'port-free.txt').write_text(proof)
    command = [PY, 'litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py', '--config', str(ROOT / leg / 'config.yaml'), '--port', '4018',
               '--num_workers', '2', '--detailed_debug', '--reload', '--use_v2_migration_resolver']
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=repo, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
    active.write_text(str(process.pid))
    (ROOT / leg / 'proxy.pid').write_text(str(process.pid))
    print('Proxy PID', process.pid, 'revision', subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=repo, text=True).strip(), flush=True)
    with (ROOT / leg / 'proxy.log').open('wb') as log:
        for line in iter(process.stdout.readline, b''):
            safe = line
            for value in credentials_values(env):
                safe = safe.replace(value.encode(), b'[REDACTED]')
            log.write(safe)
            log.flush()
    process.wait()


def credentials_values(env):

### Eight-second catalog-backed Pixverse proof

Before is `6fef129cb8ffda5f0d851f3fe45264138a024c71`. After is `1627e51e4d99625dd6b371a62f343a595138fd86`. No production code changed. The diff adds 8s cells to eight rows in both local catalog JSONs and adds catalog-derived regressions. The existing 5s cells remain unchanged. Both copies are byte-identical. The tip native extension was rebuilt with uv sync before testing and startup. The baseline used its already-built native extension and the served local table was checked before dispatch.

The deployment has no prices in litellm_params or model_info. Both legs use `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, with `LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL` unset. The real endpoint is `fal-ai/pixverse/v5/transition`. Both first and last frames are public examples from its fal schema. The loopback observer forwards the actual JSON to real fal and never supplies a catalog or a mocked provider response.

| /v1/videos, 8s, 360p | 200 | $0.00 / $0.00 | 200 | $0.24 / $0.24 | duration "8", resolution "360p" |

### Pricing sources and 1080p decisions

Raw API pages and model pages were fetched with cache-busters on 2026-11-13. Every listed schema accepts both "5" and "8". Five API records explicitly say "The prices are doubled for 8-second durations." The other three give 5s prices without an 8s billing message. Their 8s cells use the user-approved 8/5 assumption, not a vendor-confirmed price.

title: fix(huggingface): honor environment endpoints for chat completions
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Superseded by #51449, merged at `331a673114cc279b0c77eb50753f42b06a410648` during this run. Independent SDK and two-worker proxy checks on that clean commit confirmed both reported failures are fixed. This duplicate PR remains open and conflicting, and is not a merge candidate

On merged main, `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` reached the real Together endpoint with HTTP 200 on five text calls and one image call. Both environment aliases sent `huggingface/tgi` to the recording endpoint with HTTP 200 and `"model": "tgi"`. Image conversion and endpoint precedence were preserved. The same commands below were run with `REPO` pointing at `331a673114cc279b0c77eb50753f42b06a410648`. No authenticated Hugging Face or real TGI endpoint was available

Candidate reviews found no functional defect. Bugbot and Veria reported no issues; Greptile scored 4/5 and retained an unresolved request for real TGI success evidence. GitHub Actions did not start because the overlapping merge created conflicts. The candidate is not being declared ready

Problem this solves:

- Only `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` set sends chat to the URL `None`
- Env endpoint plus `huggingface/tgi` fails before any request goes out
- Env endpoint plus `provider/org/model` still gets remapped through the Hub

How it solves it:

- Read `HF_API_BASE`, then `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE`, skipping empty values
- With an env endpoint, send the model name exactly as configured
- Env requests still convert string `image_url` parts and drop `max_retries`
- Env URL is still used as given, and explicit `api_base` still wins

## User Flow

Before, an SDK user configuring a Hugging Face endpoint through the environment gets an error before the request reaches it

1. Set `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` to the endpoint's full chat-completions URL, leaving `HF_API_BASE` unset
2. Call `litellm.completion(model="huggingface/tgi", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])` with the endpoint's API key
3. The call fails with `not enough values to unpack`, or an invalid `None` URL for an `org/model` name

After, the same SDK request reaches the configured endpoint

1. Set `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` to the endpoint's full chat-completions URL, leaving `HF_API_BASE` unset
2. Call `litellm.completion(model="huggingface/tgi", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])` with the endpoint's API key
3. The endpoint receives the request with `"model": "tgi"`; `org/model` names also pass through unchanged

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51448

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Before is the merge base `df8b8d1b518adc9c72aa1046792bb05f66f00177` and After is `4430be834920c54862334d9de7f04b9038cc1f3c`. No Hugging Face token or real TGI endpoint was available. The real provider is Together's OpenAI compatible endpoint behind the `huggingface/` provider, and a local recording fixture stands in for TGI.

### Shared setup

Source prerequisites. Each leg needs a checkout of the SHA under test with the existing canonical environment already present. That means the repo's uv env synced from `uv.lock` (`~/repos/litellm/.venv`, Python 3.12, `uv.lock` is identical at both SHAs), `redis-server`, and the gitignored native module `litellm/rust_bridge/_native.abi3.so` in the checkout (sha256 `0d82ee804867324c8a7ea9ea6772dd8ec6aab7fb6cff105249fb5943fc0db478`, the Rust inputs are identical at both SHAs). Nothing is installed by these steps. In the run, `BASE=~/repos/litellm` was at the baseline and `CAND=~/verify-51448/cand/src` was a detached worktree at the candidate.

Create `~/verify-51448/{kit,proxy,logs,run,redis}` outside tracked source and save the files below at their indicated paths

Env var names are `TOGETHER_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `HF_API_BASE`, `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE` and `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP`.

Dedicated Redis, run from `~/verify-51448/redis`

```bash
redis-server --port 6390 --bind 127.0.0.1 --save "" --appendonly no --dir $PWD > ../logs/redis.log 2>&1 &
```

Recording fixture on port 18448, run from `~/verify-51448`

```bash
python kit/fixture.py 18448 logs/fixture_requests.jsonl &
```

Disposable master key. This line is equivalent to what was run, not the literal command, and any random suffix works

```bash
mkdir -p run && python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(8))" > run/mk
```

`proxy/config.yaml`

<summary>config with four deployments, router and coordination Redis on 6390</summary>

</details>

`kit/fixture.py`

<details>
<summary>local endpoint that logs path and JSON body, then returns a canned chat completion</summary>

```python
"""Controlled OpenAI-compatible recording endpoint (fixture, not a provider)."""
import json, sys, time, uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

LOG = sys.argv[2]

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        raw = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0)))
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
        except Exception:
            body = {"_raw": raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")}
        auth = self.headers.get("authorization")
        rec = {"ts": time.time(), "method": "POST", "path": self.path, "body": body,
               "authorization": ("Bearer <redacted len=%d>" % len(auth.split(" ", 1)[-1])) if auth else None}
        with open(LOG, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        out = json.dumps({
            "id": "chatcmpl-" + uuid.uuid4().hex, "object": "chat.completion", "created": int(time.time()),
            "model": body.get("model", "unknown"),
            "choices": [{"index": 0, "finish_reason": "stop",
                         "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "fixture-ok path=" + self.path}}],
            "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1, "total_tokens": 2},
        }).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("content-type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("content-length", str(len(out)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(out)

ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
```

</details>

`kit/img.txt`, one line holding a 16x16 PNG

```
data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAF0lEQVR4nGP4z8BAEiJN9aiGUQ1DSgMAkPn/Afnh+ngAAAAASUVORK5CYII=
```

`kit/proxy_client.py`, an OpenAI SDK client with `max_retries=0` that sends ten requests per leg

<details>
<summary>client source</summary>

```python
"""End-user client: OpenAI SDK against the live proxy. argv[1]=label argv[2]=out.jsonl"""
import json, os, sys, uuid, openai
label, out = sys.argv[1:3]
c = openai.OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:4448/v1", api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"], max_retries=0, timeout=60)
IMG = open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "img.txt")).read().strip()
cases = [("hf-explicit-tgi", None), ("hf-env-tgi", None), ("hf-explicit-model", None), ("hf-env-model", None),
         ("hf-env-model", IMG), ("hf-explicit-model", IMG)] + [("hf-env-model", None)] * 4
with open(out, "a") as fo:
    for model, img in cases:
        content = f"Reply with one word: pong ({uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]})"
        if img:
            content = [{"type": "text", "text": f"One word colour? ({uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]})"}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": img}]
        rec = {"label": label, "model_group": model, "image": bool(img)}
        try:
            r = c.chat.completions.with_raw_response.create(model=model, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": content}], max_tokens=16)
            p = r.parse()
            rec.update(http=r.status_code, response_model=p.model, api_base=r.headers.get("x-litellm-model-api-base"),
                       content=(p.choices[0].message.content or "")[:60])
        except openai.APIStatusError as e:
            rec.update(http=e.status_code, error=" ".join(str(e).split())[:300])
        except Exception as e:
            rec.update(http=None, error=type(e).__name__ + ": " + " ".join(str(e).split())[:300])
        fo.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        print(json.dumps(rec))
```

</details>

### Running one leg

Each leg starts one proxy, runs the client once, and then stops that proxy before the next leg starts. `REPO` is `$BASE` for Before and `$CAND` for After. `LEG_ENV` is the one env assignment the case names, or empty. `env -u` clears both Hugging Face variables and the DB URLs first, so a variable left over from a previous leg can't leak in.

Terminal 1 runs the proxy in the foreground, and Ctrl-C stops it at the end of the leg

```bash
V=~/verify-51448
cd $REPO
env -u HF_API_BASE -u HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE -u DATABASE_URL -u DIRECT_URL $LEG_ENV \
  LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-verify51448-$(cat $V/run/mk) LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  PYTHONPATH=$REPO:$REPO/litellm/proxy-extras:$REPO/litellm/enterprise \
  ~/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config $V/proxy/config.yaml --port 4448 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload 2>&1 | tee $V/logs/proxy_$LABEL.log
```

Wait until `Application startup complete` appears twice. Then terminal 2 runs the client

```bash
V=~/verify-51448
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-verify51448-$(cat $V/run/mk) ~/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python $V/kit/proxy_client.py $LABEL $V/logs/proxy_client.jsonl
tail -n 20 $V/logs/fixture_requests.jsonl
```

Set `BASE` and `CAND` to the two checkout paths above, and set `REPO`, `LABEL`, and `LEG_ENV` from the case table. `TOGETHER_API_KEY` and `T` must be exported in terminal 1. These per-leg commands are reconstructed from the leg headers the run logged and the scripts it used, so they are not a copy of shell history. Compared with the AGENTS.md proxy command, `--use_v2_migration_resolver` and the database were dropped because the change has no persistence surface. Every leg logged two `Started server process` PIDs, and the "workers flag is ignored" message never appeared. No log recorded which worker served each request.

Legs, with `T=https://api.together.xyz/v1/chat/completions`

| Case | Before label | After label | `LEG_ENV` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1 | C1 | `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE=$T` |
| 2 | P2 | C2 | `HF_API_BASE=$T` |
| 3 | P3 | C3 | `HF_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:18448/env/v1/chat/completions` |
| 3 | P3b | C3b | `HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:18448/env2/v1/chat/completions` |
| 4 | P4 | C4 | empty |

The explicit deployments answered 200 at both SHAs. One candidate no-env-leg request to the explicit Together deployment timed out at 60 seconds; the next call returned 200. This was classified as provider-side and left outside the fix.

### Before (df8b8d1b518)

#### Case 1, only HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE pointing at Together

1. Run leg P1
2. `hf-env-model` text and image requests answered 500

#### Case 2, only HF_API_BASE pointing at Together (control)

1. Run leg P2
2. `hf-env-model` text and image requests answered 200

#### Case 3, huggingface/tgi with either variable pointing at the fixture

1. Run legs P3 and P3b
2. `hf-env-tgi` answered 500 on both legs

#### Case 4, no env endpoint (control)

1. Run leg P4
2. `hf-env-model` went to the Hugging Face router and answered 401, because no HF token was set

### After (4430be83492)

#### Case 1, only HUGGINGFACE_API_BASE pointing at Together

1. Run leg C1
2. `hf-env-model` text and image requests answered 200 with Together replies

#### Case 2, only HF_API_BASE pointing at Together (control)

1. Run leg C2
2. `hf-env-model` text and image requests answered 200

#### Case 3, huggingface/tgi with either variable pointing at the fixture

1. Run legs C3 and C3b
2. `hf-env-tgi` answered 200 on both legs, and the fixture logged `"model": "tgi"` on `/env/...` and `/env2/...`

#### Case 4, no env endpoint (control)

1. Run leg C4
2. `hf-env-model` went to the Hugging Face router and answered 401, same as Before

### Tests, coverage and gates

These ran remotely at the candidate SHA using the uv.lock versions (pytest 9.0.3, respx 0.22.0, ruff 0.15.3, basedpyright 1.39.7). The uv used was 0.13.8 instead of the workflow's 0.10.9, and `uv lock --check` passed.

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/llms/huggingface -q --cov=litellm/llms/huggingface --cov-branch
```

That run passed all 65 tests with exit 0. A wider selection of `tests/unit/llms/huggingface`, `tests/unit/llms/custom_httpx`, the two URL tests and `tests/unit/llms/test_provider_chat_translation.py` reported 2723 passed and 186 skipped. That run went through a pipeline and its pytest exit code wasn't captured.

The new tests were also run against the baseline from a byte copy of the candidate test file kept outside source. That copy uses a `conftest.py` that does `from tests.unit.conftest import *`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<repo>/litellm/scripts:<repo>/litellm/runtime python -P -m pytest -c <repo>/pyproject.toml --rootdir . -p no:cacheprovider -q test_hf_chat_candidate_tests.py
```

At the baseline it exited 1 with 8 failed, 25 passed and 8 respx teardown errors on the same 8 tests. At the candidate it exited 0 with 33 passed.

Coverage of the changed code was 6 of 6 lines and 4 of 4 arcs. Branch coverage for the touched functions as a whole was 12 of 14 for `get_complete_url` and 7 of 10 for `transform_request`, and the new helper was fully covered.

Every Python lint gate from `test-linting.yml` passed with `GATE_BASE_SHA` set to the baseline, including basedpyright. No mutation suite was run.

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- No authenticated Hugging Face call and no real TGI endpoint were tested
  - Together stood in as the real provider, and a local fixture stood in for TGI
- CI and review bots are still pending

### Low

- An env URL is still used as given, unlike explicit `api_base`
- With an env endpoint, `provider/org/model` is sent as written with no Hub lookup
- No log showed which of the two workers served each request
- The 2723 test run's exit code was not captured

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: feat(fal_ai): bill fal video clips by duration and resolution
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Lets the cost map price fal video clips per clip by length and resolution, so a configured clip price is billed instead of $0 or the per-second fallback.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/8391f8983b8b4232be7ca1e1ab0e71c0
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/8391f8983b8b4232be7ca1e1ab0e71c0?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- fal.ai Pixverse bills a flat price per clip, by length and resolution
- The cost map can't store that, so these videos bill $0

How it solves it:

- New `output_cost_per_video_clip` field, duration then resolution then USD
- /v1/videos and the /fal_ai pass-through bill the matching cell first
- No matching cell falls through to the existing flat or per-second prices
- Pixverse sizes now map to fal's 360p, 540p, 720p and 1080p
- Normalize Pixverse prefixes so the right resolution reaches fal
- Send Pixverse's explicit 5s default when seconds are omitted
- Treat null billable-unit rates as absent before clip lookup

This replaces #51299 with a smaller scope. Catalog rows for the 23 Pixverse ids follow in a separate PR, since the cost map guard reads catalogs with main's reader.

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin prices a fal video deployment per clip, but the gateway can't read it

1. The admin sets `output_cost_per_video_clip` with a 5s 480p price of $0.19 on the deployment
2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4018/v1/videos for a 5s 480p clip
3. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` reads 0.025, the per-second fallback, and that is the spend recorded

After: the same request is billed the clip price

1. The admin sets the same `output_cost_per_video_clip` price
2. The developer sends the same POST http://localhost:4018/v1/videos
3. `x-litellm-response-cost` reads 0.19, and the key's spend goes up by 0.19

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10648
