## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Pixverse A, B and C verified at billing tip 4a26478f

All three cases now have real-provider evidence at **`4a26478f43f08fa924f84d36a0542f70c479f787`**. A and B were rerun at this exact tip, not carried forward from 143d577b. C uses the successful same-tip run recorded earlier and was not submitted again. Main remains the already recorded `bad8b1dae853bb1811ae19f73bbae729bf78ed2c` baseline.

| Case | Main header / persisted spend | Billing header / persisted spend | Actual billing fal payload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A, seconds "5", size "540p" | $0.00 / $0.00 | $0.29 / $0.29 | duration "5", resolution "540p" |
| B, no seconds, size "360p" | $0.00 / $0.00 | $0.17 / $0.17 | duration "5", resolution "360p" |
| C, native duration "5", resolution "360p" | HTTP 400, no generation | $0.15 / $0.15 | duration "5", resolution "360p" |

The documented provider defaults were 5s and 720p. C bills the catalog's $0.15 cell, rather than the deployment's $0.17 cell.

The setup and config are byte-identical to the preceding runs. Both serving workers, dedicated Redis port 6407 for router and coordination state, PostgreSQL spend persistence, the loopback real-fal payload observer, and the custom cost-map URL are unchanged. The catalog SHA-256 remains `67834cb1fd7d7bc4d05fa9e5d524817742f8b5bdb8ba02ad0109481561e239fa`. The captured source was remote with no fallback. No relevant fal, video cost, or pass-through changes were present between the retained main baseline and locally cached origin/main `45b726fdab098440b2688113aeeefe8406e98527`.

### Exact-tip rerun spend

Total estimated vendor spend across the Pixverse review runs is $1.15. The provider ledger was not queried. Proof services were stopped afterward. The new artifacts are under `/home/ubuntu/pixverse-pricing/review-tip-ab`.


<details>
<summary>Historical runs and provenance, including original baseline, full setup, helper source, and the completed same-tip C run</summary>

### Configured per-clip video billing

Before is main `df8b8d1b518adc9c72aa1046792bb05f66f00177`, the default-branch tip fetched and pulled before starting this work. This is archived LongCat SDK evidence, measured before the current tip. The SDK outputs below were measured at `ae833096d6a422f4cce1413ad3d2f1dcba41cc42` and are carried forward because this explicit 5s/480p LongCat path is unchanged.

#### Configuration and commands

### Historical Pixverse run originally at 143d577b

Cases A and B verify the billing and transformation fixes. Case C found a blocker. The pass-through returned HTTP 400 on both main and billing, despite the shared catalog containing its 5s/360p price. No pass-through generation reached fal, so a successful after pass-through charge is not established. No repository code was changed to work around it.

Fresh main was pulled before testing and resolved to `bad8b1dae853bb1811ae19f73bbae729bf78ed2c`. The earlier SDK run used `143d577b1c525b965a8ce978235771ca31599caa`, and the current billing tip is `4a26478f43f08fa924f84d36a0542f70c479f787`. Main's native extension was built independently from its worktree. Billing's native extension was rebuilt separately. The billing leg ran first while main's independent wheel finished building.

| Case | Main fal payload | Main cost header / persisted spend | Billing fal payload | Billing cost header / persisted spend |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A, seconds 5 and size 540p | duration "5", resolution absent, provider default 720p | $0.00 / $0.00 | duration "5", resolution "540p" | $0.29 / $0.29 |
| B, no seconds and size 360p | duration and resolution absent, provider defaults 5s/720p | $0.00 / $0.00 | duration "5", resolution "360p" | $0.17 / $0.17 |
| C, native duration 5 and resolution 360p | HTTP 400, no fal POST | no cost header or generation call ID | HTTP 400, no fal POST | no cost header or generation call ID |

All four submitted videos completed without a reported error. Total estimated vendor spend is **$0.70**, below $1.50. Recorded fixture spend is $0.46. Vendor prices and deliberately different deployment fixture prices are not interchangeable. The provider account ledger was not queried.

### Setup and runnable commands

Both legs used port 4018, two workers, the same dedicated Redis on 127.0.0.1:6407 for router and coordination state, and the existing local PostgreSQL database for spend persistence. The config was generated from `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml`. `/model/info` and `/model/cost_map/source` were checked before submitting any generation on each leg. There were no pending PostgreSQL migrations.

The actual CLI command in each worktree was the following, using that leg's config path.

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py   --config /home/ubuntu/pixverse-pricing/review-proof/LEG/config.yaml   --port 4018 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload   --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Environment variable names used were `FAL_AI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `PYTHONPATH`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=False`, `LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4028/catalog.json`, and `FAL_AI_QUEUE_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4028`. No secret values are included here. The run reused those three credentials from the existing authorized QA proxy process, without printing them. A repeat can instead supply them through its own environment and pass source PID 0 to the helper.

To observe the exact outgoing payload without editing repository code, a transparent loopback HTTP forwarder listened on port 4028. It sent the same request bytes and Authorization header to `https://queue.fal.run`, returned the real response, and logged only the target URL, JSON body, status, and provider request ID. It did not mock or generate responses. Both SDK deployments used its `api_base`. Pass-through used `FAL_AI_QUEUE_API_BASE`. Provider polling was real too. Ledger entries were reserved before forwarding, no retries were enabled, duplicate case submissions were blocked, and requests beyond the $1.50 estimate limit or outside 5s/360p/540p/720p were blocked before reaching fal.

The same process served the copied catalog at `/catalog.json`. This copy starts with fresh main's full catalog and replaces only the requested Pixverse row with the catalog branch's row. The two deployed configs are byte-identical. The cost-map URL, bytes, source revision, and deployed pricing were identical on both legs. SDK fixture prices appear only in deployment `model_info`. The catalog's 360p cell is $0.15, distinct from the deployment's $0.17.

Runnable local helper commands are below. Submissions deliberately refuse an existing response artifact, so do not rerun the generation commands in this completed proof directory. Repeating a paid run needs a fresh `QA_REVIEW_ROOT` and renewed spend authorization.

<details>
<summary>Commands, source, or recorded output</summary>

```bash
# For before use LEG=before and REPO=/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-clip-billing-main
# Supply the three exported QA credentials, or use the existing QA PID
# as the last argument instead of 0. The captured run used QA PID 96206.

$PY -u -P "$HELPER" info "$LEG"

$PY -u -P "$HELPER" case "$LEG" B
$PY -u -P "$HELPER" case "$LEG" C
```

```python
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

import httpx
import yaml

ROOT = Path(os.environ.get('QA_REVIEW_ROOT', '/home/ubuntu/pixverse-pricing/review-proof'))
CHECKOUT = Path('/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm')
PY = str(CHECKOUT / '.venv/bin/python')
ENDPOINT = 'fal-ai/pixverse/v5/text-to-video'
MODEL = 'fal_ai/' + ENDPOINT
PRICES = {'5s': {'360p': 0.17, '540p': 0.29, '720p': 0.41}}
BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:4018'
OBSERVER = 'http://127.0.0.1:4028'
LOCK = threading.Lock()


def save(path, value):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2))


def credentials(pid):
    if pid == 0:
        return {name: os.environ[name] for name in ('FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'DATABASE_URL')}
    own_qa_env = dict(part.split('=', 1) for part in Path(f'/proc/{pid}/environ').read_bytes().decode().split('\0') if '=' in part)
    return {name: own_qa_env[name] for name in ('FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'DATABASE_URL')}


def prepare():
    ROOT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for leg in ('before', 'after'):
        (ROOT / leg).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    catalog = json.loads(Path('/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-clip-billing-main/model_prices_and_context_window.json').read_text())
    source = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'litellm_fal_pixverse_clip_prices_v2:model_prices_and_context_window.json'], cwd=CHECKOUT))
    catalog[MODEL] = source[MODEL]
    save(ROOT / 'catalog.json', catalog)
    config = yaml.safe_load((CHECKOUT / 'litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml').read_text())
    config['model_list'] = [{
        'model_name': 'pixverse-review',
        'litellm_params': {'model': MODEL, 'api_key': 'os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'api_base': OBSERVER, 'use_in_pass_through': True},
        'model_info': {'mode': 'video_generation', 'output_cost_per_video_clip': PRICES},
    }]
    config['router_settings'] = {'num_retries': 0, 'redis_host': '127.0.0.1', 'redis_port': 6407}
    config['general_settings'] = {
        **config.get('general_settings', {}), 'database_url': 'os.environ/DATABASE_URL',
        'master_key': 'os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'disable_spend_logs': False,
        'proxy_batch_write_at': 1, 'disable_model_info_refresh': True,
        'coordination_redis': {'host': '127.0.0.1', 'port': 6407},
    }
    config.pop('sandbox_tools', None)
    config['litellm_settings'] = {'drop_params': True, 'num_retries': 0, 'disable_aiohttp_transport': True}
    for leg in ('before', 'after'):
        (ROOT / leg / 'config.yaml').write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config, sort_keys=False))
    print('Catalog SHA256', hashlib.sha256((ROOT / 'catalog.json').read_bytes()).hexdigest())
    print('Catalog row', json.dumps(catalog[MODEL]))
    print('Deployment clip prices', json.dumps(PRICES))


def serve():
    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, *_):
            pass

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path == '/catalog.json':
                body = (ROOT / 'catalog.json').read_bytes()
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(body)))
                self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(body)
                return
            self.forward()

        def do_POST(self):
            self.forward()

        def forward(self):
            body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0)))
            target = 'https://queue.fal.run' + self.path
            event = None
            if self.command == 'POST':
                with LOCK:
                    ledger = json.loads((ROOT / 'ledger.json').read_text()) if (ROOT / 'ledger.json').exists() else []
                    label = json.loads((ROOT / 'active-case.json').read_text())
                    data = json.loads(body)
                    seconds = float(data.get('duration', 5))
                    resolution = data.get('resolution', '720p')
                    cost = {'360p': 0.15, '540p': 0.15, '720p': 0.20}.get(resolution)
                    valid = self.path == '/' + ENDPOINT and seconds == 5 and cost is not None
                    valid = valid and not any(row['leg'] == label['leg'] and row['case'] == label['case'] for row in ledger)
                    valid = valid and len(ledger) < 6 and sum(row['estimated_cost'] for row in ledger) + (cost or 0) <= float(os.environ.get('QA_REVIEW_BUDGET', '1.50'))
                    if not valid:
                        (ROOT / 'STOP').write_text('Budget, request shape or duplicate-submission guard stopped a call')
                        self.send_error(409, 'Live proof guard stopped submission')
                        return
                    event = {**label, 'url': target, 'method': 'POST', 'body': data, 'effective_duration': seconds,
                             'effective_resolution': resolution, 'estimated_cost': cost, 'status': 'submitted'}
                    ledger.append(event)
                    save(ROOT / 'ledger.json', ledger)
                    print(json.dumps(event), flush=True)
            headers = {key: value for key, value in self.headers.items() if key.lower() in ('authorization', 'content-type', 'accept')}
            with httpx.Client(timeout=180, follow_redirects=False) as client:
                response = client.request(self.command, target, headers=headers, content=body)
            if event is not None:
                with LOCK:
                    ledger = json.loads((ROOT / 'ledger.json').read_text())
                    for entry in ledger:
                        if entry['leg'] == event['leg'] and entry['case'] == event['case']:
                            entry['status'] = response.status_code
                            entry['provider_request_id'] = response.json().get('request_id') if response.is_success else None
                    save(ROOT / 'ledger.json', ledger)
                print('Fal response', event['leg'], event['case'], response.status_code, flush=True)
            self.send_response(response.status_code)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', response.headers.get('Content-Type', 'application/json'))
            self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(response.content)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(response.content)

    print('Real-fal transparent observer and cost map listening on 127.0.0.1:4028', flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 4028), Handler).serve_forever()


def start(leg, repo, source_pid):
    env = {**os.environ, **credentials(source_pid), 'PYTHONPATH': f'{repo}:{repo}/enterprise',
           'LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP': 'False', 'LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL': OBSERVER + '/catalog.json',
           'FAL_AI_QUEUE_API_BASE': OBSERVER}
    active = ROOT / 'active-proxy.pid'
    if active.exists():
        try:
            os.killpg(int(active.read_text()), signal.SIGTERM)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pass
    for _ in range(120):
        with socket.socket() as probe:
            if probe.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1', 4018)) != 0:
                break
        time.sleep(0.25)
    listeners = subprocess.check_output(['ss', '-ltnp', '( sport = :4018 )'], text=True)
    assert len(listeners.strip().splitlines()) == 1, 'Proxy port still occupied'
    curl = subprocess.run(['curl', '--max-time', '2', '-fsS', BASE + '/health/liveliness'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert curl.returncode == 7
    proof = listeners + f'Pre-start curl exit {curl.returncode}\n' + curl.stderr
    print(proof, flush=True)
    (ROOT / leg / 'port-free.txt').write_text(proof)
    command = [PY, 'litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py', '--config', str(ROOT / leg / 'config.yaml'), '--port', '4018',
               '--num_workers', '2', '--detailed_debug', '--reload', '--use_v2_migration_resolver']
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=repo, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
    active.write_text(str(process.pid))
    (ROOT / leg / 'proxy.pid').write_text(str(process.pid))
    print('Proxy PID', process.pid, 'revision', subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=repo, text=True).strip(), flush=True)
    with (ROOT / leg / 'proxy.log').open('wb') as log:
        for line in iter(process.stdout.readline, b''):
            safe = line
            for value in credentials_values(env):
                safe = safe.replace(value.encode(), b'[REDACTED]')
            log.write(safe)
            log.flush()
    process.wait()


def credentials_values(env):
    return tuple(env[key] for key in ('FAL_AI_API_KEY', 'LITELLM_MASTER_KEY', 'DATABASE_URL') if env.get(key))


def client_for(leg):
    env = credentials(int((ROOT / leg / 'proxy.pid').read_text()))
    return httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + env['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}, timeout=180)


def info(leg):
    with client_for(leg) as client:
        for _ in range(120):
            try:
                if client.get('/health/liveliness').is_success:
                    break
            except httpx.ConnectError:
                pass
            time.sleep(1)
        response = client.get('/model/info')
        response.raise_for_status()
        rows = [{'model_name': row['model_name'], 'model': row['litellm_params']['model'],
                 'api_base': row['litellm_params']['api_base'],
                 'pricing': {key: value for key, value in row['model_info'].items() if key.startswith('output_cost') and value is not None}}
                for row in response.json()['data']]
        assert len(rows) == 1 and rows[0]['model'] == MODEL and rows[0]['pricing']['output_cost_per_video_clip'] == PRICES, rows
        source = client.get('/model/cost_map/source')
        source.raise_for_status()
        assert OBSERVER + '/catalog.json' in source.text, 'Expected custom catalog not loaded'
        save(ROOT / leg / 'model-info.json', rows)
        save(ROOT / leg / 'cost-map-source.json', source.json())
        workers = re.findall(r'Started server process\s*\[(\d+)\]', (ROOT / leg / 'proxy.log').read_text())
        assert len(set(workers)) == 2, workers
        print('GET /model/info HTTP', response.status_code, json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
        print('Serving worker PIDs', workers)
        print('GET /model/cost_map/source HTTP', source.status_code, json.dumps(source.json()))


def case(leg, name):
    folder = ROOT / leg
    assert (folder / 'model-info.json').exists() and not (ROOT / 'STOP').exists()
    assert not (folder / f'{name}-response.json').exists(), 'No duplicate submissions'
    body = {'prompt': 'A red ball rests on a white table. Static camera.'}
    if name == 'C':
        path = '/fal_ai/' + ENDPOINT
        body.update(duration='5', resolution='360p')
    else:
        path = '/v1/videos'
        body.update(model='pixverse-review', size='540p' if name == 'A' else '360p')
        if name == 'A':
            body['seconds'] = '5'
    save(ROOT / 'active-case.json', {'leg': leg, 'case': name})
    save(folder / f'{name}-request.json', body)
    ledger = json.loads((ROOT / 'ledger.json').read_text()) if (ROOT / 'ledger.json').exists() else []
    before = len(ledger)
    with client_for(leg) as client:
        response = client.post(path, json=body)
    (folder / f'{name}-response.json').write_text(response.text)
    headers = {key: value for key, value in response.headers.items() if key in ('x-litellm-call-id', 'x-litellm-response-cost', 'x-litellm-model-id')}
    save(folder / f'{name}-headers.json', headers)
    ledger = json.loads((ROOT / 'ledger.json').read_text()) if (ROOT / 'ledger.json').exists() else []
    output = {'http': response.status_code, 'headers': headers, 'fal_post_count_before_after': [before, len(ledger)],
              'response': {key: response.json().get(key) for key in ('id', 'request_id', 'status', 'seconds', 'size', 'usage', 'error', 'detail')}}
    save(folder / f'{name}-result.json', output)
    print(leg, name, json.dumps(output, indent=2))
    if len(ledger) > before:
        print('Actual forwarded Fal request', json.dumps(ledger[-1]))
    assert response.status_code == (400 if leg == 'before' and name == 'C' else 200), output
    assert len(ledger) == before + (0 if response.status_code == 400 else 1)
    if leg == 'after':
        assert abs(float(headers['x-litellm-response-cost']) - {'A': 0.29, 'B': 0.17, 'C': 0.15}[name]) < 1e-9, output


def verify(leg, cases=('A', 'B', 'C')):
    folder = ROOT / leg
    with client_for(leg) as client:
        for name in cases:
            output = json.loads((folder / f'{name}-result.json').read_text())
            if output['http'] != 200:
                print(leg, name, 'HTTP 400 before dispatch, no Fal POST and no generation call ID')
                continue
            data = json.loads((folder / f'{name}-response.json').read_text())
            if name == 'C':
                response = client.get('/fal_ai/fal-ai/pixverse/requests/' + data['request_id'] + '/status')
            else:
                response = client.get('/v1/videos/' + data['id'])
            response.raise_for_status()
            status = {key: response.json().get(key) for key in ('status', 'error')}
            save(folder / f'{name}-poll.json', status)
            call_id = output['headers'].get('x-litellm-call-id')
            assert call_id, output
            spend = client.get('/spend/logs', params={'request_id': call_id})
            spend.raise_for_status()
            rows = [{key: row.get(key) for key in ('request_id', 'spend', 'model')} for row in spend.json()]
            save(folder / f'{name}-spend.json', rows)
            print(leg, name, 'poll', json.dumps(status), 'persisted spend', json.dumps(rows))
            assert status['status'] not in ('failed', 'FAILED'), status
            assert len(rows) == 1 and abs(rows[0]['spend'] - float(output['headers']['x-litellm-response-cost'])) < 1e-9, rows


if __name__ == '__main__':
    action = sys.argv[1]
    if action == 'prepare':
        prepare()
    elif action == 'serve':
        serve()
    elif action == 'start':
        start(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4]))
    elif action == 'info':
        info(sys.argv[2])
    elif action == 'case':
        case(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    elif action == 'verify':
        verify(sys.argv[2], tuple(sys.argv[3:]) or ('A', 'B', 'C'))
```

<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f25fd2c4dfc240bdb8788452299e2c81
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f25fd2c4dfc240bdb8788452299e2c81?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A key pinned to one customer org could create another org
- The 403 came back after the new org row was written
- Introduced by #51637, same class as the member case fixed in #51548

How it solves it:

- The pinned-org check now runs before an unknown alias is registered
- Same 403 body as before, and no row is written
- A key pinned to the alias itself still auto-registers it

## User Flow

Before: a key locked to one customer org can leave a stray org behind for any name it sends, even though the call is refused

1. An admin issues a key with `metadata.customer_org_id` set to `org-a`
2. The key holder sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with header `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: org-b`, a name nobody has registered
3. The response is 403 `API key is not allowed to act for this customer member's organization`
4. The admin lists GET https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations and finds a new `org-b` they never created
5. The key holder can repeat this with any name and fill the org list with junk

After: the same refused call leaves nothing behind

1. An admin issues a key with `metadata.customer_org_id` set to `org-a`
2. The key holder sends the same POST with header `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: org-b`
3. The response is the same 403
4. The admin's org list has no `org-b`
5. The key holder can no longer create orgs outside the one the key is pinned to

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, run the same way for both legs against local Postgres and a real Anthropic call. Env vars set were `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The proxy ran with one worker, without `--reload` and without Redis, because the bug is a single request's write order and needs no shared state.

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
```


<details>
<summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
P=4310; MK=$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY; S=$(openssl rand -hex 3)
A=org-a-$S; B=org-b-$S
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "create $A: %{http_code}\n" localhost:$P/management/v1/customer_organizations -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"customer_org_id\":\"$A\",\"alias\":\"$A\"}"
KEY=$(curl -s localhost:$P/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"metadata\":{\"customer_org_id\":\"$A\"}}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "key pinned to customer_org_id=$A"
chat(){ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" localhost:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $1" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":5,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' | cut -c1-220; }
echo "--- chat with own alias $A"; chat $A
echo "--- chat with unknown alias $B"; chat $B
echo "--- org rows for $B after the 403:"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select customer_org_id, alias, created_by from \"LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable\" where customer_org_id='$B'"
echo "(rows: $(psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable\" where customer_org_id='$B'"))"
```

</details>

### Before (7a72c2b17a)

1. `./repro.sh`

```
create org-a-819ebe: 201
key pinned to customer_org_id=org-a-819ebe
--- chat with own alias org-a-819ebe
{"id":"chatcmpl-8d7bfb98-cdc5-4677-9f7d-9492d06a67e9","created":1794593935,"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hello! 👋","role"
HTTP 200
--- chat with unknown alias org-b-819ebe
{"error":{"message":"API key is not allowed to act for this customer member's organization","type":"auth_error","param":"x-litellm-customer-member-id","code":"403"}}
HTTP 403
--- org rows for org-b-819ebe after the 403:
org-b-819ebe|org-b-819ebe|x-litellm-customer-org-alias
(rows: 1)
```

### After (d929cae33d, the tip 192460a92d only changes one test expectation on top of it)

```

key pinned to customer_org_id=org-a-39ea65
--- chat with own alias org-a-39ea65
{"id":"chatcmpl-35c32225-c6f7-47a7-a14d-ff0c2a115cb9","created":1794594368,"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hello! 👋","role"
HTTP 200
--- chat with unknown alias org-b-39ea65
{"error":{"message":"API key is not allowed to act for this customer member's organization","type":"auth_error","param":"x-litellm-customer-member-id","code":"403"}}
HTTP 403
--- org rows for org-b-39ea65 after the 403:
(rows: 0)
```

Tests. `tests/integration/authorization/test_customer_org_alias_key_scope.py` drives a real proxy and Postgres. On the merge base it fails with `assert ['integration-org-90d9...'] == []` and on this branch it passes. `tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_hierarchy_auth.py` passes with 54 tests, and `make check` passes.

`tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_user_api_key_auth.py` had one case that expected 401 for a pinned key naming an unknown alias when the registration itself fails. That request now gets the 403 before registration is tried, so the case expects 403.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Pinned key plus unknown alias plus failing registration: 401 becomes 403
  - With a working database this request already returned 403 on main
- A malformed alias still returns 401 for a pinned key

title: fix(vertex_ai): report PDF tokens and cost on Gemini embedContent responses
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

PDF embeddings on Vertex Gemini Embedding 2 now report the tokens Google counted and a real cost, where before they showed 0 tokens and $0. PDF tokens are priced at the image rate, which is what Google's pricing page says.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2c7548608f254befafcd952514332e6e
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2c7548608f254befafcd952514332e6e?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- PDF embeddings on `gemini-embedding-2` report 0 tokens and $0
- Text sent with a PDF loses its tokens too
- One unknown modality discards the whole usage block

How it solves it:

- `DOCUMENT` tokens count as image tokens, at the image rate
- Any other unknown modality counts as text tokens
- Usage parsing accepts any modality name

## User Flow

Before: a developer embedding a PDF gets a vector back but no token counts, so the call is logged at $0

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"model": "gemini-embedding-2"` and a PDF file block as `input`
2. The response is 200 with a 3072-dim vector, `"prompt_tokens": 0`, `"total_tokens": 0` and `"prompt_tokens_details": null`
3. The `x-litellm-response-cost` response header reads `0.0`

After: the same request reports the tokens Vertex counted and a real cost

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with the PDF file block
2. The response is 200 with `"prompt_tokens": 258`, `"total_tokens": 258` and `"image_tokens": 258` in `prompt_tokens_details`
3. The `x-litellm-response-cost` response header reads `0.00011609999999999999`

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10391

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live Vertex calls through two proxies, the merge base on port 4101 and this branch on port 4102. Both ran with two workers sharing one dedicated Redis on port 6390, and both logs show two `Started server process` lines. Postgres was left out because the token counts and the cost are read straight from the response body and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header. Env vars used are `VERTEXAI_PROJECT`, `VERTEX_AI_DEVIN_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` and `LITELLM_DANGEROUSLY_PERMIT_WEAK_OR_UNSET_MASTER_KEY=true`

`config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-embedding-2
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/gemini-embedding-2
      vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT
      vertex_location: global
      vertex_credentials: os.environ/VERTEX_AI_DEVIN_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6390
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6390
```

Redis and proxy start, the proxy command run once in each checkout with its own port

```bash
redis-server --port 6390 --save "" --appendonly no --daemonize yes
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <port> --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Client, where `<input>` is the JSON shown in each case

```bash
curl -s -D headers.txt localhost:<port>/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-embedding-2","input":<input>}'
grep -i x-litellm-response-cost headers.txt
```

### Before (7a72c2b17a)

#### PDF only

1. `<input>` is `[{"type":"file","file":{"file_data":"gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/pdf/invoice.pdf","format":"application/pdf"}}]`
2. `usage` is `{"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens_details": null, "prompt_tokens_details": null}` with a 3072-dim vector
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0`

#### Text plus PDF

1. `<input>` is `["Summarize this invoice",{"type":"file","file":{"file_data":"gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/pdf/invoice.pdf","format":"application/pdf"}}]`
2. `usage` is `{"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens_details": null, "prompt_tokens_details": null}`
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0`

#### Image only

1. `<input>` is `[{"type":"file","file":{"file_data":"gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/image/scones.jpg","format":"image/jpeg"}}]`
2. `usage` has `"prompt_tokens": 258` and `"image_tokens": 258`
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00011609999999999999`

#### Text only

1. `<input>` is `"hello world"`
2. `usage` has `"prompt_tokens": 2` and `"text_tokens": 2`
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 4e-07`

### After (b2694055f7)

#### PDF only

1. Same `<input>` as before
2. `usage` is `{"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 258, "total_tokens": 258, "completion_tokens_details": null, "prompt_tokens_details": {"audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": null, "text_tokens": 0, "image_tokens": 258, "video_tokens": 0, "initial_prompt_tokens": null}}`
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00011609999999999999`, the same as a 258 token image

#### Text plus PDF

1. Same `<input>` as before
2. `usage` has `"prompt_tokens": 262`, `"text_tokens": 4` and `"image_tokens": 258`
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0001169`

#### Image only

1. Same `<input>` as before
2. `usage` has `"prompt_tokens": 258` and `"image_tokens": 258`, unchanged
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00011609999999999999`, unchanged

#### Text only

1. Same `<input>` as before
2. `usage` has `"prompt_tokens": 2` and `"text_tokens": 2`, unchanged
3. `x-litellm-response-cost: 4e-07`, unchanged

The two new unit tests fail on 7a72c2b17a and pass on b2694055f7

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- PDF tokens use the image rate, per Google's pricing notes
  - Source is "Document token billing" on https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, read 2026-11-13
  - That note is on the Gemini API page, the Vertex page lists no document rate
- Chat completions still bucket `DOCUMENT` tokens as text, untouched here

### Low

- Unknown modalities bill at the text rate, a guess until Google documents them
- `PromptTokensDetails.modality` is now a plain string, so `schema.d.ts` changed
- The proof ran without Postgres, so the spend log row was not checked
- AI Studio (`gemini/`) and audio or video inputs were not rerun live

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(budgets): reset 12months and other long unit spellings on their short form's schedule
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Fix the parser for dates 

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/01b5a4e32cf4447db80d8cac0171222d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/01b5a4e32cf4447db80d8cac0171222d?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `budget_duration: "12months"` or `"12mos"` is accepted as a 12 month budget
- Its spend counter then resets every midnight, not January 1
- Same for `1month`, `7days`, `2weeks`, `1hour`, `5min`, `30sec`

How it solves it:

- `_parse_duration` reads the unit the way `duration_in_seconds` already does
- Long spellings now reset on their short form's schedule
- Short forms (`12mo`, `1mo`, `30d`, `7d`) are untouched
- `3months` style values keep today's nightly reset, they never raise

## User Flow

Before: an admin who types the long spelling gets a yearly budget that refills every night

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new with `{"max_budget": 1200, "budget_duration": "12months"}` and get a 200
2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/budget/list and see `budget_reset_at` set to the next midnight UTC
3. After midnight the budget's spend is back at 0, so the $1,200 yearly cap is available again every day

After: the same request gives a budget that resets once a year

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new with `"budget_duration": "12months"` and get a 200
2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/budget/list and see `budget_reset_at` set to January 1 of next year, the same as `"12mo"`
3. Spend keeps counting against the $1,200 cap until January 1

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. The integration harness starts a real proxy with its own Postgres and Redis per worker, sends POST `/budget/new` with `{"max_budget": 1200.0, "budget_duration": "<value>"}` using the master key, then reads `created_at` and `budget_reset_at` for that `budget_id` from `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`. Both legs ran the same command on 2026-11-13 UTC. I did not run a separate hand-typed curl against a long-lived proxy, and I did not wait past a midnight to watch spend drop to 0.

```bash
T=tests/integration/management/test_listing_and_health_contracts.py
K=test_twelve_month_budget_resets_on_january_first_however_the_unit_is_spelled
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2 .venv/bin/python tests/integration/run.py management --results /tmp/integ \
  "$T::$K[12mo]" "$T::$K[12months]" "$T::$K[12mos]"
```

### Before (7a72c2b17a)

1. `12mo` passes with `budget_reset_at` 2027-01-01 00:00:00
2. `12months` fails, the stored row is `{'created_at': '2026-11-13 18:30:28.578', 'reset_at': '2026-11-14 00:00:00'}`
3. `12mos` fails, the stored row is `{'created_at': '2026-11-13 18:30:28.732', 'reset_at': '2026-11-14 00:00:00'}`
4. Result line is `2 failed, 1 passed in 106.58s`

### After (a8a0780da2)

1. `12mo`, `12months` and `12mos` all pass with `budget_reset_at` 2027-01-01 00:00:00
2. Result line is `3 passed in 116.44s`

The parser on its own, with now fixed at 2026-11-13 18:00 UTC and `get_next_standardized_reset_time(<value>, now, "UTC")`.

| `budget_duration` | Before (7a72c2b17a) | After (a8a0780da2) |
|---|---|---|
| `12mo` | 2027-01-01 | 2027-01-01 |
| `12months`, `12mos` | 2026-11-14 | 2027-01-01 |
| `1month` | 2026-11-14 | 2026-12-01 |
| `7days` | 2026-11-14 | 2026-11-16 |
| `2weeks` | 2026-11-14 | 2026-11-27 |
| `1hour` | 2026-11-14 00:00 | 2026-11-13 19:00 |
| `5min` | 2026-11-14 00:00 | 2026-11-13 18:05 |
| `30sec` | 2026-11-14 00:00:00 | 2026-11-13 18:00:30 |
| `3months` | 2026-11-14 | 2026-11-14 |
| `3mo` | raises `ValueError` | raises `ValueError` |

`tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_duration_parser.py` had 8 failing cases with the new tests on the old parser, and 78 pass with the fix.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Existing budgets stored with a long spelling move to the short form's schedule at their next reset
  - a `1hour` budget that reset nightly now resets hourly
  - a `12months` budget that reset nightly now resets January 1
- `duration_in_seconds` still ignores trailing letters, so `12monkeys` is still accepted as 12 months

### Low

- `3months` and other long month counts besides 1 and 12 still reset nightly, on purpose
  - the short form `3mo` raises, and a stored row must not start raising in the reset job
- The existing fallback test used `1hr` as its unrecognized value, it now uses `1y`

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes budget reset timing for stored long-spelled durations at next reset; existing `12months`/`1hour` budgets move from nightly to correct schedules, which corrects spend enforcement but shifts behavior for live budgets.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes budget reset scheduling when admins use **long spellings** of durations (`12months`, `7days`, `1hour`, etc.). Those strings were parsed with the raw trailing letters as the unit, so annual budgets reset nightly instead of on January 1 and other intervals followed the wrong cadence.
> 
> **`_parse_duration`** now normalizes units the same way **`duration_in_seconds`** does via **`_extract_from_regex`**, so long forms inherit their short form’s reset schedule (`12months`/`12mos` → `12mo`, `1month` → `1mo`, and so on). **Non-calendar month counts** spelled out (`3months`) still use the spelled unit so they keep the existing nightly fallback and don’t start raising like **`3mo`**.
> 
> Tests cover unit parity for long vs short forms, the `3months` edge case, integration for `12mo`/`12months`/`12mos` reset dates, and a small tweak to an unrecognized-duration fallback assertion (`1y` instead of `1hr`).

title: fix(proxy): drop a customer override expiry sent without an override
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

slight hardening

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/90b8c788a6514808b7b74b90029d900c
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/90b8c788a6514808b7b74b90029d900c?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `budget_override_expires_at` was stored on rows with no `budget_override`
- A past expiry stored that way stayed on the row
- A later `budget_override` inherited it and was silently ignored

How it solves it:

- `override_expiry()` returns `None` when the row ends up without an override
- Create paths for members and teams go through the same helper
- A new override never inherits an expiry left on an override-less row

## User Flow

Before: an admin's budget override on a customer member is accepted but never applied

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_members with `budget_override_expires_at: "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"` and no `budget_override`
2. The 201 response echoes `budget_override_expires_at: "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z"` with `budget_override: null`
3. They send PATCH https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_members/{id} with `{"budget_override": {"max_budget": 50}}`
4. The 200 response shows `budget_override.max_budget: 50` but `effective_budget.max_budget: 10`, the template value, and the 2020 expiry is still there

After: the same two requests leave the override in effect

1. They send the same POST with an expiry and no `budget_override`
2. The 201 response shows `budget_override_expires_at: null`
3. They send the same PATCH with `{"budget_override": {"max_budget": 50}}`
4. The 200 response shows `effective_budget.max_budget: 50` and `budget_override_expires_at: null`

The same applies to `/management/v1/customer_teams`, and to a PATCH that sends only the expiry.

## Relevant issues

Follow-up to #51459, which introduced these routes.

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, a local Postgres and one proxy per leg. I ran a single worker without Redis because the behavior is one database write and read with no shared router or counter state.

```bash
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://<user>:<password>@localhost:5432/<db> LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=<key>
uv run prisma db push --accept-data-loss --skip-generate
uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4311
```

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

<details>
<summary>repro.sh</summary>

```bash
B=http://127.0.0.1:4311/management/v1; H=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json")
S=$(date +%s)
j() { python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps({"budget_override": (d.get("budget_override") or {}).get("max_budget"), "budget_override_expires_at": d.get("budget_override_expires_at"), "effective_max_budget": (d.get("effective_budget") or {}).get("max_budget")}))'; }
curl -sS "${H[@]}" $B/customer_organizations -d "{\"customer_org_id\":\"org-$S\",\"default_budgets\":[{\"name\":\"base\",\"max_budget\":10}]}" >/dev/null
curl -sS "${H[@]}" $B/customer_teams -d "{\"customer_team_id\":\"team-$S\",\"parent_org_id\":\"org-$S\"}" >/dev/null
curl -sS "${H[@]}" $B/customer_members -d "{\"customer_member_id\":\"m-$S\",\"parent_team_ids\":[\"team-$S\"],\"budget_override_expires_at\":\"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z\"}" | j
curl -sS "${H[@]}" -X PATCH $B/customer_members/m-$S -d '{"budget_override":{"max_budget":50}}' | j
```

</details>

### Before (7a72c2b17a)

1. POST `customer_members` with a 2020 expiry and no `budget_override`
   `{"budget_override": null, "budget_override_expires_at": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z", "effective_max_budget": 10.0}`
2. PATCH `customer_members` with `budget_override.max_budget` 50 and no expiry
   `{"budget_override": 50.0, "budget_override_expires_at": "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z", "effective_max_budget": 10.0}`

### After (e3b24869fc, the tip before a test-only cleanup commit)

1. POST `customer_members` with a 2020 expiry and no `budget_override`
   `{"budget_override": null, "budget_override_expires_at": null, "effective_max_budget": 10.0}`
2. PATCH `customer_members` with `budget_override.max_budget` 50 and no expiry
   `{"budget_override": 50.0, "budget_override_expires_at": null, "effective_max_budget": 50.0}`

Tests. `tests/integration/management/test_customer_override_expiry.py` (members and teams, real proxy and Postgres) is 2 failed on the base and 2 passed on the fix. The three new cases in `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/test_customers.py` are 3 failed on the base and 3 passed on the fix, and the two touched unit files are 142 passed.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- An expiry sent without an override is dropped, not rejected with a 4xx
  - Chosen so no request that succeeds today starts failing
- Rows that already hold a stray expiry are not rewritten
  - The next override on them no longer inherits it

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes budget override persistence for customer hierarchy APIs; incorrect logic could affect billing limits, though scope is narrow and well-tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`budget_override_expires_at`** being persisted on customer **teams** and **members** when no **`budget_override`** exists, which could leave a past expiry on the row and make a later override look present but not affect **`effective_budget`**.
> 
> **`override_expiry`** now takes the full row, returns **`None`** whenever **`override_id`** is missing, and only reuses a stored expiry when the row already has an override. Team/member **create** and **update** paths all route expiry through this helper instead of copying the payload field directly.
> 
> Adds **integration** and **unit** tests covering expiry-only create/patch and stale DB expiry when a new override is added.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 181f31336a8cd2e36188e03c0a279c4c661a508e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: fix(ui): accept exponent notation when re-parsing stored customer budget values
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5847a6d0da7247e18d6c1a73ada274b4
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/5847a6d0da7247e18d6c1a73ada274b4?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Stored spend limits below 0.000001 load into the form as `5e-7`
- The form's own number check rejects `5e-7`
- So any budget edit on that customer cannot be saved

How it solves it:

- Spend limit and soft budget now accept an exponent suffix
- Rate limits still accept digits only

## User Flow

Before: an admin cannot change any budget field on a customer organization whose spend limit is below 0.000001

1. They open /ui/customers/manage?org=org-tiny-budget&tab=settings, where Spend limit (USD) shows `5e-7`
2. They change Requests per minute from 10 to 20 and click Save changes
3. The page shows "Enter finite, non-negative limits. Rate limits must be whole numbers." and nothing is saved

After: the same edit saves and the spend limit is kept

1. They open /ui/customers/manage?org=org-tiny-budget&tab=settings, where Spend limit (USD) shows `5e-7`
2. They change Requests per minute from 10 to 20 and click Save changes
3. The page shows "Changes saved" and the organization has `max_budget: 5e-07`, `rpm_limit: 20`

The same applies to customer teams and member overrides, and to Soft budget (USD).

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

- Proof ran one proxy worker without Redis, the change is browser-only

## Final Attestation

</details>

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, a local proxy on Postgres with no models and the dashboard dev server pointed at it. Env vars used are `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD` and `LITELLM_DANGEROUSLY_PERMIT_WEAK_OR_UNSET_MASTER_KEY=true`.

2. Set Requests per minute to 20 and click Save changes. The form shows the error and no request is sent

![before](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..zmjxdK9n82HzUUeIjGVM3jc7KjkdfPUEjG2UAv5-0xs)

![after](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..VgvKDAw8na-2KMbb0PKsmpRQ8QMpgtjr1_NhujxzStw)

Regression test, `npx vitest run "src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/customerHierarchyForms.test.ts"`, fails 2 of 41 on 7a72c2b17a and passes 41 of 41 at 7189061674.

title: fix(auth): let dashboard sessions use the user's team models
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

update area to let users see teams usage if admins allow it

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3e4ba21ee2bd49d599cc33c4486ba3b2
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3e4ba21ee2bd49d599cc33c4486ba3b2?variant=devin
Requested by: @moe-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Aria shows "No available models" for users with team-only model access
- Dashboard login key ignores team models and team access groups

How it solves it:

- Non-admin dashboard sessions reuse the personal-key team inheritance path
- Access is the user's own models plus their teams' models
- Team eligibility and budget checks reuse existing personal-key helpers
- Team-only model calls charge the granting team's budget

Intentional product change: dashboard login keys now inherit team model grants without `personal_key_model_access_from_teams`. They get model access only, never MCP or agent grants.

## User Flow

Before: an internal user whose models come only from a team (directly or via an access group) cannot use Aria

1. The admin gives the user own models `["no-default-models"]` and adds them to a team whose models are `["aria-model-group"]`
2. The user signs in at http://localhost:3000/login and opens http://localhost:3000/aria
3. The model picker shows "No available models", and GET /v1/models with the session key returns `[]`
4. POST /v1/chat/completions with `claude-sonnet-5-5` returns 403 `key_model_access_denied`

After: the same user gets their team's models in Aria

1. Same setup as above
2. Same sign in and page
3. The picker shows `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and GET /v1/models returns it
4. Aria answers a real question, and its team-only call is billed to the granting team
5. A model outside the user's own and team models still returns 403

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both proxies ran with two workers and a dedicated Redis on port 6391, using a copy of `dev_config.yaml` with a real Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` deployment tagged `model_info.access_groups: ["aria-model-group"]`, plus an untagged deployment `aria-outside-group`. Env vars are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`.

```sh
uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config aria-config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard && NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000 npm run dev
```

Seed is internal user `aria-nomodels@example.test` with models `["no-default-models"]`, only a member of `aria-model-group-team`, whose models are `["aria-model-group"]`. The client logs in with POST /v2/login, takes the session key, then calls GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions with `{"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly hello."}]}`.

### Before (46716fad56)

1. `/v1/models` returns `{"data": [], "object": "list"}`
2. `/v1/models?team_id=aria-model-group-team` returns `claude-sonnet-5-5`, so the user does have the model through the team
3. `/v1/chat/completions` returns 403 `key_model_access_denied`
4. Aria shows no models

![before](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..eh6d7N147QFOqUlLbETgWzjql8I8RyyW7WaB-w61_vE)

### After (34baa35635)

1. `/v1/models` returns `claude-sonnet-5-5`
2. `/v1/chat/completions` returns 200 with `hello`
3. `/v1/chat/completions` with `aria-outside-group` returns 403 `key_model_access_denied`
4. Aria answers "29 times 37 is 1,073." on the real model

![after](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..xGt5TfeVYgjl6vV-31RVVtDYI6POgh2kfJ4YeffLNno)

#### Own model restrictions still apply

At the same tip, a user with own models `["claude-sonnet-5-5"]` and no team, and one also in a team with only `claude-sonnet-5-5`, both list only `claude-sonnet-5-5`. Both get 200 on it and 403 on `aria-outside-group`. A user with `["no-default-models"]` and no team lists `[]` and gets 403 on both. The direct team model case (team models `["claude-sonnet-5-5"]`) behaves the same as the access group case.

### Listing filter follow-up at ff7ef8a954

Unscoped listing still returns the user's own and team models. Explicit team requests now reuse the validated team rather than reloading the owner and all their teams. Group-only requests no longer restore ordinary model names. This also fixes the failing auto-router preview test, which already had an authorized team context.

The earlier Aria screenshots remain at 34baa35635. The dashboard UI and completion authorization did not change in ff7ef8a954. The unscoped listing follows the same path with both new options unset, and the live group-only user's normal listing still returns `claude-sonnet-5-5`. The changed API filters were checked live below. No new UI screenshot was taken for this follow-up.

Shared setup uses the two-worker commands above, port 4002 for 34baa35635 and port 4000 for ff7ef8a954, with dedicated Redis on 6391. Required environment variables are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`, `ARIA_NOMODELS_PASSWORD` and `ARIA_REVIEW_PASSWORD`. Set the last two to passwords for these test accounts. The actual review account used `ARIA_NOMODELS_PASSWORD` followed by `-review`.

<details>
<summary>Complete proxy config used for both revisions</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-sonnet-5-5
    model_info:
      access_groups: [aria-model-group]
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
  - model_name: aria-outside-group
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  store_model_in_db: true
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6391
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6391
```

</details>

The review account has own models `["claude-sonnet-5-5"]` and belongs to `aria-review-restricted-team` with that same model, plus `aria-review-outside-team` with `["aria-outside-group"]`. The original `aria-nomodels` account keeps own models `["no-default-models"]` and only `aria-model-group-team` with `["aria-model-group"]`.

<details>
<summary>Seed those fixtures on a fresh proxy database</summary>

Skip this setup when reusing the existing proof database. These requests have already been applied there.

```python
import os
import requests

base = "http://127.0.0.1:4000"
admin = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]}
for user, models, password in (
    ("aria-nomodels", ["no-default-models"], os.environ["ARIA_NOMODELS_PASSWORD"]),
    ("aria-review-own-team", ["claude-sonnet-5-5"], os.environ["ARIA_REVIEW_PASSWORD"]),
):
    response = requests.post(base + "/user/new", headers=admin, json={
        "user_id": user, "user_email": user + "@example.test",
        "user_role": "internal_user", "models": models, "password": password,
    }, timeout=90)
    response.raise_for_status()
for team, models, user in (
    ("aria-model-group-team", ["aria-model-group"], "aria-nomodels"),
    ("aria-review-restricted-team", ["claude-sonnet-5-5"], "aria-review-own-team"),
    ("aria-review-outside-team", ["aria-outside-group"], "aria-review-own-team"),
):
    response = requests.post(base + "/team/new", headers=admin, json={
        "team_id": team, "models": models,
        "members_with_roles": [{"user_id": user, "role": "user"}],
    }, timeout=90)
    response.raise_for_status()
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Login and replay the listing requests against each revision</summary>

Run with `PROXY_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4002` for Before and `PROXY_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4000` for After.

```python
import base64
import json
import os
import requests

base = os.environ["PROXY_BASE"]
for user, password, paths in (
    ("aria-review-own-team", os.environ["ARIA_REVIEW_PASSWORD"], (
        "/v1/models", "/v1/models?team_id=aria-review-restricted-team",
        "/v1/models?team_id=aria-review-outside-team",
    )),
    ("aria-nomodels", os.environ["ARIA_NOMODELS_PASSWORD"], (
        "/v1/models", "/v1/models?include_model_access_groups=true&only_model_access_groups=true",
    )),
):
    response = requests.post(base + "/v2/login", json={
```

title: feat(customer-portal): configure budget groups atomically
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Existing customers have no budget group editor on main.
- Background refreshes discarded drafts in the initial implementation.
- Scalar templates blocked unrelated edits and saves could partially apply.

How it solves it:

- One grouped save commits through the existing hierarchy transaction.
- Revision checks reject stale edits before writing.
- Scoped patches preserve existing settings and reset dates.
- The first group becomes the default automatically.

## User Flow

Before, the initial PR rejected edits when an existing group used a scalar budget.

1. Open `/customers/manage?org=budget-review&tab=budget_groups` with Standard and Legacy groups.
2. Change Standard's monthly cap from 10 to 15.
3. Click Save changes. The form asks for calendar limits on Legacy.

![Before, an existing scalar group blocks the save](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/559ff95b-8d09-4073-a189-197b7cc4d3c4)

After, the same customer supports grouped edits without adding unwanted limits.

1. Open `/customers/manage?org=budget-review&tab=budget_groups` with Standard and Legacy groups.
2. Change Standard's monthly cap from 10 to 15.
3. Also change Legacy's policy, add Trial at 5/month and 60/year, and select Trial as default.
4. Click Save changes and reload. All changes persist together.

![After, the grouped configuration persists](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/181ba346-88d8-434d-819d-1c74742c4271)

Recorded browser walkthrough, 26 seconds. This GIF uses timestamped captures of the real local dashboard.

![Grouped save recorded in the real dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81406e3a-833d-4a38-a53a-ead0c9906f70)

## Design

The dashboard sends one PATCH to `/management/v1/customer_organizations/{customer_org_id}/default_budgets`. Its body contains the complete retained group list, patches for edited settings, the final default name, and the revision returned with the organization. Existing template IDs remain stable. Names may be swapped in the same save.

The existing hierarchy transaction locks the organization and its templates, checks the revision and final configuration, checks referenced deletions, then applies the writes. A validation rejection or database error applies nothing. Member assignment and existing default changes share the organization lock. The existing chunked query helper checks references before deleting groups without exceeding SQL parameter limits. The existing cache invalidation helper refreshes inherited budgets after commit.

The revision covers group configuration and the default. Usage and window resets do not make an otherwise current form stale. The server preserves the current reset dates under the template locks. A draft retains its original snapshot through query refreshes. A conflict keeps the draft visible and offers an explicit Discard edits and reload action. Successful responses update the existing TanStack query cache with server IDs before clearing the draft.

This reuses the shared create/edit fields, hierarchy transaction and budget-write helpers, typed HTTP client, public errors, and cache invalidation. The batch request replaces the browser's ordered create/update/default/delete loop. No migration or new dependency is needed.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests.
- [x] Focused tests pass locally.
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks.
- [x] The change is scoped to customer budget group configuration.
- [ ] Automated reviews on the latest commit have finished and findings are addressed.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The screenshots above use the same local customer and URL. The before screenshot reproduces the defect in PR revision `aca93af7a0`. The recording exercises the rebuilt editor at `31d94dfa7c092dd5e87960c1b136887836cb25f7`; the after screenshot verifies the final merged implementation at `0422f0f5c5513b35d7fac7a28c012b525b097b9c`. The proxy ran with two workers and a dedicated PostgreSQL database and Redis instance. No provider call is needed for this budget-management flow.

Shared setup uses `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` from the local environment. Values are not included here.

```yaml
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 59869
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 59869
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

```sh
uv sync --frozen --group proxy-dev --extra proxy
uv run --no-sync python litellm/scripts/prisma_generate_if_needed.py
uv run --no-sync prisma db push --skip-generate --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma
uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /path/to/proxy-config.yaml --port 4117 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

In another shell:

```sh
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4117 npm run dev -- --port 3017 --hostname 127.0.0.1
```

Seed the browser scenario, then sign in at `http://127.0.0.1:3017` and follow the user flow above.

```sh
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4117/management/v1/customer_organizations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"customer_org_id":"budget-review","alias":"Budget groups review","default_budget_template":"Standard","default_budgets":[{"name":"Standard","budget_limits":[{"budget_duration":"1mo","max_budget":10,"reset_at":"2027-01-15T00:00:00Z"},{"budget_duration":"12mo","max_budget":100,"reset_at":"2027-11-15T00:00:00Z"}]},{"name":"Legacy","max_budget":25,"budget_duration":"7d","rpm_limit":30}]}'
```

After merging current main at `f81006b8fd14a906f72e354f494a750cfe850b64`, the same live API checks passed again. A browser stale-save check also retained the unsaved $18 cap and displayed the conflict; Discard edits and reload restored the saved $15 cap and the other editor's change.

![Stale save preserves the draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f7f32d9-3153-40e4-83df-2161111df2b4)

The live API verification exercised additions, renames, deletion, default selection, inherited member budgets, and scoped patches. Two simultaneous saves using one revision returned 200 and 409. Retrying a committed save returned 409 without creating duplicates. Removing an assigned group returned 409 without writes. A temporary constraint failure on the dedicated QA database, injected after an earlier update and insert, rolled back both writes. The test trigger was removed afterward.

<details>
<summary>Exact live API verification script</summary>

Run with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` set and `LITELLM_TEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4117`. Use an isolated QA database with capacity for one new customer. Set `DATABASE_URL` only to an isolated QA database to include the injected-failure check, which creates and removes a temporary trigger.

```python
import json
import os
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

import httpx

BASE = os.environ.get("LITELLM_TEST_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:4117")
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]}
ORG = "budget-groups-qa-" + uuid4().hex[:8]
ROOT = "/management/v1/customer_organizations/" + ORG


def call(method, path, body=None, expected=200):
    response = httpx.request(method, BASE + path, headers=HEADERS, json=body, timeout=30)
    assert response.status_code == expected, (path, response.status_code, response.text)
    return response.json()


def configuration(org, groups, default):
    return {"expected_revision": org["budget_groups_revision"], "default_budgets": groups,
            "default_budget_template": default}


def retained(org):
    return [{"budget_id": g["budget_id"], "name": g["name"]} for g in org["default_budgets"]]


initial = call("POST", "/management/v1/customer_organizations", {
    "customer_org_id": ORG, "alias": "Grouped save QA " + ORG, "default_budget_template": "Standard",
    "default_budgets": [
        {"name": "Standard", "budget_limits": [
            {"budget_duration": "1mo", "max_budget": 10, "reset_at": "2027-01-15T00:00:00Z"},
            {"budget_duration": "12mo", "max_budget": 100, "reset_at": "2027-11-15T00:00:00Z"}]},
        {"name": "Legacy", "max_budget": 25, "budget_duration": "7d", "rpm_limit": 30},
        {"name": "Rate only", "tpm_limit": 500}, {"name": "Removable", "max_budget": 1},
    ]}, expected=201)
team = call("POST", "/management/v1/customer_teams", {"parent_org_id": ORG}, expected=201)
member = call("POST", "/management/v1/customer_members", {"parent_team_ids": [team["customer_team_id"]]}, expected=201)
before = call("GET", ROOT)
standard, legacy, rate, removable = before["default_budgets"]
rejected = configuration(before, [{"budget_id": legacy["budget_id"], "name": "Changed", "max_budget": 999},
                                 {"name": "New", "max_budget": 1}], "New")
call("PATCH", ROOT + "/default_budgets", rejected, expected=409)
assert call("GET", ROOT) == before
changed = [
    {"budget_id": standard["budget_id"], "name": "Legacy", "budget_limits": [
        {"budget_duration": "1mo", "max_budget": 15}, {"budget_duration": "12mo", "max_budget": 100}]},
    {"budget_id": legacy["budget_id"], "name": "Standard", "cap_policy": "pause_allow_increase"},
    {"budget_id": rate["budget_id"], "name": "Rate only"},
    {"name": "New", "budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "1mo", "max_budget": 30}]},
]
body = configuration(before, changed, "New")
saved = call("PATCH", ROOT + "/default_budgets", body)
assert saved["default_budgets"][0] == {**standard, "name": "Legacy", "budget_limits": [
    {**standard["budget_limits"][0], "max_budget": 15}, standard["budget_limits"][1]]}
assert saved["default_budgets"][1] == {**legacy, "name": "Standard", "cap_policy": "pause_allow_increase"}
assert saved["default_budgets"][2] == rate
assert saved["default_budget_template_id"] == saved["default_budgets"][3]["budget_id"]
assert call("GET", ROOT) == saved
inherited = call("GET", "/management/v1/customer_members/" + member["customer_member_id"])
assert inherited["effective_budget"]["budget_limits"][0]["max_budget"] == 15
call("PATCH", ROOT + "/default_budgets", body, expected=409)
assert call("GET", ROOT) == saved


def racing_save(amount):
    rows = retained(saved)
    rows[0]["budget_limits"] = [{"budget_duration": "1mo", "max_budget": amount}]
    response = httpx.patch(BASE + ROOT + "/default_budgets", headers=HEADERS,
                          json=configuration(saved, rows, "New"), timeout=30)
    return response.status_code, amount, response.json()


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
    races = list(pool.map(racing_save, [20, 25]))
assert sorted(status for status, _, _ in races) == [200, 409], races
winner = next(result for status, _, result in races if status == 200)
assert call("GET", ROOT) == winner

if os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL"):
    import psycopg
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], autocommit=True) as db:
        db.execute('''CREATE FUNCTION reject_review_group() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
        BEGIN IF NEW.name = 'qa-rejected-insert' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'QA injected constraint failure' USING ERRCODE='23505';
        END IF; RETURN NEW; END $$''')
        db.execute('CREATE TRIGGER reject_review_group BEFORE INSERT ON "LiteLLM_BudgetTable" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION reject_review_group()')
        try:
            count_before = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "LiteLLM_BudgetTable"').fetchone()[0]
            rows = retained(winner)
            rows[0]["cap_policy"] = "pause_allow_increase"
            rows.extend([{"name": "qa-created-before-failure", "max_budget": 1},
                         {"name": "qa-rejected-insert", "max_budget": 2}])
            call("PATCH", ROOT + "/default_budgets", configuration(winner, rows, "qa-created-before-failure"), expected=409)
            assert call("GET", ROOT) == winner
```
