title: fix(proxy): register a customer member in a customer org with no default budget
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Fix a bug in the upsert

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2f5f0d2ee07d42379fe469b343e2eb08
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2f5f0d2ee07d42379fe469b343e2eb08?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- First request for a new customer org drops its customer member
- Member spend for that customer org is never tracked

How it solves it:

- Register the customer member with no budget
- Admin-created customer members still require a budget

Intentional product change: a customer member registered from request headers in a customer org with no default budget is now created uncapped. Its spend is tracked and nothing limits it until an admin assigns a budget.

## User Flow

Before: a first request that names a new customer org and a new customer member succeeds, but the customer member never exists

1. Send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: brand-new-org` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id: dave`, and get 200
2. GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/brand-new-org returns 200 with the request's spend
3. GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members/dave returns 404

After: the same request registers the customer member under the new customer org

1. Send the same POST with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: after-org` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id: erin`, and get 200
2. GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/after-org returns 200 with the request's spend
3. GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members/erin returns 200 with the same spend, `parent_org_id: after-org`, `parent_team_ids: ["after-org:default"]` and `budget_id: null`

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, the same for both runs: Postgres, a dedicated Redis on port 6380, two workers, a real OpenAI call. Env vars: `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`. `--reload` was dropped so both workers serve, and two worker PIDs were confirmed in the log.

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --port 4000 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-4o-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6380
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6380
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: True
```

```
KEY=$(curl -s localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"models":["gpt-4o-mini"]}' | jq -r .key)
curl -s localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-litellm-customer-org-alias: <org>' -H 'x-litellm-customer-member-id: <member>' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'
sleep 25
curl -s localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/<org> -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
curl -s localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members/<member> -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
```

### Before (46716fad56)

1. Chat completion with org `brand-new-org`, member `dave`: HTTP 200
2. `customer_organizations/brand-new-org`: HTTP 200, `spend: 4.35e-06`
3. `customer_members/dave`: HTTP 404

### After (f1400a1f23)

1. Chat completion with org `after-org`, member `erin`: HTTP 200
2. `customer_organizations/after-org`: HTTP 200, `spend: 4.35e-06`
3. `customer_members/erin`: HTTP 200, `spend: 4.35e-06`, `parent_org_id: after-org`, `parent_team_ids: ["after-org:default"]`, `budget_id: null`

The Before run used main at 46716fad56, a few commits behind the merge base. None of the commits between them touch the registration path.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Uncapped members spend freely until an admin sets a budget
  - The customer org and customer team budgets still apply
- An admin can now edit an uncapped member without adding a budget
  - Removing the last budget from a budgeted member is still refused

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes customer billing behavior by allowing uncapped member-level spend for auto-registered users in orgs without default budgets, though org/team limits may still apply.
> 
> **Overview**
> **First-time customer members** from request headers (`x-litellm-customer-member-id`) are now created even when their organization has **no default budget template**, instead of failing with `BUDGET_REQUIRED` or never appearing in management APIs.
> 
> Auto-registration in `ensure_customer_member` calls `create_member` with **`budget_required=False`**, so the row is created with no template or override; spend is still tracked with **no member-level cap** until an admin assigns a budget. **Admin-driven** `create_member` keeps the default **`budget_required=True`**, so manually added members still need a budget.
> 
> `update_member` is tightened so **removing the last budget is only blocked for members that already had one**, and **alias-only (or other non-budget) patches** no longer clear `budget_id` / overrides—budget fields update only when explicitly present in the patch.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c90463b2b8cc66b72a0dc17a19bd8e2aaa417b0d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(customers): align budget displays with recorded reset windows
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Monthly and yearly profiles incorrectly showed “No cap”
- Calendar totals could incorrectly mark a member's budget exhausted
- The table and management summary could show different balances

How it solves it:

- Pair every limit with its own recorded budget spend
- Reuse the gateway's configured reset window calculation
- Share one display model across usage and management

Intentional product change: monthly spend uses a thin progress bar, yearly spend stays a simple amount/limit, and customer share uses a compact shaded bar. Budget comparisons follow configured reset windows. Share and tokens retain the UTC calendar month. Chart filters do not change current budgets

## User Flow

Before, a member below their monthly budget appears blocked

1. Open `/customers/usage?org=budget-design-demo&from=2026-11-01&to=2026-11-30`
2. Find Reset window, with $20 calendar usage but $8 after its configured reset
3. Observe `$20 / $10`, `$10 over`, and “Reached limit”
4. Open another member's management page. Its additional limits appear without matching balances

![Before, calendar totals incorrectly exhaust the member budget](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d358d94e-3a40-408f-93d7-ac8e1ee88c10)

After, both views compare each limit with its own recorded spend

1. Open the same customer usage route and dates
2. Find Reset window, with $20 calendar usage but $8 after its configured reset
3. Observe `$8 / $10`, `$2 remains`, and “Within budget”
4. Open the member's management page. Both monthly balances and yearly spend match the usage table

![After, independent budget balances and correct exhausted statuses](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f80dbb26-bf9c-4cf3-b83b-356ffeedde44)

## Changes

- Add batched recorded budget usage to customer hierarchy responses
- Reuse enforcement window boundaries and maintained window spend semantics
- Keep simultaneous scalar and calendar limits independent
- Share budget amounts, remaining balances, and labels across views
- Preserve configured limits when an older backend cannot report window usage

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Added meaningful regression tests
- [x] Focused backend and dashboard tests pass
- [x] Required CI/CD checks pass
- [x] Scope is limited to customer budget display
- [x] Automated reviews on the latest commit are complete

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The screenshots above compare the actual baseline and final dashboards against the same isolated gateway and persisted synthetic data. The baseline dashboard is `81597bc9cbd3ec03c4dc8efd7e36721ffa7dd4b1`; the recorded final dashboard is `0a573657e3c91c29270692e13091c41e56bef669`. Current tip `bdf00d47ce159a022020305ae2db532e8157cc9b` only narrows the budget-row query to the hierarchy page's entity type and returns early for an empty page. Dashboard sources are unchanged, and live member detail and paginated list reads returned the same four fixture balances after that correction. Both use the final backend so every response and fixture is identical. The previous UI ignores the added budget usage projection

The walkthrough shows real browser filtering, drill-down, and the management summary

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc1b13bf-5779-4f51-bb9e-ae9e16acc511

### Shared setup

Two local gateway worker PIDs served an isolated Postgres 17 database and Redis 7 instance. The gateway reset uses `America/Los_Angeles` at `09:00`, which makes the November window start `2026-11-01T17:00:00Z`. No production fixtures were changed and this display proof did not make provider requests

Set `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` for an isolated local gateway. The tested database port was 63323 and Redis port was 63326

```yaml
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 63326
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 63326
litellm_settings:
  timezone: America/Los_Angeles
  budget_reset_time: "09:00"
```

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config budget-proof.yaml \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4188 --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4188 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true \
  npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3184
```

Run the baseline dashboard from a separate checkout on port 3185. Sign into both normally

<details>
<summary>Fixture client used for the November 13 comparison</summary>

This creates safe demo entities through the management API and seeds recorded accounting rows through Prisma in the isolated database. Save as `seed-budget-proof.py` and run with the same `DATABASE_URL` and master-key environment

```python
import asyncio
import os
import json
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import httpx
from prisma import Prisma

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent
API = 'http://127.0.0.1:4188'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer '+os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}

def post(path, body):
    response = httpx.post(API+'/management/v1/'+path, headers=headers, json=body, timeout=30)
    if response.status_code == 409:
        if path == 'customer_organizations':
            return httpx.get(API+'/management/v1/customer_organizations/budget-design-demo',headers=headers).json()
        return None
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

async def main():
    org=post('customer_organizations', {
        'customer_org_id':'budget-design-demo','alias':'Budget design demo','budget':{'max_budget':1000,'budget_duration':'1mo'},
        'default_budgets':[{'name':'Monthly and annual','budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'1mo','max_budget':10},{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':100}]}],
    })
    post('customer_teams',{'customer_team_id':'demo-services','parent_org_id':org['customer_org_id'],'alias':'Services'})
    cases=[('reset-window','Reset window',20,8,62),('monthly-limit','Monthly limit',10,10,30),('yearly-limit','Yearly limit',5,5,100),('two-limits','Two monthly limits',20,8,62)]
    for member_id,alias,calendar,monthly,annual in cases:
        extra={'budget_override':{'max_budget':50,'budget_duration':'1mo','budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'1mo','max_budget':10},{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':100}]}} if member_id=='two-limits' else {}
        post('customer_members',{'customer_member_id':member_id,'alias':alias,'parent_team_ids':['demo-services'],**extra})
    db=Prisma()
    await db.connect()
    for member_id,alias,calendar,monthly,annual in cases:
        await db.litellm_customermembertable.update(where={'customer_member_id':member_id},data={'spend':40 if member_id=='two-limits' else calendar})
        for duration,spend,start in [('1mo',monthly,datetime(2026,11,1,17,tzinfo=timezone.utc)),('12mo',annual,datetime(2026,1,1,17,tzinfo=timezone.utc))]:
            await db.litellm_budgetwindowspend.upsert(where={'entity_type_entity_id_window_duration':{'entity_type':'customer_member','entity_id':member_id,'window_duration':duration}},data={'create':{'entity_type':'customer_member','entity_id':member_id,'window_duration':duration,'window_start':start,'spend':spend},'update':{'spend':spend,'window_start':start}})
        for date,spend in [('2026-11-01',calendar),('2026-03-01',annual-calendar)]:
            await db.litellm_dailycustomermemberspend.upsert(where={'id':f'{member_id}-{date}'},data={'create':{'id':f'{member_id}-{date}','date':date,'customer_org_id':org['customer_org_id'],'customer_team_id':'demo-services','customer_member_id':member_id,'model':'demo-model','api_key':'demo-key','spend':spend,'prompt_tokens':int(spend*100),'api_requests':int(spend),'successful_requests':int(spend)},'update':{'spend':spend}})
    await db.litellm_customerorganizationtable.update(where={'customer_org_id':org['customer_org_id']},data={'spend':55})
    await db.disconnect()
    evidence={member_id:httpx.get(API+'/management/v1/customer_members/'+member_id,headers=headers,timeout=20).json() for member_id,*_ in cases}
    (ROOT/'live-window-evidence.json').write_text(json.dumps(evidence,indent=2))
    for member_id,result in evidence.items():
        print(member_id,[(b['budget_duration'],b['spend'],b['max_budget'],b['window_start']) for b in result['budget_usage']])
asyncio.run(main())

```

</details>

### Before (`81597bc9cbd3ec03c4dc8efd7e36721ffa7dd4b1`)

1. Open the usage route shown above on port 3185
2. The first two rows incorrectly show “Reached limit”, as boxed above
3. Open `/customers/manage?org=budget-design-demo&team=demo-services&member=two-limits`
4. The summary shows `$40 / $50` but only text for the additional $10 and $100 limits

### After (`bdf00d47ce159a022020305ae2db532e8157cc9b`)

1. Open the same usage route on port 3184
2. Reset window shows `$8 / $10` and `$62 / $100`
3. The monthly-exhausted and yearly-exhausted members both show “Reached limit”
4. Open the same management route. It shows `$40 / $50`, `$8 / $10`, and `$62 / $100`

296 focused backend checks and 70 dashboard tests passed. Restoring the old UI fails all three independent-window integration cases. Replacing the configured reset settings with UTC fails the backend regression. The final production build and `make check` passed, including Python type gates, dashboard lint, and generated API type synchronization. The final query correction also passed all 296 focused backend checks, `make check`, and the unbounded-IN guard with zero new or stale violations. Greptile scored `bdf00d47ce1` 5/5, and Bugbot and Veria completed with no new findings. CI code-quality and Python/JavaScript security analysis passed. All six required checks passed on this commit, including lint, unit, smoke, cost-map, spend-logs, and zizmor. The separate OSV scan still flags the unchanged lockfile dependencies listed below

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Low

- Recorded spend updates after accounting flushes and excludes pending reservations
- Older backends show unavailable window usage rather than invented balances
- OSV flags unchanged `opentelemetry-api 1.45.1` and `soupsieve 2.10` dependencies

## Final Attestation

- [x] Tests cover the reported regressions and independent budget representations

</details>



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds batched window-spend reads on every customer hierarchy read/list and shares window-spend parsing with enforcement reseed logic, so incorrect window matching could affect both display and budget accounting semantics.
> 
> **Overview**
> Customer hierarchy **list and detail responses** now include a **`budget_usage`** array that pairs each effective limit (scalar cap plus each configured window) with **recorded spend**, window start, and reset time, using the same window boundaries and **`recorded_window_spend`** semantics as spend-counter reseeding.
> 
> The **customer usage and manage dashboards** consume that projection so summaries and member tables show **independent monthly/yearly limits** (progress, remaining/over, and status) instead of comparing chart-range totals to a single cap. The usage client additionally loads **UTC month and year activity** for member share and period columns without changing how chart date filters scope the main breakdown.
> 
> **Tests** cover the new backend helper, management API shape, and UI fallbacks when window usage is missing.
>

title: fix(gemini): move the November 17 shutdown date on TTS and Live preview rows to the dates on the deprecations page
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ff185aaae7bc4e9792e6d00f83aa3b3f
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/ff185aaae7bc4e9792e6d00f83aa3b3f?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Eight gemini TTS and Live rows say they shut down on 2026-11-17
- Google's deprecations page moved or withdrew that date

How it solves it:

- Four TTS rows take December 18, 2026
- Two native audio rows take March 31, 2027
- Two `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` rows drop the date

## Changes

Source for every row is https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations.md.txt, fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-13 (four fetches, same sha256 `78ac55e6...`). Every row is kind page. The columns quoted are Model, Release date, Shutdown date, Recommended replacement. All eight rows carried `deprecation_date: 2026-11-17` since #44910 (October 8), read from the same page, which no longer contains "November 17" anywhere. The release notes page has no entry about these dates, so the deprecations page is the only source

| Row | Change | Page row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` | `deprecation_date` 2026-11-17 -> 2026-12-18 | "`gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview`, February 26, 2026, December 18, 2026, `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` or `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`" |
| `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` and bare `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` | `deprecation_date` 2026-11-17 -> 2026-12-18 | "`gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts`, May 20, 2025, December 18, 2026, `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` or `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`" |
| `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts` | `deprecation_date` 2026-11-17 -> 2026-12-18 | "`gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts`, May 20, 2025, December 18, 2026, `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` or `gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts`" |
| `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` and bare `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` | `deprecation_date` 2026-11-17 -> 2027-03-31 | "`gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025`, December 12, 2025, March 31, 2027, `gemini-3.8-live`" |
| `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` and bare `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` | `deprecation_date` and `deprecation_source` removed, `successor_model` kept | "`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`, March 11, 2026, No shutdown date announced, `gemini-3.8-live`" |

`successor_model` is unchanged on every row because the page still names the same replacements. The two `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` rows end up shaped like `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview`, which also has a replacement and no announced date. Their two lines were removed by hand in both files because `apply` in replace mode re-sorts the row's keys. Every other gemini row with a row on the deprecations page already matches it

The release notes page was read raw in the same run and has no pricing or model difference from the catalog

### Delisted by the provider

No deprecation date on the deprecations page for any of these, so they stay unchanged under ruling gemini-delisted-no-date-keep: gemini-exp-1206, gemini/gemini-exp-1114, gemini/gemini-gemma-2-27b-it, gemini/gemini-gemma-2-9b-it, gemini/gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview-native-audio-09-2025, gemini/gemma-3-27b-it, gemini/imagen-3.0-fast-generate-001, gemini/imagen-3.0-generate-001, gemini/learnlm-1.5-pro-experimental, gemini/lyria-3.5-clip-preview, gemini/lyria-3.5-pro-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-fast-generate-001, gemini/veo-3.1-generate-001. gemini/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-generate-preview and gemini/veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview already carry their October 22, 2026 shutdown date and gemini-omni-1.2-flash successor

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Cost map data only, no code change, so no new tests
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_cost_map_guard.py tests/unit/proxy/common_utils/test_model_deprecation.py tests/unit/proxy/test_model_deprecations_endpoint.py -q` passes locally with both files (138 passed)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem

## Type

Bug Fix

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Data-only pricing/catalog JSON changes that affect deprecation warnings and routing hints, with no application logic modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates Gemini model catalog metadata in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and its backup so shutdown dates match [Google’s deprecations page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations) instead of the stale **2026-11-17** value from an earlier import.
> 
> **TTS preview rows** (`gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts`, `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts`, `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview`, plus the bare `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` entry) now use `deprecation_date: 2026-12-18`. **Native audio preview rows** (`gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` and `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025`) move to **2027-03-31**.
> 
> For **`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`** (prefixed and bare), **`deprecation_date`** and **`deprecation_source`** are removed because the page lists no shutdown date; **`successor_model`** is unchanged.

title: test(spend): synchronize concurrent member resets before validation completes
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

The concurrent reset test sometimes lets one request finish before the other checks the balance, so it rejects a valid response. This change holds the balance row until both requests are waiting, keeping the test focused on concurrent database updates and lifetime spending

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0b2523379fd24ea284b9e11b5d669be3
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0b2523379fd24ea284b9e11b5d669be3?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A valid early balance check makes the test fail

How it solves it:

- Observe both database lock waits before releasing the balance
- Preserve every response and lifetime balance assertion

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at b03a9fad5df69bdbdc6a55229ceb7373258b7965, explicitly authorized by the scheduled flake-heal procedure's step 8d. This changes only test scheduling and uses the existing integration rig with real PostgreSQL, Redis, a live proxy and its peer, retries disabled, and the scripted upstream. No product behavior changes

The original test starts two requests without controlling when they reach validation. Forcing the lower reset to finish first reproduces the scheduled failure, HTTP 400 with `reset_to (600.0) must be <= current spend (500.0)`. The fixed test locks the membership row and observes both requests waiting through PostgreSQL's blocking graph before releasing it. Both requests therefore validate the same original spend, exercising the intended SQL re-check without sleeps or retries

CI failure: [Job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43343240862/job/131616360140), 1 failed variant in the collected window

Local evidence at base `46716fad5650`, with identical affected test, product and harness paths after the clean rebase to `b03a9fad5df69bdbdc6a55229ceb7373258b7965`:

- The forced ordering fails unchanged code and passes the fix
- Five separate affected-function executions passed at one worker
- The entire owning file passed, 10 tests
- Removing the product SQL's `GREATEST(total_spend, spend)` in a temporary checkout makes the lifetime-floor assertion fail, observed 148.1 instead of 612.4
- The temporary product mutation was reverted
- `make lint` passes all repository gates

<details>
<summary>Local integration setup and commands</summary>

Start PostgreSQL and a local Redis instance as in `.github/scripts/ci/run_integration.sh`, apply the repository Prisma schema, and save this wrapper as `/tmp/flake_local_rig.py`. `FLAKE_REPO` selects the checkout under test. It uses `worker_stack` to allocate isolated databases and Redis namespaces and start the same proxy and peer used by accounting integration tests

```python
import json,os,subprocess,sys
from pathlib import Path
repo=os.environ.get('FLAKE_REPO','/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm')
sys.path[:0]=[repo,repo+'/tests']
os.chdir(repo)
from tests.integration._support.workers import worker_stack,GatewayProfile

group=sys.argv[1];tag=sys.argv[2];nodes=sys.argv[3:]
root=Path('/home/ubuntu/flake-run')/tag;root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
os.environ.update({'DATABASE_URL':'postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/circle_test','LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP':'True','LITELLM_MODE':'PRODUCTION','STORE_MODEL_IN_DB':'True','AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED':'true','DO_NOT_TRACK':'1','PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED':'1','LITELLM_SALT_KEY':'sk-integration-salt','PYTHONPATH':repo+':'+repo+'/tests:'+repo+'/tests/e2e'})
os.environ['PYTHONPATH']+=':/home/ubuntu'
stack=worker_stack(root,GatewayProfile(peer=group=='accounting',replica=False,cost_map=False,coverage_file=None))
with stack.resources:
 env={**os.environ,**stack.environment,'INTEGRATION_WORKERS':'1','INTEGRATION_WORKER_ISOLATION':'1'}
 repeats=int(os.environ.get('FLAKE_REPEATS','1'))
 results=[]
 for i in range(repeats):
  command=[sys.executable,'tests/integration/run.py',group,*nodes,'--results',str(root/f'run-{i+1}')]
  print('RUN',i+1,command,flush=True)
  result=subprocess.call(command,cwd=repo,env=env)
  results.append(result)
  if result:break
 (root/'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results))
 sys.exit(any(results))
```

```sh
FLAKE_REPO=/home/ubuntu/repos/flake-reset FLAKE_REPEATS=5 /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python /tmp/flake_local_rig.py accounting reset-fixed-five tests/integration/spend/test_team_member_total_spend_reconciliation.py::test_concurrent_admin_resets_leave_one_winner_and_a_lifetime_floor_at_the_old_cycle_spend
FLAKE_REPO=/home/ubuntu/repos/flake-reset /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python /tmp/flake_local_rig.py accounting reset-file tests/integration/spend/test_team_member_total_spend_reconciliation.py
make lint
```

The forced ordering wrapper lets the lower request reach its update before starting the higher request, observing either `spend=500` or an active PostgreSQL lock wait. The unchanged test returns 400 for the higher request. With the fix both updates are held until both lock waits are visible, and the assertions pass

</details>

## Type

Test

</details>

title: fix(budgets): invalidate customer hierarchy caches through stored team IDs
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Updating a budget can return an internal error because the customer lookup asks the database for a relationship that does not exist. This change follows the stored organization and team identifiers so budget updates succeed and inherited budget caches are refreshed

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0b2523379fd24ea284b9e11b5d669be3
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0b2523379fd24ea284b9e11b5d669be3?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Budget updates fail on a nonexistent customer team relationship
- Inherited team budgets also need their member caches refreshed

How it solves it:

- Follow the member's organization relationship and stored team identifiers
- Query affected teams and invalidate their members in bounded batches

## User Flow

Before, updating an existing budget returns an internal error

1. Send `POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new` with `max_budget=10` and `rpm_limit=20`
2. Send `POST https://litellm-domain/budget/update` with its ID, `max_budget=15` and `rpm_limit=30`
3. Receive HTTP 500 instead of the updated budget

After, the same update returns and stores the new limits

1. Send `POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new` with `max_budget=10` and `rpm_limit=20`
2. Send `POST https://litellm-domain/budget/update` with its ID, `max_budget=15` and `rpm_limit=30`
3. Receive HTTP 200 with both updated limits, which also persist in PostgreSQL

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 771ee7f65ce727f62d293f01f5bd120b5a0dd3e5, explicitly authorized by the scheduled flake-heal procedure's step 8d. Verification uses the workflow's accounting integration group with real PostgreSQL, Redis, two live proxies and the scripted upstream, retries disabled

MATEO-HEAL, run 1. The invalid relationship was introduced by [#51582](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51582). Under the automation's excluded-owner rule, these rows fall back to their test author, resolved to Mateo from the human commits on the test PRs

`LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable` has `parent_org` and `parent_team_ids`, with no `parent_team` relationship. The original nested query fails before an update can finish. The fix retains direct member and organization matches, finds teams using either their budget or override, then matches members with `parent_team_ids.has_some` in `IN_LIST_CHUNK_SIZE` batches

### Before, base 46716fad5650

The affected functions reproduce the scheduled error, `Could not find field at findManyLiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable.where.OR.parent_team`. The new real-database regression also fails with `POST /budget/update: 500`. The inherited-team cache regression fails on unchanged product code because the member's cached limits remain present

### After, 771ee7f65ce727f62d293f01f5bd120b5a0dd3e5

The affected functions and new real-database regression pass five consecutive executions at one worker, 12 parameter variants each time. Both whole owning files pass, 28 tests, with two pre-existing skips. The focused unit file passes all 49 tests, including real cache eviction for an inherited team budget and preservation of an unrelated member's cache. `make lint` passes all gates

CI repair 1 supplies async customer-team lookups in the existing team, tag, access-group and budget-helper unit database doubles. All five caller unit files now pass, 769 tests, and `make lint` passes again. No additional product behavior changed

The local unit run initially encountered the host SQLite 3.37.2 rejecting existing `->>` SQL. It passes with SQLite 3.46.1 from `pysqlite3-binary==0.5.4`, matching CI's support for that existing SQL. This environment repair does not change repository files

The last product edit only removes a loop-local `Final` binding rejected by the type checker, preserving the same query and invalidation. The five integration executions cover that unchanged behavior, and the 49-test unit run and lint cover the final source. Clean rebases changed neither the affected files nor their test harness

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- DeepInfra serves four active models missing from LiteLLM's cost map
- Requests log `$0` spend, and capability lookups treat them as unmapped

How it solves it:

- Adds `deepinfra/` entries for all four models to both cost maps
- Copies rates, token caps, and capability flags from DeepInfra's API

## User Flow

Before: a proxy user calling these four DeepInfra models gets zero spend tracked

1. They configure one of the four `deepinfra/` models (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash`, `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL`, or `tencent/Hy4-preview`)
2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with that model
3. The request returns HTTP 200, and `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` logs `$0` spend since no price row exists

After: the same request records prompt, completion, and cached token spend

1. They configure one of the four `deepinfra/` models (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash`, `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL`, or `tencent/Hy4-preview`)
2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with that model
3. The request returns HTTP 200, and `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` logs token spend using the matching DeepInfra rates

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description [insert handwritten description here]
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0b230bedc4904852ad50f8753ff6023b Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0b230bedc4904852ad50f8753ff6023b?variant=devin Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - GrokBot bots never call a gateway, so LiteLLM cannot see them - Admins at large companies cannot register thousands of bots one by one How it solves it: - New signed endpoint for GrokBot enterprise inference hooks returns allow or deny - Every bot seen in a hook frame is registered automatically by its bot id - Bots inherit their team's default policy, like blocked tools or required owner - Shadow mode records would-deny verdicts without blocking anyone - New External agents tab on the Agents page shows only exceptions, with bulk fixes ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin has no way to see or govern the company's GrokBot bots in LiteLLM 1. The admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=agents and only sees agents registered by hand 2. Employees keep running GrokBot bots, and none of them show up anywhere in LiteLLM After: the admin connects GrokBot once, and every bot shows up and follows team policy 1. On https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=agents they open External agents, click Connect GrokBot, paste the `whsec_` secret and copy the hook URL `https://litellm-domain/grok_bot/inference_hook/` 2. They paste that URL into GrokBot's inference hook settings, and bots appear as employees use them 3. Summary cards show bots discovered, covered by team policy, needing an owner, unmapped members and denied in 24h, with Exceptions only on 4. They select bots and click Assign team, Assign owner or Confirm owner, and Map members takes a `grokbot_member_id,litellm_user_id` CSV 5. With a policy blocking `Shell`, Shadow mode allows it and logs "Would deny", and Enforce mode returns a deny with the policy reason ![External agents summary after discovery](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..fcbi-qcbssRrZRsPvhO45bw51bWCsVb8EIc71UcF1nY) ![Decisions in shadow and enforce](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..kv-CPKbHC6HTmUZEk-FBBp0mSsGkT0DfVHQnIxc1Ouc) ![Bulk actions](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..t68XG_GPRTkHlCgBjzF2hJBumfO-JnroSdRS1QZgst0) ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy with 2 workers sharing one Redis, real Postgres, and the real dashboard on `http://localhost:3000` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true`. There was no real GrokBot enterprise tenant, so `grokbot_sim.py` sends frames signed the way the GrokBot docs describe (Standard Webhooks `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature: v1,`). Env vars are `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `GROKBOT_SIGNING_SECRET`. ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config grokbot-dev-config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4000 ``` `grokbot-dev-config.yaml` is `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` with `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis` pointed at `127.0.0.1:6397`. ### Before (a7c8f6287f) 1. There is no External agents tab on the Agents page and no `/grok_bot/inference_hook/{source_id}` route, so hook frames get a 404 ### After (d7331f8e16, recorded) 1. Connect GrokBot in Shadow mode from the UI, map 6 of 8 members via CSV, add an Engineering team policy blocking `Shell`, then send 80 signed frames from 40 bots ```bash python grokbot_sim.py --base http://127.0.0.1:4000 --source --bots 40 --actors 8 --tools ReadFile ``` ```json {"bot": "sim-bot-0", "actor": "sim-actor-0", "tool": "ReadFile", "status": 200, "verdict": {"action": "allow"}} {"summary": {"discovered": 40, "covered_by_team_policy": 10, "needs_owner": 40, "unmapped_actors": 10, "denied_24h": 0}} ``` 2. A bad signature is rejected, also through the dashboard origin URL the UI shows ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/grok_bot/inference_hook/ -H 'webhook-id: bad' -H "webhook-timestamp: $(date +%s)" -H 'webhook-signature: v1,invalid' -d '{}' ``` ```text {"detail":"Invalid webhook signature"} HTTP 401 ``` 3. With the org default policy blocking `Shell`, a Shell tool call in Shadow returns allow and the Decisions tab shows "Would deny · shadow", Enforced No. After switching to Enforce in the UI ```json {"bot": "sim-bot-0", "actor": "sim-actor-0", "tool": "Shell", "status": 200, "verdict": {"action": "deny", "deny_reason": "Your team's policy does not allow the tool Shell."}} ``` ReadFile still returns allow, and both rows show Enforced Yes. 4. Bulk Assign team on 2 bots took coverage from 10 to 12, Assign owner and Confirm owner took needs-owner from 40 to 36, and mapping the last 2 members took unmapped to 0. A resolved bot leaves Exceptions only but stays in the full list with Issues None. 5. Load. 200 concurrent signed frames across 50 bots gave p50 604 ms, p95 713 ms, max 742 ms, 0 errors, and 200 decisions persisted. The demo surfaced two counting bugs, fixed in b2bd7f5dcc. Denied (24h) counted shadow would-denies and Unmapped members counted bots instead of distinct members. Both now have regression tests that failed on the old code. The recording was made before that fix. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - Not validated against a real GrokBot enterprise tenant, only the documented contract - Only bots that send a hook frame are discovered, dormant bots stay invisible - Hook frames carry no token or cost data, so no spend governance yet - Source, policy and member caches are per worker with a 20s TTL ### Low - Inferred owner is the first mapped member seen, flagged until an admin confirms - Prompt text is never stored, only tool names and verdicts - Team policy vs org default precedence was unit tested, not shown live ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- DeepInfra V4-Pro and Kimi-K3 entries lack `supports_reasoning`
- Requests passing `reasoning_effort` get rejected or silently dropped

How it solves it:

- Added `"supports_reasoning": true` to those three DeepInfra entries
- Synced backup cost map and added unit regression tests

## User Flow

Before: a developer sending `reasoning_effort` to DeepSeek-V4-Pro or Kimi-K3 on DeepInfra gets an unsupported parameter failure instead of forwarding the parameter.

3. The request fails saying `deepinfra` does not support `reasoning_effort`, or drops `reasoning_effort` when parameter dropping is enabled

After: the same request accepts `reasoning_effort` and forwards it to DeepInfra.

1. They configure `deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, `deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813`, or `deepinfra/moonshotai/Kimi-K3` on the proxy
2. They send `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro"` and `"reasoning_effort": "low"`

title: fix(openai): add gpt-image-2.6 batch prices and drop gpt-5.5-pro long context batch prices
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2a6b292f63d342339bdc43f693d5f3fa
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2a6b292f63d342339bdc43f693d5f3fa?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.6-flare` have no batch prices
- Batch image calls on them are billed at the standard rate, twice the published price
- `gpt-5.5-pro` carries long context batch prices OpenAI no longer publishes

How it solves it:

- Adds the five `_batches` price fields to both rows
- Same fields and values as `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, both cost map files edited identically
- Removes the two `above_272k_tokens_batches` fields from `gpt-5.5-pro`

## Rows changed

Both rows are kind page. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.md, fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-13, section Multimodal models, Images, Batch tab. Prices are per 1M tokens on the page and per token in the catalog

| Key | Field | Value | Quoted cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | `input_cost_per_image_token_batches` | 4e-06 | `\| gpt-image-2.6-sunburst \| Image \| $4.00 \| $15.00 \| $1.00 \|` |
| `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | `output_cost_per_image_token_batches` | 1.5e-05 | same row, Output |
| `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | `cache_read_input_image_token_cost_batches` | 1e-06 | same row, Cached input |
| `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | `input_cost_per_token_batches` | 2.5e-06 | `\| gpt-image-2.6-sunburst \| Text \| $2.50 \| - \| $0.625 \|` |
| `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | `cache_read_input_token_cost_batches` | 6.25e-07 | same row, Cached input |
| `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | `input_cost_per_image_token_batches` | 4e-06 | `\| gpt-image-2.6-flare \| Image \| $4.00 \| $15.00 \| $1.00 \|` |
| `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | `output_cost_per_image_token_batches` | 1.5e-05 | same row, Output |
| `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | `cache_read_input_image_token_cost_batches` | 1e-06 | same row, Cached input |
| `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | `input_cost_per_token_batches` | 2.5e-06 | `\| gpt-image-2.6-flare \| Text \| $2.50 \| - \| $0.625 \|` |
| `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | `cache_read_input_token_cost_batches` | 6.25e-07 | same row, Cached input |

`cache_read_input_image_token_cost_batches` is the field ruling openai-images-batch-cached-input-add-field added for the other gpt-image rows, and the code reading it merged in #50997. The standard prices on both rows already match the page and are unchanged

The rest of the page was compared cell by cell against the openai rows (624 flagship cells plus the image, audio, transcription, specialized and fine-tuning tables) with no other stated price differing from the catalog

## Fields removed

Ruling openai-long-context-dash-remove-above-272k-after-recheck says to remove the `above_272k_tokens` fields the pricing page now shows as `-`, but only after a recheck confirms no source still states them. The two rows were checked separately on 2026-11-13, every page fetched raw with a cache buster

`gpt-5.5-pro` loses `input_cost_per_token_above_272k_tokens_batches` (3e-05) and `output_cost_per_token_above_272k_tokens_batches` (0.000135), kind page. Every other field on the row is byte identical, so the standard long context prices stay

| Source | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| pricing.md, Batch table | `\| gpt-5.5-pro (<272K context length) \| $15.00 \| $90.00 \| - \| - \| - \| - \| - \| - \| - \| - \|`, long context input and output are `-` |
| pricing.md, Flex table | the same row and the same `-` cells, and the catalog never had flex long context fields for it |
| pricing.md, Standard table | `\| gpt-5.5-pro (<272K context length) \| $30.00 \| $180.00 \| - \| - \| - \| $60.00 \| $270.00 \| - \| - \| - \|`, so the standard long context prices are still published |
| pricing.md, Batch table siblings | `gpt-5.5` still shows `$5.00` and `$22.50` and `gpt-5.4-pro` still shows `$30.00` and `$135.00` for long context, so the `-` is specific to this row |
| pricing.md prose | the only long context sentence is "Short context: ≤272K input tokens. Long context: >272K input tokens." |
| models/gpt-5.5-pro.md | lists Input $30 and Output $180 with two notes, on cached input and regional processing, and nothing about prompts over 272K. The gpt-5.4-pro page by contrast says ">272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full session for standard, batch, and flex" |
| changelog.md | the GPT-5.5 Pro release entry states no prices |
| guides/batch.md and guides/flex-processing.md | no mention of 272K, long context or gpt-5.5-pro |

`tests/unit/test_cost_calculator.py` had a check that every openai row with a long context rate and a batch rate also declares the batch long context rate, and it failed on `gpt-5.5-pro` after the removal. The check now skips `gpt-5.5-pro` through a named set that cites the pricing page and the date. With the two fields gone, a `gpt-5.5-pro` batch request above 272K input tokens is billed at the flat batch rate (1.5e-05 input, 9e-05 output) where it was billed 3e-05 and 0.000135 before

The edit deletes those two lines in both cost map files directly. `apply` in replace mode was tried first and it re-sorted the row's keys and inlined `search_context_cost_per_query`, which would have changed fields the ruling says must stay byte identical

## Open items

`gpt-5.6-cyber` is left unchanged. The pricing page Specialized table shows `| gpt-5.6-cyber (long context) | - | - | - | - | - |`, but https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-cyber.md still says "Prompts with >272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full request." and "Cache writes are billed at 1.25x the uncached input token rate." The catalog's `input_cost_per_token_above_272k_tokens` 2.5e-05 and `output_cost_per_token_above_272k_tokens` 0.0001125 are exactly 2x and 1.5x the short context prices, so a source still states them. The same page gives "Maximum input tokens: 272,000", so no request can reach that tier and the fields are inert either way. The sibling `gpt-5.5-cyber-preview` shows the same `-` row and `gpt-6-cyber` still lists long context prices

## Delisted by the provider

Ids missing from the list API with no date on https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md, left for a human: `daybreak-blue-latest`, `daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-5.5-cyber`, `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `gpt-6-cyber`, `gpt-6-rosalind`, `gpt-6-astra-law`, `gpt-rosalind-discovery`, `gpt-rosalind-research`, `gpt-4o-search-preview`, `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview`. The trusted access and law ids are priced on the pricing page, so the list key most likely lacks access to them

Already dated in the catalog, no change: the other 32 delisted ids, including `gpt-5-chat` and `gpt-5-chat-latest` under ruling openai-gpt-5-chat-deprecation-date

Coverage gaps rather than delistings: `openai/container` (container pricing pseudo key) and `text-embedding-ada-002-v2` (alias of `text-embedding-ada-002`)

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Data change plus one test exemption. `pytest tests/unit/test_cost_calculator.py -k "declares_the_batch_tier or batch"` gives 67 passed at 731556e, and the two `declares_the_batch_tier[input_cost_per_token]` and `[output_cost_per_token]` cases failed in CI at 7db40e3 with `['gpt-5.5-pro'] == []`. The two cost map files are byte identical after both edits, the new fields are the ones `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` already carries, and a parsed comparison against the previous commit shows `gpt-5.5-pro` differs only by the two removed fields

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Data-only pricing catalog edits with no runtime logic changes; affects cost calculation accuracy for specific OpenAI models.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates OpenAI model cost catalog entries in **`model_prices_and_context_window.json`** and the LiteLLM backup so batch billing matches current published pricing.
> 
> For **`gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`** and **`gpt-image-2.6-flare`**, adds the five `*_batches` fields (image/text input, output, and cached-read costs) so batch API usage is charged at half the standard rate instead of falling back to non-batch prices.
> 
> For **`gpt-5.5-pro`**, removes **`input_cost_per_token_above_272k_tokens_batches`** and **`output_cost_per_token_above_272k_tokens_batches`** because OpenAI’s batch pricing table no longer lists long-context batch tiers for that model; standard long-context batch fields elsewhere on the row are unchanged.

title: fix: restore customer budget alerts after hierarchy schema changes
body:
Refs #51579 and #51582.

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

makes a bug fix to budget alert webhooks to make sure we don't send duplicate alerts

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Recurring customer alerts use a lifetime deduplication key.
- Member alerts query a removed team relation.
- Team alerts ignore their effective budget override.

How it solves it:

- Reuse the hierarchy owner’s budget reset calculation.
- Resolve member organization through its current parent organization.
- Read team overrides and apply their expiry.

Intentional product change: member budget events contain organization and member identity; team ID and alias are null because member spend aggregates across team memberships. Team budget events retain their team identity.

## User Flow

Before: customer budget alerts do not follow the current hierarchy schema.

1. Configure a customer budget webhook and recurring organization, team, or member budgets.
2. Send customer-attributed requests until spend crosses a threshold.
3. Member alerts are missing; other alerts report a lifetime period.
4. In the next budget period, the lifetime claim suppresses another crossing.

After: customer alerts use the effective budget and its current period.

1. Configure a customer budget webhook and recurring organization, team, or member budgets.
2. Send customer-attributed requests until spend crosses a threshold.
3. Receive alerts with the customer identity, threshold, and budget reset time.
4. Receive another alert after the next period crosses its threshold.

## Validation

Base: `46716fad56505ae5a0dc118a64da7a1bd6061ea3`.

- Updated regression fixtures fail before the production patch: **18 failed, 15 passed**.
- Focused alert, webhook transport, and hierarchy helper tests pass after the patch: **72 passed**.
- Source/test Ruff checks and formatter checks pass.
- Strict Ruff, type discipline, and test quality delta gates pass against the base.

```bash
uv run --no-sync pytest \
  tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking/test_customer_budget_alerts.py \
  tests/unit/integrations/test_customer_budget_webhook.py \
  tests/unit/proxy/management_helpers/test_customer_hierarchy.py -q
```

The fixtures match the current Prisma hierarchy: budget clocks live on related budget rows, and members have a parent organization plus team IDs. Query doubles reject removed relations. Tests cover all three scopes, duplicate suppression, later periods, active and expired overrides, inherited windows, and nullable member team context.

## Before and after verification

Used disposable PostgreSQL with the current generated Prisma client and a real HTTP webhook receiver. Committed $2 spend for an organization, team, and member in two distinct budget periods, then ran alert detection twice per period.

| Scope | Before: total events | After: total events |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Organization | 2, incorrect lifetime period | 4, two per reset period |
| Team | 2, incorrect lifetime period | 4, two per reset period |
| Member | 0, removed-relation query error | 4, two per reset period |

After the fix, each scope emits one soft and one hard event per period despite repeated detection. Member events contain the organization and member with null team fields. Four additional real-row cases verify active and expired team/member overrides, thresholds, and reset clocks.

This proves committed spend rows → Prisma lookup → alert detection → real HTTP delivery. It does not exercise the full proxy authentication, routing, provider, or spend-queue flow. No provider calls were made for this proof.

## Check limitations

`uv run black .` could not reach Black because the editable native rebuild exhausted available disk. The no-sync run reached Black but found 28 parse failures in unchanged Python 3.12 files under the installed Python 3.11 formatter; formatter-only changes were restored. All 72 focused tests and scoped Ruff/format checks passed again after restoration. Full `make check` could not run because its setup requires that native rebuild.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR’s scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Automated reviews have finished and findings are addressed

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: refactor(router): shape attempt kwargs in router-core
body: router-core now decides the fallback-hop parts of each attempt's kwargs and hands them to Python on the attempt step, with no change in behaviour. Just moves some logic into the rust core ## How A new `shape` module in router-core builds an `AttemptShape` from the `Attempt` it already has. The shape says which group a fallback hop writes into the metadata `model_group` (set when `fallback_level > 0`), whether the attempt is a hop (`fallback_depth > 0`), and whether the hop drops the request's `mock_timeout` because the deployment does not set its own. python-bridge sends it on every `attempt` step as `shape`, and `_native.pyi` types it On the Python side `_Driver._call` reads the shape once. `attempt_call` takes `hop_model_group` in place of `fallback_level`, `_strip_undecryptable_reasoning` gates on `fallback_hop`, and `WalkMetadata.stamp` uses `fallback_hop` to pick between stamping the caller's own metadata dict and a copy, and `drops_mock_timeout` to drop the request `mock_timeout`. Before this, each of those re-derived the same answer from the step's depth and level, the walk scope's hop kwargs and the deployment's params The values that stay in Python are the ones that are live Python objects or that read Python-only settings. That covers the caller's own metadata dict the proxy reads back, the client objects, the Logging object, deployment params Python overlays with live values (secret reference markers, Exception `mock_response`, callables), the timeout chain (its router settings and `default_litellm_params` live in Python and can hold `httpx.Timeout`), tool merge, clientside credentials, tags and the `max_parallel_requests` slot. Those still run in `update_kwargs_with_deployment`, `_set_timeouts` and `enter_deployment_slot` as before, and the driver applies the Rust decisions around them ## Test results `cargo test -p litellm-router-core` passes (249 + 107), including new rstest cases in `shape.rs` for the hop group, the hop flag, the `mock_timeout` drop and the field names that cross to Python. `cargo test -p litellm-python-bridge --lib router::` passes 43 tests, and the fallback test now checks the shape on the hop's attempt step. `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt` are clean for both crates With the native lib rebuilt from this branch, `pytest tests/unit/test_router tests/unit/router_rust` plus the encrypted content affinity and continuation prefill check tests give 5180 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `test_router_uses_the_proxy_host_without_importing_the_proxy_first`, which runs a bare subprocess that cannot import `litellm` because my local venv was synced with `--no-install-project`. It is unrelated to this diff. The ruff strict, type discipline and test quality gates pass against main, and basedpyright reports the same counts on the touched files before and after ## Caveats The hop decisions are equivalent to the old Python reads because every `fallback` event reaches `WalkMetadata.hop` and router-core gives each hop scope the attempt's own `fallback_depth`. The `mock_timeout` check now reads key presence on router-core's deployment record instead of the dict Python built. The two differ only if Kubernetes pod discovery, or Python's own copy of a default deployment whose id is not a string, added or removed a `mock_timeout` key, and neither path does that today This is a first slice of the attempt glue port. The full move of `update_kwargs_with_deployment`, `_set_timeouts`, `_with_live_params`, `shape_attempt_kwargs` and slot entry needs router-core to hold the router timeout settings and `default_litellm_params`, and to model the live param overlays, before it can match Python exactly. No Python bug was found or copied in the moved logic ---

title: fix(mistral): forward metadata in embedding requests
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/52346a6c785947b3aa788ea1718b4583
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/52346a6c785947b3aa788ea1718b4583?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `mistral/mistral-embed` silently drops the documented `metadata` field
- LiteLLM treats `metadata` as its own logging kwarg and strips it

How it solves it:

- Mistral embeddings forward the caller's `metadata` as a top-level body field
- On the proxy, only the client's own metadata is sent, never proxy-injected fields

## User Flow

Before: a developer tagging Mistral embedding requests with `metadata` never gets it to Mistral

1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings with `"model": "mistral-embed"` and `"metadata": {"label": "lit10695"}`
2. The request to Mistral goes out with only `model` and `input`
3. They get a 200 with an embedding, but Mistral never saw the metadata

After: the same request reaches Mistral with the metadata attached

1. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings with `"metadata": {"label": "lit10695"}`
2. The request to Mistral now carries `"metadata": {"label": "lit10695"}` and nothing the proxy added, like key info or headers
3. They get a 200 with the same embedding shape

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10695

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy against the real Mistral API with one worker and no Redis, since this is stateless request serialization with no routing or shared counters. `MISTRAL_API_KEY` is set in the environment.

Config `qa_config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mistral-embed
    litellm_params:
      model: mistral/mistral-embed
      api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-lit10695-local
```

Proxy command

```sh
env -u DATABASE_URL -u DIRECT_URL LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --num_workers 1 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4106
```

Request

```sh
curl -sS -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4106/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit10695-local' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"mistral-embed","input":["metadata regression"],"metadata":{"label":"lit10695"}}'
```

### Before (6d15d68bc84e)

1. Status `200`, with one 1024-dim embedding
2. The debug log shows the outgoing request has no metadata

```text
POST Request Sent from LiteLLM:
curl -X POST \
https://api.mistral.ai/v1 \
-d '{'model': 'mistral-embed', 'input': ['metadata regression']}'
```

### After (5562926109d6)

1. Status `200`, with one 1024-dim embedding
2. The debug log shows metadata going out. It sits under `extra_body` here because this log is printed before the OpenAI SDK merges `extra_body` into the top-level JSON, which the regression test checks on the actual HTTP body

```text
POST Request Sent from LiteLLM:
curl -X POST \
https://api.mistral.ai/v1 \
-d '{'model': 'mistral-embed', 'input': ['metadata regression'], 'extra_body': {'metadata': {'label': 'lit10695'}}}'
```

The new test in `tests/unit/llms/mistral/test_mistral_embedding.py` captures the outgoing HTTP body. It fails 3 of 6 cases on main and passes all 6 with the fix.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Proxy users already sending `metadata` for logging now also send it to Mistral
  - Mistral rejects non-string-ish nested values with 422, so odd logging metadata could start failing

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: feat(ui): let admins control Aria access for internal users
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

let admins control what access internal users have through aria

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3e4ba21ee2bd49d599cc33c4486ba3b2
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3e4ba21ee2bd49d599cc33c4486ba3b2?variant=devin
Requested by: @moe-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Internal users can ask Aria about their own spend only
- Admins have no way to turn Aria off or on for internal users

How it solves it:

- New UI setting `aria_internal_user_access`, default `own_usage`
- `none` hides Aria, `own_and_team_usage` adds a team usage tool
- Proxy admins and admin viewers ignore the setting

## User Flow

Before: an internal user asks Aria about their team's spend and Aria refuses

1. The internal user opens http://localhost:3000/aria and asks "How much did my team spend today?"
2. Aria says it can only see their own usage

After: the admin picks what internal users get, and team spend questions get real answers

1. The admin opens http://localhost:3000/admin-panel?tab=ui-settings and sets "Aria access for internal users" to Own and team usage
2. The internal user opens http://localhost:3000/aria and asks the same question
3. Aria calls GET /team/daily/activity/aggregated and answers with their permitted team spend and a chart
4. With No access selected, the Aria link and chat page are gone for internal users

Team usage goes through the existing endpoint, which already limits non-admins to their own teams and, unless they are team admins, their own keys. So the new option grants nothing the user could not already read on the Usage page.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Proxy started from the repo root with a copy of `dev_config.yaml` pointing router and coordination Redis at a dedicated instance on port 6391, with a real Anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5` deployment. Env vars are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`.

```sh
uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config aria-config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee proxy.log
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard && NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4000 npm run dev
```

Seed data is an internal user `aria-proof@example.test` who is a regular member of `aria-proof-team`, plus a team key that made one real `claude-sonnet-5-5` call (via /user/new, /team/new, /key/generate, /v1/chat/completions, all 200).

### Before (616471d400)

1. As the internal user, open http://localhost:3000/aria and ask "How much did my team spend today? Please query team usage, not just my own usage."
2. Aria refuses team usage and offers own usage instead

![before](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..SX9b2xKOGUPDuwQ67XykmMUp4p8Z-0rt_NceL4y2rlQ)

### After (8ccbb51abb)

#### No access

1. As admin, set "Aria access for internal users" to No access in UI Settings
2. As the internal user, the sidebar has no Aria link and /aria has no chat input

![admin none](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..1cBWFftu9QE91qWByiseI9KjmxsN6S66kIRi730GuKo)
![internal none](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..O57M1qXGGXw-SnaIZUS9HTPUQdgE8tPxzPMoiR_Hb4Y)

#### Own usage only (default)

1. As admin, select Own usage only
2. The internal user asks for their spend and their team's spend. Aria returns $0.006838 of own spend and refuses the team part, same as today

![admin own](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..p1nocBOsLATjsEOdGejbM4t3qM9wTZIY20KWAIuUpOE)
![internal own](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..m3rZlVUHMJoed8n4rrQcFwD1CQr1sh0NVdVq6U-BPFA)

#### Own and team usage

1. As admin, select Own and team usage
2. The internal user asks the team question. Aria reports $0.000072, 1 request, 20 tokens for Aria proof team with a chart
3. Proxy log shows `GET /team/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=2026-11-13&end_date=2026-11-13&api_key_limit=20 200 OK` with no user override

![admin team](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..BKuetqbPPK68J9YKJZw7qC_qA3EsyyW76w07zuwzZeE)
![internal team](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..0Ko0Guz6X6mrbZtaE0h1ViLzNvh74qVxgacL517BB5k)

Focused checks passed: `tests/unit/proxy/ui_crud_endpoints/test_proxy_setting_endpoints.py` (241 passed), dashboard vitest for UISettings, useUISettings, LiteAdmin integration, agent and usage chart tests, dashboard typecheck, and `make lint`.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Before screenshot used the base frontend against the same feature proxy
  - The base frontend never reads the new setting, so this does not change the result
- Aria still shows "no models" for users who get models only via teams. That is a separate fix in a follow-up PR

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes authorization and which usage APIs Aria can call for internal users, though team queries still rely on existing gateway enforcement.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`aria_internal_user_access`** as a persisted admin UI setting (`none`, `own_usage`, `own_and_team_usage`; default **`own_usage`**) alongside the existing global **`disable_aria`** switch. Proxy admins and proxy-wide spend viewers are unchanged.
> 
> The Admin Panel UI Settings page gets a new selector to set internal-user Aria access, with the same config-precedence read-only behavior as other managed fields. **`useUISettings`** is typed around `values` / `source` / `field_schema` so consumers can read the new flag.
> 
> **LiteAdmin / Aria** reads the setting for internal users: **`none`** removes Aria entry points and sessions; **`own_usage`** keeps today’s user-only usage tools; **`own_and_team_usage`** widens usage scope to **`user_and_teams`**, exposes **`get_team_usage_data`**, and updates prompts, welcome copy, and chart labels accordingly. Integration and agent tests cover visibility, tool lists, and team query behavior.
> 
> Backend UI-settings CRUD tests include round-trip, validation, non-admin denial, and config override for the new field.
>

title: fix(mcp): backport #51578 to lts/1.108.x
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

<!-- The author writes this in their own words, and it can be left empty. AI agents never write here and leave the
     placeholder line below as is, and when updating an existing PR they keep whatever the author wrote. Keep this heading
     Say what the PR does for users and why, then anything that keeps it working over time (a sync job, a config someone owns)
     No bullets, tables, or code names here. Everything else goes inside the Details block below -->

backport of https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51578 to `lts/1.108.x`. users on 1.108 reconnecting datadog mcp got stuck looping between datadog's allow screen and the connect page, and ended on "Authentication incomplete", because we ask datadog for its one catch-all permission, mcp_all, and it answers with a few hundred detailed ones. now whatever comes back counts for mcp_all, so they connect in one go, and sign-ins that don't ask for mcp_all work the same as before

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

backport of https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51578 to `lts/1.108.x`. cherry-picked from `b67cdcc34e` on main with no conflicts, git moved the 3 files to this line's `_experimental/mcp_server` paths by itself

Problem this solves:

- datadog mcp sign-in loops between datadog and the connect page
- datadog answers `mcp_all` with about 300 detailed scopes, never `mcp_all`
- the next try re-asks them all and the cookie passes 4096 bytes
- the browser drops it and the user sees "Authentication incomplete"

How it solves it:

- any saved grant that isn't empty covers `mcp_all`
- a request for `mcp_all` doesn't re-ask the old grant
- other scopes in that request are still checked by name
- a request without `mcp_all` works exactly like before

Intentional product change: a client that asks for `mcp_all` now counts as connected with any saved grant for that server, also on a server that lists other scopes next to `mcp_all`, so the user isn't sent back to consent. the provider still decides what the token can do

```diff
 connect check, for each requested scope
   granted if the saved grant has it
+  or it is mcp_all and the saved grant is not empty

 reconnect asks the provider for
-  the old grant plus the new request
+  only the new request, when it asks for mcp_all
+  the old grant plus the new request, otherwise
```

## User Flow

Before: a user whose datadog mcp sign-in expired can't reconnect from their mcp client

1. their mcp client opens https://litellm-domain/authorize/mcp-session for the datadog server, and the browser sends them to datadog
2. they approve on datadog and land on https://litellm-domain/ui/connect, which still shows Connect
3. they click Connect, approve on datadog again, and land on "Authentication incomplete. You can close this window."
4. every later try ends the same way, so the client never gets signed in

After: the same user finishes in one pass

1. their mcp client opens https://litellm-domain/authorize/mcp-session for the datadog server, and the browser sends them to datadog
2. they approve on datadog and land on https://litellm-domain/ui/connect, which now shows Finish connecting
3. they click Finish connecting and the mcp client is signed in

## Affected release

regression since v1.107.0-rc.1, from #45886. reproduced below on v1.108.7

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

same diff as main apart from paths. `git show b67cdcc34e` and `git show e560657afd` have identical added and removed lines

live run on this line. before is the `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.7` image as shipped, and its 2 mcp source files are byte for byte the ones at the line tip `36095e9bdf`. after is the same container with this branch's 2 source files copied in, byte for byte the ones at `e560657afd`. the proxy has its own fresh postgres, and the test user is an internal user

the provider is a local stand-in on 127.0.0.1 with two servers. `ddfake_repro` acts like datadog, it publishes only `mcp_all`, approves right away, and answers the token call with 244 detailed scopes and no `mcp_all`. `echo_repro` grants exactly the scopes it was asked for, for the cases without `mcp_all`

case 1 runs in headless chrome on the real connect page, so chrome applies its own cookie limit. a script then replays every case by playing the mcp client and the connect page's own calls, and it drops any cookie over 4096 bytes

<details>
<summary>how to rerun it</summary>
