```python
"""Local stand-in OAuth provider. /authorize and /token act like Datadog: asked for mcp_all, they grant a long
list of granular scopes. /echo/authorize and /echo/token grant exactly the scopes that were asked for.

Listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Logs each request's path and scope length to stdout.
"""

import json
import pathlib
import secrets
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

PORT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 9311
GRANT_SIZE = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 300
REAL = [l.strip() for l in (pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "scopes.txt").read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
AVG = round(sum(map(len, REAL)) / len(REAL))
PADDED = REAL + [f"{REAL[i % len(REAL)]}_{i}"[:AVG] for i in range(GRANT_SIZE - len(REAL))]
GRANTED = " ".join(dict.fromkeys(PADDED[:GRANT_SIZE]))
ECHO: dict[str, str] = {}


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *args: object) -> None:
        pass

    def _json(self, status: int, body: dict) -> None:
        raw = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(raw)

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        url = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path)
        q = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(url.query))
        if url.path in ("/authorize", "/echo/authorize"):
            scope = q.get("scope", "")
            code = "fake-code-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(8)
            if url.path.startswith("/echo"):
                ECHO[code] = scope
                ECHO["last"] = scope
            log(f"AUTHORIZE {url.path} scope has {len(scope.split())} names ({len(scope)} chars): {scope[:80]}")
            target = q["redirect_uri"] + ("&" if "?" in q["redirect_uri"] else "?") + urllib.parse.urlencode(
                {"code": code, "state": q.get("state", "")}
            )
            self.send_response(302)
            self.send_header("Location", target)
            self.end_headers()
            return
        log(f"GET {url.path} -> 404")
        self._json(404, {"error": "not_found"})

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        form = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(self.rfile.read(length).decode()))
        if self.path.startswith(("/token", "/echo/token")):
            granted = ECHO.get(form.get("code", ""), ECHO.get("last", "")) if self.path.startswith("/echo") else GRANTED
            log(f"TOKEN {self.path} grant_type={form.get('grant_type')} -> granting {len(granted.split())} scopes")
            self._json(
                200,
                {
                    "access_token": "fake-dd-access-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(16),
                    "refresh_token": "fake-dd-refresh-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(16),
                    "token_type": "Bearer",
                    "expires_in": 3600,
                    "scope": granted,
                },
            )
            return
        log(f"POST {self.path} -> 404")
        self._json(404, {"error": "not_found"})


log(f"fake Datadog on 127.0.0.1:{PORT}, grants {len(GRANTED.split())} scopes ({len(GRANTED)} chars)")
HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Handler).serve_forever()
```

```python
"""Drives a real headless Chrome through LiteLLM's Connect page for the Datadog-like server and takes screenshots.

usage: shoot.py <label> <max_rounds> [--reset]
The browser follows the page's own redirects and Chrome applies its own cookie size limit. The script only
clicks the button a user would click and takes a screenshot each time the browser comes to rest.
Prints the scope count each sign-in asks the provider for and the size of each sign-in cookie. Prints no secrets.
"""

import base64
import os
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import re
import secrets
import sys
import urllib.parse

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

BASE = os.environ.get("PROXY", "http://localhost:4002")
SERVER = os.environ.get("MCP_SERVER", "ddfake_repro")
PROVIDER = "http://127.0.0.1:9311"
CLIENT_REDIRECT = "http://127.0.0.1:8898/cb"
HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
LABEL = sys.argv[1]
MAX_ROUNDS = int(sys.argv[2])
SHOTS = HERE / "shots"

token = (HERE / "token.txt").read_text().strip()
payload = token.split(".")[1]
session_key = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload + "=" * (-len(payload) % 4)))["key"]


def challenge() -> str:
    verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest()).rstrip(b"=").decode()


def shot(page, name: str) -> None:
    button = page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("connect", re.I))
    if button.count():
        button.first.evaluate("e => { e.style.outline = '3px solid #e11d48'; e.style.outlineOffset = '4px'; }")
    path = SHOTS / f"{LABEL}-{name}.png"
    page.screenshot(path=str(path), full_page=False)
    print(f"    screenshot {path.name}")


def describe(page, context, handle: str) -> None:
    data = context.request.get(f"{BASE}/authorize/flow?flow={urllib.parse.quote(handle)}").json()
    print(f"  browser is on {page.url.split('?')[0]}")
    print(f"  page says: {' '.join(page.inner_text('body').split())[:170]}")
    print(f"  /authorize/flow: connected={data.get('connected')} requested_scopes={data.get('requested_scopes')}")


def settle(page) -> None:
    """Waits until the browser has stayed on one URL for a few seconds."""
    last, still = page.url, 0
    for _ in range(80):
        page.wait_for_timeout(250)
        still = still + 1 if page.url == last else 0
        last = page.url
        if still >= 24:
            return


with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(channel="chrome", headless=True)
    context = browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1180, "height": 760})
    context.add_cookies([{"name": "token", "value": token, "url": BASE}])
    page = context.new_page()

    def on_request(request) -> None:
        if request.url.startswith(f"{PROVIDER}/authorize"):
            scope = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(urllib.parse.urlsplit(request.url).query)).get("scope", "")
            print(f"    browser is sent to the provider asking for {len(scope.split())} scope(s)")

    def on_response(response) -> None:
        if response.url.startswith(BASE) and "/oauth/" in response.url and "/authorize" in response.url:
            for header in response.headers_array():
                if header["name"].lower() == "set-cookie" and header["value"].startswith("mcp_oauth_state"):
                    name, _, rest = header["value"].partition("=")
                    print(f"    sign-in cookie is {len(name) + len(rest.split(';', 1)[0])} bytes")
        if response.url.startswith(f"{BASE}/callback"):
            print(f"    LiteLLM /callback -> {response.status}")

    context.route(
        re.compile(r"^http://127\.0\.0\.1:8898/.*"),
        lambda route: route.fulfill(
            status=200,
            content_type="text/html",
            body="<html><body style='font:20px sans-serif;padding:40px'>MCP client: sign-in code received."
            " The client is signed in.</body></html>",
        ),
    )
    page.on("request", on_request)
    page.on("response", on_response)

    if "--reset" in sys.argv:
        deleted = context.request.delete(
            f"{BASE}/v1/mcp/server/{SERVER}/oauth-user-credential", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {session_key}"}
        )
        print(f"== reset: deleted this user's saved grant -> {deleted.status}")

    registered = context.request.post(
        f"{BASE}/register",
        data={
            "client_name": "fake mcp client",
            "redirect_uris": [CLIENT_REDIRECT],
            "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
            "response_types": ["code"],
            "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
        },
    ).json()
    query = urllib.parse.urlencode(
        {
            "client_id": registered["client_id"],
            "redirect_uri": CLIENT_REDIRECT,
            "state": secrets.token_urlsafe(12),
            "code_challenge": challenge(),
            "code_challenge_method": "S256",
            "response_type": "code",
            "resource": f"{BASE}/mcp/{SERVER}",
            "scope": "mcp_all",
        }
    )
    print("== the MCP client opens /authorize/mcp-session (scope=mcp_all) in the browser")
    page.goto(f"{BASE}/authorize/mcp-session?{query}", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
    handle = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(urllib.parse.urlsplit(page.url).query)).get("connect_flow", "")
    settle(page)
    describe(page, context, handle)
    shot(page, "0-first-landing")

    for attempt in range(1, MAX_ROUNDS + 1):
        button = page.get_by_role("button", name=re.compile("connect", re.I))
        if not page.url.startswith(f"{BASE}/ui/connect") or not button.count():
            break
        label = button.first.inner_text()
        print(f"\n== the user clicks '{label}'")
        button.first.click()
        settle(page)
        describe(page, context, handle)
        shot(page, f"{attempt}-after-{label.lower().replace(' ', '-')}")

    browser.close()
```

```python
"""Plays an MCP client plus the Connect page's own calls for one MCP server, without a browser.

usage: control.py <server> <flow scope> [--signin "<scope>"] [--reset]
  <flow scope>   the scopes the MCP client asks the gateway for (space separated)
  --signin       do one provider sign-in the way the Connect page does, asking for this scope
  --reset        delete this user's saved grant first
Cookies over 4096 bytes are dropped like a browser does. Prints no tokens or keys.
"""

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import secrets
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

BASE = os.environ.get("PROXY", "http://localhost:4003")
HOST = urllib.parse.urlsplit(BASE).netloc
CLIENT_REDIRECT = "http://127.0.0.1:8898/cb"
LIMIT = 4096
HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
SERVER, FLOW_SCOPE = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
SIGNIN = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--signin") + 1] if "--signin" in sys.argv else None
token = (HERE / "token.txt").read_text().strip()
jar: dict[str, str] = {"token": token}
payload = token.split(".")[1]
KEY = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload + "=" * (-len(payload) % 4)))["key"]
AUTH = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"}


class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, *args, **kwargs):  # noqa: ANN002, ANN003
        return None


opener = urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect)


def request(method: str, url: str, data: bytes | None = None, headers: dict[str, str] | None = None):
    hdrs = dict(headers or {})
    if urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).netloc == HOST:
        hdrs["Cookie"] = "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in jar.items())
    try:
        resp = opener.open(urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method, headers=hdrs), timeout=30)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        resp = error
    for raw in resp.headers.get_all("Set-Cookie") or []:
        name, _, rest = raw.partition("=")
        value = rest.split(";", 1)[0]
        if "Max-Age=0" in raw or value in ('""', ""):
            jar.pop(name, None)
        elif len(name) + len(value) > LIMIT:
            print(f"    cookie {name[:16]}... is {len(name) + len(value)} bytes, dropped (limit {LIMIT})")
        else:
            if name.startswith("mcp_oauth_state"):
                print(f"    sign-in cookie is {len(name) + len(value)} bytes")
            jar[name] = value
    return resp.status, resp.headers.get("Location"), resp.read().decode(errors="replace")


def pkce() -> tuple[str, str]:
    verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)
    return verifier, base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest()).rstrip(b"=").decode()


def flow(handle: str, label: str) -> None:
    _, _, body = request("GET", f"{BASE}/authorize/flow?flow={urllib.parse.quote(handle)}")
    data = json.loads(body)
    print(f"  {label}: connected={data.get('connected')} requested_scopes={data.get('requested_scopes')}")


if "--reset" in sys.argv:
    status, _, _ = request("DELETE", f"{BASE}/v1/mcp/server/{SERVER}/oauth-user-credential", None, AUTH)
    print(f"== reset: deleted the saved grant -> {status}")

_, _, body = request(
    "POST",
    f"{BASE}/register",
    json.dumps(
        {
            "client_name": "control client",
            "redirect_uris": [CLIENT_REDIRECT],
            "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
            "response_types": ["code"],
            "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
        }
    ).encode(),
    {"Content-Type": "application/json"},
)
client_id = json.loads(body)["client_id"]
query = urllib.parse.urlencode(
    {
        "client_id": client_id,
        "redirect_uri": CLIENT_REDIRECT,
        "state": secrets.token_urlsafe(12),
        "code_challenge": pkce()[1],
        "code_challenge_method": "S256",
        "response_type": "code",
        "resource": f"{BASE}/mcp/{SERVER}",
        "scope": FLOW_SCOPE,
    }
)
status, location, _ = request("GET", f"{BASE}/authorize/mcp-session?{query}")
handle = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(urllib.parse.urlsplit(location or "").query)).get("connect_flow", "")
print(f"== client asks the gateway for '{FLOW_SCOPE}' on {SERVER} -> {status}")
flow(handle, "connect page")

if SIGNIN is not None:
    verifier, challenge = pkce()
    ui_callback = f"{BASE}/ui/mcp/oauth/callback"
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode(
        {
            "redirect_uri": ui_callback,
            "state": secrets.token_urlsafe(16),
            "response_type": "code",
            "code_challenge": challenge,
            "code_challenge_method": "S256",
            "scope": SIGNIN,
        }
    )
    print(f"== provider sign-in asking for '{SIGNIN}'")
    status, location, body = request("GET", f"{BASE}/v1/mcp/server/oauth/{SERVER}/authorize?{q}")
    asked = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(urllib.parse.urlsplit(location or "").query)).get("scope", "")
    names = asked if len(asked) < 90 else f"{asked[:60]}..."
    print(f"  gateway sends the browser to the provider ({status}) asking for {len(asked.split())} scope(s): {names}")
    if not location:
        print(f"  no redirect, stopping: {body.strip()[:160]}")
        sys.exit(1)
    status, location, _ = request("GET", location)
    status, location, body = request("GET", location)
    print(f"  /callback -> {status} {'' if location else body.strip()[:80]}")
    if location and "code=" in location:
        code = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(urllib.parse.urlsplit(location).query))["code"]
        form = urllib.parse.urlencode(
            {"grant_type": "authorization_code", "code": code, "code_verifier": verifier, "redirect_uri": ui_callback}
        ).encode()
        status, _, body = request(
            "POST",
            f"{BASE}/v1/mcp/server/oauth/{SERVER}/token",
            form,
            {**AUTH, "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
        )
        tokens = json.loads(body)
        granted = tokens.get("scope", "")
        print(f"  token exchange -> {status}, provider granted {len(granted.split())} scope(s)")
        status, _, _ = request(
            "POST",
            f"{BASE}/v1/mcp/server/{SERVER}/oauth-user-credential",
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "access_token": tokens.get("access_token"),
                    "refresh_token": tokens.get("refresh_token"),
                    "expires_in": tokens.get("expires_in"),
                    "scopes": [s for s in granted.split(" ") if s],
                }
            ).encode(),
            {**AUTH, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        print(f"  page saves the grant -> {status}")
    flow(handle, "connect page after sign-in")

status, location, body = request(
    "POST",
    f"{BASE}/authorize/complete",
    urllib.parse.urlencode({"flow": handle}).encode(),
    {"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
)
outcome = "client gets a sign-in code" if status == 303 and "code=" in (location or "") else body.strip()[:110]
print(f"== finish connecting -> {status} {outcome}")
```

title: fix(proxy): run the boot legacy empty models counts one at a time
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ab2b597479044be69cd0d79f0b6c0dc8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/ab2b597479044be69cd0d79f0b6c0dc8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The boot check from #50720 fires six count queries at once
- Each one takes its own database connection during startup

How it solves it:

- The six counts now run one after another
- Same six counts and the same warning text

## User Flow

Before: an operator restarting the proxy sees a burst of parallel count queries on the database

1. They start the proxy with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at a Postgres that has keys and teams
2. While it boots they run `SELECT ... FROM pg_stat_activity` and see several `SELECT COUNT(*)` queries active at once
3. The proxy logs the deprecated model access defaults warning with its counts

After: the same boot runs one count query at a time

1. They start the proxy with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at a Postgres that has keys and teams
2. While it boots they run `SELECT ... FROM pg_stat_activity` and see at most one `SELECT COUNT(*)` query active
3. The proxy logs the same warning with the same counts

## Relevant issues

Follow-up to #50720

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. A local Postgres database with the proxy schema already applied, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` exported, and this `config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

The counts finish in milliseconds on a small database, so the script holds a lock on the key table to keep them in flight long enough to list them. One worker and no Redis, since the check runs once per worker at boot and does not touch router state

```bash
Q="FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname=current_database() AND wait_event_type='Lock' AND query ILIKE '%COUNT(%LiteLLM_VerificationToken%'"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'BEGIN' -c 'LOCK TABLE "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE' -c 'SELECT pg_sleep(75)' &
sleep 1
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4750 --num_workers 1 > proxy.log 2>&1 &
until [ "$(psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "SELECT count(*) $Q")" -ge 1 ]; do sleep 2; done
sleep 5
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT pid, wait_event_type, left(regexp_replace(query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 70) AS query $Q ORDER BY pid"
```

### Before (616471d400)

1. Run the script above. Four key counts are waiting at the same time. The two team counts run on another table, so the lock does not hold them

```
  pid  | wait_event_type |                                 query
-------+-----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------
 11005 | Lock            | SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT "public"."LiteLLM_VerificationToken"."tok
 11008 | Lock            | SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT "public"."LiteLLM_VerificationToken"."tok
 11011 | Lock            | SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT "public"."LiteLLM_VerificationToken"."tok
 11012 | Lock            | SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT "public"."LiteLLM_VerificationToken"."tok
(4 rows)
```

### After (07d93b3fed)

1. Run the same script. One key count is waiting

```
  pid  | wait_event_type |                                 query
-------+-----------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------
 18670 | Lock            | SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT "public"."LiteLLM_VerificationToken"."tok
(1 row)
```

Open connections, same setup without the lock. Count the proxy's connections with `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname=current_database() AND pid <> pg_backend_pid()` every 0.5s during boot and again 20s after startup, one run per commit

```
616471d400  peak while booting 8, 20s after startup 8 (all idle)
07d93b3fed  peak while booting 4, 20s after startup 4 (all idle)
```

Tests at both commits. The unit test counts how many `count` calls overlap, and the integration test does the lock and `pg_stat_activity` check above against a harness-owned proxy and Postgres

```
$ pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_legacy_empty_models_check.py -q
616471d400  E  assert 6 == 1   (1 failed, 18 passed)
07d93b3fed  19 passed

$ INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2 python tests/integration/run.py management "tests/integration/authorization/test_legacy_empty_models_boot_warning.py::test_boot_runs_the_deprecated_defaults_counts_one_at_a_time"
616471d400  E  assert 2 == 1   (1 failed)
07d93b3fed  1 passed
```

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- The check takes six round trips in a row now, still in a background task
- One combined query was not used, it needs raw SQL over two tables

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Problem this solves:

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `is_default` on a template duplicated the org's stored `default_budget_template_id`
- a sole template still had to be flagged by hand
- no way to move the default to another template after create

How it solves it:

- `POST /customer_organizations` takes `default_budget_template`, the name of one inline template
- a single inline template is the default on its own, several with no name means no default
- `PATCH /customer_organizations/{id}` takes `default_budget_template_id` to move or clear the default
- `is_default` is gone from `BudgetTemplate`, `TemplatePatch` and the Organization response
- dashboard create form sends the name, `schema.d.ts` regenerated with `npm run gen:api`

Intentional product change: the org create and template routes no longer accept `is_default`. A body that still sends it gets a 422, since the models forbid extra fields.

## User Flow

Before: an admin creating an org with two templates has to flag one of them and cannot change the choice later

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations with `default_budgets: [{"name": "standard", "is_default": true}, {"name": "power"}]`
2. The 201 response lists both templates with `is_default` plus `default_budget_template_id`, which say the same thing twice
3. They send PATCH https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations/acme with `{"default_budget_template_id": "<power id>"}` and get a 422, the field is unknown

After: the admin names the default once and can move it later

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations with `default_budgets: [{"name": "standard"}, {"name": "power"}], "default_budget_template": "standard"`
2. The 201 response shows `default_budget_template_id` pointing at the generated id of `standard`, templates carry no `is_default`
3. They send PATCH https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations/acme with `{"default_budget_template_id": "<power id>"}` and get 200 with the pointer moved, so new members with no `budget_id` land on `power`
4. Naming a template that is not in `default_budgets`, or an id from another org on PATCH, gets a 422

title: fix(terraform): preserve live metadata and controls on team/project updates
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:
- Unrelated Terraform edits overwrite live budgets and metadata.
- Null limits and nested member windows refresh incorrectly.

How it solves it:
- Send changed attributes only; retain existing create behavior.
- Merge metadata deltas into fresh, lossless server JSON.
- Clear null budget state and decode nested member budgets.

## User Flow

Before: an owned metadata edit overwrites unrelated live settings.
1. Plan a team metadata change from `owner=old` to `owner=new`.
2. Before applying, an administrator changes the budget, RPM limit, and adds nested metadata.
3. Apply the plan: live budget/RPM values revert and nested metadata disappears.

After: the same edit preserves settings outside the planned change.
1. Plan a team metadata change from `owner=old` to `owner=new`.
2. Before applying, an administrator changes the budget, RPM limit, and adds nested metadata.
3. Apply the plan: only `owner` changes; current budgets and foreign metadata survive.

The same partial-update and metadata-delta behavior is implemented for projects. Explicit zero, false, empty-list/map changes keep their clearing semantics; empty team permissions use the dedicated endpoint.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Added behavior regressions using real SDK prior-state/diff transitions and stateful HTTP handlers.
- [x] `go test -timeout 120s ./...` passes, including provider and endpoint-audit packages.
- [x] `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, and affected-file `gofmt` pass.
- [x] Scope limited to team/project update and refresh correctness; docs/changelog updated.
- [ ] Required upstream CI and automated review have completed.
- [x] GitHub `license/cla` check passes; no agreement was signed by automation.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Control-plane smoke used the actual Go resource Create/Read/Update callbacks against **LiteLLM v1.109.0 and PostgreSQL 16** in fresh, isolated local Docker containers. No shared gateway writes, cloud calls, inference requests, licensing bypass, or proxy source modifications. The model entry is only a local fixture; the management APIs and database are real.

Shared setup: create an isolated Docker network, run PostgreSQL 16 with `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER`, and `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, then start the cached official image with `DATABASE_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`. Those credentials were generated for this localhost-only smoke; no real credentials are included here.

```sh
docker network create "$SMOKE_NETWORK"
docker run --rm --name "$SMOKE_DB" --network "$SMOKE_NETWORK"   -e POSTGRES_DB -e POSTGRES_USER -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD postgres:16-alpine
docker run --rm --name "$SMOKE_PROXY" --network "$SMOKE_NETWORK"   -p 127.0.0.1:49173:4000 -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro"   -e DATABASE_URL -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY   ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.109.0 --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000
```

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: smoke-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: synthetic-local-only
      mock_response: local-smoke

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

<details>
<summary>Exact standalone Go driver; save as /tmp/team-update-smoke.go</summary>

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "strings"

    provider "github.com/BerriAI/terraform-provider-litellm/litellm"
    "github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk/v2/helper/schema"
    "github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk/v2/terraform"
    "github.com/google/uuid"
)

func call(base, key, method, path string, body map[string]interface{}) map[string]interface{} {
    var input string
    if body != nil { encoded, err := json.Marshal(body); if err != nil { panic(err) }; input=string(encoded) }
    request, err := http.NewRequest(method, base+path, strings.NewReader(input)); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    request.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
    request.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    response, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(request); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer response.Body.Close()
    var result map[string]interface{}
    decoder := json.NewDecoder(response.Body); decoder.UseNumber()
    if err := decoder.Decode(&result); err != nil { panic(err) }
    if response.StatusCode >= 300 { panic(fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: %d %v", method,path,response.StatusCode,result)) }
    return result
}
func main() {
    base, key := os.Args[1], os.Args[2]
    teamID := uuid.New().String()
    resource := provider.ResourceLiteLLMTeam()
    fields := map[string]interface{}{
        "team_id":teamID,"team_alias":"provider-safety-smoke", "models":[]interface{}{"smoke-model"},
        "max_budget":500.0,"rpm_limit":100,"tpm_limit":5000,"budget_duration":"1d",
        "metadata":map[string]interface{}{"owner":"old","eur_budget":"0","encoded":"[]"},
    }
    data := schema.InternalMap(resource.Schema)
    config := terraform.NewResourceConfigRaw(fields)
    initialDiff, err := resource.Diff(context.Background(), nil, config, nil); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    initial, err := data.Data(nil, initialDiff); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    client := provider.NewClient(base,key,false)
    if err := resource.Create(initial,client); err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer call(base,key,"POST","/team/delete",map[string]interface{}{"team_ids":[]string{teamID}})
    prior := initial.State()
    fields["metadata"] = map[string]interface{}{"owner":"new","eur_budget":"0","encoded":"[]"}
    diff, err := resource.Diff(context.Background(),prior,terraform.NewResourceConfigRaw(fields),nil); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    update, err := data.Data(prior,diff); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    liveMetadata := map[string]interface{}{
        "owner":"old","eur_budget":"0","encoded":"[]",
        "foreign_map":map[string]interface{}{"nested":true},"foreign_array":[]string{"live"},
        "foreign_flag":true,"large_id":json.Number("9007199254740993"),
    }
    call(base,key,"POST","/team/update",map[string]interface{}{"team_id":teamID,"max_budget":700.0,"rpm_limit":200,"metadata":liveMetadata})
    before := call(base,key,"GET","/team/info?team_id="+teamID,nil)["team_info"].(map[string]interface{})
    if err := resource.Update(update,client); err != nil { panic(err) }
    after := call(base,key,"GET","/team/info?team_id="+teamID,nil)["team_info"].(map[string]interface{})
    beforeJSON, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{"max_budget":before["max_budget"],"rpm_limit":before["rpm_limit"],"budget_reset_at":before["budget_reset_at"],"metadata":before["metadata"]})
    afterJSON, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{"max_budget":after["max_budget"],"rpm_limit":after["rpm_limit"],"budget_reset_at":after["budget_reset_at"],"metadata":after["metadata"]})
    fmt.Printf("BEFORE %s\nAFTER %s\n",beforeJSON,afterJSON)
    metadata := after["metadata"].(map[string]interface{})
    preserved := metadata["foreign_flag"]==true && metadata["foreign_map"]!=nil && metadata["foreign_array"]!=nil && metadata["large_id"]==json.Number("9007199254740993") && after["max_budget"]==json.Number("700.0")
    // JSON encoders may spell integral numeric values without a decimal point.
    budget, _ := after["max_budget"].(json.Number)
    preserved = metadata["foreign_flag"]==true && metadata["foreign_map"]!=nil && metadata["foreign_array"]!=nil && metadata["large_id"]==json.Number("9007199254740993") && (budget.String()=="700" || budget.String()=="700.0")
    fmt.Printf("PRESERVED=%t OWNER_UPDATED=%t\n",preserved,metadata["owner"]=="new")
}
```
</details>

### Before (`6a1f81b9f8bd365718e781c50141fd3164721dbb`, upstream base)

1. From the base checkout's `litellm/deploy/terraform/provider`, run:
   `go run /tmp/team-update-smoke.go http://127.0.0.1:49173 "$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"`.
2. Observed budget **700 → 500**, RPM **200 → 100**; foreign map, array, boolean, and exact numeric ID disappear. The intended owner edit succeeds:

```text
PRESERVED=false OWNER_UPDATED=true
```

### After (`9166ec4`, tested tip)

1. Run the identical command from this branch's provider directory.
2. Budget remains **700**, RPM remains **200**, reset time remains `2026-11-14T00:00:00Z`, and all foreign JSON survives, including `9007199254740993`; `owner` changes to `new`:

```text
PRESERVED=true OWNER_UPDATED=true
```

All six original failure groups were observed failing against unmodified resource code before implementation. The combined provider suite now passes: unrelated team/project updates preserve controls and budget rows, apply-time metadata changes survive, owned-key removals are narrow, null linked budgets clear stale state, nested member duration refreshes, and declared strings including encoded arrays/EUR `"0"` retain their types.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Medium
- Metadata GET/POST is not atomic; no API CAS exists here.
- Real project-write smoke needs a legitimate enterprise license.
  - Local `/project/new` returned **403**: `Project management is an enterprise feature`; `LITELLM_LICENSE` was absent. Project behavior is covered by the actual resource implementation with stateful HTTP regressions, not claimed as licensed end-to-end verification.
- Existing callers need an official provider release to receive this fix.


## Review remediation — `0149f2d`

The metadata-log exposure review is fixed for both team and project updates. Only identifiers are logged; live metadata is neither printed nor copied for redaction. The new credential-exposure regression failed on both resources before the change and passes after. Full `go test -timeout 120s ./...`, vet and build pass at this tip.

The original control-plane proof at `9166ec4` carries forward: this follow-up changes only logging plus its behavior regression/changelog; update payloads and refresh behavior are unchanged, and the complete suite passes.

### Logging privacy: Before (`9166ec4`) / After (`0149f2d`)

The same isolated LiteLLM v1.109.0/PostgreSQL 16 management APIs were used, with generated local-only credentials. This run copied the config into the container with `docker cp` rather than using a host bind mount. No shared gateway writes or inference occurred.

1. With the shared proxy configuration above, save the driver below as `/tmp/logging-smoke.go`. From each checkout's `litellm/deploy/terraform/provider`, run `go run /tmp/logging-smoke.go http://127.0.0.1:49173 "$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"`.
2. Before: `FOREIGN_VALUE_PRESERVED=true LOG_SECRET_ABSENT=false` (failure).
3. After: `FOREIGN_VALUE_PRESERVED=true LOG_SECRET_ABSENT=true` (pass).

The real proxy redacts recognized callback credentials in `/team/info`, so runtime log proof uses an unredacted foreign nested sentinel. The actual team/project resource regressions separately exercise unredacted callback metadata with HTTP fixtures; licensed project E2E remains unclaimed.

<details><summary>Exact logging smoke driver</summary>

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "bytes"
    "log"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "strings"

    provider "github.com/BerriAI/terraform-provider-litellm/litellm"
    "github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk/v2/helper/schema"
    "github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-sdk/v2/terraform"
    "github.com/google/uuid"
)

func call(base, key, method, path string, body map[string]interface{}) map[string]interface{} {
    var input string
    if body != nil { encoded, err := json.Marshal(body); if err != nil { panic(err) }; input=string(encoded) }
    request, err := http.NewRequest(method, base+path, strings.NewReader(input)); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    request.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
    request.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    response, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(request); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer response.Body.Close()
    var result map[string]interface{}
    decoder := json.NewDecoder(response.Body); decoder.UseNumber()
    if err := decoder.Decode(&result); err != nil { panic(err) }
    if response.StatusCode >= 300 { panic(fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: %d %v", method,path,response.StatusCode,result)) }
    return result
}
func main() {
    var capturedLogs bytes.Buffer
    log.SetOutput(&capturedLogs)
    base, key := os.Args[1], os.Args[2]
    teamID := uuid.New().String()
    resource := provider.ResourceLiteLLMTeam()
    fields := map[string]interface{}{
        "team_id":teamID,"team_alias":"provider-safety-smoke", "models":[]interface{}{"smoke-model"},
        "max_budget":500.0,"rpm_limit":100,"tpm_limit":5000,"budget_duration":"1d",
        "metadata":map[string]interface{}{"owner":"old","eur_budget":"0","encoded":"[]"},
    }
    data := schema.InternalMap(resource.Schema)
    config := terraform.NewResourceConfigRaw(fields)
    initialDiff, err := resource.Diff(context.Background(), nil, config, nil); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    initial, err := data.Data(nil, initialDiff); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    client := provider.NewClient(base,key,false)
    if err := resource.Create(initial,client); err != nil { panic(err) }
    defer call(base,key,"POST","/team/delete",map[string]interface{}{"team_ids":[]string{teamID}})
    prior := initial.State()
    fields["metadata"] = map[string]interface{}{"owner":"new","eur_budget":"0","encoded":"[]"}
    diff, err := resource.Diff(context.Background(),prior,terraform.NewResourceConfigRaw(fields),nil); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    update, err := data.Data(prior,diff); if err != nil { panic(err) }
    liveMetadata := map[string]interface{}{
        "operator_context": map[string]interface{}{"opaque_value":"synthetic-nested-callback-credential"},
        "owner":"old","eur_budget":"0","encoded":"[]",
        "foreign_map":map[string]interface{}{"nested":true},"foreign_array":[]string{"live"},
        "foreign_flag":true,"large_id":json.Number("9007199254740993"),
    }
    call(base,key,"POST","/team/update",map[string]interface{}{"team_id":teamID,"max_budget":700.0,"rpm_limit":200,"metadata":liveMetadata})
    before := call(base,key,"GET","/team/info?team_id="+teamID,nil)["team_info"].(map[string]interface{})
    if err := resource.Update(update,client); err != nil { panic(err) }
    after := call(base,key,"GET","/team/info?team_id="+teamID,nil)["team_info"].(map[string]interface{})

    _ = before
    metadata := after["metadata"].(map[string]interface{})
    credential := metadata["operator_context"].(map[string]interface{})["opaque_value"]
    preserved := credential == "synthetic-nested-callback-credential"
    excluded := !strings.Contains(capturedLogs.String(), "synthetic-nested-callback-credential")
    fmt.Printf("FOREIGN_VALUE_PRESERVED=%t LOG_SECRET_ABSENT=%t\n",preserved,excluded)
    if !preserved || !excluded { panic("callback preservation or log privacy failed") }
}
```
</details>

</details>

## TLDR

Polish commit `752857778d` is pushed on `litellm_playground_customer_context`.

Problem this solves:

- Testing customer context requires entering headers by hand
- Customer budgets are missing from the Playground
- Messages lacks Anthropic Python and curl examples

How it solves it:

- Load customer selectors through existing management APIs
- Keep customer context in the existing custom headers
- Refetch settled budgets and preserve budget error details
- Link customer details to the Playground
- Generate endpoint-specific snippets without embedding the active key

Intentional product change: the Playground adds a Customer control and a customer budget strip. Customer org and customer member detail pages gain Test in Playground. Existing custom headers remain editable and customer context is clearable

The polish pass gives Python examples normal keyword arguments and four-space indentation. Curl keeps one header per continued line, and long prompts retain horizontal scrolling without changing copied code. Inspector uses controlled tab state. Budget labels are muted, identities and values are emphasized, spend and remaining values align in columns, and each limited scope gets a usage bar. The 422 row has a divider. The customer chip has an ellipsis and a full-value tooltip.

The configured live gateway base resolves to `http://localhost:3000`, whose dashboard development rewrites forward API requests to the proxy on 4000. All six regenerated examples ran successfully against that base. OpenAI examples append `/v1`, while Anthropic supplies `/v1/messages` through its SDK.

## User Flow

Before, testing a customer request requires manually entering its customer headers

1. Open `/playground` and enter the customer org alias and customer member ID under Settings, Advanced, Custom headers
2. Choose Chat Completions, Responses, or Messages, select a compatible model, and send a prompt
3. The request succeeds, but no customer budget strip appears

After, the same request can be tested with visible customer selectors and budgets

1. Open `/playground` and choose a customer org and optional customer member under Customer
2. Choose Chat Completions, Responses, or Messages, select a compatible model, and send a prompt
3. The request succeeds and the strip shows settled customer spend and remaining budgets
4. Open Inspector, Code to copy Python or curl with customer headers and an environment-variable key

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Soniox v6, four DeepInfra models and Perplexity Gemini 4 Hydrogen have no cost row
- Several rows carry capabilities or prices their provider docs contradict
- Retired Soniox, Bedrock Claude and Azure Whisper rows lack correct dates

How it solves it:

- Adds the missing rows at the published rates, with a `source` on each
- Fixes flags, limits and prices against each provider's official page
- Adds `deprecation_date` and `deprecation_source` from official lifecycle pages

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin running a newly released model sees no spend, or the wrong capability check

1. They add `deepinfra/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` or `soniox/stt-async-v6` as a model and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions (or /v1/audio/transcriptions)
2. The request is logged at $0 because the model has no cost map row
3. A call to `vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash-cyber` with `tools` is refused as unsupported, though Google documents function calling

After: the same admin sees real spend and the documented capabilities

1. They add the same model and send the same request
2. The request is logged at the provider's published rate
3. The same `tools` call to `vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash-cyber` goes through

title: fix(proxy): resolve customer members by email
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/29f847874b2a4dffa38b47fff1e219f5
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/29f847874b2a4dffa38b47fff1e219f5?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Email callers cannot reuse their existing customer member
- Email-shaped IDs silently create a second customer member

How it solves it:

- Store normalized customer member email with customer org uniqueness
- Resolve a new email header through existing customer hierarchy

Intentional product change: clients can send the customer org alias and `x-litellm-customer-member-email`. Email without an alias returns 400. Conflicting customer member ID and email return 403. Existing customer member ID header behavior remains unchanged

## User Flow

Before, the developer cannot identify an existing customer member by email

1. They POST email to `http://127.0.0.1:4016/management/v1/customer_members` and receive 422
2. They retry without email and receive a customer member ID
3. Alias and email requests to Responses, Chat Completions and Messages return 200, but do not charge that customer member
4. Putting email in the customer member ID header creates a second customer member

After, the developer stores an email and reuses the same customer member

1. They POST email to `http://127.0.0.1:4016/management/v1/customer_members` and receive 201 with normalized email
2. Alias and email requests to Responses, Chat Completions and Messages return 200
3. The existing customer member receives the combined paid cost, without a second customer member

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is isolated to customer member email
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

No PR was opened, so CI and bot review are pending

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Shared setup and commands

Both phases used the same PostgreSQL database, shared Redis on port 6383, and two Uvicorn workers on port 4016. The existing proxies on 4000 and 4001 were left untouched. Both temporary QA instances were stopped after their checks

The client verified two worker PIDs with established serving connections after 24 concurrent authenticated management requests. Before served through {"275114":13,"275115":12}. After served through {"275682":12,"275683":13}. Worker affinity for individual inference requests was not isolated

The baseline source was unchanged main at `6abacd329b70dc668f69c705eb7118fbd639cd96`, except for the copied regression test. The nullable email column and composite index were applied to the local QA database before both phases. Main rejects email on customer member create with 422, so the baseline retries without email and seeds only that newly created QA customer member's email with SQL. This supplies an existing email-bearing customer member without changing main's request handling. Main still ignores the new header. No migration rewrites customer data

Environment names were `DATABASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `PYTHONPATH`, and `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true`. The client recovered the existing QA environment from dashboard process 147419 and read the master key from `/home/ubuntu/.qa-master-key`. No key values are included here. On another host, supply those variables and replace the local process-environment recovery with `ENV = dict(os.environ)`

The project virtualenv and native extension were shared with the baseline worktree. The exact commands were

```bash
git worktree add --detach /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr6-before origin/main
ln -s /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr6-before/.venv
ln -s /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/litellm/rust_bridge/_native.abi3.so /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr6-before/litellm/rust_bridge/_native.abi3.so
/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/pr6-live.py before > /home/ubuntu/pr6-before-live.log 2>&1
/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/pr6-live.py after > /home/ubuntu/pr6-after-live.log 2>&1
```

The client starts each proxy with this command and its source-specific working directory and PYTHONPATH

```bash
<worktree>/.venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli \
  --config /home/ubuntu/pr3-config.yaml --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4016
```

Reload was omitted to preserve two actual serving workers. Database schema updates were disabled during startup because the schema-only migration had already been applied to the QA database. An initial run without the V2 resolver printed a missing-root-schema diff warning. It was discarded and both recorded phases were rerun with the V2 resolver

<details>
<summary>Exact shared proxy config</summary>

```yaml
environment_variables:
  WEBHOOK_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8808
model_list:
  - model_name: qa-gpt
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: qa-claude
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  alerting: [webhook]
  alert_types: [budget_alerts]
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6383
router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6383
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact live client, setup, schema application, assertions and cleanup</summary>

Save this as `/home/ubuntu/pr6-live.py` and invoke it with `before` and `after` as shown above. The two source paths at the top select the baseline and feature checkout. It creates fresh customer orgs, customer teams, customer members and virtual keys on every run

```python
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from urllib.parse import urlparse
import uuid

import httpx
import psutil

PHASE = sys.argv[1]
ROOT = Path('/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr6-before' if PHASE == 'before' else '/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm')
entries = Path('/proc/147419/environ').read_bytes().split(b'\0')
ENV = {**os.environ, **{e.split(b'=', 1)[0].decode(): e.split(b'=', 1)[1].decode() for e in entries if b'=' in e}}
ENV['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY'] = Path('/home/ubuntu/.qa-master-key').read_text().strip()
ENV['PYTHONPATH'] = str(ROOT) + ':' + str(ROOT / 'enterprise')
ENV['DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE'] = 'true'
BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:4016'
ADMIN = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + ENV['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}
CLIENT = httpx.Client(timeout=180)
DB = urlparse(ENV['DATABASE_URL'])
LOG = Path('/home/ubuntu/pr6-' + PHASE + '-proxy.log')
name = 'pr6-' + PHASE + '-' + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
email = name + '@example.test'
member_id = name + '-customer-member'
clients = []

def sql(query, decode=True):
    response = subprocess.run(['psql', '-X', '-At', '-h', DB.hostname, '-p', str(DB.port or 5432),
                               '-U', DB.username, '-d', DB.path.lstrip('/'), '-c', query],
                              env={**ENV, 'PGPASSWORD': DB.password}, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
    return json.loads(response.stdout) if decode and response.stdout.strip() else None

def manage(method, path, body=None, expected=200):
    response = CLIENT.request(method, BASE + path, headers=ADMIN, json=body)
    assert response.status_code == expected, response.text
    return response.json() if response.content else None

def infer(endpoint, headers):
    body = {'model': 'qa-claude' if endpoint == 'messages' else 'qa-gpt'}
    if endpoint == 'responses':
        body.update(input='Reply only OK', max_output_tokens=64)
    else:
        body.update(messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply only OK'}],
                    **({'max_tokens': 64} if endpoint == 'messages' else {'max_completion_tokens': 64}))
    response = CLIENT.post(BASE + '/v1/' + endpoint, json=body, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, **headers})
    record = {'endpoint': '/v1/' + endpoint, 'status': response.status_code}
    if response.status_code == 200:
        record['response_cost'] = float(response.headers['x-litellm-response-cost'])
        assert record['response_cost'] > 0, record
    else:
        record['error'] = response.json()
    print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
    return record

def members():
    return sql('SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(s),\'[]\') FROM (SELECT m.customer_member_id, m.email, m.spend, m.parent_team_id '
               'FROM "LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable" m JOIN "LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable" t '
               'ON m.parent_team_id=t.customer_team_id WHERE t.parent_org_id=\'' + name + '\' ORDER BY m.customer_member_id) s')

def settled(expected, expected_original):
    for attempt in range(180):
        rows = members()
        spend = sql('SELECT spend FROM "LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable" WHERE customer_org_id=\'' + name + '\'')
        original = next(r for r in rows if r['customer_member_id'] == member_id)
        if abs(spend - expected) < 1e-9 and abs(original['spend'] - expected_original) < 1e-9:
            return {'customer_org_spend': spend, 'customer_members': rows}
        time.sleep(1)
    raise AssertionError({'expected': expected, 'expected_original': expected_original, 'rows': rows, 'actual': spend})

if PHASE == 'before':
    migration = Path('/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/litellm/proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/migrations/20261113120000_customer_member_email/migration.sql').read_text()
    sql('BEGIN;\n' + migration + '\nCOMMIT;', decode=False)

with LOG.open('w') as log:
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(ROOT / '.venv/bin/python'), '-m', 'litellm.proxy.proxy_cli',
                                '--config', '/home/ubuntu/pr3-config.yaml', '--num_workers', '2',
                                '--detailed_debug', '--use_v2_migration_resolver', '--port', '4016'], cwd=ROOT, env=ENV,
                               stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, start_new_session=True)
try:
    for attempt in range(180):
        try:
            if CLIENT.get(BASE + '/health/readiness', headers=ADMIN).status_code == 200 and LOG.read_text().count('Application startup complete') >= 2:
                break
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            pass
        time.sleep(1)
    else:
        raise RuntimeError('Both proxy workers did not become ready')
    clients = [httpx.Client(timeout=60) for _ in range(24)]
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=24) as pool:
        statuses = list(pool.map(lambda c: c.get(BASE + '/management/v1/customer_organizations', headers=ADMIN).status_code, clients))
    assert set(statuses) == {200}, statuses
    serving = {}
    for child in psutil.Process(process.pid).children(recursive=True):
        count = sum(c.laddr.port == 4016 and c.status == 'ESTABLISHED' for c in child.net_connections(kind='tcp'))
        if count:
            serving[str(child.pid)] = count
    assert len(serving) == 2, serving
    manage('POST', '/management/v1/customer_organizations', {'customer_org_id': name, 'alias': name,
           'budget': {'max_budget': 10}, 'default_budgets': [{'name': 'default', 'is_default': True, 'max_budget': 10}]}, 201)
    manage('POST', '/management/v1/customer_teams', {'customer_team_id': name + '-customer-team', 'parent_org_id': name}, 201)
    member_body = {'customer_member_id': member_id, 'parent_team_id': name + '-customer-team', 'email': ' ' + email.upper() + ' '}
    creation = manage('POST', '/management/v1/customer_members', member_body, 422 if PHASE == 'before' else 201)
    if PHASE == 'before':
        member_body.pop('email')
        manage('POST', '/management/v1/customer_members', member_body, 201)
        sql('UPDATE "LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable" SET email=\'' + email + '\' WHERE customer_member_id=\'' + member_id + '\'', decode=False)
    else:
        assert creation['email'] == email, creation
    key = manage('POST', '/key/generate', {'models': ['qa-gpt', 'qa-claude'], 'metadata': {'customer_org_id': name}})['key']
    headers = {'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': name, 'x-litellm-customer-member-email': email.upper()}
    calls = [infer(endpoint, headers) for endpoint in ('responses', 'chat/completions', 'messages')]
    assert [call['status'] for call in calls] == [200, 200, 200], calls
    cost = sum(call['response_cost'] for call in calls)
    attributed = settled(cost, 0 if PHASE == 'before' else cost)
    print(json.dumps({'phase': PHASE, 'existing_customer_member_attribution': attributed}), flush=True)
    if PHASE == 'before':
        legacy = infer('responses', {'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': name, 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': email})
        assert legacy['status'] == 200
        legacy_attributed = settled(cost + legacy['response_cost'], 0)
        assert len(legacy_attributed['customer_members']) == 2, legacy_attributed
        extra = {'legacy_email_in_member_id': legacy_attributed}
    else:
        unknown_headers = {**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-member-email': 'new-' + email}
        unknown = infer('responses', unknown_headers)
        assert unknown['status'] == 200
        repeated = infer('responses', unknown_headers)
        assert repeated['status'] == 200
        total = cost + unknown['response_cost'] + repeated['response_cost']
        unknown_attributed = settled(total, cost)
        assert len(unknown_attributed['customer_members']) == 2, unknown_attributed
        new_member = next(row for row in unknown_attributed['customer_members'] if row['customer_member_id'] != member_id)
        assert new_member['email'] == 'new-' + email
        assert new_member['parent_team_id'] == name + ':default'
        assert abs(new_member['spend'] - unknown['response_cost'] - repeated['response_cost']) < 1e-9
        missing = infer('responses', {'x-litellm-customer-member-email': email})
        mismatch = infer('responses', {**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': member_id, 'x-litellm-customer-member-email': 'new-' + email})
        assert missing['status'] == 400
        assert mismatch['status'] == 403
        duplicate = manage('POST', '/management/v1/customer_members', {'parent_team_id': name + ':default', 'email': email}, 409)
        manage('PATCH', '/management/v1/customer_members/' + member_id, {'email': 'changed-' + email})
        changed = infer('responses', {**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-member-email': 'changed-' + email, 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': member_id})
        assert changed['status'] == 200
        assert infer('responses', {**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': member_id})['status'] == 403
        final = settled(total + changed['response_cost'], cost + changed['response_cost'])
        def race(index):
            return httpx.post(BASE + '/management/v1/customer_members', headers=ADMIN, timeout=60, json={
                'customer_member_id': name + '-racing-customer-member-' + str(index),
                'parent_team_id': name + '-customer-team', 'email': 'race-' + email}).status_code
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool:
            race_statuses = list(pool.map(race, range(6)))
        assert sorted(race_statuses) == [201, 409, 409, 409, 409, 409], race_statuses
        manage('PATCH', '/management/v1/customer_members/' + member_id, {'budget_override': {'max_budget': 0}})
        over_budget = infer('responses', {**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-member-email': 'changed-' + email})
        assert over_budget['status'] == 422
        extra = {'unknown_email': unknown_attributed, 'email_without_alias': missing, 'id_email_mismatch': mismatch,
                 'duplicate_email': duplicate, 'email_update': changed, 'final_attribution': final, 'budget_denied': over_budget,
                 'concurrent_email_creates': race_statuses}
    evidence = {'phase': PHASE, 'serving_workers': serving, 'email_create_status': 422 if PHASE == 'before' else 201,
                'existing_customer_member_id': member_id, 'email': email, 'calls': calls,
                'existing_customer_member_attribution': attributed, **extra}
    Path('/home/ubuntu/pr6-' + PHASE + '.json').write_text(json.dumps(evidence, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({'phase': PHASE, 'result': 'PASS', 'serving_workers': serving}), flush=True)
finally:
    for client in clients:
        client.close()
    CLIENT.close()
    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
```

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Severe

- Email writes require upgraded workers for application-level duplicate enforcement
- The lookup index is created synchronously at proxy boot

### Medium

- Existing email-shaped customer member IDs need explicit email assignment
- Email backfill and automatic customer member merging are not included
- Optional UI display is skipped, generated API types are updated

### Low

- Streaming, alert delivery and database outages were not live-tested
- Worker affinity and concurrent email updates were not isolated
- CI and bot reviews await PR creation

Email-shaped values in `x-litellm-customer-member-id` remain literal IDs. Clients must adopt `x-litellm-customer-member-email` and populate existing customer members' email using the management API. There is no backfill or automatic merge of older email-shaped IDs

Both headers require the selected customer's stored email to match, including a 403 when its stored email is null. Unknown ID plus unused email creates that ID and email together. An email already belonging to another customer member does not override the supplied ID

Uniqueness is scoped to the customer org and serialized with its existing PostgreSQL row lock. Older workers or direct SQL can bypass application-level normalization and duplicate checks, so roll out email-writing workers together. The nonunique composite index supports lookup within customer teams. Index creation at boot was not load-tested

Email lookup maps to the existing customer member hierarchy, scope checks and spend accounting. No spend-log schema, queueing, budget algorithm or alert transport was changed. Customer alert delivery, streaming, database outages, worker-affinity cache invalidation and concurrent email updates were not separately live-tested

Only generated dashboard API types changed. The optional email display was skipped because the customer hierarchy list uses shared customer team/customer member rows and its detail is a separate settings form, with no existing email slot. There is no UI change or visual claim

## CI and authorization review follow-up

The review found that a denied key could claim an unused email in another customer org before returning 403. The customer org binding is now checked before any customer member lookup or registration. The migration also begins with the required transaction-local lock timeout

Before the fix, a key bound to another customer org sends an unused email and its chosen customer member ID to POST `/v1/responses`. It receives 403, but the email remains registered to that ID. The legitimate caller then sends their own customer member ID and the same email and receives 403

After the fix, the same denied request returns 403 without creating a customer member. The legitimate caller receives 200 and owns the sole customer member registered to that email

The before run used `3ee995505b`. The after run used `974f19325c`. Both ran with two serving workers and shared Redis using the proxy configuration above. The live client and outputs are saved outside the repo at `/home/ubuntu/pr6-review-live.py`, `/home/ubuntu/pr6-review-before.json` and `/home/ubuntu/pr6-review-after.json`

```text
Before    denied 403    customer members after denial 1    legitimate caller 403
After     denied 403    customer members after denial 0    legitimate caller 200
```

```bash
  -d '{"model":"qa-gpt","input":"Reply only OK","max_output_tokens":64}'
curl -sS -o legitimate.json -w '%{http_code}\n' "$BASE/v1/responses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OWNER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $CUSTOMER_ORG_ALIAS" \
  -H "x-litellm-customer-member-email: $UNUSED_EMAIL" \
  -H 'x-litellm-customer-member-id: legitimate-member-id' \
  -d '{"model":"qa-gpt","input":"Reply only OK","max_output_tokens":64}'
```

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- together_ai/elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 has no function calling or structured output flags
- Together documents both for this model

How it solves it:

- Adds supports_function_calling and supports_response_schema, both true, to that row

## Rows

together_ai/elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 (kind page, existing row, two fields added, nothing else on the row changes)

supports_function_calling true and supports_response_schema true come from two Together pages, both fetched raw on 2026-11-13.

The November 10, 2026 entry on https://docs.together.ai/docs/changelog says "elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0: 262,144 context length, FP8 quantization, function calling, and structured outputs. Pricing: $0.60 input / $3.00 output / $0.06 cached input (per 1M tokens)".

The Chat models table on https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/models has the row "Elorian Labs | Glimpse 1.0 | elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 | 262144 | $0.60 | $0.06 | $3.00 | FP8 | Yes | Yes", where the last two columns are Function calling and Structured outputs.

Prices and context length on the row already match those two sources and GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models, so they are left alone.

## Changed pages checked

https://docs.together.ai/docs/changelog: the newest entry is November 12 (thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small), which the catalog already matches. The November 10 entry is the source for this change. The November 5 entry (moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) matches the catalog. LiquidAI/LFM2.5-8B-A1B stays out, it is absent from /v1/models and the serverless models page and an open question with the maintainer covers it.

https://api.together.ai/v1/models: all 80 priced ids compared against the catalog, 0 price mismatches.

## Delisted by the provider

together-ai-21.1b-41b, together-ai-4.1b-8b, together-ai-41.1b-80b, together-ai-8.1b-21b, together-ai-81.1b-110b, together-ai-embedding-151m-to-350m, together-ai-embedding-up-to-150m and together-ai-up-to-4b are generic size tier keys that /v1/models never lists by design, so they are a coverage gap and not delistings. No key is deleted.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

title: feat(proxy): add per-model project batch enqueued token limits
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description We run each application as its own project under a shared team, and right now there is no way to cap how many batch tokens one application can have queued for a given model. This lets an admin set that cap per model on the project, so one app can’t fill up the queue for everyone else on the team. Tokens are given back when the batch finishes or is cancelled, same as the existing key and team caps.
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Batch enqueued token limits read only key and team metadata, so a project cannot get its own per-model cap - Rotating custom-auth tokens get a fresh key scope each time How it solves it: - New admin-only per-model `model_batch_enqueued_token_limit` in project metadata. An invalid map answers 400 - A batch charges its routed model and every capped model its rows name, refunded when it ends - A project cap lifts per-minute checks only when it caps every model in the batch. Daily caps always apply - `-latest` and dated snapshot names count toward their base model's cap - `/project/update` with only top-level fields keeps the stored metadata - The Admin UI edits the cap per model, read-only for team admins - Docs in BerriAI/litellm-docs#3021 ## User Flow Before: one app's queued gpt-5.5 batch tokens cannot be capped apart from its team 1. The admin sets `model_batch_enqueued_token_limit` to `{"gpt-5.5": 1000000}` with POST https://litellm-domain/project/update 2. The app sends a 1.5M-token gpt-5.5 batch to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches 3. It gets 200, since the project limit is never read After: the limit holds for that app alone 1. The admin sends the same project update 2. The app sends the same batch 3. It gets 429 naming project_model `:gpt-5.5` with any rotating token 4. Other models still pass, and ended batches free their tokens 5. A team admin gets 403 on raising or removing the limit 6. In https://litellm-domain/ui/projects a proxy admin edits the limit, and a team admin sees it read-only ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10766 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Each leg runs two 2-worker proxies sharing Postgres and Redis (`$P`, `$Q`) against the real OpenAI Batch API, with custom auth mapping two rotating tokens to one project Last updated: 94a2f8355f. QA ran on 94a2f8355f, except UI cases 7 and 10, which ran on 153c797863
Why the UI proof carries to the tip Changes since 153c797863 are a34816b2f0, which rewrites one TypeScript expression so strict type checking can narrow it, with the same runtime result, and 94a2f8355f, which changes only the two batch hooks and their tests. UI cases 7 and 10 save projects and keys, and no batch hook runs on those routes. Verification: `git diff --stat 153c797863 94a2f8355f` lists only those files, `npm run typecheck` passes, and the 182 project UI tests pass
Proxy start command, env vars, config.yaml, custom auth module, request files, and case scripts Env vars: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (as `MASTER`), `LITELLM_LICENSE`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_HOST`, `REDIS_PORT` ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port

--num_workers 2 --timeout_worker_healthcheck 60 --telemetry False --use_prisma_db_push ``` config.yaml ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.5 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.5 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: gpt-5.4-nano litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-nano api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: gpt-5.5-priority litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.5 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: custom_auth: qa_custom_auth.user_api_key_auth custom_auth_run_common_checks: true team_admin_editable_team_fields: ["projects"] ``` qa_custom_auth.py, next to config.yaml ```python import os from fastapi import Request from litellm.proxy._types import LitellmUserRoles, UserAPIKeyAuth CALLERS = { "sk-app-token-a": {"user_id": "batch-svc", "team_id": "data-platform", "project_id": "batch-app-project"}, "sk-app-token-b": {"user_id": "batch-svc", "team_id": "data-platform", "project_id": "batch-app-project"}, "sk-team-lead": {"user_id": "team-lead", "team_id": "data-platform"}, "sk-project-daily-capped": { "user_id": "batch-svc", "team_id": "data-platform", "project_id": "batch-app-project", "tpd_limit": 1000, }, "sk-priority-minute-capped": { "user_id": "batch-svc", "team_id": "data-platform", "project_id": "priority-app-project", "tpm_limit": 1000, }, "sk-daily-capped": { "user_id": "batch-svc", "team_id": "data-platform", "metadata": {"batch_enqueued_token_limit": 100000}, "tpd_limit": 1000, }, } async def user_api_key_auth(request: Request, api_key: str) -> UserAPIKeyAuth: if api_key == os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]: return UserAPIKeyAuth(api_key=api_key, user_role=LitellmUserRoles.PROXY_ADMIN) caller = CALLERS.get(api_key) if caller is None: raise Exception("unknown caller") return UserAPIKeyAuth(api_key=api_key, **caller) ``` Request bodies ``` $ cat user-admin.json {"user_id": "team-lead"} $ cat user-svc.json {"user_id": "batch-svc"} $ cat team.json {"team_id": "data-platform", "team_alias": "data-platform", "members_with_roles": [{"role": "admin", "user_id": "team-lead"}, {"role": "user", "user_id": "batch-svc"}]} $ cat project.json {"project_id": "batch-app-project", "team_id": "data-platform", "project_alias": "batch-app", "metadata": {"model_batch_enqueued_token_limit": {"gpt-5.5": 2000}}} $ cat project-raise.json {"project_id": "batch-app-project", "metadata": {"model_batch_enqueued_token_limit": {"gpt-5.5": 100000000}}} $ cat project-priority.json {"project_id": "priority-app-project", "team_id": "data-platform", "project_alias": "priority-app", "metadata": {"model_batch_enqueued_token_limit": {"gpt-5.5-priority": 2000}}} ``` Batch input files, 3 rows of 200 words each (1221 tokens per file) ``` for m in gpt-5.5 gpt-5.4-nano gpt-5.5-priority gpt-5.5-2026-04-23; do jq -cn --arg m $m 'range(1; 4) | {custom_id: "r\(.)", method: "POST", url: "/v1/chat/completions", body: {model: $m, messages: [{role: "user", content: ([range(200)] | map("enqueued") | join(" "))}]}}' > $m-batch.jsonl; done ``` The case scripts are in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/88ec2e8f558022ce3acf258fc4a7ebd0). Each runs as `MASTER=... zsh caseN.sh $P $Q` on both legs, and case12.sh also needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`

Case 7 and 10 setup, ui_leg.sh, and ui_flow.py Each leg's dashboard ran from its own tree with `LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=$P NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true npx next dev -p ` in `litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard`. For these cases only, each `$P` proxy was restarted with `PROXY_BASE_URL` pointing at its dashboard and with this change to qa_custom_auth.py, which hands unknown keys to built-in auth so the dashboard session can sign in ```diff -async def user_api_key_auth(request: Request, api_key: str) -> UserAPIKeyAuth: +async def user_api_key_auth(request: Request, api_key: str) -> UserAPIKeyAuth | str: @@ - raise Exception("unknown caller") + return api_key ``` Case 7 runs as `MASTER=... zsh ui_leg.sh $P before|after` To repeat it, set the cap with the first command, open `/ui/projects`, click `batch-app-project` in the ID column, click Edit Project, open Advanced Settings, scroll to Model-Specific Limits, click Save Changes, then read the project back with the last command Case 10 exports throwaway `TEAM_LEAD_PASSWORD` and `TEAM_LEAD_NEW_PASSWORD` and runs `MASTER=... zsh ui_leg_team.sh $P before-team` (after-team on the head leg) `ui_leg.sh`, `ui_flow.py`, `ui_leg_team.sh` and `ui_flow_team.py` are in [the case scripts gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/88ec2e8f558022ce3acf258fc4a7ebd0)

Cancel A, retry B | 200, 200 | 200, 200 | | 4. Team admin raises cap | 200, saved | 403 | | 5. Key allowance, daily cap | 200 | 200 | | 6. gpt-5.5 rows as nano | 200 | 429, project_model | | 7. Admin saves in UI | cap as text | cap kept | | 8. Over key daily cap | 429 | 429 | | 9. Managed file, key TPM | 429 | 200 | | 10. Team admin clears TPM in UI | cap as text | cap kept | | 11.
