/live-pr-risk at 94a2f8355f Base ac1cc5111c and head 94a2f8355f on the QA rig above, plus one pod booted from the base tree on the head's Postgres and Redis for the mixed-version cell. Scripts and raw output are in the [gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/32ce8daf888dde2fb25b80c5cdc3b40a) **Breaking.** None found **Backward incompatible.** Both are intended and listed under Decisions - `/project/update` without `metadata` merges top-level fields onto the stored metadata. Base dropped the stored cap and `owner_note` on a `model_rpm_limit` update, and with `enforce_project_model_quota` it answered 400 to rpm-only and tags-only updates. Head keeps them and answers 200 (P1, Q1). Shipped in 9647af3b46 - With `skip_batch_input_file_rate_limiting_for_providers: ["openai"]`, base skipped input-file limits only for a body-routed batch and answered 429 by `x-litellm-model` header or `?model=`. Head answers 200 for all three (S1). Shipped in 94a2f8355f **Mixed versions (M1).** A key cap reserved on a head pod is refunded when a base pod cancels the batch. A project cap is not, so the next batch gets 429 with 779 of 2000 left, while the same cancel on a head pod frees it. This is the Medium caveat. Nothing that worked on base changes **Regression risk.** `litellm-enterprise` installed from PyPI lags the proxy until the next release bump publishes it, so a pip install mixing versions misses the project endpoint changes. Docker images build from the workspace and are not affected | Dependent | Status | | --- | --- | | Reservation save and refund | live (QA 3, M1) | | Refund after pre-call reject | live (QA 8) | | Provider skip list | live (S1) | | Project per-minute lift | live (QA 9) | | `/project/update` write | live (P1) | | Project model quota | live (Q1) | | Key and team admin gate | integration | | Project admin gate, Admin UI | live (QA 4, 7, 10) | | Lookup by deployment id | unit, fake router | **Integration sweep at the head.** Management 126 passed and providers 49 passed, with 2 skips the suite already marks as known bugs. Accounting passed 14, and 4 `test_batch_poll_starvation` cases hit their 180 s timeout while the machine was loaded. Rerun alone, those 4 pass on both base and head **Not verified.** The deployment id lookup against a real router registry, pass-through routes whose guardrails reach the batch post-call hook, and the new fail-open branch in the pre-call hook, which no realistic input raises into Merge ref: main is 9 commits past the merge base, touching only Together AI entries in `constants.py` and `en.json`, so the cells were not rerun on a merged tree
## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - Older pods drop the project part of a refund. A pod on the older version reads the record without `project_scopes`, refunds only key and team, then deletes it. Every new reservation refreshes the counter's 8-day TTL, so under steady traffic the leaked tokens stay until someone deletes `batch_enqueued_tokens:project_model::`. A rollback with capped batches in flight hits it too, so setting caps after the rollout does not cover every case ### Low - Custom auth leaves the cap off unless `custom_auth_run_common_checks` or `enable_post_custom_auth_checks` is set, the same as existing project TPM limits. Native JWT sets no project - A capped project reads each batch's input file at create - `"metadata": null` from a team admin on a capped project gets a 403. Leaving out `metadata` works
Decisions - Rows uploaded with `model=` keep their own model names, so the batch charges each capped model they name. Charging only the routing model was rejected because case 6 shows it lets a gpt-5.5 file skip the gpt-5.5 cap - Managed files charge only the model they route to, because upload already rewrote their rows to the deployment model. A cap on that model alone covers them, so their per-minute checks are skipped too - A key or team enqueued allowance still turns off every other batch check, as the batches docs promise - The routing model is read the way batch create routes: the file-bound model, then the body `model`, then `?model=`, then the `x-litellm-model` header - With `skip_batch_input_file_rate_limiting_for_providers` set, a batch routed by `?model=` or the `x-litellm-model` header now skips input-file limits the same as one routed by the body `model`. Keeping the body-only check was rejected because it limited the same batch differently by how the model was sent - A project cap keeps daily caps and skips per-minute ones only when it caps the routing model and every model the rows name. A batch's tokens run over hours, so a per-minute window would reject any large batch outright. Skipping on the routing model alone was rejected because it also turned off the project ITPM and OTPM limits of the other row models - A `-latest` name is charged under the cap of the model it points to, the same way the per-minute limiter matches it. A dated snapshot such as `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` also counts toward its base model's cap, since rows can name any model the provider serves. A listed dated name keeps its own cap too - The limit map takes only JSON integers, so `true`, `"2000"` and `2000.0` answer 400 instead of being read as numbers - A `/project/update` that leaves out `metadata` now merges its top-level fields onto the stored metadata. Replacing was rejected because a top-level `model_tpm_limit` silently dropped the cap and every other key. An update that sends `metadata` still replaces it, so the Admin UI can still remove keys - Project scopes are stored apart from key and team scopes, so an older pod can still refund the key and team part - The Admin UI edits the cap as a Batch Enqueued Token Limit field in each Model-Specific Limits row. A save with no batch value sends no cap map, so a team admin can still save a project that has no cap. The field is read-only for team admins, and their saves send back the stored cap, since the API answers 403 to any change they make to it - `"metadata": null` on `/project/update` counts as an empty map in the admin-only check. Special-casing it in that shared check was rejected, since leaving out `metadata` already keeps the stored map
## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Provisioning retries fail and duplicate customer org aliases break requests

How it solves it:

- Add idempotent customer org and customer member upsert APIs
- Reject conflicting aliases inside shared, locked transactions

Intentional product change: customer org creates and alias edits now return 409 for aliases owned by another customer org, rather than accepting duplicates that break customer alias lookup

## User Flow

Before, provisioning retries fail and duplicate aliases break customer requests

1. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations with an alias and budgets returns 201
2. Repeat the create with its ID and receive 409. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/upsert returns 405
3. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members again with the same customer member ID returns 409
4. Create another customer org with the same alias and receive 201
5. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses with the customer alias and customer member headers returns 400, as do Chat Completions and Messages

After, idempotent provisioning preserves identities and conflicting aliases fail during onboarding

1. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations with an alias and budgets still returns 201
2. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/upsert returns 200 with created=true, then created=false on repeat
3. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_members/upsert with customer org alias and customer member ID returns 200 on creation and retry
4. Create another customer org with the same alias and receive 409 with a clear conflict message
5. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses with the upserted identities returns 200 with attributed spend, as do Chat Completions and Messages

No PR was opened. CI and automated review checks remain pending

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Shared setup

<details>
<summary>Proxy configuration and exact curl client</summary>

The proxy used PostgreSQL 14 on localhost:5432 and the existing QA database. Redis on localhost:6383 was shared by both workers through router_settings and general_settings.coordination_redis. No schema change or migration was needed

Both proxies used two workers. Port 4000 handled the curl proof. Port 4001 remained available with fail-open disabled. No database outage was introduced in this proof. Reload was omitted to keep the two workers stable during worktree comparisons, and the proxies were restarted explicitly

The required environment variable names are DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and LITELLM_MASTER_KEY. Existing provider and database credentials were inherited from the local QA environment. The master key was loaded from /home/ubuntu/.qa-master-key, which remains mode 600. No credential values appear here

The launched proxy argv was the following for each checkout. CHECKOUT was /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr4-main for Before and /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm for After

```bash
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="$(</home/ubuntu/.qa-master-key)"
export DATABASE_URL OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
export PYTHONPATH="$CHECKOUT:$CHECKOUT/enterprise"
cd "$CHECKOUT"
/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config /home/ubuntu/pr4-on.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --port 4000
```

```python
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx

phase = sys.argv[1]
stem = 'pr5-' + phase + '-' + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
master = Path('/home/ubuntu/.qa-master-key').read_text().strip()
db = urlparse(os.environ['DATABASE_URL'])
results = {'phase': phase, 'stem': stem, 'calls': [], 'inference': [], 'races': {}}
output = Path('/home/ubuntu/pr5-' + phase + '.json')


def save():
    output.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))


def sql(query):
    command = ['psql', '-X', '-At', '-h', db.hostname, '-p', str(db.port or 5432),
               '-U', db.username, '-d', db.path.lstrip('/'), '-c', query]
    response = subprocess.run(command, env={**os.environ, 'PGPASSWORD': db.password},
                              capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return json.loads(response.stdout)


def curl(method, path, body, expected=None, key=None, customer=None, label=None, secret=False):
    command = ['curl', '-sS', '-D', '-', '-X', method, 'http://localhost:4000' + path,
               '-H', 'Authorization: Bearer ' + (key or master), '-H', 'Content-Type: application/json']
    if customer:
        command += ['-H', 'x-litellm-customer-org-alias: ' + customer[0],
                    '-H', 'x-litellm-customer-member-id: ' + customer[1]]
    command += ['--data', json.dumps(body), '-w', '\n__STATUS__%{http_code}']
    response = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    raw, _, status = response.stdout.rpartition('\n__STATUS__')
    header_text, _, body_text = raw.partition('\n\n')
    headers = {line.partition(':')[0].lower(): line.partition(':')[2].strip()
               for line in header_text.splitlines()[1:] if ':' in line}
    payload = json.loads(body_text)
    display = shlex.join(command).replace(master, '$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY')
    display = display.replace("'Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY'", '"Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"')
    if key:
        display = display.replace(key, '$VIRTUAL_KEY')
        display = display.replace("'Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY'", '"Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY"')
    record = {'label': label or path, 'command': display, 'status': int(status),
              'body': {'key': '<not printed>'} if secret else payload,
              'response_cost': headers.get('x-litellm-response-cost')}
    results['calls'].append(record)
    print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
    save()
    if expected is not None:
        assert int(status) == expected, record
    return payload, record


for port in (4000, 4001):
    for attempt in range(180):
        try:
            health = httpx.get(f'http://localhost:{port}/health/readiness',
                               headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + master}, timeout=5)
            if health.status_code == 200:
                break
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            pass
        time.sleep(1)
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Proxy {port} did not start')

results['preexisting_duplicate_alias_groups'] = sql(
    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT alias FROM "LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable" '
    'WHERE alias IS NOT NULL GROUP BY alias HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) d')
generated, _ = curl('POST', '/key/generate', {'models': ['qa-gpt', 'qa-claude']}, 200, secret=True)
virtual = generated['key']
base = '/management/v1/'
repeat_body = {'customer_org_id': stem + '-repeat', 'alias': stem + '-repeat',
               'budget': {'max_budget': 10}, 'default_budgets': [{'name': 'default', 'max_budget': 10}]}
curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations', repeat_body, 201, label='create')
curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations', repeat_body, 409, label='duplicate create')
legacy_team = {'customer_team_id': stem + '-repeat-team', 'parent_org_id': stem + '-repeat'}
curl('POST', base + 'customer_teams', legacy_team, 201)
legacy_member = {'customer_member_id': stem + '-repeat-member', 'parent_team_id': stem + '-repeat-team'}
curl('POST', base + 'customer_members', legacy_member, 201)
curl('POST', base + 'customer_members', legacy_member, 409, label='duplicate customer member create')

org_payload = {'alias': stem, 'budget': {'max_budget': 10},
               'default_budgets': [{'name': 'standard', 'max_budget': 10}]}
org, org_record = curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations/upsert', org_payload,
                       200 if phase == 'after' else 405, label='customer org upsert first')
if phase == 'before':
    curl('POST', base + 'customer_members/upsert',
         {'customer_member_id': stem + '-member', 'customer_org_alias': stem}, 405)
    ambiguous_body = {**repeat_body, 'customer_org_id': stem + '-duplicate'}
    curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations', ambiguous_body, 201, label='duplicate alias accepted')
    identity = (stem + '-repeat', stem + '-repeat-member')
else:
    assert org['created'] is True
    repeated, _ = curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations/upsert', org_payload, 200,
                       label='customer org upsert repeat')
    assert repeated == {**org, 'created': False}
    changed, _ = curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations/upsert',
                      {'customer_org_id': org['customer_org_id'], 'budget': {'max_budget': 20}}, 200,
                      label='customer org upsert update by id')
    assert changed['budget_id'] == org['budget_id'] and changed['budget']['max_budget'] == 20
    member_payload = {'customer_org_alias': stem, 'customer_member_id': stem + '-member', 'alias': 'customer member'}
    member, _ = curl('POST', base + 'customer_members/upsert', member_payload, 200,
                     label='customer member upsert first')
    assert member['created'] is True and member['parent_team_id'] == org['customer_org_id'] + ':default'
    repeated_member, _ = curl('POST', base + 'customer_members/upsert', member_payload, 200,
                              label='customer member upsert repeat')
    assert repeated_member == {**member, 'created': False}
    changed_member, _ = curl('POST', base + 'customer_members/upsert',
                             {**member_payload, 'alias': 'updated customer member', 'budget_override': {'max_budget': 7}},
                             200, label='customer member upsert update')
    assert changed_member['effective_budget']['max_budget'] == 7
    curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations', {'customer_org_id': stem + '-duplicate', 'alias': stem}, 409,
         label='duplicate alias rejected at create')
    curl('PATCH', base + 'customer_organizations/' + stem + '-repeat', {'alias': stem}, 409,
         label='duplicate alias rejected at update')
    curl('POST', base + 'customer_members/upsert',
         {'customer_org_id': stem + '-repeat', 'customer_member_id': stem + '-member'}, 409,
         label='cross customer org move rejected')
    identity = (stem, stem + '-member')
    results['resolved_identity'] = {'customer_org_id': org['customer_org_id'], 'customer_org_alias': stem,
                                    'customer_team_id': member['parent_team_id'], 'customer_member_id': member['customer_member_id']}

for endpoint in ('responses', 'chat/completions', 'messages'):
    body = {'model': 'qa-claude' if endpoint == 'messages' else 'qa-gpt', 'stream': False}
    if endpoint == 'responses':
        body.update(input='Say OK', max_output_tokens=8)
    else:
        body.update(messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Say OK'}], max_tokens=8)
    response, record = curl('POST', '/v1/' + endpoint, body, 200 if phase == 'after' else 400,
                            key=virtual, customer=identity, label=endpoint)
    results['inference'].append(record)

if phase == 'after':
    expected_cost = sum(float(record['response_cost']) for record in results['inference'])
    customer_org_id = org['customer_org_id']
    member_id = identity[1]
    query = ('SELECT json_build_object('
             "'customer_org_spend', (SELECT spend FROM \"LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable\" "
             f"WHERE customer_org_id='{customer_org_id}'), "
             "'customer_team_spend', (SELECT spend FROM \"LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable\" "
             f"WHERE customer_team_id='{member['parent_team_id']}'), "
             "'customer_member_spend', (SELECT spend FROM \"LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable\" "
             f"WHERE customer_member_id='{member_id}'), "
             "'daily', (SELECT json_agg(d) FROM (SELECT customer_org_id, customer_team_id, customer_member_id, "
             'endpoint, model, spend, api_requests FROM "LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend" '
             f"WHERE customer_org_id='{customer_org_id}' AND customer_member_id='{member_id}') d))")
    for attempt in range(90):
        attribution = sql(query)
        amounts = [attribution[field] for field in ('customer_org_spend', 'customer_team_spend', 'customer_member_spend')]
        daily = attribution['daily'] or []
        if (all(abs(value - expected_cost) < 1e-10 for value in amounts)
                and sum(row['api_requests'] for row in daily) == 3):
            break
        time.sleep(2)
    else:
        raise AssertionError(attribution)
    results['attribution'] = {'expected_response_cost_sum': expected_cost, 'sql': query, **attribution}
    print(json.dumps({'attribution': results['attribution']}), flush=True)
    for scope, resource, payload in (
        ('customer_org', 'customer_organizations/upsert', {'alias': stem + '-race'}),
        ('customer_member', 'customer_members/upsert', {'customer_org_alias': stem, 'customer_member_id': stem + '-race-member'}),
    ):
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as executor:
            records = list(executor.map(lambda _: curl('POST', base + resource, payload, 200)[1], range(6)))
        created_count = sum(record['body']['created'] for record in records)
        assert created_count == 1, records
        results['races'][scope] = {'statuses': [record['status'] for record in records], 'created_count': created_count}
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as executor:
        records = list(executor.map(lambda n: curl('POST', base + 'customer_organizations',
                            {'customer_org_id': stem + '-race-duplicate-' + str(n), 'alias': stem + '-race-duplicate'})[1], range(6)))
    statuses = sorted(record['status'] for record in records)
    assert statuses == [201, 409, 409, 409, 409, 409], statuses
    results['races']['duplicate_alias'] = {'statuses': statuses}

save()
print(json.dumps({'phase': phase, 'inference_statuses': [record['status'] for record in results['inference']],
                  'races': results['races'], 'preexisting_duplicate_alias_groups': results['preexisting_duplicate_alias_groups']}), flush=True)
```

### Implementation and API semantics

Both routes follow the existing /management/v1 customer route prefix and admin authorization. They return the resolved customer entity plus created. Existing create endpoints keep their 201 response and duplicate-ID 409 contract

Customer org upsert uses customer_org_id when supplied, otherwise alias. Omitted fields retain their values. Supplied default_budgets merge by name, keep existing template IDs and retain omitted templates. A single supplied template becomes default, while multiple templates require exactly one marked default. This avoids deleting budgets referenced by existing customer members

Customer member upsert uses customer_member_id with customer_org_id or customer_org_alias. When both customer org identifiers are supplied they must match. It reuses alias, budget_id, budget_override and budget_override_expires_at from the existing customer member models. An omitted parent_team_id selects the default customer team, including on updates. Customer team changes within the same customer org are allowed, but customer org changes and foreign customer teams return 409

Alias checks run inside the same PostgreSQL transaction as the write, under a shared transaction-scoped advisory lock used by customer org create, update and upsert. Customer org row locks also protect upsert snapshots against existing template writers. No unique index or migration was added because installations can already contain duplicate aliases. The Before replay created such a duplicate pair, which remained present during After without blocking startup. Legacy ambiguous alias lookups through upsert return 409. Existing duplicate rows are left unchanged

All customer management writers must use the updated implementation for the application-level uniqueness guarantee. A mixed-version rollout or direct SQL writer can bypass it. Redis remains shared across both workers, and successful upserts invalidate the existing customer hierarchy caches

title: fix(proxy): admit cold customer hierarchy requests during database outages
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer lookups after auth still fail during database outages
- Admitted requests lose customer attribution before spend recovery

How it solves it:

- Gate downstream recovery on verified keys and transient outages
- Keep asserted customer identity and the key's customer org binding
- Resolve customer attribution inside the accounting delivery transaction
- Commit customer spend and delivery acknowledgement together

## User Flow

Before, a known key reaches auth but fails before the provider.

1. The admin enables fail-open and authenticates a virtual key while PostgreSQL is online.
2. They stop PostgreSQL and POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions or /v1/messages with cold customer headers.
3. Messages returns 500. Responses and chat return 400 in this environment. An unknown key returns 503.

After, the same request reaches the provider and retains its customer identity.

1. The admin enables fail-open and authenticates a virtual key while PostgreSQL is online.
2. They stop PostgreSQL and POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions or /v1/messages with cold customer headers.
3. All three return 200. Recovery attributes each charge once. An unknown key still returns 503.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Shared setup

Both phases use two serving workers, dedicated shared Redis on localhost port 6383, and local PostgreSQL cluster 14/main on port 5432. Reload is omitted to keep two actual workers. Each phase creates a new customer org, customer team, customer member and virtual key through management APIs. The key is bound to that customer org. Twenty concurrent GET /key/info requests authenticate the key on both workers without requesting a customer hierarchy. The runner checks that Redis has no customer hierarchy keys for the new identity before stopping PostgreSQL. pg_isready confirms the real outage.

The live provider models are OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol and Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5. The environment provides DATABASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and LITELLM_MASTER_KEY. The local runner inherits these from the existing QA environment process. No credentials are embedded in the config or this body. DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true prevents schema changes. The old base reports the additional email column already present in the QA database. It is not removed. Both checkouts use the existing compatible native artifact.

The common config is /home/ubuntu/pr4-auth-review.yaml.

```yaml
environment_variables:
  WEBHOOK_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8808
model_list:
  - model_name: qa-gpt
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: qa-claude
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  allow_requests_on_db_unavailable: true
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6383
router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6383
litellm_settings:
  enable_redis_auth_cache: true
  drop_params: true
```

The effective launch is below, from $ROOT/litellm/proxy. ROOT is /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr4-downstream-before at 53cc5e9674 for Before, and /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-pr4-attribution for After.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT:$ROOT/enterprise"
export DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true
export MAX_STRING_LENGTH_STDOUT_LOG=20000
/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli \
  --config /home/ubuntu/pr4-auth-review.yaml --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4000
```

### Before at 53cc5e9674

1. Run /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/pr4-downstream-repro.py.
2. The cached known key is admitted by auth with the cold customer org alias and customer member ID. The log says DB unavailable, admitting request without customer hierarchy.
3. All three requests then fail in add_litellm_data_to_request -> resolve_customer_usage -> litellm_customerorganizationtable.find_unique. This second read comes from the key's customer org binding. It runs after auth and before provider dispatch.

The database lookup failure is reproduced, including a 500 on Messages. The exact OpenAI-route 500 and Can't reach database text reported by Ishaan are not reproduced here. The installed Prisma decoder raises AttributeError when its database error payload has meta=null. Responses and chat map that to 400, while Messages maps it to 500. Auth already recognizes the underlying transient Prisma code. An immediate-outage run and a run with a five-second delay show the same downstream path, ruling out only an in-flight shutdown race. Both phases retain the same runtime dependency environment.

### Historical After at c6f588815f

1. Run /home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/pr4-downstream-after.py.
2. Responses returns 200 on worker 442500 at $0.000068. Chat Completions returns 200 on worker 442501 at $0.000058. Messages returns 200 on worker 442500 at $0.000136.
3. The unknown-key probe returns 503. The runner leaves PostgreSQL stopped for another ten seconds, allowing failed spend flushes, then restores it.
4. The three customer scope rows, customer daily accounting, virtual-key DB spend and Redis spend:key counter each settle at $0.000262. All three spend logs retain the asserted customer identity and key binding. All three accounting deliveries are applied.
5. Two concurrent SQL connections retry the same spend-log inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, matching the writer's duplicate handling. Both insert zero rows. After another ten seconds, the entire recovery snapshot is unchanged, including delivery count, customer spend, key spend and Redis spend.

This retry checks the spend-write boundary. It does not send a second paid provider request. The two actual serving workers handled paid requests. The Redis comparison is the virtual key's live spend counter. Customer scope counter families were not present in the c6f588815f live-proof checkout. The merge below brings them in from main. Customer attribution is checked against all three scope rows and customer daily accounting.

The caller's submitted customer member ID is preserved. This branch has no customer member email header, so the email extension is intentionally omitted. When a submitted customer org alias conflicts with the authenticated key binding, the key binding remains authoritative. Unit cases cover both a matching customer member and a foreign customer member. The foreign customer member never receives spend.

```python
        schema = 'pr4_merge_' + uuid.uuid4().hex
        expanded = query
        for index, argument in enumerate(arguments, 1):

        sql = f'''BEGIN; CREATE SCHEMA "{schema}"; SET LOCAL search_path TO "{schema}";
            CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable" (customer_org_id text PRIMARY KEY, alias text);
            CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable" (customer_team_id text PRIMARY KEY, parent_org_id text);
            CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable" (customer_member_id text PRIMARY KEY, parent_org_id text, parent_team_ids text[]);

            INSERT INTO "LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable" VALUES ('team-a','org-a'),('second-team-a','org-a'),('foreign-team','org-b');

                ('member-no-team','org-a',ARRAY[]::text[]),
                ('member-b','org-b',ARRAY['foreign-team']);
            SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(result), '[]'::json) FROM ({expanded}) result;
            ROLLBACK;
        '''
        result = subprocess.run([
            'psql','-X','-qAt','-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1','-h',database.hostname,
            '-p',str(database.port or 5432),'-U',database.username,'-d',database.path.lstrip('/'),'-f','-',
        ],env={**self.environment,'PGPASSWORD':database.password},input=sql,capture_output=True,text=True,check=True)
        return json.loads(result.stdout)


async def main():
    environment = {**os.environ, **psutil.Process(147419).environ()}
    results = []
    if True:
        cases = [
            ('member-a', None, {'customer_org_id':'org-a','customer_team_id':'team-a','customer_member_id':'member-a'}),
            ('member-a', 'second-team-a', {'customer_org_id':'org-a','customer_team_id':'second-team-a','customer_member_id':'member-a'}),
```

Problem this solves:

- Customer details take space above request metrics
- Customer IDs lack recognition labels and navigation
- Unauthorized requests must not persist another customer's hierarchy

- Show a collapsed Customer accordion below Metrics

- Keep IDs copyable and link recognized customer scopes
- Show legacy user-only identities as Asserted
- Persist aliases from the authorized snapshot without extra log-time lookups
- Refresh current customer spend before access and budget checks

Intentional product change: Customer details start collapsed below Metrics. Expand the row to see IDs and navigation links.

```python
import json
import os
import time
import uuid

import httpx

base = 'http://127.0.0.1:4000'
admin = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}
client = httpx.Client(timeout=180)
clients = [httpx.Client(timeout=180) for _ in range(24)]

def create(path, body):
    response = client.post(base + path, headers=admin, json=body)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()

name = 'pr3-accordion-' + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
create('/management/v1/customer_organizations', {'customer_org_id': name, 'alias': name + '-org', 'budget': {'max_budget': 10}, 'default_budgets': [{'name': 'default', 'is_default': True, 'max_budget': 10}]})
create('/management/v1/customer_teams', {'customer_team_id': name + '-team', 'alias': 'Customer team display', 'parent_org_id': name})
create('/management/v1/customer_members', {'customer_member_id': name + '-member', 'alias': 'Customer member display', 'parent_team_id': name + '-team'})
key = create('/key/generate', {'models': ['qa-gpt', 'qa-claude']})['key']
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, 'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': name + '-org', 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': name + '-member'}
results = []
started = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime())
for endpoint in ('responses', 'chat/completions', 'messages', 'legacy'):
    body = {'model': 'qa-claude' if endpoint == 'messages' else 'qa-gpt'}
    if endpoint == 'responses':
        body.update(input='Reply only OK', max_output_tokens=64)
    else:
        body.update(messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply only OK'}], **({'max_tokens': 64} if endpoint == 'messages' else {'max_completion_tokens': 64}))
    if endpoint == 'legacy':
        body['user'] = name + '-legacy-customer'
    response = clients[len(results)].post(base + '/v1/' + ('chat/completions' if endpoint == 'legacy' else endpoint),
                                          headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key} if endpoint == 'legacy' else headers, json=body)
    assert response.status_code == 200, (endpoint, response.text)
    results.append({'endpoint': endpoint, 'status': response.status_code})

budget_name = name + '-budget'
create('/management/v1/customer_organizations', {'customer_org_id': budget_name, 'alias': budget_name,
       'budget': {'max_budget': 0.0000000001}, 'default_budgets': [{'name': 'default', 'is_default': True, 'max_budget': 10}]})
create('/management/v1/customer_teams', {'customer_team_id': budget_name + '-team', 'parent_org_id': budget_name})
create('/management/v1/customer_members', {'customer_member_id': budget_name + '-member', 'parent_team_id': budget_name + '-team'})
budget_headers = {**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': budget_name, 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': budget_name + '-member'}
paid = clients[0].post(base + '/v1/responses', headers=budget_headers,
        json={'model': 'qa-gpt', 'input': 'Reply only OK', 'max_output_tokens': 64})
assert paid.status_code == 200, paid.text
for _ in range(180):
    spend = client.get(base + '/management/v1/customer_organizations/' + budget_name, headers=admin)
    spend.raise_for_status()
    if spend.json()['spend'] > 0.0000000001:
        break
    time.sleep(.5)
else:
    raise AssertionError('Paid customer spend did not settle')
denials = []
for endpoint in ('responses', 'chat/completions', 'messages'):
    body = {'model': 'qa-claude' if endpoint == 'messages' else 'qa-gpt'}
    if endpoint == 'responses':
        body.update(input='Reply only OK', max_output_tokens=64)
    else:
        body.update(messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply only OK'}], **({'max_tokens': 64} if endpoint == 'messages' else {'max_completion_tokens': 64}))
```

title: fix(types): build Usage schemas eagerly so parallel first requests cannot race
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description A burst of parallel requests hitting a freshly started proxy worker could fail some of them with an internal schema error while building the usage object. This makes the usage types build their validation schema once at import, so concurrent first requests can no longer race on it
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Parallel first requests on a fresh worker sometimes fail with `AttributeError` - `Usage` builds its pydantic schema lazily, and concurrent rebuilds race How it solves it: - `Usage` and its two token-detail wrappers set `defer_build=False` - New regression test in `tests/unit/types/test_types_utils.py` forces the race in a fresh subprocess ## User Flow Before: some requests in a burst against a freshly booted proxy worker fail 1. The admin starts or restarts the proxy 2. A client fires many POST /v1/chat/completions requests at once 3. A few come back as errors mentioning `type object 'Usage' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'` After: the same burst succeeds for every request 1. The admin starts or restarts the proxy 2. A client fires many POST /v1/chat/completions requests at once 3. Every request returns 200 with a `usage` object ## Relevant issues Seen in the scheduled integration run https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/42958083166/job/130317851934 in `tests/integration/observability/test_langtrace_delivery.py::test_langtrace_two_workers_deliver_every_burst_span_exactly_once` ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The race is timing dependent, so the deterministic red/green proof is the regression test. It runs a fresh subprocess where eight threads construct each model at once, with a barrier holding them right before pydantic deletes the half built schema (falling back to a plain start barrier if that pydantic line ever changes). The live burst below did not reproduce the race on the base, so it shows the fix is safe under the real flow, not a natural reproduction Shared setup. Two workers with `--reload`, one dedicated local Redis shared by `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`, database free (`DATABASE_URL` and `DIRECT_URL` unset), `LITELLM_RUST=0` and `LITELLM_RUST_FIRST=0` to exercise the Python path. Env vars `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `USAGE_RACE_MASTER_KEY`. Each boot waits for both workers' `Application startup complete`, then fires 24 simultaneous requests with no warm up, five fresh boots per revision ```sh redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6397 --save '' --appendonly no python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config usage_race_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4197 ```
usage_race_config.yaml ```yaml model_list: - model_name: usage-race-haiku litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 6397 num_retries: 0 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/USAGE_RACE_MASTER_KEY coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6397 ```
Runner and burst client, exactly as run ```python import asyncio import collections import json import os from pathlib import Path import re import signal import subprocess import sys import threading import time import httpx ROOT = Path('/home/ubuntu') LOGS = ROOT / 'usage_race_logs' LOGS.mkdir(exist_ok=True) PYTHON = '/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python' CONFIG = ROOT / 'usage_race_config.yaml' KEY = 'sk-usage-race-local-only' SECRET_VALUES = tuple(value for name, value in os.environ.items() if ('KEY' in name or 'TOKEN' in name) and len(value) > 10) def redact(text): for value in SECRET_VALUES: text = text.replace(value, '[REDACTED]') return text async def burst(): event = asyncio.Event() async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120, limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=24)) as client: async def request(index): await event.wait() try: response = await client.post( 'http://127.0.0.1:4197/v1/chat/completions', headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + KEY}, json={'model': 'usage-race-haiku', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply with OK'}], 'max_tokens': 16}, ) body = response.json() return {'status': response.status_code, 'model': body.get('model'), 'usage': body.get('usage'), 'error': redact(str(body.get('error')))[:500] if response.status_code != 200 else None} except Exception as error: return {'status': 'exception', 'error': redact(str(error))} tasks = tuple(asyncio.create_task(request(index)) for index in range(24)) event.set() return await asyncio.gather(*tasks) def run(label, checkout, number): logfile = LOGS / f'{label}-{number}.log' environment = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONPATH': f'{checkout}:{checkout}/enterprise', 'LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP': 'True', 'USAGE_RACE_MASTER_KEY': KEY, 'LITELLM_RUST': '0', 'LITELLM_RUST_FIRST': '0'} environment.pop('DATABASE_URL', None) environment.pop('DIRECT_URL', None) command = [PYTHON, 'litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py', '--config', str(CONFIG), '--num_workers', '2', '--detailed_debug', '--reload', '--use_v2_migration_resolver', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '4197'] process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=checkout, env=environment, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, start_new_session=True) def capture(): with logfile.open('w') as stream: for line in process.stdout: stream.write(redact(line)) stream.flush() reader = threading.Thread(target=capture) reader.start() try: deadline = time.monotonic() + 180 while time.monotonic() < deadline: text = logfile.read_text() if logfile.exists() else '' if text.count('Application startup complete.') >= 2: break if process.poll() is not None: raise RuntimeError(f'{label} boot {number} exited {process.returncode}; see {logfile}') time.sleep(0.05) else: raise RuntimeError(f'{label} boot {number} startup timed out; see {logfile}') results = asyncio.run(burst()) text = logfile.read_text() summary = {'revision': label, 'boot': number, 'requests': len(results), 'status_counts': dict(collections.Counter(str(result['status']) for result in results)), 'non_200': sum(result['status'] != 200 for result in results), 'schema_error_lines': sum('__pydantic_core_schema__' in line for line in text.splitlines()), 'worker_pids': sorted(set(re.findall(r'Started server process \[(\d+)\]', text))), 'errors': [result['error'] for result in results if result['status'] != 200], 'models': sorted(set(result.get('model') or '' for result in results))} (LOGS / f'{label}-{number}.json').write_text(json.dumps({'summary': summary, 'responses': results}, indent=2)) print(json.dumps(summary), flush=True) return summary finally: os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM) try: process.wait(timeout=30) except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL) process.wait() reader.join(timeout=10) if __name__ == '__main__': redis = subprocess.Popen(['redis-server', '--bind', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '6397', '--save', '', '--appendonly', 'no'], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT) try: for label, checkout in [('base', '/home/ubuntu/usage-schema-baseline'), ('tip', '/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm')]: for number in range(1, 6): run(label, checkout, number) finally: redis.terminate() redis.wait(timeout=10) ```
### Before (072290e78f27) 1. Regression probe on unfixed code ```text RED exit 1 File ".../pydantic/main.py", line 668, in model_rebuild delattr(cls, attr) AttributeError: type object 'Usage' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__' ``` 2. Live burst, 5 fresh boots x 24 requests. 120 of 120 returned 200, zero `__pydantic_core_schema__` log lines (race did not trigger naturally) ### After (8671620eb313) 1. Regression probe on the fix ```text GREEN exit 0 Usage: 8 parallel constructions passed PromptTokensDetailsWrapper: 8 parallel constructions passed CompletionTokensDetailsWrapper: 8 parallel constructions passed ``` 2. Live burst, 5 fresh boots x 24 requests. 120 of 120 returned 200 with a `usage` object, zero `__pydantic_core_schema__` log lines
Per boot live output, base then tip ```json {"revision":"base","boot":1,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["29244","29245"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"base","boot":2,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["30144","30145"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"base","boot":3,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["30530","30531"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"base","boot":4,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["30806","30807"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"base","boot":5,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["31070","31071"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"tip","boot":1,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["31308","31309"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"tip","boot":2,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["31554","31555"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"tip","boot":3,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["31805","31806"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"tip","boot":4,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["32040","32041"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} {"revision":"tip","boot":5,"requests":24,"status_counts":{"200":24},"non_200":0,"schema_error_lines":0,"worker_pids":["32393","32394"],"errors":[],"models":["usage-race-haiku"]} ```
3. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run pytest tests/unit/types/test_types_utils.py -q` at bc906018df7 gives 82 passed, and the race test goes red (`type object 'Usage' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'`) with the three `defer_build=False` lines removed ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Low - Eager build adds roughly 40ms to `import litellm` - Other OpenAI derived response models (`Message`, `Delta`, `ModelResponse`, ...) stay lazily built - Not seen failing, kept out to keep this scoped - Latent race, no single introducing PR found ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: fix(tests): run the worker-replacement chaos test under strict supervision
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description The fine-tuning chaos test that kills each proxy worker could time out in CI because its proxy ran with the long healthcheck meant for the worker-pause test, so uvicorn took minutes to notice each dead worker. This gives the kill test its own proxy with normal supervision and lets the module use the calibrated per-test timeout, so the scheduled `extensions` run stops failing on it
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `test_a_replaced_worker_still_sends_the_provider_file_ids` hit pytest-timeout (>480s) in scheduled run [42680944695](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/42680944695/job/129374969994) - Its shared fixture used `WorkerHealthcheck.LENIENT`, which is `12 x import_seconds`, 262s on that box - uvicorn 0.51.0 only reaps a worker killed during an unanswered ping after the healthcheck expires, so two sequential kills can burn over 480s - The module's fixed `timeout(480)` also bypassed the calibrated budget (920s on that box) How it solves it: - Split the module fixture into `rig` (STRICT, 5s healthcheck) and `suspension_rig` (LENIENT) - Only `test_each_worker_alone_sends_the_provider_file_ids` suspends workers, so only it uses LENIENT - Dropped the fixed 480s override so the module follows `_support/budget.py` calibration like other owned-proxy tests - Both kills, replacement readiness waits and every assertion are unchanged Triage verdict is a test/harness bug, not a product or infra fault. The CI proxy log for gw11 shows both killed workers were reaped and replaced (`Child process [102829] died`, then `Started server process [269067]` ready about 280s after test start). The harness and lockfile have no diff between the last passing sha `d10de278c1` and the failing `457365f`, the combination came in with #46552 ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup is local PostgreSQL and Redis per `tests/integration/README.md`, two-worker owned proxies built by the same `_rig` the test uses. The script suspends each worker for 0.8s so the supervisor has a ping in flight, SIGKILLs it, then measures kill to reap and kill to replacement readiness. LENIENT was scaled to this box's calibration (36s), STRICT stays 5s
real_proxy_healthcheck_proof.py ```python import time, threading from pathlib import Path from integration._support.process import WorkerHealthcheck, WorkerKill, healthcheck_seconds from integration.compatibility.test_fine_tuning_managed_files_chaos import _rig root = Path("real-proxy-proof"); root.mkdir(exist_ok=True) for healthcheck in (WorkerHealthcheck.LENIENT, WorkerHealthcheck.STRICT): with _rig(root / healthcheck.value, healthcheck) as rig: before = sorted(rig.owned.worker_pids()) for pid in before: victim, before_kill = rig.owned._victim(pid) victim.suspend(); time.sleep(0.8) started = time.monotonic(); reaped = [] def observe_reap(): while victim.is_running(): time.sleep(0.01) reaped.append(time.monotonic() - started) t = threading.Thread(target=observe_reap, daemon=True); t.start() WorkerKill(victim, threading.Event())() replacement = rig.owned._replacement_of(victim, before_kill) t.join(timeout=1) print(f"{healthcheck.value}: healthcheck={healthcheck_seconds(healthcheck)}s killed={pid} " f"replacement={replacement} kill_to_reap={reaped[0]:.3f}s " f"kill_to_replacement_ready={time.monotonic() - started:.3f}s") ```
### Before (072290e78f, fixture used LENIENT for the kill test) ```text lenient: healthcheck=36s killed=14213 replacement=14539 kill_to_reap=35.327s kill_to_replacement_ready=46.494s lenient: healthcheck=36s killed=14214 replacement=14756 kill_to_reap=35.464s kill_to_replacement_ready=50.644s ``` Each kill waits out the full lenient healthcheck. At CI's 262s that is two waits over 480s, which is the reported timeout inside `_wait_until_reaped` ### After (41e0d91295, kill test uses STRICT) ```text strict: healthcheck=5s killed=15080 replacement=15287 kill_to_reap=4.517s kill_to_replacement_ready=17.320s strict: healthcheck=5s killed=15081 replacement=15424 kill_to_reap=4.338s kill_to_replacement_ready=15.431s ``` Full module at the tip via `uv run python tests/integration/run.py extensions` filtered to this file, two pytest workers ```text 23.34s call tests/integration/compatibility/test_fine_tuning_managed_files_chaos.py::test_a_replaced_worker_still_sends_the_provider_file_ids ======================== 5 passed in 155.46s (0:02:35) ========================= execution complete=True passed=5 skipped=0 ``` Gates were `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `scripts/test_quality_gate.py --base origin/main`, all clean ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) ### Low - The suspension test now boots its own two-worker proxy, adding one proxy boot to the module - The original 480s CI timeout was not reproduced end to end locally, only the per-kill delay
--- --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Test harness only—no production code; adds one extra proxy boot for the suspension test. > > **Overview** > Refactors the fine-tuning managed-files chaos module so **proxy worker supervision matches each test**: shared setup is a `_rig` helper parameterized by `WorkerHealthcheck`, with **`rig` using STRICT** and a new **`suspension_rig` using LENIENT**. > > The worker **suspension** test now uses `suspension_rig`; the **kill-and-replace** test (and the rest) keep `rig`, avoiding long LENIENT healthcheck waits when workers are SIGKILL’d. The module-level **`pytest.mark.timeout(480)`** is removed so timeouts follow the integration budget calibration like other owned-proxy tests. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ef2a26698842c630fc4476cc8f4d0eff7b16bfa9. title: fix(types): build Usage schemas eagerly so parallel first requests cannot race
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

A burst of parallel requests hitting a freshly started proxy worker could fail some of them with an internal schema error while building the usage object. This makes the usage types build their validation schema once at import, so concurrent first requests can no longer race on it

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Parallel first requests on a fresh worker sometimes fail with `AttributeError`
- `Usage` builds its pydantic schema lazily, and concurrent rebuilds race

How it solves it:

- `Usage` and its two token-detail wrappers set `defer_build=False`
- New regression test in `tests/integration/sdk/test_usage_schema_build.py` forces the race in a fresh subprocess

## User Flow

Before: some requests in a burst against a freshly booted proxy worker fail

1. The admin starts or restarts the proxy
2. A client fires many POST /v1/chat/completions requests at once
3. A few come back as errors mentioning `type object 'Usage' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'`

After: the same burst succeeds for every request

1. The admin starts or restarts the proxy
2. A client fires many POST /v1/chat/completions requests at once
3. Every request returns 200 with a `usage` object

## Relevant issues

Seen in the scheduled integration run https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/42958083166/job/130317851934 in `tests/integration/observability/test_langtrace_delivery.py::test_langtrace_two_workers_deliver_every_burst_span_exactly_once`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The race is timing dependent, so the deterministic red/green proof is the regression test. It runs a fresh subprocess where eight threads construct each model at once, with a barrier holding them right before pydantic deletes the half built schema (falling back to a plain start barrier if that pydantic line ever changes). The live burst below did not reproduce the race on the base, so it shows the fix is safe under the real flow, not a natural reproduction

Shared setup. Two workers with `--reload`, one dedicated local Redis shared by `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`, database free (`DATABASE_URL` and `DIRECT_URL` unset), `LITELLM_RUST=0` and `LITELLM_RUST_FIRST=0` to exercise the Python path. Env vars `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `USAGE_RACE_MASTER_KEY`. Each boot waits for both workers' `Application startup complete`, then fires 24 simultaneous requests with no warm up, five fresh boots per revision

```sh
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6397 --save '' --appendonly no
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config usage_race_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4197
```

<details>
<summary>usage_race_config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: usage-race-haiku
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6397
  num_retries: 0
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/USAGE_RACE_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6397
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Runner and burst client, exactly as run</summary>

```python
import asyncio
import collections
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import httpx

ROOT = Path('/home/ubuntu')
LOGS = ROOT / 'usage_race_logs'
LOGS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
PYTHON = '/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python'
CONFIG = ROOT / 'usage_race_config.yaml'
KEY = 'sk-usage-race-local-only'
SECRET_VALUES = tuple(value for name, value in os.environ.items() if ('KEY' in name or 'TOKEN' in name) and len(value) > 10)


def redact(text):
    for value in SECRET_VALUES:
        text = text.replace(value, '[REDACTED]')
    return text


async def burst():
    event = asyncio.Event()
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=120, limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=24)) as client:
        async def request(index):
            await event.wait()
            try:
                response = await client.post(
                    'http://127.0.0.1:4197/v1/chat/completions',
                    headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + KEY},
                    json={'model': 'usage-race-haiku', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply with OK'}], 'max_tokens': 16},
                )
                body = response.json()
                return {'status': response.status_code, 'model': body.get('model'), 'usage': body.get('usage'),
                        'error': redact(str(body.get('error')))[:500] if response.status_code != 200 else None}
            except Exception as error:
                return {'status': 'exception', 'error': redact(str(error))}
        tasks = tuple(asyncio.create_task(request(index)) for index in range(24))
        event.set()
        return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)


def run(label, checkout, number):
    logfile = LOGS / f'{label}-{number}.log'
    environment = {**os.environ, 'PYTHONPATH': f'{checkout}:{checkout}/enterprise',
                   'LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP': 'True', 'USAGE_RACE_MASTER_KEY': KEY,
                   'LITELLM_RUST': '0', 'LITELLM_RUST_FIRST': '0'}
    environment.pop('DATABASE_URL', None)
    environment.pop('DIRECT_URL', None)
    command = [PYTHON, 'litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py', '--config', str(CONFIG), '--num_workers', '2',
               '--detailed_debug', '--reload', '--use_v2_migration_resolver', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '4197']
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=checkout, env=environment, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                               stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, start_new_session=True)
    def capture():
        with logfile.open('w') as stream:
            for line in process.stdout:
                stream.write(redact(line))
                stream.flush()
    reader = threading.Thread(target=capture)
    reader.start()
    try:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 180
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            text = logfile.read_text() if logfile.exists() else ''
            if text.count('Application startup complete.') >= 2:
                break
            if process.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError(f'{label} boot {number} exited {process.returncode}; see {logfile}')
            time.sleep(0.05)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f'{label} boot {number} startup timed out; see {logfile}')
        results = asyncio.run(burst())
        text = logfile.read_text()
        summary = {'revision': label, 'boot': number, 'requests': len(results),
                   'status_counts': dict(collections.Counter(str(result['status']) for result in results)),
                   'non_200': sum(result['status'] != 200 for result in results),
                   'schema_error_lines': sum('__pydantic_core_schema__' in line for line in text.splitlines()),
                   'worker_pids': sorted(set(re.findall(r'Started server process \[(\d+)\]', text))),
                   'errors': [result['error'] for result in results if result['status'] != 200],
                   'models': sorted(set(result.get('model') or '' for result in results))}
        (LOGS / f'{label}-{number}.json').write_text(json.dumps({'summary': summary, 'responses': results}, indent=2))
        print(json.dumps(summary), flush=True)
        return summary
    finally:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=30)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            process.wait()
        reader.join(timeout=10)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    redis = subprocess.Popen(['redis-server', '--bind', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '6397', '--save', '', '--appendonly', 'no'],
                             stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    try:
        for label, checkout in [('base', '/home/ubuntu/usage-schema-baseline'), ('tip', '/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm')]:
            for number in range(1, 6):
                run(label, checkout, number)
    finally:
        redis.terminate()
        redis.wait(timeout=10)
```

</details>

### Before (072290e78f27)

1. Regression probe on unfixed code

```text
RED exit 1
  File ".../pydantic/main.py", line 668, in model_rebuild
    delattr(cls, attr)
AttributeError: type object 'Usage' has no attribute '__pydantic_core_schema__'
```

2. Live burst, 5 fresh boots x 24 requests. 120 of 120 returned 200, zero `__pydantic_core_schema__` log lines (race did not trigger naturally)

### After (8671620eb313)


2. Live burst, 5 fresh boots x 24 requests. 120 of 120 returned 200 with a `usage` object, zero `__pydantic_core_schema__` log lines

</details>

3. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run pytest tests/integration/sdk/test_usage_schema_build.py tests/unit/types -q` gives 1972 passed, and `make check` passes

## Type

title: fix(bedrock): log invoke embedding replies as embedding responses
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Native Bedrock `/invoke` calls to the Titan embedding models returned the vector fine, but the success log handed that reply to the chat transformer, which looks for `results[0].outputText` and blew up, so the call logged no usage and no spend. This sends an embedding reply through the same transformer the `/embeddings` endpoint uses, which keeps the vector and the provider's `inputTextTokenCount`.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Native `/invoke` embedding replies crash the success log
- Every Titan embedding passthrough request bills $0
- Same failure as #14627, which went stale without a fix

How it solves it:

- Detect the vector shape on `invoke` replies before the chat path
- Reuse the embedding transformer the `/embeddings` endpoint uses
- Mark the call as an embedding call so it is priced as one

## User Flow

Before: the vector comes back, but the request never turns into a billable log line

1. The app sends POST `https://litellm-domain/bedrock/model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0/invoke` with `{"inputText": "hello"}`
2. It gets 200 with `{"embedding": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], "inputTextTokenCount": 20}`
3. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows that request with no token counts and $0 spend, because the success callback raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`

After: the same call logs the provider's own token count and real spend

1. The app sends the same POST
2. It gets the same 200 body, byte for byte
3. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows 20 prompt tokens and $0.0000004 for that request

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51455

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Recorded exception, per AGENTS.md eligibility: this is a mechanical fix to one branch of the passthrough logging path, so focused checks stand in for a live run. Recorded at `4dad0bc513b75029e2a274143536bf50a7e56a4d`, scope is the two files in the diff, and the runs below are that commit before the patch and with it.

Rationale for skipping the live run: reproducing needs a real Bedrock embedding call and this environment has no AWS credentials. The reply body is the documented provider shape, served over a real socket so the logging path parses bytes rather than a hand-built object.

**Focused tests, before the patch (the new cases fail):**

```
$ pytest tests/unit/llms/bedrock/passthrough/test_bedrock_passthrough_transformation.py -k "titan_embedding or generation_reply_is_still" -q
FAILED ...test_invoke_titan_embedding_reply_is_priced_from_the_provider_token_count
FAILED ...test_invoke_titan_embedding_reply_is_logged_as_an_embedding_response[amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0]
FAILED ...test_invoke_titan_embedding_reply_is_logged_as_an_embedding_response[bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0]
3 failed, 1 passed, 114 deselected
```

**Focused tests, after the patch:**

```
$ pytest tests/unit/llms/bedrock/passthrough/test_bedrock_passthrough_transformation.py -k "titan_embedding or generation_reply_is_still" -q
4 passed, 114 deselected
```

**Whole test files touched or next to the change:**

```
$ pytest tests/unit/llms/bedrock/passthrough/ -q
344 passed

$ pytest tests/unit/llms/bedrock/ -q
4350 passed, 1 skipped
```

**Same failure and fix through the logging seam**, a local server answering the `/invoke` body and `Logging.normalize_logging_result` run on the response it gets back:

```
Before: logged: RAISED BedrockError: Error processing={"embedding": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], "inputTextTokenCount": 20},
        Received error='NoneType' object is not subscriptable
        spend:  lost, the success callback never ran

After:  logged: EmbeddingResponse
        vector: [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]
        usage:  prompt=20 completion=0
        cost:   4e-07
        expect: 4e-07
```

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Only the `{"embedding": [...]}` shape takes the new path: Titan text v1/v2 and titan-embed-image
- Cohere embed on `/invoke` still goes down the chat path and logs nothing, same as before this PR
- A model the embedding transformer does not know falls back to the old chat path, so it fails the way it does today instead of failing differently
- Assumed, not tested live: the proxy reaches this with the deployment's model string, with or without the `bedrock/` prefix, so the parametrized test covers both

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: feat(proxy): customer budget rollup, reset on the budget row's window, named templates, team overrides, multi-window limits and pause_allow_increase
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Rolls the customer budget work from #51562, #51569, #51565 and #51577 into one branch, fixes what their reviews found, and adds the `pause_allow_increase` cap policy with an admin-reviewed increase request queue. Co-authored by Tin for the parts absorbed from #51565 and #51577.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

</details>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer rows kept their own reset clock, so rows on one template reset at different times
- Budget rows had no name, orgs still used `budget_ids`, teams had no override, members no `parent_org_id`
- Reusable customer budgets could not hold a monthly and an annual cap at once
- Customer creation in the dashboard could not define member budget groups
- A paused member had no way to ask for more, and the error gave no next step
- Reset rollover used the template's cap, not the member's effective one, and read every member at once

How it solves it:

- Customer orgs, teams and members reset on their budget row's window (from #51562)
- `name` on budget rows, `budget_template_ids`, team overrides with expiry, member `parent_org_id` and `parent_team_ids` (from #51569)
- `budget_limits` on `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`, enforced for customer scopes through the existing window counters (from #51565)
- Customer-create dialog with named member budget groups (from #51577)
- `cap_policy` on budgets; `pause_allow_increase` opens `POST /management/v1/customer_budget_increase_requests`, reviewed by admins the way MCP and skill submissions are. A key pinned to a `customer_org_id` can only file for that org's members, every request needs a future `expires_at`, one pending request per member, and an approval never revives an expired override or outlives an active one
- Teams and members reset in keyset pages before the cascade, each row against its own effective cap, each page committed on its own
- Resubmitting a template's duration keeps its reset clock

Intentional product change: a template edit that repeats the same `budget_duration` no longer pushes the window out; a changed duration still starts a new window. Customer team and member resets now land in their own commits ahead of the budget row's window advance.

## User Flow

Before: a member on a $100/month template who hits the cap is told only that the budget is exceeded, and the admin has no queue to grant more

1. Admin creates the org with POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations and a `monthly` template, `max_budget: 100`, `budget_duration: 30d`
2. The member's requests with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id` run until spend reaches 100
3. The next POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions returns 400 `ExceededBudget: customer_member=... over budget. Spend=100.0, Budget=100`
4. The admin edits the template through PATCH .../default_budgets/{id} with the same `budget_duration`; the window silently moves out another 30 days with the spend still at 100

After: the template says what a paused member can do, the member's integration files a request, the admin approves it from a queue, and the member is unblocked under a temporary cap

1. Admin creates the same org, now with `"cap_policy": "pause_allow_increase"` and `"budget_limits": [{"budget_duration": "30d", "max_budget": 100}, {"budget_duration": "1y", "max_budget": 1000}]` on the template
2. At the cap, POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions returns 400 `ExceededBudget: ... Request a temporary increase through POST /management/v1/customer_budget_increase_requests.`
3. The integration sends POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_budget_increase_requests with `customer_member_id`, `requested_max_budget: 250`, `expires_at`, `reason`; 201 with `"status": "pending_review"`
4. The admin lists GET https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_budget_increase_requests?status=pending_review and calls PUT .../{request_id}/approve; 200 `"status": "approved"`, the member's `budget_override.max_budget` is 250 until `expires_at`
5. The member's next chat completion returns 200; a second approve of the same request returns 409

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proof against a running proxy is pending and will replace this section before review is requested. Focused suites at the tip: `tests/unit/proxy/common_utils/test_reset_budget_job.py`, `tests/unit/repositories/test_unit_of_work.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/management_helpers/test_customer_hierarchy.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/test_customers.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/test_customer_budget_increase_requests.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_hierarchy_auth.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking/test_customer_window_accounting.py`, all green.

## Type

🆕 New Feature
🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Severe

- Migrations `20261113120000` (two), `20261113130000` and `20261113140000` run at boot: column adds, a rename, one new table, no row rewrites

### Medium

- No dashboard page for the increase request queue yet, admins use the API
- `cap_policy` only shapes the customer hierarchy error; keys and teams keep today's message
- Workers without a Redis lease could still clear a customer org's spend twice, as every other cascade table on main today

### Low

- The windows check on customer scopes is new in this branch; keys and teams keep their existing checkers

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: feat(ui): show and pick vector stores for access groups
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description you could only add vector stores to an access group through the api, and the dashboard didn't show them on the group or the team. now the group forms have a vector stores tab, the group page lists its stores by name, and a team's page lists the stores it gets from its groups.
Details ## TLDR problem: - access groups can hold vector stores, but only through the api - the dashboard has no control for them - it doesn't show them on a group or on a team either fix: - the create and edit forms get a Vector Stores tab - the group page lists the group's stores by name, and the groups table counts them - a team's page lists the stores it gets from its groups, marked with the group - the edit form sends the stores only after that tab was opened, like the other tabs Intentional product change: the create form is 28px wider, the same width as the edit form. the tab rows of both forms and of the group page wrap when the window is too narrow for one row, and the group page's tab row is 3px taller. one more tab doesn't fit the old widths. nothing is removed. ## User Flow before: an admin can't put a vector store in an access group from the dashboard, or see which stores a team gets from a group 1. admin opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=access-groups` and clicks Create Access Group 2. the form has tabs for General Info, Models, MCP Servers, Agents and Skills. there's no place to pick a vector store 3. the only way is `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/access_group` with `access_vector_store_ids` 4. the team's page under `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams` then says "No vector stores configured", though the group limits the team to that store after: the admin picks the stores in the form, and sees them on the group and on the team 1. admin opens the same page and clicks Create Access Group 2. the form has a Vector Stores tab. they pick `HR policies (store-b)` and click Create Group 3. the groups table shows the new group with 1 vector store, and the group's page lists `HR policies` under Vector Stores 4. the team's page lists the group's store under Vector Stores, marked `(access group)` 5. the edit form has the same tab with the saved stores. removing them all and saving empties the list ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2937 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`.
