title: fix(proxy): alert on customer org, customer team, and customer member budgets
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Triggers webhook alerts when customers hit their budget limits 

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer org, customer team and customer member crossings need notifications
- Daily dedupe expiry can repeat alerts within a monthly budget period
- Replica lag can hide the final crossing

How it solves it:

- Emit frozen events through registered custom loggers after durable spend commits
- POST raw JSON through a configurable generic webhook
- Claim each event by event type, customer scope, entity ID and period in Redis
- Keep finite claims through budget_reset_at, rounded up to a whole second
- Keep lifetime claims for 100 years instead of inheriting a short cache default
- Read committed spend from writer_db

Intentional product change: customer budget thresholds emit generic webhook events when enabled. No Slack settings are required.

The cumulative PR diff touches neither `litellm/integrations/SlackAlerting/` nor `litellm/types/integrations/slack_alerting.py`. The existing generic API logger expects request payloads, so this uses a small non-request webhook logger.

`CustomLogger.async_on_customer_budget_event` defaults to a no-op. `CustomerBudgetAlerting.detect_committed_batch` handles committed batches. `emit` deduplicates and fans out to interested custom loggers. Buffered spend writing and accounting delivery call this entrypoint after commit.

## User Flow

Before, daily claim expiry can repeat a monthly alert.

1. Configure a webhook and monthly customer org, customer team and customer member budgets
2. Send paid Responses, Chat Completions and Messages requests across the thresholds
3. Observe one soft and one hard event per customer scope
4. Continue paid requests after a day and observe repeated events

After, claims last through the budget period.

1. Configure a webhook and monthly customer org, customer team and customer member budgets
2. Send paid Responses, Chat Completions and Messages requests across the thresholds
3. Observe one soft and one hard event per customer scope
4. Continue requests and restart both workers without receiving another event for that period

The old daily-expiry failure was reproduced with a controlled clock against the previous implementation at `a129fa748a1286c57ac2f0af2d3091bdac25c5aa`. The new live run checks repeated paid bursts, worker restarts and actual Redis TTLs. It does not simulate a month passing live.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Tested commit `7618135e447ffddbc5574ec3a5e58dbcd5dc83a2`.

POST requests to `http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` used the same customer org and customer member headers. All three initial bursts sent 20 parallel requests, split 7 Responses, 7 Chat Completions and 6 Messages. Each burst returned 20 HTTP 200 responses with real provider costs.

The first crossing delivered exactly six events. The next two paid bursts left every receiver count at one. Restarting the supervisor replaced both workers, then another 20-request burst returned HTTP 422 and left all counts unchanged.

| Event | First burst | Second burst | Third burst | After worker restart |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| customer_member/budget_crossed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| customer_member/soft_budget_crossed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| customer_org/budget_crossed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| customer_org/soft_budget_crossed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| customer_team/budget_crossed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| customer_team/soft_budget_crossed | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Total | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 |

Workers `417912` and `417913` both served paid requests. Restarted workers `418681` and `418682` both served the final requests. The runner maps each response's client TCP port to its serving worker immediately after the response.

Customer org, customer team and customer member spend each matched the total paid response cost, **0.005204**. Every Redis claim had value **3**, proving the same event was detected on three committed paid batches but delivered once. Every claim retained **2,591,908 seconds**, nearly 30 days.

![Receiver counts remain unchanged across paid bursts and restarts](/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-counts.png)

The screenshot renders `file:///home/ubuntu/pr2-period-counts.html` from the captured results. Raw events are saved in `/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-receiver.json`. Full stage results, endpoint responses and worker PIDs are in `/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-live.json`.

## Exact configuration and replay

Required environment variables are `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. PostgreSQL listens on 5432. Shared Redis listens on 6383. The HTTP receiver listens on 8808 and appends raw POST bodies to `/home/ubuntu/customer-qa-webhooks.jsonl`.

The exact proxy config is below. There is no `alerting: ["webhook"]`.

```yaml
environment_variables:
  CUSTOMER_BUDGET_WEBHOOK_HEADERS: '{"X-QA-Proof":"customer-budget-period"}'
  CUSTOMER_BUDGET_WEBHOOK_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8808
general_settings:
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6383
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
litellm_settings:
  callbacks:
  - customer_budget_webhook
  drop_params: true
model_list:
- litellm_params:
    api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
    model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
  model_name: qa-gpt
- litellm_params:
    api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
  model_name: qa-claude
router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6383
```

The normal `callbacks` list enables the webhook. URL and headers above are environment configuration. Alternatively, `callback_specific_params.customer_budget_webhook` accepts `endpoint` and `headers`.

The proxy used this command from `/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm-alerts-review/litellm/proxy`, with the checkout and its enterprise directory in PYTHONPATH:

```bash
../../.venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli \
  --config /home/ubuntu/pr2-period-config.yaml --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4000
```

Reload is omitted to retain two serving workers.

The fixture sets soft budget **0.0000000005**, max budget **0.000000001** and duration **30d** at every customer scope. A setup-only SQL transaction assigns the same reset timestamp, 30 days ahead, to the three newly created QA rows. It does not change any other customer's records or spend. This makes the live finite-period TTL check explicit instead of waiting for reset scheduling.

<details>
<summary>Receiver code</summary>

```python
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        body=self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('content-length','0')))
        with Path('/home/ubuntu/customer-qa-webhooks.jsonl').open('ab') as f: f.write(body+b'\n')
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'ok')
HTTPServer(('0.0.0.0',8808),Handler).serve_forever()
```

Create the empty log with `touch /home/ubuntu/customer-qa-webhooks.jsonl`, then run `python3 /home/ubuntu/customer-qa-webhook.py`. It has no authentication and is only a local QA receiver.

</details>

```python
def manage(method, path, body=None, expected=200):
    response = client.request(method,base+path,headers=admin,json=body)
    assert response.status_code==expected, response.text
    return response.json()

def received():
    return [json.loads(line) for line in receiver.read_bytes()[offset:].decode().splitlines() if name in line]

def counts():
    return dict(sorted(Counter(p['scope']+'/'+p['event'] for p in received()).items()))

def start(label):
    log_path = Path('/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-proxy-'+label+'.log')
    log = log_path.open('w')
    logs.append(log)
    process = subprocess.Popen([str(root/'.venv/bin/python'),'-m','litellm.proxy.proxy_cli',
        '--config',str(config_path),'--num_workers','2','--detailed_debug',
        '--use_v2_migration_resolver','--port','4000'],cwd=root/'litellm/proxy',env=env,
        stdout=log,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,start_new_session=True)
    processes.append(process)
    for _ in range(180):
        assert process.poll() is None, 'Proxy exited. See '+str(log_path)
        try:
            if client.get(base+'/health/readiness',headers=admin).status_code==200 and log_path.read_text().count('Application startup complete')>=2:
                return process
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            pass
        time.sleep(1)
    raise RuntimeError('Two workers did not become ready')

def stop(process):
    if process.poll() is None:
        os.killpg(process.pid,signal.SIGTERM)
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=30)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            os.killpg(process.pid,signal.SIGKILL)
            process.wait()

def worker_ports(process):
    return {connection.raddr.port:str(worker.pid)
        for worker in psutil.Process(process.pid).children(recursive=True)
        for connection in worker.net_connections(kind='tcp')
        if connection.laddr.port==4000 and connection.status=='ESTABLISHED'}

def connect(process):
    connections = [httpx.Client(timeout=180) for _ in range(20)]
    clients.extend(connections)
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=20) as pool:
        statuses = list(pool.map(lambda c:c.get(base+'/health/readiness',headers=admin).status_code,connections))
    ports = worker_ports(process)
    assert set(statuses)=={200} and len(set(ports.values()))==2, ports
    return connections

def post(item):
    index, connection = item
    endpoint = ('responses','chat/completions','messages')[index%3]
    body = {'model':'qa-claude' if endpoint=='messages' else 'qa-gpt'}
    if endpoint=='responses':
        body.update(input='Reply only OK',max_output_tokens=64)
    else:
        body.update(messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Reply only OK'}],
                    **({'max_tokens':64} if endpoint=='messages' else {'max_completion_tokens':64}))
    response = connection.post(base+'/v1/'+endpoint,headers=headers,json=body)
    assert response.status_code in (200,422), response.text
    address = response.extensions['network_stream'].get_extra_info('client_addr')
    cost = float(response.headers.get('x-litellm-response-cost',0))
    assert response.status_code!=200 or cost>0, 'Paid response cost missing'
    ports = worker_ports(process)
    return {'endpoint':endpoint,'status':response.status_code,'cost':cost,'client_port':address[1],
            'worker_pid':ports[address[1]]}

def snapshot(label, responses, process, expected_spend):
    for _ in range(240):
        org = manage('GET','/management/v1/customer_organizations/'+name)
        if org['spend']+1e-9>=expected_spend and len(received())==6:
            break
        time.sleep(.5)
    assert abs(org['spend']-expected_spend)<1e-9, (org['spend'],expected_spend)
    team = manage('GET','/management/v1/customer_teams/'+name+':default')
    member = manage('GET','/management/v1/customer_members/'+name+'-member')
    assert abs(team['spend']-org['spend'])<1e-9 and abs(member['spend']-org['spend'])<1e-9
    observed = counts()
    assert len(observed)==6 and set(observed.values())=={1}, observed
    mapped = responses
    assert len({row['worker_pid'] for row in mapped})==2
    if label=='first_crossing':
        assert all(any(row['endpoint']==endpoint and row['status']==200 for row in mapped)
                   for endpoint in ('responses','chat/completions','messages'))
        assert len({row['worker_pid'] for row in mapped if row['status']==200})==2
    stage = {'stage':label,'counts':observed,'total_events':sum(observed.values()),
             'spend':org['spend'],'workers':sorted({row['worker_pid'] for row in mapped}),
             'response_counts':dict(Counter(str(row['status']) for row in mapped)), 'requests':mapped}
    result['stages'].append(stage)
    Path('/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-live.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in stage.items() if k!='requests'}),flush=True)

try:
    process = start('initial')
    connections = connect(process)
    key = manage('POST','/key/generate',{'models':['qa-gpt','qa-claude']})['key']
    budget = {'max_budget':1e-9,'soft_budget':5e-10,'budget_duration':'30d'}
    manage('POST','/management/v1/customer_organizations',{'customer_org_id':name,'alias':name,'budget':budget,
            'default_budgets':[{'name':'default','is_default':True,**budget}]},201)
    manage('POST','/management/v1/customer_teams',{'customer_team_id':name+':default','alias':'Customer team',
            'parent_org_id':name,'budget':budget},201)
    manage('POST','/management/v1/customer_members',{'customer_member_id':name+'-member',
            'alias':'Customer member','parent_team_id':name+':default'},201)
    db = urlparse(env['DATABASE_URL'])
    sql = 'BEGIN; '+ ' '.join('UPDATE "'+table+'" SET budget_reset_at=NOW()+INTERVAL \'30 days\' WHERE '+column+"='"+entity+"';"
        for table,column,entity in [('LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable','customer_org_id',name),
           ('LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable','customer_team_id',name+':default'),
           ('LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable','customer_member_id',name+'-member')])+' COMMIT;'
    subprocess.run(['psql','-X','-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1','-h',db.hostname,'-U',db.username,'-d',db.path.lstrip('/'),'-c',sql],
        env={**os.environ,'PGPASSWORD':db.password},capture_output=True,text=True,check=True)
    headers = {'Authorization':'Bearer '+key,'x-litellm-customer-org-alias':name,
               'x-litellm-customer-member-id':name+'-member'}
    spend = 0.0
    for label in ('first_crossing','repeat_burst_1','repeat_burst_2'):
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=20) as pool:
            responses = list(pool.map(post,enumerate(connections)))
        spend += sum(row['cost'] for row in responses)
        snapshot(label,responses,process,spend)
    for connection in connections:
        connection.close()
    stop(process)
    process = start('restarted')
    connections = connect(process)
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=20) as pool:
        responses = list(pool.map(post,enumerate(connections)))
    spend += sum(row['cost'] for row in responses)
    snapshot('after_both_workers_restarted',responses,process,spend)
    result['events'] = received()
    result['claims'] = []
    for event in result['events']:
        identity = json.dumps((event['event'],event['scope'],event['entity_id'],event['period']))
        digest = hashlib.sha256(identity.encode()).hexdigest()
        keys = list(rdb.scan_iter(match='*customer_budget_alerts:'+digest))
        assert len(keys)==1,keys
        ttl = rdb.ttl(keys[0])
        assert ttl>86400,ttl
        result['claims'].append({'event':event['event'],'scope':event['scope'],
                                 'value':rdb.get(keys[0]),'ttl_seconds':ttl,'period':event['period']})
    Path('/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-live.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
    Path('/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-receiver.json').write_text(json.dumps(result['events'],indent=2))
    print(json.dumps({'claims':result['claims'],'result':'PASS'}),flush=True)
finally:
    for connection in clients:
        connection.close()
    for process in processes:
        stop(process)
    for log in logs:
        log.close()
    client.close()
```

</details>

The exact local runner is retained at `/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-live.py` and its output at `/home/ubuntu/pr2-period-live.log`.

## Checks

The new regression exercises both a monthly period and lifetime spending. It advances the clock past two days, then to the last microsecond of the monthly period or one year into lifetime spending. The old 24-hour implementation delivered six events instead of two in each case.

```text
2 failed, 17 deselected in 2.24s
```

Mapped customer event, webhook, spend writer and accounting worker suites passed:

```text
279 passed, 11 warnings in 53.74s
```

These include the lagging-replica regression for all three customer scopes. Replica spend is zero, writer spend is two and the cap is one. The writer lookup still emits the crossing.

`make lint` exited 0:

```text
OK: no strict rule grew past its merge-base count (base origin/main)
OK: no LIT rule grew past its merge-base count (base origin/main)
OK: no OA rule grew past its merge-base count (base origin/main)
OK: no TQ rule grew past its merge-base count (base origin/main)
OK: every basedpyright rule is within its ceiling (94881 errors total, base 32cb45a3d887)
```

Commands were:

```bash
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking/test_customer_budget_alerts.py \
  tests/unit/integrations/test_customer_budget_webhook.py \
  tests/unit/proxy/db/test_db_spend_update_writer.py \
  tests/unit/accounting/test_worker.py -q
make lint

```

The first live attempt lost TCP-to-worker attribution after idle connections closed during spend settlement. The runner now records attribution immediately after each response. The final run above passed.

Replied on the prior Slack escaping discussion that Slack is no longer touched.

## Type

## Caveats

- A webhook failure is logged without replaying committed spend or retrying the same period claim
- This branch predates the merged hard-cap freshness work, so cached admission allowed the later paid bursts. Cold workers denied the final burst
- Local artifact paths must be copied with the proof to view screenshots elsewhere

title: fix(mcp): treat the mcp_all scope as a wildcard any grant covers
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description users reconnecting datadog mcp got stuck looping between datadog's allow screen and the connect page, and ended on "Authentication incomplete". we ask datadog for its one catch-all permission, mcp_all, and it answers with a few hundred detailed ones, so we never found the one we asked for. now whatever comes back counts for mcp_all, so they connect in one go, and sign-ins that don't ask for mcp_all work the same as before
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/387b97e454674d06b6725e368620e953 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/387b97e454674d06b6725e368620e953?variant=devin Requested by: @shrey-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - datadog mcp sign-in loops between datadog and the connect page - datadog answers `mcp_all` with about 300 detailed scopes, never `mcp_all` - the next try re-asks them all and the cookie passes 4096 bytes - the browser drops it and the user sees "Authentication incomplete" How it solves it: - any saved grant that isn't empty covers `mcp_all` - a request for `mcp_all` doesn't re-ask the old grant - other scopes in that request are still checked by name - a request without `mcp_all` works exactly like before Intentional product change: a client that asks for `mcp_all` now counts as connected with any saved grant for that server, also on a server that lists other scopes next to `mcp_all`, so the user isn't sent back to consent. the provider still decides what the token can do ```diff connect check, for each requested scope granted if the saved grant has it + or it is mcp_all and the saved grant is not empty reconnect asks the provider for - the old grant plus the new request + only the new request, when it asks for mcp_all + the old grant plus the new request, otherwise ``` ## User Flow Before: a user whose datadog mcp sign-in expired can't reconnect from their mcp client 1. their mcp client opens https://litellm-domain/authorize/mcp-session for the datadog server, and the browser sends them to datadog 2. they approve on datadog and land on https://litellm-domain/ui/connect, which still shows Connect 3. they click Connect, approve on datadog again, and land on "Authentication incomplete. You can close this window." 4. every later try ends the same way, so the client never gets signed in After: the same user finishes in one pass 1. their mcp client opens https://litellm-domain/authorize/mcp-session for the datadog server, and the browser sends them to datadog 2. they approve on datadog and land on https://litellm-domain/ui/connect, which now shows Finish connecting 3. they click Finish connecting and the mcp client is signed in ## Affected release regression since v1.107.0-rc.1, from #45886 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix real datadog mcp server on app.datadoghq.com, real chrome, same clicks on both proxies. both times datadog answered `mcp_all` with 229 scopes and no `mcp_all` ### Before (865eb25555) 1. mcp client opens the sign-in link, datadog asks to approve (1 scope requested) 2. after approving, litellm still shows Connect ![connect page still shows Connect](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..y0xdahEIDRjOgtaP5MZudawwiwd-IxuE4ces0Esz26E) 3. clicking Connect re-asks datadog for 230 scopes, the sign-in cookie hits 7901 bytes, and after approving again the browser ends here ![Authentication incomplete](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..eKRaOVOQd7W2kA5BZvILM4V6U5CFbY6ES93vrwHM33o) ### After (f3f7151394) 1. same sign-in link, same datadog consent (1 scope requested) 2. after approving, litellm shows Finish connecting ![connect page shows Finish connecting](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..SujpAHPu7XDyHARM-E-KVL5oH_6m9dg7_T3B5TpCG-Y) 3. clicking Finish connecting lands on the mcp client's callback with a code, no second trip to datadog ![mcp client callback](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..89aZwNXz1UhssX6jxSdzylGmMDBwzuNIR3ikVuND6Oc) 4. the client then swaps the code for a token (200) and `tools/list` through the proxy returns 37 datadog tools
how to rerun the real datadog run each proxy runs from its own worktree with its own empty postgres db ```bash PYTHONPATH="$WORKTREE:$WORKTREE/enterprise" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config dd-config.yaml --port 4010 --num_workers 1 ``` `dd-config.yaml` is only `master_key`, `database_url` and `store_model_in_db: true`. the client was registered with datadog through `POST https://app.datadoghq.com/api/v2/oauth2/register` with redirect `http://localhost:4010/callback`, which issued a public client with no secret. the server was added with ```bash curl -X POST localhost:4010/v1/mcp/server -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "server_id": "datadog_real", "server_name": "datadog_real", "url": "https://mcp.datadoghq.com/api/unstable/mcp-server/mcp", "transport": "http", "auth_type": "oauth2", "oauth2_flow": "authorization_code", "authorization_url": "https://app.datadoghq.com/oauth2/v1/authorize", "token_url": "https://app.datadoghq.com/api/v2/oauth2/token", "credentials": {"client_id": "", "scopes": ["mcp_all"]} }' ``` an internal user with access to `datadog_real` then follows the flow above in chrome, starting from `/authorize/mcp-session?scope=mcp_all&resource=http://localhost:4010/mcp/datadog_real` with a client registered at the proxy's `/register`
earlier run against a local datadog stand-in, plus the unit-level check the proxy is the `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.0` image, signed into the ui as an internal user. before is that image as shipped. after is the same container with 2 source files copied over v1.108.0's copies. those 2 files are v1.108.0's own plus #50717, which this sits on, plus this pr's code lines (on v1.108.0 they live under `_experimental/`). a docstring was reworded after the run and no code changed, so the tested code lines are the ones at f3f7151394 the provider is a local stand-in for datadog's oauth server on 127.0.0.1. it publishes only `mcp_all`, approves right away, and answers the token call with 244 detailed scopes and no `mcp_all`, the reply shape a real datadog sign-in returned a script registers as an mcp client, then headless chrome opens the client's sign-in link and clicks through the real connect page, so chrome applies its own cookie limit. the script answers the client's own callback url with a one line page, so the last screenshot shows where the browser ends up
how to rerun it before, the stock image. i used a v1.108.0 container that was already running on 127.0.0.1:4002 with its own postgres, and this starts one like it ```bash docker run --rm --name litellm-proof -p 127.0.0.1:4002:4000 -v $PWD/config.yaml:/app/config.yaml \ -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY -e LITELLM_SALT_KEY -e DATABASE_URL \ ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.0 --config=/app/config.yaml --port 4000 ``` after, the same container with the 2 patched files copied in ```bash D=/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server docker cp oauth_utils.py litellm-proof:$D/oauth_utils.py docker cp discoverable_endpoints.py litellm-proof:$D/discoverable_endpoints.py docker restart litellm-proof ``` the mcp server, registered once as the proxy admin ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4002/v1/mcp/server -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{ "server_id": "ddfake_repro", "server_name": "ddfake_repro", "url": "http://host.docker.internal:9311/mcp", "transport": "http", "auth_type": "oauth2", "oauth2_flow": "authorization_code", "authorization_url": "http://127.0.0.1:9311/authorize", "token_url": "http://host.docker.internal:9311/token", "credentials": {"client_id": "fake-client", "client_secret": "fake-secret", "scopes": ["mcp_all"]} }' ``` the stand-in provider, run as `python fake_datadog.py 9311`. `scopes.txt` next to it holds one datadog scope name per line ```python """Local stand-in for Datadog's OAuth server: asked for mcp_all, it grants a long list of granular scopes. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Logs each request's path and scope length to stdout. """ import json import pathlib import secrets import sys import time import urllib.parse from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer PORT = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 9311 GRANT_SIZE = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 300 REAL = [l.strip() for l in (pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "scopes.txt").read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()] AVG = round(sum(map(len, REAL)) / len(REAL)) PADDED = REAL + [f"{REAL[i % len(REAL)]}_{i}"[:AVG] for i in range(GRANT_SIZE - len(REAL))] GRANTED = " ".join(dict.fromkeys(PADDED[:GRANT_SIZE])) def log(msg: str) -> None: print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True) class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def log_message(self, *args: object) -> None: pass def _json(self, status: int, body: dict) -> None: raw = json.dumps(body).encode() self.send_response(status) self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(raw) def do_GET(self) -> None: url = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path) q = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(url.query)) if url.path == "/authorize": scope = q.get("scope", "") log(f"AUTHORIZE scope has {len(scope.split())} names ({len(scope)} chars), mcp_all={'mcp_all' in scope.split()}") target = q["redirect_uri"] + ("&" if "?" in q["redirect_uri"] else "?") + urllib.parse.urlencode( {"code": "fake-code-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(8), "state": q.get("state", "")} ) self.send_response(302) self.send_header("Location", target) self.end_headers() return log(f"GET {url.path} -> 404") self._json(404, {"error": "not_found"}) def do_POST(self) -> None: length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0) form = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(self.rfile.read(length).decode())) if self.path.startswith("/token"): log(f"TOKEN grant_type={form.get('grant_type')} -> granting {len(GRANTED.split())} scopes, no mcp_all") self._json( 200, { "access_token": "fake-dd-access-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(16), "refresh_token": "fake-dd-refresh-" + secrets.token_urlsafe(16), "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "scope": GRANTED, }, ) return log(f"POST {self.path} -> 404") self._json(404, {"error": "not_found"}) log(f"fake Datadog on 127.0.0.1:{PORT}, grants {len(GRANTED.split())} scopes ({len(GRANTED)} chars)") HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Handler).serve_forever() ``` the browser run, `python shoot.py before 4 --reset` and `python shoot.py after 4 --reset`. `token.txt` next to it holds the ui session token from `POST /v2/login` ```python """Drives a real headless Chrome through LiteLLM's Connect page for the Datadog-like server and takes screenshots. usage: shoot.py

title: feat(ui): create customers with member budget groups
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## Dependency

**Merge blocked on #51510's customer budget-template API.** Current main and the published #51510 revision reject `budget_limits` in `OrganizationCreate.default_budgets`. This UI-only PR deliberately exposes that missing contract through TypeScript. Rebase after the backend and generated types land, then verify customer creation end to end.

This is the smaller customer-creation alternative to #51516. It contains six UI/test files with 655 additions and 46 deletions. It adds no migrations, backend enforcement, approval flow, or cap-policy controls. #51516 remains open and unchanged.

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer creation cannot configure reusable member budget groups.

How it solves it:

- Collect named groups with monthly and annual budget amounts.
- Select the default group for new members.
- Submit groups and customer limits in one creation request.

Intentional product change: customer creation asks for a display name, an optional customer ID, and editable member budget groups. This smaller version does not include the cap-policy selector from #51516.

## User Flow

Before: `/ui/customers` only collects a customer ID and display alias.

1. Open `/ui/customers` and choose Create Customer.
2. Enter the customer's ID and display alias.
3. Create the customer without configuring member budget groups.

Intended after, once #51510 supplies the required API:

1. Open `/ui/customers` and choose Create Customer.
2. Enter a name and optionally an ID, aggregate budget, and rate limits.
3. Edit named groups, monthly/annual amounts, and the default group.
4. Create the customer and its groups together.

The form retains entered values after a failed request and resets after a successful request. Empty amounts omit that cap, and zero remains a valid cap. Client-side validation checks group names, limits, and default selection.

## Validation

The 24 focused tests passed across the payload builder, real dialog component tree, and customer-page integration. Network calls are stubbed in integration tests; this is not live proof.

```sh
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npx vitest run   'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/customerOrganizationForm.test.ts'   'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/CreateCustomerDialog.integration.test.tsx'   'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/page.integration.test.tsx'
```

Four deliberate regressions were caught: dropping the annual limit, ignoring the selected default, dropping a zero amount, and accepting duplicate names.

The repository dashboard lint stage passed, including Prettier, ESLint, and all lint budgets, with `make -o bootstrap check-inner` using installed dashboard dependencies. The initial `make check` bootstrap was stopped because it rebuilt unrelated native dependencies. `git diff --check` passed.

Production TypeScript checking currently reports the missing `BudgetTemplate.budget_limits` field. No type suppression or hand-edited generated schema was added.

Validation was run on the identical six-file patch before rebasing onto current main. The intervening main commits do not change these customer components, tests, or the budget-template contract. Current head: 769082500cc496a23afe2eac65b5c5e05a3f9581.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live customer-creation proof, screenshots, and a recording remain blocked on the API dependency above. No successful end-to-end behavior is claimed. The prior #51516 screenshots are not reused as proof of this revision.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests.
- [x] The focused tests covering this change pass locally.
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks.
- [x] My PR's scope is isolated to customer-creation UI.
- [ ] Automated reviews on the latest commit have completed and findings are addressed.

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### High

- Creation requires #51510's multiple-limit budget-template API and generated types.
- Until then, TypeScript fails and the backend rejects the payload.

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests and live proof cover the real customer workflow and its edge cases.

title: fix(budgets): enforce customer limits against shared spend counters
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Warm workers admit requests after customer budgets are exceeded.

How it solves it:

- Read shared spend counters for organizations, teams, and members.
- Increment counters for successful calls and billed failed attempts.
- Reseed counters from spend rows after resets or eviction.

## User Flow

Before, a developer sees successful requests after a customer's budget is exceeded.

1. Set an organization, team, or member budget below one request's cost.
2. Call `http://127.0.0.1:41485/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, or `/v1/messages` with organization alias and member ID.
3. Confirm recorded spend exceeds the budget using the customer API.
4. Repeat the request. Some warm workers still return 200.

After, workers enforce the recorded spend and respect subsequent budget edits.

1. Set an organization, team, or member budget below one request's cost.
2. Call `http://127.0.0.1:41483/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, or `/v1/messages` with organization alias and member ID.
3. Confirm recorded spend exceeds the budget using the customer API.
4. Repeat the request. All return 422. Raising the budget allows requests again, and restoring it blocks them.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished and its findings are addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The independent live baseline was `28540cecc0e65b9e7252689cc42d0e2d9fd187f5`. The live candidate was `dd077797c189b61b6ef0d2e70990889633fe7805`. Current base `32cb45a3d8875321efd8adab9ddccb5ff41d8d9a` adds only successor metadata for unrelated audio/realtime models. Current tip `672ec3f2196577553866f7ad8ea6c0ddcc6b31f8` has byte-identical customer, spend, and accounting code to the tested candidate. This is a verified neutral rebase, not a claim that the server loaded the newer hash.

With separate storage per revision, the baseline admitted 17 of 72 requests after persisted customer spend exceeded its cap. The candidate blocked all 72. After increasing limits, all 36 recovery requests succeeded. Restoring limits blocked all 36 follow-up requests. The test waits for persisted spend before evaluating enforcement, so it does not confuse initial write latency with the defect.

396 focused Python tests pass, plus three native counter-key tests and five real PostgreSQL reset tests. The billed-failure regression fails two cases without the fix and passes with it. `make check` passes at the current tip. The local Logfire pytest plugin is disabled because its installed telemetry dependency cannot import `LogData`.

### Shared setup

Run two workers per checkout. Baseline and candidate must have separate PostgreSQL databases and Redis instances, since accounting workers share queues within each instance. Use fresh UTF8 databases, separate dependency environments, and the native library built from each checkout. Both runs use real provider calls through the internal gateway.

Supply `DATABASE_URL`, `QA_REDIS_HOST`, `QA_REDIS_PORT`, `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE`, and `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` at runtime. Use the clearly fake local-only `QA_MASTER_KEY` value in the client below. `WEBHOOK_URL` can point to a disposable local receiver, as it did during this QA. No webhook assertion is part of these cases. The model IDs and Messages native output maximum were verified against the current catalog.

<details>
<summary>Save proxy-config.yaml and start each proxy</summary>



Use port 41485 for baseline, 41483 for the enforcement candidate, and 41486 for the Messages candidate. Check `/health/liveliness` before starting the client. Use different Redis and database settings for each process group.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Save qa_client.py beside the reproduction script</summary>

```python
import json
import os
import re
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

BASE = os.environ.get('QA_PROXY_URL', 'http://127.0.0.1:41483')
MASTER = 'sk-qa-placeholder-not-a-real-secret'
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SENSITIVE_FIELDS = {'key', 'token', 'api_key', 'access_token', 'refresh_token', 'password', 'authorization'}
PRIVATE = tuple(filter(None, (
    os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY'),
    os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE'),
    urlsplit(os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE', '')).hostname,
)))

def clean(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: '[REDACTED]' if k.lower() in SENSITIVE_FIELDS else clean(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [clean(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if value.startswith('resp_') and len(value) > 128:
            return '[opaque response ID omitted]'
        for secret in PRIVATE:
            value = value.replace(secret, '[REDACTED]')
        return re.sub(r'\bsk-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{12,}', '[REDACTED]', value)
    return value

def api(method, path, body=None, *, key=MASTER, headers=None, label=None, quiet=False):
    started = time.monotonic()
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path, method=method,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
        headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', **(headers or {})},
    )
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        text = response.read().decode()
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            data = text
        status = response.status
        metadata = {k: v for k, v in response.headers.items() if k.lower() in {'content-type', 'x-litellm-response-cost'}}
    record = clean({
        'at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), 'label': label, 'method': method, 'path': path,
        'request': body, 'customer_headers': headers, 'status': status,
        'elapsed_seconds': round(time.monotonic() - started, 3), 'response_headers': metadata, 'response': data,
    })
    with (WORK / 'api-evidence.jsonl').open('a') as evidence:
        evidence.write(json.dumps(record) + '\n')
    if not quiet:
        print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
    return status, data

def org(org_id, alias, *, budget=10, template=1):
    return api('POST', '/management/v1/customer_organizations', {
        'customer_org_id': org_id, 'alias': alias,
        'budget': {'max_budget': budget, 'budget_duration': '1mo'},
        'default_budgets': [{'name': 'Standard', 'max_budget': template, 'budget_duration': '1mo', 'is_default': True}],
    })

def customer_headers(alias, member=None):
    return {'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': alias, **({'x-litellm-customer-member-id': member} if member else {})}

def virtual_key(alias, *, org_id=None):
    status, data = api('POST', '/key/generate', {
        'key_alias': alias, 'models': ['qa-openai', 'qa-anthropic'],
        **({'metadata': {'customer_org_id': org_id}} if org_id else {}),
    }, quiet=True)
    assert status == 200, clean(data)
    return data['key']

def infer(route, *, alias, member, key=MASTER, label=None, quiet=False, **extra):
    headers = customer_headers(alias, member)
    if route == 'chat':
        path, body = '/v1/chat/completions', {
            'model': 'qa-openai', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply exactly QA OK.'}], **extra,
        }
    elif route == 'responses':
        path, body = '/v1/responses', {'model': 'qa-openai', 'input': 'Reply exactly QA OK.', **extra}
    else:
        path, body = '/v1/messages', {
            'model': 'qa-anthropic', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply exactly QA OK.'}],
            'max_tokens': 128000, **extra,
        }
    return api('POST', path, body, key=key, headers=headers, label=label or route, quiet=quiet)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Save budget-crossing-v2.py</summary>

```python
import json, os, time
from qa_client import api, infer, virtual_key
phase=os.environ.get('QA_PHASE','fixed')
run_id=os.environ.get('QA_RUN_ID',phase)
key=virtual_key('qa-budget-crossing-'+run_id)
for route in ('chat','responses','messages'):
    for level in ('org','team','member'):
        identity='qa-cross-'+run_id+'-'+route+'-'+level
        member=identity+'-member'
        status,_=api('POST','/management/v1/customer_organizations',{
            'customer_org_id':identity,'alias':identity,
            'budget':{'max_budget':0.000001 if level=='org' else 10,'budget_duration':'1mo'},
            'default_budgets':[{'name':'Standard','max_budget':0.000001 if level=='member' else 1,'budget_duration':'1mo','is_default':True}],
        },quiet=True)
        assert status==201
        if level=='team':
            status,_=api('POST','/management/v1/customer_teams',{'customer_team_id':identity+'-group','parent_org_id':identity,'budget':{'max_budget':0.000001}},quiet=True)
            assert status==201
            status,_=api('POST','/management/v1/customer_members',{'customer_member_id':member,'parent_team_id':identity+'-group'},quiet=True)
            assert status==201
        path='/management/v1/'+({'org':'customer_organizations/'+identity,'team':'customer_teams/'+identity+'-group','member':'customer_members/'+member}[level])
        first,_=infer(route,alias=identity,member=member,key=key,label=identity+'-first',quiet=True)
        assert first==200, first
        start=time.monotonic()
        for poll in range(40):
            _,current=api('GET',path,quiet=True,label=identity+'-persisted')
            if current['spend']>0: break
            time.sleep(0.5)
        assert current['spend']>0
        statuses=[infer(route,alias=identity,member=member,key=key,label=identity+'-after-excess-'+str(i),quiet=True)[0] for i in range(8)]
        print(json.dumps({'phase':phase,'route':route,'level':level,'cap':0.000001,'persisted_spend':current['spend'],'persist_wait_seconds':round(time.monotonic()-start,3),'after_excess':statuses}),flush=True)
        if phase=='fixed':
            assert statuses==[422]*8
            patch={'budget_override':{'max_budget':1}} if level=='member' else {'budget':{'max_budget':1}}
            status,_=api('PATCH',path,patch,quiet=True,label=identity+'-raise-limit')
            assert status==200
            recovered=[infer(route,alias=identity,member=member,key=key,label=identity+'-raised-'+str(i),quiet=True)[0] for i in range(4)]
            assert recovered==[200]*4,recovered
            patch={'budget_override':None} if level=='member' else {'budget':{'max_budget':0.000001}}
            status,_=api('PATCH',path,patch,quiet=True,label=identity+'-restore-limit')
            assert status==200
            denied=[infer(route,alias=identity,member=member,key=key,label=identity+'-restored-'+str(i),quiet=True)[0] for i in range(4)]
            print(json.dumps({'phase':phase,'route':route,'level':level,'raised_limit':recovered,'restored_limit':denied}),flush=True)
            assert denied==[422]*4,denied
```

title: fix(usage): include Messages requests in endpoint breakdowns
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Messages spend totals included requests missing from endpoint breakdowns.

How it solves it:

- Map both Messages call types to `/messages`.
- Verify accounting preserves route totals, including retries.

## User Flow

Before, a developer cannot reconcile customer usage by endpoint.

1. Create a customer organization with a default member budget.
2. Send one request each to `http://127.0.0.1:41485/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/messages` with the organization alias and member ID.
3. Read `http://127.0.0.1:41485/management/v1/customer_members/daily/activity`, filtered to that member and date.
4. Observe three successful requests, but only two in endpoint breakdowns.

After, the same customer usage includes all three endpoints.

1. Create a customer organization with a default member budget.
2. Send one request each to `http://127.0.0.1:41486/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/messages` with the organization alias and member ID.
3. Read `http://127.0.0.1:41486/management/v1/customer_members/daily/activity`, filtered to that member and date.
4. Observe three successful requests and one under each endpoint.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished and its findings are addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The independent live baseline was `28540cecc0e65b9e7252689cc42d0e2d9fd187f5`. The live candidate was `eb3c5c00e305e4ef1362a8c12b5e677fff456e9c`. Current base `32cb45a3d8875321efd8adab9ddccb5ff41d8d9a` adds only successor metadata for unrelated audio/realtime models. Current tip `51788d5fa0137bdcbbb86c94d5dd53756f7c94c2` has byte-identical customer, routing, and accounting code to the tested candidate. This is a verified neutral rebase, not a claim that the server loaded the newer hash.

The new accounting regression fails four Messages cases on the base and passes after the mapping change. At current tip, 362 focused tests pass. `make check` passes at this tip. The local Logfire pytest plugin is disabled because its installed telemetry dependency cannot import `LogData`.

### Shared setup

Run two workers per checkout. Baseline and candidate must have separate PostgreSQL databases and Redis instances, since accounting workers share queues within each instance. Use fresh UTF8 databases, separate dependency environments, and the native library built from each checkout. Both runs use real provider calls through the internal gateway.

Supply `DATABASE_URL`, `QA_REDIS_HOST`, `QA_REDIS_PORT`, `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE`, and `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` at runtime. Use the clearly fake local-only `QA_MASTER_KEY` value in the client below. `WEBHOOK_URL` can point to a disposable local receiver, as it did during this QA. No webhook assertion is part of these cases. The model IDs and Messages native output maximum were verified against the current catalog.

<details>
<summary>Save proxy-config.yaml and start each proxy</summary>


<details>
<summary>Save qa_client.py beside the reproduction script</summary>

```python
import json
import os
import re
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

BASE = os.environ.get('QA_PROXY_URL', 'http://127.0.0.1:41483')
MASTER = 'sk-qa-placeholder-not-a-real-secret'
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SENSITIVE_FIELDS = {'key', 'token', 'api_key', 'access_token', 'refresh_token', 'password', 'authorization'}
PRIVATE = tuple(filter(None, (
    os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY'),
    os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE'),
    urlsplit(os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE', '')).hostname,
)))

def clean(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: '[REDACTED]' if k.lower() in SENSITIVE_FIELDS else clean(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [clean(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if value.startswith('resp_') and len(value) > 128:
            return '[opaque response ID omitted]'
        for secret in PRIVATE:
            value = value.replace(secret, '[REDACTED]')
        return re.sub(r'\bsk-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{12,}', '[REDACTED]', value)
    return value

def api(method, path, body=None, *, key=MASTER, headers=None, label=None, quiet=False):
    started = time.monotonic()
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path, method=method,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
        headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', **(headers or {})},
    )
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        text = response.read().decode()
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            data = text
        status = response.status
        metadata = {k: v for k, v in response.headers.items() if k.lower() in {'content-type', 'x-litellm-response-cost'}}
    record = clean({
        'at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), 'label': label, 'method': method, 'path': path,
        'request': body, 'customer_headers': headers, 'status': status,
        'elapsed_seconds': round(time.monotonic() - started, 3), 'response_headers': metadata, 'response': data,
    })
    with (WORK / 'api-evidence.jsonl').open('a') as evidence:
        evidence.write(json.dumps(record) + '\n')
    if not quiet:
        print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
    return status, data

def org(org_id, alias, *, budget=10, template=1):
    return api('POST', '/management/v1/customer_organizations', {
        'customer_org_id': org_id, 'alias': alias,
        'budget': {'max_budget': budget, 'budget_duration': '1mo'},
        'default_budgets': [{'name': 'Standard', 'max_budget': template, 'budget_duration': '1mo', 'is_default': True}],
    })

def customer_headers(alias, member=None):
    return {'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': alias, **({'x-litellm-customer-member-id': member} if member else {})}

def virtual_key(alias, *, org_id=None):
    status, data = api('POST', '/key/generate', {
        'key_alias': alias, 'models': ['qa-openai', 'qa-anthropic'],
        **({'metadata': {'customer_org_id': org_id}} if org_id else {}),
    }, quiet=True)
    assert status == 200, clean(data)
    return data['key']

def infer(route, *, alias, member, key=MASTER, label=None, quiet=False, **extra):
    headers = customer_headers(alias, member)
    if route == 'chat':
        path, body = '/v1/chat/completions', {
            'model': 'qa-openai', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply exactly QA OK.'}], **extra,
        }
    elif route == 'responses':
        path, body = '/v1/responses', {'model': 'qa-openai', 'input': 'Reply exactly QA OK.', **extra}
    else:
        path, body = '/v1/messages', {
            'model': 'qa-anthropic', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply exactly QA OK.'}],
            'max_tokens': 128000, **extra,
        }
    return api('POST', path, body, key=key, headers=headers, label=label or route, quiet=quiet)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Save messages-usage-proof.py</summary>

```python
import json
import os
import time
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from qa_client import BASE, api, infer, virtual_key

phase = os.environ.get('QA_PHASE', 'fixed')
run_id = os.environ.get('QA_RUN_ID', phase)
identity = 'qa-endpoint-' + run_id
for _ in range(300):
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + '/health/liveliness', timeout=2) as response:
            if response.status == 200:
                break
    except OSError:
        time.sleep(1)
else:
    raise SystemExit('QA proxy did not start')
key = virtual_key(identity)
status, _ = api('POST', '/management/v1/customer_organizations', {
    'customer_org_id': identity,
    'alias': identity,
    'default_budgets': [{'name': 'Standard', 'max_budget': 1, 'is_default': True}],
}, quiet=True)
assert status == 201
for route in ('chat', 'responses', 'messages'):
    status, _ = infer(route, alias=identity, member=identity, key=key, label=identity+'-'+route, quiet=True)
    assert status == 200, (route, status)
day = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
path = '/management/v1/customer_members/daily/activity?customer_member_ids=' + identity
path += '&start_date=' + day + '&end_date=' + day + '&page_size=100'
for _ in range(120):
    status, usage = api('GET', path, quiet=True, label=identity+'-usage')
    assert status == 200
    total = sum(row['metrics']['successful_requests'] for row in usage['results'])
    if total == 3:
        break
    time.sleep(0.5)
assert total == 3, usage
endpoints = {
    name: value['metrics']['successful_requests']
    for row in usage['results']
    for name, value in row['breakdown']['endpoints'].items()
}
print(json.dumps({'phase': phase, 'total_requests': total, 'endpoint_requests': endpoints}), flush=True)
if phase == 'fixed':
    assert endpoints == {'/chat/completions': 1, '/responses': 1, '/messages': 1}, endpoints
```

</details>

Run the reproduction once against each fresh environment.

```sh
QA_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:41485 QA_PHASE=baseline QA_RUN_ID=utf8-base python3 messages-usage-proof.py
QA_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:41486 QA_PHASE=fixed QA_RUN_ID=utf8-fixed python3 messages-usage-proof.py
```

### Before (28540cecc0e)

#### Chat Completions

1. The script sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` and gets 200.
2. Customer daily usage includes `/chat/completions` with one successful request.

#### Responses

1. The script sends `POST /v1/responses` and gets 200.
2. Customer daily usage includes `/responses` with one successful request.


### After (eb3c5c00e305, equivalent current tip 51788d5fa013)

1. The same script sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` and gets 200.
2. Customer daily usage includes `/chat/completions` with one successful request.

#### Responses

1. The same script sends `POST /v1/responses` and gets 200.
2. Customer daily usage includes `/responses` with one successful request.

#### Messages

1. The same script sends `POST /v1/messages` and gets 200.
2. Customer daily usage includes `/messages` with one successful request. All three endpoint counts reconcile with the total.

```json
{"phase": "fixed", "total_requests": 3, "endpoint_requests": {"/chat/completions": 1, "/messages": 1, "/responses": 1}}
```

## Caveats

### Medium

- Existing daily usage rows are not backfilled.

## Type

Bug Fix

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow mapping and test updates in usage accounting; no auth or payment logic changes. Existing daily rows are not backfilled per PR notes.
> 
> **Overview**

Unit tests now assert the projected `endpoint` for those call types (including retries) and expect **`/messages`** in proxy required-param error paths.

title: refactor(rust): replace veil with Redacted<T> and SecretValue
body: - Secrets were hidden from `Debug` three ways: `SecretValue`, veil attributes, and hand-written impls. Bare `#[redact]` printed asterisks while `with = "[REDACTED]"` printed `[REDACTED]` - veil had to be a direct dependency of 15 crates, because its derive emits `veil::private` paths that cannot be wrapped - `secret-value` now holds the only redaction types and veil leaves the workspace - `Redacted` prints only `[REDACTED]`, does not need `T: Debug`, (de)serializes as `T`, and gives the value up through `expose()` or `into_inner()` - `SecretValue` wraps `Redacted` and keeps its constant-time `eq` - `#[source] Redacted` hides only `Debug`. `Display` and the source chain pass through, and `litellm_error::find` looks through it like it does `Source` - AWS and Vertex credential params become `Option`. Proxy URLs, provider handles, vault bodies, `Secret::Bool`/`Json` and every secret manager error cause move onto `Redacted` - A redacted cause converted with `?` gets one `impl From` instead of `#[from]` - The rust-redaction and rust-error skills now name the two types as the only redaction tools - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is clean at this tip, and the tests of every touched crate pass (secret-value, error, auth-*, http, config, secrets*, gateway-mcp, gateway-auth, redis-connect with Docker, gateway redis, python-bridge router and secrets) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

title: feat(proxy): name budget rows, give customer teams an override and members a parent org
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/21a173095a2f4d3b8d906617f2cf0ce8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/21a173095a2f4d3b8d906617f2cf0ce8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

Builds on #51562, which drops `budget_reset_at` from the customer tables. This PR targets that branch and retargets to main when it lands.

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Template names lived in a JSON map on the org row, not on the budget
- `budget_ids` on the org did not say what the list was for
- Only members could carry a temporary budget override, teams could not
- A member knew its team but not its organization

How it solves it:

- `name` on `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`, `budget_names` dropped from the org
- Org `budget_ids` -> `budget_template_ids`, `default_budget_id` -> `default_budget_template_id`
- Teams get `budget_override_id` + `budget_override_expires_at`, enforced and reset like members
- Members get `parent_org_id` (backfilled from the team, migration `20261113130000`)
- API: `Team` gains `budget_override`, `effective_budget`; `CustomerMember` gains `parent_org_id`

Intentional product change: the organization response field `default_budget_id` is renamed `default_budget_template_id`, so a client reading the old name gets nothing until it switches. The dashboard is updated in this PR.

## User Flow

Before: an admin cannot put a temporary cap on one customer team, only on single members

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_teams with `"budget": {"max_budget": 50}` and `"budget_override": {"max_budget": 500}` and gets `422 budget_override: Extra inputs are not permitted`
2. They retry without the override, the team is created at 50 and every member request is checked against 50
3. GET https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations/{id} lists templates by name read from a JSON map on the org row, with `default_budget_id`

After: the same admin caps or boosts a team until a date and reads the org's templates by their own name

1. The same POST returns 201 with `budget_override`, `budget_override_expires_at` and `effective_budget.max_budget: 500`
2. Member requests under that team are checked against 500 until the expiry, then against 50 again

title: fix(proxy): enforce settled customer budgets across workers
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

QA fix, ensure customer budget enforcement works across workers. Before this in multi worker settings customer budgets were crossing their amounts. For example, if you set a $100 budget and you had three workers, you are able to spend up to $300. This keeps it in sync across workers. 

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>
Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/cb652710bdbf47a5a1b885344793944b?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Requests continue after settled spend reaches the customer budget
- Cached organization spend misses charges from other members

How it solves it:

- Read shared settled spend before customer budget checks
- Reseed missing counters through the existing spend-counter DB lookup

Intentional product change: requests that previously slipped through stale spend checks now receive the existing 422 budget error. A request admitted below the cap can still finish and cross it

## User Flow

Before, the customer keeps receiving successful responses after committed spend exceeds the organization budget

1. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations with an alias, a $0.0002 cap, and a default member budget
2. Send two POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses requests with organization-alias and member-ID headers, one member per request
3. GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/{customer_org_id} shows $0.000272 spent against the $0.0002 cap
4. Send another POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses as the first member and still receive 200

After, the same workflow rejects the next request once spend has settled

1. POST http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations with an alias, a $0.0002 cap, and a default member budget
2. Send two POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses requests with organization-alias and member-ID headers, one member per request
3. GET http://localhost:4000/management/v1/customer_organizations/{customer_org_id} shows $0.000272 spent against the $0.0002 cap
4. Send another POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses as the first member and receive 422 with `budget_exceeded`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

Local lint and relevant tests passed. Current CI status is recorded in the follow-up below. Pending checks are not counted as passing

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

### Shared spend-counter rework

Customer budget checks now use `proxy_server.get_current_spend`, just like key, team, user and org budgets. `SpendCounterReseed.from_db` reads the matching customer org, customer team or customer member row. It checks the counter's budget period against `budget_reset_at` before seeding. The hierarchy refresh parameters and callback are gone.

The three mapped files printed `112 passed in 10.30s`. They cover all customer scopes, missing counters, shared workers, reset periods, unavailable rows, malformed periods and settlement without double counting. `make lint` exited 0 and printed `OK: every basedpyright rule is within its ceiling (94885 errors total, base 216a33071289)`.

The latest real-provider recheck used two serving workers on port 4016 and the same shared Redis on 6383. Worker connection counts were `353807=13` and `353808=12`. Each route started with a new customer org capped at `$0.000000001`. The first request returned 200. After its spend reached PostgreSQL, all 24 pooled clients returned 422, including clients connected to both workers. Another customer member in the same customer org also returned 422. Deleting the exact customer org counter from Redis still returned 422 and restored precisely the PostgreSQL spend.

| Route | Settled spend | Requests after settlement | After Redis deletion | DB-reseeded spend |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| `/v1/responses` | 0.000068 | 24 x 422 | 422 | 0.000068 |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 0.000058 | 24 x 422 | 422 | 0.000058 |
| `/v1/messages` | 0.000136 | 24 x 422 | 422 | 0.000136 |

The runner is `/home/ubuntu/pr1-reseed-live.py`, its printed output is `/home/ubuntu/pr1-reseed-live.log`, and the worker counts and assertions are `/home/ubuntu/pr1-reseed-live.json`. The temporary proxy was stopped afterward. Existing proxies were left running.

<details>
<summary>Recheck commands and counter deletion</summary>

The environment provides `DATABASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`. The config remains the same dedicated-Redis config shown below. The runtime was started with the following command from `litellm/proxy`.

```bash
../../.venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli \
  --config /home/ubuntu/pr3-config.yaml \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4016
```

For each route, create a new customer org with a positive cap smaller than one provider call, send the first request and poll its management endpoint until `spend` exceeds that cap. Retry the same headers on the route and expect 422. The runner deletes only the newly created QA customer org's exact counter and verifies both the next 422 and equality with PostgreSQL.

```python
counter = f"spend:customer_org:{customer_org_id}:lifetime"
assert float(cache.get(counter)) >= cap
assert cache.delete(counter) == 1
response = client.post(base + route, headers=headers, json=body)
assert response.status_code == 422
assert float(cache.get(counter)) == customer_org["spend"]
```

```bash
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_spend.py \
  tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_hierarchy_auth.py \
  tests/unit/proxy/db/test_spend_counter_reseed.py -q
make lint
```

</details>

### Shared setup

Both captures use a DB-backed proxy on http://localhost:4000 with two workers and one dedicated shared Redis instance on localhost:6383. PostgreSQL is on localhost:5432. These are real provider requests, not mocks

Run from `/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm` with an initialized local database and generated Prisma client. Provide `DATABASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP` through the environment. The bundled model cost map was enabled. Credential values are omitted

Use the same configuration for both revisions

<details>
<summary>Proxy configuration, saved as /home/ubuntu/customer-qa.yaml</summary>

```yaml
environment_variables:
  WEBHOOK_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8808
model_list:
  - model_name: qa-gpt
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.6
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: qa-claude
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  alerting: [webhook]
  alert_types: [budget_alerts]
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6383
router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6383
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

</details>

Start the merge-base runtime with the command used for the baseline

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/customer-qa.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4000 > /home/ubuntu/pr1-before-proxy.log 2>&1
```

Stop that runtime before starting the tested tip with the final command

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/customer-qa.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --port 4000 > /home/ubuntu/pr1-verified-proxy.log 2>&1
```

Reload was disabled because edits to evidence files under /home/ubuntu restarted the proxy. Two workers were retained. The migration-resolver flag is a deprecated no-op on this main revision, so it was omitted from the final command

The final serving worker PIDs were 72679 and 72680. Eight separate readiness connections returned 200, and established server sockets belonged to both PIDs. Individual budget requests were not pinned to a worker

The client creates a fresh organization and virtual key, sends request one as member A and request two as member B, waits for persisted spend, then retries member A. Use fresh organization IDs when repeating the run to avoid duplicate-create conflicts. Both client versions below replace only the local master-key literal with an environment lookup. Request bodies and header names match the captures

### Before (216a33071289de6f72fd76b09ae7607a33e8c40a)

Only Responses has a captured live baseline. Chat Completions and Messages were not captured on the merge base, and their Before cases below are marked accordingly

<details>
<summary>Baseline client, save as /home/ubuntu/pr1-live.py</summary>

```python
import argparse
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('phase')
p.add_argument('--all', action='store_true')
a = p.parse_args()
base = 'http://localhost:4000'
admin = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}
rows = []
for endpoint in ('responses', 'chat/completions', 'messages') if a.all else ('responses',):
    name = f'pr1-{a.phase}-{endpoint.replace("/", "-")}'
    r = httpx.post(base + '/management/v1/customer_organizations', headers=admin, json={
        'customer_org_id': name, 'alias': name, 'budget': {'max_budget': 0.0002},
        'default_budgets': [{'name': 'default', 'is_default': True, 'max_budget': 5}]})
    assert r.status_code == 201, r.text
    key = httpx.post(base + '/key/generate', headers=admin, json={'models': ['qa-gpt', 'qa-claude']}).json()['key']
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, 'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': name,
               'x-litellm-customer-member-id': name + '-a'}
    body = {'model': 'qa-claude' if endpoint == 'messages' else 'qa-gpt'}
    if endpoint == 'responses':
        body.update(input='Reply only OK', max_output_tokens=64)
    else:
        body.update(messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply only OK'}],
                    **({'max_tokens': 64} if endpoint == 'messages' else {'max_completion_tokens': 64}))
    for n in range(2):
        r = httpx.post(base + '/v1/' + endpoint, headers={**headers, 'x-litellm-customer-member-id': name + ('-a' if n == 0 else '-b')}, json=body, timeout=90)
        rows.append({'endpoint': endpoint, 'call': n + 1, 'status': r.status_code,
                     'cost': r.headers.get('x-litellm-response-cost'), 'error': r.json().get('error')})
    for _ in range(40):
        org = httpx.get(base + '/management/v1/customer_organizations/' + name, headers=admin).json()
        if org['spend'] >= 0.0002:
            break
        time.sleep(0.5)
    assert org['spend'] >= 0.0002, org
    print(name, 'committed spend', org['spend'], flush=True)
    for n in range(8):
        r = httpx.post(base + '/v1/' + endpoint, headers=headers, json=body, timeout=90)
        rows.append({'endpoint': endpoint, 'call': n + 3, 'status': r.status_code,
                     'cost': r.headers.get('x-litellm-response-cost'), 'error': r.json().get('error')})
        if a.phase == 'before':
            break
    print(json.dumps(rows[-10:], indent=2), flush=True)
Path('/home/ubuntu/pr1-' + a.phase + '.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2))
```

The final client extends the spend-flush polling window from 20 to 90 seconds. An earlier attempt reached the 20-second harness timeout while a batch flush completed after approximately 26 seconds. No proxy configuration or write interval changed

Each case below shows the recorded rows for its first three calls from that single invocation. Calls four through ten also returned 422 for every endpoint, giving 24 rejected post-crossing probes in total

#### /v1/responses

2. Wait for committed spend of $0.000272, then retry member A and observe 422 with `budget_exceeded`
