title: feat(budgets): add concurrent monthly and annual customer limits
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- One reusable customer budget could enforce only one spend period.

How it solves it:

- Add simultaneous monthly and annual limits to existing budgets.
- Reuse customer hierarchy admission, reservations, settlement, and window accounting.
- Extend the existing budget form and table.

Intentional product change: the spend-period selector gains “per month and year,” showing two independently editable amounts.

## User Flow

Before, an admin can select only one spend period for a reusable budget.

1. Open the Budgets page at `/ui/budgets/`.
2. Select Create Budget and enter a budget ID.
3. Select one spend period and enter one limit.

After, the same form supports both limits together.

1. Open the Budgets page at `/ui/budgets/`.
2. Select Create Budget and enter a budget ID.
3. Select “per month and year,” enter both limits, and save.
4. Edit either limit and see both amounts in the budget table.

## Implementation

Adds one nullable `budget_limits` JSON column to the existing budget table, using the existing window-entry shape and calendar helpers. Customer organizations, teams, and members retain their existing budget assignments and overrides. Each entity has independent monthly and annual balances in the existing `LiteLLM_BudgetWindowSpend` table. The existing `get_current_spend` checks, transactional writer, rollover handling, reservation pipeline, and ledger projection are reused. Customer window checks use the same database-spend floor and stale-counter repair as internal-user enforcement, while rejecting unverifiable shared counters.

Budget updates use the existing validation, repository write, and cache invalidation flow. Consumers that only support scalar budgets reject concurrent windows. Existing single-period monthly and annual budgets retain their current behavior.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Automated reviews on the latest commit have finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The real local dashboard demo creates a $50 monthly / $500 annual budget, edits only the annual cap to $600, and verifies both saved limits. The screenshot and real 15-second recording are attached below. The editor also preserves and displays an existing single-period cap when calendar limits are present.

Local checks cover admission, accounting, management compatibility, and UI behavior. The latest fixes passed 755 accounting tests, 85 reservation/scalar-budget tests, 37 router/auth tests, 72 UI tests, 10 UI type tests, and production UI typechecking. Endpoint regressions passed all 15 affected cases plus 178 related tests. The shared-enforcement change additionally passed 196 focused tests. Six stale-counter regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward; the performance test confirms one Redis batch read per admission and reuse of cached database totals. Full `make check` passed. Fresh CI and automated reviews remain pending.

### Live enforcement verification

After the shared-enforcement change, an actual two-worker local proxy used dedicated Redis and PostgreSQL plus real provider requests. Each of `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/messages` returned 200 under both caps. Setting either the monthly or annual cap to zero produced 422 `budget_exceeded` before another provider request. Both durable window balances matched total billed cost, $0.000167, within floating-point precision.

The baseline proxy at `28540cecc0e6` rejected the same customer-organization body containing `budget.budget_limits` with 422, `Extra inputs are not permitted`. The changed proxy accepted it with 201 and returned both independent reset dates.

<details>
<summary>Local reproduction setup</summary>

Use isolated PostgreSQL and Redis. Set `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` locally. The provider credential must have access to the development gateway.

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: profiles-demo
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-terra
      api_base: https://gateway.product-dev.internal.litellm.ai/v1
      api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6401
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  database_connection_pool_limit: 5
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6401
  proxy_batch_write_at: 1
  disable_error_logs: true
litellm_settings:
  timezone: America/New_York
  drop_params: true
```

```sh
uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/budget-windows.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4101 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

With an admin token, create a budget through `POST /budget/new` with `budget_limits` set to `[{"budget_duration":"1mo","max_budget":10},{"budget_duration":"12mo","max_budget":100}]`. Create an organization, team, and member through `/management/v1/customer_organizations`, `/management/v1/customer_teams`, and `/management/v1/customer_members`, assigning that budget ID to the member. Generate a virtual key with `POST /key/generate` and send requests with `x-litellm-customer-member-id` set to the member ID.

The successful request bodies were:

```json
{"model":"profiles-demo","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply OK."}],"max_completion_tokens":32}
{"model":"profiles-demo","input":"Reply OK.","max_output_tokens":32}
{"model":"profiles-demo","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply OK."}],"max_tokens":32}
```

Update the same budget through `/budget/update`, first with annual maximum zero and monthly maximum 10, then monthly maximum zero and annual maximum 100. Repeat each request and expect the corresponding window's 422 error. Restore the limits afterward.

The local dashboard runs at `http://localhost:3081/ui/budgets/`. The recording creates $50 monthly / $500 annual, edits the annual amount to $600, and verifies both amounts in the table. A fresh baseline UI screenshot remains unavailable because the local browser's password-manager dialog blocked that capture; the baseline API comparison above was completed.

</details>

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Medium

- Concurrent windows apply to customer hierarchies and calendar month/year periods.
- Deferred request attribution retains existing main behavior.

## Final Attestation

- [ ] Final CI, automated review, and live enforcement verification complete

</details>

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cfbb079-0d98-4fe2-9186-31a30330ce06

![concurrent-budgets-result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d69b4731-ffa6-4695-a35d-5bd213c5f0f4)


The same editor exposes both limits on an existing mixed configuration ($100/month and $25/day):

![Existing monthly and daily limits remain visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41743d2f-105a-48b6-9976-8d7517eb239b)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes budget schema, enforcement, Redis spend counters, and customer admission/accounting—security- and billing-critical paths with cross-pod consistency requirements.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **concurrent calendar budget windows** (`budget_limits` on `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`) so a single reusable budget can enforce independent **monthly (`1mo`) and annual (`12mo`)** caps, primarily for **customer org/team/member** hierarchies.
> 
> **Storage & API:** Adds a `budget_limits` JSON column (migration + Prisma), `BudgetLimit` / `BudgetWriteRequest`, and budget create/update paths that initialize reset times and persist window JSON. Management list/info surfaces `budget_limits`.
> 
> **Scope restrictions:** Keys, teams, end users, projects, and other scalar budget consumers **reject** budgets that have `budget_limits`; updates that add windows are blocked while non–customer-hierarchy references still point at the budget. Scalar `LiteLLM_BudgetTable` input rejects `budget_limits` outside customer flows.
> 
> **Enforcement & accounting:** Customer scopes carry `budget_limits`; admission runs **per-window** checks with authoritative spend reads. Spend counters gain **customer window keys** (Python + Rust), reseed/strict paths, reservation metadata with `window_reset_at`, and post-call / failure accounting wired through `customer_accounting_counters` and stamped request metadata.
> 
> **UI:** Budget create/edit adds **“per month and year”**, maps form values to `budget_limits`, and the table shows multiple window amounts (including zero) instead of “Unlimited.”
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a3fdd68aed7d9740f1ac3225c97ac618793e0c0d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

body:
## Summary

`gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview-2024-12-17` and `gpt-4o-mini-realtime-preview-2024-12-17` already carry `deprecation_date` 2027-01-20 and `deprecation_source` from OpenAI's deprecations page, but no `successor_model`. The page rows that date comes from name a replacement, so this PR records `gpt-audio-1.5` and `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` on them. Both replacements already have openai rows in the catalog with the same `mode` (chat and realtime) and no shutdown date. No price or date changes

## Evidence (kind: page, matched through the family row)

Source is https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations (fetched raw as `deprecations.md`, sha256 `7abd85d0...`), table "Upcoming deprecations"

| Shutdown date | Affected model or feature | Status | Recommended replacement | Notice date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Jan 20, 2027 | `gpt-4o-mini-realtime` | Deprecated | `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` | Jul 20, 2026 |
| Jan 20, 2027 | `gpt-4o-mini-audio` | Deprecated | `gpt-audio-1.5` | Jul 20, 2026 |

The page names the family (`gpt-4o-mini-audio`, `gpt-4o-mini-realtime`) and not the dated preview snapshot. The two catalog rows are the only openai rows in those families and their existing 2027-01-20 date can only come from these two page rows. The sibling rows `gpt-4o-audio-preview-2024-12-17` and `gpt-4o-audio-preview-2025-06-03` already record `gpt-audio-1.5` the same way from the `gpt-4o-audio` row

| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview-2024-12-17` | none | `gpt-audio-1.5` |
| `gpt-4o-mini-realtime-preview-2024-12-17` | none | `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` |

## Rest of the page

Every other model row in the "Upcoming deprecations" and "Past deprecations" tables was compared with the openai rows in the catalog (date, `deprecation_source` and first named replacement) and matches now that #51492 is merged. `gpt-4o-search-preview` and `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview` are left unchanged, their date is an open question outside this PR

## Delisted by the provider

Not returned by `GET /v1/models` for the sync key. Dated rows already carry their page dates. Undated with no deprecation entry on the page are `daybreak-blue-latest`, `daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-5.5-cyber`, `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `gpt-6-astra-law`, `gpt-6-cyber`, `gpt-6-rosalind`, `gpt-rosalind-discovery`, `gpt-rosalind-research`, `openai/container`, `text-embedding-ada-002-v2`, `gpt-4o-search-preview` and `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview`

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/21a173095a2f4d3b8d906617f2cf0ce8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/21a173095a2f4d3b8d906617f2cf0ce8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer org, team and member rows kept a `budget_reset_at` of their own
- Their `budget_id` row already carries `budget_duration` and `budget_reset_at`
- The budget row's window was ignored for customer spend

How it solves it:

- Drop `budget_reset_at` from the three customer tables (migration `20261113120000`)
- The budget-table cascade now zeroes the customer rows a due budget row governs
- A member follows its unexpired override when it has a duration, else its template
- Customer budget writes stamp `budget_reset_at` from `budget_duration` like `/budget/new`
- API responses keep `budget_reset_at`, read from the governing budget row

Intentional product change: every row on one budget template resets at the same moment, the template's window, instead of each member on its own clock from creation.

## User Flow

Before: a customer org created with a 30 day budget never shows when it resets, and its spend ignores the budget's window

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_organizations with `"budget": {"max_budget": 100, "budget_duration": "1d"}` and gets `"budget_reset_at": null`
2. The app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `x-litellm-customer-member-id`, the org, team and member show the cost
3. The budget row's own reset time passes, the next GET https://litellm-domain/management/v1/customer_members/{id} still shows the spend and a fresh `budget_reset_at` a day out

After: the same org reports its window at creation and its spend resets when that window ends

1. Admin sends the same POST and gets `"budget_reset_at": "2026-11-14T00:00:00Z"` on the org, the team and the member
2. The app sends the same chat completion, the org, team and member show the cost
3. The budget row's reset time passes, the next GET shows `"spend": 0.0` and `budget_reset_at` moved to the next window

- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup: local Postgres (one database per leg, pushed from that leg's `litellm/proxy/schema.prisma`), one local Redis on 6379 shared by both workers, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in the environment. Both legs ran two uvicorn workers; `--reload` was dropped because this checkout's uvicorn serves one worker when reloading. The reset job was made to tick every 30s with `proxy_budget_rescheduler_min_time: 30` / `max_time: 31`.

<details>
<summary>config.yaml and proxy commands</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-4o-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
  proxy_budget_rescheduler_min_time: 30
  proxy_budget_rescheduler_max_time: 31

litellm_settings:
  drop_params: True
```

```bash

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://.../litellm_qa_after python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/qa/config.yaml --port 4010 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
# before, a worktree at the merge base with a Prisma client generated from its own schema
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://.../litellm_qa_before PYTHONPATH=<worktree> python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/qa/config.yaml --port 4011 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Client steps, identical on both legs</summary>

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:$PORT/management/v1/customer_organizations -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_org_id":"qa-org","budget":{"max_budget":100,"budget_duration":"1d"},"default_budgets":[{"name":"standard","max_budget":10,"budget_duration":"1d","is_default":true}]}'
curl -X POST localhost:$PORT/management/v1/customer_teams -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_team_id":"qa-team","parent_org_id":"qa-org","budget":{"max_budget":50,"budget_duration":"1d"}}'
curl -X POST localhost:$PORT/management/v1/customer_members -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_member_id":"qa-member","parent_team_id":"qa-team"}'
VK=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:$PORT/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"models":["gpt-4o-mini"]}' | jq -r .key)
curl -X POST localhost:$PORT/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $VK" -H "x-litellm-customer-member-id: qa-member" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'
sleep 25   # spend flush
# read the three customer rows and their governing budget rows, then move every governing budget row's window into the past
psql ... -c "UPDATE \"LiteLLM_BudgetTable\" SET budget_reset_at = NOW() - INTERVAL '1 minute' WHERE budget_id IN (<org, team and member template budget ids>)"
sleep 45   # one reset job tick
curl localhost:$PORT/management/v1/customer_members/qa-member -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
```

</details>

### Before (27e9a04d62)

1. Org, team and member create responses all carry `budget_reset_at: null`
2. Chat completion `HTTP 200`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 4.35e-06`; after the flush the org, team and member rows each hold `spend 4.35e-06`, their own `budget_reset_at` is NULL, and the budget rows' `budget_reset_at` is NULL
3. After the tick with the budget rows' window in the past: budget rows advanced to `2026-11-14 00:00`, the three customer rows still hold `spend 4.35e-06` and now carry their own `budget_reset_at 2026-11-14 00:00`
4. GET member: `spend 4.35e-06`, `budget_reset_at 2026-11-14T00:00:00Z`

### After (f12882a3aa)

1. Org, team and member create responses all carry `budget_reset_at: 2026-11-14T00:00:00Z`, read from their budget rows, which were stamped at creation
2. Chat completion `HTTP 200`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 4.35e-06`; after the flush the org, team and member rows each hold `spend 4.35e-06`
3. After the tick with the budget rows' window in the past: budget rows advanced to `2026-11-14 00:00` and the three customer rows hold `spend 0.0`
4. GET member: `spend 0.0`, `budget_reset_at 2026-11-14T00:00:00Z`

Integration tests against real Postgres (`tests/integration/database/test_spendlogs_ledger_parity.py -k customer`, 11 passed) cover the same reset path plus the member override cases; removing the customer writes from the cascade fails 12 of the 13 customer tests.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Severe

- Migration drops a column from three tables shipped in the v1.111.0 dev line only
- A member's accrued spend is zeroed by its template's first due window, not its own clock

### Medium

- Budget rows created by the dev line with a duration but no `budget_reset_at` reset on the next tick, which zeroes customer spend accrued so far once

### Low

- `budget_reset_at` on customer API responses is now derived, not stored, so it is read-only in fact as well as in the schema

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: fix(utils): register ollama deployment prices from the built-in catalog without calling the provider
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

A trailing-slash embedding test failed once because setting up an Ollama deployment made the proxy call the default local Ollama address to look up model prices, and in the test run that address happened to belong to another test's fake provider. Price registration now reads LiteLLM's built-in price catalog instead of calling a provider, so adding an Ollama model no longer sends a surprise request to whatever listens on that port. A new integration test covers this with separate configured and default fake providers

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0018b787be4347e394bc450ca32e1f1e
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0018b787be4347e394bc450ca32e1f1e?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Registering an Ollama deployment's prices called `/api/show` on localhost:11434
- That request hit an unrelated test peer, failing its exact request check

How it solves it:

- Price registration reads the built-in catalog, no provider call
- Regression test with separate configured and default peers

CI evidence: [job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43287547813/job/131424823901), failed 1 time; recorded requests were `POST /api/show` then `POST /vy/v1/embeddings`, then `KeyError('api')`

Mechanism: `litellm/utils.py` price lookup used the live model-info API, which for Ollama posts `/api/show` to the default `localhost:11434` (`litellm/llms/ollama/common_utils.py`), a port the harness can assign to another peer

Fix: read built-in prices without contacting the provider; existing pricing unit tests move their failure injections to the catalog boundary with all assertions kept

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 194a5953e3953374077176ec276768e7cf3919d9: proven with the integration rig at 1 worker, retries off

1. Unchanged product code (and as a temporary break): 2 failed, the original `/api/show` plus `KeyError('api')` and the new regression
2. Fix, target five times: 8 passed each run
3. Fix, whole file once: 76 passed
4. Rebased live regression: 1 passed; pricing unit files: 626 passed
5. `make lint`: exit 0

<details>
<summary>Full evidence</summary>

# Heal C evidence

## Delivery

Branch `litellm_flakeheal_20261113_test_embedding_base_that_already_names_t`

Tip `194a5953e3953374077176ec276768e7cf3919d9`

Pushed with `git push origin HEAD`. `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/litellm_flakeheal_20261113_test_embedding_base_that_already_names_t` returned `194a5953e3953374077176ec276768e7cf3919d9`, matching local HEAD

No PR opened and no workflow dispatched

## Cause and change

Adding an Ollama deployment caused the built-in price lookup at `litellm/utils.py:4117` to call the live model-info API without the deployment's API base. `OllamaModelInfo.get_runtime_model_info` sent `POST /api/show` through `litellm.module_level_client` at `litellm/llms/ollama/common_utils.py:247-249`, using the default `http://localhost:11434` from line 138. The harness could assign that port to the Voyage test's peer

The price lookup now uses the existing catalog-only helper at `litellm/utils.py:4100-4102`. This fixes the unwanted network call rather than hiding a request or reserving only one provider port. Public Ollama model-info lookup and inference code are unchanged

Only three files changed

- `litellm/utils.py` changes the built-in registration lookup to the catalog-only helper and adjusts its return annotation
- `tests/integration/providers/test_api_base_trailing_slash_wire.py:317` adds a live regression with two separate owned peers and a private proxy. A unique, unmapped Ollama model has an explicit embedding base, while `OLLAMA_API_BASE` points to the other peer. The embedding and its exact request must succeed, and the default peer's entire log must contain only a successful control GET
- `tests/unit/test_register_model_custom_pricing.py` moves existing failure and reload injections to the catalog lookup boundary. Every existing assertion is retained

The original target name and all its assertions are unchanged, including `assert_one_request(wire.drain(), row.target, marker)` at line 314

## Evidence connecting the sender and receiver

Original failure run `43287547813`, job `131424823901`, SHA `d723545320080fd6e1dd3a4f24fb58af880e067b`

Job URL https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43287547813/job/131424823901

Full job log `ci-job.log` came from `gh run view 43287547813 --log-failed --job 131424823901`. Original artifact files remain under `/tmp/art/43287547813-providers/integration-providers`

The original failure recorded `[('POST', '/api/show'), ('POST', '/vy/v1/embeddings')]` and `Owned HTTP peer failed: KeyError('api')`

CI worker `gw12` used the 11400 port block. Its private PDF proxy was logged on 11425; following the worker's subsequent peer allocations places the failing Voyage peer on 11434. This is a reconstruction from allocation order, not a sender-address log. An Ollama timeout case using `ollama/nomic-embed-text` ran concurrently on `gw13`. The CI artifacts do not contain the sender PID or its call stack

The independent `trace-router.py` replay records the actual stack from a real Router construction through deployment-price registration, `_get_builtin_model_info_for_registration`, `lookup_model_info_for_registration`, and `OllamaModelInfo.get_runtime_model_info(api_base=None)`. Despite an explicit deployment API base of port 10000, the default listener on 11434 received `/api/show` with `{"name":"nomic-embed-text"}`, while the deployment listener received nothing. See `router-observation.json` and `router-observation.log`

An external diagnostic pytest plugin advanced the real allocator until the original Voyage peer owned 11434 and concurrently constructed a real Ollama Router with a different explicit API base. No product functions, responses or request logs were mocked or filtered. On unchanged product code this reproduced the original target's exact failure, and the captured stack identifies price registration as the source. On the fix the same forced placement passed and recorded zero runtime-model-info calls

## Rig

Commands ran from `/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm`

```bash
sudo service postgresql start
/home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-A/bin/redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6389 --save "" --appendonly no --daemonize yes --pidfile /home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-C/redis.pid --logfile /home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-C/redis.log
make install-test-deps
```

PostgreSQL 14.24, dedicated CI-version Redis 7.2.16, scripted upstream and owned proxy, synthetic credentials, `num_retries=0`. The proxy was restarted after the product fix so the repeated runs used newly loaded source. `start-proxy.sh`, `env.sh`, `setup.log`, `upstream.log`, `proxy.log`, `proxy-fixed.log` and `seed-router-settings-fixed.json` preserve setup details

Local differences from CI are Redis on dedicated port 6389 and no CI cgroup firewall. All provider traffic uses scripted local peers

The integration commands below begin with `source /home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-C/env.sh`. Let `F=tests/integration/providers/test_api_base_trailing_slash_wire.py` and `E=/home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-C`

## Unchanged main

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F::test_embedding_base_that_already_names_the_route_is_sent_as_is" --results "$E/base-target-w1"
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F" --results "$E/base-file-w1"
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=4 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F::test_embedding_base_that_already_names_the_route_is_sent_as_is" --results "$E/base-target-w4"
```

```text
============================== 8 passed in 8.30s ===============================
============================= 75 passed in 42.71s ==============================
============================== 8 passed in 52.28s ===============================
```

The natural runs did not reproduce the port collision. The controlled replay did reproduce it at one worker, so further escalation to eight workers or a workflow dispatch was unnecessary

## Red on main and temporary product break

After adding the final regression, both product lines were temporarily restored to unchanged main. `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- litellm/utils.py` succeeded before the run, proving the product file was byte-identical to the initial main base `d30b2b9b26213c79aa4cc50f962730f55d2479c5`

```bash
env -u OLLAMA_API_KEY -u OLLAMA_API_BASE PYTEST_PLUGINS=heal_c_port_replay INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F::test_embedding_base_that_already_names_the_route_is_sent_as_is" "$F::test_explicit_ollama_embedding_base_does_not_probe_the_default_server" --results "$E/main-price-registration-mutation-w1"
```

```text
=================== 2 failed, 7 passed, 7 warnings in 49.57s ===================
```

The original Voyage case failed with `KeyError('api')` and the same unwanted `/api/show` request as CI. In this real-registration replay the embedding arrived before the probe, reversing their CI arrival order but violating the identical exact-request assertion. The new regression failed because the default peer received `[('POST', '/api/show'), ('GET', '/control')]` instead of exactly `[('GET', '/control')]`

The product fix was restored exactly; `sha256sum --check fixed-utils.sha256` printed `litellm/utils.py: OK`

## Green controlled replay and final five target runs

The same diagnostic command with only the original target selected passed after restoring the fix

```text
======================== 8 passed, 5 warnings in 8.32s =========================
```

`fixed-probe-1.json` records listener `[11434]` and zero runtime-model-info calls

A second diagnostic repetition failed in the external hook with `No owned listener observed before the case completed`, not at the product's request assertion. That diagnostic failure was disclosed immediately. The five required final runs were then performed without the hook; the standalone controlled replay above remains the red/green mechanism proof

```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F::test_embedding_base_that_already_names_the_route_is_sent_as_is" --results "$E/final-target-w1-$i"
done
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F" --results "$E/fixed-file-w1"
```

```text
============================== 8 passed in 8.98s ===============================
============================== 8 passed in 8.17s ===============================
============================== 8 passed in 8.16s ===============================
============================== 8 passed in 7.67s ===============================
============================== 8 passed in 7.89s ===============================
======================== 76 passed in 83.02s (0:01:23) =========================
```

The 76-case file includes the final unique-model regression and had no unrelated failures

## Fresh-main rebase and unit checks

Rebased with `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main`, first onto `216a33071289de6f72fd76b09ae7607a33e8c40a` and finally onto `efe349de9f366b7f1b7d1181d9cbaea39504757b`

No incoming commits touched the target test file, so the conditional five unchanged-main runs were not required. Incoming changes to `utils.py` only affected Nace decisions, not the registration helper. On the rebased source, the live regression and the relevant unit files were checked again

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py providers "$F::test_explicit_ollama_embedding_base_does_not_probe_the_default_server" --results "$E/rebased-regression-w1"
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/test_register_model_custom_pricing.py tests/unit/test_register_model_zero_cost_persistence.py tests/unit/test_model_cost_aliases.py tests/unit/test_router_model_cost_isolation.py tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_model_cost_table.py -q
```

```text
============================== 1 passed in 42.88s ==============================
626 passed, 584 warnings in 76.96s (0:01:16)
```

An earlier run of those same unit files also passed all 626 cases in 77.14s. Warnings are existing deprecated Router API usage in the unit cases

The formatter and final rebase left the checked `utils.py` AST and both test files unchanged, verified by AST and byte comparisons. No checks with unchanged inputs were repeated just for the formatting commit

## Lint

The first `make lint` ran with the integration-only `PYTHONPATH` and failed the e2e type check with 14785 errors, beginning with missing stubs for `e2e_config`. It also caught the changed generator expression needing formatting. The expression was formatted, and lint was restarted in the normal repo environment without loading the integration environment. A focused environment check then printed `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes`, and the full e2e type check in the final lint run also printed zero errors

Final command `make lint > /home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-C/lint-final.log 2>&1`, with all queue and lock waits allowed to finish

Final `make lint` exited 0 after the queues and locks completed

```text
All checks passed!
All checks passed!
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
OK: every basedpyright rule is within its ceiling (94885 errors total, base efe349de9f36)
```

## Cleanup and limitations

Owned proxy and scripted upstream stopped with two verified roots, three owned processes, no forced termination and no survivors. Dedicated Redis on 6389 was verified against its PID file and stopped. Shared PostgreSQL and host Redis on 6379 were left alone

The temporary diagnostic `.pth` path was removed. Diagnostic scripts and logs remain outside the repository in this evidence directory

The first generic CI cleanup scan encountered an unrelated restricted `/proc` entry. Local cleanup therefore selected only processes with the expected proxy/upstream command, UID and Heal C identity before stopping their owned descendants

Final verification printed `Cleanup verified: no owned proxy/upstream, Redis6389 closed, diagnostic path absent`

Final `git status --short` contains only the pre-existing `?? litellm-rust/`. Two commits were pushed, the change and a formatter-only follow-up, both using the requested `test(providers): ...` style

No UI changes were made, so no visual check was needed. The original CI sender PID was not recorded; the named sender path was traced live and the identical failure was reproduced through real registration and the original test assertions

</details>

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix
✅ Test

</details>

title: fix(proxy): prevent customer registration into another organization's team
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Rejected requests could create members under another customer organization.

How it solves it:

- Check the default team's parent before registering a member.
- Return 403 with an explanation of the conflicting team.

## User Flow

Before, a conflicting default team causes a rejected request to create a member under the wrong customer.

1. An admin creates `qa-org-c:default` under customer `qa-org-b`.
2. A developer calls `http://127.0.0.1:41483/v1/responses` with organization alias `qa-tenant-c` and a new member ID.
3. The request returns 403, but the member appears under `qa-org-b`.

After, the same conflict is rejected before a member is created.

1. An admin creates `qa-org-c:default` under customer `qa-org-b`.
2. A developer calls `http://127.0.0.1:41483/v1/responses` with organization alias `qa-tenant-c` and a new member ID.
3. The request returns 403 explaining the conflicting team, and no member appears under the other customer.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished and its findings are addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Verified with two proxy workers sharing a dedicated PostgreSQL database and Redis. Both workers listened on the same proxy port before and after. The comparison used explicitly restarted processes to keep each loaded revision fixed. Successful controls made real provider calls through the internal gateway. No provider call is needed for a rejected identity.

The branch was refreshed onto main `efe349de9f3` before publication. The only intervening base change concerns provider file-ID ownership, outside these customer and text-only inference paths. The tested customer files are byte-identical at current tip `13ee110e5b81ea1fd779272c011cf44f9eddb88a`. The before/after evidence below retains its original tested revisions.

The original parent-check regression fails on the base. At the tested tip, 202 targeted tests pass, including the unit test directory coverage checks, and `make check` passes. The shared SQLite test fixture now uses a positional placeholder, which fixes its Python 3.14 binding error. The installed Logfire pytest plugin was disabled because its telemetry dependency could not import `LogData`.

### Shared setup

Use an empty dedicated database and Redis instance. Supply `DATABASE_URL`, `QA_REDIS_HOST`, `QA_REDIS_PORT`, `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE`, and `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` at runtime. Set `QA_MASTER_KEY` to the clearly fake local-only value used in the client below. The gateway model IDs and the Messages native output maximum were checked against the current model catalog.


The webhook setting is unrelated to this fix. For this QA environment, `WEBHOOK_URL` pointed to a local receiver at `http://127.0.0.1:41484/events`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Client helper, save as qa_client.py</summary>

```python
import json
import os
import re
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

BASE = 'http://127.0.0.1:41483'
MASTER = 'sk-qa-placeholder-not-a-real-secret'
WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SENSITIVE_FIELDS = {'key', 'token', 'api_key', 'access_token', 'refresh_token', 'password', 'authorization'}
PRIVATE = tuple(filter(None, (
    os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY'),
    os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE'),
    urlsplit(os.environ.get('LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE', '')).hostname,
)))

def clean(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: '[REDACTED]' if k.lower() in SENSITIVE_FIELDS else clean(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [clean(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if value.startswith('resp_') and len(value) > 128:
            return '[opaque response ID omitted]'
        for secret in PRIVATE:
            value = value.replace(secret, '[REDACTED]')
        return re.sub(r'\bsk-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{12,}', '[REDACTED]', value)
    return value

def api(method, path, body=None, *, key=MASTER, headers=None, label=None, quiet=False):
    started = time.monotonic()
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path, method=method,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
        headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', **(headers or {})},
    )
    try:
        response = urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        text = response.read().decode()
        try:
            data = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            data = text
        status = response.status
        metadata = {k: v for k, v in response.headers.items() if k.lower() in {'content-type', 'x-litellm-response-cost'}}
    record = clean({
        'at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), 'label': label, 'method': method, 'path': path,
        'request': body, 'customer_headers': headers, 'status': status,
        'elapsed_seconds': round(time.monotonic() - started, 3), 'response_headers': metadata, 'response': data,
    })
    with (WORK / 'api-evidence.jsonl').open('a') as evidence:
        evidence.write(json.dumps(record) + '\n')
    if not quiet:
        print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
    return status, data

def org(org_id, alias, *, budget=10, template=1):
    return api('POST', '/management/v1/customer_organizations', {
        'customer_org_id': org_id, 'alias': alias,
        'budget': {'max_budget': budget, 'budget_duration': '1mo'},
        'default_budgets': [{'name': 'Standard', 'max_budget': template, 'budget_duration': '1mo', 'is_default': True}],
    })

def customer_headers(alias, member=None):
    return {'x-litellm-customer-org-alias': alias, **({'x-litellm-customer-member-id': member} if member else {})}

def virtual_key(alias, *, org_id=None):
    status, data = api('POST', '/key/generate', {
        'key_alias': alias, 'models': ['qa-openai', 'qa-anthropic'],
        **({'metadata': {'customer_org_id': org_id}} if org_id else {}),
    }, quiet=True)
    assert status == 200, clean(data)
    return data['key']

def infer(route, *, alias, member, key=MASTER, label=None, quiet=False, **extra):
    headers = customer_headers(alias, member)
    if route == 'chat':
        path, body = '/v1/chat/completions', {
            'model': 'qa-openai', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply exactly QA OK.'}], **extra,
        }
    elif route == 'responses':
        path, body = '/v1/responses', {'model': 'qa-openai', 'input': 'Reply exactly QA OK.', **extra}
    else:
        path, body = '/v1/messages', {
            'model': 'qa-anthropic', 'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply exactly QA OK.'}],
            'max_tokens': 128000, **extra,
        }
    return api('POST', path, body, key=key, headers=headers, label=label or route, quiet=quiet)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Create the three customers and conflicting default team</summary>

```python
from qa_client import api, org

for suffix in ("a", "b", "c"):
    org("qa-org-" + suffix, "qa-tenant-" + suffix)
api("POST", "/management/v1/customer_teams", {
    "customer_team_id": "qa-org-c:default",
    "parent_org_id": "qa-org-b",
})
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Run collision-proof.py for each revision</summary>

```python
import os
from qa_client import api, infer, virtual_key
phase=os.environ.get('QA_PHASE','before')
key=virtual_key('qa-collision-'+phase)
for route in ('chat','responses','messages'):
    member='qa-collision-'+route
    before_status,_=api('GET','/management/v1/customer_members/'+member,label=phase+'-'+route+'-absent')
    assert before_status==404
    status,result=infer(route,alias='qa-tenant-c',member=member,key=key)
    after_status,member_result=api('GET','/management/v1/customer_members/'+member,label=phase+'-'+route+'-lookup')
    assert status==403
    assert after_status==(200 if phase=='before' else 404)
    if after_status==200:
        assert member_result['parent_team_id']=='qa-org-c:default'
        api('DELETE','/management/v1/customer_members/'+member,label=phase+'-'+route+'-cleanup')
    valid_status,_=infer(route,alias='qa-tenant-a',member='qa-valid-'+phase+'-'+route,key=key)
    assert valid_status==200
print('Collision proof '+phase+' passed for chat, Responses and Messages.')
```

```sh
QA_PHASE=before python3 collision-proof.py
# Restart the proxy on the fixed revision, preserving the same QA database.
QA_PHASE=after python3 collision-proof.py
```

</details>

### Before, 216a33071289de6f72fd76b09ae7607a33e8c40a

#### Chat Completions

1. POST `/v1/chat/completions` returns 403.
2. GET the new member returns 200 with parent `qa-org-c:default`, which belongs to `qa-org-b`.
3. The valid customer control returns 200.

#### Responses

1. POST `/v1/responses` returns 403.
2. GET the new member returns 200 with the same incorrect parent.
3. The valid customer control returns 200.

#### Messages

1. POST `/v1/messages` returns 403.
2. GET the new member returns 200 with the same incorrect parent.
3. The valid customer control returns 200.

### After, 78a497ab799cb6b2844a040aaebfedb1fe87711b

#### Chat Completions

1. POST `/v1/chat/completions` returns 403, `The default customer team belongs to a different organization`.
2. GET the new member returns 404. No member was created.
3. The valid customer control returns 200.

#### Responses

1. POST `/v1/responses` returns 403 with the same explanation.
2. GET the new member returns 404. No member was created.
3. The valid customer control returns 200.

#### Messages

1. POST `/v1/messages` returns 403 with the same explanation in the Anthropic error shape.
2. GET the new member returns 404. No member was created.
3. The valid customer control returns 200.

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Medium

- Existing members created under an incorrect parent require admin cleanup.

## Final Attestation

- [x] Regression tests and live requests cover the changed registration boundary.

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes customer member auto-registration and auth error handling in the proxy; wrong-team conflicts now hard-fail with 403 instead of silently creating cross-org members.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a bug where **auto-registration** could create customer members under another org’s default team when that team ID was owned by a different `parent_org_id`.
> 
> **`ensure_customer_member`** now verifies the resolved default team’s `parent_org_id` matches the requested organization; mismatches return **`Failure(ErrorCode.FORBIDDEN)`** instead of creating a member. **`_register_member`** turns that into a **403** auth error explaining the default team belongs to a different organization, rather than logging and falling through like other registration failures.
> 
> Tests cover the forbidden-vs-budget-required status codes and a conflicting default-team scenario. The shared SQLite test DB adapter swaps a PostgreSQL-style placeholder for **`?`** so raw queries bind correctly on Python 3.14.

title: test(observability): identify team datastore spans by team id in otel excluded services matrix
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

An OpenTelemetry integration test started failing after #51428 added a cache lookup that runs before key authentication finishes. The test decided which Redis spans belong to a team by checking whether they sat directly under the auth span, so the new, correctly operator-only lookup was counted as a team span that should have been exported. This PR identifies team spans by the team id they actually carry, keeping every assertion exact

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0018b787be4347e394bc450ca32e1f1e
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0018b787be4347e394bc450ca32e1f1e?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Cache-hit twin test failed 3 times after #51428
- Test guessed team spans from parent span shape

How it solves it:

- Identify team datastore spans by their exported team id
- All assertions and timeouts unchanged

CI evidence: [job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43343240862/job/131616359986), failed 3 times

Mechanism: the test's post-auth classifier treated "not directly parented by the auth span" as post-auth, which is coupled to span layout; #51428 added a pre-auth `redis.get auth_cache` lookup outside the auth span that is correctly operator-only

Fix: classify by `litellm.team.id`, which is only set after authentication

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 67bb6ffe5c2cb364a50c258e9fb1e7dbfefbc6f8: test-only change, proven with the integration rig at 1 worker (`INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions <node-or-file>`, retries off)

1. Unchanged main, whole file: 1 failed, 95 passed, the same missing span as CI
2. Fix, the function five times: 4 passed each run
3. Fix, whole file once: 96 passed
4. Temporary product break (response-cache Redis spans dropped from team export): 2 failed, then restored
5. `make lint`: exit 0

<details>
<summary>Full evidence</summary>

## Heal B evidence

Branch `litellm_flakeheal_20261113_test_unconfigured_cache_hit_twin_keeps_d`

Tip `67bb6ffe5c2cb364a50c258e9fb1e7dbfefbc6f8`

Pushed yes, with the remote tip verified against the local 40-character SHA

Only `tests/integration/observability/test_otel_excluded_services_matrix.py` changes, with five inserted lines and two deleted lines

### What changed

The test now recognizes authenticated datastore spans by their exported team identity, `litellm.team.id`, rather than their parent span

The proxy seeds that identity after the auth span closes. The pre-auth `redis.get auth_cache` lookup added by #51428 correctly has no team identity and stays operator-only. Authenticated datastore spans carry team identity and must appear in the tenant trace

All assertions, timeouts and polling conditions remain unchanged apart from the helper's classification rule, including the requirement that every classified datastore span ID appears in the tenant trace. No retries, skips, xfails or product changes were added

### Rig and environment

The rig follows `.github/workflows/test-integration.yml` and `.github/scripts/ci/run_integration.sh`, using PostgreSQL started with `sudo service postgresql start`, Redis 7.2.16, the scripted upstream and real proxy processes

The runner used `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1` throughout. The file itself starts private two-worker proxies for its fan-out and worker-loss checks. The runner disables the pytest retry plugins, and both the shared and owned proxies use `num_retries=0`

The local setup reused Heal A's environment, with the Heal B run ID and dedicated Redis on port 6389. Setup helpers and logs are under `/home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-B`. Local PostgreSQL is 14.24, and no CI cgroup egress firewall was installed. Requests use synthetic local fixtures and no provider credentials

After rebasing across native Redis changes, `make install-test-deps` rebuilt the native extension and generated Prisma successfully. The shared proxy was restarted and retries were reseeded with the CI helper's request

```bash
source /home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-B/env.sh
curl --noproxy '*' -sSf -X POST "$INTEGRATION_PROXY_URL/config/update" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"router_settings": {"num_retries": 0}}'
```

The following abbreviations expand to the exact verification paths

```bash
E=/home/ubuntu/scratchpad/heal-B
F=tests/integration/observability/test_otel_excluded_services_matrix.py
T="$F::test_unconfigured_cache_hit_twin_keeps_datastore_spans"
source "$E/env.sh"
```

### Red on unchanged main

The branch started at fresh main `865eb25555eece66b5080951605aacc42868a40e`

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions "$T" --results "$E/base-target-w1" > "$E/base-target-w1.log" 2>&1
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions "$F" --results "$E/base-file-w1" > "$E/base-file-w1.log" 2>&1
```

```text
============= 1 failed, 3 passed, 2 warnings in 164.29s (0:02:44) =============
============= 1 failed, 95 passed, 2 warnings in 820.01s (0:13:40) =============
```

Both failures demanded operator-only `redis.get auth_cache` spans from the tenant trace. No other test failed in the unchanged whole-file run. Counts 4 and 8 were not needed because the failure reproduced at 1

A recorded real OTLP trace also isolates the mechanism with fixed input. Its pre-auth cache read has no team identity and is absent from the tenant export, while its authenticated response-cache read carries team identity and reaches the tenant

```bash
uv run --no-sync python "$E/replay-classifier.py"
```

On the original classifier, exit 1

```text
Missing classified post-auth spans: ('redis.get auth_cache', 'redis.get auth_cache')
AssertionError: ('redis.get auth_cache', 'redis.get auth_cache')
```

On the replacement classifier, exit 0

```text
Missing classified post-auth spans: ()
Captured trace replay passed
```

Raw snapshots and the trace-specific observation are saved as `baseline-sink-10200.json`, `baseline-sink-10201.json` and `classification-observation.json` under the evidence directory

### Rebase and fresh-main reproduction

```bash
git fetch origin main
git rebase origin/main
git log --format='%H %s' 865eb25555eece66b5080951605aacc42868a40e..origin/main -- "$F"
```

Rebase succeeded onto `f4f94cc848fcfc84ae19450c4e2f8bd52f45e883`. The target-file history command printed nothing, so the conditional five unchanged-main runs were not required

Main nevertheless brought substantial native Redis and auth changes, so verification was repeated on the new base. The original helper was temporarily restored, and `git diff --exit-code origin/main` exited 0, confirming the tracked working tree exactly matched that main revision

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions "$T" --results "$E/rebased-base-target-w1-1" > "$E/rebased-base-target-w1-1.log" 2>&1
```

```text
============= 1 failed, 3 passed, 2 warnings in 169.19s (0:02:49) ==============
```

The same missing pre-auth `redis.get auth_cache` span reproduced. The committed helper was then restored exactly

### Temporary product break on the rebased source

The following temporary condition was added to tenant destination filtering in `litellm/integrations/otel/plumbing/providers.py`, suppressing real response-cache Redis spans

```diff
                 or not _in_scope(span, destination.span_scope)
+                or span.name == "redis.get llm_response"
                 or _is_excluded_database_span(
```

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions "$T" --results "$E/rebased-mutation-target-w1" > "$E/rebased-mutation-target-w1.log" 2>&1
```

```text
============= 2 failed, 2 passed, 2 warnings in 210.68s (0:03:30) ==============
```

Both messages variants failed the existing assertion that Redis spans reach the tenant. The product mutation was removed, and `git diff --exit-code` exited 0 before the final positive runs

### Final fixed verification on the rebased commit

One attempt run alongside lint timed out before the changed classifier was called

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions "$T" --results "$E/rebased-fix-target-w1-1" > "$E/rebased-fix-target-w1-1.log" 2>&1
```

```text
E   Failed: Timeout (>120.0s) from pytest-timeout.
119.40s setup    tests/integration/observability/test_otel_excluded_services_matrix.py::test_unconfigured_cache_hit_twin_keeps_datastore_spans[null_block-chat]
============= 1 failed, 3 passed, 2 warnings in 188.08s (0:03:08) ==============
```

The timeout includes module fixture setup. Proxy readiness took 111.49 seconds in that fixture, compared with 51.54 and 56.24 seconds in the fresh unchanged-main run. The stack stopped while reading the next sink cursor, before any call to the changed helper. Concurrent lint is a suspected source of startup contention, not a proven cause. Lint was allowed to finish before all subsequent runs, without changing source, waits or timeouts

```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  INTEGRATION_WORKERS=1 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions "$T" --results "$E/rebased-serial-fix-target-w1-$i" > "$E/rebased-serial-fix-target-w1-$i.log" 2>&1 || exit "$?"
```

The two warnings concern Pydantic's handling of `ReadOnly` TypedDict fields and also appear on unchanged main. Installed Pydantic 2.13.4 and typing-extensions 4.15.0 match the lockfile entries

### Lint on the rebased source

```text
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

### Earlier checks before rebase

The same fix had already passed five target runs and the whole file on the original base, using `fix-target-w1-1` through `fix-target-w1-5` and `fix-file-w1` as the corresponding results paths

Both mutations were restored exactly

## Summary

The fal-ai pricing sync adds the Decart Lucy 5B image-to-video endpoint, one of the 10 fal-ai ids whose llms.txt pages 404ed in the previous run.

## Rows

**fal_ai/decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video** (kind page). Fal's model list emits this endpoint as `fal-ai/decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video`, but https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video 301s to https://fal.ai/models/decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video and that page's llms.txt states `Model ID: decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video`, so the row takes the canonical id, the key form the other `fal_ai/decart/` rows use. title: feat(db): take the rollup lock_timeout from the caller and keep team lock statements unnamed under PgBouncer
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description [insert handwritten description here]
Details Stacked on #49801, the fifth PR of the native DB foundation stack. ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Native rollup transactions hardcode a 5000ms `lock_timeout` - Python reads it from `SPEND_ROLLUP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS`, so the two paths can disagree - Team lock and member spend statements are always prepared by name - Prisma sends them unnamed under `pgbouncer=true` How it solves it: - `begin` takes the `lock_timeout` from the caller as whole positive milliseconds (`NonZeroU32`), like `SPEND_ROLLUP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` - A `Duration` let a sub-millisecond or zero value become `0ms`, which Postgres reads as no timeout - It binds the value into `set_config`, the same SQL Python sends - `begin`, `lock_team` and `add_team_member_spend` take a `named` flag - They run through `Statements`, which sends unnamed statements when the cache is off Nothing outside `crates/db` calls these three functions yet, so no user sees a change from this PR alone. ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix E2E exception at d73d1a64af2. Scope is `crates/db/src/spend/team_lock.rs`, `crates/db/src/spend/team_member_spend.rs`, one renamed `.sqlx` query file for the parameterised `set_config` query and one row of `crates/db/AGENTS.md`. `begin`, `lock_team` and `add_team_member_spend` have no caller outside the db crate, checked with a grep across `litellm/rust/crates`. No request to a running proxy reaches this code before or after the change, so there is no user flow to run. Lock behavior would normally need live proof, and the PR that adds the first caller owes it. Until then the db crate's integration tests run the real SQL against a Prisma-migrated Postgres 18.6 with no mocks. Static checks at the tip, both clean. ```bash SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo check --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-db --tests --locked SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo check --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-python-bridge --locked SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo clippy --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-db --tests --locked -- -D warnings cargo fmt --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-db -- --check ``` The two touched test modules, with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at the local Prisma-migrated Postgres. ```bash SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo test --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-db --locked -- --include-ignored spend::team_lock spend::team_member_spend ``` ``` test spend::team_lock::tests::team_lock_is_held_until_rollback::case_1_transaction_scoped ... ok test spend::team_member_spend::tests::membership_spend_preserves_roster_guard_and_fractional_costs::case_1_zero_then_quarter ... ok test spend::team_member_spend::tests::membership_spend_preserves_roster_guard_and_fractional_costs::case_2_zero_then_eighth ... ok test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 108 filtered out ``` The whole db crate suite against the same database. ```bash SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo test --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-db --locked -- --include-ignored ``` ``` test result: ok. 111 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out ``` The lock test opens the transaction with a 1500ms timeout and reads `current_setting('lock_timeout')` back from Postgres. With `begin` changed to ignore the caller's value and send 5000ms, it fails. ``` assertion `left == right` failed left: "5s" right: "1500ms" ``` ## Type New Feature ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - No test in this PR calls the three functions with `named` false - The unnamed path itself is tested on `Statements` in #49798 - A caller passing the wrong flag here would not fail a test ### Low - No production caller yet, so live proxy proof waits for the first one - The caller must pass `SPEND_ROLLUP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` itself, nothing here reads it ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

title: feat(proxy): run requests with unknown customer ids untracked instead of refusing them
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

upsert customer requests instead of rejecting

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customers send `x-litellm-customer-org-alias` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id` from code paths where the ids are not always set up on our side yet
- Today an id the proxy does not know turns the request into a 401, so a customer's traffic fails over an attribution header
- The headers are for tracking spend, they should never be the reason a request is refused

How it solves it:

- An unknown member id or unknown alias is logged at warning and the request runs without that customer level
- Alias known, member unknown and not registrable (org has no default budget): the request is charged to the organization alone
- Alias of org B with a member of org A is still 403, an alias two orgs share is still 400, those are misconfigurations the caller must see
- `resolve_customer_hierarchy` now returns `CustomerHierarchyAuth | None`, which is what `UserAPIKeyAuth.customer_hierarchy` already was
- Review follow-ups from https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51546: the key's `customer_org_id` scope is checked against the aliased organization before the registrar runs, so a key pinned to org A gets its 403 for org B's alias without creating rows there; customer headers are ignored on routes the builder serves without credentials (`/`, `/routes`, `/health/*`); a member id past the shared 256-character identifier bound is not registered and the organization alone is charged

Stacked on https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51546 and https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51543, rebased on main after https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51489 merged. This PR's own commits are `235dae20c1` and `7812aa8523`.

## User Flow

Before: an id we do not know fails the request

1. The app sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a shared key and `x-litellm-customer-member-id: user-9`, for a user who exists in no organization yet
2. 401 `customer member not found: user-9`
3. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: nobody` alone is also 401, and an alias of an org with no default budget plus a new member id is 401 too

After: the request runs, spend lands wherever the proxy can place it

1. Same request with `x-litellm-customer-member-id: user-9`
2. 200, nothing is charged to a customer row, the proxy log says `Customer x-litellm-customer-member-id not tracked, member not found: user-9`
3. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: nobody` alone is 200 and untracked. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: acme` plus a member id the org cannot register is 200 and the org's `spend` grows, with a daily row carrying the org id and an empty member id
4. A member of another org with alias `acme` is still 403, a shared alias still 400

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Same rig as https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51543: proxy on the tested commit with 2 workers, local Postgres, one Redis for `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`, real OpenAI calls to `gpt-5-mini`, env vars `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_customer_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

Setup, master key, `S` a run suffix:

```
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id":"$S-nobudget","alias":"$S-nobudget","budget":{"max_budget":100}}
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id":"$S-org","alias":"$S-acme","default_budgets":[{"name":"std","max_budget":10,"is_default":true}]}
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id":"$S-dup1","alias":"$S-shared"}
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id":"$S-dup2","alias":"$S-shared"}
POST /key/generate {"key_alias":"$S-svc"}   -> $VK
```

Each request is `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $VK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'` plus the listed headers.

### Before (10b1b051ab)

```
new member, no alias:         401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer member not found: up1794541346-user9", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-member-id", "code": "401"}
new member, org w/o budget:   401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer member not found: up1794541346-user10", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-member-id", "code": "401"}
unknown alias:                401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer organization alias not found: nobody-al1794540823", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-org-alias", "code": "401"}
```

### After (7c0f23db39)

```
unknown member, no alias:        200 {"id": "chatcmpl-Ejcbjd79wXq8InDKrkw08bVOirNgV"}
unknown alias only:              200 {"id": "chatcmpl-Ejcbktl7NTUNdb3pz5d2Pw2qwv0Sk"}
unknown alias + unknown member:  200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcbldY9ZSnjL1hMhIlS7g14ckYyQ"}
org w/o default budget + member: 200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcbmHhZykQzO1AarVHdfFrPnTASa"}
registered member (PR 2 path):   200 {"id": "chatcmpl-Ejcbn1tTJgxLa4w5BgTtBYEXUG6Qo"}
member of org A + alias of B:    403 {"message": "Customer member un1794541873-user2 does not belong to the organization aliased un1794541873-nobudget", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-org-alias", "code": "403"}
shared alias (ambiguous):        400 {"message": "Customer organization alias is not unique: un1794541873-shared", "type": "bad_request_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-org-alias", "code": "400"}
```

Rows after the 30s flush. The three untracked calls charged no customer row, the unregistrable member's call landed on its org only:

```
org     un1794541873-nobudget  spend=1.2e-05
org     un1794541873-org       spend=1.2e-05
org     un1794541873-dup1      spend=0
org     un1794541873-dup2      spend=0
member  un1794541873-user2     parent_team_id=un1794541873-org:default  spend=1.2e-05
daily   org=un1794541873-nobudget  member=""                   api_requests=1
daily   org=un1794541873-org       member=un1794541873-user2  api_requests=1
```

Focused checks at the tip: `pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_hierarchy_auth.py tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_member_auto_create.py tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_user_api_key_auth.py -k customer` 33 passed. `basedpyright` on the touched files 0 errors. `ruff_strict_gate.py` and `type_discipline_gate.py` against the base branch: no rule grew. Mutation check: raising in `_untracked` instead of returning `None` turns `test_an_unknown_member_or_a_proxy_without_a_database_runs_the_request_untracked` and `test_an_unknown_alias_runs_untracked_and_a_shared_alias_is_rejected_as_ambiguous` red, returning `None` instead of `organization` when registration fails turns `test_an_unknown_member_runs_untracked_without_an_alias_and_on_the_organization_when_registration_fails` red.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A typo in the member or alias header now silently drops the request from customer spend tracking. The warning log line is the only signal. A `reject_unknown_customer_ids` setting for deployments that want the old 401 is a one-flag follow-up if wanted

### Low

- Until https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51546, https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51543 and https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51489 merge this diff includes their commits

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

### Review follow-ups (7812aa8523)

Unit tests, run at the tip with `uv run pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_hierarchy_auth.py tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_user_api_key_auth_request_flow.py -k "pinned_to_another_organization_is_refused or identifier_bound or public_route_ignores"`, 3 passed. Mutation: with the source changes stashed and the tests kept, the same three fail (403 raised after the registrar already ran, `u * 257` registered, `/` with both headers read `litellm_customerorganizationtable`).

title: feat(proxy): register unknown customer members in the aliased organization's default team
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customers send `x-litellm-customer-org-alias` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id` on every call
- Their users show up for the first time on their first request
- Today that first request is refused with 401 until an admin creates the member

How it solves it:

- Unknown member plus a known alias creates the member in the org's `default` team
- The `default` team (`<org_id>:default`) is created on first use, on the org's default budget
- Registration goes through the same management helper the API uses, one row under races
- No alias, or an org without a default budget, keeps the 401
- `ensure_customer_member` is injected into auth, so tests swap it without patching

Stacked on https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51543, rebased on main after https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51489 merged. This PR's own commits start at `6fdc6368e9`.

## User Flow

Before: a customer's new user is refused until an admin registers them

1. Admin creates an org with `POST /management/v1/customer_organizations` `{"customer_org_id": "org-1", "alias": "acme", "default_budgets": [{"name": "std", "max_budget": 10, "is_default": true}]}`
2. The app sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: acme` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id: user-7` for a user nobody registered
3. 401 `customer member not found: user-7`
4. The admin has to `POST /management/v1/customer_members` first, then the user can work

After: the same first request works and the user is registered on the org default budget

1. Same org, same headers
2. 200. `GET /management/v1/customer_members/user-7` now shows `parent_team_id: "org-1:default"` and `effective_budget.max_budget: 10`
3. Every later call with those headers charges `user-7`, and the member's cap is enforced like any registered member (422 once spend passes 10)
4. The member header without an alias, or an alias of an org that has no default budget, is still 401

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)

- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Same rig as https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51543: proxy on the tested commit with 2 workers, local Postgres, one Redis for `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`, real OpenAI calls to `gpt-5-mini`, env vars `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_customer_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

Setup, master key, `S` a run suffix. The member cap is tiny so one call crosses it:

```
POST /management/v1/customer_organizations {"customer_org_id":"$S-org","alias":"$S-acme","default_budgets":[{"name":"std","max_budget":0.00002,"is_default":true}]}

POST /key/generate {"key_alias":"$S-svc"}   -> $VK
```

Each request is `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $VK" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'` plus the listed headers.

### Before (dec32d29b7)

#### A member nobody registered is refused

1. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $S-acme` + `x-litellm-customer-member-id: new-$S` -> `401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer member not found: new-al1794540823", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-member-id", "code": "401"}`

### After (10b1b051ab)

#### First request registers the member, later ones are budgeted

```
new member + alias (1st):     200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcTEjwKL84NTBWnFpakEpOD2WIDS"}
same member + alias (2nd):    200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcTFlP8rBg4qTrPQAK9JKHfEKVid"}
second new member + alias:    200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcTGZAaGGBuvUKkY7RdA91qfoUFK"}
new member, no alias:         401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer member not found: up1794541346-user9", ...}
new member, org w/o budget:   401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer member not found: up1794541346-user10", ...}
```

Rows written (`created_by` is the header name so the audit trail says who made them):

```
team    up1794541346-org:default   alias=default  parent_org_id=up1794541346-org  created_by=x-litellm-customer-member-id
member  up1794541346-user7         parent_team_id=up1794541346-org:default  budget_id set
member  up1794541346-user8         parent_team_id=up1794541346-org:default  budget_id set
GET /management/v1/customer_members/up1794541346-user7 -> parent_team_id "up1794541346-org:default", effective_budget.max_budget 2e-05
```

70s later, past the cache TTL:

```
same member + alias (3rd):    422 {"message": "ExceededBudget: customer_member=up1794541346-user7 over budget. Spend=2.4e-05, Budget=2e-05", "type": "budget_exceeded", "code": "422"}
spend  up1794541346-user7  2.4e-05
spend  up1794541346-user8  1.2e-05
```

Focused checks at the tip: `pytest tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_member_auto_create.py tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_customer_hierarchy_auth.py` 28 passed. `ruff_strict_gate.py` and `type_discipline_gate.py` against the base branch: no rule grew. Mutation check: returning `None` from `_register_member` turns `test_a_member_the_aliased_organization_has_never_seen_is_registered_there_and_served` red, skipping the `ALREADY_EXISTS` retry in `ensure_customer_member` turns `test_registering_the_same_member_twice_keeps_one_row_and_reuses_an_existing_default_team` red.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Any caller holding a key can create member rows in an org by sending new ids with its alias. Pin keys to an org with `metadata.customer_org_id` (403 on other orgs) where that matters

### Low

- An org without a default budget still gets its empty `default` team created on the first attempt
- The first request from a new user pays two extra writes (team on first use, then member)
- Until https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51543 and https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51489 merge this diff includes their commits

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
