title: fix(cost-map): restore backward compatibility after the Rust loader move
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- This is followup on https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50501
- An invalid cost map below is one with a top-level value that is not an object, for example `"_comment": "mirrored 2026-11-30"` next to the model rows

| Case | Before #50501 | After #50501 (main today) | After this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cost map saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark or as UTF-16 | Loads | Reload 502, startup falls back to the bundled map | Loads |
| `alias_of` row that also carries other fields | Served as its target | Name dropped, model unmapped | Served as its target |
| `register_model(url)` with `LITELLM_OFFLINE_MODE=true` | No request | Makes the request | No request |
| `register_model(None)` | No-op | `TypeError` | No-op |
| POST /reload/model_cost_map with an invalid cost map | 500, prices kept | 500, one worker's prices change | 502, prices kept |
| Starting the proxy, or running `import litellm`, with an invalid cost map | The import raises, so the process does not start | The import raises, so the process does not start | Starts on the bundled map and reports the reason in `fallback_reason` |
| `refetch_model_cost_map` | Returns the map, caller publishes | Installs and publishes in one step | Installs and publishes in one step |
| `register_model(url)` with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` | URL ignored | Makes the request | Makes the request |
| `NaN`, `Infinity`, out-of-range numbers | Accepted | Document refused | Document refused |
| UTF-16 without a byte order mark, UTF-32 | Accepted | Refused | Refused |
| Public names `RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`, `FALLBACK_GENERALIZATIONS_KEY`, `RETRYABLE_FETCH_STATUS_CODES`, `git_blob_id` | Importable | `ImportError` | Importable, same values and same function |
| `utils._runtime_registered_model_cost`, which downstream test code replaces | A dict of kept registrations | `AttributeError` | An always-empty dict, since registrations now live in Rust |
| Other private names #50501 removed | Importable | `ImportError` | `ImportError` |

The first four rows are restored exactly. The next two are fixed to something new, a clean 502 and a startup that survives. The four rows after that are left as main has them. The last three rows follow one rule, now written in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/AGENTS.md`. A removed name comes back when it is public and shipped in a stable release, or when it is private, outside code calls it, and the compat keeps that code working. A private name whose old behavior cannot be kept stays removed, because an `ImportError` names what changed and a no-op that answers wrongly hides it

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A refused cost map reload could still change one worker's prices
- A cost map saved with a byte order mark stopped loading
- An `alias_of` row carrying other fields lost its model name
- `register_model(url)` made a network request in offline mode
- Public loader names and `register_model(None)` broke for SDK callers

How it solves it:

- Refuse a document whose top-level value is not a row
- Read UTF-8 and UTF-16 documents that start with a byte order mark
- Serve an `alias_of` row as its target
- Skip the URL fetch when `LITELLM_OFFLINE_MODE` is set
- Bring back the public names and one private name outside code uses

Intentional product change: a cost map with a top-level value that is not an object is now refused as a whole. A reload answers 502 and keeps prices where it used to answer 500, and boot falls back to the bundled map where the import used to fail.

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin reloads a self-hosted cost map that carries a comment key. The reload reports a failure, but one worker starts billing the new prices

1. They host their own cost map and add `"_comment": "mirrored 2026-11-30"` next to the model rows
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/reload/model_cost_map and get 500 with `'str' object has no attribute 'get'`
3. GET https://litellm-domain/model/info shows the new price on some calls and the old price on others
4. The same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions is billed at two costs, depending on which worker answers

After: the same reload is refused cleanly and every worker keeps the old prices

1. They host their own cost map and add `"_comment": "mirrored 2026-11-30"` next to the model rows
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/reload/model_cost_map and get 502 naming `_comment` and saying current pricing data was kept
3. GET https://litellm-domain/model/info shows the old price on every call
4. Every POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions is billed at the old cost

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, identical for both runs

- Postgres in local Docker with a fresh database per run, and one dedicated `redis-server --port 6390`, flushed before each run
- A local cost server on port 8765 hands out the bundled cost map. A `state` file picks what the next GET returns, and `<kind> <N>` multiplies the input and output price of `gpt-5.4-nano` and `gemini/gemini-4-carbon` by N
- Proxy command, run from the checkout under test

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config proof_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

- `--reload` is dropped from the usual QA command. It makes each worker re-read a `.env` with override, which would replace this proof's database and cost map URL. Two worker PIDs were checked on both runs
- Env var names: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` (placeholder, never called), `LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/cost.json`, `LITELLM_MODE=PRODUCTION`, `PYTHONPATH` set to the checkout
- `proof_config.yaml` is `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` plus the lines below. The real provider calls go to `gpt-5.4-nano` through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, priced from the catalog row the cost server scales

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-4-carbon
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-4-carbon
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
  - model_name: real-nano
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/openai/gpt-5.4-nano
      api_base: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
      api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY
    model_info:
      base_model: gpt-5.4-nano
general_settings:
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  proxy_config_reload_interval_seconds: 5
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6390
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6390
```

<details>
<summary>cost_server.py</summary>

```python
"""Serves the bundled cost map with two rows scaled. The state file picks what the next GET returns."""

import json
import sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

MAP, STATE, PORT = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3])
BUNDLED = json.loads(MAP.read_text())
ROWS = ("gemini/gemini-4-carbon", "gpt-5.4-nano")
FIELDS = ("input_cost_per_token", "output_cost_per_token")
POINTER = {"gemini/carbon-latest": {"alias_of": "gemini/gemini-4-carbon", "input_cost_per_token": 9e-06}}


def document(scale: float, extra: dict) -> str:
    scaled = {row: {**BUNDLED[row], **{field: BUNDLED[row][field] * scale for field in FIELDS}} for row in ROWS}
    return json.dumps({**BUNDLED, **scaled, **extra})


def body(state: str) -> bytes:
    kind, _, scale = state.partition(" ")
    match kind:
        case "plain":
            return document(float(scale), {}).encode()
        case "comment":
            return document(float(scale), {"_comment": "mirrored 2026-11-30"}).encode()
        case "bom":
            return b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + document(float(scale), {}).encode()
        case "utf16":
            return document(float(scale), {}).encode("utf-16")
        case "pointer":
            return document(float(scale), POINTER).encode()
    raise ValueError(state)


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        payload = body(STATE.read_text().strip())
        with STATE.with_suffix(".requests").open("a") as log:
            log.write(f"GET {self.path}\n")
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(payload)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(payload)

    def log_message(self, *_: object) -> None:
        return


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", PORT), Handler).serve_forever()
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Shell helpers used by the cases</summary>

```bash
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
JSON="Content-Type: application/json"
reload() { curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/reload/model_cost_map -H "$AUTH" -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" | cut -c1-200; }
# The listed input price of real-nano over 60 calls, so both workers answer
listed() { sleep 6; for i in $(seq 60); do curl -s localhost:4000/model/info -H "$AUTH" | jq -c '[.data[] | select(.model_name=="real-nano") | .model_info.input_cost_per_token][0]'; done | sort | uniq -c; }
# Six real chat completions and the cost each response reports
billed() { for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "$AUTH" -H "$JSON" -d '{"model":"real-nano","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word: ok"}]}' | grep -i "^x-litellm-response-cost:" | tr -d "\r"; done | sort | uniq -c; }
```

</details>

Every case starts from `echo "plain 1" > state` and a successful reload, so both workers list `2E-7` and bill `8.85e-06` for the 13 prompt and 5 completion tokens of the test call

### Before (f85aa27c162)

#### Case 1, a cost map with a top-level comment string

1. `echo "comment 5" > state` then `reload`
```
{"detail":"Failed to reload model cost map: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'"}
HTTP 500
```
2. `listed`
```
  51 0.000001
   9 2E-7
```
3. `billed`
```
   5 x-litellm-response-cost: 4.425e-05
   1 x-litellm-response-cost: 8.85e-06
```

#### Case 2, a cost map saved with a byte order mark, then one saved as UTF-16

1. `echo "bom 2" > state` then `reload`
```
{"detail":"Failed to reload model cost map: invalid JSON from http://127.0.0.1:8765/cost.json: catalog: invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1. Current pricing data was kept."}
HTTP 502
```
2. `echo "utf16 3" > state` then `reload` gives the same 502
3. `listed` and `billed`
```
  60 2E-7
   6 x-litellm-response-cost: 8.85e-06
```

#### Case 3, an alias_of row that also carries a price

1. `echo "pointer 1" > state` then `reload` answers 200. The document now has `"gemini/carbon-latest": {"alias_of": "gemini/gemini-4-carbon", "input_cost_per_token": 9e-06}`
2. POST localhost:4000/spend/calculate with a `completion_response` for model `gemini/carbon-latest` and 1000 prompt plus 1000 completion tokens, 12 times
```
  12 {"error":{"message":"This model isn't mapped yet. model=gemini/carbon-latest, custom_llm_p
```

#### Case 4, SDK register_model(url) in offline mode

1. `: > state.requests; LITELLM_OFFLINE_MODE=true python -c 'import litellm; litellm.register_model("http://127.0.0.1:8765/cost.json")' > /dev/null 2>&1; wc -l < state.requests`
```
       1
```

#### Case 5, names and inputs SDK callers use

1. `python -c 'from litellm.litellm_core_utils.get_model_cost_map import RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS; print(sorted(RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS))'`
```
ImportError: cannot import name 'RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS' from 'litellm.litellm_core_utils.get_model_cost_map'
```
2. `python -c 'import litellm; print(litellm.register_model(None))'`
```
TypeError: 'None' is not an instance of 'str'
```

### After (7d622a7cd3c)

The cases below ran at b68aedbcdf2. The tip adds only the restored names, the rule in `AGENTS.md` and unit tests, and the unit and SDK integration suites pass at the tip

#### Case 1, a cost map with a top-level comment string

1. `echo "comment 5" > state` then `reload`
```
{"detail":"Failed to reload model cost map: invalid JSON from http://127.0.0.1:8765/cost.json: _comment: a host table cannot serve a top-level value that is not a JSON object. Current pricing data was kept."}
HTTP 502
```
2. `listed`
```
  60 2E-7
```
3. `billed`
```
   6 x-litellm-response-cost: 8.85e-06
```

#### Case 2, a cost map saved with a byte order mark, then one saved as UTF-16

1. `echo "bom 2" > state` then `reload` answers 200, and `listed` shows the doubled price on both workers
```
{"message":"Price data reloaded successfully! 5972 models updated.","status":"success","models_count":5972, ...
HTTP 200
  60 4E-7
```
2. `echo "utf16 3" > state` then `reload` answers 200, and `listed` shows the tripled price
```
  60 6E-7
```
3. `billed`
```
   6 x-litellm-response-cost: 2.655e-05
```

#### Case 3, an alias_of row that also carries a price

1. `echo "pointer 1" > state` then `reload` answers 200
2. The same 12 POST localhost:4000/spend/calculate calls are priced as the target row
```
  12 {"cost":0.012}
```

#### Case 4, SDK register_model(url) in offline mode

1. The same command
```
       0
```

#### Case 5, names and inputs SDK callers use

1. The same import
```
['fallback_generalizations', 'sample_spec']
```
2. The same call
```
None
```

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- The edited proxy integration test did not run locally
  - `tests/integration/pricing` needs the Linux runner, so it first runs on main or with the `run-ci` label
  - Case 1 above covers the same behavior on a live proxy
- `utils._runtime_registered_model_cost` is importable but always empty
  - Code that replaces it in a test fixture keeps working, code that reads registrations from it sees none

### Low

- Private names #50501 removed stay removed when no outside caller was found or the old behavior cannot be kept
  - `_fetch_remote_model_cost_map_with_retry` and its sync twin have outside callers, but they pass an `httpx` client the fetch no longer uses
  - No outside caller was found for `_alias_groups`, `_expand_model_aliases`, `_cost_map_source_info`, `_finalize_loaded_model_cost_map`, `load_local_model_cost_map_with_revision`, `utils._model_cost_mutation_generation`, `utils._rebuild_model_cost_lowercase_map`, `utils._replace_cost_map_entry`, or the 21 helpers and types of the old Python fetch
  - The search was GitHub code search, which does not see private repos
- `refetch_model_cost_map` still installs and publishes in one step, as on main
- `register_model(url)` still fetches under `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP`, since that flag only says where the cost map comes from
- UTF-16 without a byte order mark and UTF-32 are still refused
- `NaN`, `Infinity` and out-of-range numbers are still refused
- The proof drops `--reload`, for the reason given in the shared setup

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: feat(proxy): name the customer organization by alias with x-litellm-customer-org-alias
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f9b98a5475934384a855b4b568918369?variant=devin
Requested by: @ishaan-j-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customers send one shared key per service and name the customer in headers
- Their apps know the customer by alias and the user by id, not by our org id
- `x-litellm-customer-member-id` alone cannot say which customer the request is for

How it solves it:

- New header `x-litellm-customer-org-alias`, resolved through `LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable.alias`
- Both headers: member resolved, alias must match the member's org, else 403
- Alias alone: org budget enforced, spend and daily rows charged to the org only
- Unknown alias 401, alias shared by several orgs 400
- Org alias changes evict the cached alias lookup

Rebased on main after https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51489 merged, the diff is now only this PR. Commits `cb8031d605` and `c623248c18`.

## User Flow

Before: a service key names the customer by alias and the proxy ignores it, so the request runs unbudgeted and unattributed

1. Admin creates an org with `POST /management/v1/customer_organizations` `{"customer_org_id": "org-1", "alias": "acme", "budget": {"max_budget": 100}}`
2. The app sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: acme` and `x-litellm-customer-member-id: user-7`
3. 200, but the alias is never read: a wrong alias, or an alias of another customer, also returns 200
4. With only the alias header the request is 200 and no customer row records the spend

After: the same headers charge the right organization and refuse the wrong one

1. Same org, same headers
2. 200, the member's org is checked against `acme`. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: other-customer` with that member returns 403 naming the header
3. With only the alias header the request is 200, the org's `spend` grows, and `GET /management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity?customer_org_ids=org-1` shows the request with an empty team and member
4. An alias no org carries returns 401, an alias two orgs share returns 400 `Customer organization alias is not unique`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem

### Before (4edfc4c891)

#### Alias header is ignored

1. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $S-acme` -> `200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcNBlvV3GosNuK5ETtRe72oAcx5m"}`
2. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: nobody-$S` -> `200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcNCZmwgcbrqfDQssdYCq50Yd05f"}`

```
alias + member (mismatch):    403 {"message": "Customer member al1794540823-member does not belong to the organization aliased al1794540823-other", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-org-alias", "code": "403"}
alias only:                   200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcKo0FTjDjXDaxXedQLp5iDOkqBg"}

unknown alias:                401 {"message": "Authentication Error - customer organization alias not found: nobody-al1794540823", "type": "auth_error", "param": "x-litellm-customer-org-alias", "code": "401"}

no header:                    200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcKrJVLRrGbprpETM2pPJrXMElcr"}
```

#### Alias rename evicts the cached lookup

1. `PATCH /management/v1/customer_organizations/$S-org {"alias":"$S-renamed"}` -> 200
2. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $S-acme` -> `401 customer organization alias not found`
3. `x-litellm-customer-org-alias: $S-renamed` -> `200 {"id": "chatcmpl-EjcKszD7O6ElphbStdarbC9rl40S3"}`

#### Spend lands on the right rows (after a 30s flush)

```

org    al1794540823-org2    0
team   al1794540823-team    2.4e-05                 (the 2 member calls)
```

### Medium

- `alias` is not unique in the schema, so two orgs with one alias make it unusable (400) until an admin renames one

title: fix(ci): update Soup Sieve across supported Python versions
body:
Refs #51521.

OSV flags Soup Sieve 2.9.2 in the existing CI lockfile. Update only this package while preserving the supported Python range and the lockfile's relative age policy.

| Interpreter | Resolution | Advisory status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python 3.11.5+ | Soup Sieve 4.1 | Both reported advisories patched |
| Python 3.10 / 3.11.0–3.11.4 | Soup Sieve 2.10 | Sibling-selector advisory patched; descendant-selector advisory remains unpatched |

The [descendant-selector fix](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f) requires Python 3.11.5+. The older-interpreter branch gets an exception through 2027-02-01, matching the repository's existing compatibility policy. Beautiful Soup enters through the `ci` group; its sole repository caller is the manual Bedrock pricing parser, which uses `find`/`find_all` against the fixed AWS page and does not evaluate CSS selectors. SDK and proxy source modules do not import Beautiful Soup or Soup Sieve.

Actual scan before at `eb811913f1` and after at `28aa0e3c9b0f8ff98a49cfd844c69544ac3f67a5`, using the same OSV scanner v2.3.8 command:

```sh
osv-scanner scan source --config .github/osv-scanner.toml \
  -L uv.lock \
  -L litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard/package-lock.json \
  -L litellm/vscode-extension/package-lock.json
```

```text
Before: Total 1 package affected by 2 known vulnerabilities
After:  No issues found
```

The after result includes the explicit legacy exception above; it does not mean older interpreters received the missing patch.

Validation: CI-pinned uv 0.10.9 accepts `uv lock --check`; dependency traversal across 30 Python/OS combinations preserves every other package/version; Beautiful Soup parsing smoke checks pass on Python 3.10.20 and 3.12.13. Lock revision 5 and `exclude-newer-span = "P3D"` remain unchanged.

title: feat(s3-log): replace the python s3_v2 logger with a rust callback
body: On main, after #51526. Draft, not run in a live proxy. Ports the s3_v2 `S3Logger` to a Rust callback behind the CustomLoggerV2 contract, makes it the only implementation and deletes the Python logger. The callback keeps its name (`s3_v2`), list position and settings, so no config changes. `LITELLM_NATIVE_S3_V2` is removed in its own commit ## What this adds - `callbacks-s3-log`, a Rust port of the s3_v2 `S3Logger`, with the bridge constructor `NativeS3Log` and the Python glue `litellm/integrations/s3_v3.py` - It reads typed contract fields (`standard_logging_payload_ref`, `log_id`, `cold_storage_object_key`, `logged_key_identity`, `attempt_timing`) and renders bodies through `PayloadRef` with `safe_dumps` semantics. Prompts-only uses `null_keys` - It keeps today's object keys, prefixes, cold storage key reuse, headers, SigV4/SSE/web identity signing, batching, retries and requeue order, the queue limits, batch files, audit events, batch line items and cold storage reads - The no-log and caller opt-out checks, async-line-only delivery and the non-mapping payload count stay in the Python glue - `standard_logging_payload_excluded_fields` is honoured (found missing by the litefuzz run on the ports) ## Settings warnings - Invalid s3 settings log the same `s3 logging: ...` warnings as Python on the `LiteLLM` logger, with Python's `%r` text (`'maybe'`, `True`, `None`) and `type(value).__name__` for a non-string SSE value. Before this, warnings raised while the logger was built or while an attempt was logged went nowhere (litefuzz build 214 N3) - The logger captures the Python log context when it is built and uses it for construction and for the attempt hook, so warnings from the hook carry the construction-time session and trace ids rather than the request's - An unknown `s3_partition_granularity` warns once per distinct value, as Python's cache did; an invalid `s3_log_prompts_only` warns on every log, as before - The drop warning prints the retry age as Python does, `3600` or `None`, not `Some(3600)` (N4) ## Host calls - Stay: `callback_failed`, `render`, `web_identity_token` and the log sink - Whether s3_v2 is the cold storage logger is a constructor value. Proxy startup applies `litellm_settings` before the logger is built and a running proxy cannot change the setting, so the value is the one the host call read. SDK code that sets `litellm.cold_storage_custom_logger` after the logger exists does not reach that logger - The region from the environment (`AWS_REGION`, then `AWS_REGION_NAME`, only when `s3_region_name` is unset) is resolved once at construction. A later env or secret change does not reach an existing logger - The batch upload failed host call is removed. A partially failed flush returns `(queued, failed, total)` to Python, which logs the same record as before (logger `LiteLLM`, ERROR, with the `S3BatchUploadError` attached). No Python call is made while the queue mutex is held ## Base64 strip - With `s3_strip_base64_files` on, a small V2 writer `S3StripBase64Files` is placed right before its s3 logger in every callback list and patches `messages` on `standard_logging_payload` at `log_prepare`. S3 itself keeps `honors_no_log` - Behaviour change: callbacks before and after s3 now see the stripped messages, where before only the S3 object was stripped - The writer patches only on the async logging line and only when the s3 no-log and opt-out checks pass; otherwise other callbacks see the original messages - `log_prepare` runs on success only, so failed attempts are still stripped at `attempt_ended`, for the S3 object only - Uploaded bytes are the same as before the change for success, excluded fields and failure inputs - With strip off no writer is registered. The writer appears in callback listings as `S3StripBase64Files` ## Float rendering - `python-compat` `format_float` now rounds a float exactly half-way between two shortest decimal texts to even, as CPython's repr does (for example `response_time` 0.07872390747070312 was stored as ...313). This changes the shared encoder, so every Rust caller of `float_repr` and `json::dumps` gets CPython's digits. The case is pinned by a new CPython fixture row in `generated/values.json` ## Python deleted and kept - `litellm/integrations/s3_v2.py` is now a 3-line re-export of the Rust-backed `S3Logger` in `s3_v3.py`; 1,226 implementation lines deleted - About 9,100 lines of original tests deleted; their `_rust.py` replicas stay ## Breaking for subclasses - `S3Logger` is no longer a Python `CustomLogger` whose hooks do the work. A subclass that overrides `async_log_success_event` or other hooks, or calls private helpers such as `create_s3_batch_logging_element`, is no longer called or no longer finds them. A search of public GitHub code found four repositories doing this ## Tests - The existing Python test files are replicated against the Rust callback as `_rust.py` with the same names, inputs and expected values - The differential suite no longer has a Python side: Python's outputs were recorded before deletion into `tests/unit/integrations/s3_v2_golden/python_s3_v2.json` (177 entries) and Rust is compared against them - CI on ba93dcd1: all lint, type, Rust and unit checks green; Image Scan `verify (backend)` and `verify (migrations)` fail repo-wide ## Type gate - The logger registry on main is typed to return `CustomLogger | None` and the Rust-backed `S3Logger` is not one, which adds one `reportReturnType` error at `litellm_logging.py:6511`. The callback typing is not widened here. The count is held at its ceiling by fixing an existing `reportReturnType` error in `proxy_server.py`: `_routed_count_deployment` now narrows the routed deployment to a mapping, which it always is on that path ## Known differences from the Python logger - A response id with non-ASCII characters is uploaded, with the raw UTF-8 id in the `Content-Disposition` filename. Python never uploaded it: httpx refuses non-ASCII header values, so the flush raised `UnicodeEncodeError` and the element stayed queued, failing at every flush (litefuzz build 214 N1) - The attempt hook only enqueues, as Python did, but awaited Rust callbacks run after every legacy callback on the logging line - A payload that is not a Mapping but has a `.get` is counted as a failure, where Python would call its `.get` - Settings warnings from the attempt hook carry the session and trace ids from when the logger was built - An integer setting too large for 64 bits is carried as text, so its warning shows it quoted - When S3 answers an upload with a 303, the follow-up GET has no `Content-Type` header, where httpx kept it. reqwest drops content headers when a redirect turns the method into GET. The outcome and object count are the same, and S3 does not answer a PUT with 303 (litefuzz build 214 N5) ---

title: fix(langfuse): reserve span capacity for failure usage attributes
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Fixes to span capacity to unblock flaky test

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Failed Langfuse spans can lose existing attributes near capacity
- Failure usage fields were missing from the reserved space

How it solves it:

- Reserve only the pending failure usage fields
- Keep existing attributes ahead of derived trace fields
- Test the real failure callback across capacity boundaries

## User Flow

Before, a failed chat with many tools can lose trace metadata

1. Enable Langfuse OTel logging with a 128-attribute limit
2. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with 35 or 36 tools to a failing provider
3. Receive HTTP 500 and inspect the exported generation span
4. Find an existing metadata or span-kind attribute missing when trace fields are derived

After, the same failed chat preserves the existing attributes

1. Enable Langfuse OTel logging with a 128-attribute limit
2. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with 35 or 36 tools to a failing provider
3. Receive HTTP 500 and inspect the exported generation span
4. Find the existing attributes preserved, with no additional dropped attributes compared with joining a trace

## Relevant issues

Regression following #51443, exposed by the capacity test introduced in #42705

Original [failed job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43317684530/job/131529882785)

## Implementation

Langfuse already reserves slots for error attributes before deriving trace name, tags, input and output. Failure logging then appends an unknown-usage marker and, when available, an estimated input-token count. This change includes those pending keys in the reservation and subtracts keys already present on the span

The existing mapped unit file now exercises the real failure callback across 30–40 tools, with no usage marker, recovered usage, unknown usage and an estimate. The original integration test and its assertions remain unchanged

Current tip `d083da9852b4a9281dbdf3302973168855db774b` includes an explicit `Final[frozenset[str]]` annotation for the pending keys. All 585 affected tests, the canonical local type gate and CI lint pass. Independent source verification passed again at this tip, and Greptile (5/5), Cursor Bugbot and Veria report no findings

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The affected test files pass locally
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR only solves the failure-span capacity regression
- [x] Every automated review on the latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Local causality check ran the identical 33-case callback harness at `5ebc284053fade43e9205946d0c1569e92630848`, immediately before #51443, and its merge commit `dc1284d3d2c9745643a418ded63a67a94276868e`. Before merging, all cases pass. After merging, the unknown-usage case loses `openinference.span.kind`, and the estimated-usage case also loses `metadata`. The fixed commit passes all 33

Local live testing at the regression commit has 10 passes and two assertion failures. At `6e47f43744203d2b6b7d97b7e303626aae71f465`, all 12 live cases pass, and both formerly failing cases pass again with fresh services. Both runs use two source-proxy workers, isolated PostgreSQL/Redis, a scripted upstream and a real OTLP HTTP sink. This checks exported attributes without paid model calls

Independent Devin execution used source builds at the exact merge base and final tip. Both revisions have identical dependency locks, Rust sources and database schemas. Each run recorded its source SHA, clean tracked files, worktree import paths and two serving proxy worker PIDs. The independent run reproduced both baseline failures and passed every candidate case without further changes

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the live cases</summary>

Use the checked-out revision's frozen proxy and test dependencies, a disposable PostgreSQL database and an installed Redis server. Supply `DATABASE_URL` through the environment. The runner creates and removes isolated databases, Redis processes, proxies and HTTP peers

```bash
uv sync --inexact --frozen --group proxy-dev --group e2e-dev --extra proxy
uv run --no-sync python litellm/scripts/prisma_generate_if_needed.py
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/tests"
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True

uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py extensions   tests/integration/observability/test_langfuse_otel_trace_fields.py::test_trace_fields_never_evict_or_drop_another_attribute_of_a_full_span   --workers 2 --results /tmp/langfuse-capacity-results
```

The unchanged test's `v1` fixture sets `OTEL_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_COUNT_LIMIT=128`, `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_HOST` for its local sink. It derives the source proxy config from `tests/integration/proxy_config.yaml`, sets `litellm_settings.callbacks` to `[langfuse_otel]` and `langfuse_default_tags` to `[cache_hit]`, and registers a model pointing at the scripted upstream. The owned proxy helper configures both router Redis and coordination Redis for the dedicated instance

Its target source-proxy command is

```bash
python -m integration._support.proxy   --config "$GENERATED_CONFIG" --host 127.0.0.1   --num_workers 2 --timeout_worker_healthcheck 5   --use_prisma_db_push --port "$PROXY_PORT"
```

Reload is omitted by the integration harness. The same harness and worker count run before and after. The client issues paired requests, first with a caller-supplied `metadata.trace_id`, then with a W3C `traceparent` header. It checks HTTP 200 or the scripted HTTP 500, waits for the actual exported spans, and requires that deriving trace fields preserves the joined span's attribute keys and dropped count

The exact config construction, request bodies, scripted upstream, OTLP decoder and assertions are in the unchanged [live test](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/d083da9852b4a9281dbdf3302973168855db774b/tests/integration/observability/test_langfuse_otel_trace_fields.py)

</details>

### Before (78db4f1662fedc4eafa94855d7b9d20756799150)

The independent live run finished with 10 passed and 2 failed in 176.9 seconds. `35-fail-` loses `openinference.span.kind`; `36-fail-` loses `metadata`. Both fail the original attribute-preservation assertion. The new regression test against baseline source passes 42 cases and fails exactly `unknown-usage-37` and `estimated-usage-37`

### After (d083da9852b4a9281dbdf3302973168855db774b)

The identical independent live run finished with 12 passed in 184.8 seconds. A fresh-service repeat of `35-fail-` and `36-fail-` passed both cases in 96.3 seconds. Both affected unit files passed independently, 585 tests including all 44 new capacity cases. Temporary services, worktrees and build environments were removed

Local affected unit suites pass, 585 tests and two subtests. Changed executable-line coverage is 4/4 and the modified function's measured branches are 4/4. Module coverage is 275/292 lines and 76/86 branches, separate from repository-wide coverage. The completed [Codecov report](https://app.codecov.io/gh/BerriAI/litellm/commit/d083da9852b4a9281dbdf3302973168855db774b) reports 100% patch coverage (3/3 coverable changed lines, with the type-only annotation excluded by its Python coverage version) and 85.52% repository coverage

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/integrations/test_langfuse_otel.py   tests/unit/integrations/test_opentelemetry.py   --cov=litellm.integrations.langfuse.langfuse_otel --cov-branch
```

Type-discipline, test-quality, OpenAPI and canonical basedpyright budget gates pass. Test-tree Ruff and changed-source formatting pass. Whole-tree Ruff and the strict gate report two pre-existing import-order findings in unchanged database files, outside this fix

Required lint, smoke, unit, cost-map, spend-log and security-workflow checks pass at `d083da9`, along with the contributor agreement. The optional OSV dependency scan fails on existing `soupsieve` advisories in unchanged `uv.lock`, outside this fix

## Type

Bug Fix

</details>

title: test(providers): compare sagemaker embedding bodies exactly and assert caller encoding wins
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Two SageMaker embedding wire tests failed in the scheduled integration runs after #51335 changed how the request body is assembled. One compared request bodies as raw text, so it broke when the same fields came out in a different order, and the other still expected the old rule where deployment extra body settings beat the caller's encoding format, which #51335 deliberately reversed. This PR compares the parsed bodies exactly and updates the second test to assert the new intended precedence

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0018b787be4347e394bc450ca32e1f1e
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0018b787be4347e394bc450ca32e1f1e?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

title: feat(custom-logger-v2): add the contract for rust callbacks and bind the proxy request scope
body:
The Rust side of CustomLoggerV2: the contract a Rust callback implements, the typed fields it reads, and how it asks Python for something mid-call. Step 0 (#51214) is merged, so this is now based on main. No Rust callback ships in this PR; the five ports (#51535, #51537, #51539, #51540, #51541) stack on it, each behind its own env flag, default off

## Possible after, not before

- A Rust callback at any position in `litellm.callbacks`, reading typed values instead of the legacy kwargs dict
- A port that reproduces a Python callback exactly, including for malformed inputs, because the boundary carries what Python holds instead of rejecting it
- A Rust handler that looks something up in Python only when it finds it needs to (a spend counter reseed on a counter miss), with the Python code running in the caller's own task

## How

- `litellm/rust/crates/callbacks`: the `Callback` trait with a typed per-request `State` and the object-safe `ErasedCallback` it is stored as, `Manifest`, `Field` bits (47 fields), `contract.json`, typed records (`record.rs`), `Scalar` (`scalar.rs`), and typed host calls (`host.rs`)
- `litellm/rust/crates/callbacks-python`: `RustCallback`, the by-reference payload with a `safe_dumps`-compatible renderer (`payload.rs`, writing strings and floats with `python-compat`'s `json` writers), and the host-call transport (`hosted.rs`)
- Python: `litellm/integrations/custom_logger_v2/{field_sources,derivations,rust,enums}.py` (the package has a README), `litellm/proxy/v2_proxy_fields.py`, and the pydantic records in `litellm/types/integrations/custom_logger_v2.py`
- Typed fields come from field sources: a function over the hook's arguments, computed lazily and once per hook. A subscription that declares a write to one fails at declaration. `budget_reservation` and `rate_limit_statuses` are the two mapped, writable ones, so only the pre_call tables are named `*_SOURCES` and the rest `DERIVED_*_FIELDS`
- `CallFacts` is built on every line
- Lenient boundary: a member keeps the value and type Python reads. `Scalar` is text, int (to i128), float (inf and NaN carried both ways), bool, or `Stringified { text, truthy, hashable, integer, type_name, hash_error }` for anything else, with `str()`, `bool()` and `hash()` taken on the Python side. A member is named in `rejected` only when touching the value raises in Python
- Key identity at request hooks comes from the auth object only. At logging hooks it is `logged_key_identity`, from the proxy-stamped `user_api_key_*` payload metadata the Python loggers read today
- The standard logging payload crosses by reference and is rendered by the host with bytes identical to `safe_dumps`
- Host calls: a port declares `impl HostCall for X { const NAME; type Reply }`, calls `host.call(x).await`, and its Python glue serves a method of that name, sync or async. `RustCallback.start` returns the existing host-python `Execution`, driven by the existing `rust_bridge.execution` driver, so the Python method runs on the caller's thread and an awaitable is awaited in the caller's task. `Callback::handle(&HookInput, Option<&State>)` and `RustCallback.handle` are the plain path
- Follows main's #51439: team `model_preferences` members are gone, and `limiter_request` serves `fallback_on_saturation`, `fallback_on_saturation_invalid` and `fallback_walk_armed`

The per-field and per-member tables, with the Python source expression for each, are kept outside the repo and can be added to the PR on request

## Test results

On the tip, built from this branch's sources

- `tests/unit/integrations/custom_logger_v2`, `test_v2_hook_routing`, `test_v2_proxy_fields`: 511 passed, 7 failed. The 7 are `test_a_stringified_value_carries_the_error_text_python_raises_when_it_hashes_or_matches_it`, which compares against Python's unhashable-type message; Python 3.14 reworded it, and they fail the same way before this push
- `test_litellm_logging` and `test_callback_filters_v2_dispatch` were not rerun after the last push
- `cargo test`: `litellm-callbacks` 120 passed; `litellm-callbacks-python` 13 unit, 17 host-call, 1 non-finite, 2 payload, 2 round-trip, 1 stringified passed; `litellm-python-compat` 133 passed. On macOS the payload test binary needs an ad hoc re-sign (`codesign -s -`) to run locally
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt`: clean
- ruff (strict and tests configs), type discipline and test quality gates: clean on the touched files
- Not run: the type check gate (its environment could not be provisioned), the integration suite, a litefuzz run

## Caveats

- History is not one commit: the branch carries the pre-squash step 0 commits, a bridge commit recording that main holds step 0, and merges. The diff against main is the change
- `test_an_sdk_call_hands_attempt_ended_the_key_identity_its_logged_metadata_carries` failed once under `-n 3` and passes alone and on rerun
- The end-to-end host-call tests with a real Rust callback run as an embedded-Python cargo test, because `_native` exports no test callback
- On stages the dispatcher gathers and on sync lines, a host call runs in a child task with a copied context, as Python callbacks on those stages do today
- Not preserved exactly: a logged payload that is present but not a mapping (a Rust callback sees it as missing), `int()`/`float()` of non-builtin numbers (`Decimal`, numpy), subclasses of str/int/float (carried as the base type), an object that is not a Mapping but has `.get`, a generator in tags or entries (consumed by the read), an entry `reserved_cost` of None versus missing
- Not in this PR: an async-line-only subscription option, `OptOutBy::Caller` for Rust callbacks, per-model limit maps, a write from a shielded handler surviving cancellation
- The proxy releases a refused attempt's hold by calling the failure hook on instances of the Python limiter class only, so a Rust capacity callback is not reached on that path

title: fix(proxy): keep call id, model and key logging on keys refused before the body is read
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Keys refused before the request body is read now get the same failure logs as before, with the caller's call id, the requested model, the endpoint and the key's own logging destinations. Small JSON bodies are still read for logging, big ones never are, so the memory fix from #51428 holds

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4c9f5f25d4784b849a3bb5241a326426
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/4c9f5f25d4784b849a3bb5241a326426?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- #51428 refuses blocked and over-limit cached keys before reading the body
- Its failure hook got empty request data
- Failure logs lost the caller's `x-litellm-call-id`, model and endpoint call type
- Prometheus counted those 429s under `model=""`
- Key-level Langfuse destinations never got the trace
- Four scheduled integration tests went red (run 43317684530)

How it solves it:

- Build failure data from headers, route and the cached key, no body needed
- Attach the key and team logging config the normal path attaches
- Read the body only when it declares JSON with Content-Length up to 64 KiB
- The 64 KiB cap is also enforced on the bytes actually streamed
- That read gives up after 1 second, so a stalled upload still gets its 401 or 429 right away
- Model lookup is best effort, so a missing body model never turns the rejection into a 400
- Only `model` and trace metadata (tags, session and trace ids) come from that body
- `_call_type_for_route` now classifies compact responses, interactions and POST videos

## User Flow

Before: a team whose key hit its rpm limit sees the 429 but loses its failure logs

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `x-litellm-call-id: abc` past the key's rpm limit
2. They get `429 Rate limit exceeded for api_key`
3. Their key-level Langfuse project never gets a trace for it, and Prometheus counts the failure under an empty model
4. The failure log carries a random call id, so they cannot match it to `abc`

After: the same refused request is logged the way it was before #51428

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `x-litellm-call-id: abc`
2. They get the same `429 Rate limit exceeded for api_key`
3. Their Langfuse project gets the trace with its user id and tags, and Prometheus counts it under the requested model
4. The failure log carries call id `abc` and the chat completions call type

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Proof runs the integration rig, a real proxy with Postgres, Redis and a scripted upstream, against the four tests that went red in https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43317684530

Shared setup

```bash
sudo service postgresql start
redis-server --daemonize yes
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2 uv run --no-sync python tests/integration/run.py <group> -- <node ids below>
```

```
tests/integration/observability/test_prometheus_provider_auth_failure.py::test_a_key_rate_limit_rejected_at_the_proxy_is_still_counted_as_before
```

### Before (origin/main)

1. Providers tests, `4 failed, 5 passed, 2 warnings in 351.12s` (messages, compact responses, interactions and the cached chat twin lose their call type)
2. Observability tests, `2 failed, 6 warnings in 126.62s` (no Langfuse trace fields, Prometheus counts under `model=""`)

🐛 Bug Fix

  - Bounded per request, so the multi-MB OOM case from #51428 stays unread
- Bodies over 64 KiB, chunked, non-JSON or slower than 1 second lose body-only fields in failure logs
  - Model, tags and trace user id are missing there, call id and key destinations are kept

### Low

title: feat(proxy): count bounded DB lookups in flight per worker
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Nothing records how many auth DB lookups run at once per worker
- That number sizes the native pool before auth reads move to Rust

How it solves it:

- Counts every bounded DB lookup from admission until its task stops
- Exposes a gauge and an at-admission histogram on `/metrics/`
- Adds a DB lookups row to the all-metrics Grafana dashboard

## User Flow

Before: an operator sizing database connections cannot see how many auth lookups hit Postgres at once

1. They run the proxy with `callbacks: ["prometheus"]` and send 200 requests at once, each with a different virtual key
2. They open GET http://localhost:4010/metrics/ and search for `db_lookup`
3. Nothing matches, so the only signal is a stalled lookup after the fact

After: the same scrape shows how many lookups were running each time one started

1. They run the proxy with `callbacks: ["prometheus"]` and send 200 requests at once, each with a different virtual key
2. They open GET http://localhost:4010/metrics/ and search for `db_lookup`
3. `litellm_db_lookup_in_flight` shows the current count on the busiest worker, and `litellm_db_lookup_in_flight_at_admission` gives the p50 / p95 / p99 of that count

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, run the same way for both sides. The metric only depends on auth lookups, so the requests are `GET /v1/models` and no provider is called. Two worker PIDs served in both runs.

Proxy, started from the checkout under test with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` (a fresh local Postgres database) and `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` (an empty directory) set:

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4010 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

`config.yaml` is a copy of `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` with one dedicated Redis for both Redis settings and the Prometheus callback added:

```diff
 general_settings:
   master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
+  coordination_redis:
+    host: 127.0.0.1
+    port: 6395
 litellm_settings:
   callbacks:
     - code_interpreter_interception
+    - prometheus
+
+router_settings:
+  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
+  redis_port: 6395
```

<details>
<summary>make_keys.py, creates the 200 virtual keys once</summary>

```python
import asyncio, os, sys
import httpx

BASE = sys.argv[1]
COUNT = int(sys.argv[2])
OUT = sys.argv[3]


async def main() -> None:
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}"}
    limits = httpx.Limits(max_connections=10)
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=BASE, headers=headers, timeout=60, limits=limits) as client:
        responses = await asyncio.gather(*(client.post("/key/generate", json={}) for _ in range(COUNT)))
    keys = [r.json()["key"] for r in responses if r.status_code == 200]
    with open(OUT, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(keys))
    print(f"generated {len(keys)} of {COUNT} keys")


asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>burst.py, sends one request per key at the same time</summary>

```python
import asyncio, collections, sys
import httpx

BASE = sys.argv[1]
KEYS = open(sys.argv[2]).read().split()


async def main() -> None:
    limits = httpx.Limits(max_connections=len(KEYS))
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=BASE, timeout=60, limits=limits) as client:
        responses = await asyncio.gather(
            *(client.get("/v1/models", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}) for key in KEYS)
        )
    print(f"{len(KEYS)} distinct keys, statuses: {dict(collections.Counter(r.status_code for r in responses))}")


asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

Each side ran these steps after `python make_keys.py http://127.0.0.1:4010 200 keys.txt` had created the keys. Stop the proxy, run `redis-cli -p 6395 FLUSHALL`, start the proxy again so every key misses the cache, then

```bash
python burst.py http://127.0.0.1:4010 keys.txt
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" http://127.0.0.1:4010/metrics/ | grep litellm_db_lookup | grep -v _created
```

### Before (78db4f1662f)

1. `burst.py` prints `200 distinct keys, statuses: {200: 200}`
2. The `curl` prints nothing. The scrape has 33 `litellm_` sample lines and none mention `db_lookup`

### After (fbb77769839)

1. `burst.py` prints `200 distinct keys, statuses: {200: 200}`
2. The `curl` prints both metrics. The gauge is back at 0 once the burst has finished

<details>
<summary>curl output</summary>


title: fix(ui): align customer member budget form with API contract
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer member settings read and submit an unsupported template field.
- The same mismatch breaks main's dashboard build and typecheck.

How it solves it:

- Read and submit the API's existing `budget_id`.
- Test template loading, selection, clearing, and unchanged member settings.

The backend and generated schema already agree. This changes two production lines and corrects the test fixtures. No backend, generated schema, annual budget, or dependency changes.

## User Flow

Before, the member's stored template is missing and template changes fail.

1. Open `/ui/customers/manage?org=budget-form-qa-org&team=budget-form-qa-team&member=budget-form-qa-member&tab=settings`.
2. The member uses Standard, but Budget template displays No template.
3. Select Pro and save. The form reports `budget_template_id: Extra inputs are not permitted`.

![Before, the stored Standard template displays as No template](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dddf50fd-3124-414f-ab90-7fc9024e21fe)

![Before, saving a template fails validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d302995e-f711-4ec7-a584-bf9dd1b16992)

After, the same member displays its stored template and saves changes.

1. Open the same page with the same seeded member.
2. Budget template displays Standard (default).
3. Select Pro and save. Changes saved appears, and Pro remains after reload.
4. Select No template and save. The override and expiry remain after reload.

![After, the same member correctly displays Standard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98d54857-d1fb-48b8-ae74-48823bdac53d)

## Relevant issues

The failure is present on main at `78db4f1662fedc4eafa94855d7b9d20756799150`, in the customer settings code introduced by #51507. [Main's failing dashboard job](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43346741116/job/131627798659) reports the same TS2339 reproduced locally.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests.
- [x] The focused test files covering this change pass locally.
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks.
- [x] My PR only solves one specific problem.
- [ ] Every automated review on the latest commit has finished.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Baseline `78db4f1662fedc4eafa94855d7b9d20756799150`. Tested fix `d69010538679ee8ee815e7d0063c9472f0b3f8d1`.

The screenshots above show the real dashboard connected to the real proxy and isolated local Postgres. The recording shows selecting Pro, saving, reloading, then clearing the template, saving, and reloading. It contains timestamped CUA browser captures encoded as MP4, with a cut between the selection and clearing sequences.

<!-- demo-video -->
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60816cca-eb9b-40a1-b251-7196336f23aa

### Shared local setup

Node 26.10.0, Python 3.13.16, PostgreSQL 18, and a dedicated Redis instance. The local database contains only safe QA records. No model call is needed for this management form. Both baseline and fixed UI use the same proxy, two serving worker processes, Redis instance, and database.

<details>
<summary>Install, database setup, configuration, and startup commands</summary>

Run from a fresh checkout of the revision being tested. Set `QA_ROOT` to an empty local directory.

```sh
export QA_ROOT=/tmp/customer-member-budget-qa
mkdir -p "$QA_ROOT"
uv sync --inexact --frozen --extra proxy --group proxy-dev --group e2e-dev
uv run --no-sync python litellm/scripts/prisma_generate_if_needed.py

initdb -D "$QA_ROOT/pgdata" -A trust
pg_ctl -D "$QA_ROOT/pgdata" -l "$QA_ROOT/postgres.log" \
  -o '-h 127.0.0.1 -p 55474' start
createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55474 main_ui_budget_fix
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6406 --save '' --appendonly no \
  --daemonize yes --pidfile "$QA_ROOT/redis.pid" --logfile "$QA_ROOT/redis.log"

export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://$(whoami)@127.0.0.1:55474/main_ui_budget_fix"
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="sk-local-$(openssl rand -hex 20)"
export UI_USERNAME=admin
export UI_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -hex 16)"
export LITELLM_MODE=DEV
export STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True
uv run --no-sync prisma db push --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma --skip-generate
```

Save this as `$QA_ROOT/proxy.yaml`.

```yaml
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6406
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6406
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

Start the real proxy.

```sh
LITELLM_RUST_FIRST=0 uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config "$QA_ROOT/proxy.yaml" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4106 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

The migration resolver adopted the freshly pushed empty database schema and reported no pending migrations. The proxy served two workers, PIDs 36332 and 36333.

In another shell, start the actual dashboard.

```sh
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npm ci
NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4106 \
  npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3106
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Create the safe organization, templates, team, and member</summary>

Run with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in the environment. This uses the public management API.

```python
import json
import os
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

base = "http://127.0.0.1:4106/management/v1"

def call(method, path, body=None):
    request = Request(
        base + path,
        data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None,
        headers={
            "Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"],
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        method=method,
    )
    with urlopen(request) as response:
        print(method, path, response.status)
        return json.load(response)

org = call("POST", "/customer_organizations", {
    "customer_org_id": "budget-form-qa-org",
    "alias": "Budget form QA",
    "default_budgets": [
        {"name": "Standard", "is_default": True, "max_budget": 10, "rpm_limit": 5},
        {"name": "Pro", "max_budget": 50, "rpm_limit": 20},
    ],
})
call("POST", "/customer_teams", {
    "customer_team_id": "budget-form-qa-team",
    "parent_org_id": "budget-form-qa-org",
    "alias": "QA team",
})
print(json.dumps(call("POST", "/customer_members", {
    "customer_member_id": "budget-form-qa-member",
    "parent_team_id": "budget-form-qa-team",
    "alias": "QA member",
    "budget_id": org["default_budget_id"],
    "budget_override": {"max_budget": 20, "rpm_limit": 4},
    "budget_override_expires_at": "2027-12-01T12:00:00Z",
}), indent=2))
```

All three creates returned HTTP 201.

</details>

### Before

1. Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` in `litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard`. Typecheck reports TS2339 at lines 69 and 128. The production build fails at line 69.
2. Log in at `http://127.0.0.1:3106/ui/login/` using the local credentials above. Open the member URL under User Flow.
3. Observe No template, then select Pro and save. The real API returns HTTP 422 and the form displays the field validation error shown above.
4. Apply only this PR's test changes to the baseline production code. Run the two focused form/settings files. Nine assertions fail and 19 pass.

### After

1. Open the same member on the fixed UI. Standard (default) appears.
2. Select Pro, save, and reload. Pro remains. A real API GET confirms the Pro `budget_id`, the unchanged $20 / 4 RPM override, and the unchanged expiry.
3. Select No template, save, and reload. A GET confirms `budget_id: null`, with the override and expiry unchanged.
4. Select Pro and disable Override the template budget, then save. Rename the member and save again. A GET confirms the new alias, the Pro template, null override and expiry, and effective limits of $50 / 20 RPM.

Read the persisted result after each action.

```sh
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:4106/management/v1/customer_members/budget-form-qa-member \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
```

### Local checks

All checks passed on the tested fix.

```sh
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npx vitest run \
  'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/customerHierarchyForms.test.ts' \
  'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/CustomerHierarchySettings.integration.test.tsx' \
  'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/manage/page.integration.test.tsx'
# 3 files, 35 tests passed
npm run typecheck
# exit 0
npm run build
# exit 0, static dashboard pages generated
cd ../../..
make check
# PASS, dashboard formatting, ESLint, and lint budgets
```

The existing test renders real children and stubs only fetch, so it is renamed to `.integration.test.tsx` as required by the dashboard's test conventions. Generated API types are unchanged because the backend contract is unchanged.

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Low

- CI and automated reviews are pending.
- The demo is local only.
- The unrelated SoupSieve OSV issue remains out of scope.

## Final Attestation

- [x] Tests cover the reproduced regression and relevant member budget transitions.

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> UI-only field rename and test updates; no backend or auth changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes the customer member settings form so it reads and PATCHes **`budget_id`** instead of the non-existent **`budget_template_id`**, matching the management API and generated types (unblocking typecheck/build).
> 
> Member template selection, clearing to “No template”, and alias-only saves are covered by updated fixtures and new unit/integration assertions that expect **`budget_id`** in request bodies without touching overrides unless the user changes them.

title: fix(logging): run every callback under the span an SDK caller passed
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description [insert handwritten description here]
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Native Redis spans parent under a request span contextvar - The SDK router scopes it around the call, which a stream outlives - Three callbacks reopened the scope from kwargs by hand - The sync stream success path had no wrap at all How it solves it: - The four `Logging` handlers anchor the span around their dispatch - Every `CustomLogger` callback sees it, streamed or not, sync or async - Plain `litellm.completion` calls without a Router are covered too - The per-callback wraps in `lowest_tpm_rpm_v2` and `model_rate_limit_check` are gone - A span already anchored, as on the proxy, is kept - The wrap in `Router._release` is gone, a probe showed it never fired outside the router scope ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The change is SDK-only, so there is no proxy request to show. Proxy requests anchor the span at auth and are unchanged. The proof is an SDK `Router` call against real OpenRouter and a real Redis, with litellm's default OTel logger exporting to memory. The caller passes its own span as `litellm_parent_otel_span`, and the script counts the `redis` spans exported under it. The default logger drops a Redis span that has no parent, so a lost parent shows up as a missing span Shared setup, run from `/tmp` so each side imports its own checkout 1. `docker run -d --name span-proof-redis -p 127.0.0.1:6392:6379 redis:7.4.1` 2. Env var `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` 3. Each run: `docker exec span-proof-redis redis-cli flushall`, then `PYTHONPATH= python span_proof.py`
span_proof.py ```python import asyncio import os from collections import Counter import litellm from litellm.integrations.opentelemetry import OpenTelemetry, OpenTelemetryConfig from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter exporter = InMemorySpanExporter() otel = OpenTelemetry(config=OpenTelemetryConfig(exporter=exporter)) litellm.callbacks = [otel] litellm.service_callback = [otel] router = litellm.Router( model_list=[ { "model_name": "haiku", "litellm_params": { "model": "openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "api_key": os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"], "tpm": 1_000_000, "rpm": 1_000, "itpm": 1_000_000, "otpm": 1_000_000, }, } ], redis_host="127.0.0.1", redis_port=6392, routing_strategy="usage-based-routing-v2", optional_pre_call_checks=["enforce_model_rate_limits"], ) REQUEST = {"model": "haiku", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in one word"}], "max_tokens": 10} def report(label, caller): caller_id = caller.get_span_context().span_id redis = [s for s in exporter.get_finished_spans() if s.name == "redis"] under_caller = Counter(s.attributes.get("call_type") for s in redis if s.parent and s.parent.span_id == caller_id) print(f"{label}: {len(redis)} redis spans, {sum(under_caller.values())} under the caller span") for call_type, count in sorted(under_caller.items()): print(f" {call_type} x{count}") exporter.clear() async def async_case(stream): caller = otel.tracer.start_span("caller") response = await router.acompletion(**REQUEST, stream=stream, metadata={"litellm_parent_otel_span": caller}) if stream: async for _ in response: pass await asyncio.sleep(3) caller.end() report(f"async {'stream' if stream else 'non-stream'}", caller) def sync_case(stream): caller = otel.tracer.start_span("caller") response = router.completion(**REQUEST, stream=stream, metadata={"litellm_parent_otel_span": caller}) if stream: for _ in response: pass import time time.sleep(3) caller.end() report(f"sync {'stream' if stream else 'non-stream'}", caller) async def main(): await async_case(stream=False) await async_case(stream=True) await asyncio.to_thread(sync_case, False) await asyncio.to_thread(sync_case, True) asyncio.run(main()) ```
### Before (2e8ebfd0652, the stack tip under this PR) ``` async non-stream: 12 redis spans, 12 under the caller span async stream: 9 redis spans, 9 under the caller span sync non-stream: 15 redis spans, 15 under the caller span sync stream: 8 redis spans, 8 under the caller span batch_get_cache x1 get_cache x2 increment_cache x4 increment_pipeline x1 ``` ### After (f6927f2dd54) ``` async non-stream: 12 redis spans, 12 under the caller span async stream: 9 redis spans, 9 under the caller span sync non-stream: 13 redis spans, 13 under the caller span sync stream: 10 redis spans, 10 under the caller span batch_get_cache x1 get_cache x2 increment_cache x6 increment_pipeline x1 ``` After a sync stream, two `increment_cache` spans from the success callbacks are missing on Before and present on After. Three rounds gave 8 and 10 every time. The other counts move by one or two between rounds with cache-read timing on both sides, and every exported span sits under the caller span on both The regression test `test_every_callback_runs_under_the_span_an_sdk_caller_passed` in `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_litellm_logging.py` covers eight cases with no Router, sync and async, each as a plain success, a streamed success, a failure and a failure after the first chunk. All eight fail with the `litellm_logging.py` change reverted ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - `make_call` and the websocket entry have no test for the span - Both keep their own wrap, which this PR does not touch - The live run showed no async stream difference - Before already wrapped the async callbacks it exercises ### Low - Stacked on #51383 because the span helper lands in #50862 - This anchor goes away once Rust talks to its stores directly, the follow-up raised on #50357

title: feat(customer-portal): complete hierarchy management
body:
Refs #51459. Follow-up to #51507.

Open Customer Portal → Customer organizations → a customer organization to see Usage, Customer teams, Customer members, and Settings. This extends the customer organization list on main with detail management for customer teams and customer members.

- Create customer teams and customer members from their parent. Show customer organization-wide members with a customer team link and server pagination.
- Show recorded spend against the configured budget in the header and Usage summary, with a direct Edit budget link.
- Select configured models with search and provider logos. Empty selections inherit permissions; customer restrictions intersect with gateway-key and parent permissions, including fallbacks.
- Use LiteLLM’s shared delete dialog with identifier confirmation. Organization/team deletion sends `cascade=true`; the API keeps its existing 409 default without that flag. Deletion preserves usage history and budgets still referenced by surviving records.

Management remains proxy-admin-only. Lists use server pagination; customer members can be filtered by customer organization or customer team.

Before at `c834eb6`, model settings used a text field and the customer organization view exposed only the customer teams tab.

![Before: member settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/c834eb6f475b5f3bf2fe7519cac3077de21b5995/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/member-settings.png)

After at `ff79c04ea4a29575736331005b212242df26d9f6`, the organization view exposes both lists and its budget. Browser proof uses synthetic local records. I created Research and Taylor Brooks through the UI, then saved a $75 member override and selected models; the member API returned those settings.

![Customer organization and customer teams](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/43d55ab2b91e4cccccf014c5f813a2b70a4e89f9/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/teams.png)

![Customer members](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/43d55ab2b91e4cccccf014c5f813a2b70a4e89f9/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/members.png)

![Searchable member models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/43d55ab2b91e4cccccf014c5f813a2b70a4e89f9/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/member-settings.png)

![Shared delete confirmation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/43d55ab2b91e4cccccf014c5f813a2b70a4e89f9/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/delete-confirmation.png)

Actual curl proof used a controlled HTTP provider. Before at `6685525`, the same bound key could call a model excluded by its customer organization. After at `ff79c04ea4a29575736331005b212242df26d9f6`, it receives 403 and sends zero provider requests:

```sh
curl --request POST "$PROXY_BASE/v1/chat/completions" \
  --header "@$SCOPED_KEY_HEADERS" --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"model":"usage-proof-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Synthetic before-after permission check"}]}'
```

```text
Before: HTTP 200 {"object":"chat.completion","model":"usage-proof-model",...}
After:  HTTP 403 {"error":{"type":"customer_model_access_denied","param":"model","code":"403",...}}
```

On the final source, chat and Responses each returned 200 for an allowed model; member, key, and organization restrictions returned 403 with no provider calls. The populated hierarchy returned 409 without cascade, then 204 with this request; its organization, team, and member each returned 404 afterward:

```sh
curl --request DELETE "$PROXY_BASE/management/v1/customer_organizations/$ORG_ID?cascade=true" \
  --header "@$ADMIN_HEADERS"
```

A surviving key kept its shared budget relation and returned `422 budget_exceeded` before and after deletion. Daily usage totals also stayed unchanged. [Captured setup, requests, and response excerpts](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/43d55ab2b91e4cccccf014c5f813a2b70a4e89f9/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/api-proof.md).

Provider passthrough now applies the same customer restrictions before forwarding and after hooks. In an actual controlled HTTP run, the same bound key returned200 for an excluded model before at `43d55ab2b9` merged with `eb811913f1`; after at `ff79c04ea4a29575736331005b212242df26d9f6`, it returns403 with zero provider calls. Allowed requests still return200, and gateway-key restrictions still apply. [Captured setup, curl, and responses](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/ff79c04ea4a29575736331005b212242df26d9f6/.github/pr-assets/customer-hierarchy-settings/passthrough-api-proof.md).

CI fixes use the existing bounded deletion helper and typed batch scopes; formatting checks pass. The vector-store component now cancels its reset timer on unmount, fixing the unhandled timer error in the full UI suite. Separate baseline OSV fix: #51542.

Validation:237 focused UI tests;83 customer-policy tests;1,769 broader auth/passthrough tests;103 hierarchy tests; production TypeScript, Prettier/ESLint, Ruff, full type gate, strict/type/test-quality and unbounded-IN gates. Existing unrelated lint warnings remain unchanged.
