title: feat(budgets): add temporary increase requests and admin approval
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Users need approval for temporary monthly or annual allowances

How it solves it:

- Request an amount, expiry and reason from Budget requests
- Another proxy administrator approves or rejects the request
- Approval preserves spend and expires through existing budget enforcement

Intentional product change: adds a Budget requests page for internal users and proxy administrators

## User Flow

Before, the requester cannot submit a budget increase

1. Open `/budget-requests/`
2. See a 404 page

![Before, the page is absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1a381f6-9557-402a-a1d8-8e1491947dc1)

After, the requester submits an increase for administrator review

1. Open `/budget-requests/`
2. Enter an amount, a configured limit, a future UTC expiry and reason
3. Submit and see Pending review
4. A different proxy administrator reviews and approves the request
5. See Approved, with the allowance included in the selected limit

![After, the annual profile cap is raised from $500 to $575](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a97898df-a28b-4141-9739-7f348fd7f273)

## Relevant issues

- Adds personal temporary budget requests and administrator decisions
- Depends on #51510, with base branch `litellm_budget_profiles`

## Changes

- Reuses Skills Hub requester ownership and writable-identity checks
- Follows Skills/MCP pending review, decision dialog and toast patterns
- Applies the existing personal grant writer in the decision transaction
- Serializes decisions and duplicates, with ten new requests per hour
- Adds scoped pagination, audit history and rejection reasons

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Before `84e2fb028e0a`, the real proxy returns 404 for the new route and the dashboard page is absent, shown above

The UI recording at `e5ff8a007f1` shows the real dashboard approving an annual $75 allowance on a $500 profile, shown above. A stored expired $900 override stays inactive. Current tip `058870f4968` additionally clears an inactive expiry when no override is stored. That case passes a regression and live HTTP verification; the recorded UI behavior is unchanged

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e5b6c60-3abe-4c86-a821-f1de06663c6e

An annual-only requester also submits $50 without changing the duration selector, which defaults to the configured annual window

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06c9dfbd-0fa2-4365-ae8f-8584189c7e54

![Annual-only request form](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8610f89b-735d-490d-99fc-3dbfd5249f6a)

Verified against isolated PostgreSQL and Redis with two proxy workers. Ten concurrent submissions return one request and ten concurrent approvals apply one grant. Unauthorized decisions return 403, unowned detail returns 404, and opposite repeated decisions return 409

Expired override regression, before `fcd48eacd77` returns 409 despite effective profile limits of $100/$500. After `058870f4968` returns 201 and approval yields $150/$500, preserving spend. Expiry equality and active override rejection pass regression tests

A real development-gateway completion is blocked at a zero monthly cap, succeeds after a $1 approval, and blocks again after the 90-second grant expires. Nonzero spend remains recorded

Greptile 5/5, Veria and Bugbot pass on current tip `058870f4968`, with all findings addressed

Local checks pass, 38 backend tests, 22 dashboard tests, 22 tracing tests, nine migration idempotency tests, 53 test-path checks and `BASE_REF=origin/litellm_budget_profiles make check`. The production dashboard build, Prisma generation, schema application and migration replay pass. All seven deliberate mutations covering self-review, ownership, active grants, grant application, submission quota, expired override eligibility and stale-limit replacement are caught by tests

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the live proof</summary>

Run from the repository with its `.venv`. Use an isolated PostgreSQL database and Redis instance. Supply `BUDGET_REQUESTS_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`, `LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY` and an identified proxy admin's `BUDGET_REVIEWER_KEY` privately

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: budget-demo
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-terra
      api_base: https://gateway.product-dev.internal.litellm.ai/v1
      api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6497
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/BUDGET_REQUESTS_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  database_connection_pool_limit: 5
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6497
  allow_requests_on_db_unavailable: false
  proxy_batch_write_at: 1
  disable_error_logs: true
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
```

```sh
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://tin@localhost:5432/litellm_budget_approvals_20261112
export PROXY_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4197
export LITELLM_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3197
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/litellm/proxy-extras"
.venv/bin/prisma db push --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma --skip-generate
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config proxy.yaml --port 4197 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
# Separate terminal
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4197 ../../scripts/with_dashboard_node.sh npm run dev:webpack -- --port 3197
```

Baseline uses the same configuration at `84e2fb028e0a` with separate ports 4198/3198/6498 and database `litellm_budget_approvals_baseline_20261112`. Open `/budget-requests/` and GET `/management/v1/budget_increase_requests` with an administrator key. Both return 404

For the UI proof, assign an internal user an annual $500 profile with `pause_allow_increase`, sign in, then follow the After steps above. For expired override proof, add an already-expired personal $900 annual override before submitting the request

Save and run the following scripts using `.venv/bin/python`. They create isolated test users

```python
import asyncio, json, os
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import httpx
work=Path.cwd()
private={'master':os.environ['BUDGET_REQUESTS_MASTER_KEY']}; run='concurrent-'+__import__('uuid').uuid4().hex[:8]+'-'
base=os.environ.get('PROXY_BASE_URL','http://localhost:4197')
path='/management/v1/budget_increase_requests'
async def main():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=base,timeout=45) as client:
        async def call(method,url,token,body=None,expected=200):
            response=await client.request(method,url,headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+token},json=body)
            if response.status_code!=expected:
                safe=response.text.replace(token,'[redacted]').replace(private['master'],'[redacted]')
                raise AssertionError(f'{method} {url}: {response.status_code}: {safe[:900]}')
            return response.json()
        for name in ('requester','other','reviewer'):
            record=await call('POST','/user/new',private['master'],{'user_id':run+name,'user_email':run+name+'@budget-demo.example','user_role':'proxy_admin' if name=='reviewer' else 'internal_user','auto_create_key':True})
            private[name]=record['key']
        pass
        for name in ('requester','other'):
            await call('PATCH','/management/v1/budget_assignments/user/'+run+name,private['master'],{'budget_override':{'budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'1mo','max_budget':100},{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':500}],'cap_policy':'pause_allow_increase'}})
        request={'amount':50,'duration':'1mo','expires_at':(datetime.now(timezone.utc)+timedelta(hours=1)).isoformat(),'reason':'Finish the monthly report'}
        submitted=await asyncio.gather(*(call('POST',path,private['requester'],request,201) for _ in range(10)))
        assert len({row['id'] for row in submitted})==1
        rid=submitted[0]['id']
        assert (await call('GET',path,private['other']))['requests']==[]
        await call('GET',path+'/'+rid,private['other'],expected=404)
        await call('PUT',path+'/'+rid+'/approve',private['other'],expected=403)
        approved=await asyncio.gather(*(call('PUT',path+'/'+rid+'/approve',private['reviewer']) for _ in range(10)))
        assert len({row['reviewed_at'] for row in approved})==1
        own=await call('GET',path+'/me',private['requester'])
        assert [w['max_budget'] for w in own['windows']]==[150,500],own
        await call('PUT',path+'/'+rid+'/reject',private['reviewer'],{'reason':'No'},409)
        unrelated=await call('GET',path+'/me',private['other'])
        assert [w['max_budget'] for w in unrelated['windows']]==[100,500]
        rejected=await call('POST',path,private['other'],{**request,'duration':'12mo'},201)
        await call('PUT',path+'/'+rejected['id']+'/reject',private['reviewer'],{'reason':'Use the remaining annual budget'})
        (work/'live-evidence.json').write_text(json.dumps({'concurrent_submissions':10,'distinct_requests':1,'concurrent_approvals':10,'distinct_decisions':1,'limits_after_approval':[150,500],'other_user_limits':[100,500],'unauthorized_decision':403,'unowned_detail':404,'rejection':'recorded without grant'},indent=2))
        print('PASS: ten concurrent submits deduplicated, ten approvals apply once, owner scope and admin authorization, rejection preserves budget')
asyncio.run(main())
```

```python
import asyncio, json, uuid, os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
import httpx
work=Path.cwd()
private={'master':os.environ['BUDGET_REQUESTS_MASTER_KEY'],'reviewer':os.environ['BUDGET_REVIEWER_KEY']}
async def main():
 async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=os.environ.get('PROXY_BASE_URL','http://localhost:4197'),timeout=60) as client:
  async def call(method,url,key,data=None):
   return await client.request(method,url,headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+key},json=data)
  user='approval-expiry-'+uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
  created=await call('POST','/user/new',private['master'],{'user_id':user,'auto_create_key':True})
  assert created.status_code==200, ('create',created.status_code)
  key=created.json()['key']
  assigned=await call('PATCH','/management/v1/budget_assignments/user/'+user,private['master'],{'budget_override':{'budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'1mo','max_budget':0},{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':500}],'cap_policy':'pause_allow_increase'}})
  assert assigned.status_code==200,('assign',assigned.status_code)
  payload={'model':'budget-demo','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'Reply OK'}],'max_tokens':10}
  blocked=await call('POST','/v1/chat/completions',key,payload)
  assert blocked.status_code==422 and 'budget' in blocked.text.lower(),('before',blocked.status_code)
  print('Before approval: inference blocked by personal monthly budget',flush=True)
  expiry=datetime.now(timezone.utc)+timedelta(seconds=90)
  submitted=await call('POST','/management/v1/budget_increase_requests',key,{'amount':1,'duration':'1mo','expires_at':expiry.isoformat(),'reason':'Complete one verification request'})
  assert submitted.status_code==201,('submit',submitted.status_code)
  approved=await call('PUT','/management/v1/budget_increase_requests/'+submitted.json()['id']+'/approve',private['reviewer'])
  assert approved.status_code==200,('approve',approved.status_code)
  resumed=await call('POST','/v1/chat/completions',key,payload)
  if resumed.status_code!=200:
   print('Provider proof failed after approval:',resumed.status_code, 'error type',resumed.json().get('error',{}).get('type'),flush=True)
   (work/'provider-error-private.json').write_text(resumed.text);(work/'provider-error-private.json').chmod(0o600)
   return
  assert resumed.json()['usage']['total_tokens']>0
  print('After approval: real provider completion succeeded with token usage',flush=True)
  await asyncio.sleep(max(0,(expiry-datetime.now(timezone.utc)).total_seconds())+1)
  expired=await call('POST','/v1/chat/completions',key,payload)
  assert expired.status_code==422 and 'budget' in expired.text.lower(),('expired',expired.status_code)
  info=await call('GET','/user/info?user_id='+user,private['master'])
  spend=info.json()['user_info']['spend']
  assert spend>0, ('spend',spend)
  evidence={'before':blocked.status_code,'approved':approved.status_code,'completion':resumed.status_code,'tokens':resumed.json()['usage']['total_tokens'],'after_expiry':expired.status_code,'spend_retained':spend,'provider':'configured dev gateway','user_id':user}
  (work/'provider-evidence.json').write_text(json.dumps(evidence,indent=2))
  print('After expiry: inference blocked again; nonzero spend retained',flush=True)
asyncio.run(main())
```

The following also verifies expired override fallback. Run with `--before` on `fcd48eacd77` to observe the rejected request

```python
import asyncio,json,uuid,sys,os
from datetime import datetime,timedelta,timezone
from pathlib import Path
import httpx
work=Path(__file__).parent
private={'master':os.environ['BUDGET_REQUESTS_MASTER_KEY'],'reviewer':os.environ['BUDGET_REVIEWER_KEY']}
async def main():
 async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url='http://localhost:4197',timeout=30) as c:
  async def call(method,path,key,data=None,expected=200):
   r=await c.request(method,path,headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+key},json=data)
   assert r.status_code==expected,(method,path,r.status_code)
   return r.json()
  uid='expired-override-'+uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
  profile=await call('POST','/budget/new',private['master'],{'is_profile':True,'budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'1mo','max_budget':100},{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':500}],'cap_policy':'pause_allow_increase'})
  person=await call('POST','/user/new',private['master'],{'user_id':uid,'auto_create_key':True})
  await call('PATCH','/management/v1/budget_assignments/user/'+uid,private['master'],{'budget_template_id':profile['budget_id'],'budget_override':{'budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'1mo','max_budget':900}],'cap_policy':'pause_until_reset'},'budget_override_expires_at':(datetime.now(timezone.utc)-timedelta(hours=1)).isoformat()})
  own=await call('GET','/management/v1/budget_increase_requests/me',person['key'])
  assert [w['max_budget'] for w in own['windows']]==[100,500]
  request={'amount':50,'duration':'1mo','expires_at':(datetime.now(timezone.utc)+timedelta(hours=1)).isoformat(),'reason':'Complete work after override expiry'}
  r=await c.post('/management/v1/budget_increase_requests',headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+person['key']},json=request)
  print('Profile fallback limits',[w['max_budget'] for w in own['windows']], 'submission HTTP',r.status_code,flush=True)
  if '--before' in sys.argv:
   assert r.status_code==409
   return
  assert r.status_code==201,r.status_code
  await call('PUT','/management/v1/budget_increase_requests/'+r.json()['id']+'/approve',private['reviewer'])
  after=await call('GET','/management/v1/budget_increase_requests/me',person['key'])
  assert [w['max_budget'] for w in after['windows']]==[150,500]
  assert after['effective_budget']['cap_policy']=='pause_allow_increase'
  print('Approved profile limits',[w['max_budget'] for w in after['windows']], 'expired personal cap900 stays inactive',flush=True)
asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Medium

title: fix(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): read a model's saturation from Redis so every worker agrees on it
body:
<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2548aa9ed444483f8e7cc4aaf1a2544d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2548aa9ed444483f8e7cc4aaf1a2544d?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:
- Each proxy worker read a model's saturation from its own in-memory cache
- That copy held only the usage the worker served itself
- Steady traffic kept the copy alive past `saturation_check_cache_ttl`
- Two workers behind one Redis disagreed on whether a model was saturated
- A team past its share kept being served by the worker that thought the model idle

How it solves it:
- The saturation read now goes to Redis itself, through `BATCH_COUNTER_READ_SCRIPT`, and the count is written back to memory for `saturation_check_cache_ttl`
- `DualCache.async_get_cache` could not be used for it, since that answers from memory first whenever the worker holds a copy
- The count is written back only when memory holds nothing for the counter, as `DualCache` backfilled a miss, so the copy the limiter keeps for the whole window keeps its TTL and a Redis outage still falls back to it
- A failed Redis read falls back to the worker's own copy, as the limiter's counter reads fall back to the local mirror
- Without Redis, memory is all there is, as before
- `RateLimitStore.get_from_redis` is the one new read; the limiter's other reads are unchanged

## User Flow

Before: a team over its share is still served by whichever worker has not seen the other teams' traffic
1. A proxy admin runs two workers behind one Redis with `dynamic_rate_limiter_v3`, one model at `tpm: 1000`, every team at `model_tpm_limit: 100`
2. Team A sends 4 POST /v1/chat/completions while the model is idle and gets 200 each, 120 tokens borrowed
3. Six other teams send 3 requests each, 660 of 1000 tokens are used, past the 50% saturation threshold
4. Team A sends 12 more requests and gets 200 eight times before its first 429 `model_per_team_saturated`, since one worker's own cache still read the model as idle
After: every worker holds team A to the same fresh 100 token share
1. Same setup, same two workers, same Redis
2. Team A sends 4 requests while the model is idle and gets 200 each
3. Six other teams send 3 requests each, 660 of 1000 tokens are used
4. Team A sends more requests and gets 200 exactly three times, then 429 `model_per_team_saturated` with `retry-after: 60`, whichever worker answers

## Linear ticket

Relates to LIT-10562

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Two-worker proxy, one local Redis, a synthetic OpenAI-shaped upstream on 127.0.0.1:9009 that bills 30 tokens a call, Redis flushed and the proxy restarted between legs. Same driver for both legs: team A borrows 120 tokens idle, six teams use 90 each, then team A retries until its first 429.

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: shared-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini
      api_key: synthetic-openai-key
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9009/v1
      tpm: 1000
      rpm: 1000

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"]
  priority_reservation:
    interactive: 0.6
    batch: 0.4
  priority_reservation_settings:
    default_priority: 1.0
    saturation_threshold: 0.5
    team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams: true
    saturation_check_cache_ttl: 2

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

Before, `origin/main` at `c8036300bf`:

```text
six other teams used 90 each, the model is at 660 of 1000 tokens, past the 50% saturation threshold
t=  5.2s team-a   200
t=  5.3s team-a   200
t=  5.4s team-a   200
t=  5.5s team-a   200
t=  5.6s team-a   200
t=  5.7s team-a   200
t=  5.8s team-a   200
t=  5.9s team-a   200
t=  5.9s team-a   429 rate_limited_by=model_per_team_saturated retry-after=60
team-a was served 8 times under saturation (a fresh 100-token share is 3 calls)
```

Per-worker saturation reads from the before log, the two workers' series interleave and never agree:

```text
... 360.0 390.0 720.0 420.0 750.0 450.0 480.0 780.0 510.0 ...
```

After, this PR:

```text
six other teams used 90 each, the model is at 660 of 1000 tokens, past the 50% saturation threshold
t=  5.6s team-a   200
t=  5.8s team-a   200
t=  5.9s team-a   200
t=  6.0s team-a   429 rate_limited_by=model_per_team_saturated retry-after=60
team-a was served 3 times under saturation (a fresh 100-token share is 3 calls)
```

The after log shows one series every worker reads, 30 tokens a step:

```text
240.0 270.0 300.0 330.0 360.0 390.0 420.0 450.0 480.0 510.0 540.0 570.0 600.0 630.0 660.0 690.0 720.0 750.0
```

Unit: `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py` 136 passed (plus 13 in `tests/unit/redis/stores/test_rate_limits.py`); the new `test_every_worker_reads_the_models_saturation_from_redis_not_from_what_it_served_itself` fails on main (`assert 0.03 == 0.7`). `make lint-ruff-strict` and `make lint-type-discipline` pass.

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes saturation detection for team/priority enforcement in multi-worker proxy deployments; behavior is more strict when saturated, with deliberate degrade-to-local on Redis errors.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Model saturation checks in `dynamic_rate_limiter_v3` now read the authoritative counter from Redis** instead of `RateLimits.get`, which prefers each worker's in-memory copy and caused workers to disagree on whether a model was saturated.
> 
> A new **`get_from_redis`** on the rate-limits store fetches counts via **`read_counters`** / the batch counter read script, backfills local memory only when empty (preserving window-long local copies), and falls back to local memory when Redis is absent or fails.
> 
> **Unit tests** cover shared Redis across workers, Redis read failures, and no-Redis deployments; **fake rate-limit** test helpers gained `counter_pairs` and local read fallbacks.
>

title: fix(interactions): bind Deep Research agents and record their costs
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Runs agents only through matching deployments
- Blocks nested selector overrides
- Records agent costs and extends background billing polling to 130 minutes

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## Current verification

Current head `1404b053dedfaa7a44dbcb1d2f5de363131fadf2`. The approved test-only follow-up fixes the Bedrock signing test by controlling the clock for both signatures. The original request-body and signature assertions remain. No production code changed relative to the independently verified rebased heads `2de5b86b` and `d161a6e4`. Fresh focused verification, canonical checks, CI and reviews are running. Earlier proof below is historical until the current verification summary is refreshed

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Vertex Deep Research agents fail or silently run the wrong model
- Deep Research jobs are logged at $0 with no cost-map row
- Background billing stops polling after one hour

How it solves it:

- Send the agent, not the deployment model, when both are set
- Refuse an agent paired with another model's deployment
- Reject nested selector overrides that bypass agent binding
- Bill create, poll and stream under the agent's identity
- Add the Vertex Deep Research cost-map row
- Raise the default background cost poll window to 130 minutes

Intentional product change: A request that sets both `model` and `agent` must name a deployment of that agent. Otherwise it returns 400 before provider access, including for the master key. A conflicting `extra_body.agent`, or any `extra_body.model` alongside an agent, also returns 400. Matching agent duplicates and unrelated extra fields remain supported

## User Flow

Before, a Deep Research request can fail or run without the requested agent, and agent usage can be logged at zero cost

1. POST http://localhost:4049/v1beta/interactions with `model: vertex-dr`, `agent: deep-research-preview-04-2026` and `background: true`
2. Vertex rejects it with HTTP 400 because the agent was sent as a model
3. The same request with `model: vertex-argon` returns 200 but runs the ordinary model with no research
4. An SDK Deep Research job finishes with real usage but is logged at $0 cost

After, the same job runs the agent on the chosen deployment and is billed for it

1. POST http://localhost:4049/v1beta/interactions with `model: vertex-dr`, `agent: deep-research-preview-04-2026` and `background: true`
2. Receive HTTP 200 and an interaction that runs the Deep Research agent
3. The same request with `model: vertex-argon` returns 400 before reaching Vertex
4. When the job completes, its spend log records usage priced from the agent's row
5. A key limited to `vertex-argon` cannot reach the agent through `vertex-dr`

## Relevant issues

Fixes #49767

Last of three approved stacked PRs. This PR targets the branch of [PR #51511](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51511), which adds Vertex interaction follow-ups and selector authorization

Companion documentation [BerriAI/litellm-docs#2975](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/2975)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] Affected tests pass at the current head
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] Scope is isolated to this layer of the approved stack
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

This is the final PR in the stack, targeting lifecycle PR #51511

Current head `4416b06ce431da2c1452913f2eefa073036a3f35`, parent PR head `e484ff4a9b7ff9904d34878c5ee02cc7ebbfa4bf`

Greptile identified an `extra_body` override of the checked agent. An independent wire-level reproduction confirmed it at the previous head. The current commit rejects conflicting nested selectors before OAuth or provider access and adds sync, async and proxy regressions

Independent final-tip verification passes on source-built `4416b06c`. Canonical checks pass against the immediate parent PR. The requested CI rerun is complete for tests. The same unrelated hook-test and dependency-scan failures remain

### Shared setup

Environment: `VERTEXAI_PROJECT`, `VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS` (service-account JSON), `DATABASE_URL` (Postgres), `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. Leave `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` unset

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: vertex-argon
    litellm_params: {model: vertex_ai/gemini-4-argon, vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT, vertex_location: global, vertex_credentials: os.environ/VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS}
  - model_name: vertex-dr
    litellm_params: {model: vertex_ai/deep-research-preview-04-2026, vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT, vertex_location: global, vertex_credentials: os.environ/VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS}
router_settings: {redis_host: 127.0.0.1, redis_port: 6399}
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis: {host: 127.0.0.1, port: 6399}
litellm_settings: {drop_params: true}
```

</details>

```bash
uv sync --inexact --frozen --extra proxy --group proxy-dev
.venv/bin/prisma generate --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4049 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
P=http://localhost:4049
K=$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
H='content-type: application/json'
newkey() { curl -s -X POST $P/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "$H" -d "{\"models\":$1}" | jq -r .key; }
KA=$(newkey '["vertex-argon"]'); KD=$(newkey '["vertex-dr"]')
```

<details>
<summary>Agent binding and restricted keys</summary>

```bash
curl -s $P/v1beta/interactions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KD" -H "$H" -d '{"model":"vertex-dr","agent":"deep-research-preview-04-2026","input":"In two sentences, what is the capital of France and why?","background":true}'
curl -s $P/v1beta/interactions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K"  -H "$H" -d '{"model":"vertex-argon","agent":"deep-research-preview-04-2026","input":"In two sentences, what is the capital of France and why?","background":true}'
curl -s $P/v1beta/interactions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KA" -H "$H" -d '{"model":"vertex-dr","agent":"deep-research-preview-04-2026","input":"In two sentences, what is the capital of France and why?","background":true}'
curl -s $P/v1beta/interactions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KD" -H "$H" -d '{"model":"vertex-argon","agent":"deep-research-preview-04-2026","input":"In two sentences, what is the capital of France and why?","background":true}'
```

After the first job completes, read its settled spend row

```sql
select request_id, model, model_group, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens,
       metadata->'usage_object', metadata->'model_map_information'->>'model_map_key'
from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
where request_id = '<interaction id>';
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>sdk_settle_probe.py</summary>

Run `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python sdk_settle_probe.py` with the shared environment

```python
import os, json, asyncio, time, litellm
from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger
t0 = time.time()
class Cap(CustomLogger):
    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        slo = kwargs.get("standard_logging_object") or {}
        print(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time()-t0), "event": "success", "call_type": kwargs.get("call_type"), "kwargs.model": kwargs.get("model"), "slo.model": slo.get("model"), "slo.provider": slo.get("custom_llm_provider"), "slo.response_cost": slo.get("response_cost"), "kwargs.response_cost": kwargs.get("response_cost"), "status": getattr(response_obj, "status", None), "id": getattr(response_obj, "id", None), "model_map_key": (slo.get("model_map_information") or {}).get("model_map_key"), "usage": (slo.get("prompt_tokens"), slo.get("completion_tokens"))}), flush=True)
    async def async_log_failure_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        print(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time()-t0), "event": "failure", "err": str(kwargs.get("exception"))[:300]}), flush=True)
litellm.callbacks = [Cap()]
creds = dict(vertex_project=os.environ["VERTEXAI_PROJECT"], vertex_location="global", vertex_credentials=os.environ["VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS"])
async def main():
    r = await litellm.interactions.acreate(agent="deep-research-preview-04-2026", custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai", input="What is 2+2? One sentence.", background=True, **creds)
    print("CREATED", r.id, r.status, flush=True)
    for _ in range(90):
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
        tasks = [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if t is not asyncio.current_task()]
        if not tasks:
            print("no pending tasks left at t=", round(time.time()-t0)); break
    g = await litellm.interactions.aget(interaction_id=r.id, custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai", **creds)
    print("FINAL", g.id, g.status, "agent=", g.agent, flush=True)
asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>sdk_stream_probe.py</summary>

Run `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python sdk_stream_probe.py` with the shared environment

```python
import os, json, asyncio, time, litellm
from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger
t0 = time.time()
class Cap(CustomLogger):
    async def async_log_success_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        slo = kwargs.get("standard_logging_object") or {}
        print(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time()-t0), "event": "success", "call_type": kwargs.get("call_type"), "stream": kwargs.get("stream"), "slo.model": slo.get("model"), "slo.provider": slo.get("custom_llm_provider"), "slo.response_cost": slo.get("response_cost"), "model_map_key": (slo.get("model_map_information") or {}).get("model_map_key"), "status": getattr(response_obj, "status", None), "agent": getattr(response_obj, "agent", None), "usage": (slo.get("prompt_tokens"), slo.get("completion_tokens")), "usage_object": (slo.get("metadata") or {}).get("usage_object")}), flush=True)
    async def async_log_failure_event(self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time):
        print(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time()-t0), "event": "failure", "err": str(kwargs.get("exception"))[:300]}), flush=True)
litellm.callbacks = [Cap()]
creds = dict(vertex_project=os.environ["VERTEXAI_PROJECT"], vertex_location="global", vertex_credentials=os.environ["VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS"])
async def main():
    stream = await litellm.interactions.acreate(agent="deep-research-preview-04-2026", custom_llm_provider="vertex_ai", input="What is 2+2? One sentence.", stream=True,
        background=True, **creds)
    n = 0; last = None; FIRST_ID = None
    async for ev in stream:
        n += 1; last = ev
        if FIRST_ID is None:
            FIRST_ID = getattr(ev, "interaction_id", None) or getattr(ev, "id", None) or (getattr(ev, "interaction", None) and getattr(ev.interaction, "id", None))
            print("FIRST_EVENT", getattr(ev, "event_type", None), "id=", FIRST_ID, flush=True)
    print("STREAM_DONE events=", n, "last.event_type=", getattr(last, "event_type", None), "last.status=", getattr(last, "status", None), "id=", FIRST_ID, flush=True)
    for _ in range(30):
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
        if not [t for t in asyncio.all_tasks() if t is not asyncio.current_task()]:
            break
asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

### Before (`e484ff4a9b7ff9904d34878c5ee02cc7ebbfa4bf`)

1. Send `vertex-dr` with the Deep Research agent. Vertex returns 400 because the agent is sent as a model
2. Send `vertex-argon` with that agent. The proxy returns 200 and silently runs the ordinary model without an agent, including with the master key
3. Cross-group keys remain denied with 403
4. Agent-only SDK background jobs complete in both stream and non-stream modes, but log an empty model and cost `0.0` despite provider usage

The four changed test files produce 10 failures and 927 passes on this parent. The failures cover agent pricing, deployment binding, agent configuration and the longer polling window

### After (`4416b06ce431da2c1452913f2eefa073036a3f35`)

1. The `vertex-dr` request returns 200, runs `deep-research-preview-04-2026` and settles with the agent identity
2. `vertex-argon` plus that agent returns 400 before provider access, including with the master key. Ordinary model-only requests still work
3. Cross-group keys remain denied with 403
4. The proxy spend row retains group `vertex-dr`. SDK stream and non-stream settlement now log the agent identity and nonzero cost

| Flow | Observed input tokens | Observed output tokens | Recorded cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Proxy background agent | 23,801 | 4,742 | $0.160506 |
| Proxy matching `extra_body.agent` | 11,117 | 1,277 | $0.037558 |
| SDK non-stream | 11,121 | 1,692 | $0.0352002 |
| SDK stream | 17,848 | 1,895 | $0.072436 |

These are measured outcomes, not fixed provider-output assertions. The proxy job records four web searches, and the stream records one. The non-stream job has 4,081 cached tokens measured through a follow-up GET. Its zero search count is inferred by cost reconciliation because that GET has no search field

Costs reconcile with the checked-in map. The proxy job is `23801 × 0.000002 + 4742 × 0.000012 + 4 × 0.014 = 0.160506`. The matching-agent control has no searches or cache and totals `0.037558`. SDK stream totals `17848 × 0.000002 + 1895 × 0.000012 + 0.014 = 0.072436`. SDK non-stream totals `(11121 − 4081) × 0.000002 + 4081 × 0.0000002 + 1692 × 0.000012 = 0.0352002`

Before worker PIDs were 305569/305570. Final-head workers were 340486/340487 on port 4049, with dedicated Redis 6399 for routing and coordination. Native SHA-256 starts `a4a17a96`, rebuilt from `f4d71df3` using `uv sync --reinstall-package litellm`. Every native build input, including the root and backup price maps embedded by Rust, is identical between `f4d71df3` and `4416b06c`, so this exact native is reused with final Python source

<details>
<summary>Nested selector refusal and allowed duplicate, exact live requests</summary>

Run with the shared setup above

```bash
AG=deep-research-preview-04-2026
```

title: feat(ui): create customer budget groups with monthly, yearly, and cap policies
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer creation cannot configure member budgets or cap policies.

How it solves it:

- Create a customer with monthly and yearly member budgets.
- Choose each group's behavior when either cap is reached.
- Use the same choices when creating reusable budget profiles.

Intentional product change: customer creation requires a name and starts with editable `power_user`, `default_user`, and `low_user` groups. Each group has independent monthly and yearly caps and an **At the cap** choice. The default policy is **Pause until reset**. **Pause and allow temporary increase requests** enables the request policy provided by #51520. Requests need admin approval. Waiting disables requests until the exceeded limits reset. The optional Alias is the API customer ID, as its helper explains.

This PR is stacked on #51520 (`litellm_budget_increase_approvals`), which depends on #51510 and #51508. The parent branch predates main changes already present here, so the comparison includes already-merged main changes until the parent is updated. The new implementation is isolated in commit `cbc3666a7aa31ac0281f143bca45178dbc73fe36`. Compatibility fixes connect the parent's profile code to the customer member `budget_id` and `budget_override_id` names already merged in #51490, including profile assignment, member reads, list counts, and deletion checks.

## User Flow

Before, customer creation cannot configure member budgets or what happens at the cap.

1. Open `/customers` and click **Create Customer**.
2. Enter the customer ID and display alias.
3. The form offers no member budget groups or cap-policy choice.

![Before customer creation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6920a2cb-c990-4013-911d-b52a04436ff2)

After, customer and member budgets are saved together with independent policies.

1. Open `/customers` and click **Create Customer**.
2. Enter the customer name, optional alias, and monthly cap.
3. Set monthly/yearly limits and **At the cap** for each group.
4. Select the default group and click **Create customer**.

![Customer groups with independent cap policies](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/943e3f2d-5630-4224-ae00-f9ede5c79ce6)

The same choices appear at `/budgets` when creating a **Reusable profile**. The helper explains approval and the customer-member limitation.

![Reusable budget profile cap policy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a94ee407-f342-4723-8584-05c1b9b36eee)

The starter monthly/yearly amounts remain $200/$2,000, $50/$500, and $10/$100. `default_user` starts selected. Groups can be added, renamed, or removed. Each needs at least one cap. Zero is preserved and blank amounts are omitted. Failed submissions retain policies and budgets, while successful creation resets the form.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests.
- [x] The focused test files covering my change pass locally.
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks.
- [x] My changes address customer budget creation and stack compatibility.
- [ ] Every automated review on the latest commit has finished.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e19cf281-6d68-41b8-87e4-4605a68e9d6c

The recording shows the actual dashboard creating `customer-cap-policy-demo` against the live proxy. The API uses PostgreSQL and dedicated Redis. There are no mocked handlers or configured inference models. This verifies creation, persistence, inheritance, and request eligibility. It does not claim new inference enforcement or customer-member self-service.

### Before

The original main baseline `56d665939406d38fc2641e277b365cde1f2d7b36` has the same create component as main merge base `78db4f1662f`. It has only identity fields, shown in the Before screenshot. The prior version of this PR at `fb1163a9b4687910605509841995a2b8086db8a5` added groups but hardcoded `pause_until_reset`. The new choice removes that hardcoding.

### After (`cbc3666a7aa31ac0281f143bca45178dbc73fe36`)

1. Create `Customer cap policy demo`, alias `customer-cap-policy-demo`, with a $1,000 monthly customer cap.
2. Allow requests for `power_user` and `default_user`. Leave `low_user` at **Pause until reset** and submit.
3. At `/budgets`, create `cap-profile-demo-allow` with $100/month, $1,000/year, and requests allowed. Create `cap-profile-demo-wait` with $50/month, $500/year, and the default wait policy.
4. Run the client below. Both customer policies persist, members inherit the correct policy and both calendar caps, and internal-user request eligibility returns 201 or 409 as configured.

The recording and screenshots were captured from this final UI code. Subsequent compatibility test and Python formatting changes do not alter the recorded UI behavior.

<details>
<summary>Local startup and exact persistence verification client</summary>

Use this branch's normal proxy and dashboard dependencies and generated Prisma client. Provision an isolated local PostgreSQL database matching the branch schema. The recorded run used the existing isolated customer-budget demo database, and startup applied the stacked migrations. Set `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_SALT_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` to local test values.

Start a dedicated Redis instance.

```sh
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6392 --save '' --appendonly no
```

Save the following as `demo.yaml`.

```yaml
general_settings:
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6392
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  store_model_in_db: true
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6392
sandbox_tools:
- litellm_params:
    api_key: os.environ/E2B_API_KEY
    sandbox_provider: e2b
  sandbox_tool_name: e2b_sandbox
```

Start the proxy from the repository root.

```sh
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config demo.yaml \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4089 --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Both worker processes reached application startup complete. From `litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard`, start the dashboard.

```sh
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4089 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true \
  npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3076
```

Sign in through the real login form and follow the browser steps above. The local demo is `http://127.0.0.1:3076/customers`. The baseline dashboard used the same proxy and Redis settings on port 3077.

Run this client with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` set to the same local test key. It creates isolated teams, members, and internal users. Keys stay in memory and are never printed.

```python
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from uuid import uuid4

BASE = os.environ.get('CUSTOMER_DEMO_URL', 'http://127.0.0.1:4089')
MASTER = os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']


def request(path, body=None, method=None, token=MASTER):
    req = Request(BASE + path, data=None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode(), method=method,
                  headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + token, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    try:
        with urlopen(req, timeout=30) as response:
            return response.status, json.load(response)
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, json.load(error)


status, org = request('/management/v1/customer_organizations/customer-cap-policy-demo')
assert status == 200
profiles = {item['name']: item for item in org['default_budgets']}
assert {name: item['cap_policy'] for name, item in profiles.items()} == {
    'power_user': 'pause_allow_increase', 'default_user': 'pause_allow_increase', 'low_user': 'pause_until_reset'}
assert org['default_budget_id'] == profiles['default_user']['budget_id']
status, team = request('/management/v1/customer_teams', {'parent_org_id': org['customer_org_id']})
assert status == 201
for name, expected in [('default_user', 'pause_allow_increase'), ('low_user', 'pause_until_reset')]:
    payload = {'parent_team_id': team['customer_team_id']}
    if name != 'default_user':
        payload['budget_id'] = profiles[name]['budget_id']
    status, member = request('/management/v1/customer_members', payload)
    assert status == 201
    assert member['effective_budget']['cap_policy'] == expected
    status, assignment = request('/management/v1/budget_assignments/customer_member/' + member['customer_member_id'])
    assert status == 200
    assert assignment['effective_budget']['cap_policy'] == expected
    assert len(assignment['windows']) == 2
print('PASS customer groups persisted both policies and members inherited their selected policy and both caps.')

status, budgets = request('/management/v1/budgets?page_size=100')
assert status == 200
by_id = {item['budget_id']: item for item in budgets['data']}
for suffix, policy, expected_status in [('allow', 'pause_allow_increase', 201), ('wait', 'pause_until_reset', 409)]:
    profile_id = 'cap-profile-demo-' + suffix
    assert by_id[profile_id]['cap_policy'] == policy
    user_id = 'cap-policy-' + suffix + '-' + uuid4().hex[:8]
    status, user = request('/user/new', {'user_id': user_id, 'user_role': 'internal_user'})
    assert status == 200, 'local test user creation failed'
    token = user['key']
    status, assignment = request('/management/v1/budget_assignments/user/' + user_id, {'budget_id': profile_id}, 'PATCH')
    assert status == 200
    assert assignment['effective_budget']['cap_policy'] == policy
    status, increase = request('/management/v1/budget_increase_requests', {
        'amount': 10, 'duration': '1mo',
        'expires_at': (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(hours=1)).isoformat(),
        'reason': 'Local cap policy verification'}, token=token)
    assert status == expected_status, (suffix, status, increase.get('detail'))
    if suffix == 'allow':
        assert increase['status'] == 'pending_review'
    else:
        assert 'does not allow increase requests' in increase['detail']
    print(f'PASS profile {suffix} persisted {policy}; internal-user request returned {status}.')
```

Observed output:

```text
PASS customer groups persisted both policies and members inherited their selected policy and both caps.
PASS profile allow persisted pause_allow_increase; internal-user request returned 201.
PASS profile wait persisted pause_until_reset; internal-user request returned 409.
```

</details>

### Local checks

63 frontend tests pass across eight focused customer, profile, assignment, and request files. 228 backend tests pass across eight customer, budget, assignment, request, and auth files. Production TypeScript, focused ESLint, Prettier, generated API types, and whitespace checks pass. `BASE_REF=origin/litellm_budget_increase_approvals make check` passed, including Python lint/type gates, dashboard lint budgets, and API schema sync.

<summary>Focused test commands</summary>

```sh
python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/test_customers.py \
  tests/unit/proxy/management_helpers/test_customer_hierarchy.py \

  tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_budget_endpoints.py -q
BASE_REF=origin/litellm_budget_increase_approvals make check
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npm run typecheck
npx vitest run \
  'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/customerOrganizationForm.test.ts' \
  'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/CreateCustomerDialog.integration.test.tsx' \
  'src/app/(dashboard)/customers/_components/customerHierarchyForms.test.ts' \

  'src/app/(dashboard)/budget-requests/_components/BudgetRequests.integration.test.tsx'
```

</details>

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Medium

- Merge after #51520 and its budget dependencies.
- Customer-member self-service still needs trusted identity mapping.

- CI and automated reviews are pending on this update.

title: test(security): finish request accounting before changing Vault config
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Two Vault config tests failed on the scheduled integration run because they saw the proxy read a Vault secret after the Vault config was deleted. Tracing showed the read came from spend logging for a request sent before the delete, still running in the background, not from Vault being turned back on. This PR makes both tests wait for each request's spend row to be saved before changing the Vault config, keeping the strict no-Vault-traffic-after-delete checks

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description [insert handwritten description here]
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9c87c045c80c4d50967fb8f3fddfb398 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/9c87c045c80c4d50967fb8f3fddfb398?variant=devin Requested by: @narmstrong-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - String request overrides cause HTTP 500 on the RC How it solves it: - Backport #51502 to `rc/1.110.0` - Ignore standalone fallback strings and retain configured fallbacks - Parse `max_fallbacks` with a bounded Pydantic integer - Return HTTP 400 for other invalid override values Intentional product change: standalone strings in the three fallback override fields are ignored. Integer-valued strings, booleans, and whole-number floats are accepted for `max_fallbacks` within the Rust `u32` range. Explicit nulls, empty lists, literal-`True` flags, and derived request fields retain their meaning. ## User Flow Before, requests carrying string overrides fail before serving the model response. 1. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"fallbacks": "default"` or `"max_fallbacks": "2"` 2. Receive HTTP 500 with a router request shape error After, fallback strings are ignored and integer strings are parsed. 1. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"fallbacks": "default"` or `"max_fallbacks": "2"` 2. Receive the model response using configured fallbacks, or HTTP 400 for other invalid values ## Backport Cherry-picked merged source https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51502 at `07fe19bb15604abe4eae568ed3499e8fa7e8a583` onto RC base `bf3cb0cd7bd46310142940a88d2cc32912c1bb66`. The pick applied without conflicts and preserves its original author and provenance. No dependency or version changes are included. Requested in https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0AT6SHSM60/p1794533117166979 within the thread requesting the v1.110.0 RC fix. ## Affected release Regression since v1.110.0-dev.1. ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10711 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] Meaningful regression tests are included from the source PR - [x] Focused tests pass on the RC branch - [ ] Required CI checks pass - [x] Scope is limited to the requested cherry-pick - [ ] Latest automated reviews are complete ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix At `1fd0a115ce0f6a3ccedf032d14b69c059436cb75`, the RC worktree passed 196 fallback, characterization, and request-override tests, plus 2 selection tests. The RC native extension was built with `cargo build --release --locked --offline --manifest-path litellm-rust/crates/python-bridge/Cargo.toml --features extension-module`. Python imports were verified to resolve to the RC worktree. `git diff --check origin/rc/1.110.0...HEAD` passed. Ruff strict, type-discipline, test-quality, and basedpyright count gates passed against `origin/rc/1.110.0`. The working tree is clean and the backport patch ID matches the merged source patch ID. title: fix(interactions): route Vertex lifecycle calls through the selected deployment
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Routes GET, cancel and DELETE through the selected Vertex deployment
- Checks deployment access and fixes Vertex’s cancellation URL
- Includes the small Bedrock flaky-test fix

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## Current verification

Current head `1858a117158eaed10bb0b1be2399931cc4311e79`, immediate parent `50946dd4388ba825f9a8ae80f095b2908c9d6e3a`

Independent real-provider proxy verification was executed at product head `2de5b86bb7e13c7bb821066a0eb5febaa3f12396` against parent `50946dd4388ba825f9a8ae80f095b2908c9d6e3a`, after the rebase. The only change from that tested head to current `1858a117` is the Bedrock test clock fix, one test file with seven additions and two deletions. Production and native-build inputs are identical, so the live evidence carries forward to this test-only commit

The existing config, proxy start command and client commands below were reused unchanged on dedicated Redis 6399, port 4049 and two workers, with real Vertex calls. Source-native hash prefix `e11e4718` was built at `50946dd4` and reused at `2de5b86b` because native inputs are identical

| Same user flow | Before `50946dd4` | After `2de5b86b`, unchanged at `1858a117` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query-pinned GET, cancel and DELETE | 403, raw deployment ID rejected | 200 for all three operations |
| Header-pinned GET, cancel and DELETE | Selector ignored, Gemini default returns 500 without a Gemini key | 200 through the selected Vertex deployment |
| Key restricted to another group | Denied | 403 before provider access |
| Unknown selector | Denied | 403 |
| Public-only key pins shared-private deployment | Denied | 400 |
| Wildcard, private or owning-group grant pins shared-private | Selector handling fails before Vertex | 200 through shared-private |
| Group selector with public grant | Selector handling fails before Vertex | Routes to shared-public |
| Wildcard grant cancels and deletes private interaction | Selector handling fails before Vertex | 200 for both |

At `2de5b86b`, the three changed test files pass 1,107 tests, versus 79 failures and 1,028 passes when those tests run on parent source. Mapped directories pass 5,742 tests with two skips. Canonical checks pass against `50946dd4`

At current `1858a117`, the fixed Bedrock test passes, its mapped file passes all 92 tests, and four deterministic checks establish the old one-second clock failure and rejection of altered bodies. `make check BASE_REF=50946dd4388ba825f9a8ae80f095b2908c9d6e3a` passes. No new provider run was needed for the test-only change. Full CI and the requested review refresh are tracked separately

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Vertex interaction GET, cancel and DELETE always go to Google AI Studio
- Vertex cancel is sent to `:cancel` instead of Google's `/cancel`

How it solves it:

- Route by-ID calls through a model group or deployment ID
- Authorize that selector against the key and team like any model
- Keep the Google AI Studio default when no selector is sent
- Send Vertex cancel to the documented `/cancel` path

Intentional product change: A by-ID call that names a model group or deployment ID now needs model access to that group, so a key without it gets 403 instead of reaching the provider

## User Flow

Before, a Vertex interaction is created but cannot be read, cancelled or deleted

1. POST http://localhost:4049/v1beta/interactions with `model: vertex-argon`, an input and `background: true`
2. Receive HTTP 200 with a real Vertex interaction ID
3. With an owning-group key, GET http://localhost:4049/v1beta/interactions/{id}?model={deployment-id} returns 403
4. The same deployment ID in `x-litellm-model` reaches the Gemini default and returns 500

After, the same job is managed on the deployment that created it

1. POST http://localhost:4049/v1beta/interactions with `model: vertex-argon`, an input and `background: true`
2. Receive HTTP 200 with an interaction ID and an `x-litellm-model-id` header
3. GET http://localhost:4049/v1beta/interactions/{id}?model={x-litellm-model-id} returns HTTP 200 and the job status
4. POST .../{id}/cancel and DELETE with the same ID, as a query parameter or `x-litellm-model` header, return `cancelled` and `success: true`
5. A key without access to that deployment's model group gets 403 before any provider call

## Relevant issues

Related to #49767

Second of three approved stacked PRs. This PR targets the branch of #51442, which adds the shared deployment access-group filter these pinned calls rely on. [Deep Research execution and billing #51517](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/51517) targets this branch

Companion documentation [BerriAI/litellm-docs#2975](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/2975)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] All 1,107 tests in the three changed test files pass at this head
- [x] Applicable in-scope CI checks completed, with unrelated failures recorded below
- [x] Scope is isolated to this layer of the approved stack
- [x] Current-tip Greptile, Bugbot and Veria reviews finished with no unresolved actionable findings

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The current rebase results are in Current verification above. The commands and fixtures below were reused unchanged. Older SHA-specific results are retained as historical context

Head `e484ff4a9b7ff9904d34878c5ee02cc7ebbfa4bf`, parent `ee3232575b5ef80ec54033f5ba70c63796501682` (PR 1 head). Same rig on both sides, only the checkout differs. Rust/build inputs unchanged vs the parent (`git diff ee323257 e484ff4a -- litellm/rust litellm/rust_bridge Cargo.lock Cargo.toml pyproject.toml uv.lock` is empty), so the PR 1 native (sha256 3726e615…) is reused; `uv sync --inexact --frozen --extra proxy --group proxy-dev` at e484 audited 229 packages and rebuilt nothing (editable install, Python-only diff).

Rig: real Vertex, one project, location `global`, no Gemini credentials in the environment (so the unchanged no-selector default shows as the Gemini-default error), 2 uvicorn workers (before pids 277854/277855, after 285205/285206), dedicated task Redis `127.0.0.1:6399` (bind 127.0.0.1, `save ""`, appendonly off, maxmemory 256mb) for both `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`, Postgres DB `issue49767`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. Env: `VERTEXAI_PROJECT`, `VERTEXAI_CREDENTIALS` (service-account JSON), `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` (unused here). The full executed configuration is below. Port 4049 both sides.

### Before (`ee3232575b5ef80ec54033f5ba70c63796501682`)

1. Run the creation and follow-up commands above with the owning-group key
2. Deployment-ID query requests return 403. Header selectors are ignored and reach the Gemini default
3. Cancel and DELETE cannot manage the created Vertex interaction

### After (`e484ff4a9b7ff9904d34878c5ee02cc7ebbfa4bf`)

1. Run the same commands with the same grants and configuration
2. Both selectors reach the creating deployment and return 200
3. Cancel returns `cancelled`, DELETE returns `success: true`, and unauthorized deployment pins remain blocked

| case (`$DID` = deployment id from `x-litellm-model-id` on create) | before ee323257 | after e484ff4a |
|---|---|---|
| KA `[vertex-argon]` GET `$ID?model=$DID` | 403 `key_model_access_denied` on the raw id | 200 `in_progress`, served by the pinned Vertex deployment |
| KA GET `$ID` + `x-litellm-model: $DID` | header ignored, 500 Gemini default `Google API key is required` | 200 `in_progress` |
| KD `[vertex-dr]` GET/cancel/DELETE with `$DID` (query or header) | query 403 on the raw id, header 500 Gemini default | 403 `The requested model 'vertex-argon' is not available for this API key` (id authorized as its group, no upstream call) |
| KA GET `$ID?model=no-such-deployment` | 403 | 403 (unknown selector refused at auth) |
| KA POST `$ID/cancel` header `$DID`, then DELETE `$ID?model=$DID` | 500 Gemini default, 403 | 200 `cancelled`, 200 `success: true` |
| KA POST `$ID2/cancel?model=$DID`, then DELETE `$ID2` header `$DID` | 403, 500 Gemini default | 200 `cancelled`, 200 `success: true` |
| master GET `$ID` no selector | 500 Gemini default (unchanged) | 500 Gemini default (unchanged) |
| KPUB `[public-scope]` GET/cancel/DELETE `$ID3` pinned `shared-private`, query and header | 403 raw id (query) / 500 Gemini default (header) | 400 `You passed in model=shared-private. There are no healthy deployments` |
| KWILD `[vertex-sh*, public-scope]`, KPRIV `[private-scope]`, KGRP `[vertex-shared, public-scope]` on `shared-private` | same before pattern | 200 served `shared-private`; KWILD cancel 200 `cancelled`, DELETE 200 |
| KPUB / KWILD selector `vertex-shared` (group) | 500 Gemini default | 200 served `shared-public` (filter narrows the group to the caller's deployment) |

Vertex cancel path: `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/interactions/transformation.py` now sends `/cancel` (the `:cancel` form returned 404 from Vertex in the earlier live run); live cancel above returns 200 `cancelled`.

Tests and gates at e484ff4a (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -W ignore ...` from the checkout root):
```bash

```
Rows a one-project live rig cannot show (distinct projects per deployment, the pinned deployment's own credentials) are covered by the committed respx tests in `tests/unit/proxy/google_endpoints/test_endpoints.py`, not by live evidence. Vertex jobs created by this proof are deleted directly on Vertex afterwards. Workspace Rust gates via the PR's CI (no Rust change in this PR).

### Team ownership review evidence

Veria's proposed cross-team leak was tested independently at `e484ff4a9b7ff9904d34878c5ee02cc7ebbfa4bf` against parent `ee3232575b5ef80ec54033f5ba70c63796501682`, without changing source

The later [selection filter](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/e484ff4a9b7ff9904d34878c5ee02cc7ebbfa4bf/litellm/rust/crates/router-core/src/select.rs#L348) applies `filter_team_based` to resolved deployments, including pinned IDs. It calls `Deployment::usable_by_team`, which rejects a deployment owned by another team. `filter_reserved` only handles access windows and is not the ownership check

| Probe | Parent | Lifecycle head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Team B pins team A, GET/cancel/DELETE with query/header | 403 query or 500 ignored header, no team-A provider call | All six return 429, no provider call |
| Team B pins its own deployment | Selector unavailable | All six return 200 from team B |
| Team B uses the shared group | Selector unavailable | All six return 200 from team B |
| Team B creates through shared group | Existing control | 200 from team B |

The proxy fixture passed 19 cases. A separate router probe changed only `model_info.team_id`, confirming the other-team pin is refused when owned and selectable when global. These are mocked-provider tests for the review concern, separate from the real Vertex lifecycle evidence above

<details><summary>veria_team_step_attribution.py, exact disposable verification fixture</summary>

```python
"""Which router step drops team-A's deployment when a team-B caller pins its id (no proxy, no upstream).
Run from the litellm checkout: .venv/bin/python <this file>."""
import asyncio, json, sys
from typing import Final
import litellm

GROUP: Final = "shared"

def dep(deployment_id: str, team_id: str | None) -> dict:
    creds = {"type": "authorized_user", "client_id": "c", "client_secret": "s", "refresh_token": "r", "quota_project_id": "q"}
    info = {"id": deployment_id, "team_public_model_name": GROUP}
    return {
        "model_name": GROUP,
        "litellm_params": {"model": "vertex_ai/gemini-4-argon", "vertex_project": f"{deployment_id}-project",
                           "vertex_location": "global", "vertex_credentials": json.dumps(creds)},
        "model_info": info | ({"team_id": team_id} if team_id else {}),
    }

async def pick(router: litellm.Router, model: str, team_id: str | None) -> str:
    kwargs = {"metadata": {"user_api_key_team_id": team_id}} if team_id else {}
    try:
        d = await router.async_get_available_deployment(model=model, request_kwargs=kwargs)
        return f"SELECTED {d['model_info']['id']} ({d['litellm_params']['vertex_project']})"
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"{type(e).__name__} {str(e).splitlines()[0][:160]}"

async def main() -> None:
    for label, a_team in (("dep-a team-owned by team-a", "team-a"), ("dep-a global (no team_id)", None)):
        router = litellm.Router(model_list=[dep("dep-a", a_team), dep("dep-b", "team-b")])
        print(f"== {label}; dep-b team-owned by team-b")
        # resolution step alone: the deployments the router lists for that name and caller team
        for name, team in (("dep-a", "team-b"), ("dep-a", "team-a"), (GROUP, "team-b")):
            listed = [d["model_info"]["id"] for d in (router.get_model_list(model_name=name, team_id=team) or [])]
            print(f"  resolve  model={name:6} team={team}: lists {listed}")
        for name, team in (("dep-a", "team-b"), ("dep-a", "team-a"), ("dep-a", None), ("dep-b", "team-b"), (GROUP, "team-b")):
            print(f"  select   model={name:6} team={team}: {await pick(router, name, team)}")

asyncio.run(main())
```

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- People need independent monthly and annual spending caps.
- Personal overrides must expire without resetting accumulated spend.

How it solves it:

- Add reusable profiles and personal assignments to Budgets.
- Reuse existing calendar, reservation, and accounting machinery.
- Cache policy sources and check current spend during admission.
- Preserve creator attribution for deferred and failed billable work.
- Reject stale edits and unsupported budget assignments.

Rebuilt on main at 89632ca1bee. Annual budgets and customer hierarchy enforcement are already merged. This PR adds personal policy enforcement on top of those features.

## User Flow

Before, admins cannot assign independent calendar caps through the Budgets page.

1. Open `/ui/budgets` and select Create Budget.
2. Configure one shared budget and reset period.
3. There is no reusable per-person monthly and annual profile.

After, admins can reuse a profile while keeping each person's spend independent.

1. Open `/ui/budgets` and select Create Budget.
2. Create a per-person profile with monthly and annual caps.
3. Select Assign budgets and load an internal user or customer member.
4. Assign the profile, change personal limits, and save.
5. The saved effective limits show each enforced cap and reset.

![Saved monthly override with inherited annual cap](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/406ec480-ede1-4f86-8634-503a090e591b)

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Meaningful policy, management, accounting, and dashboard tests added.
- [x] Focused management, accounting, and dashboard suites pass locally.
- [ ] Repository-wide checks and required CI pass.
- [x] Scope stays within personal budget profiles and enforcement.
- [ ] Automated reviews cover the latest commit and findings are addressed.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The real dashboard recording shows saving a $75 personal monthly override while retaining the profile's $500 annual cap. The screenshot above shows the saved result from the running proxy.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b6037d4-f532-47f2-8f6f-a7cc779f5193

Local baseline and rebuilt proxies run with two workers each, separate PostgreSQL databases, and dedicated Redis instances. The rebuilt proxy accepted the same profile for two internal users and completed a real provider request. Its monthly and annual durable spend rows both matched the response cost of $0.000034.

Focused validation includes 536 management tests, 71 dashboard tests, 939 accounting/security tests, and 374 managed-billing tests. These suites overlap, so these counts are not a combined total. The auth regression run passed 835 cases with one metadata expectation failure, and that case passed after updating the expectation for the new empty authenticated window list.

Final enforcement scenarios, baseline UI proof, repository-wide lint, and current-tip CI are still being completed. Rust CI is under investigation. This is a regular PR for review, not a claim that it is merge-ready.

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Medium

- Existing usage is not backfilled into personal calendar windows.
- Unknown request costs cannot reserve an estimated maximum.
- Final CI, review findings, and complete live proof remain pending.

### Low

- Request and approval workflow remains separate in #51520.
- Existing parent, key, team, and organization ceilings still apply.

</details>
