title: feat(budgets): support annual calendar reset periods
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add annual budgets

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Budget forms and reset validation do not support annual budgets.

How it solves it:

- Add `12mo` budgets that reset on January 1.
- Use the configured timezone and reset time.
- Count the whole calendar year, including leap days.
- Reuse existing spend counters, persistence, and cache recovery.

Intentional product change: Budget forms offer a per year reset period.

## User Flow

Before, the admin cannot choose an annual budget.

1. Open `/budgets` and click Create Budget.
2. Enter `annual-calendar-proof` with a $1,200 spend limit.
3. Open Reset period. The options stop at per month.

![Before, reset options stop at per month](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38ef0f78-8b57-4726-b50e-60d9197fd95d)

After, the admin can save an annual budget.

1. Open `/budgets` and click Create Budget.
2. Enter `annual-calendar-proof` with a $1,200 spend limit.
3. Select per year and click Create budget. The new budget appears.

![After, per year selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28fa5705-d89a-4f8f-b825-cb1487085b23)

## Design

The new path applies only to annual `12mo` budgets. It uses the existing month-shift and timezone helpers to calculate the beginning of the year represented by the saved reset deadline. Annual admission, settlement, reset persistence and projected-spend alerts share that calculation. Annual deadlines are compared as timezone-aware instants, and annual reset jobs use their captured clock value.

Existing monthly, daily, weekly, hourly, minute and second schedules and accounting boundaries keep their behavior from main. The spend writer, recovery queries and upsert are unchanged. A comparison against `f85aa27c162c` verified 1,344 existing-duration cases with zero differences across reset schedules, admission starts, alert windows, calendar helpers and persisted reset starts.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests.
- [x] Focused backend and dashboard tests pass locally.
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks.
- [x] The PR only adds annual budget support.
- [ ] Every automated review covers the latest commit.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The screenshots and real UI recording show creating and saving a $1,200 annual budget. They were captured at `8dc9ff31e53`. The dashboard implementation is unchanged in the final annual-only revision. Fresh API verification on the final code uses two workers, PostgreSQL, Redis, and the configured development model gateway.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97ce51c9-e8b2-402b-bd2a-ca9f23bdbce4

![Saved annual budget](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68c792bc-0042-4821-88b3-e5fde21a0d91)

### Shared setup

Check out `f85aa27c162c` and `949145d09d484792e071fdaf6e4ad1af90f011a8` separately. Install their Python and dashboard dependencies and generate Prisma. Use separate local databases named `litellm_annual_before_20261112` and `litellm_annual_after_20261112`. The proof used the local PostgreSQL role `tin`. Export `LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD` and `PROXY_ADMIN_ID` in each process environment. Set `PYTHONPATH` to that process's checkout root.

The final config is below. The baseline changes only Redis port `6397` to `6396` and uses its separate database environment variable.

<details>
<summary>Proxy config and startup commands</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: annual-demo
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-terra
      api_base: https://gateway.product-dev.internal.litellm.ai/v1
      api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_DEV_API_KEY
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6397
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  database_connection_pool_limit: 5
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6397
  proxy_batch_write_at: 1
  disable_error_logs: true
litellm_settings:
  timezone: America/New_York
  drop_params: true
```

From each checkout root, the proxy commands were:

```bash
# Baseline environment uses its own DATABASE_URL and PYTHONPATH.
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6396 --save '' --appendonly no
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config before.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4096 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver

# Final environment uses its own DATABASE_URL and PYTHONPATH.
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6397 --save '' --appendonly no
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config after.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4097 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Both logs showed two serving worker PIDs. The dashboard commands, from each dashboard directory, were:

```bash
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL='' npm run dev -- --webpack --port 3078
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4097 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL='' npm run dev -- --port 3079
```

Baseline used webpack because Turbopack could not resolve its shared dependency symlink. The retained screenshots show the same annual form implementation before this rebase. Open `http://localhost:3078/budgets` and `http://localhost:3079/budgets`, log in with the configured local UI credentials, and follow the User Flow above.

</details>

Run the script below with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` exported. It omits generated keys from its output.

<details>
<summary>Exact annual creation, settlement and cold-cache client</summary>

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json, os, subprocess, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
master=os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']
evidence=[]
def call(port,path,data,key=master):
 request=urllib.request.Request(f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}',data=json.dumps(data).encode(),headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+key,'Content-Type':'application/json'})
 try:
  with urllib.request.urlopen(request,timeout=90) as response:
   return response.status,json.load(response),dict(response.headers)
 except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
  return error.code,json.load(error),dict(error.headers)
body={'models':['annual-demo'],'budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':1}]}
cases=(
 ('/v1/chat/completions',{'model':'annual-demo','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'Reply OK.'}],'max_completion_tokens':64}),
 ('/v1/responses',{'model':'annual-demo','input':'Reply OK.','max_output_tokens':64}),
 ('/v1/messages',{'model':'annual-demo','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'Reply OK.'}],'max_tokens':64}),
)
for label,port,path,request in ((label,port,path,request) for label,port in [('before',4096),('after',4097)] for path,request in cases):
 status,result,_=call(port,'/key/generate',body)
 evidence.append({'stage':label,'endpoint':path,'action':'create annual budget key','status':status,'budget_limits':result.get('budget_limits'),'error':result.get('error')})
 print(label,'create annual budget',status,flush=True)
 if label=='before':
  assert status==500 and 'only support 1 month' in result['error']['message']
  continue
 assert status==200
 key=result['key']; hashed=hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()
 reset=result['budget_limits'][0]['reset_at']
 now=datetime.now(timezone.utc)
 assert datetime.fromisoformat(reset.replace('Z','+00:00')).astimezone(timezone.utc)==datetime(now.year+1,1,1,5,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
 status,result,headers=call(port,path,request,key)
 print(path,'real provider request',status,flush=True)
 assert status==200, result.get('error')
 cost=float(headers['x-litellm-response-cost']); assert cost>0
 evidence.append({'stage':label,'endpoint':path,'action':'real provider request','status':status,'usage':result['usage'],'cost':cost})
 sql=f'''SELECT json_build_object('window_start',window_start,'spend',spend) FROM "LiteLLM_BudgetWindowSpend" WHERE entity_type='key' AND entity_id='{hashed}' AND window_duration='12mo' '''
 for attempt in range(30):
  raw=subprocess.check_output(['psql','postgresql://tin@127.0.0.1:5432/litellm_annual_after_20261112','-Atc',sql],text=True).strip()
  persisted=json.loads(raw) if raw else None
  if persisted and abs(persisted['spend']-cost)<1e-9: break
  time.sleep(1)
 assert persisted and abs(persisted['spend']-cost)<1e-9,persisted
 assert persisted['window_start'].startswith(f'{now.year}-01-01T05:00:00')
 evidence.append({'stage':label,'action':'durable annual spend','row':persisted})
 status,result,_=call(port,'/key/update',{'key':key,'budget_limits':[{'budget_duration':'12mo','max_budget':cost}]})
 assert status==200,result.get('error')
 subprocess.run(['redis-cli','-p','6397','DEL',f'spend:key:{hashed}:window:12mo'],check=True,capture_output=True)
 status,result,_=call(port,path,request,key)
 print(path,'cold-cache request at annual cap',status,flush=True)
 assert status in [422,429] and result['error'].get('litellm_error_type', result['error']['type'])=='budget_exceeded',result
 evidence.append({'stage':label,'endpoint':path,'action':'cold-cache request at annual cap','status':status,'error':result['error'].get('litellm_error_type', result['error']['type'])})
Path(__file__).with_name('evidence.json').write_text(json.dumps(evidence,indent=2))
print('annual live proof passed',flush=True)
```

</details>

### Before (`f85aa27c162c`)

Annual key creation returns HTTP 500 with `Monthly resets currently only support 1 month intervals` for each of the three endpoint scenarios. The form has no per year option, as shown above.

### After (`949145d09d484792e071fdaf6e4ad1af90f011a8`)

Annual key creation returns HTTP 200 with reset `2027-01-01T00:00:00-05:00`. Each endpoint succeeds with a real provider and persists the exact charged cost in the annual window beginning `2026-01-01T05:00:00Z`.

| Endpoint | Provider request | At annual cap after Redis eviction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/v1/chat/completions` | 200 | 422, budget exceeded |
| `/v1/responses` | 200 | 422, budget exceeded |
| `/v1/messages` | 200 | 422, budget exceeded |

### Existing-period compatibility

Run the same script below on main at `f85aa27c162c` and on the final checkout, passing separate output filenames. It exercises actual production functions with a fixed clock and records persistence calls at the database boundary. Both outputs contain 1,344 cases and compare identically. The annual live proxy check above separately verifies actual persistence and inference.

<details>
<summary>Existing-period comparison script</summary>

From each checkout, run `PYTHONPATH="$PWD" uv run --no-sync python check_existing_periods.py output.json`. Compare the two output files with `cmp`.

```python
import asyncio, json, sys
from datetime import datetime, time, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
from litellm.litellm_core_utils import duration_parser as dates
from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.budget_reservation import get_budget_window_start
from litellm.proxy.common_utils.reset_budget_job import ResetBudgetJob
from litellm.proxy._types import Litellm_EntityType
from litellm.proxy.utils import _reset_window

class Database:
    def __init__(self): self.db=self; self.parameters=None
    async def execute_raw(self, query, *parameters): self.parameters=parameters; return 1

async def main():
    snapshots=[]
    instants=('2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00','2026-03-08T06:59:59+00:00','2026-11-01T05:59:59+00:00','2026-10-03T15:29:59+00:00','2026-04-04T14:59:59+00:00','2028-02-29T12:00:00+00:00','2100-03-01T12:00:00+00:00')
    durations=('1s','45s','1m','30m','1h','2h','24h','1d','7d','30d','1w','1mo','hourly','daily','weekly','monthly')
    for duration in durations:
        for zone in ('UTC','America/New_York','Australia/Lord_Howe','Asia/Kathmandu'):
            for raw in instants:
                instant=datetime.fromisoformat(raw)
                end=dates.get_next_standardized_reset_time(duration,instant,zone,time(12,30))
                for stored in (end,datetime.fromisoformat(end.isoformat()),end.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)):
                    db=Database()
                    await ResetBudgetJob._roll_window_spend_row(db,Litellm_EntityType.KEY,'parity',duration,stored)
                    snapshots.append({
                        'duration':duration,'zone':zone,'now':raw,'stored':stored.isoformat(),
                        'next_reset':end.isoformat(),
                        'calendar_helper_start':dates.get_budget_window_start(duration,stored).isoformat(),
                        'admission_start':get_budget_window_start({'budget_duration':duration,'reset_at':stored}).isoformat(),
                        'alert_window':[x.isoformat() for x in _reset_window(duration,stored)],
                        'persisted_start':db.parameters[3].isoformat(),
                    })
    Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(json.dumps(snapshots,sort_keys=True,indent=2))
    print(len(snapshots),'existing duration cases recorded')
with patch('time.time',return_value=datetime(2028,3,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp()):
    asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

Tests cover January 1 equality, custom reset times, leap years, the 2100 century exception, stored offsets, naive UTC timestamps, timezone changes, annual reset deadlines and cold counters. title: feat(ui): manage customer organizations, teams, and members
body:
Refs #51459.

Customer usage pages show analytics, but admins need a way to manage the organization, its teams, and individual members. This adds scoped Teams, Members, and Settings navigation using the existing management APIs.

- Edit display names and budgets without changing IDs or parents.
- Select member budget templates, overrides, and expiry.
- Confirm deletion, show blocked-parent errors, and return to the parent after success.
- Keep usage links and breadcrumbs available at each level.

The UI remains proxy-admin-only. Child tables use parent filters and server pagination. Analytics and management share the hierarchy resolver.

title: feat(ui): add deployment-wide Aria visibility setting
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add admin disabling/hiding of aria across all of gateway

Closes [LIT-10736](https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-10736/feature-proxy-wide-admin-setting-to-hide-aria-agent-for-all-users-in).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Admins cannot hide Aria across their deployment

How it solves it:

- Adds “Hide Aria Agent for everyone” under UI Settings
- Saves the choice through existing admin settings
- Applies to navigation, Usage, shortcuts, and direct Aria URLs

Intentional product change: opting in hides Aria for all users, including admins, so deployments can remove its UI entry points

## User Flow

Before, the admin cannot hide Aria for everyone

1. Open `/admin-panel` and select UI Settings
2. Look for a deployment-wide Aria switch, which is missing
3. Members still see Aria Agent in navigation and Ask Aria on `/usage`

![Before, Aria remains visible and the global setting is missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4830e538-989b-46b8-b629-aaef6eccb5e7)

After, the admin can hide Aria for everyone

1. Open `/admin-panel` and select UI Settings
2. Enable “Hide Aria Agent for everyone”
3. Members lose both links on their next settings refresh
4. Opening `/aria` shows “Aria is not available for this session.”

![After, the saved global switch hides Aria](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a5a0b10-62c9-4bf0-84bc-017b403efe9f)

## Changes

- Adds `disable_aria`, defaulting to false, to the existing UI settings contract
- Reuses the admin-only write path, persistence, and config precedence
- Gates the shared Aria session and refreshes settings every 30 seconds
- Scopes settings queries to the active gateway and disables config-owned edits

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished and findings are addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The screenshots above use the same admin URL and isolated test database. The recording shows the real dashboard hiding, restoring, and hiding Aria again

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e65c0a3-a422-4548-807f-10a7c5065c68

Shared setup used Postgres 16 on port 5439, Redis 7 on port 6399, a two-worker proxy on port 4199, and the dashboard on port 3099. Both revisions used the same database and Redis. No model calls were needed for UI visibility

<details>
<summary>Local setup and replay commands</summary>

Use a prepared repository virtualenv and dashboard dependencies. Set `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, `UI_PASSWORD`, and `ARIA_MEMBER_PASSWORD` to isolated local test values. The database name used here is `aria_e2e`. Do not load production credentials

Save this as `aria-config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6399
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  store_model_in_db: true
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6399
```

Select the baseline or final checkout as `$ARIA_TREE` and use the same configuration for each run. The isolated database was initialized with Prisma's `db push`

```sh
cd "$ARIA_TREE"
.venv/bin/prisma db push --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma --skip-generate
export PYTHONPATH="$ARIA_TREE"
export STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True
export PROXY_BASE_URL=http://aria-e2e.localhost:4199
export LITELLM_CORS_ORIGINS=http://aria-e2e.localhost:3099,http://aria-member.localhost:3099
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True
export DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=True
export LITELLM_LOG=ERROR
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config "$ARIA_CONFIG" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4199 --num_workers 2
```

In another terminal

```sh
cd "$ARIA_TREE/litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard"
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4199 \
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://aria-e2e.localhost:4199 \
../../scripts/with_dashboard_node.sh npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3099
```

Baseline used `npm run dev:webpack` with the same arguments. Final used the default Turbopack development server. The final production build also passed

Create the member on the live proxy

```sh
curl -fsS http://aria-e2e.localhost:4199/user/new \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"user_id":"aria-member","user_email":"aria-member@example.test","user_role":"internal_user","auto_create_key":false}'
```

The local fixture password was seeded with the application's password hash and the real Prisma client

```python
import asyncio
import os
from prisma import Prisma
from litellm.proxy.utils import hash_password

async def seed():
    db = Prisma()
    await db.connect()
    await db.litellm_usertable.update(
        where={"user_id": "aria-member"},
        data={"password": hash_password(os.environ["ARIA_MEMBER_PASSWORD"])},
    )
    await db.disconnect()

asyncio.run(seed())
```

Sign in as the admin at `http://aria-e2e.localhost:3099`, and as `aria-member@example.test` at `http://aria-member.localhost:3099` so each has a separate browser session. Keep the member's `/usage` page open while changing the admin switch

</details>

### Before (`a7052ea8a80296ca3db064e438904f562f176933`)

1. Open `http://aria-e2e.localhost:3099/admin-panel` and select UI Settings
2. Observe no global Aria switch and the visible sidebar link, as pictured above

### After (`4f4a6706e89c6775d3961b2b1000d0962a519b7f`)

Current tip is `804546873949b5c75e4905c7312eebf2de2131a4`. The live proof and production build above were captured at `4f4a670`; the only later changes add four lines to two test mocks. Product source is identical between those revisions. Both affected test files pass all 78 tests, and the scoped `make check` passes, so the recorded proof carries forward under the repository’s neutral-diff rule

1. Enable the new switch on the same page and observe the success toast and hidden admin link
2. Leave the member dashboard open and observe both Aria links disappear without reloading
3. Open the member's `/aria` URL and observe the unavailable message with no composer
4. Reload admin settings and confirm the switch stays enabled, then disable it and observe Aria return
5. At a 390 × 844 viewport, open the member navigation drawer and confirm Aria is absent while hidden

Local validation passed 232 backend tests, 433 UI tests with two existing expected failures, `make check`, the production dashboard build, and CI test-ownership guards. The UI selection includes 70 Aria integration cases. Mutation checks caught removal of the visibility gate, and nine backend cases failed against baseline

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Low

- Active dashboards refresh visibility every 30 seconds
- This controls UI visibility, without revoking API permissions

## Final Attestation

- [x] Tests cover persistence, roles, config precedence, gateway switches, and active-session cleanup

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Deployment-wide UI gating affects all roles (including admins) and depends on timely settings polling; misconfiguration could hide Aria unexpectedly but does not change API auth.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a deployment-wide **`disable_aria`** flag to the existing UI settings API and admin panel, with a new **“Hide Aria Agent for everyone”** toggle that persists like other UI settings and respects config precedence when set in YAML.
> 
> When enabled, the dashboard **withholds the LiteAdmin/Aria session** (navigation links, Ask Aria, shortcuts) after UI settings load, **polls `/get/ui_settings` every 30 seconds**, and **clears active Aria conversations** when visibility flips. **`useUISettings`** now passes the **active proxy base URL** into `getUiSettings` and includes it in the React Query key so **switching gateways** does not reuse another deployment’s settings.
> 
> Backend and UI tests cover round-trip persistence, validation, admin-only updates, config overrides, and multi-gateway visibility behavior.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 804546873949b5c75e4905c7312eebf2de2131a4. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: fix(files): match every spelling of a provider file id in the ownership check (lts/1.108.x)
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e0e96689d6d347669888d9d85a15e4ef
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/e0e96689d6d347669888d9d85a15e4ef?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Backport of #51498 to lts/1.108.x, which carries #51032 as `23b716e2a3`. The enterprise hook lives at `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/` on this line, git remapped the path and the test tails were re-applied by hand.

Problem this solves:

- The provider file ownership check matched the stored id by exact string only
- A Gemini batch output can be addressed as `files/<id>`, `files%2F<id>`, `<id>/` or its URL
- Those spellings found no ownership row and passed through to the same Google file

How it solves it:

- `canonical_provider_file_id` collapses every spelling to the bare id
- `provider_file_id_spellings` unwraps a model-encoded id and adds the `files/` and Gemini URL forms, so `enforce_provider_file_access` matches rows written before ids were canonicalized
- `canonical_provider_file_id` leaves every URL or URI that is not on Gemini's host opaque, so an upload whose storage URL happens to contain `files/<id>` (an Azure blob named `upload.files%2Ffile-victim`) can never index someone else's id
- `store_unified_file_id` and `store_batch_output_file_ownership` index the canonical id, and `get_unified_file_ids_for_provider_file_ids` maps a provider's listing back to the row by canonical id

## User Flow

Before: a key on another team reads a Gemini batch output it does not own by respelling the file id

1. Team A's key runs a Gemini batch through POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches and its output file is registered to team A
2. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/batch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 403
3. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/files%2Fbatch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 200 with team A's rows
4. Another user could read any output file whose Google file name they knew

After: every spelling of the id is held to the same ownership row

1. Team A's key runs the same batch and its output file is registered to team A
2. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/batch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 403
3. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/files%2Fbatch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 403, same for `batch-out1/` and the full Gemini URL
4. Team A's key still reads the file under any of those spellings, and a file nobody registered still passes through as before

## Relevant issues

Finding F-1 on #51032, backport of #51498

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live run on this line, two proxies off lts/1.108.x against one Postgres and a real Gemini key, the line tip on :4021 and this branch on :4020, with `gemini/gemini-3.8-flash` (Gemini retired `gemini-2.5-flash` for new keys). On each proxy team A uploads a batch input, runs a batch to completion and team B then asks for the output file under every spelling.

```bash
# per proxy, PORT 4021 (line tip) then 4020 (this branch)
PYTHONPATH=$PWD/enterprise:$PWD python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port $PORT --use_v2_migration_resolver
curl -s -X POST $H/team/new -H "$MK" -d '{"team_alias":"team-a"}'   # and team-b, then /key/generate for each
curl -s -X POST $H/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KA" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names=gemini-flash -F file=@input.jsonl
curl -s -X POST $H/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KA" -d '{"input_file_id":"<unified id>","endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","completion_window":"24h","model":"gemini-flash"}'
# poll GET $H/v1/batches/<id> until completed, decode output_file_id to its provider id, then
for sp in "$BARE" "files/$BARE" "files%2F$BARE" "$BARE/"; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" $H/v1/files/$sp/content -H "Authorization: Bearer $KB"; done
```

title: fix(router): validate request fields and ignore scalar fallback overrides
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description More leniently accept request fields, and return a 400 not 500
Details Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9c87c045c80c4d50967fb8f3fddfb398 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/9c87c045c80c4d50967fb8f3fddfb398?variant=devin Requested by: @narmstrong-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - String fallback overrides fail with HTTP 500 How it solves it: - Validate request start fields through frozen `RequestStartFields` - Ignore standalone strings in all three fallback override fields - Parse `max_fallbacks` with a bounded Pydantic integer - Return HTTP 400 for invalid override values Intentional product change: standalone string fallback overrides are ignored, leaving configured fallbacks in effect. Other malformed fallback overrides return HTTP 400 instead of a router shape error. Normal Pydantic integer coercion accepts booleans, whole-number floats, and integer-valued strings within the Rust `u32` range. Explicit fallback nulls, empty lists, literal-`True` flags, derived caller fields, and retry handling retain their meaning. ## User Flow Before, requests carrying string fallback overrides fail before serving the model response. 1. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"fallbacks": "default"` or `"max_fallbacks": "2"` 2. Receive HTTP 500 with `the router request does not have the shape router-core reads` After, standalone fallback strings are ignored, integer strings are parsed, and other malformed values return HTTP 400. 1. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"fallbacks": "default"` or `"max_fallbacks": "2"` 2. Receive the model response using configured fallbacks, or HTTP 400 for other invalid override values ## Relevant issues Fixes #51396 ## Affected release Regression since v1.110.0-dev.1. The originating thread requests an RC backport after the main fix lands. No backport has been made. ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10711 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished and its findings are addressed ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live-proxy proof against the final implementation is pending. Earlier local reproduction returned HTTP 500 for both string fallback overrides and an invalid `max_fallbacks` string. That run used mock settings and does not satisfy the real-provider proof requirement. At `22fc056aef`, 196 focused fallback, characterization, and request-override tests passed. The Ruff strict, type-discipline, and test-quality gates passed against `origin/main`, and `git diff --check` passed. The type-check gate is still running. These are supplementary regression checks, not live proof. ## Caveats ### Medium - Final live proof, CI, and CLA clearance remain outstanding

Problem this solves:

How it solves it:

- Adds together_ai/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small priced from GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models

## Rows

together_ai/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small (kind api, new row)

Prices come from GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models, id `thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small`: `pricing.input = 0.3`, `pricing.output = 1`, `pricing.cached_input = 0.03` per 1M tokens, so input_cost_per_token 3e-07, output_cost_per_token 1e-06, cache_read_input_token_cost 3e-08. The same response gives `context_length: 1048576`, written as max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens the way the sibling together_ai rows carry the Together context length (inherited_from: together_ai/thinkingmachines/Inkling for the max_output_tokens convention, Together publishes no separate output limit). `type: chat` gives mode chat. The November 12, 2026 changelog entry on https://docs.together.ai/docs/changelog states the same values: "thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small: 1,048,576 context length, NVFP4 quantization, text and image input, function calling, and structured outputs. Pricing: $0.30 input / $1.00 output / $0.03 cached input (per 1M tokens)". The serverless catalog on https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless-models lists the row "Thinking Machines | Inkling 2 Small | thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small | 1048576 | $0.30 | $0.03 | $1.00 | NVFP4 | Yes | Yes" under the Function calling and Structured outputs columns, and the pricing page https://www.together.ai/pricing shows "Inkling 2 Small | $0.30 | $0.03 (cached) | $1.00".

supports_prompt_caching true follows from the `pricing.cached_input` meter. supports_function_calling true and supports_response_schema true come from the changelog sentence and the two Yes cells quoted above. supports_vision true comes from "text and image input" in the changelog and from the model appearing in the Vision models table on the serverless catalog page. supports_reasoning true comes from the Together model page https://www.together.ai/models/inkling-2-small, which tags the model Chat, Reasoning and Vision and states "Reasoning effort is variable per request; published results use effort 0.99 (xhigh) with temperature 1.0". supports_tool_choice true comes from Together's function calling best practices page https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/function-calling/best-practices, which documents tool_choice for every function calling model: "The tool_choice parameter decides whether the model may call a tool on a given request. \"auto\" (default): the model decides whether to call a tool or reply with text. \"required\": the model must call at least one tool", and the serverless catalog lists this model with Function calling Yes. supports_parallel_function_calling is left off because no Together page states parallel tool calls for this model.

https://api.together.ai/v1/models: all 80 priced chat ids compared against the catalog, 0 price mismatches. Inkling-2-Small was the only priced id without a row.

https://docs.together.ai/docs/changelog: the November 12 entry announces Inkling-2-Small (this row). The November 10 (elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0) and November 5 (moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) entries match the catalog. No other price or deprecation announcement differs from the catalog. together-ai-21.1b-41b, together-ai-4.1b-8b, together-ai-41.1b-80b, together-ai-8.1b-21b, together-ai-81.1b-110b, together-ai-embedding-151m-to-350m, together-ai-embedding-up-to-150m and together-ai-up-to-4b are generic size tier keys that /v1/models never lists by design, so they are a coverage gap and not delistings. No key is deleted.

title: chore(cost-map): add fal_ai/google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.2/upscale priced per second of upscaled video
body:
## Summary

Adds one fal_ai row, `fal_ai/google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.2/upscale`, kind page. The id was left unpriced by earlier fal-ai syncs because its page bills by source and target resolution. The target resolution tiers map onto the `output_cost_per_second_*` fields the sibling upscale rows (`fal_ai/fal-ai/bytedance-upscaler/upscale/video`, `fal_ai/blackforestlabs/flux-video-upscale`) already use, so the row follows that shape and takes the higher rate where the 1080p tier depends on the source resolution, with the caveat in `metadata.comment`.

## Row evidence

Source: https://fal.ai/models/google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.2/upscale (fetched raw from its llms.txt on 2026-11-13)

Pricing quote: "Billing is calculated per second of upscaled output video, based on the source and target resolution. Upscaling **360p to 720p** or **720p to 1080p** costs about **$0.041** per second; **360p to 1080p** costs **$0.0819** per second; and **720p or 1080p to 4K** costs **$0.1638** per second. The target resolution must be higher than the source. Upscaling a **10-second 720p** clip to **1080p** costs about **$0.41**, or about **$1.64** to **4K**."

- `output_cost_per_second_720p: 0.041` from "360p to 720p ... costs about $0.041 per second"
- `output_cost_per_second_1080p: 0.0819` from "360p to 1080p costs $0.0819 per second". The 1080p target has two source-dependent rates ("720p to 1080p costs about $0.041 per second" is the other) and the cost calculator selects by target resolution alone, so the row takes the higher one and never undercounts, the same convention `fal_ai/blackforestlabs/flux-video-upscale` uses when the rate depends on the source. A 720p source upscaled to 1080p is overcounted by $0.0409 per second, named in `metadata.comment`
- `output_cost_per_second_4k: 0.1638` from "720p or 1080p to 4K costs $0.1638 per second"
- `output_cost_per_second: 0.0819`, the default resolution (1080p) rate, same convention as the sibling gemini-omni-flash rows. Input schema quote: "`resolution` ... The target resolution of the upscaled video. Must be higher than the source video's resolution. Default value: `"1080p"` ... Options: `"720p"`, `"1080p"`, `"4k"`"
- `mode: video_generation`, `supported_endpoints: ["/v1/videos"]`, `supported_output_modalities: ["video"]` from "Category: video-to-video" and the output schema "`video` (`File`, required): The generated video"
- `supported_modalities: ["video"]`: the input schema has only `video_url` and `resolution`, no prompt field
- No `input_cost_per_token`: unlike the v1.2 generation siblings, the page states no token price

Cross-check: `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing?endpoint_id=google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.2/upscale` returns a single base price of `0.0273` per `seconds` with no tiers, which matches none of the page tiers (it is the 360p rate the sibling v1.2 rows record), so the row trusts llms.txt as the fal-ai lane prescribes.

## Still unpriced

Ten fal-ai ids re-checked raw this run still have no `llms.txt` page (HTTP 404) and are not in the fal pricing API ("Endpoint(s) not found"): fal-ai/decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video, fal-ai/luma-photon, fal-ai/luma-photon/flash, fal-ai/luma-photon/flash/modify, fal-ai/luma-photon/flash/reframe, fal-ai/luma-photon/modify, fal-ai/luma-photon/reframe, fal-ai/magi-distilled, fal-ai/magi-distilled/extend-video, fal-ai/magi-distilled/image-to-video. They stay out of the catalog.

Ruling fal-ai-promotional-rates-apply-until-promotion-ends does not apply, the page states no promotional rate.

title: fix(files): match every spelling of a provider file id in the ownership check
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

fix gemini batches bug

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e0e96689d6d347669888d9d85a15e4ef
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/e0e96689d6d347669888d9d85a15e4ef?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The provider file ownership check matched the stored id by exact string only
- A Gemini batch output can be addressed as `files/<id>`, `files%2F<id>`, `<id>/` or its URL
- Those spellings found no ownership row and passed through to the same Google file

How it solves it:

- `canonical_provider_file_id` collapses every spelling to the bare id
- `provider_file_id_spellings` unwraps a model-encoded id and adds the `files/` and Gemini URL forms, so `enforce_provider_file_access` also matches upload rows written before ids were canonicalized
- `canonical_provider_file_id` leaves every URL or URI that is not on Gemini's host opaque, so an upload whose storage URL happens to contain `files/<id>` (an Azure blob named `upload.files%2Ffile-victim`) can never index someone else's id
- `store_unified_file_id` and `store_batch_output_file_ownership` index the canonical id, and `get_unified_file_ids_for_provider_file_ids` maps a provider's listing back to the row by canonical id, so a Gemini URI still finds its managed file

## User Flow

Before: a key on another team reads a Gemini batch output it does not own by respelling the file id

1. Team A's key runs a Gemini batch through POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches and its output file is registered to team A
2. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/batch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 403
3. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/files%2Fbatch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 200 with team A's rows
4. Another user could read any output file whose Google file name they knew

After: every spelling of the id is held to the same ownership row

1. Team A's key runs the same batch and its output file is registered to team A
2. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/batch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 403
3. Team B's key sends GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/files%2Fbatch-out1/content?provider=gemini and gets 403, same for `batch-out1/` and the full Gemini URL
4. Team A's key still reads the file under any of those spellings, and a file nobody registered still passes through as before

## Relevant issues

Finding F-1 on #51032

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy with Postgres, one `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash` deployment named `gemini-flash`, two teams with one virtual key each. Team A uploads a file through the proxy as a managed file, then team B asks for that file's content under every spelling of its Gemini id, as the finding on #51032 did. Gemini only serves the content of generated files, so a request that reaches Google answers 400 `Only GENERATED files can be downloaded` while a request the proxy stops answers 403. Before, every spelling from team B reaches Google. After, every spelling from team B is refused and every spelling from team A still reaches Google. The same file ids are used against both proxies, so the row written by the base proxy (the full Gemini URI) is the one the fixed proxy checks.

<details>
<summary>Rig (same for both proxies, base at main 0721e9aa8b on :4011 and the tip on :4010)</summary>

```yaml
# config.yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-flash
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

```
$ LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost:5432/litellm GEMINI_API_KEY=... \
  python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4011 --use_v2_migration_resolver   # base
$ ... --port 4010 ...   # tip
$ curl -X POST :4011/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -d '{"team_id":"team-a","models":["gemini-flash"]}'   # and team-b
$ curl -X POST :4011/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -d '{"team_id":"team-a","models":["gemini-flash"]}'  # KEY_A, and KEY_B for team-b
$ curl -X POST :4011/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names=gemini-flash -F file=@input.jsonl
$ for sp in "$ID" "files/$ID" "files%2F$ID" "$ID/" "$WRAPPED"; do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" ":$PORT/gemini/v1/files/$sp/content?provider=gemini" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"; done
```

`$WRAPPED` is `encode_file_id_with_model(ID, "gemini-flash")`, the model-encoded id from the Greptile finding.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Before and after, row stored by the base proxy</summary>

```
ROW stored by main 0721e9aa8b as URI: {https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/files/h38uznfhl7fk}|team-a
BEFORE (main 0721e9aa8b, :4011)
teamB  h38uznfhl7fk                                                   -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
teamB  files/h38uznfhl7fk                                             -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
teamB  files%2Fh38uznfhl7fk                                           -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
teamB  h38uznfhl7fk/                                                  -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
teamB  file-bGl0ZWxsbTpoMzh1em5maGw3Zms7bW9kZWwsZ2VtaW5pLWZsYXNo      -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
teamA  h38uznfhl7fk                                                   -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
teamA  files/h38uznfhl7fk                                             -> 400 {"error":{"message":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": 400,\n
```

title: feat(proxy): add customer usage tracking and drilldowns
body:
Refs #51459.

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Feat - Customer Portal, allow spend by customer org, team and members 

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer organizations need usage drilldowns across teams and members.

How it solves it:

- Tracks validated customer attribution through the accounting ledger.
- Reuses shared daily analytics and the Usage page styling.
- Matches chart breakdowns with Top X rankings.
- Shows member spend, tokens, caps, and budget status.

Intentional product change: adds `/ui/customers/usage/?org=<customer_org_id>` for the customer organization detail view. The chart switches between models, API keys, and teams. Member names in the table open each member’s usage. A separate member spend table stays below the rankings.

## User Flow

Before, the customer usage detail page is unavailable.

1. Open `/ui/customers/usage/?org=demo-org`.
2. The page returns 404.

![Before at main 6685525fa2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e3c2cfeb0f037fa322f50c28f1fb7e8d32e1a7c7/.github/pr-assets/customer-usage-detail/before-main-6685525.png)

After, the detail page shows usage for the selected customer scope.

1. Open the same customer usage route.
2. Choose a chart breakdown and spend, tokens, or requests.
3. Read the matching Top X table and drill into teams or members.
4. Review member spend and configured caps underneath.

![Customer usage overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e3c2cfeb0f037fa322f50c28f1fb7e8d32e1a7c7/.github/pr-assets/customer-usage-detail/final-overview.png)

![Top teams and member spend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e3c2cfeb0f037fa322f50c28f1fb7e8d32e1a7c7/.github/pr-assets/customer-usage-detail/final-report.png)

## APIs

All three routes are proxy-admin-only and return `SpendAnalyticsPaginatedResponse`.

```text
GET /management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity?customer_org_ids=...
GET /management/v1/customer_teams/daily/activity?customer_team_ids=...
GET /management/v1/customer_members/daily/activity?customer_member_ids=...
```

They accept the shared date, model, API key, page, and page-size parameters and matching `exclude_*_ids`. Each delegates to `get_daily_activity` with `litellm_dailycustomermemberspend`; entities and aliases follow the queried level. The UI reads spend and effective budgets from the existing hierarchy APIs.

Request attribution uses `metadata.customer_org_id`, `customer_team_id`, or `customer_member_id`. Ancestors are resolved and checked before provider calls. Non-admin keys must have an admin-assigned customer organization binding.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Before was captured at `6685525fa2`: the new UI and all three API routes return 404 while the existing Usage page returns 200.

After screenshots use synthetic demo data. The live proxy ran with two workers, dedicated Redis, and a controlled OpenAI-compatible upstream. One request with 100 prompt and 20 completion tokens added $0.14, 120 tokens, and one request to the organization, team, and member totals. Cross-organization attribution and key rebinding were rejected, and repeated accounting flushes added no duplicate usage. The analytics components and accounting behavior remain covered after merging the current target branch.

## Customer identifier error proof

Actual curl requests used the registered proxy app at `8fa3bd7`, a controlled auth fixture bound to `org-1`, and a customer DB fixture with `member-2` under another org. Before loaded the resolver from `e3c2cfe`; after used `8fa3bd7`. These checks stopped before provider dispatch and used no external database or credentials.

Before:

```bash
curl --silent --show-error --max-time 15 --request POST --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"model":"controlled-model","metadata":{"customer_member_id":"missing-member"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"controlled"}]}' http://127.0.0.1:50362/v1/chat/completions --write-out '
%{http_code}'
```

```text
HTTP 400
{"error":{"message":"The customer usage organization, team, or member does not exist.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"400"}}
```

```bash
curl --silent --show-error --max-time 15 --request POST --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"model":"controlled-model","metadata":{"customer_member_id":"member-2"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"controlled"}]}' http://127.0.0.1:50362/v1/chat/completions --write-out '
%{http_code}'
```

```text
HTTP 400
{"error":{"message":"Customer usage identifiers must belong to the same organization and team.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"400"}}
```

After, both requests return the same response:

```bash
curl --silent --show-error --max-time 15 --request POST --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"model":"controlled-model","metadata":{"customer_member_id":"missing-member"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"controlled"}]}' http://127.0.0.1:50379/v1/chat/completions --write-out '
%{http_code}'
curl --silent --show-error --max-time 15 --request POST --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"model":"controlled-model","metadata":{"customer_member_id":"member-2"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"controlled"}]}' http://127.0.0.1:50379/v1/chat/completions --write-out '
%{http_code}'
```

```text
HTTP 403
{"error":{"message":"Customer usage must match the customer organization assigned to this API key.","type":"permission_error","param":null,"code":"403"}}
```

The same missing and cross-org cases on `POST /v1/responses` also returned identical 403 responses, using `litellm_metadata.customer_member_id` and `input: "controlled"`.

## Validation

Production UI build, production TypeScript checks, zero-warning UI ESLint, source Ruff, changed-source formatting, import checks, 34 UI tests, 203 targeted backend tests, and 105 customer auth tests passed. Shared analytics and ledger replay regressions also passed.

CI follow-up fixes regenerate the API enum, remove an unreachable database guard, register the new table for tracing, and update the spend-log snapshots. Rate-limit metric tests now follow the existing idle-borrowing behavior. Customer key flows reuse validated metadata through typed boundaries.

At `8fa3bd7`: 825 key-management, 348 auth/customer/onboarding, 278 spend-management, 126 rate-limiter, 26 tracing/Pub/Sub, 29 follow-up metadata, and 34 customer UI tests passed. Production UI build, TypeScript, ESLint, Ruff and strict lint passed.

All required GitHub checks passed on `8fa3bd7`. The PR merged as `df8b3b4`.

## Caveats

### Medium

- A final local whole-project type-check run also ran out of disk space; focused type checks passed. GitHub’s complete Python check passed on the final PR head.
- Full `make check` did not complete because its native dependency build exhausted local disk space.
- Whole-tree Black hit the same limit. Unrelated formatter changes were restored.
- Hierarchy tracking requires the accounting ledger. Budget status uses stored spend and configured caps.

## Final Attestation

- [x] Tests cover customer scope isolation, paging, breakdown selection, budget display, and accounting retries.

</details>

title: fix(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): a capped borrower keeps its cap on its own counter and gets a fresh share at saturation
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2548aa9ed444483f8e7cc4aaf1a2544d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2548aa9ed444483f8e7cc4aaf1a2544d?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:
- Follow-up to #51415: a capped team's cap ran on its share counter
- So its idle usage kept counting and it got no fresh share at saturation
- Six share metric unit tests broke on main when #51415 met #51417

How it solves it:
- The cap gets its own counter, `model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple`, counting all usage this window
- The share counter still counts only usage made while the model is saturated
- Each counter carries its own reservation and window through fallbacks, failures and WebSocket turns
- A prompt without `max_tokens` is sized against the share whether the model is idle or saturated
- Capped idle teams and idle fallbacks still publish `litellm_dynamic_limiter_borrowed_tokens` from the cap counter
- The metric tests saturate the model from a separate priority class before measuring

## User Flow

Before: a team with `team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple: 3` is held the moment another team shows up
1. Team A, `model_tpm_limit: 100`, sends four POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions while the model is idle and uses 120 tokens, under its 300 cap
2. Team C starts sending the same request and the model passes `saturation_threshold`
3. Team A's next request gets 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated` and `retry-after: 60`, since its 120 idle tokens sit on its share counter
4. Team B, a newcomer under its share, gets 200

After: the same team gets its full share once the model saturates, and its cap still bounds its total
1. Team A sends the same four requests while idle and uses 120 tokens, under its 300 cap
2. Team C starts sending and the model passes `saturation_threshold`
3. Team A's next three requests get 200, then the fourth gets 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated` once it spent 100 tokens under saturation
4. Team D, `team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple: 1.1`, that used 90 tokens while idle gets 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple`, its cap of 110 has no room for another request
5. Team B gets 200

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites to CI
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live two-worker proxy, before on `main` (`a7052ea8a8`) and after at `82c399fcba`, same config, same Redis, same driver. The commits after it change the WebSocket frame refresh and the share gauges only, each with its own unit test, not the chat completion path the proof drives. The upstream is a synthetic OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1:9009 that answers every chat completion with 20 prompt and 10 completion tokens, so each call is 30 tokens.

<details>
<summary>Proxy command and config</summary>

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

`--reload` is dropped so both workers serve, two worker PIDs confirmed in the log for each leg. Env: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`. Redis flushed between legs.

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: shared-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini
      api_key: synthetic-openai-key
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9009/v1
      tpm: 1000
      rpm: 1000

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"]
  priority_reservation:
    interactive: 0.6
    batch: 0.4
  priority_reservation_settings:
    default_priority: 1.0
    saturation_threshold: 0.25
    team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams: true
    saturation_check_cache_ttl: 2

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Driver</summary>

Four teams, each created with `POST /team/new` carrying `metadata.model_tpm_limit: {"shared-model": 100}`, team A also `team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple: 3`, team D `1.1`, then one key per team from `POST /key/generate`. Every call is `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "shared-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "cap <timestamp>"}]}`. Team A sends 4 calls idle (120 tokens), team D 3 calls idle (90 tokens), team C 16 calls so the model passes 25% saturation, then after a 4 second pause for the saturation cache team A is called until it gets a 429, then team D once, then team B once.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Before, main a7052ea8a8</summary>

```text
t=  0.3s team-a(3x) 200
t=  0.4s team-a(3x) 200
t=  0.6s team-a(3x) 200
t=  0.7s team-a(3x) 200
team-a (share 100, cap 300) borrowed 120 tokens while the model was idle
t=  0.9s team-d(1.1x) 200
t=  1.0s team-d(1.1x) 200
t=  1.1s team-d(1.1x) 200
team-d (share 100, cap 110) borrowed 90 tokens while the model was idle
... team-c 16 calls, 200 until the model saturates, then 429 model_per_team_saturated on its own share
team-c used 480, the model is at 690 of 1000 tokens, past the 25% saturation threshold
t=  6.4s team-a(3x) 429 rate_limited_by=model_per_team_saturated retry-after=60
t=  6.4s team-d(1.1x) 429 rate_limited_by=model_per_team_saturated retry-after=60
t=  6.5s team-b     200
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>After, tip 82c399fcba</summary>

```text
t=  0.2s team-a(3x) 200
t=  0.3s team-a(3x) 200
t=  0.3s team-a(3x) 200
t=  0.4s team-a(3x) 200
team-a (share 100, cap 300) borrowed 120 tokens while the model was idle
t=  0.5s team-d(1.1x) 200
t=  0.7s team-d(1.1x) 200
t=  0.8s team-d(1.1x) 200
team-d (share 100, cap 110) borrowed 90 tokens while the model was idle
... team-c 16 calls, 200 until the model saturates, then 429 model_per_team_saturated on its own share
team-c used 480, the model is at 690 of 1000 tokens, past the 25% saturation threshold
t=  6.1s team-a(3x) 200
t=  6.2s team-a(3x) 200
t=  6.3s team-a(3x) 200
t=  6.4s team-a(3x) 429 rate_limited_by=model_per_team_saturated retry-after=60
t=  6.5s team-d(1.1x) 429 rate_limited_by=model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple retry-after=60
t=  6.5s team-b     200
```

</details>

Team A, capped at 3x, is held at once on main and gets its fresh 100 tokens at the tip, three 30-token calls then a 429 on its share. Team D at 1.1x had 20 tokens of cap left and is refused on both, on main as saturated and at the tip for the reason that applies, its borrow cap. Team B is admitted on both.

Unit: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py -q` at the tip, 132 passed. The capped tests fail on `main` (the share counter reads -50 where the tip reads a fresh 100, and the capped team is refused at saturation). The two reservation tests and the two round-two tests fail without their fix and pass with it. `main` itself has 6 failures in this file in the share metric tests, repaired here.

Observed while proving, not changed here: each worker reads `model_saturation_check` through the in-memory side of the dual cache, and with steady traffic that copy keeps its TTL and drifts from Redis by the tokens the other worker served, so the two workers disagree on whether the model is saturated. That is why the threshold is 0.25 in this proof rather than 0.5.

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core team borrowing, atomic rate-limit increments, and settlement across pre-call, fallback, WebSocket, and failure paths; incorrect counter wiring could admit over-limit traffic or mis-report limits.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR **splits capped team borrowing into two counters**: the existing **share** counter (`model_per_team_saturated`) only accrues usage while the model is saturated, and a new **borrow cap** counter (`model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple`) tracks all usage in the window when `team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple` is set.
> 
> **Admission and holds** now enforce the cap while idle and the share once saturated; token reservations are still **sized from the team's share limit**, not the cap. Request stash and fallback holds carry separate share/cap descriptors, reservations, and settlement windows through success, failure, WebSocket turns, and router fallbacks.
> 
> **429 semantics** route borrow-cap breaches via descriptor key to `model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple` instead of treating idle cap usage as saturated share. **Prometheus share/borrow metrics** use `_capped_idle_share` so idle capped teams still publish borrowed tokens against the cap counter while reading share size from the share descriptor.
> 
> Unit tests cover idle vs saturated capped borrowers, reservation sizing, WebSocket transitions, and updated metric expectations.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c8ef191093224e5a6d9016390455171c09ed1c29. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(spend): add daily customer usage and budget resets
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add customer spend tracking on requests and budget resets on customer tables

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer usage has no daily history or recurring budget resets.

How it solves it:

- Add daily customer usage rows to existing accounting delivery.
- Reset customer budgets through the existing reset job.

## User Flow

Before, customer spend stays charged after its recurring budget period.

1. An admin creates a customer hierarchy with recurring budgets.
2. Their application calls `POST https://proxy.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with `x-litellm-customer-member-id` and receives 200.
3. After the period expires, the member still shows the old spend.

After, recurring customer budgets reset while daily usage history remains available.

1. An admin creates a customer hierarchy with recurring budgets.
2. Their application calls `POST https://proxy.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with `x-litellm-customer-member-id` and receives 200.
3. After the period expires and the reset job runs, current spend resets and historical daily usage remains.

## Scope

Stacked on #51489. That PR owns hierarchy authentication, request metadata and running spend increments. This PR consumes its resolved IDs and adds `LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend` plus customer organization, team and member budget resets. There is no new hierarchy lookup or second charge to the running counters.

The daily table carries all three customer IDs and existing daily metrics. Its unique key includes the parent IDs so reusing a deleted member ID under another parent preserves historical attribution. Dates are UTC. Ledger delivery writes the daily row inside its existing transaction. Legacy delivery uses the existing daily queue, Redis buffer and bulk upsert.

The reset job initializes schedules without erasing spend, uses the active member override or template duration, and preserves concurrent charges with the existing guarded decrement. It evicts affected hierarchy caches after commit and broadcasts through the existing cache mechanism. Daily history is retained. Effective duration changes are evaluated when an existing schedule becomes due.

The migration changes schema only and is idempotent. `litellm-proxy-extras` moves from 0.4.114 to 0.4.115 so its package can distribute the migration. No core or enterprise version bump, provider changes, activity APIs or management UI changes are included.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live before/after passed against base `de6abf91c36` and this PR at `e8a89bb6176`. Each run used a fresh PostgreSQL database, two serving workers, dedicated Redis, and real calls through the internal gateway. After was exercised with both ledger delivery and legacy Redis buffering. Current tip `084af9ec6d9` is based on `9c80dbaab14`. Since the live run, our follow-ups document query bounds, chart the customer Redis queue metrics and update an existing recovery test fixture. The base follow-up adds a service-target label and typing/test cleanup, with no identity, cost or SQL changes. These follow-ups leave the tested accounting behavior unchanged, so the live proof is carried forward.

All 550 focused unit tests and 13 PostgreSQL cases pass on `0a30b204aef`. The database cases cover ledger and legacy delivery, retained/disabled spend logs, daily-write rollback/retry, concurrent charges, override expiry and hierarchy cache invalidation. Schema copies match, all 242 migrations passed the no-data-rewrite check, and 53 CI-coverage checks passed. The unbounded-query checker reports zero new findings.

Four deliberate mutations were detected. Dropping the daily projection, using the wrong date, suppressing the reset decrement, and keeping stale hierarchy caches each made the relevant tests fail. The unmodified implementation passed.

Python lint, strict/type-discipline/test-quality/OpenAPI-doc gates, the type delta gate against `de6abf91c36`, and e2e type checking passed. Lazy OpenAPI and dashboard API type regeneration passed with no diff. Those checks and the 550-test run above precede the latest CI follow-up. Current CI and automated reviews are rerunning.


E2E exception at `084af9ec6d9` applies only to the CI follow-up. It adds the three customer queue series to the existing Grafana panels and passes the two required customer queue inputs to the existing recovery test. No accounting implementation changed. The two failures were observed in CI at `0a30b204aef`. After the fix, 10 dashboard tests and 121 spend, Redis and CI-coverage tests pass, along with `make check`, formatting, JSON validation and secret scanning. Codecov is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>CI follow-up verification</summary>

```bash
PYDANTIC_DISABLE_PLUGINS=__all__ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:logfire -q --tb=short tests/unit/integrations/test_prometheus_metric_name_consistency.py
# 10 passed
PYDANTIC_DISABLE_PLUGINS=__all__ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:logfire -q --tb=short tests/unit/proxy/db/test_model_access_group_spend.py tests/unit/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/test_redis_update_buffer.py tests/unit/test_assert_ci_coverage.py
# 121 passed
PYDANTIC_DISABLE_PLUGINS=__all__ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true make check BASE_REF=origin/litellm_customer_hierarchy_enforcement LINT_DEP_INSTALL=
# PASS
```

The first local run combined the integration and proxy groups. The proxy collection hook sorted all tests by name, exposing an existing missing spend-log storage metric in the dashboard fixture. Both the hook and the affected metric code are unchanged from the pinned base. Running the groups separately, as CI does, passed. That unrelated order dependency is outside this fix.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Shared live setup, client requests and database checks</summary>

Use a fresh scratch PostgreSQL database in `DATABASE_URL` for each checkout. Export `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE`, `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` and `CUSTOMER_SPEND_UPSTREAM_MODEL`. The upstream alias was `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, selected from the internal gateway inventory. The reported costs below use the configured test rates.

The schema was initialized with the following code, inside the checkout being tested.

```python
import os, subprocess
from pathlib import Path
import psycopg
schema = subprocess.check_output([
    "python", "-m", "prisma", "migrate", "diff", "--from-empty",
    "--to-schema-datamodel", "litellm/schema.prisma", "--script",
], text=True)
with psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) as db:
    db.execute(schema)
migration = Path("litellm/proxy-extras/litellm_proxy_extras/migrations/20261113000000_customer_spend/migration.sql")
if migration.exists():
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) as db:
        db.execute(migration.read_text())
        db.execute(migration.read_text())
```

This is the ledger configuration. The legacy run changes `use_spend_logs_ledger` to `false` and `use_redis_transaction_buffer` to `true`.

```yaml
general_settings:
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6498
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  proxy_batch_write_at: 1
  proxy_budget_rescheduler_max_time: 5
  proxy_budget_rescheduler_min_time: 5
  use_redis_transaction_buffer: false
  use_spend_logs_ledger: true
litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
model_list:
- litellm_params:
    api_base: os.environ/LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE
    api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY
    input_cost_per_token: 1.0e-06
    model: os.environ/CUSTOMER_SPEND_UPSTREAM_MODEL
    output_cost_per_token: 2.0e-06
  model_name: customer-spend-qa
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6498

```

```bash
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6498 --save '' --appendonly no
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa.yaml --port 4198 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

The process environment also set `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true`, `LITELLM_COLLECTOR_ENABLED=false`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true` and `PYDANTIC_DISABLE_PLUGINS=__all__`. Reload was omitted because Uvicorn disables multiple workers in reload mode. Two serving worker PIDs were verified in every run.

```python
import json, os, time
from pathlib import Path
import httpx, psycopg
from psycopg import sql

api = httpx.Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:4198",
                   headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]}, timeout=180)
for route, body in (
    ("customer_organizations", {"customer_org_id": "qa-org", "budget": {"max_budget": 100, "budget_duration": "1d"}, "default_budgets": [{"name": "default", "max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "1d"}]}),
    ("customer_teams", {"customer_team_id": "qa-team", "parent_org_id": "qa-org", "budget": {"max_budget": 100, "budget_duration": "1d"}}),
    ("customer_members", {"customer_member_id": "qa-member", "parent_team_id": "qa-team"}),
):
    response = api.post("/management/v1/" + route, json=body)
    assert response.is_success
key_response = api.post("/key/generate", json={})
assert key_response.is_success
api.headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + key_response.json()["key"]
maximum = json.loads(Path("model_prices_and_context_window.json").read_text())["gpt-6.1-sol"]["max_output_tokens"]
requests = (
    ("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": "customer-spend-qa", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word hello."}]}),
    ("/v1/responses", {"model": "customer-spend-qa", "input": "Reply with the word hello."}),
    ("/v1/messages", {"model": "customer-spend-qa", "max_tokens": maximum, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with the word hello."}]}),
)
for route, body in requests:
    response = api.post(route, json=body, headers={"x-litellm-customer-member-id": "qa-member"})
    assert response.is_success, (response.status_code, response.text)
    print(route, response.status_code, response.headers.get("x-litellm-response-cost"))

tables = ("LiteLLM_CustomerMemberTable", "LiteLLM_CustomerTeamTable", "LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable")
def snapshot():
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) as db:
        totals = tuple(db.execute(sql.SQL("SELECT spend FROM {}").format(sql.Identifier(table))).fetchone()[0] for table in tables)
        costs = db.execute('SELECT spend FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE model_group=%s', ("customer-spend-qa",)).fetchall()
        exists = db.execute("SELECT to_regclass(%s)", ('"LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend"',)).fetchone()[0]
        daily = db.execute('SELECT SUM(spend), SUM(api_requests) FROM "LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend"').fetchone() if exists else None
        return totals, costs, daily
for _ in range(90):
    totals, costs, daily = snapshot()
    if len(costs) == 3 and all(abs(value-sum(row[0] for row in costs)) < 1e-10 for value in totals) and (daily is None or daily[1] == 3):
        break
    time.sleep(1)
assert len(costs) == 3
assert all(abs(value-sum(row[0] for row in costs)) < 1e-10 for value in totals)
if daily is not None:
    assert abs(daily[0]-sum(row[0] for row in costs)) < 1e-10 and daily[1] == 3
response = api.post(requests[0][0], json=requests[0][1])
assert response.is_success
for _ in range(90):
    if len(snapshot()[1]) == 4:
        break
    time.sleep(1)
assert len(snapshot()[1]) == 4
assert snapshot()[0] == totals and snapshot()[2] == daily

with psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]) as db:
    for table in tables:
        db.execute(sql.SQL("UPDATE {} SET budget_reset_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP-INTERVAL '1 day'").format(sql.Identifier(table)))
for attempt in range(30):
    reset_totals = snapshot()[0]
    if daily is not None and all(abs(value) < 1e-10 for value in reset_totals):
        break
    if daily is None and attempt >= 10:
        break
    time.sleep(1)
assert reset_totals == (totals if daily is None else (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
assert snapshot()[2] == daily
```

</details>

### Stored results

Each cell is the total for the three attributed requests. The request without the header returned 200 and left customer totals and daily history unchanged in every run.

| Run | Each customer counter | Daily spend | Daily requests | Each counter after forced reset |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

Legacy Redis buffering also returned 200 on each of the three endpoints. In both after runs, daily spend matched the billed total, counted all three requests, and stayed unchanged after the budgets reset. All three scratch databases and dedicated proxy/Redis processes were removed after the runs.

## Type

## Final Attestation

</details>

> Extends the spend accounting and budget-reset paths with a new daily rollup entity; behavior is heavily tested but mistakes could mis-attribute usage or reset customer budgets incorrectly.

title: fix(openai): point gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-pro, o3 and o3-pro at the GPT-6 models as successor
body:
## Summary

OpenAI's deprecations page changed the recommended replacement for the December 11, 2026 shutdown of the GPT-5 and o3 families from the GPT-5.6 models to the GPT-6 models. This PR moves `successor_model` on the 12 openai rows for `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-5-pro`, `o3` and `o3-pro` (aliases plus dated snapshots) to `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra` or `gpt-6-luna`, which all have rows in the catalog already. It also adds the missing `deprecation_source` on `o3`, the only one of the 12 rows that had a date without it. No price or date changes

## Evidence (kind: page)

Source is https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations (fetched raw as `deprecations.md` four times, same content each time), table "Upcoming deprecations"

| Shutdown date | Affected model or feature | Status | Recommended replacement | Notice date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dec 11, 2026 | `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-2025-08-07` | Deprecated | `gpt-6.1-sol` | Jun 11, 2026 |
| Dec 11, 2026 | `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07` | Deprecated | `gpt-6.1-terra` | Jun 11, 2026 |
| Dec 11, 2026 | `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07` | Deprecated | `gpt-6-luna` | Jun 11, 2026 |
| Dec 11, 2026 | `gpt-5-pro`, `gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06` | Deprecated | `gpt-6.1-sol` (`reasoning.mode: pro`) in the Responses API | Jun 11, 2026 |
| Dec 11, 2026 | `o3`, `o3-2025-04-16` | Deprecated | `gpt-6.1-sol` | Jun 11, 2026 |
| Dec 11, 2026 | `o3-pro`, `o3-pro-2025-06-10` | Deprecated | `gpt-6.1-sol` (`reasoning.mode: pro`) in the Responses API | Jun 11, 2026 |

For the two pro rows the cell names `gpt-6.1-sol` with pro reasoning mode, so `successor_model` is `gpt-6.1-sol`, the same way `o1-pro` already records its "`gpt-5.6-sol` (`reasoning.mode: pro`)" cell as `gpt-5.6-sol`

## Rows changed

| Key | `successor_model` before | `successor_model` after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-5` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `gpt-5-2025-08-07` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `gpt-5-mini` | `gpt-5.6-terra` | `gpt-6.1-terra` |
| `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07` | `gpt-5.6-terra` | `gpt-6.1-terra` |
| `gpt-5-nano` | `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-6-luna` |
| `gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07` | `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-6-luna` |
| `gpt-5-pro` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `o3` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `o3-2025-04-16` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `o3-pro` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `o3-pro-2025-06-10` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |

`o3` also gains `deprecation_source` https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations for its existing `deprecation_date` 2026-12-11

## Rest of the page

Every other model row in the "Upcoming deprecations" and "Past deprecations" tables was compared with the openai rows in the catalog (date and first named replacement) and matches, including the Dec 1, 2026 GPT Image rows that #51475 moved to `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`. `gpt-4o-search-preview` and `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview` are left unchanged, their date is an open question outside this PR

## Delisted by the provider

Not returned by `GET /v1/models` for the sync key. Dated rows already carry their page dates. Undated with no deprecation entry on the page are `daybreak-blue-latest`, `daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-5.5-cyber`, `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `gpt-6-astra-law`, `gpt-6-cyber`, `gpt-6-rosalind`, `gpt-rosalind-discovery`, `gpt-rosalind-research`, `openai/container`, `text-embedding-ada-002-v2`, `gpt-4o-search-preview` and `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview`
