title: feat(ui): show customer organization usage and budget utilization
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customers cannot compare organization usage across reporting periods
- The list lacks budget percentages and member counts

How it solves it:

- Build on the merged #51495 usage backend
- Aggregate visible organizations through the existing SQL usage helpers
- Show Customer, Spend, Requests, Tokens, and Members
- Keep budget amounts and percentages inside Spend
- Limit custom dates to the API's 400-day maximum

This PR targets `main`, including #51495 at `df8b3b498e3`. The customer usage schema, attribution, accounting, and three existing activity routes come from that merged backend. The aggregate route extends its existing usage module and reuses its metadata helpers. Chargebacks removal remains in #51474.

Intentional product change: Customers lists customer organizations instead of end users. The old list's keys, status, and block controls become organization requests, tokens, and members. Create Customer creates an organization. Customer names open the existing usage drilldown with the selected dates.

## User Flow

Before, the customer list cannot show organization totals for a selected period.

1. Open `/customers` as a proxy admin.
2. See individual end users and spend this month.
3. There is no organization date selector or member count.

![Before, end-user customer list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa1909b1-e4e8-4a8d-90aa-4c32914e7c72)

After, the same page shows organization totals and current budget details.

1. Open `/customers` as a proxy admin.
2. Select this month, previous month, YTD, or custom dates.
3. Read Spend, Requests, Tokens, and Members, then select a customer for its drilldown.

![After, organization overview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f161798-5dea-483f-a6dc-cf1febb43e66)

November shows $51.00 / $500.00 and 10.2% used. YTD shows $551.00, with the current $51.00 / $500.00 budget counter labeled underneath in the same cell. Members includes all three registered members, including one without usage.

![YTD keeps the current budget separate from historical spend](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec08ce1d-be8b-4a29-9298-14eec4710993)

The date picker explains the 400-day limit and disables Apply for longer ranges. An invalid saved URL falls back to this month instead of sending an over-limit query. The bound matches the backend's difference between start and end dates.

![An over-limit range cannot be applied](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7b24252-916f-4d1f-8b68-2d3553f5fd92)

## API contracts and performance

The list loads one organization page, including stored spend, effective maximum budget, and member counts computed in one query across its teams. Search happens before pagination. It then sends one usage request for the visible organization IDs.

```text
GET /management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity/aggregated
    ?start_date=2026-11-01&end_date=2026-11-30
    &customer_org_ids=customer-a,customer-b
```

The route returns the existing `SpendAnalyticsPaginatedResponse`. It uses `get_daily_activity_aggregated` and the shared SQL grouping queries over `LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend`. Dates are inclusive UTC days, bounded to the existing 400-day span, with at most 100 organizations. Model and API-key filters apply before aggregation. SQL computes complete daily totals across every matching row. The browser combines these bounded daily summaries into period totals without fetching raw pages. Key breakdowns contain one key, while totals include every key.

The organization, team, and member daily activity APIs and the drilldown use #51495. Attribution follows that backend's validated request metadata and key bindings. Historical totals use recorded hierarchy IDs. This PR does not remap the request's `user` field or add another writer.

A local response over 20,000 daily rows and distinct keys returned $200, 40,000 requests, and 800,000 tokens in 163 ms, using 6,601 bytes and `has_more=false`. This is a local measurement, not a production latency guarantee.

Budget percentages use the stored organization spend and effective maximum, including an active temporary increase. Missing limits, $0 limits, and percentages above 100% have explicit states. These are reporting values, not a change to inference budget enforcement.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The screenshots show the actual dashboard with synthetic local data. Baseline revision `2cefb06b4f2` has the same Customers page as the merged `df8b3b498e3` base. Rebuilt overview proof was captured at `09fec90e048`; the final date-limit proof is from `56d66593940`. Both used the same local Postgres data. The roughly 20-second recording switches November, October, and YTD, then opens the inherited organization drilldown.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16d2e7f2-1acb-4f5f-af56-abff761eb943

The actual merged Prisma schema was generated and used for the live checks, including required empty-string dimensions and the absence of a customer PTU column. Organization, team, and member November reads returned $51, $31, and $31. Customer A returned $51 for November, $200 for October, and $551 for YTD. Stored spend remained $51, maximum $500, and member count 3.

580 focused backend tests passed, including the customer routes, shared SQL aggregation, Prisma span audit, vector-store warning regression, and dynamic rate limiter tests. Customer UI tests, the 24 shared date-picker tests, production TypeScript, and `make check` passed. Removing member counting makes its HTTP regression fail. Removing the picker limit makes the new over-limit regression fail. Both implementations were restored and verified.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the local reporting demo</summary>

Use an isolated Postgres database with the repository migrations applied and dedicated Redis on port 6378. Set `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` locally. These reporting checks use seeded rows and make no provider calls.

```sh
uv sync --inexact --frozen --extra proxy --group proxy-dev --group e2e-dev
.venv/bin/python litellm/scripts/prisma_generate_if_needed.py
```

Save this as `customer-usage-demo.yaml`.

```yaml
model_list: []
litellm_settings:
  telemetry: false
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6378
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6378
```

```sh
.venv/bin/python -u litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config customer-usage-demo.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4071 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver

cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4071 npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3073
```

Create the hierarchy in a fresh local database.

```python
import json, os, urllib.request
base = "http://127.0.0.1:4071/management/v1"
def post(path, payload):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"], "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
        return json.load(response)
for identifier, alias, maximum in [("customer-a", "Customer A", 500), ("customer-b", "Customer B", 100), ("customer-empty", "New customer", None)]:
    post("/customer_organizations", {"customer_org_id": identifier, "alias": alias, "budget": {"max_budget": maximum}, "default_budgets": [{"name": "Standard", "max_budget": 1000}]})
for team, org in [("team-a1", "customer-a"), ("team-a2", "customer-a"), ("team-b", "customer-b")]:
    post("/customer_teams", {"customer_team_id": team, "parent_org_id": org})
for member, team in [("member-a1", "team-a1"), ("member-a2", "team-a2"), ("member-b", "team-b")]:
    post("/customer_members", {"customer_member_id": member, "parent_team_id": team})
```

Save the following local fixtures as `seed.sql` and run `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f seed.sql`. The table comes from #51495's normal migration.

```sql
INSERT INTO "LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend" (id, customer_member_id, customer_team_id, customer_org_id, date, api_key, model, model_group, custom_llm_provider, endpoint, spend, api_requests, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, successful_requests)
VALUES
('contract-a-nov-1','member-a1','team-a1','customer-a','2026-11-01','demo-key-1','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',31,120,9000,3000,120),
('contract-a-nov-2','member-a2','team-a2','customer-a','2026-11-10','demo-key-2','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',20,80,6000,2000,80),
('contract-b-nov','member-b','team-b','customer-b','2026-11-05','demo-key-1','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',25,90,6000,3000,90),
('contract-a-oct','member-a1','team-a1','customer-a','2026-10-05','demo-key-1','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',200,600,40000,20000,600),
('contract-b-oct','member-b','team-b','customer-b','2026-10-05','demo-key-1','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',80,400,25000,15000,400),
('contract-a-jan','member-a1','team-a1','customer-a','2026-01-05','demo-key-1','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',300,1000,60000,40000,1000),
('contract-b-jan','member-b','team-b','customer-b','2026-01-05','demo-key-1','demo-model','demo-model','openai','/chat/completions',100,500,30000,20000,500)
ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;
UPDATE "LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable" SET spend=51 WHERE customer_org_id='customer-a';
UPDATE "LiteLLM_CustomerOrganizationTable" SET spend=25 WHERE customer_org_id='customer-b';

```

This client creates the inactive member and load-test organization, then verifies all three existing activity APIs and the new batched aggregate API.

```python
import json, os, time, urllib.request, urllib.error, subprocess
from pathlib import Path
BASE='http://127.0.0.1:4071'
def call(path, data=None, method='GET'):
    req=urllib.request.Request(BASE+path,data=json.dumps(data).encode() if data is not None else None,headers={'Authorization':'Bearer '+os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY'],'Content-Type':'application/json'},method=method)
    start=time.perf_counter()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=120) as response:
        raw=response.read()
        return json.loads(raw),round((time.perf_counter()-start)*1000,1),len(raw)
def create(path,data):
    try:return call(path,data,'POST')
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        if e.code!=409:raise
create('/management/v1/customer_members',{'customer_member_id':'member-a3','parent_team_id':'team-a1'})
create('/management/v1/customer_organizations',{'customer_org_id':'customer-load','alias':'Load test customer','default_budgets':[{'name':'standard','max_budget':1000}]})
create('/management/v1/customer_teams',{'customer_team_id':'team-load','parent_org_id':'customer-load'})
create('/management/v1/customer_members',{'customer_member_id':'member-load','parent_team_id':'team-load'})
sql='''INSERT INTO "LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend" (id, customer_member_id, customer_team_id, customer_org_id, date, api_key, model, spend, api_requests, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
SELECT 'contract-load-' || n, 'member-load', 'team-load', 'customer-load', '2026-11-01', 'load-key-' || n, 'demo-model', 0.01, 2, 30, 10 FROM generate_series(1,20000) n
ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING;
ANALYZE "LiteLLM_DailyCustomerMemberSpend";'''
subprocess.run(['psql',os.environ['DATABASE_URL'],'-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1'],input=sql,text=True,check=True,stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
proof={}
for level,field,identifier,expected in [('customer_organizations','customer_org','customer-a',51),('customer_teams','customer_team','team-a1',31),('customer_members','customer_member','member-a1',31)]:
    path=f'/management/v1/{level}/daily/activity?start_date=2026-11-01&end_date=2026-11-30&{field}_ids={identifier}'
    data,ms,size=call(path)
    assert data['metadata']['total_spend']==expected,data
    proof[level]={'spend':data['metadata']['total_spend'],'elapsed_ms':ms,'results':len(data['results'])}
for label,start,end,expected in [('November','2026-11-01','2026-11-30',51),('October','2026-10-01','2026-10-31',200),('YTD','2026-01-01','2026-11-13',551)]:
    data,ms,size=call(f'/management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date={start}&end_date={end}&customer_org_ids=customer-a')
    assert data['metadata']['total_spend']==expected,data
    org=call('/management/v1/customer_organizations/customer-a')[0]
    assert org['spend']==51 and org['budget']['max_budget']==500 and org['member_count']==3,org
    proof[label]={'spend':expected,'budget_spend':org['spend'],'max_budget':org['budget']['max_budget'],'members':org['member_count'],'elapsed_ms':ms,'bytes':size}
path='/management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=2026-11-01&end_date=2026-11-30&customer_org_ids=customer-load'
data,ms,size=call(path)
assert abs(data['metadata']['total_spend']-200)<1e-8,data
assert data['metadata']['total_api_requests']==40000 and data['metadata']['total_tokens']==800000,data
assert data['metadata']['total_pages']==1 and data['metadata']['has_more'] is False,data
proof['load']={'daily_rows':20000,'spend':data['metadata']['total_spend'],'requests':data['metadata']['total_api_requests'],'tokens':data['metadata']['total_tokens'],'http_requests':1,'pages':1,'elapsed_ms':ms,'bytes':size,'key_limit':data['metadata']['api_key_limit']}
Path('customer-usage-proof.json').write_text(json.dumps(proof,indent=2))
print(json.dumps(proof,indent=2))

```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:3073/customers`, log in, and select November 2026, October 2026, and YTD. Select Customer A to verify the drilldown preserves the dates. Enter February 1, 2024 through April 5, 2025 to verify the inline 400-day message and disabled Apply. For the before view, run the baseline dashboard on port 3071 against the same database.

</details>

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] Focused backend and dashboard tests pass locally
- [ ] All required CI/CD checks pass on the latest commit
- [x] The scope is customer organization usage and budget visibility
- [x] Automated reviews have finished on the latest commit

## Review and CI

The earlier Python 3.10 imports, dashboard typing, query-span audit, and vector-store warning assertion were corrected. The merged backend includes the dynamic rate-limiter test fixes. The current local suites pass.

Greptile identified the missing date-picker limit. `56d66593940` adds that limit and regression coverage. Greptile reviewed `56d66593940` at 5/5 with no new actionable findings. Bugbot reviewed the same commit and found no new issues. Veria reported no new issues and returned a neutral check. The date-limit thread is resolved. The remaining CI jobs are still running.

The [OSV check](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43341599527/job/131610969286) currently fails on SoupSieve 2.9.2 in the unchanged `main` lockfile. This PR leaves the security gate and dependency policy unchanged.

## Caveats

The proof verifies reporting against synthetic persisted usage. It does not claim new end-to-end inference attribution or budget enforcement. Those remain owned by the merged backend. Date-filtered spend can differ from the current budget counter.

## Type

New Feature

title: feat: email key owners before opted-in virtual keys expire
body: ## Summary Previously, there was no way for virtual key owners to recieve advance notification when their key is about to expire. This PR adds a background job that iterates through non expired/non blocked keys, and sends out email notifs. There is a global setting to turn this feature on, and a global config to set the number of days before expiry to send out emails. This can also be set/overridden per-key within its metadata. Delivery stamps are stored in redis to keep a record of delivery and prevent re-sends. the expiry days can tonly be between 1-7. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/33ca7374c9264c5297caf6ef4899ba86 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/33ca7374c9264c5297caf6ef4899ba86?variant=devin Requested by: @mrinal-berri ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Key owners get no warning before virtual keys expire. How it solves it: - `general_settings.key_expiry_alert_days: ` sets the warning window for every key with an expiry date and an owner email, including keys that already exist. Like the other scheduled emails (model deprecations, performance alerts), the `Virtual Key Expiring` email event defaults off, so an admin also turns it on under Email Notifications (`PATCH /email/event_settings`). The value is read on every run, like the performance alert and spend capture jobs, so a UI or `/config/field/update` edit applies without a restart. - `metadata.key_expiry_alert_days: ` on a key overrides the global value for that key. - The owner gets one email when the key has N days or fewer left. Changing the key's expiry re-arms it. - One worker runs the job per 12-hour clock window. Pods' interval timers fire at their own boot time plus jitter, so the shared `PodLockManager` lock is named after the window the run falls in (`litellm_key_expiry_alert_job:`, using the same `int(now // window) * window` bucketing as `file_usage_caps`) and held for one interval: the first pod to fire in a window runs, every other pod in that window skips, and the next window is a new key, so no pod blocks its own next run. A scan that raises frees the window for another pod. If Redis cannot answer (including an open circuit breaker), the pod runs anyway. - Shared Redis claims per key, expiry and day count stop duplicate emails across workers, pods and runs. Both values are a single integer from 1 to 365. `/key/generate` and `/key/update` reject anything else (lists, booleans, strings, 0) with HTTP 400. An invalid global value is logged on each run and ignored (per-key values keep working); a setup error leaves only the expiry job unscheduled, and every other background job still registers. Emails go only to the owner's `user_email` and show the alias or an abbreviated key name (never the raw key). The job runs every 12 hours by default (`LITELLM_KEY_EXPIRY_ALERT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`). No UI or schema change. ## User Flow Before, no expiry warning exists. 1. title: fix(proxy): import soundfile lazily in the transcribe logging handler
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Anthropic and Bedrock messages streams no longer require soundfile to be installed. The audio library now loads only when Transcribe measures media duration, with a regression test for importing the streaming handler without it. A separately approved test-only fix isolates verbose logging in the vector-store fallback test while preserving its exact warning assertions

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Current head is `4deba52d80630016e559b8fd6a9a26782a1234cd`, updated with main including #51523. That upstream fix aligns the member budget form with the API and adds regression coverage. Fresh CI and bot reviews are pending

At the previous tip `013c4db4`, all unit tests, lint and real Anthropic/Bedrock streaming verification passed. Greptile scored 5/5, and Bugbot and Veria reported no issues. Dashboard build failed on an upstream API-field mismatch, now fixed by #51523. The prior security scan failure was unrelated to this diff. Earlier proof below is historical, not current-tip evidence

The current PR scope remains the soundfile import fix and its regression test

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Messages streaming crashed when soundfile was not installed
- Hit both Anthropic and Bedrock through `litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate`

How it solves it:

- soundfile now loads only when Transcribe media duration is measured
- Regression test imports the pass-through logging stack with soundfile blocked

## User Flow

Before: a Python SDK user without the `proxy` extra gets an import error on every messages stream

1. They install litellm with fastapi, orjson, backoff and redis but without soundfile
2. They call `litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate(..., stream=True)` against Anthropic or Bedrock
3. The call raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'soundfile'` and no stream comes back

After: the same call streams normally

1. They install litellm with fastapi, orjson, backoff and redis but without soundfile
2. They call `litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate(..., stream=True)` against Anthropic or Bedrock
3. The stream completes and the text arrives as usual

## Relevant issues

Fixes #45379

## Affected release

Regression in v1.103.0, still present on main

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] Affected tests are being refreshed on Devin at the current tip. The previous tip passed 105 tests remotely
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Run on a Devin VM, no proxy involved since this is the SDK import path. Each venv is Python 3.12 with litellm installed editable from the tested commit and base deps plus fastapi 0.162.5, orjson 3.13.0, backoff 2.2.1 and redis 8.1.0. `venv-sf` adds soundfile 0.14.0 as the control. Env var names are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for Anthropic, and `AWS_PROFILE` plus `AWS_REGION_NAME=us-east-1` for Bedrock. Models are the latest Sonnet listed in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` for each provider

<details>
<summary>kit/run_case.sh, exactly as run</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: run_case.sh <venv> <label> <provider: anthropic|bedrock> <model>
set -u
ROOT=$HOME/verify/45379
VENV=$1; LABEL=$2; PROVIDER=$3; MODEL=$4
LOG=$ROOT/logs/$LABEL.log
cd "$ROOT/kit"
unset AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
if [ "$PROVIDER" = bedrock ]; then export AWS_PROFILE=litellm-dev AWS_REGION_NAME=us-east-1; fi
{
  echo "# $(date -u +%FT%TZ) label=$LABEL venv=$VENV model=$MODEL"
  echo "# cmd: $ROOT/$VENV/bin/python $ROOT/kit/stream_case.py $MODEL"
  "$ROOT/$VENV/bin/python" "$ROOT/kit/stream_case.py" "$MODEL"
  echo "# exit=$?"
} > "$LOG" 2>&1
grep -E "^(RESULT|ModuleNotFoundError|ImportError|# exit)" "$LOG" | cut -c1-900
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>kit/stream_case.py, exactly as run</summary>

```python
"""Disposable driver for BerriAI/litellm#45379. Lives outside tracked source."""
import asyncio
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import traceback
import uuid

import httpx

MODEL = sys.argv[1]
HTTP_LOG = []
_orig_send = httpx.AsyncClient.send


async def _send(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    entry = {"method": request.method, "host": request.url.host, "path": request.url.path}
    HTTP_LOG.append(entry)
    try:
        response = await _orig_send(self, request, *args, **kwargs)
    except BaseException as exc:
        entry["error"] = type(exc).__name__
        raise
    entry["status"] = response.status_code
    return response


httpx.AsyncClient.send = _send

import litellm  # noqa: E402

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(litellm.__file__)))
SHA = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
DIRTY = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


async def main():
    nonce = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
    result = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "litellm_file": litellm.__file__,
        "sha": SHA,
        "tracked_dirty": bool(DIRTY),
        "python": sys.version.split()[0],
        "soundfile_installed": importlib.util.find_spec("soundfile") is not None,
        "nonce": nonce,
    }
    events = []
    text = []
    try:
        response = await litellm.anthropic.messages.acreate(
            model=MODEL,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": f"Reply with the single word pong. ref {nonce}"}],
            max_tokens=16,
            stream=True,
        )
        async for chunk in response:
            raw = chunk.decode() if isinstance(chunk, (bytes, bytearray)) else str(chunk)
            for line in raw.splitlines():
                if line.startswith("event:"):
                    events.append(line.split(":", 1)[1].strip())
                if line.startswith("data:"):
                    try:
                        data = json.loads(line.split(":", 1)[1])
                    except ValueError:
                        continue
                    delta = data.get("delta") or {}
                    if delta.get("type") == "text_delta":
                        text.append(delta.get("text", ""))
        result.update(outcome="STREAM_OK", event_types=sorted(set(events)), event_count=len(events), text="".join(text))
    except BaseException as exc:
        traceback.print_exc()
        result.update(
            outcome="EXCEPTION",
            exc_type=type(exc).__name__,
            exc_msg=str(exc)[:500],
            missing_module=getattr(exc, "name", None),
        )
    result["http_requests"] = HTTP_LOG
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    print("RESULT " + json.dumps(result))


asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

### Before (40debbb9c0c)

1. `venv-nosf/bin/python -c "import litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.success_handler"` exits 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'soundfile'` raised at `transcribe_passthrough_logging_handler.py:16`. Importing `litellm.llms.anthropic.messages.native.streaming_iterator` fails the same way
2. `kit/run_case.sh venv-nosf 70_final_nosf_anthropic anthropic anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` prints `outcome: EXCEPTION`, `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'soundfile'`
3. `kit/run_case.sh venv-nosf 71_final_nosf_bedrock bedrock bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` shows `invoke-with-response-stream` returning 200, then the same `ModuleNotFoundError`
4. The `venv-sf` control runs of both commands print `STREAM_OK` with text `pong`

### After (0733d273d75)

1. Both imports in `venv-nosf` exit 0
2. `kit/run_case.sh venv-nosf c20_cand_nosf_anthropic anthropic anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` prints `STREAM_OK`, 7 event types, text `pong`
3. `kit/run_case.sh venv-nosf c21_cand_nosf_bedrock bedrock bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` prints `STREAM_OK`, upstream 200, 6 event types, text `pong`
4. The `venv-sf` control runs still print `STREAM_OK` with text `pong`

The final-tip Anthropic runs use one Rust bridge module built from the `0733d273` tree and loaded for both SHAs. The Rust and packaging sources are identical at both SHAs. Earlier Anthropic runs against a stale shared native module failed before any request at both SHAs and are excluded

#### Transcribe duration still works

A generated 8 kHz mono WAV of 20000 frames, measured through `media_file_seconds` and `measure_media_seconds`. This ran at `284cdd89`, and the handler file is unchanged at `0733d273`

```
venv-sf:   soundfile_loaded_before_call=false  media_file_seconds=2.5  soundfile_loaded_after_call=true
           measure_media_seconds=2.5  probe_attempts=1  charged=0.0012 (at 0.0004/s)  max_job_cost=11.52
venv-nosf: direct_outcome=RAISED  raised_type=ModuleNotFoundError  raised_is_ImportError=true
           measure_media_seconds=null  probe_attempts=3  charged=11.52  max_job_cost=11.52
```

#### Unit tests and gates

The mapped file `tests/unit/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/test_transcribe_passthrough_logging_handler.py` passes at 0733d273 (105 passed, serial and `-n 4`). Random-order runs with seeds 1 to 4 also passed at 284cdd8, which has the same handler and test file. On base source with only the new test file applied, `test_passthrough_logging_imports_without_soundfile_installed` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: import of soundfile halted; None in sys.modules`. The `ruff_strict_gate`, `type_discipline_gate`, `test_quality_gate`, `openapi_docs_gate` and `type_check_gate` scripts all pass at 0733d273 with `--base 40debbb9`, and so do `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files

Changed executable-line coverage is 1/1. The touched duration function has 10/10 statements and 2/2 branches covered. Missing-soundfile error behavior was verified separately on Devin

#### Vector-store test isolation

At 0733d273, `test_hook_falls_back_to_the_sdk_when_the_runtime_has_no_router` and its whole file (51 tests) pass with `litellm.set_verbose` initially False and initially True, and the incoming value is restored after teardown. At 40debbb9 and 284cdd89 the same test fails with `assert 2 == 1` when the flag starts True. The `integrations` shard passed in CI at that previous tip

#### CI at 0733d273

95 checks pass. `llms-bedrock` and `key-generation` hit checkout timeouts and passed on one retry each. `proxy-hooks-client` fails on six assertions in `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py`, and the `unit passed` aggregate fails with it. This PR does not touch that file or the rate limiter, so those failures are left alone and the PR is not mergeable until they are resolved

## Type

Bug fix

## Caveats

### Low

- Whole-tree formatting fails in untouched `_native.pyi`, identically on baseline
- Without soundfile, Transcribe pricing charges the maximum duration
  - The existing retry fallback catches the import error, same as any unreadable media

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The regression test fails at the baseline and passes at this tip, and real Anthropic and Bedrock streaming flows were verified before and after

</details>


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small import-scope change with a regression test; transcribe duration measurement still depends on soundfile when that code path runs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves the **`soundfile`** dependency out of module import time in the transcribe pass-through logging handler so paths like **`success_handler`** and Anthropic/Bedrock message streaming no longer require the optional proxy extra at import.
> 
> **`soundfile`** is now imported only inside **`media_file_seconds`** when Transcribe actually measures media duration; behavior when the library is present is unchanged, and missing **`soundfile`** still falls through to the existing max-duration charging path.
>

title: fix(cost): preserve Bedrock cross-region pricing for Messages
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Fixes Bedrock cross-region pricing for streaming and non-streaming Messages requests, including cached tokens
- Preserves the configured regional rate when Bedrock returns the same model without its region prefix, keeping recorded spend consistent with client-visible cost
- Keeps explicit pricing overrides and genuinely different response models working as before
- Adds regression coverage and updates the Langfuse test to calculate expected cost from regional pricing instead of a hardcoded global price

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Bedrock Messages spend drops cross-region profile pricing
- Streamed usage costs disagree with recorded spend

How it solves it:

- Keep profile pricing when Bedrock strips its region prefix
- Preserve explicit pricing and different served models

## User Flow

Before, Messages requests record the global rate for cross-region profiles

1. Configure a Bedrock EU, US or Japan profile without pricing overrides
2. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with streaming enabled or disabled
3. Inspect the request at https://litellm-domain/spend/logs and observe global-priced spend
4. For streaming requests, observe regional usage.cost disagreeing with recorded spend

After, Messages requests record the configured profile's rate

1. Configure a Bedrock EU, US or Japan profile without pricing overrides
2. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with streaming enabled or disabled
3. Inspect the request at https://litellm-domain/spend/logs and observe regional-priced spend
4. For streaming requests, observe usage.cost agreeing with recorded spend

## Relevant issues

Fixes #46286

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] Affected tests pass, executed remotely on Devin under the requested workflow
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [x] Every automated review on the latest commit is complete and findings addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Baseline `40debbb9c0c0a243f1c438b4689f2b2cf1c93e78`, verified final tip `ff4678478d5f405209159d90cae4a0e5af7a9a4b`

The Langfuse export regression derives expected cost from the configured profile's rates and request usage. The final-tip cost-calculator and Langfuse files passed all 720 tests. The repaired Langfuse test fails against baseline global-priced behavior and passes with the fix

Devin independently executed real Bedrock requests against both source commits, using two proxy workers, dedicated Redis and PostgreSQL. The matrix covers EU, US and Japan Messages cache writes, cache reads, streaming reads, and streaming/non-streaming chat controls

All 33 new regressions pass at the candidate. Against unchanged baseline source, all 18 defect cases fail at the global rate and all 15 compatibility controls pass

<details>
<summary>Shared setup and exact verification scripts</summary>

```python
"""Live case driver for issue #46286. Usage: run_cases.py <base_url> <out_json> [groups...]"""
import json, os, random, sys, time, uuid
import httpx

BASE = sys.argv[1]
OUT = sys.argv[2]
GROUPS = sys.argv[3:] or ["bedrock-eu-haiku-4-5", "bedrock-us-haiku-4-5"]
KEY = os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]
H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}", "content-type": "application/json"}

def fresh_system(n_words=6000):
    seed = uuid.uuid4().hex
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    words = ["alpha","beta","gamma","delta","omega","kappa","sigma","theta","lambda","zeta","orbit","quartz","maple","river","stone","cloud"]
    body = " ".join(f"{rnd.choice(words)}{rnd.randint(0,9999)}" for _ in range(n_words))
    return f"Reference corpus {seed}. {body}\nAnswer with the single word OK."

def nonce():
    return uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]

def messages_req(model, system, stream):
    return {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": 20,
        "system": [{"type": "text", "text": system, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"nonce {nonce()}: reply OK"}],
        "stream": stream,
    }

def chat_req(model, system, stream):
    body = {
        "model": model,
        "max_tokens": 20,
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": system, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}]},
            {"role": "user", "content": f"nonce {nonce()}: reply OK"},
        ],
        "stream": stream,
    }
    if stream:
        body["stream_options"] = {"include_usage": True}
    return body

def post(path, body):
    with httpx.Client(timeout=120) as c:
        if not body.get("stream"):
            r = c.post(BASE + path, headers=H, json=body)
            return r.status_code, dict(r.headers), r.json(), None
        with c.stream("POST", BASE + path, headers=H, json=body) as r:
            events = []
            for line in r.iter_lines():
                if line.startswith("data:"):
                    payload = line[5:].strip()
                    if payload and payload != "[DONE]":
                        try:
                            events.append(json.loads(payload))
                        except json.JSONDecodeError:
                            events.append({"_raw": payload})
            return r.status_code, dict(r.headers), None, events

def summarize_messages(resp, events):
    if resp is not None:
        return {"id": resp.get("id"), "model": resp.get("model"), "usage": resp.get("usage")}
    start = next((e for e in events if e.get("type") == "message_start"), {})
    delta = next((e for e in reversed(events) if e.get("type") == "message_delta"), {})
    msg = start.get("message", {})
    return {"id": msg.get("id"), "model": msg.get("model"), "message_start_usage": msg.get("usage"),
            "message_delta_usage": delta.get("usage"), "stream_events": len(events)}

def summarize_chat(resp, events):
    if resp is not None:
        return {"id": resp.get("id"), "model": resp.get("model"), "usage": resp.get("usage")}
    usage = next((e.get("usage") for e in reversed(events) if e.get("usage")), None)
    ids = {e.get("id") for e in events if e.get("id")}
    models = {e.get("model") for e in events if e.get("model")}
    return {"id": sorted(ids), "model": sorted(models), "usage": usage, "stream_events": len(events)}

results = []
for group in GROUPS:
    system = fresh_system()
    cases = [
        ("messages_nonstream_cache_write", "/v1/messages", messages_req(group, system, False), summarize_messages),
        ("messages_nonstream_cache_read", "/v1/messages", messages_req(group, system, False), summarize_messages),
        ("messages_stream_cache_read", "/v1/messages", messages_req(group, system, True), summarize_messages),
        ("chat_stream_cache_read", "/v1/chat/completions", chat_req(group, system, True), summarize_chat),
        ("chat_nonstream_cache_read", "/v1/chat/completions", chat_req(group, system, False), summarize_chat),
    ]
    for name, path, body, summ in cases:
        t0 = time.time()
        status, headers, resp, events = post(path, body)
        hdr = {k: v for k, v in headers.items() if k.startswith("x-litellm")}
        row = {"group": group, "case": name, "path": path, "stream": bool(body.get("stream")), "status": status,
               "headers": hdr, "summary": summ(resp, events), "elapsed_s": round(time.time() - t0, 2)}
        if resp is not None:
            row["response"] = resp
        if events is not None:
            row["events"] = events
        results.append(row)
        print(json.dumps({k: row[k] for k in ("group", "case", "status", "summary")}, default=str))
        print("   headers:", json.dumps({k: hdr.get(k) for k in ("x-litellm-response-cost", "x-litellm-call-id", "x-litellm-model-id", "x-litellm-model-group")}))
        time.sleep(1.5)

json.dump(results, open(OUT, "w"), indent=1, default=str)
print("wrote", OUT)
```

```python
"""Read LiteLLM_SpendLogs rows for the ids in a run_cases.py output and compute rate verdicts from the SHA's cost map."""
import json, os, sys
import psycopg2
os.environ.setdefault("LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP", "True")
import litellm

run = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
conn = psycopg2.connect(os.environ["QA_DATABASE_URL"])
cur = conn.cursor()

def rates(key):
    e = litellm.model_cost[key]
    return (e["input_cost_per_token"], e["output_cost_per_token"], e.get("cache_creation_input_token_cost"), e.get("cache_read_input_token_cost"))

def cost(key, u):
    i, o, cw, cr = rates(key)
    return u["in"] * i + u["out"] * o + u["cw"] * (cw or 0) + u["cr"] * (cr or 0)

def usage_from_meta(meta, row_prompt, row_completion):
    uo = (meta or {}).get("usage_object") or {}
    cw = uo.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0
    cr = uo.get("cache_read_input_tokens") or 0
    if "input_tokens" in uo:
        return {"in": uo.get("input_tokens", 0), "out": uo.get("output_tokens", 0), "cw": cw, "cr": cr}
    ptd = uo.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}
    cr = cr or ptd.get("cached_tokens") or 0
    cw = cw or uo.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0
    pt = uo.get("prompt_tokens", row_prompt)
    return {"in": pt - cr - cw, "out": uo.get("completion_tokens", row_completion), "cw": cw, "cr": cr}

out = []
for r in run:
    s = r["summary"]
    ids = s["id"] if isinstance(s["id"], list) else [s["id"]]
    call_id = r["headers"].get("x-litellm-call-id")
    cur.execute('select request_id, model, custom_llm_provider, model_group, model_id, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, metadata, call_type, status from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" where request_id = any(%s) or litellm_call_id = %s', (ids, call_id))
    rows = cur.fetchall()
    region = r["group"].split("-")[1]
    regional = f"{region}.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"
    glob = "anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"
    for row in rows:
        req_id, model, provider, group, model_id, spend, pt, ct, meta, call_type, status = row
        u = usage_from_meta(meta, pt, ct)
        exp_regional, exp_global = cost(regional, u), cost(glob, u)
        tol = 2e-7
        verdict = "REGIONAL" if abs(spend - exp_regional) <= tol else ("GLOBAL" if abs(spend - exp_global) <= tol else "NEITHER")
        hdr_cost = r["headers"].get("x-litellm-response-cost")
        stream_cost = None
        if r["stream"] and r["path"] == "/v1/messages":
            stream_cost = (s.get("message_delta_usage") or {}).get("cost")
        elif r["stream"]:
            stream_cost = (s.get("usage") or {}).get("cost")
        rec = {"group": r["group"], "case": r["case"], "request_id": req_id, "spend_log_model": model, "custom_llm_provider": provider,
               "model_group": group, "call_type": call_type, "status": status, "usage": u, "spend": spend,
               "expected_regional": round(exp_regional, 10), "expected_global": round(exp_global, 10), "verdict": verdict,
               "x-litellm-response-cost": hdr_cost, "streamed_usage_cost": stream_cost, "client_visible_model": s.get("model"),
               "usage_object": (meta or {}).get("usage_object")}
        out.append(rec)
        print(f"{r['group']:22s} {r['case']:30s} spend={spend:.10f} regional={exp_regional:.10f} global={exp_global:.10f} -> {verdict:8s} hdr={hdr_cost} streamcost={stream_cost} usage={u} log.model={model} provider={provider} group={group} client.model={s.get('model')}")
    if not rows:
        print(f"{r['group']:22s} {r['case']:30s} NO SPEND ROW yet for ids={ids} call_id={call_id}")
json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[2], "w"), indent=1, default=str)
```

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

title

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The three deprecated fireworks `deepseek-v4-flash` rows name `deepseek-v4-flash-0731` as successor
- That model is itself retired (`deprecation_date` 2026-09-25) and no longer served

How it solves it:

title: fix(fal_ai): bill Luma Ray v3.2 videos at fal's 540p default resolution
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

bug fix

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e0e96689d6d347669888d9d85a15e4ef
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/e0e96689d6d347669888d9d85a15e4ef?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- fal Luma Ray v3.2 videos with no `resolution` were billed at the 720p rate
- fal's own default for those endpoints is 540p, so default requests billed 2x (1.5x on video-to-video)

How it solves it:

- A Luma Ray profile in the fal video transformation with `default_resolution` 540p
- Default requests now stamp `video_resolution: 540p` and price from `output_cost_per_second`

## User Flow

Before: a developer generating a Luma video through the gateway with no resolution set is charged twice the fal price

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos with `"model": "fal_ai/luma/agent/ray/v3.2/text-to-video"`, a prompt and `"seconds": "5"`, no `size`
2. fal renders the clip at its default 540p and charges $0.50
3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at $1.00, the 720p rate

After: the same request is charged the 540p rate fal actually billed

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos with `"model": "fal_ai/luma/agent/ray/v3.2/text-to-video"`, a prompt and `"seconds": "5"`, no `size`
2. fal renders the clip at its default 540p and charges $0.50
3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request at $0.50

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 0721e9aa8b. The diff is one profile table entry plus a `startswith` dispatch in `_profile_for_model`, and the only consumer of `default_resolution` is the `video_resolution` usage stamp that `default_video_cost_calculator` reads, so the focused test covers the whole path from request to priced rate without a paid fal render.

fal's default, from fal's own OpenAPI for each endpoint (`https://fal.ai/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=luma/agent/ray/v3.2/<endpoint>`), `resolution` default `540p`, enum `540p`, `720p`, `1080p`, for text-to-video, image-to-video, reframe and video-to-video.

Regression sensitivity, the new test fails on the merge base and passes on the tip:

```
$ git stash push -- litellm/llms/fal_ai/videos/transformation.py
```

🐛 Bug Fix

### Low

## Summary

OpenAI's deprecations page updated the recommended replacement for the December 1, 2026 GPT Image shutdown from the GPT-Image-2.5 models to the GPT-Image-2.6 models. This PR moves `successor_model` on the 40 openai rows for `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-1.5-2025-12-16` and `chatgpt-image-latest` (base keys plus their quality and size variant keys) from `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` to `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`. No price, date or other field changes. `gpt-image-1` keeps `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` because its October 23, 2026 row on the same page still names the 2.5 models.

## Evidence (kind: page)

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations (fetched raw as `deprecations.md`), section "2026-06-02: GPT Image model deprecations"

| Shutdown date | Model / system | Recommended replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dec 1, 2026 | `gpt-image-1-mini` | `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.6-flare` |
| Dec 1, 2026 | `gpt-image-1.5` \| `gpt-image-1.5-2025-12-16` | `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.6-flare` |
| Dec 1, 2026 | `chatgpt-image-latest` | `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.6-flare` |

The page names two replacements. The first one, `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, is written to `successor_model`, matching how the `gpt-image-2` rows already record this page's "`gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.6-flare`" cell.

Unchanged on the same page, so `gpt-image-1` rows stay on `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`:

remove chargebacks page on customer portal and just show it on the home screen

<details>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

How it solves it:

- Remove the page, dedicated helpers, tests, and translation block.
- Remove Chargebacks navigation, workspace routing, and legacy URL mapping.

Intentional product change: Customer Portal shows Customers only. The standalone Chargebacks report, grouping controls, and CSV export are removed. Direct Chargebacks URLs no longer render the report. Shared customer usage APIs remain available.

## User Flow

Before, opening the Chargebacks URL still displays the report.

1. Sign in and open `http://127.0.0.1:3072/chargebacks/`.
2. See the monthly report with grouping controls and Export CSV.

![Before, the old Chargebacks URL still displays its report](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf05d804-70be-48a2-b5f6-7f7dc8dd8ebf)

After, the same URL no longer displays a Chargebacks page.

1. Sign in and open `http://127.0.0.1:3072/chargebacks/`.
2. See Not Found. Open `/customers/` to continue using Customers.

![After, the removed Chargebacks route returns Not Found](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c59e7135-b87f-474b-8e36-c847f95b6322)

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Relevant routing, layout, and sidebar tests pass, 77 tests.
- [x] ESLint has no errors. Prettier, TypeScript, and diff checks pass.
- [ ] Required CI/CD checks pass on the latest commit.
- [x] Scope is limited to removing the standalone Chargebacks page.
- [ ] Automated reviews have finished on the latest commit.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Used the real dashboard, a local proxy with two workers, and dedicated Postgres and Redis instances. The same safe test data was used before and after. No mocked API responses or model calls were needed to verify page removal.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the local demo</summary>

Create a dedicated local Postgres database. Set `DATABASE_URL` to that database and set `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_USERNAME`, and `UI_PASSWORD` to local demo credentials. No production credentials are required

Save this as `config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list: []
litellm_settings:
  telemetry: false
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6378
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6378
```

From the repository root, prepare the environment and start Redis

```sh
uv sync --frozen --extra proxy --extra extra_proxy --no-dev
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"
prisma generate --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma
redis-server --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 6378 --save '' --appendonly no
```

In another terminal, start the proxy with the same environment variables

```sh
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4071 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Start the dashboard in another terminal

```sh
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4071 NEXT_PUBLIC_USE_REWRITES=true npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3072
```

Visit `http://127.0.0.1:3072/customers/` and sign in with the local demo credentials. The development server serves the page at `/customers/`; deployed proxies serve it at `/ui/customers/`

</details>

### Before (bef5369af48)

The navigation-only revision still renders `/chargebacks/`, as shown in the screenshot above. The separate Customers page also loads.

### After (2cefb06b4f2)

The same `/chargebacks/` URL returns Not Found. `/customers/` still loads and the sidebar contains Customers only. Recorded from an isolated checkout of the published revision.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddcefb8a-108b-4d10-9909-04540fd1cd43

```sh
npm run typecheck
git diff --check
```

ESLint reports two existing style warnings in the shared files, with no errors. A source search finds no remaining Chargebacks page references.

## Type

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `lite login` and Claude Code gateway sign-in never finish on SAML-only proxies
- The browser lands on the dashboard and the CLI polls until expiry

How it solves it:

- The SAML login carries the CLI login id in RelayState
- The SAML callback hands CLI sign-ins to the existing CLI completion flow
- CLI sign-ins over SAML also work on DISABLE_ADMIN_UI nodes, matching OAuth

The code change is Mateo's commit from `litellm_saml_cli_sso_login`, cherry-picked onto current main unchanged.

## User Flow

Before: a developer on a proxy whose only SSO is SAML can't sign Claude Code in

1. They run `/login` in Claude Code (or `lite login`) against the gateway, which opens http://proxy/sso/key/generate?source=litellm-cli&key=cli-...

```python
import httpx, json, sys, time
base = 'http://localhost:4100'
device = httpx.post(base + '/claude_code_gateway/oauth/device_authorization', data={'client_id': 'qa'}).json()
print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in device.items() if k != 'device_code'}))
for attempt in range(120):
    reply = httpx.post(base + '/claude_code_gateway/oauth/token', data={
        'grant_type': 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code', 'device_code': device['device_code']})
    body = reply.json()

        print('Anthropic HTTP', r.status_code, r.text); sys.exit(0)
    if attempt % 12 == 0:

    time.sleep(5)
```

you could only add vector stores to an access group through the api, and the dashboard didn't show them on the group or the team. now the group forms have a vector stores tab, the group page lists its stores by name, and a team's page lists the stores it gets from its groups.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

problem:

- access groups can hold vector stores, but only through the api
- the dashboard has no control for them
- it doesn't show them on a group or on a team either

fix:

- the create and edit forms get a Vector Stores tab
- the group page lists the group's stores by name, and the groups table counts them
- a team's page lists the stores it gets from its groups, marked with the group
- the edit form sends the stores only after that tab was opened, like the other tabs

Intentional product change: the create form is 28px wider, the same width as the edit form. the tab rows of both forms and of the group page wrap when the window is too narrow for one row, and the group page's tab row is 3px taller. one more tab doesn't fit the old widths. nothing is removed.

## User Flow

before: an admin can't put a vector store in an access group from the dashboard, or see which stores a team gets from a group

1. admin opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=access-groups` and clicks Create Access Group
2. the form has tabs for General Info, Models, MCP Servers, Agents and Skills. there's no place to pick a vector store
3. the only way is `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/access_group` with `access_vector_store_ids`
4. the team's page under `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams` then says "No vector stores configured", though the group limits the team to that store

after: the admin picks the stores in the form, and sees them on the group and on the team

1. admin opens the same page and clicks Create Access Group
2. the form has a Vector Stores tab. they pick `HR policies (store-b)` and click Create Group
3. the groups table shows the new group with 1 vector store, and the group's page lists `HR policies` under Vector Stores
4. the team's page lists the group's store under Vector Stores, marked `(access group)`
5. the edit form has the same tab with the saved stores. removing them all and saving empties the list

title: fix(mcp): route aggregate resources/read to the server that lists the URI
body:
## Summary

Previously, a resources/read call to the aggregate /mcp route hard failed on more than 1 server. To find the right server to serve the resource, the request's resource uri must be matched against the servers' resource list.

Now, each server's resources are iterated through to find which one can serve the resource read. It is served through the mcp discovery cache and rate limits still apply.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b552d4748e454348b893f800c2ec18e0
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/b552d4748e454348b893f800c2ec18e0?variant=devin
Requested by: @mrinal-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `resources/read` on aggregate `/mcp` fails once 2+ servers are allowed
- MCP App widgets never render through the aggregate endpoint

How it solves it:

- Lists each allowed server's resources concurrently, reusing the discovery cache
- Reads from the single server whose listing has the exact URI
- Two owners or no owner return an MCP error that says which
- A failed listing returns an MCP error and never counts as "not the owner"
  - Every owner error is an MCP `INVALID_REQUEST`, so 2026-07-28 clients see the reason
- A stdio server blocked on this proxy is skipped, never listed or charged
- Every listable candidate passes its MCP RPM check before it is listed
- The caller's shared bearer never reaches the gateway-picked owner
  - This covers lookups too, and legacy oauth2 delegates and OAuth pass-through servers
- Remaining listings are cancelled as soon as one fails
- The single-server path is unchanged

## User Flow

Before: a client connected to aggregate `/mcp` with two MCP servers allowed cannot load a widget resource

1. The client opens a session on POST http://localhost:4000/mcp/ with `x-mcp-servers: vanilla,everything`
2. `resources/list` returns `ui://get-time/mcp-app.html`
3. `resources/read` on that URI returns `400: Multiple MCP servers configured; read_resource currently supports exactly one allowed server.`
4. The widget never renders, while the same read on `/vanilla/mcp` works

After: the same read comes back with the widget HTML from the server that listed it

1. The client opens a session on POST http://localhost:4000/mcp/ with `x-mcp-servers: vanilla,everything`
2. `resources/list` returns `ui://get-time/mcp-app.html`
3. `resources/read` returns the `text/html;profile=mcp-app` contents from `vanilla`
4. If two allowed servers both list the URI, the read returns an error that names both servers and points to `/{server_name}/mcp` or `x-mcp-servers`

## Relevant issues

Fixes #34906

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Setup: three real upstream MCP servers from the official MCP packages, run unmodified. Two of them are MCP Apps examples that both publish `ui://get-time/mcp-app.html`.

```bash
PORT=9111 node node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/server-basic-vanillajs/dist/index.js
PORT=9112 node node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/server-basic-react/dist/index.js
PORT=9113 node node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything/dist/index.js streamableHttp
```

The config is a copy of `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` with these overrides. Both workers share one dedicated Redis (`redis-server --port 6390`, flushed before each leg) so MCP RPM counters are shared. The same two-worker setup ran for every leg.

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/REPRO_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6390

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6390

mcp_servers:
  vanilla:
    transport: http
    url: http://127.0.0.1:9111/mcp
    allow_all_keys: true
  react:
    transport: http
    url: http://127.0.0.1:9112/mcp
    allow_all_keys: true
  everything:
    transport: http
    url: http://127.0.0.1:9113/mcp
    allow_all_keys: true
  local:
    transport: stdio
    rpm: 1
    command: node
    args: ["node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything/dist/index.js", "stdio"]
    allow_all_keys: true
```

`LITELLM_ENABLE_MCP_STDIO` is unset, so `local` is blocked on this proxy, which is the default. Its `rpm: 1` shows whether reads that can never reach it still use up its limit.

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4106 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Client (official mcp Python SDK, streamable HTTP):

```python
import asyncio
import json
import os
import httpx2
from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client

async def run(label, path, scope, uri):
    headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + os.environ['REPRO_MASTER_KEY']}
    if scope:
        headers['x-mcp-servers'] = scope
    async with httpx2.AsyncClient(headers=headers, timeout=90) as http:
        async with streamable_http_client('http://127.0.0.1:4106' + path, http_client=http) as streams:
            async with ClientSession(streams[0], streams[1]) as session:
                await session.initialize()
                try:
                    result = await session.read_resource(uri)
                    output = {'case': label, 'ok': True, 'contents': [{'uri': str(c.uri), 'length': len(c.text), 'mime': c.mime_type} for c in result.contents]}
                except Exception as error:
                    output = {'case': label, 'ok': False, 'error': str(error)}
                print(json.dumps(output), flush=True)

async def main():
    if os.environ.get('DOWN_CASE'):
        await run('listing-failure', '/mcp/', 'vanilla,everything', 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html')
        return
    for args in [
        ('unique', '/mcp/', 'vanilla,everything', 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html'),
        ('ambiguous', '/mcp/', None, 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html'),
        ('missing', '/mcp/', 'vanilla,everything', 'ui://nobody/missing.html'),
        ('single-path', '/vanilla/mcp', None, 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html'),
        ('single-scope', '/mcp/', 'vanilla', 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html'),
        ('stdio-in-scope', '/mcp/', 'vanilla,everything,local', 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html'),
    ]:
        await run(*args)

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Before (5ebc284053)

```text
{"case": "unique", "ok": false, "error": "400: Multiple MCP servers configured; read_resource currently supports exactly one allowed server."}
{"case": "ambiguous", "ok": false, "error": "400: Multiple MCP servers configured; read_resource currently supports exactly one allowed server."}
{"case": "missing", "ok": false, "error": "400: Multiple MCP servers configured; read_resource currently supports exactly one allowed server."}
{"case": "single-path", "ok": true, "contents": [{"uri": "ui://get-time/mcp-app.html", "length": 243811, "mime": "text/html;profile=mcp-app"}]}
{"case": "single-scope", "ok": true, "contents": [{"uri": "ui://get-time/mcp-app.html", "length": 243811, "mime": "text/html;profile=mcp-app"}]}
{"case": "stdio-in-scope", "ok": false, "error": "400: Multiple MCP servers configured; read_resource currently supports exactly one allowed server."}
{"case": "listing-failure", "ok": false, "error": "400: Multiple MCP servers configured; read_resource currently supports exactly one allowed server."}
```

### Earlier revisions of this PR

At cc565359e1 the blocked `local` server counted as a failed listing, so any aggregate read with it in scope returned 502.

```text
{"case": "ambiguous", "ok": false, "error": "502: Unable to list resources from MCP server 'local'; resource owner is unknown."}
{"case": "stdio-in-scope", "ok": false, "error": "502: Unable to list resources from MCP server 'local'; resource owner is unknown."}
```

At a8561da612 the blocked `local` server was still rate checked on every aggregate read, though it is never listed. The `ambiguous` read used its one request, so the next read with it in scope was rejected.

```text
{"case": "stdio-in-scope", "ok": false, "error": "429: Rate limit exceeded for mcp_server: c39977597832124a25e0ecc5c552dbee. Limit type: requests. Current limit: 1, Remaining: 0. Limit resets at: 2026-11-13 00:16:42 UTC"}
```

### After (a21d93b8b3)

```text
{"case": "unique", "ok": true, "contents": [{"uri": "ui://get-time/mcp-app.html", "length": 243811, "mime": "text/html;profile=mcp-app"}]}
{"case": "ambiguous", "ok": false, "error": "Resource URI 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html' is ambiguous across MCP servers: react, vanilla. Use /{server_name}/mcp or x-mcp-servers to select one server."}
{"case": "missing", "ok": false, "error": "Resource 'ui://nobody/missing.html' not found on any allowed MCP server."}
{"case": "single-path", "ok": true, "contents": [{"uri": "ui://get-time/mcp-app.html", "length": 243811, "mime": "text/html;profile=mcp-app"}]}
{"case": "single-scope", "ok": true, "contents": [{"uri": "ui://get-time/mcp-app.html", "length": 243811, "mime": "text/html;profile=mcp-app"}]}
{"case": "stdio-in-scope", "ok": true, "contents": [{"uri": "ui://get-time/mcp-app.html", "length": 243811, "mime": "text/html;profile=mcp-app"}]}
```

With the `everything` server stopped, `DOWN_CASE=1` returns this instead of guessing an owner.

```text
{"case": "listing-failure", "ok": false, "error": "Unable to list resources from MCP server 'everything'; resource owner is unknown."}
```

Owner failures now reach the client as an MCP `INVALID_REQUEST` error, the same way the list handlers report theirs, so the HTTP status prefix is gone from the message.

### Modern protocol (2026-07-28)

Same setup with `mcp_advertised_versions` extended to `2026-07-28` and the client calling `session.discover()` instead of `initialize()`. On that protocol the MCP SDK replaces any error that is not an `MCPError` with a generic one, so before this change the reason never reached the client.

At 501ecfeff6:

```text
{"case": "ambiguous", "protocol": "2026-07-28", "ok": false, "error": "Internal server error"}
{"case": "missing", "protocol": "2026-07-28", "ok": false, "error": "Internal server error"}
{"case": "listing-failure", "protocol": "2026-07-28", "ok": false, "error": "Internal server error"}
```

At a21d93b8b3:

```text
{"case": "ambiguous", "protocol": "2026-07-28", "ok": false, "error": "Resource URI 'ui://get-time/mcp-app.html' is ambiguous across MCP servers: react, vanilla. Use /{server_name}/mcp or x-mcp-servers to select one server."}
{"case": "missing", "protocol": "2026-07-28", "ok": false, "error": "Resource 'ui://nobody/missing.html' not found on any allowed MCP server."}
{"case": "listing-failure", "protocol": "2026-07-28", "ok": false, "error": "Unable to list resources from MCP server 'everything'; resource owner is unknown."}
```

The success cases return the widget on both protocols.

The regression test `test_resource_read_requires_unique_owner_from_complete_listings` in `tests/unit/proxy/mcp_server/test_operations.py` covers nine cases and runs the real rate limiter. Undoing each fix turns its case red. Dropping the header scope on the final read fails `scoped_bearer`, because the owner then gets the caller's bearer. Skipping the candidate RPM check fails `rate_limited`, because a second read of a missing URI is a 404 again and not a rate-limit error. Charging the owner a second time fails every success case under `rpm: 1`. Leaving siblings running fails `slow_failure`, because the hung listing is never cancelled. In `legacy_delegates` both servers are legacy `oauth2` delegates. Forwarding the caller bearer on either the owner lookups or the final read fails that case. The test reads through the MCP operation handler, so removing the `MCPError` conversion fails every error case. In `blocked_stdio` the blocked stdio server forwards the caller bearer and has already used its `rpm: 1`. Rate checking it fails the read, and keeping it in the header scope withholds the bearer from the real owner, so both fail that case. Making the manager treat a blocked stdio server as a failed listing no longer changes any result, because the read skips those servers before listing. The live proof covers the stdio and RPM fixes. The bearer and cancellation fixes are covered by the unit cases only, since the official example servers don't echo auth headers.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix
✅ Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Only exact URIs from `resources/list` route
  - URIs built from templates, or `?v=` variants the upstream never lists, return 404
- One allowed server that is down blocks every aggregate read with an error
- Each aggregate read uses one MCP RPM unit on every listable allowed server
  - One server over its limit rejects the whole read, since it might be the owner
- Servers that consume the caller's `Authorization` get no shared header in a multi-server read
  - That covers client-forwarded, legacy oauth2 delegate and OAuth pass-through servers
  - They need per-server `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` headers
- An upstream auth challenge during listing surfaces as a listing error, not 401
- A cold cache adds one listing per allowed server to each read
  - The discovery cache is per worker with a 60s default TTL

### Low

- Live proof only covered unauthenticated local upstreams, not OAuth upstreams
- The listing cache cancels a shared listing only after its last waiter leaves

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes multi-server resource routing, concurrent upstream listings, credential forwarding, and error surfaces on a security-sensitive MCP path; behavior shifts for aggregate reads and failure modes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Aggregate `resources/read` now picks the owning MCP server** instead of rejecting requests when more than one server is in scope. For multi-server reads, the gateway concurrently lists each listable candidate (skipping blocked stdio), applies per-server rate limits, matches the requested URI against listed resources, and reads only from the unique owner.
> 
> Listing failures, ambiguity, missing URIs, and rate limits surface as structured **`MCPError` (`INVALID_REQUEST`)** with explicit messages; **`list_resources_from_server`** and **`ResourceListingFailed`** replace silent empty lists on listing errors. **Caller `Authorization` is withheld** during gateway-selected owner lookup and the final read when fan-out would replay one token across multiple consuming servers; **`caller_authorization_fans_out`** treats aggregate reads as scoped fan-out. Tests cover owner resolution, auth withholding, cancellation, and MCP protocol error mapping.

title: fix(azure): backport Azure OpenAI Decisions support to lts/1.108.x (#48529)
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `azure/` deployments get a 400 on `/v1/decisions` on 1.108.x
- Only `azure_ai/` was registered for Decisions on this line

How it solves it:

- Backports #48529, Azure OpenAI Decisions with API key or Entra ID auth
- Brings its prerequisite #46539 plus two small Azure helpers

Intentional product change: `azure_ai/` Decisions deployments with no API key now try Entra ID (from #46539), and their missing-credential 401 names both options.

## User Flow

Before: a developer calling Decisions on an Azure OpenAI deployment is refused by the gateway before Azure is called

1. The proxy admin adds a deployment with `model: azure/gpt-6-luna` and the resource's `api_base` and `api_key`
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/decisions with `"model": "gpt-6-luna"`, an `input` message and three `questions`
3. The response is 400 `Unknown Decisions provider 'azure'`, with a supported list that has `azure_ai` but no `azure`

After: the same request is answered by the Azure deployment

1. The proxy admin adds a deployment with `model: azure/gpt-6-luna` and the resource's `api_base` and `api_key`
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/decisions with `"model": "gpt-6-luna"`, an `input` message and three `questions`
3. The response is 200 with one answer per question and a `usage` block
4. The `x-litellm-response-cost` header is non-zero and the spend log row carries the same amount

## Backport contents

Picks #48529 and its prerequisite #46539, plus two Azure helpers hand-ported from #46377 and #47348. No version or dependency bumps.

<details>
<summary>Per-commit notes</summary>

- [x] https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48529 picked as 0d16d5eb4d from e5757934fd. One conflict, in the provider set of `tests/unit/decisions/test_main.py`. The line's set is kept and `azure` is added. `lm_studio` from main's set is left out because the line has no LM Studio Decisions support
- [x] https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/46539 picked clean as e18b03d84c from caad4d6204. #48529 needs it for the `litellm_params` argument and the async variant of the Decisions environment check
- [x] 42f2276528 is a hand-port of two helpers #48529 calls, `BaseAzureLLM.resolve_azure_api_base` from https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/46377 and `cached_azure_ad_token_refresh_provider` from https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/47348. Only those hunks of `litellm/llms/azure/common_utils.py` are taken, and the existing URL helper now calls the extracted resolver so its behavior is the same
- Not picked: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/49863, which later changed the Entra failure status on main and is marked breaking
- Version: unchanged, no `enterprise/` or `litellm-proxy-extras/` change
- Dependency bumps: none. Every package the sweep flagged is at the same version on main or has no fixed release

</details>

Gauntlet-mini: SURVIVED, 5/5 lenses, 0 confirmed, run ba5213415825, reviewed 0d16d5eb4d. The five lenses were run in sequence by one agent, since this session had no subagent tool.

<details>
<summary>Rejected findings and strongest dissent</summary>

- Rejected: the line's Azure URL helper still rewrites `/openai` to `/openai/v1` with a plain string replace. Decisions never passes an `api_version`, so that branch is not reached
- Rejected: the `azure_ai/` missing-credential message changed. It is what #46539 intends and its integration test asserts the new text
- Rejected: removing the strip of a caller-sent `api-key` header fails no test. The same gap exists on main, so it is listed under Caveats instead of fixed here
- Strongest dissent: a keyless `azure/` deployment with no usable Entra identity answers 500. It matches main at the picked commit and is listed under Caveats

</details>

## Relevant issues

Backport of https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/48529 to `lts/1.108.x`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Real Azure deployments, no mocks. Each leg ran 2 uvicorn workers with its own Redis and Postgres, no `--reload`.

| Case | Before (1b769ce7d8) | After (0d16d5eb4d) |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/decisions` and `/decisions`, model `gpt-6-luna` or `azure/gpt-6-luna` | 400 `Unknown Decisions provider 'azure'` | 200, three answers, cost 4.01e-05 |
| `GET /spend/logs` for that call | `failure` row, spend 0 | `success` row, provider `azure`, 401 tokens, spend 4.01e-05 |
| Bad Azure key | 400 unknown provider | 401 from Azure |
| Missing Azure deployment | 400 unknown provider | 404 `DeploymentNotFound` from Azure |
| `azure_ai/` Microsoft-Decision-1 with an API key | 200, cost 4.956e-06 | same |
| Azure chat completions | 200 `ok` | same |
| Azure `/v1/responses`, three api_version settings | 200 `completed` | same |
| Python SDK `litellm.decisions` and `litellm.adecisions` | `BadRequestError` unknown provider | three answers, 401 tokens |
| `tests/e2e/llm_translation` Azure OpenAI tests | 11 passed | 11 passed |

Not proven live: Entra ID auth, see Caveats. The curl lines below are shown without their output filter, the exact lines are in the collapsed block.

<details>
<summary>Setup (proxy command, config, env var names, request body)</summary>

### Before (1b769ce7d8)

#### Decisions on the Azure OpenAI deployment
