title: feat(proxy): router_settings.fallback_on_saturation walks key and team fallbacks before a model saturates, replacing team model_preferences
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Team `router_settings.fallbacks` now run on the proxy's own 429s, a new opt-in `router_settings.fallback_on_saturation` makes that walk start at `saturation_threshold` instead of at a refusal, and `team_metadata.model_preferences` from #51350 is removed since fallbacks now cover it.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5830c318df3d4a3f8be0e230bbc7b0b2
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/5830c318df3d4a3f8be0e230bbc7b0b2?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Team `router_settings.fallbacks` were ignored on proxy-side 429s, only key and global lists ran
- The pre-call fallback walk never checked that the caller may call the fallback model, that the fallback is within its per-model and access-group budgets, that it passes the pricing rules, that the budget reserved at auth still fits it, or charged the fallback's spend to the groups that grant it
- #51350 added `team_metadata.model_preferences`, a second knob doing what fallbacks do
- Fallbacks only run after a refusal, so a flexible team fills a model before leaving it

How it solves it:

- `_configured_fallbacks` resolves Key > Team > Global through `get_hierarchical_router_settings`
- `_fallback_grant` runs the auth-time checks on each fallback, on the model group the fallback is served by once `model_group_alias` is applied, so an alias cannot skip the served model's budgets: `is_model_authorized_for_token` while access is enforced, `_fallback_pricing_admits` (no unpriced fallback while `block_requests_for_models_without_pricing` is on, no priced fallback for a zero-cost request), `_is_within_every_model_budget` (zero-cost models skip it, as at auth), `collect_matched_model_access_groups` plus `_model_access_group_max_budget_check` on the groups the request's `budget_reservation` does not already hold (the hold sits in the same counter, so it must not refuse its own fallback), `_reservation_covers` (the fallback costs no more per token than the model the reservation was estimated for, read through `registry().group()`, and the held access groups grant it), and the served fallback's groups are stamped on `matched_model_access_groups` so spend lands on them, restored when the walk moves on
- New `router_settings.fallback_on_saturation` (default off) on keys and teams, only the saved key or team setting counts, a `router_settings_override.fallback_on_saturation` in the request body is dropped in place (`drop_client_saturation_opt_in`), the request stays the caller's object
- At or above `saturation_threshold` the limiter raises a `model_saturation_fallback` 429 and the walk runs; that handoff carries no `rate_limited_by` reason, so the throttle metric from #51417 does not count it
- `_fallback_refusal_ends_the_walk`: at saturation a fallback refused for any reason (rate limit, guardrail, budget) is a miss, and when none admits the request goes back to the requested model, stamped so the limiter admits or refuses it as before; off saturation only a hard per-model 429 or a non-rate-limit failure ends the walk, as today
- `_release_pre_call_hold` gives back what the limiters hold for a model the walk leaves: the registered v3 limiter's slot and tokens, and the dynamic limiter's team-share reservation through its new `async_post_call_failure_hook` (also run by `post_call_failure_hook`, so a guardrail refusal after admission refunds it too)
- An exhausted saturation walk replays with the `model` argument the first attempt saw, so chained `model_alias_map` entries apply once
- `model_preferences`, `x-litellm-model-steered-from` and the stash field from #51350 are removed, and the steering test that landed with #51417 is rewritten for the saturation handoff

Intentional product change: `team_metadata.model_preferences` (merged today in #51350, unreleased) no longer does anything. The same behavior is `router_settings: {"fallbacks": [...], "fallback_on_saturation": true}` on the team.

## User Flow

Before: a team whose fallbacks live on the team gets a 429 from the proxy's own rate limiter and no fallback runs

1. Admin sends POST /team/new with `"router_settings": {"fallbacks": [{"luna": ["opus"]}]}` and a key for it
2. The key sends POST /v1/chat/completions for `luna` once `luna` is at its RPM limit
3. 429 "Model capacity reached for luna", no `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks` header, `opus` idle

After: the same team is served by `opus`, and with `fallback_on_saturation` it leaves `luna` before `luna` is full

1. Admin sends POST /team/new with `"router_settings": {"fallbacks": [{"luna": ["opus"]}], "fallback_on_saturation": true}`
2. The key sends POST /v1/chat/completions for `luna` once `luna` is at 50% of its RPM (`saturation_threshold`)
3. 200 from `opus` with `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 1` and `x-litellm-fallback-reason: rate_limit:model_saturation_fallback`, spend logged against `opus` and the access groups that grant `opus`
4. A team on `luna` only keeps getting 200s from `luna`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup: the integration harness boots a real proxy per worker against its own Postgres, with a scripted upstream standing in for OpenAI (the behavior under test is the proxy's own rate limiter, the upstream only has to answer 200). Two deployments of `openai/gpt-5.6` are created through POST /model/new, the preferred one with `rpm: 2` and the fallback with `rpm: 1000`, `dynamic_rate_limiter_v3` is on with `saturation_threshold: 0.5` and `saturation_check_cache_ttl: 1`. The test file is the runbook: `tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_on_saturation.py`.

```bash
INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2 LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/python tests/integration/run.py providers tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_on_saturation.py
```

### Before (91808ed2cf)

Not run live. On the merge base `/team/new` accepts `router_settings.fallback_on_saturation` as an unknown key and nothing reads it, and `_configured_fallbacks` reads only `user_api_key_dict.router_settings` (the key column) or the router's list, so a team-level `fallbacks` entry never runs on a `ProxyRateLimitError`. The first case below would fail at the `x-litellm-fallback-reason` assertion with a 429 from `luna`.

### After (ebb08392bb)

#### A team with fallback_on_saturation is served by its fallback once the model saturates

1. Rigid team key: POST /v1/chat/completions for the preferred model, 200, `x-litellm-model-id` is the preferred deployment, no fallback header
2. Flexible team key (team `router_settings` as above): POST /v1/chat/completions for the preferred model, 200, `x-litellm-fallback-reason: rate_limit:model_saturation_fallback`, `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 1`, `x-litellm-model-id` is the fallback deployment
3. Rigid team key again: 200 from the preferred deployment, no fallback header
4. `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.model_group` for the fallback response is the fallback model

#### A fallback the team may not call is never used

1. Team allowed only the preferred model, `fallbacks` pointing at a model it may not call, `fallback_on_saturation: true`
2. First request 200 from the preferred deployment
3. Every later 200 is from the preferred deployment with no fallback header, until the preferred deployment's own 429 arrives (so the walk ran past saturation and skipped the forbidden model)

```
tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_on_saturation.py::test_a_team_with_fallback_on_saturation_is_served_by_its_fallback_once_the_model_saturates PASSED
tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_on_saturation.py::test_a_fallback_the_team_may_not_call_is_never_used PASSED
========================= 2 passed in 76.97s (0:01:16) =========================
```

Unit at the same tip: `tests/unit/proxy/test_common_request_processing.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/common_utils/test_proxy_rate_limit_error.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/test_response_polling_pre_call_checks.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/test_litellm_pre_call_utils.py` (all pass at the tip. Before `3477a01` six limiter metric tests in `test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py` failed locally because the merge kept stale copies of them, that commit takes main's versions. The same commit fixes a regression the codex passthrough tests caught, the fallback walk invented an empty `metadata` bucket on a request that had none, so the provider saw an extra field. `378b604` then moves the walk marker out of the body entirely into a request `ContextVar`, armed and disarmed by `_pre_call_with_fallbacks`, so requests without metadata still fall back and caller metadata is never rewritten. The same commit refuses every pre-call fallback for an agent-owned key, the auth-time `refuse_agent_keys` contract the removed steering code also followed. `591e4ed` moves the exhausted state into the same `ContextVar`, so no client field can arm, skip or exhaust the walk, checks the end user's model allowlist on every fallback candidate through `can_customer_access_model`, and runs the v3 limiter's failure hook for a fallback the proxy refused after admitting it, so its slot and tokens are released before the walk moves on. `01bf61d` loads that end user only when a database is connected, so a request that names a `user` on a proxy without one keeps its fallbacks. `5ecc82e` grants each fallback on the group its alias is served by, and releases the rate limited model's slot and token hold before the walk's first attempt, since the next attempt overwrites the request's limiter stash and would otherwise leave that hold charged until the window resets. The next commit checks each fallback's per-model budgets on its listed name, its served group and that group's resolved model, the chain auth checks. `491d23e` adds the dynamic limiter's `async_post_call_failure_hook` so the walk refunds its team-share reservation, replays an exhausted walk with the pre-call `model` argument so aliases are not applied twice, and drives the hold-release test through the real v3 limiter with one slot per key). New cases cover team-level fallbacks on a local 429, a fallback the key may not call, a fallback over its per-model budget, a fallback over its access-group budget, a fallback in a group the request already holds, an unpriced fallback while unpriced models are blocked, a fallback priced above the reserved estimate, a fallback outside the reserved access groups, a fallback aliased to a model over its budget, spend charged to the fallback's groups, a client body that tries to opt in, a fallback refused at saturation, the return to the requested model when no fallback has room, and the saturation handoff not counting as a throttle. `ruff_strict_gate.py`, `type_check_gate.py`, `type_discipline_gate.py`, `test_quality_gate.py`, `router_surface_check.py` and ruff pass against the merge base.

## Type

🆕 New Feature
🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- The pre-call walk now enforces fallback model access, pricing, per-model and access-group budgets and the auth-time budget reservation, a key that relied on reaching a forbidden, unpriced or over-budget fallback through a local 429 gets the primary 429 instead (same contract the router already applies to its own fallbacks, `enforce_fallback_model_access: false` restores the access part)
- Access groups the request did not reserve against at auth get the plain budget read, the same `disable_budget_reservation` contract the auth-time fallback candidates use, so concurrent fallbacks can overshoot such a group's ceiling slightly
- The saturation read is cached `saturation_check_cache_ttl` seconds, so the walk lags a burst by up to that long

### Low

- A request that walks every fallback at saturation runs the pre-call hooks once more on the requested model
- Fallback budget and access-group lookups add cached team, membership and project reads per fallback candidate, only on the 429 path

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(proxy): fallback_on_saturation walks key and team fallbacks before a model saturates, replacing team_metadata.model_preferences

Team router_settings.fallbacks now fire on proxy-side rate limits: the pre-call
fallback walk reads router settings Key > Team > Global instead of the key's
column alone, and skips a fallback the caller may not call.

A key or team with router_settings.fallback_on_saturation: true walks that same
fallback list as soon as the requested model reaches saturation_threshold in
dynamic_rate_limiter_v3, and goes back to the requested model when no fallback
admits the request. Responses carry x-litellm-fallback-reason:
rate_limit:model_saturation_fallback.

Removes the team_metadata.model_preferences steering and the
x-litellm-model-steered-from header from #51350, which did the same job through
a second knob.

* fix(proxy): strict bool for fallback_on_saturation, drop a stale import and settle the pre-call tests

fallback_on_saturation only turns on for a real boolean true, so a string like "yes" in router_settings no longer enables it. The saturation unit test reads saturation through the limiter's cache, so it asserts the threshold was reached instead of an exact count. The response polling test now hands the pre-call path an awaitable router_settings lookup, as the pre-call fallback walk reads Key > Team settings before the first call.

* fix(proxy): pre-call fallbacks pass the budget and access-group checks a direct request does

A fallback the pre-call walk picks now has to clear every per-model budget layer and the budgets of the access
groups that grant it, and its spend is charged to those groups instead of the requested model's. At saturation a
fallback that fails for any reason counts as a miss and the request goes back to the requested model. The client
body can no longer opt itself into the saturation walk through router_settings_override, only the saved key or team
router_settings can. The integration test for a forbidden fallback waits for the preferred model's own 429 so it
cannot pass before saturation.

* refactor(proxy): one helper decides which refused fallbacks end the pre-call walk

_pre_call_with_fallbacks had grown past the strict C901 ceiling, so the two except clauses fold into one and _fallback_refusal_ends_the_walk carries the rule: at saturation every refusal is a miss, otherwise only a non-rate-limit failure or a hard per-model 429 reaches the caller.

* fix(proxy): keep the caller's request object through the pre-call fallback walk

Copying the request to drop a client fallback_on_saturation opt-in handed the hooks a different dict than the one the caller holds, so header metadata written into one never reached the other (test_add_litellm_metadata_from_request_headers). drop_client_saturation_opt_in now edits the request in place.

* fix(proxy): pre-call fallbacks keep the pricing and budget-reservation rules a direct request passes

A fallback is skipped when unpriced models are blocked and it has no pricing, when a zero-cost request would land on a priced model, and when the budget auth reserved for the requested model does not fit it (higher per-token prices, or reserved against an access group that does not grant it).

* refactor(proxy): read fallback prices through the router registry entry point

router_surface_check only lets the router surface shrink, so the per-token price lookup goes through registry().group() instead of the deprecated get_model_group_info.

* fix(proxy): a fallback's group budget check skips the groups the request already holds

The auth-time reservation sits in the same counter the plain budget read uses, so a fallback in a group the request already reserved against was refused by its own hold once the group was within one estimate of max_budget. Groups without a hold keep the plain read.

* test(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): the throttle metric test from main uses fallback_on_saturation instead of the removed steering

A saturation handoff carries no rate_limited_by reason, so it is never counted as a throttle.

* fix(proxy): the saturation handoff only fires under the fallback walk

_pre_call_with_fallbacks arms the request before the hooks run, so routes that call the hooks directly (batches, fine-tuning, polling, images) keep admitting or refusing an opted-in key on a saturated model as before instead of surfacing the handoff 429.

* style(proxy): keep the cast-ok reason within the line length

* fix(proxy): never invent a metadata bucket when arming the saturation fallback walk, take main's limiter metric tests

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(proxy): arm the saturation fallback walk in the request context, refuse fallbacks for agent-owned keys

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(proxy): keep the saturation walk state out of the body, check the end user's allowlist on fallbacks, release a refused fallback's rate limit hold

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(proxy): only load the end user for fallback checks when a database is connected

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(proxy): grant pre-call fallbacks on the model an alias serves and release the rate limited model's hold before the walk

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(proxy): check a pre-call fallback's per-model budgets on its listed name and its served group, as auth does

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(proxy): assert the listed fallback name's budget blocks an aliased fallback, not the order of budget reads

Co-Authored-By: Devin AI <158243242+devin-ai-integration[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(proxy): release the dynamic limiter's reservation when the fallback walk leaves a model, and replay an exhausted walk with the requested model

The dynamic rate limiter admits through its own inner v3 limiter, so the walk's hold release never reached its team-share
reservation. It now exposes async_post_call_failure_hook, which refunds that reservation when the proxy refuses a request
after admission, and _release_pre_call_hold calls it next to the registered limiter.

An exhausted saturation walk replayed with the already aliased model name, so chained model_alias_map entries moved the
request on to a further alias. It now replays with the model argument the first attempt saw.

The hold-release test drives the real v3 limiter with one slot per key instead of recording hook calls.

title: fix(azure): strip GPT-5 routing marker from Responses deployments
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Azure Responses requests now send the deployment name without the GPT-5 routing marker
- SDK regression tests check the outgoing request for plain and combined routing markers

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves

- Azure receives a routing marker as the deployment name

How it solves it

- Strip the existing marker before sending Responses requests
- Check outgoing SDK request bodies with deterministic regression tests

## User Flow

Before, a configured GPT-5 deployment cannot serve Responses requests

1. Configure a model with `azure/gpt5_series/<deployment>`
2. Send `POST http://localhost:4867/v1/responses` with that model alias and an input
3. Azure receives the marker and returns a deployment error

After, the same configured deployment serves the request

1. Configure a model with `azure/gpt5_series/<deployment>`
2. Send `POST http://localhost:4867/v1/responses` with that model alias and an input
3. Azure receives the bare deployment name and returns a completed response

## Relevant issues

Fixes #46866

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] Affected tests pass on the exact candidate in Devin
- [x] Applicable in-scope CI checks have completed successfully
- [x] The change only fixes Azure Responses routing-marker leakage
- [ ] Required automated reviews have completed on the current tip

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Independent Devin Ultra verification used baseline `d29ac75af1519566ab7593034e76935bbc203ec1` and candidate `e15ff9e0357e529ba5a366ecf2fbca7d229dd6d5`, with real Azure calls and two proxy workers sharing dedicated Redis

### Before (d29ac75af1519566ab7593034e76935bbc203ec1)

1. Run the SDK script below with `azure/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano`, then send the corresponding proxy request
2. Observe outgoing `model=gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano`, SDK `NotFoundError`, and proxy HTTP 404
3. Repeat with `azure/responses/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano`, with the same failure

### After (e15ff9e0357e529ba5a366ecf2fbca7d229dd6d5)

1. Run the same SDK script and corresponding proxy request
2. Observe outgoing `model=gpt-5.4-nano`, a completed SDK response, and proxy HTTP 200
3. Repeat with `azure/responses/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano`, also successful

| configured model | baseline d29ac75a SDK | baseline proxy (2 workers+Redis) | candidate e15ff9e0 SDK | candidate proxy (2 workers+Redis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| azure/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano | sent `gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano`, NotFoundError DeploymentNotFound | same, HTTP 404 | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, completed "pong" | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, HTTP 200 "pong" |
| azure/responses/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano | sent `gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano`, NotFoundError | same, HTTP 404 | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, "pong" | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, HTTP 200 "pong" |
| azure/gpt-5.4-nano | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, "pong" | HTTP 200 "pong" | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, Azure 429 rate_limit_exceeded (quota; body already correct) | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, HTTP 200 "pong" |
| azure/o_series/gpt-5.4-nano | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, "pong" | HTTP 200 "pong" | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, Azure 429 (body correct) | sent `gpt-5.4-nano`, HTTP 200 "pong" |
| azure/gpt5_series/does-not-exist-46866 | sent `gpt5_series/does-not-exist-46866`, NotFoundError | same, HTTP 404 | sent `does-not-exist-46866`, NotFoundError DeploymentNotFound | sent `does-not-exist-46866`, HTTP 404 |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction setup and exact client commands</summary>

Set `AZURE_API_BASE`, `AZURE_API_KEY`, and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in the shell. The Azure deployment used here was named `gpt-5.4-nano`. Use source checkouts of the recorded commits with the frozen dependency environment

Save this as `sdk_live.py` outside tracked source and run `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python sdk_live.py azure/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano` from each checkout with its source on `PYTHONPATH`

```python
import json, os, sys
import httpx
import litellm
from litellm.llms.custom_httpx.http_handler import HTTPHandler

model = sys.argv[1]
sent = {}

def record(request: httpx.Request) -> None:
    sent["url"] = str(request.url).replace(os.environ["AZURE_API_BASE"].rstrip("/"), "<AZURE_API_BASE>")
    sent["body_model"] = json.loads(request.content)["model"]

client = HTTPHandler()
client.client = httpx.Client(event_hooks={"request": [record]}, timeout=60)
status, detail = "ok", ""
try:
    r = litellm.responses(
        model=model, input="Reply with the single word pong.",
        api_base=os.environ["AZURE_API_BASE"], api_key=os.environ["AZURE_API_KEY"],
        api_version="2025-04-01-preview", client=client, max_output_tokens=64,
    )
    detail = json.dumps({"response_model": r.model, "status": r.status, "output_text": r.output_text[:80]})
except Exception as e:
    status = type(e).__name__
    detail = " ".join(str(e).replace(os.environ["AZURE_API_KEY"], "<redacted>").split())[:500]
print("litellm:", litellm.__file__)
print("requested_model:", model)
print("sent:", json.dumps(sent))
print("result:", status, detail)
```

**proxy_live_config.yaml**
```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: azure-gpt5-routed
    litellm_params: {model: azure/gpt5_series/gpt-5.4-nano, api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE, api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY, api_version: "2025-04-01-preview"}
  - model_name: azure-gpt5-responses-combined
```

title: fix(bedrock): send max_tokens and priority in Cohere embedding requests
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Bedrock and SageMaker Cohere embeddings now forward max_tokens and priority to the provider instead of silently dropping them, so callers can cap how much of each input gets embedded and models that do not support the fields return a clear error.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a063bf3bb18842e298c49b81ad785102
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/a063bf3bb18842e298c49b81ad785102?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Bedrock Cohere embeddings silently dropped `max_tokens` from the request body
- SageMaker Cohere embeddings silently dropped `max_tokens` and `priority`
- `CohereEmbeddingRequest` doubles as the field allowlist and lacked both keys

How it solves it:

- Adds `max_tokens` and `priority` to `CohereEmbeddingRequest`
- Bedrock and SageMaker Cohere transforms now keep both fields in the body
- Regression tests capture the outgoing body and fail on main

## User Flow

Before: a developer embedding long documents through Bedrock Cohere v4 sets `max_tokens` and it has no effect

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"model": "cohere-v4"`, a long text and `"max_tokens": 16`
2. They get a 200 and a vector that matches the one they get without `max_tokens` (cosine 0.9999, inside provider drift), so the full text was embedded
3. Their request to the same route with `"model": "cohere-v3"` and `"max_tokens": 16` also returns 200 with the field silently ignored

After: the same request embeds only the first 16 tokens, and unsupported models say so

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/embeddings with `"model": "cohere-v4"`, the long text and `"max_tokens": 16`
2. They get a 200 and a clearly different vector (cosine 0.9117 vs the no-`max_tokens` call), so Bedrock truncated the input as asked
3. Their `"model": "cohere-v3"` request with `"max_tokens": 16` now returns 400 with Bedrock's own text, `extraneous key [max_tokens] is not permitted`, instead of a silent no-op

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10696

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. Two proxies ran side by side from separate checkouts, the merge base on port 4001 and the tip on port 4000, both against real Bedrock in us-east-1 through the `litellm-dev` AWS profile. One worker and no Redis, because the change is request-body serialization with no shared router or spend state, so a second worker or Redis would not change what the provider receives.

Proxy start, run once per checkout with its own `--port`:

```
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=<redacted> python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config /home/ubuntu/qa/lit10696_config.yaml --port 4001 --num_workers 1 --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee base_proxy.log
LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=<redacted> python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config /home/ubuntu/qa/lit10696_config.yaml --port 4000 --num_workers 1 --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee tip_proxy.log
```

`lit10696_config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: cohere-v4
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/cohere.embed-v4:0
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
      aws_profile_name: litellm-dev
  - model_name: cohere-v3
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/cohere.embed-english-v3
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
      aws_profile_name: litellm-dev

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

<details>
<summary>Client, `python lit10696_client.py <port>`, embeds a 169 token text with no extras, then with `max_tokens=16`, then with `priority=5`, and prints the cosine against the baseline</summary>

```python
import json, math, os, sys, urllib.request

port = sys.argv[1]
URL = f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/embeddings"
TEXT = "LiteLLM is an AI gateway that proxies requests across many providers. " * 12

def embed(model, **extra):
    body = json.dumps({"model": model, "input": [TEXT], **extra}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        URL,
        data=body,
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
            out = json.loads(r.read())
            return r.status, out["data"][0]["embedding"], out.get("usage")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, None, e.read().decode()[:400]

def cos(a, b):
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b)) / math.sqrt(
        sum(x * x for x in a) * sum(y * y for y in b)
    )

for model in ("cohere-v4", "cohere-v3"):
    s, base, u = embed(model)
    print(f"[{port}] {model} baseline: status={s} usage={u}")
    for extra in ({"max_tokens": 16}, {"priority": 5}):
        s, v, u = embed(model, **extra)
        if v is None:
            print(f"[{port}] {model} {extra}: status={s} error={u}")
        else:
            print(f"[{port}] {model} {extra}: status={s} usage={u} cosine_vs_baseline={cos(base, v):.4f}")
```

</details>

### Before (d29ac75af1)

#### Bedrock Cohere v4 and v3, `max_tokens` and `priority` silently dropped

1. `python lit10696_client.py 4001`
2. Output (usage trimmed), every call returns 200 and every vector sits inside provider repeat drift of the baseline:

```
[4001] cohere-v4 baseline: status=200 prompt_tokens=169
[4001] cohere-v4 {'max_tokens': 16}: status=200 cosine_vs_baseline=0.9999
[4001] cohere-v4 {'priority': 5}: status=200 cosine_vs_baseline=1.0000
[4001] cohere-v3 baseline: status=200 prompt_tokens=169
[4001] cohere-v3 {'max_tokens': 16}: status=200 cosine_vs_baseline=0.9999
[4001] cohere-v3 {'priority': 5}: status=200 cosine_vs_baseline=0.9999
```

3. `grep -c "'max_tokens': 16" base_proxy.log` returns 0, the field never appears in any `POST Request Sent from LiteLLM` body

### After (1334896b69)

#### Bedrock Cohere v4 and v3, `max_tokens` and `priority` reach Bedrock

1. `python lit10696_client.py 4000`
2. Output (usage trimmed). v4 with `max_tokens=16` now returns a clearly different vector, v4 accepts `priority`, and v3 returns Bedrock's own validation error for both fields:

```
[4000] cohere-v4 baseline: status=200 prompt_tokens=169
[4000] cohere-v4 {'max_tokens': 16}: status=200 cosine_vs_baseline=0.9117
[4000] cohere-v4 {'priority': 5}: status=200 cosine_vs_baseline=1.0000
[4000] cohere-v3 baseline: status=200 prompt_tokens=169
[4000] cohere-v3 {'max_tokens': 16}: status=400 error={"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {\"message\":\"Malformed input request: #: extraneous key [max_tokens] is not permitted, please reformat your input and try again.\"} ...
[4000] cohere-v3 {'priority': 5}: status=400 error={"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {\"message\":\"Malformed input request: #: extraneous key [priority] is not permitted, please reformat your input and try again.\"} ...
```

3. The tip proxy log shows the outgoing Bedrock body now carries the field:

```
POST Request Sent from LiteLLM:
curl -X POST \
https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/cohere.embed-v4:0/invoke \
-d '{'input_type': 'search_document', 'texts': ['LiteLLM is an AI gateway ...'], 'max_tokens': 16}'
```

#### Regression tests

1. `uv run pytest tests/unit/llms/bedrock/embed/test_bedrock_embedding.py tests/unit/llms/sagemaker/test_sagemaker_embedding_voyage.py -k "max_tokens_and_priority"`
2. On the merge base (d29ac75af1) both new tests fail, the captured Bedrock body and the SageMaker transform output lack `max_tokens` and `priority`. On the tip both pass.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Bedrock Cohere v3 now returns 400 for `max_tokens` or `priority` where it used to ignore them silently
  - Bedrock's v3 schema rejects both keys, so callers passing them to v3 must stop sending them
  - Prompt usage reported by the proxy stays at the input token count either way, Bedrock does not report the truncated count

### Low

- SageMaker Cohere is covered by the transform-level regression test only. No SageMaker Cohere endpoint or credential exists in the QA vaults, and the `litellm-dev` AWS role is denied `sagemaker:*`. The SageMaker config calls the same `BedrockCohereEmbeddingConfig.transform_request` that the live Bedrock proof exercises
- `extra_body` for embedding providers with custom handlers is still not unwrapped, tracked separately in LIT-10698

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes embedding request serialization across Bedrock/SageMaker Cohere paths; unsupported models may return 400 where callers previously saw silent no-ops.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Cohere embedding calls through Bedrock and SageMaker now honor `max_tokens` and `priority` instead of stripping them from the provider payload.**
> 
> `CohereEmbeddingRequest` gains `max_tokens` and `priority` as allowed fields, which updates the Bedrock Cohere transform allowlist so those kwargs flow into the InvokeModel body (SageMaker Cohere reuses the same transform). New unit tests assert the Bedrock HTTP body and SageMaker request transform include `max_tokens`, `priority`, and related options like `truncate`.
> 
> **Behavior note:** models that do not accept these keys (e.g. Bedrock Cohere v3) will now surface provider validation errors rather than silently ignoring the parameters.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1334896b69a90955b48bd030a0af917522c8195c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(model-catalog): read output_cost_per_video in the rust registry check
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

teaches the cost map check about a per-video price field so the 27 fal.ai per-video rows in #51225 can land.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/bf0d5a571db44ed1bb5d685251587e15
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/bf0d5a571db44ed1bb5d685251587e15?variant=devin
Requested by: @kenneth-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `cost-map-guard` runs the base branch's `check-registry` on a PR's cost map
- So a new price field and the rows using it cannot land together
- #51225 adds `output_cost_per_video` rows and fails the guard for that reason

How it solves it:

- Adds `OutputUnit::Video` and parses `output_cost_per_video` as a flat price key
- Adds `video` to `FLAT_KEY_PATTERN`, so the generated JSON schema accepts the key as well
- Adds no cost map rows and changes no Python

## User Flow

Before: a contributor cannot add a cost map row that uses `output_cost_per_video`

1. They open a PR against `main` that adds `"output_cost_per_video": 0.02` to a row in `model_prices_and_context_window.json`
2. The required `cost-map-guard` check fails with `<model>.output_cost_per_video: not a field litellm reads`

After: the same PR passes the check

1. They open a PR against `main` that adds `"output_cost_per_video": 0.02` to a row in `model_prices_and_context_window.json`
2. The required `cost-map-guard` check passes

## Linear ticket

Part of LIT-10647, resolved by #51225

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at `0845bc2512`. The diff is 9 added lines and 1 removed in three Rust files: one enum variant, one parser arm with its test case, and the `video` alternative in `FLAT_KEY_PATTERN` with two cases in the test that keeps that pattern and the parser in agreement. No proxy or provider path reads the new variant, so there is no request to send before and after. The check that changes is `check-registry`, the binary `cost-map-guard` runs, so the proof runs that binary on the cost map from #51225 (the one with the 27 `output_cost_per_video` rows) at `main` and at the tip. This is the same split #51365 used for `output_cost_per_billable_unit`.

At `d29ac75af1` (`main`):

```console
$ cargo run --locked --quiet --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-model-catalog --bin check-registry -- model_prices_and_context_window.json
fal_ai/fal-ai/auto-caption.output_cost_per_video: not a field litellm reads
fal_ai/fal-ai/hunyuan-video.output_cost_per_video: not a field litellm reads
fal_ai/fal-ai/hunyuan-video-image-to-video.output_cost_per_video: not a field litellm reads
... (27 lines in total, one per row)
$ echo $?
1
```

At `0845bc2512` (tip):

```console
$ cargo run --locked --quiet --manifest-path litellm/rust/Cargo.toml -p litellm-model-catalog --bin check-registry -- model_prices_and_context_window.json
$ echo $?
0
```

The tip also passes `check-registry` on `main`'s own cost map (exit 0), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on `litellm-model-catalog` and `litellm-cost`, and `cargo test` on both crates (335 tests), including the new `flat_key` parser case and the two `FLAT_KEY_PATTERN` agreement cases for `output_cost_per_video` and `input_cost_per_video`. Dropping `video` from `FLAT_KEY_PATTERN` fails the agreement test.

## Type

🚄 Infrastructure

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Nothing reads `OutputUnit::Video` for pricing yet; #51225 adds the Python cost paths and the rows

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: feat(vertex_ai): add vertex_ai/gemini-4-hydrogen from the Vertex pricing page
body:
## Summary

Adds `vertex_ai/gemini-4-hydrogen` (kind page). The Vertex pricing page https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing (now served at https://cloud.google.com/model-garden/pricing) gained a Gemini 4 Hydrogen row in its Gemini 4 Standard, Priority and Flex/Batch tables, and the google-models page lists it under "Generally available Gemini models". The rest of the page re-rendered with identical prices: 190 per-token cells across 29 existing vertex rows were compared against the catalog with 0 mismatches, so no other row changes.

## Row evidence

Pricing page, Gemini 4 Standard table: "Gemini 4 Hydrogen | Input (text, image, video, audio) | Global | $1.50 | $0.075 | $1.875 ***" and "Text output (response and reasoning) | Global | $7.50". Non-global cells are 1.1x ($1.65 input, $8.25 output), so `regional_endpoint_uplift_multiplier: 1.1` like the sibling Gemini 4 rows.

Priority table: "Gemini 4 Hydrogen | Input (text, image, video, audio) | Global | $2.70 | $0.135" and "Text output (response and reasoning) | Global | $13.50". Flex/Batch table: "Gemini 4 Hydrogen | Input (text, image, video, audio) | Global | $0.75 | $0.0375" and "Text output (response and reasoning) | Global | $3.75". Written as `_priority`, `_batches` and `_flex` fields. One input price covers text, image, video and audio, so `input_cost_per_audio_token` equals the text input price for each tier.

Model page https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/4-hydrogen: "Model ID gemini-4-hydrogen", "Context window 1,048,576", "Maximum output tokens 1,048,576", modalities Text input and output, Image, Audio and Video input only, "Thinking Supported", "Structured output Supported", "Function calling Supported", "URL context Supported", "Computer use Supported", "Gemini Live API Not supported", "Batch inference Supported", "Standard PayGo with Usage Tiers, Flex PayGo, Priority PayGo Supported", "Hydrogen supports implicit caching only (4,096-token minimum)" (`prompt_cache_min_tokens: 4096`), "Setting thinking_budget or thinking_level=\"MINIMAL\" returns an HTTP 400 validation error" (`supports_minimal_reasoning_effort: false`). [insert handwritten description here]

<details>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The portal lacks recent totals and customer billing PDFs.

How it solves it:

- Show customer-wide spend and tokens for the last 30 days.
- Download a branded invoice with model and daily usage.
- Remove the duplicate Chargebacks navigation item.

Intentional product change: Customer usage defaults to 30 inclusive dates. The date picker controls the invoice period. Monthly table figures keep their existing period.

Before, customers have monthly table totals and no invoice download.

1. Open `/customers` and see the monthly customer table.
2. See a separate Chargebacks navigation item.
3. Open `/customers?id=portal-rules-demo` without a PDF action.

After, the portal shows recent totals and downloads a customer invoice.

1. Open `/customers` and see 30-day Spend and Tokens above the table.
2. Use the customer portal menu without the duplicate Chargebacks item.
3. Open the same customer, choose dates, and click Generate invoice PDF.

![Portal after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/f9520c44d39bc9025358cd372a04e50fc902d022/proof/customer-billing/list-after.png)

Before captures the unchanged UI at `382588a365`. After captures `5cc98b29545830cb1262295ea1200e1f0a6c6c47`, whose tree matches tested local commit `c2d5ffead0`. Both use the same URLs and synthetic data on a local two-worker gateway with PostgreSQL and shared Redis. List screenshots use the same search text. The summary remains global when the list is filtered.

The native browser downloaded `litellm-usage-invoice-2026-10-14-2026-11-12.pdf` after clicking the button. The request returned HTTP 200, `application/pdf`, and `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

The downloaded document has two pages and exactly 30 daily rows. It includes all three serving model groups, 20,166 requests, 12,600,180 tokens, and $252.000081 of recorded usage. Both pages were rendered and visually checked.

The existing customer activity scope supplies all-key totals and serving model groups. ReportLab was already locked for development and is now included in the proxy extra. The PDF uses the existing packaged LiteLLM logo and shows recorded usage costs.

196 mapped backend tests passed. The 14 invoice cases passed again after final layout changes. 77 targeted UI tests, TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Knip, Ruff formatting, and the strict Ruff, type-discipline, test-quality, and OpenAPI gates passed.

title: fix(otel): report the provider model in experimental GenAI traces
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Fixes gen_ai.response.model to report the provider’s actual model instead of the client-facing alias
- Applies only with OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental
- Preserves legacy telemetry, response aliases and auto-router behavior
- Adds regression coverage for streaming, non-streaming and fallback cases

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Aliased requests hide the served model in experimental traces

How it solves it:

- Read the preserved provider model before falling back
- Keep legacy telemetry and client aliases unchanged

## User Flow

Before, experimental traces identify the alias as the responding model

1. Enable `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`
2. Send `POST http://localhost:4100/v1/chat/completions` using a configured model alias
3. Observe `gen_ai.response.model` containing the alias, with or without streaming

After, experimental traces identify the provider's responding model

1. Enable `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`
2. Send `POST http://localhost:4100/v1/chat/completions` using a configured model alias
3. Observe `gen_ai.response.model` containing the provider model, with or without streaming

The response body and `litellm.model_group` still contain the alias. Without the experimental setting, telemetry behavior stays unchanged

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51029

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] Affected tests pass on the exact candidate source in Devin
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR only solves one specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on the latest commit has finished and findings are addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Independent source verification used baseline `00bd56760d8aba58185dacc1adb29f985fe6769b` and candidate `1f0b6167713686c18e1050ec60a55976c49e2e07`, with two proxy workers sharing dedicated Redis

The direct-provider cases called OpenAI without transforming its response. A separately labeled controlled-upstream case forwarded real calls and replaced only the returned model name to distinguish the client alias, deployment and served name

<details>
<summary>Exact verification setup and client code</summary>

Setup used for both source revisions

Checkouts: baseline 00bd56760d8aba58185dacc1adb29f985fe6769b in ~/repos/litellm; candidate 1f0b6167713686c18e1050ec60a55976c49e2e07 in a worktree (`git worktree add --detach ~/repos/litellm-cand <SHA>`). One venv from the main checkout (`uv sync --inexact --frozen --extra proxy --group proxy-dev --group e2e-dev --reinstall-package litellm`); the prebuilt `litellm/rust_bridge/_native.abi3.so` is copied into the worktree because the branch touches no Rust. Candidate processes run from the worktree with `PYTHONPATH=$HOME/repos/litellm-cand` so it shadows the editable install (verified via `python -c "import litellm; print(litellm.__file__)"`).

Env var NAMES: OPENAI_API_KEY (real provider), LITELLM_MASTER_KEY (disposable local value), DATABASE_URL (disposable Postgres db litellm_qa_51029), LITELLM_LOG=DEBUG, OTEL_EXPORTER=otlp_http, OTEL_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4399, and for the experimental run only OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental. Gotcha: `callback_settings.otel` in the config is ignored by the legacy OpenTelemetry init at these SHAs (console exporter chosen), so the exporter is wired through OTEL_EXPORTER/OTEL_ENDPOINT.

Dedicated Redis (shared by both workers):
```
mkdir -p ~/qa/51029/redis && cd ~/qa/51029/redis && setsid nohup redis-server --port 6390 --bind 127.0.0.1 --dir ~/qa/51029/redis --save "" --appendonly no > ~/qa/51029/logs/redis_6390.log 2>&1 &
redis-cli -p 6390 ping   # PONG
```
OTLP sink (repo test fixture, records spans, GET /__spans?since=N):
```
cd ~/repos/litellm && PYTHONPATH=tests .venv/bin/python -P -m integration._support.otlp_sink --port 4399
```
Controlled-upstream shim (leg B only, NOT direct provider evidence; forwards to real api.openai.com, rewrites only the returned model; code below):
```
cd ~/repos/litellm && OPENAI_API_KEY=... .venv/bin/python ~/qa/51029/kit/shim.py 4311
```
Config ~/qa/51029/rig/config.yaml = copy of litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml with these deltas:
```yaml
model_list:   # appended
  - model_name: qa-alias-51029
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: qa-alias-vllm-51029
    litellm_params:
      model: hosted_vllm/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4311/v1
      api_key: shim-no-auth
general_settings:
  coordination_redis: {host: 127.0.0.1, port: 6390}
router_settings: {redis_host: 127.0.0.1, redis_port: 6390}
litellm_settings:
  callbacks: [..., otel]   # otel appended
callback_settings:
  otel: {exporter: http/json, endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:4399, use_simple_processor: true}   # ignored at these SHAs, see gotcha
```
Proxy, legacy mode (two worker PIDs served in every boot, no "workers flag is ignored" message):
```
cd ~/repos/litellm-cand && PYTHONPATH=$HOME/repos/litellm-cand LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... DATABASE_URL=... LITELLM_LOG=DEBUG \
  OTEL_EXPORTER=otlp_http OTEL_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4399 \
  ~/repos/litellm/.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/qa/51029/rig/config.yaml --port 4100 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee proxy_legacy.log
```
Experimental mode: same command plus OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental, tee to proxy_genai_latest.log. Baseline proxy: identical, run from ~/repos/litellm without PYTHONPATH. Between modes the proxy is stopped by the PIDs recorded from `pgrep -af "proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/qa/51029/rig/config.yaml"` (task-owned only).

Client driver (4 cases per mode: alias A then alias B, non-stream then stream; code below):
```
cd ~/repos/litellm && MODE=<label> OUT=<dir> PROXY_LOG=<proxy log> LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... \
  .venv/bin/python ~/qa/51029/kit/drive.py qa-alias-51029 qa-alias-vllm-51029
```
It writes cases_<MODE>_<stamp>.json with body model(s), response headers, the litellm_request span attributes matched by litellm.call_id, and the span's hidden_params keys.


Client driver saved as `~/qa/51029/kit/drive.py`

```python
"""Drive alias cases through a live proxy and read back OTel spans from the OTLP sink."""
import json, os, sys, time, uuid
import httpx

PROXY = os.environ.get("PROXY", "http://127.0.0.1:4100")
SINK = os.environ.get("SINK", "http://127.0.0.1:4399")
KEY = os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]
MODE = os.environ.get("MODE", "legacy")
OUT = os.environ.get("OUT", os.path.expanduser("~/qa/51029/artifacts"))
ATTRS = ["gen_ai.request.model", "gen_ai.response.model", "litellm.model_group", "litellm.provider.model",
         "gen_ai.system", "gen_ai.provider.name", "gen_ai.request.stream", "llm.is_streaming", "litellm.call_id"]
HDRS = ["x-litellm-call-id", "x-litellm-model-id", "x-litellm-model-group", "x-litellm-model-name",
        "x-litellm-response-model", "x-litellm-attempted-retries", "x-litellm-response-cost"]

def run(alias, stream):
    nonce = uuid.uuid4().hex
    body = {"model": alias, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Reply with the single word ok. nonce={nonce}"}]}
    if stream:
        body |= {"stream": True, "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}}
    with httpx.Client(timeout=120) as c:
        r = c.post(f"{PROXY}/v1/chat/completions", json=body, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"})
    headers = {k: r.headers.get(k) for k in HDRS if r.headers.get(k)}
    if stream:
        models, usage = set(), None
        for line in r.text.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]":
                d = json.loads(line[6:])
                if d.get("model"): models.add(d["model"])
                if d.get("usage"): usage = d["usage"]
        body_model = sorted(models)
    else:
        d = r.json(); body_model = d.get("model"); usage = d.get("usage")
    return {"status": r.status_code, "call_id": headers.get("x-litellm-call-id"), "headers": headers,
            "body_model": body_model, "usage": usage, "raw": r.text}

LOG = os.environ.get("PROXY_LOG")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(__file__))
from spans_from_log import spans as log_spans

def spans_for(call_ids, seconds=60):
    deadline = time.time() + seconds
    found = {}
    while time.time() < deadline:
        spans = httpx.get(f"{SINK}/__spans", params={"since": 0}, timeout=15).json()["spans"]
        if LOG:
            spans = spans + log_spans(LOG)
        for s in spans:
            a = s["attributes"]
            cid = a.get("litellm.call_id")
            if cid in call_ids and "gen_ai.response.model" in a:
                found[cid] = s
        if len(found) == len(call_ids):
            break
        time.sleep(1)
    return found

cases = [(alias, stream) for alias in sys.argv[1:] for stream in (False, True)]
results = {}
for alias, stream in cases:
    results[(alias, stream)] = run(alias, stream)
found = spans_for({r["call_id"] for r in results.values() if r["call_id"]})
report = []
for (alias, stream), r in results.items():
    s = found.get(r["call_id"])
    a = s["attributes"] if s else {}
    hp = a.get("hidden_params")
    hpd = json.loads(hp) if isinstance(hp, str) else (hp or {})
    row = {"mode": MODE, "alias": alias, "stream": stream, "status": r["status"], "call_id": r["call_id"],
           "headers": r["headers"], "body_model": r["body_model"], "usage": r["usage"],
           "span_name": s["name"] if s else None, "span_source": ("sink" if s and "trace_id" in s else "console-log") if s else None, "span": {k: a.get(k) for k in ATTRS},
           "hidden_params_keys": sorted(hpd.keys()), "hidden_params_litellm_model_name": hpd.get("litellm_model_name"),
           "hidden_params_provider_response_model": hpd.get("provider_response_model"),
           "all_attr_keys": sorted(a.keys())}
    report.append(row)
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in row.items() if k not in ("all_attr_keys",)}, indent=None))
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
stamp = time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
with open(f"{OUT}/cases_{MODE}_{stamp}.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"report": report, "raw": {f"{a}|{'stream' if s else 'nonstream'}": r["raw"] for (a, s), r in results.items()},
               "spans": {cid: sp for cid, sp in found.items()}}, f, indent=1)
print("wrote", f"{OUT}/cases_{MODE}_{stamp}.json")
```
spans_from_log.py (only used when the proxy was on the console exporter; every reported case has span_source=sink):
```python
"""Extract console-exported OTel spans (pretty JSON blocks) from a proxy log."""
import json, sys

def spans(path):
    out, buf = [], None
    for line in open(path, errors="replace"):
        if line == "{\n":
            buf = [line]
        elif buf is not None:
            buf.append(line)
            if line == "}\n":
                try:
                    out.append(json.loads("".join(buf)))
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    pass
                buf = None
    return out
```



Controlled upstream saved as `~/qa/51029/kit/shim.py`, started as `shim.py 4311`. Leg B supplement only, NOT direct provider evidence: it makes the real OpenAI call and rewrites only the returned `model` (vLLM served-model-name analogue) so alias, deployment and provider-returned names are three distinct values. Reads OPENAI_API_KEY from env; no secrets embedded.

```python
"""OpenAI-compatible forwarding shim: real upstream call, response `model` rewritten to a served name (vLLM served-model-name analogue)."""
import json, os, sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
import httpx

UPSTREAM = "https://api.openai.com"
SERVED = os.environ.get("SERVED_MODEL", "gpt-6.1-sol-served")
KEY = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
LOG = open(os.path.expanduser("~/qa/51029/logs/shim.log"), "a")

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        LOG.write("%s %s\n" % (self.address_string(), fmt % args)); LOG.flush()
    def do_POST(self):
        body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        LOG.write(f"upstream request model={body.get('model')!r} stream={body.get('stream')}\n"); LOG.flush()
        path = self.path if self.path.startswith("/v1/") else "/v1" + self.path
        with httpx.Client(timeout=120) as c, c.stream("POST", UPSTREAM + path, json=body, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"}) as r:
            self.send_response(r.status_code)
            ctype = r.headers.get("content-type", "application/json")
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            if body.get("stream") and r.status_code == 200:
                self.end_headers()
                for line in r.iter_lines():
                    if line.startswith("data: ") and line != "data: [DONE]":
                        d = json.loads(line[6:])
                        if "model" in d:
                            LOG.write(f"upstream chunk model={d['model']!r} -> {SERVED!r}\n")
                            d["model"] = SERVED
                        line = "data: " + json.dumps(d)
                    self.wfile.write((line + "\n").encode()); self.wfile.flush()
                LOG.flush()
                return
            data = b"".join(r.iter_bytes())
            if r.status_code == 200:
                d = json.loads(data)
                LOG.write(f"upstream response model={d.get('model')!r} -> {SERVED!r}\n"); LOG.flush()
                d["model"] = SERVED
                data = json.dumps(d).encode()
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(data))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(data)

ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
```
Direct leg A needs none of this: alias qa-alias-51029 -> openai/gpt-6.1-sol with api_key os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY, and OpenAI's returned model (gpt-6.1-sol, equal to the deployment) is reported untouched.




</details>

### Before, 00bd56760d8aba58185dacc1adb29f985fe6769b

1. Run the setup below without the experimental setting, then with `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`
2. Run the driver for streamed and non-streamed requests to each alias
3. All eight requests return HTTP 200. `gen_ai.response.model` equals the client alias in both modes

### After, 1f0b6167713686c18e1050ec60a55976c49e2e07

1. Run the same setup without the experimental setting, then with `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`
2. Run the same driver for streamed and non-streamed requests to each alias
3. All eight requests return HTTP 200. Experimental spans now report the provider model, while default spans keep the alias

| Mode | Upstream | Streaming | Baseline response model | Candidate response model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | Direct provider | Off and on | `qa-alias-51029` | `qa-alias-51029` |
| Experimental | Direct provider | Off and on | `qa-alias-51029` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| Default | Controlled forwarding shim | Off and on | `qa-alias-vllm-51029` | `qa-alias-vllm-51029` |
| Experimental | Controlled forwarding shim | Off and on | `qa-alias-vllm-51029` | `gpt-6.1-sol-served` |

In every case, the response body and `litellm.model_group` retain the client alias. `gen_ai.request.model` remains `gpt-6.1-sol`. The direct provider returned `gpt-6.1-sol` unchanged, and only the labeled shim replaced the returned model for the three-name comparison

### Regression tests and gates

The final mapped suite passed 2,300 tests. The focused selection passed all nine cases at the candidate. Running the same test file outside tracked source against the baseline produced four expected failures and five passes, proving the regression catches provider-model selection, streaming, deployment fallback and auto-router provider precedence

All 16 changed executable lines are covered, with both outcomes hit at all three changed-line branch points. The response-model helper has both outcomes covered at both branch points. Separately, the touched file has 85.7% line coverage and 77.2% branch coverage, not repository-wide coverage

Three relevant alias integration cases passed. The vertex billing assertion also fails on the baseline and is unrelated, so it was left unchanged

title: fix(proxy): refuse blocked and over-limit keys before reading the request body
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

fix the fact that repeated 429s with big image bodies OOM the proxy

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/aba5a28de37d4ff19161685399cf6012
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/aba5a28de37d4ff19161685399cf6012?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A client retrying 429s with multi-megabyte image bodies OOM-killed proxy pods (Pylon #11782, a customer on 1.108.4)
- Auth read and buffered the whole body before the rate limiter or the blocked-key check ran
- Each refused 5 MB request cost a full 5 MB buffer, 150 of them a second ate 8 GiB pods

How it solves it:

- Auth first looks the key up in its cache, from the headers alone
- A blocked key gets its 401, an exhausted key-level RPM or parallel limit its 429, before the body is read
- The limiter check is read-only, so admitted requests are still charged on the unchanged path
- Cache misses, JWTs, custom auth and non-LLM routes take the unchanged path

## User Flow

Before: a retry loop against a rate-limited key buffers every payload in full and the proxy pods run out of memory

1. The team's service sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a 5 MB base64 image using a key limited to 300 rpm
2. Past the limit, each retry gets `429 Rate limit exceeded for api_key` only after the proxy has read all 5 MB
3. Retrying without backoff at 150 requests a second, the pods climb to their 8 GiB limit and get OOM-killed
4. With most pods restarting, the requests under the limit fail too

After: the same retry loop gets its 429s from the headers and the pods stay flat

1. The team's service sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same key and 5 MB image
2. Past the limit, each retry gets the same `429 Rate limit exceeded for api_key` with its `retry-after` header right after the headers arrive, the body is never read
3. The flood keeps the pods at their idle memory and the requests under the limit keep being served
4. A key blocked through POST https://litellm-domain/key/block gets its 401 the same way, before the body

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. One proxy worker, one Anthropic deployment, Postgres for keys, no Redis (the limiter's in-memory counters, the customer's single-worker case). Env vars: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`.

<details>
<summary>config.yaml and proxy command</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-oom-repro-master-7f3a9c2e1b4d6e8f
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
litellm_settings:
  set_verbose: false
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port 4100 --num_workers 1
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>early_reject.py, the headers-only probe (creates a key with rpm_limit 1 and max_parallel_requests 1, trips it, then sends the headers plus 1 KB of a declared 5 MB body over a raw socket)</summary>

```python
import socket, sys, time
import httpx
url, master, port = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
with httpx.Client(timeout=60) as c:
    key = c.post(f"{url}/key/generate", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {master}"},
                 json={"rpm_limit": 1, "max_parallel_requests": 1, "models": ["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]}).json()["key"]
    hdrs = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}
    small = {"model": "anthropic-haiku-4-5", "max_tokens": 5, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}
    r1 = c.post(f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", headers=hdrs, json=small)
    r2 = c.post(f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", headers=hdrs, json=small)
    print("warm-up:", r1.status_code, "then", r2.status_code, r2.text[:120])
total = 5 * 1024 * 1024
s = socket.create_connection(("localhost", port))
s.sendall((f"POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nAuthorization: Bearer {key}\r\n"
           f"Content-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {total}\r\n\r\n").encode())
s.sendall(b'{"model": "anthropic-haiku-4-5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "' + b"A" * 900)
s.settimeout(4)
t = time.time()
try:
    data = s.recv(4096)
    print(f"RESPONSE after {time.time()-t:.2f}s with only 1 KB of {total:,} body bytes sent:", data.split(b"\r\n")[0])
except socket.timeout:
    print(f"NO RESPONSE within 4s: proxy is waiting for the remaining {total-980:,} body bytes before answering")
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>flood.py, the retry flood (same key shape, 100 concurrent clients re-sending a 5 MB base64 image body for 30 s, worker RSS sampled from /proc every 2 s)</summary>

```python
import asyncio, base64, json, os, subprocess, sys, time
import httpx

url, master, seconds, conc, mb = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4]), float(sys.argv[5])

def worker_pids():
    out = subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-f", "proxy_cli"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
    return [int(p) for p in out]

def rss_mb(pid):
    try:
        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/status") as f:
            for line in f:
                if line.startswith("VmRSS"):
                    return int(line.split()[1]) / 1024
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 0.0
    return 0.0

async def main():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60) as c:
        r = await c.post(f"{url}/key/generate", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {master}"},
                         json={"rpm_limit": 1, "max_parallel_requests": 1, "models": ["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]})
        key = r.json()["key"]
        image = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(int(mb * 1024 * 1024 * 3 / 4))).decode()
        body = json.dumps({"model": "anthropic-haiku-4-5", "max_tokens": 5, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "what is this"},
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{image}"}}]}]}).encode()
        print(f"body bytes={len(body):,} key={key[:12]}...")
        hdrs = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
        pids = worker_pids()
        print("pids", pids, "rss before MB", [round(rss_mb(p)) for p in pids])
        counts = {}
        lat = []
        stop = time.time() + seconds
        peak = 0.0
        async def one():
            while time.time() < stop:
                t = time.time()
                try:
                    resp = await c.post(f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", headers=hdrs, content=body)
                    counts[resp.status_code] = counts.get(resp.status_code, 0) + 1
                except Exception as e:
                    counts[type(e).__name__] = counts.get(type(e).__name__, 0) + 1
                lat.append(time.time() - t)
        async def sample():
            nonlocal peak
            while time.time() < stop:
                total = sum(rss_mb(p) for p in pids)
                peak = max(peak, total)
                print(f"t+{seconds - (stop - time.time()):4.0f}s rss MB={total:7.0f} done={sum(counts.values())} {counts}", flush=True)
                await asyncio.sleep(2)
        await asyncio.gather(sample(), *[one() for _ in range(conc)])
        print(f"PEAK rss MB={peak:.0f} responses={counts} mean latency={sum(lat)/max(1,len(lat)):.2f}s")
asyncio.run(main())
```

</details>

### Before (b60df93c46)

#### Headers-only probe

1. `python early_reject.py http://localhost:4100 $MASTER_KEY 4100`
2. Output: `warm-up: 200 then 429 {"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded for api_key: 974d0e04...` then `NO RESPONSE within 4s: proxy is waiting for the remaining 5,241,900 body bytes before answering`

#### Retry flood

1. `python flood.py http://localhost:4100 $MASTER_KEY 30 100 5`
2. Worker RSS went from 790 MB to a 2860 MB peak while answering 728 x 429 in 30 s, mean latency 4.33 s per refused request

<details>
<summary>flood output</summary>

```
body bytes=5,243,087 key=sk-s_5xs_DcE...
pids [27473, 27477] rss before MB [2, 788]
t+   0s rss MB=    790 done=0 {}
t+   2s rss MB=   1378 done=20 {429: 20}
t+   4s rss MB=   1699 done=81 {429: 80, 400: 1}
t+   6s rss MB=   1895 done=146 {429: 145, 400: 1}
t+   8s rss MB=   1994 done=207 {429: 206, 400: 1}
t+  10s rss MB=   2054 done=251 {429: 250, 400: 1}
t+  12s rss MB=   2249 done=281 {429: 280, 400: 1}
t+  14s rss MB=   2334 done=314 {429: 313, 400: 1}
t+  16s rss MB=   2375 done=346 {429: 345, 400: 1}
t+  18s rss MB=   2397 done=373 {429: 372, 400: 1}
t+  20s rss MB=   2453 done=403 {429: 402, 400: 1}
t+  22s rss MB=   2608 done=454 {429: 453, 400: 1}
t+  24s rss MB=   2738 done=516 {429: 515, 400: 1}
t+  26s rss MB=   2845 done=556 {429: 555, 400: 1}
t+  28s rss MB=   2860 done=587 {429: 586, 400: 1}
PEAK rss MB=2860 responses={429: 728, 400: 1} mean latency=4.33s
```

The single 400 is the one admitted request, Anthropic rejecting the random bytes as an image.

</details>

### After (9362e554fb, the later commits 4cd8104f72 and e48960788b only change which header the key is read from and how that setting is read)

#### Headers-only probe

1. `python early_reject.py http://localhost:4100 $MASTER_KEY 4100`
2. Output: `warm-up: 200 then 429 {"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded for api_key: 94cabbcf...` then `RESPONSE after 0.01s with only 1 KB of 5,242,880 body bytes sent: b'HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests'`

#### Retry flood

1. `python flood.py http://localhost:4100 $MASTER_KEY 30 100 5`
2. Worker RSS went from 880 MB to a 1197 MB peak while answering 3282 x 429 in 30 s, mean latency 0.93 s per refused request (the time to upload 5 MB that the proxy now discards without buffering). The same flood on 15aa3eef74, the first revision, held at 1087 to 1110 MB with 4794 refusals

<details>
<summary>flood output</summary>

```
body bytes=5,243,087 key=sk-RywmHNqLt...
pids [62658, 62666, 62668] rss before MB [4, 2, 874]
t+   0s rss MB=    880 done=0 {}
t+   2s rss MB=   1180 done=63 {429: 62, 400: 1}
t+   4s rss MB=   1183 done=312 {429: 311, 400: 1}
t+   6s rss MB=   1183 done=501 {429: 500, 400: 1}
t+   8s rss MB=   1185 done=720 {429: 719, 400: 1}
t+  10s rss MB=   1185 done=971 {429: 970, 400: 1}
t+  12s rss MB=   1187 done=1232 {429: 1231, 400: 1}
t+  14s rss MB=   1191 done=1428 {429: 1427, 400: 1}
t+  16s rss MB=   1192 done=1591 {429: 1590, 400: 1}
t+  18s rss MB=   1192 done=1892 {429: 1891, 400: 1}
t+  20s rss MB=   1193 done=2208 {429: 2207, 400: 1}
t+  22s rss MB=   1193 done=2400 {429: 2399, 400: 1}

t+  26s rss MB=   1197 done=2841 {429: 2840, 400: 1}
t+  28s rss MB=   1197 done=3025 {429: 3024, 400: 1}
PEAK rss MB=1197 responses={429: 3282, 400: 1} mean latency=0.93s
```

</details>

#### Tests

1. `tests/integration/authorization/test_reject_before_body.py` sends the headers and 1 KB of a declared 8 MB body over a raw socket and reads the status through the same socket. On b60df93c46 both cases time out waiting for a response (the proxy is waiting for the body), on 9362e554fb both pass (429 for a key with `rpm_limit: 1`, 401 for a key blocked through `/key/block`). Run through the integration harness (management group) against the scripted upstream.
2. `tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_user_api_key_auth_request_flow.py`, two tests whose request `receive` raises if the body is ever read: a cached key past its rpm limit gets a 429 with `rate_limited_by: api_key`, a cached blocked key gets its 401, and both record the failure through `post_call_failure_hook`.
3. `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_parallel_request_limiter_v3.py`, two tests: the headers-only check refuses an exhausted key without incrementing its counter, and skips per-model limits that need the body.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Only key-level, user, team, org and tag-free limits can be refused early. Per-model limits still need the body
- The early 429 does not count toward the window, so a flood no longer starves the key's own admitted requests. Admitted requests are charged as before
- Only the `Authorization` header is checked early. Keys sent through `x-api-key` or custom headers take the unchanged path

### Low

- The early refusal needs the key in the auth cache, so the first request from a cold key always reads its body. Retry floods hit warm keys
- Non-Redis proof above. With Redis the read-only check does one batched read of the key's counters per refused request, the same read the normal path already does

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes ordering on the hot authentication path for LLM routes and adds an early rate-limit branch, but only when the key is already cached and limits are header-evaluable.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stops the proxy from buffering large request bodies when the caller’s API key can already be rejected from headers alone—addressing OOM from clients retrying 429s with multi‑MB payloads.
> 
> **Auth** now runs `_reject_from_headers_before_reading_body` on LLM routes *before* parsing the body: it resolves the bearer token, loads a **cache-only** key record, returns **401** for blocked keys, and delegates to the v3 parallel/rate limiter for an early **429** when key-level (non–model-specific) limits are exhausted. Cache misses and non-v3 limiters keep the existing full auth path.
> 
> **Limiter** adds `raise_if_over_limit_before_body`, which builds descriptors with an empty body and calls `should_rate_limit` in **read-only** mode so refused floods do not increment counters; admitted requests are still charged in `async_pre_call_hook`.
> 
> Integration tests use a raw socket with a partial body; unit tests assert the body `receive` is never called on early refusal.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e48960788bc8d6f5dbf36fe4f7cc65c7105fd5b8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
