title: feat(github_copilot): support GitHub App authentication with PEM upload
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

This adds GitHub App authentication to the GitHub Copilot provider so production applications can connect without a user login. Administrators upload the App’s PEM key in the dashboard, where LiteLLM stores it encrypted and automatically refreshes installation tokens. Each application can use its own App credential for separate routing, usage tracking, and gateway limits.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Copilot service applications cannot authenticate with GitHub App installations.

How it solves it:

- Adds GitHub App to the existing Copilot credential form.
- Uploads PEM files through existing encrypted credential storage.
- Refreshes installation tokens and separates App credentials across deployments.

Intentional product change: Administrators can choose GitHub App and upload its PEM. Existing authentication modes remain available. The new UI needs neither container PEM mounts nor an Enterprise secret-manager integration.

### Design

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

The UI reuses the provider file-upload control used by Vertex AI service-account JSON. The existing credential API encrypts the PEM before database persistence and masks readback. Only proxy administrators can write the App fields. The UI offers PEM upload only and preserves a masked saved key on edit. Replacing the uploaded file rotates it.

The API validates an unencrypted RSA key of at least 2048 bits, up to 16 KiB. Signing keys are retrieved from named credentials only at authentication time and excluded from both credential-to-model-kwargs paths. They are not sent upstream as model parameters. Errors do not echo private-key contents. Production requires HTTPS and a protected, stable proxy encryption key. The running proxy must be trusted because it holds decrypted credentials in memory.

The provider signs short-lived JWTs and requests only `organization_copilot_requests: read`. Installation tokens stay in bounded process-local caches, refresh two minutes before expiry, and coordinate concurrent refreshes within each worker. Cache identity includes the App, installation, host, credential name or reference, and uploaded key contents, and a cached token is served without reading a referenced secret again. Token requests run off the shared thread pool and finish even when the caller that started them is cancelled. Refresh failures fail closed, with bounded retry cooldowns and sanitized errors. Token requests follow litellm's `ssl_verify` settings and do not follow redirects.

Existing routing, cooldown, monitoring, and credential ownership controls apply. A Copilot deployment that names a credential that is not loaded keeps the shared device login fallback it has on base, and one that also sets `github_copilot_auth_type: github_app` answers 400 and reports unhealthy on `/health` instead. When GitHub rejects the App installation token request, the call answers 401, the router cools the deployment down, and Prometheus counts a deployment failure. App deployments report the App endpoint as their `api_base` in response headers, spend logs, and metrics, and per-user sessions keep reporting the deployment's configured `api_base` as on base. Caller bearer/integration headers are replaced with the resolved App identity, and device-login requests keep their existing header handling. App requests use the shared response cache like other deployments. YAML and SDK callers can still use server-side secret references. Separate App deployments support distinct LiteLLM budgets and limits, but do not guarantee independent GitHub organization quotas.

</details>

## User Flow

Before, an administrator cannot create an App-authenticated Copilot connection.

1. Open `/models-and-endpoints`, select LLM Credentials, then Add Credential.
2. Select Github Copilot and open Auth Type.
3. Only Shared device login and Per-user GitHub OAuth appear.

![Before, Copilot authentication choices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giladk1221/litellm-docs/d053191a5c08e08d506f5014d22429152aabaa01/img/github-copilot-app-before.jpg)

After, an administrator can connect a service through a GitHub App.

1. Open `/models-and-endpoints`, select LLM Credentials, then Add Credential.
2. Select Github Copilot and choose GitHub App under Auth Type.
3. Enter the App client ID and installation ID, upload the PEM, then save.
4. Add a model with that credential. Requests succeed without personal GitHub login.

![After, PEM upload and field information icons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giladk1221/litellm-docs/d053191a5c08e08d506f5014d22429152aabaa01/img/github-copilot-app-after.jpg)

![Saved deployment using the uploaded credential](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/giladk1221/litellm-docs/d053191a5c08e08d506f5014d22429152aabaa01/img/github-copilot-app-model.jpg)

## Relevant issues

[Companion documentation PR](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/2969) covers dashboard upload, API, SDK configuration, key rotation, and separate application credentials. Merge it after the feature.

[GitHub server-to-server authentication](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-sdk/auth/server-to-server-tokens) defines the installation-token flow. [GitHub SDK multi-tenancy](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/copilot/how-tos/copilot-sdk/setup/multi-tenancy) documents the `copilot-developer-cli` integration ID used by App requests.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The focused test files covering my change pass locally
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

Required CI and the Bugbot and Greptile reviews at d58f62bc5e passed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Last updated: d58f62bc5e. QA ran on 3058f0a57f. Changes since QA are the review fixes in the rounds below, each run again live, and the five App and five device-login endpoints passed again on 6380fa164d

QA ran on 3058f0a57f (After) against the merge base 40981a5d89 (Before) with real GitHub Copilot calls and no mocks. Each leg ran two proxy instances with two workers each on one Postgres, alternating requests. App cases use a real GitHub App (Copilot Requests read only) on a Copilot Business test organization, with no device-login token on any proxy. Device-login cases use a real Copilot Free token

| Case | Before 40981a5d89 | After 3058f0a57f |
|---|---|---|
| UI Auth Type choices | No GitHub App | GitHub App listed |
| UI saves App credential and model | Not possible | Saved, chat works |
| Chat, App credential | Device-login error | `pong` |
| Chat stream, App credential | Device-login error | `1, 2, 3, 4, 5` |
| `/v1/messages`, App credential | Device-login error | `pong` |
| `/v1/responses`, App credential | Device-login error | `completed`, `pong` |
| Embeddings, App credential | Device-login error | 1536 dims |
| `/health`, App deployment | Unhealthy | Healthy |
| Body sets installation ID | Device-login error | 401, server-owned |
| Body sets private key ref | Device-login error | 401, server-owned |
| Body overrides credential name | Device-login error | 400 |
| PEM in credential readback | Masked | Masked |
| Device login, five endpoints | All pass | All pass |

### Headline case, Admin UI

Before, Add Credential with Github Copilot offers only Shared device login and Per-user GitHub OAuth

![Before, Copilot Auth Type choices](https://github.com/mateo-berri/qa-screenshots/releases/download/assets-8/pr51427-3058f0a57f-base_authtypes.png)

After, GitHub App is offered, and the credential saves with the uploaded PEM

Steps on the dashboard dev server (`npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`, pointed at the proxy)

1. Open http://localhost:3000/models-and-endpoints, click LLM Credentials, then Add Credential
2. Set Credential Name to `copilot-app-ui`, pick Github Copilot as Provider, then pick GitHub App under Auth Type
3. Fill App client ID and Installation ID, click Click to Upload and pick the App's `.pem` file, then click Add Credential
4. Open Add Model, pick Github Copilot and `github_copilot/gpt-4.1`, set Public Model Name to `copilot-app-ui-chat`, pick `copilot-app-ui` under Existing Credentials, then click Add Model
5. Call `copilot-app-ui-chat` on each instance with the commands below

- None found. A per-user session reports the deployment's configured `api_base` again, as on base, and App deployments still report the App host

- `github_copilot_app_id` now also accepts an integer, a widening that keeps every string value working

- `get_api_base` consumers, the `x-litellm-model-api-base` header and the spend log `api_base`: verified live at 6380fa164d, both name the App host for an App model saved with an `api_base` and for streamed and plain App chat

- Only `copilot-developer-cli` integration ID works with App tokens

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Medium

- An unloaded credential falls back to device login as on base, unless the deployment sets `github_copilot_auth_type: github_app`. Dashboard App models do not set it
- An App deployment ignores its configured `api_base`
- An App deployment with an invalid credential answers 400 without failover or cooldown

### Low

- A cached App token outlives an early revocation until near expiry. A rolling restart clears it
- An inline App key in YAML or SDK params answers 400, first seen at request time
- GHE.com, Claude through an App and the Prometheus fallback did not run live
- The Rust router keeps every server-owned `*_ref` pointer unresolved, Anthropic WIF ones too, like the Python loader

<details><summary>Decisions</summary>

A Copilot deployment that names a credential that is not loaded keeps the fallback to the shared device login it has on base, because refusing it turned working base configs from 200 into 400. A deployment that sets `github_copilot_auth_type: github_app` is the fail-closed choice and answers 400 with no upstream call. Refusing at attach time was rejected because it also turned a caller's credential override on a shared device deployment from 200 into 400. Raising an authentication error for that 400 was rejected because it cools the deployment down and hides the misconfiguration behind a 429

When GitHub rejects the installation token request with 401, 403 or 404, the provider raises `DeploymentCredentialAuthenticationError`, a subclass of `AuthenticationError`, so callers and the router see the same 401 and cooldown and Prometheus counts a deployment failure. Counting every pre-call `AuthenticationError` was rejected because it would also count callers' invalid LiteLLM keys

An App private key on a deployment must come from a stored credential, which is encrypted, or a secret reference, so an inline key answers 400 at request time. Checking it at config load was rejected because it would need a startup validation path for one provider

An App deployment sends requests to, and reports, the Copilot endpoint of its App host, so the installation token only ever goes to that host. Honoring a configured `api_base` was rejected because it would send the token wherever that value points. Per-user sessions already ignore a configured `api_base` for their calls the same way

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [x] Focused tests cover the implemented behavior and identified edge cases.
- [x] Required CI and automated reviews are complete.
- [x] 6380fa164d passes /live-pr-risk

> Adds **GitHub App** as a server-owned GitHub Copilot auth mode: admins configure App ID, installation ID, and PEM (upload or secret ref); the proxy mints and caches installation tokens and attaches them as an internal session.

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Duplicate of #51421, which already contains the same backend and UI implementation.

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customers cannot configure model allowances or their own backups.

How it solves it:

- Add customer-wide and per-model TPM/RPM in customer forms.
- Store ordered customer fallbacks and enforce target access/limits.
- Support K/M/B input and restore obvious list navigation.

Intentional product change: customer forms gain collapsed Rate limits and Fallbacks sections. Customer rules replace inherited fallback chains when configured; leaving gateway defaults enabled preserves inheritance.

## User Flow

Before, the customer form has no controls for model allowances or fallback rules.

1. Open `/ui/customers?id=portal-rules-demo` and click Edit.
2. The dialog only offers alias and budget fields.

![Before customer settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e074f426806abc173f9444899501244aa46090a8/.github/pr-proof/customer-rules/customer-edit-before.png)

After, the same customer can have shared allowances and an ordered fallback chain.

1. Open `/ui/customers?id=portal-rules-demo` and click Edit.
2. Expand Rate limits and enter customer-wide or model limits. Typing `100K` shows `= 100,000` immediately.
3. Expand Fallbacks, choose a primary and ordered backups, then Save. Reopening Edit preserves their order.
4. Use Back to customers at the top, or browser Back, to return to the list.

![Customer rate limits and shorthand preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e074f426806abc173f9444899501244aa46090a8/.github/pr-proof/customer-rules/customer-edit-limits-after.png)

![Ordered customer fallback chain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e074f426806abc173f9444899501244aa46090a8/.github/pr-proof/customer-rules/customer-edit-fallbacks-after.png)

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Before uses main `b60df93c46`. After uses the UI shipped in `0bf2b9015786436d520c93fc5d18b76700f48592`. Both captures use the same customer route, synthetic data and 1280×1000 viewport. The later backend type-boundary edits and test-fixture updates leave the captured UI unchanged.

The native browser flow created a customer, saved customer-wide and per-model limits, saved a customer-specific fallback, and reopened Edit to add and persist a second backup. Screenshots above show the resulting controls. The final backend also served requests through separate service keys with the same customer ID and returned `x-litellm-fallback-reason: rate_limit:model_per_end_user` when using the customer's backup.

The wire-level routing cases in `tests/integration/routing/test_customer_fallbacks.py` start a fresh two-worker proxy and controlled HTTP upstream. They verify shared model allowances across three keys, customer isolation, inheritance/disable/clear behavior, client override rejection, target authorization, and target/customer-wide limits. This uses synthetic inference, not a real provider.

## Validation

- 737 standard auth tests, 44 focused customer/auth tests, 12 two-worker integration cases, and 4 router-settings fixture cases passed.
- 42 UI tests passed. Dashboard typecheck, scoped ESLint, Prettier and lint budgets passed.
- API types and lazy OpenAPI snapshot were regenerated and checked.

title: feat(customer): configure shared limits and customer fallback chains
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

- Allow setting TPM/RPM per model group for customers on gateway 
- Allow setting fallbacks per customer on the gateway

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customers need shared model limits and their own fallback order.

How it solves it:

- Save customer limits and regular fallback rules in the portal.
- Resolve trusted settings once for quota handling and dispatch.
- Use the existing override merger for Router-only arguments.

Intentional product change: Create and Edit use collapsed Rate limits and Fallbacks sections with aligned shadcn controls, live K/M/B previews, and editable fallback order. Customer details include Back to customers.

## User Flow

Before, an admin can enter overall limits but cannot configure customer fallback rules.

1. Open `/ui/customers` and click Create customer.
2. See plain TPM/RPM inputs without model limits or customer fallbacks.

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/c2e8eb5509f186e5c1f365df2ef2bc7f602921a3/.github/pr-proof/customer-settings/customer-create-before-annotated.png)

After, an admin can configure the customer's shared allowance and fallback order together.

1. Open `/ui/customers` and click Create customer.
2. Expand Rate limits and set overall or model-group TPM/RPM.
3. Type `100K` and see `= 100,000` immediately.
4. Expand Fallbacks and choose the customer's regular fallback order.
5. Save, open the customer, and use Back to customers.

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/c2e8eb5509f186e5c1f365df2ef2bc7f602921a3/.github/pr-proof/customer-settings/customer-create-after-annotated.png)

![Large-number preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/c2e8eb5509f186e5c1f365df2ef2bc7f602921a3/.github/pr-proof/customer-settings/desktop-rate-limits-preview.png)

![Ordered fallback editor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/c2e8eb5509f186e5c1f365df2ef2bc7f602921a3/.github/pr-proof/customer-settings/desktop-fallbacks-connected.png)

The empty forms use the same URL and viewport. Red rectangles mark the changed controls. The desktop images show unsaved editor drafts. Backend review fixes do not change this UI.

## Backend behavior

Admins save nullable `fallbacks` through `/customer/new` or `/customer/update`. Omitted updates preserve the value. Null inherits existing policy, an empty list disables regular fallbacks, and a configured list replaces the customer's regular chain. Context-window and content-policy rules retain their independent inheritance.

`ProxyConfig` resolves customer, key, and team settings into a typed internal value. Quota handling and dispatch share that value, with gateway defaults retained on the Router. Authentication checks a read-only view of client options. The existing override merger enforces trusted precedence and filters Router-only fields from direct calls. There are no auth-body sentinel writes, final customer reinjection, or new inference payload parameters.

Fallback target access, budgets, and rate limits still apply. Client rules cannot replace the saved customer regular chain. Validation rejects duplicate targets, self references, and cycles.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The original native-UI proof created a synthetic customer with overall TPM 10,000 and RPM 20, primary TPM 2,000 and RPM 1, and primary-to-reserve fallback. Three service keys sent the same trusted customer id. Captured Assistant/API/Background results were primary 200, reserve 200, and reserve 200. The fallback reason was `rate_limit:model_per_end_user`. An overall-limited customer returned 200 followed by 429 with `rate_limited_by: end_user`. Native Edit saved new limits while retaining the fallback.

### Before review fixes, c2e8eb55

A saved regular customer chain replaced separate context-window and content-policy chains. Live ordinary, context, and content failures all returned 200 from the customer backup.

### After review fixes, 9222d325a4078b8ec6a644830a63ab553e88b660

The same live configuration, requests, two workers, shared Redis, PostgreSQL, and controlled OpenAI-compatible TCP upstream now produce:

| Failure | Before serving group | After serving group | HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary | Customer backup | Customer backup | 200 |
| Context window | Customer backup | Context backup | 200 |
| Content policy | Customer backup | Content backup | 200 |

Captured upstream calls confirm primary followed by the selected target. No routing-control fields reached that upstream. This uses synthetic data and a controlled provider, with no paid provider calls.

Six direct-call and per-kind regressions fail against `c2e8eb55` and pass after the fix. Direct-call regressions use real HTTP transport to a controlled provider and verify that the original provider failure is preserved instead of starting the SDK's incompatible fallback path. Direct native-proxy pass-through validation remains unverified because that configuration rejects the unknown model before dispatch.

The live HTTP suite is `tests/integration/routing/test_customer_fallbacks.py`. It owns its two-worker proxy, model configuration, customers, keys, controlled upstream, and cleanup. It covers shared quotas, customer isolation, target access and limits, inheritance, disable/clear behavior, per-kind chains, ignored overridden client rules, and custom-router rejection.

Actual focused commands, with harness credentials supplied through protected environment variables:

```bash
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/integration/routing/test_customer_fallbacks.py -q
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/proxy/test_route_llm_request.py tests/unit/proxy/common_utils/test_customer_fallbacks.py -q
```

## Validation

462 focused backend and UI tests pass across routing, quota/hierarchy, schema/cache, and fallback access/budget guards. All 20 live HTTP cases pass. CI coverage ownership checks pass. Whole-tree Ruff, scoped formatting, strict-rule, type-discipline, test-quality, and the whole-tree typing delta gate pass. API generation produces no schema changes. The update has no merge conflicts with main.

Merged main at `8ba416ab` in `e3afee94`. The customer-detail resolution retains daily usage, Back navigation, and saved rules. Seven UI integration tests and the full dashboard typecheck pass. The policy resolver and its four other production files are unchanged by this merge, verified against `9222d325`, where the whole-tree typing delta gate passed.

The repo-wide Black run was stopped after rewriting unrelated files. All formatter churn was restored. Canonical Ruff formatting passes for changed production files. CI and automated reviews for the updated tip are pending. The previous tip's Python, UI, and API-type jobs passed; its code-quality job failed while checking out the separate documentation repository.


Coverage follow-up at `fae9497e` adds twelve behavioral regression cases for fallback persistence, explicit clearing, customer policy loading and cache isolation, ignored client overrides, denied-target skipping, overall limits, and requests without a Router or principal. Local coverage records all 118 executable changed Python lines, 100%, with no missing patch lines. The two-path auth regression also fails when the saved-policy assignment is removed in memory. The wider checks found and corrected an outdated restricted-customer registry expectation. No production code, exclusions, or coverage thresholds changed. Repository test lint and quality checks pass. Codecov will recalculate from CI on this tip.

## Caveats

### Medium

- Budget and customer updates use separate existing API calls.
- Shared budget edits affect their linked entities.
- Fallback attempts consume RPM under existing accounting behavior.
- Customer policies reject custom `user_config` routers without target guards.

</details>

title: feat(alerts): add management controls and opt-in daily summaries
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

connect performance alerts to slack/email and make ui more intuitive

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Deprecation alerts have no gateway-wide off switch.
- Performance alerts cannot send email or Slack summaries.

How it solves it:

- Adds Manage alerts with admin-only controls for both categories.
- Adds separate, opt-in daily performance email and Slack summaries.
- Reuses existing connections and database delivery receipts.

Intentional product change: Manage alerts replaces the page switch. Both UI categories default on. Existing deprecation delivery choices stay unchanged. New performance delivery requires opting in separately for email and Slack. Email setup now explains both categories.

## User Flow

Before, admins can switch performance monitoring off but cannot manage deprecations or receive performance summaries.

1. Open `/ui/alerts` as a gateway admin.
2. See a performance switch and its free-alert counter.
3. Open Set up email reminders. It only describes model deprecations.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/143e5b22-f9dd-4681-881d-b1d1916b09f6)

After, admins manage both categories and choose which notifications to receive.

1. Open `/ui/alerts` as a gateway admin.
2. Open Manage alerts to control performance monitoring and model deprecations.
3. Open Set up email reminders for both categories, then enable the desired email events in Email Settings.
4. For Slack summaries, enable Performance Alerts on the existing Slack connection.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba95fbd4-1ef9-4bed-96a7-4615071a22c8)

![Manage alerts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9a232df-19fc-4d35-85b4-21f039824478)

![Email setup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c656b012-069a-4d15-9ccb-449b388da1b0)

## Delivery behavior

Performance summaries contain up to five new open findings and a link to all alerts. A destination reserves its daily slot before sending, allowing at most one attempt per 24 hours. Empty checks do not consume that slot. Email goes to gateway admins, not team members or view-only admins. Failed sends retain their cursor and retry the next day. This also prevents an uncertain delivery after a worker crash from being retried immediately. Separate destinations have independent receipts, so a failed webhook does not resend successful email deliveries.

The first summary only includes findings from the preceding day. Delivery reads five compact alert records and pages admin recipients in groups of 100. It does not rescan usage aggregates. The existing detector, thresholds, cadence and serving-worker arrangement stay unchanged. The notification job checks every five minutes and uses the existing database for coordination across workers. Exhausting the free allowance still allows delivery of the final saved findings.

The global deprecation switch also stops the existing email and Slack retirement reminders. Email deprecations remain opt-in, and the existing default Slack event selection is unchanged. The free counter is lifetime generated alerts, including resolved and dismissed ones.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The focused test files pass locally
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] This PR only covers alert controls and notification delivery
- [x] Automated reviews on the latest commit are complete and addressed

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Tested `88a4aed16c4`. Before screenshots use the frontend from `b60df93c465`, against the same isolated QA backend and the same three synthetic alert records. After screenshots use 33dafa5d0d1. The follow-up only changes delivery and tests, so the displayed UI is identical at this tip. Images are attached to the PR, not committed to the repository.

### Shared setup

Use an isolated PostgreSQL database and Redis on localhost port 56548. Load `DATABASE_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` through your environment. The demo uses the local `UI_USERNAME` and `UI_PASSWORD` environment variables. No provider calls are needed for this feature.

<details>
<summary>Proxy and dashboard commands</summary>

The QA configuration was:

```yaml
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 56548
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  store_model_in_db: true
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 56548
```

```sh
PYTHONPATH=.:litellm/enterprise .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config qa.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 54248 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver

cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54248 npm run dev -- --port 55249 --hostname 127.0.0.1
```

The proxy reported two serving workers. Open `http://localhost:55249/alerts` for next dev. The deployed static dashboard uses `/ui/alerts`.

</details>

### Before, b60df93c465

1. Open the Alerts page with the three demo findings. Only the performance switch is present, as pictured above.
2. Open Set up email reminders. The instructions cover model deprecations only.

### After, 88a4aed16c4

1. Open the same page. Manage alerts is beside the title and the plan note is below it.
2. Disable model deprecations, reload and reopen the dialog. The preference remains off. Restore it to on.
3. Set up email reminders now explains separate opt-ins, recipients and timing for both categories.
4. Against local SMTP and webhook receivers, connect both channels without opting in. Observe zero messages.
5. Opt in and run two concurrent senders. Observe one admin email and one Slack summary. View-only and internal users receive no email.
6. Run again immediately. Observe no additional messages. Both messages link to the Alerts page.

Local results were 127 focused backend tests, 33 UI tests, four real PostgreSQL delivery tests and two live proxy preference cases. The database cases cover concurrent and restarted workers, failed deliveries, five-item summaries and historical-alert exclusion after a failed first send, next-day retries after a crash, and new findings after an empty check. Python lint and type gates, dashboard lint and API generation, and outgoing secret scans pass. Four notification tests also pass on Python 3.10. The new job-delivery regression fails there with the original timeout wrapper.

<details>
<summary>Local SMTP, webhook and API proof script</summary>

Save as `delivery_proof.py`. With the proxy running and at least one new open performance alert, run:

```sh
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python aiosmtpd==1.4.6
PYTHONPATH=.:litellm/enterprise .venv/bin/python delivery_proof.py
```

The receivers bind only to localhost and send no external notifications.

```python
import asyncio
import hashlib
import json
import os
import threading
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from email import policy
from email.parser import BytesParser
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

from aiosmtpd.controller import Controller
import httpx
import psycopg

os.environ.update(SMTP_HOST='127.0.0.1', SMTP_PORT='54359', SMTP_TLS='False', SMTP_USE_SSL='False', SMTP_SENDER_EMAIL='alerts@example.com', PROXY_BASE_URL='http://localhost:55249')
for key in ('SMTP_USERNAME', 'SMTP_PASSWORD'):
    os.environ.pop(key, None)

from litellm.integrations.performance_alert_notifications import PerformanceAlertNotifier
from litellm.integrations.SlackAlerting.slack_alerting import SlackAlerting
from litellm.proxy.common_utils.user_api_key_cache import UserApiKeyCache
from litellm.proxy.utils import PrismaClient, ProxyLogging
from litellm.repositories.alert_repository import AlertRepository
from litellm.repositories.config_repository import ConfigRepository
from litellm.types.integrations.slack_alerting import AlertType

mail = []
posts = []
class Inbox:
    async def handle_DATA(self, server, session, envelope):
        mail.append(BytesParser(policy=policy.default).parsebytes(envelope.content))
        return '250 OK'
class Webhook(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        posts.append(json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers['Content-Length']))))
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'ok')
    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

smtp = Controller(Inbox(), hostname='127.0.0.1', port=54359)
web = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 54360), Webhook)
threading.Thread(target=web.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
smtp.start()

async def main():
    client = PrismaClient(os.environ['DATABASE_URL'], ProxyLogging(UserApiKeyCache()))
    await client.connect()
    config = ConfigRepository(client, use_writer=True)
    alerts = AlertRepository(client)
    previous = await config.get_param('general_settings')
    tag = uuid.uuid4().hex
    addresses = tuple(f'{role}-{tag}@example.com' for role in ('admin','viewer','internal'))
    webhook = f'http://127.0.0.1:54360/{tag}'
    try:
        with psycopg.connect(os.environ['DATABASE_URL']) as connection:
            for role, address in zip(('proxy_admin','proxy_admin_viewer','internal_user'), addresses):
                connection.execute('INSERT INTO "LiteLLM_UserTable" (user_id,user_email,user_role) VALUES (%s,%s,%s)',(address,address,role))
        notifier = PerformanceAlertNotifier(config, alerts)
        await config.set_param('general_settings', {'email_settings': {}})
        await notifier.run(SlackAlerting(alerting=['slack'],default_webhook_url=webhook))
        assert not mail and not posts
        print('Connected email and Slack without performance opt-in: 0 messages')
        await config.set_param('general_settings', {'email_settings': {'Performance Alerts': True}})
        opted_in = SlackAlerting(alerting=['slack'],alert_types=[AlertType.performance_alerts],default_webhook_url=webhook)
        await asyncio.gather(notifier.run(opted_in), PerformanceAlertNotifier(config, alerts).run(opted_in))
        ours = [item for item in mail if str(item['To']) in addresses]
        assert len(ours) == 1 and str(ours[0]['To']) == addresses[0]
        assert len(posts) == 1
        assert 1 <= posts[0]['text'].count('?alert=') <= 5
        assert 'See all alerts' in posts[0]['text']
        assert 'See all alerts' in ours[0].get_body(preferencelist=('plain',)).get_content()
        count = len(mail)
        await notifier.run(opted_in)
        assert len(mail) == count and len(posts) == 1
        print('Two concurrent senders: 1 admin email and 1 Slack summary; viewer and internal user excluded')
        print('Immediate repeat: 0 additional messages; both messages link to Alerts')
        Path(__file__).with_name('performance-summary.html').write_text(ours[0].get_body(preferencelist=('html',)).get_content())
        Path(__file__).with_name('performance-slack.json').write_text(json.dumps(posts[0],indent=2))
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url='http://127.0.0.1:54248', headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer '+os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}, trust_env=False, timeout=30) as api:
            before = (await api.get('/alerts/monitoring')).json()
            for enabled in (False,True):
                changed = await api.patch('/alerts/monitoring',json={'model_deprecations_enabled':enabled})
                assert changed.status_code == 200
                assert changed.json() == {**before,'model_deprecations_enabled':enabled}
                assert (await api.get('/alerts/monitoring')).json() == changed.json()
            print('Live proxy PATCH/GET: deprecation preference persists; performance allowance and state unchanged')
    finally:
        if previous:
            await config.set_param('general_settings',previous.param_value)
        else:
            await client.writer_db.execute_raw('DELETE FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE param_name=$1','general_settings')
        with psycopg.connect(os.environ['DATABASE_URL']) as connection:
            connection.execute('DELETE FROM "LiteLLM_UserTable" WHERE user_id=ANY(%s)',(list(addresses),))
            for destination in ('slack:'+webhook, *('email:'+address for address in addresses)):
                key='performance_alert_digest:'+hashlib.sha256(destination.encode()).hexdigest()
                connection.execute('DELETE FROM "LiteLLM_Config" WHERE param_name=%s',(key,))
        await client.disconnect()
try:
    asyncio.run(main())
finally:
    smtp.stop()
    web.shutdown()
```

</details>

## Type

New Feature

## Caveats

### Medium

- An uncertain delivery can repeat the next day.
- The Python 3.10 notification tests pass. Full database proof uses Python 3.13 because main already calls unsupported `asyncio.timeout` during Prisma startup.

## Final Attestation

title: feat(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): prometheus share, borrowed and throttle metrics per team and model
body:
Adds three Prometheus series to the dynamic rate limiter so an operator can read a team's share on a model, how far it runs past that share, and how often and why the limiter refused it, straight from `/metrics`. The throttle counter's `reason` label is the same value the caller sees in the 429's `rate_limited_by` header, so the two always agree.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/dd0c94581f174366af0781c8df46dcc8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/dd0c94581f174366af0781c8df46dcc8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Operators cannot see a team's dynamic limiter share from Prometheus
- Nothing shows how far a team runs past its share
- A 429 from the limiter leaves no per team, per model, per reason trail

How it solves it:

- `litellm_dynamic_limiter_share_tokens` gauge, the team's share on the model
- `litellm_dynamic_limiter_borrowed_tokens` gauge, tokens used above that share, 0 under it
- `litellm_dynamic_limiter_throttled_total` counter, `reason` is the 429's `rate_limited_by` header
- Both gauges refresh from actual usage when a request settles
- A failing metrics sink never changes admission or the 429

## User Flow

Before: a platform operator watching Prometheus cannot tell a starved team from one over its share

1. The operator sets `callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3", "prometheus"]` and gives a team `model_tpm_limit: {"metered-model": 100}`
2. The team sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions until the model saturates and gets `429` with header `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated`
3. The operator opens https://litellm-domain/metrics and finds no series about the team's share, its overuse or the refusals

After: the same scrape answers all three questions

1. Same config, same team, same requests, same `429` with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated`
2. https://litellm-domain/metrics shows `litellm_dynamic_limiter_share_tokens{team=...,model_group="metered-model"} 100`
3. Next to it `litellm_dynamic_limiter_borrowed_tokens{...} 580`, the tokens the team used above 100 this window
4. And `litellm_dynamic_limiter_throttled_total{...,reason="model_per_team_saturated"} 8`, one per refused request, the reason matching the header

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10563

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup for both legs. Proxy with two workers sharing one local Redis and a Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`), real OpenAI calls to `gpt-4.1-mini`, env vars `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_LICENSE`. Ran without `--reload` because reload mode exited on this checkout, so the two worker PIDs come from `--num_workers 2` and were checked in the log (`Started server process` twice) on both legs.

<details>
<summary>proof.sh, creates a team with `model_tpm_limit` 100 on the model, a key, sends 16 requests, scrapes /metrics</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: proof.sh <leg> ; proxy must be up on :4123
set -u
P=http://127.0.0.1:4123; MK=${LITELLM_MASTER_KEY}
TEAM=$(curl -s -X POST $P/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"team_alias":"analytics-'$1'","metadata":{"model_tpm_limit":{"metered-model":100}}}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["team_id"])')
KEY=$(curl -s -X POST $P/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"'$TEAM'"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "team_id=$TEAM"
for i in $(seq 1 16); do
  curl -s -o /tmp/body.$$ -D /tmp/hdr.$$ -X POST $P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"metered-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"write 150 words about the number '$i'"}],"max_tokens":120}'
  st=$(head -1 /tmp/hdr.$$ | awk '{print $2}'); rb=$(grep -i '^rate_limited_by' /tmp/hdr.$$ | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')
  tk=$(python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]));print(d.get("usage",{}).get("total_tokens","-"))' /tmp/body.$$ 2>/dev/null)
  msg=""; [ "$st" != "200" ] && msg=$(python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]));e=d.get("error",d);print(str(e.get("message",e))[:110])' /tmp/body.$$ 2>/dev/null)
  echo "request $i: HTTP $st total_tokens=$tk rate_limited_by=${rb:-} ${msg:+error=\"$msg\"}"
done
sleep 3
echo "--- /metrics | grep litellm_dynamic_limiter"
curl -sL $P/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" | grep "^litellm_dynamic_limiter" || echo "(no litellm_dynamic_limiter series)"
```

Tests at the tip. `pytest tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py` 122 passed (steered alternate refusals, fallback-served shares and the joined priority label added after review round 1). `tests/unit/integrations/test_prometheus_metric_name_consistency.py` 10 passed, the all-metrics Grafana dashboard charts the three new families as that test requires. `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2 .venv/bin/python tests/integration/run.py providers tests/integration/routing/test_dynamic_limiter_prometheus_metrics.py` 2 passed at the tip and 2 failed with the three source files stashed (no `litellm_dynamic_limiter` series on `/metrics`). `make lint` passed.

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Refusals without a `rate_limited_by` header are not counted
  - the model ceiling 429 ("Model capacity reached") carries no header today, so it has no `reason` to publish
- With several workers the gauges aggregate with `livemostrecent`, the value written by whichever live worker settled the team's latest request
  - a worker reads the team counter from Redis at settlement, so the gauge trails the true total by at most one in-flight request

### Low

- Gauges keep their last value until the team's next request settles, there is no reset at the window edge
- `priority` is `default` for keys without a priority in their metadata

> Changes are additive metrics and observability hooks on the rate limiter path; failures are caught so limiter behavior is unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **Prometheus observability** for **dynamic rate limiter v3**: three new metric families and wiring from admission, refusals, and token settlement.
> 
> **`litellm_dynamic_limiter_share_tokens`** and **`litellm_dynamic_limiter_borrowed_tokens`** (gauges, `livemostrecent` for multi-worker) are updated when a request settles (success or failure), using the team’s binding share on the served model group—including fallback-served traffic. **`litellm_dynamic_limiter_throttled_total`** increments on each 429 that reaches the client, with **`reason`** matching the response’s **`rate_limited_by`** header (plus team, model group, priority, and rate limit type). Metric emission is wrapped so **failures in the metrics sink do not change admission or 429 behavior**.
> 
> Prometheus types gain **`reason`** and **`priority`** labels; Grafana’s all-metrics dashboard adds a **Dynamic rate limiter** row for the new series. Coverage includes unit tests on the hook + Prometheus registry and an integration test that scrapes `/metrics` under saturation.

title: fix(skills): honor dashboard user and team grants
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

allow users to access private skills that they have access to

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Dashboard members see public skills but miss granted private skills
- User settings lack a direct Skills grant control

How it solves it:

- Resolve current user, team and team access-group grants
- Use authenticated Skills reads inside the embedded AI Hub
- Reuse the existing user permission editor and update endpoint

Intentional product change: dashboard members can now browse skills explicitly granted to their user account, alongside current team grants; ordinary API keys keep their existing scope

## User Flow

Before: a member with user and team grants sees only one public skill

1. An admin grants private skills to the member and their team
2. The member signs in and opens `/model-hub-table`, then Skills Hub
3. Only `visibility-public` appears; granted private skills are missing

![Before: only public skills](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28401f40-2e2c-4959-91fd-414b88ca8205)

After: the same member sees four authorized skills and can open their content and version history

1. An admin grants private skills to the member and their team
2. The member signs in and opens `/model-hub-table`, then Skills Hub
3. Public, direct user, team and team access-group skills appear
4. Other users' grants and personal-key-only grants remain hidden

![After: granted private skills](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9ec9868-fe3b-4084-949d-7f7be4830c30)

The existing `/users` editor now supports selecting and clearing direct Skills grants

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before user editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5234895a-6f1b-4071-9882-6c224ba5033b) | ![After user editor](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a00b1ab6-b0f4-492b-a95b-49aaaeba0300) |

## Relevant issues

- Fix dashboard catalog and private read consistency
- Make existing direct-user Skills permissions editable and revocable

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10318

## Changes

- Keep shared Skills authorization as the read policy owner
- Reload user permissions and verify live, unblocked team membership
- Preserve independent grants when one source cannot be loaded
- Scope embedded catalog caching and detail requests to the session
- Reuse `SkillSelector` and protected `/user/update` permission merging

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Real gateway with two workers, PostgreSQL 18, Redis and the actual dashboard; synthetic data, no provider inference

### Before (`b60df93c4657f93a3aa9baa23bb86b576d356093`)

1. Run the client below after starting the baseline snapshot
2. Both dashboard catalogs return only `visibility-public`; granted user/team/group content returns 404
3. Personal key returns key/public; team key returns team/group/public
4. Open the member AI Hub and admin user editor: see the before screenshots above

### After (`7188f5adc02bd955e98511ac6955cbf08c36a4a3`)

1. Run the same client against the final snapshot with the same database
2. Both dashboard catalogs return public/user/team/group; all three private content reads return 200
3. Personal and team keys keep the same scopes as baseline
4. Open the member AI Hub and admin user editor: see the after screenshots above
5. Clear/save the direct grant: it disappears on the member's next read while team grants remain; selecting/saving restores it

Actual member catalog, private detail and version history at `7269aa0`. The final amendment only adds a regression test; every production file is byte-identical:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b7220b6-087f-46c8-8c92-330930d98801

<details>
<summary>Admin grant selection and save recording</summary>

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abc1fd21-2df3-4ec3-a3ff-c657112e65be

User-editor screenshots and this admin recording were captured at `aaa04b2`. Their source files are byte-identical at the current tip after the directory-only rebase, with form tests and live grant/revoke checks rerun

</details>

Additional live checks passed: private detail/content/current ZIP/version metadata/retained ZIP; direct revocation, team blocking and membership removal without re-login; unrelated grants hidden; privileged mutations denied

Local checks: production dashboard build and staged `make check` passed; 173 backend and 163 dashboard tests passed; resolver line coverage 99.19%; all seven authorization mutations killed, including stale permission-cache reuse

<details>
<summary>Reproduce with an isolated database and synthetic accounts</summary>

Use a separate checkout for each revision, with its bootstrapped dependencies and an empty local `.env`. Point `DATABASE_URL` at a disposable PostgreSQL database and run the repository migrations before startup. Start Redis on 56318. Set `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `UI_PASSWORD` and `DEMO_MEMBER_PASSWORD` privately to local test values

`config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list: []
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 56318
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 56318
litellm_settings:
  public_skills_index: true
```

From the selected source root:

```bash
export UI_USERNAME=visibility-admin
export PROXY_BASE_URL=http://lit10318.localhost:41318
export LITELLM_CORS_ORIGINS=http://lit10318.localhost:31318
export LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True
export DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config config.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 41318 \
  --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

In a separate terminal:

```bash
cd litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://lit10318.localhost:41318 \
LENS_DEV_PROXY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:41318 \
../../scripts/with_dashboard_node.sh npm run dev:webpack -- --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 31318
```

Save this as `reproduce.py`, then run `.venv/bin/python reproduce.py`. It uses the existing invite/onboarding/login flow and prints no credentials

```python
import io
import json
import os
import zipfile

import httpx
import jwt

base = os.environ.get("DEMO_PROXY_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:41318")
admin = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]}
password = os.environ["DEMO_MEMBER_PASSWORD"]
client = httpx.Client(base_url=base, headers=admin, timeout=60)


def call(method, path, **kwargs):
    response = client.request(method, path, **kwargs)
    if response.is_error:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{method} {path}: {response.status_code}")
    return response.json()


for name in ("visibility-public", "visibility-team", "visibility-user", "visibility-group", "visibility-key"):
    if client.get("/skill-hub/skills/" + name).status_code == 404:
        data = io.BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(data, "w") as archive:
            archive.writestr("SKILL.md", f"---\nname: {name}\ndescription: Synthetic visibility check\n---\n\nUse this checklist.\n")
        call("POST", "/skill-hub/skills/upload", data={"version": "1.0.0"},
             files={"file": ("skill.zip", data.getvalue(), "application/zip")})
    if name != "visibility-public":
        call("POST", "/skill-hub/skills/" + name + "/unpublish", json={})

if client.get("/v2/user/info", params={"user_id": "visibility-member"}).status_code != 200:
    call("POST", "/user/new", json={"user_id": "visibility-member", "user_email": "member@lit10318.invalid",
         "user_role": "internal_user", "auto_create_key": False})
    invite = call("POST", "/invitation/new", json={"user_id": "visibility-member"})["id"]
    onboarding = call("GET", "/onboarding/get_token", params={"invite_link": invite})
    token = jwt.decode(onboarding["token"], options={"verify_signature": False})["key"]
    call("POST", "/onboarding/claim_token", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + token},
```

title: fix(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): a borrower gets its full share back once the model saturates
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

dynamic rate limiting

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/2548aa9ed444483f8e7cc4aaf1a2544d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/2548aa9ed444483f8e7cc4aaf1a2544d?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:
- A team that borrowed idle capacity is refused the moment the model saturates
- Its idle-time tokens sat on the share counter for the rest of the minute
- The customer asked for each active service to regain its share under contention

How it solves it:
- Team share counters only count requests admitted while the model is saturated
- Idle-time borrowing is not charged, so the borrower gets its full share back at once
- A team below its share is still admitted ahead of a borrower, the model's own `tpm` still caps the total
- Applies to the request path, router fallback targets and Responses WebSocket turns alike

Intentional product change: with `team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams` on, a team that borrowed past its share while the model was idle is no longer refused as soon as the model saturates. It gets a fresh share for the rest of the window. Tokens it used while borrowing still count toward the model's `tpm`, so the aggregate does not grow.

## User Flow

Before: a service that borrowed idle capacity gets a 429 the instant another team shows up, and stays refused until the minute turns
1. Team A's service sends 17 POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions on `shared-model` (model `tpm: 1000`, both teams `model_tpm_limit: 100`) while team B is quiet, all 200
2. The model is past 50% of its `tpm`, so the limiter holds every team to its share
3. Team A's next POST gets 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated` and `retry-after: 60`, though the model has 490 tokens of room
4. Team B's first POST gets 200, team A keeps getting 429 for the rest of the minute

After: the same service keeps its 100 token share alongside team B, and is only held once it has used that share
1. Team A's service sends the same 17 POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions while team B is quiet, all 200
2. The model is past 50% of its `tpm`, so the limiter holds every team to its share
3. Team A's next POST gets 200, its 510 borrowed tokens are not charged against its share
4. Team B's first POST gets 200, team A is served beside it until it has used 100 tokens under saturation, then gets 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated`
5. Team B keeps getting 200

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10562

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy, two uvicorn workers sharing one Redis for router state and rate limit counters, a scripted OpenAI-shaped upstream on 127.0.0.1:9009 that answers every chat completion with 30 total tokens. Same config, same driver, same worker count for both legs, Redis flushed between legs. Base is `origin/main` at `382588a365`, fix is this branch at `91e6936de5`. The commit after it, `0293bd62`, only changes what a router fallback to an idle model settles, which this flow does not exercise.

Proxy command, run from the repo root with the base checked out and then with this branch

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/live/lit10562/config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Both legs served from three PIDs on :4000, the parent and two workers, checked with `ss -ltnp`.

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: shared-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4.1-mini
      api_key: synthetic-openai-key
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9009/v1
      tpm: 1000
      rpm: 1000

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"]
  priority_reservation:
    interactive: 0.6
    batch: 0.4
  priority_reservation_settings:
    default_priority: 1.0
    saturation_threshold: 0.5
    team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams: true
    saturation_check_cache_ttl: 2

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>driver.py, creates two teams with model_tpm_limit 100 and plays the flow</summary>

```python
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import httpx

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:4000"
MASTER = os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]
MODEL = "shared-model"
LABEL = sys.argv[1]
admin = httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {MASTER}"}, timeout=30)


def team_key(alias: str) -> str:
    team = admin.post("/team/new", json={"team_alias": f"{LABEL}-{alias}-{int(time.time())}",
                                         "metadata": {"model_tpm_limit": {MODEL: 100}}}).json()
    key = admin.post("/key/generate", json={"team_id": team["team_id"]}).json()
    return key["key"]


def call(key: str) -> httpx.Response:
    return httpx.post(f"{BASE}/v1/chat/completions", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, timeout=30,
                      json={"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"recovery {time.time()}"}]})


def show(who: str, r: httpx.Response, t0: float) -> None:
    extra = "" if r.status_code == 200 else f" rate_limited_by={r.headers.get('rate_limited_by')} retry-after={r.headers.get('retry-after')}"
    print(f"t={time.monotonic()-t0:5.1f}s {who:<8} {r.status_code}{extra}", flush=True)
    if r.status_code != 200 and os.environ.get("SHOW_BODY"):
        print("   body:", r.text[:400], flush=True)


def dump_redis(tag: str) -> None:
    if not os.environ.get("SHOW_BODY"):
        return
    import subprocess
    keys = [k for k in subprocess.run(["redis-cli", "--scan"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split() if "litellm_config" not in k]
    for k in sorted(keys):
        kind = subprocess.run(["redis-cli", "type", k], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
        val = subprocess.run(["redis-cli", "get", k], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip() if kind == "string" else subprocess.run(["redis-cli", "hgetall", k], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.replace("\n", " ")
        print(f"   [{tag}] {k} = {val[:160]}", flush=True)


a, b = team_key("team-a"), team_key("team-b")
t0 = time.monotonic()
for i in range(17):
    r = call(a); show("team-a", r, t0)
print("team-a has 510 tokens on the model this minute, the model is past 50% saturation", flush=True)
time.sleep(4)
dump_redis("before forgiven call")
r = call(a); show("team-a", r, t0)
dump_redis("after forgiven call")
print(f"team-a first request under saturation: {r.status_code}", flush=True)
r = call(b); show("team-b", r, t0)
for i in range(10):
    time.sleep(0.5)
    r = call(a); show("team-a", r, t0)
    if r.status_code == 429:
        break
r = call(b); show("team-b", r, t0)
```

</details>

Before, `origin/main`

```text

```

After, this branch


> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes saturation-gated team TPM/RPM accounting and fallback settlement in the v3 proxy rate limiter—critical request-path behavior—but scope is limited to idle-capacity borrowing semantics with extensive test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> When **`team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams`** is enabled, teams that consumed idle capacity no longer keep that usage on their per-team share counters after the model crosses the saturation threshold.
> 
> **Request admission** now stashes and enforces **`borrowing_team_model_limit`** only as the saturated share descriptor, and drops the extra atomic increments that bumped team (and some priority) counters while the model was still idle. **Router fallback** and **WebSocket turn** paths follow the same rule: team counters are charged only while the share is enforced; idle targets are check-only and **`BorrowingTeamModelHold`** can carry a **null** descriptor so settlement forgives target usage and returns the admitting reservation instead.
> 
> Coverage adds an integration scenario for borrower recovery beside a newcomer, plus unit tests renames/assertions for forgiven idle usage, fallback holds, and related borrowing edge cases.

title: fix(router): read malformed request fallback settings leniently
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Requests that pass a malformed `fallbacks` value (for example a string instead of a list) or a non-integer `max_fallbacks` currently fail with a 500 before routing. This PR reads those request-level fallback settings leniently, matching how the fallback walk and router settings already handle them, so the request is served instead of failing. Regression tests cover the malformed shapes from #51396.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A request with a non-list `fallbacks` value or a non-integer `max_fallbacks` fails before routing
- The proxy answers 500 with a router-core shape error, so the client gets nothing to act on

How it solves it:

- Read the three fallback lists through the same lenient reader the fallback walk already uses, so a non-list names no fallback
- Parse `max_fallbacks` the way the router settings already do, and leave the router limit in place when it is not a count

## User Flow

Before: a client sending `fallbacks` as a string gets a 500 back, so the request never reaches a model

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"fallbacks": "default"` in the body
2. The proxy answers 500 with "the router request does not have the shape router-core reads"
3. The request never reaches a model, and the client cannot tell what to fix from the response

After: the same request is served, so the client gets a response

1. They send the same POST with `"fallbacks": "default"` in the body
2. The proxy treats the malformed value as naming no fallback and routes the request
3. The model answers normally

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51396

## Affected release

regression in v1.110.0-rc.1

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more

E2E exception at ec06349d. Scope: one function in the router core plus its regression test. Rationale: the change is a focused validation fix, the regression test reproduces the reported defect exactly, and the issue's own repro runs end to end through the router core with a mock response and no network. - `pytest tests/unit/test_router/test_router_fallbacks.py::test_malformed_request_fallback_settings_are_served` on the base code with the new test: 5 failed, 2 passed. At the tip: 7 passed
- `pytest tests/unit/test_router/test_router_fallbacks.py` at the tip: 87 passed

The test file carries pre-existing format drift elsewhere in it, and the added test matches the formatter output. `ruff check` on both files: one pre-existing PYI047 finding on an untouched line, left alone, and one pre-existing I001 import sorting finding in the test file, also left alone. ruff_strict_gate: OK, no strict rule grew past its merge-base count. type_discipline_gate: OK, no LIT rule grew past its merge-base count. test_quality_gate: OK, no TQ rule grew past its merge-base count. openapi_docs_gate: OK, no OA rule grew past its merge-base count. type_check_gate: not run to completion locally, the whole tree basedpyright pass is killed by the kernel on this 6 GB machine with exit 247. body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add fal nano banana 2.1

<details>

Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/7d236b5bf1aa49198a835b94e179d976?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Fal's Nano Banana 2.1 has no cost map row, so it bills $0
- `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` is sent to `fal-ai/google/...` and Fal answers 404
- Fal bills it by tokens but returns no usage, only an `x-fal-billable-units` header
- Seedance reference-to-video drops `input_reference`, and Fal fails the job

How it solves it:

- Adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` and `/edit` rows to both cost maps
- Adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest` and `/edit` aliases pointing at them
- Keeps owner-qualified ids like `google/...` as they are in the Fal URL
- Adds `output_cost_per_billable_unit`, billed as the header value times that price
- Lets a deployment's own `output_cost_per_billable_unit` replace the catalog price
- Teaches the Rust registry check the new field, the same two commits as #51365
- Falls back to Fal's per-image price by resolution when the header is missing
- Sends `input_reference` as `image_urls` on Seedance reference-to-video
- Keeps `/fal_ai` passthrough closed to rows billed by reported units

## User Flow

Before: a developer who wants Fal's Nano Banana 2.1 cannot generate an image through the proxy

1. The proxy admin adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` to `model_list` as `fal-nano-banana-2.1` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `"model": "fal-nano-banana-2.1"`
3. They get HTTP 404, `Application "google" not found`

After: the same request returns an image and is billed what Fal charged for it

1. The proxy admin adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` to `model_list` as `fal-nano-banana-2.1` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `"model": "fal-nano-banana-2.1"`
3. They get HTTP 200 with one image URL and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.049490441`, the dollar amount Fal reported for that call
4. `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest` and POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits with `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest/edit` behave the same way

Env vars set: `FAL_AI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. The package was reinstalled on each checkout so the bundled cost map matched the commit.

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: fal-nano-banana-2.1
    litellm_params:
      model: fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1
      api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY
  - model_name: fal-nano-banana-latest
    litellm_params:
      model: fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest
      api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY
  - model_name: fal-nano-banana-latest-edit
    litellm_params:
      model: fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest/edit
      api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY
  - model_name: fal-seedance-r2v
    litellm_params:
      model: fal_ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video
      api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY
  - model_name: fal-nano-banana-2.1-edit-custom-unit-price
    litellm_params:
      model: fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1/edit
      api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY
    model_info:
      output_cost_per_billable_unit: 2.0

router_settings:
  redis_host: localhost
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: localhost
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Client calls</summary>

```bash
IMG="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/hub/master/images/dog.jpg"
curl -s -o dog.jpg "$IMG"

# gen21
curl -s -D - http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "fal-nano-banana-2.1", "prompt": "a red paper boat on a pond, flat illustration"}'

# genlatest
curl -s -D - http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "fal-nano-banana-latest", "prompt": "a red paper boat on a pond, flat illustration"}'

# editlatest
curl -s -D - http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \
  -F model=fal-nano-banana-latest-edit -F "prompt=make the dog wear a small blue hat" -F "image=@dog.jpg"

# editcustomunit
curl -s -D - http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \
  -F model=fal-nano-banana-2.1-edit-custom-unit-price -F "prompt=make the dog wear a small blue hat" -F "image=@dog.jpg"

# ptnb21, then ptnb2 with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 in place of google/nano-banana-2.1
curl -s -D - http://localhost:4000/fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "a red paper boat on a pond, flat illustration"}'

# r2v, then poll GET /v1/videos/<id> and download GET /v1/videos/<id>/content
curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/videos -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\": \"fal-seedance-r2v\", \"prompt\": \"the dog from the reference image running on a beach\", \"seconds\": \"5\", \"size\": \"854x480\", \"input_reference\": \"$IMG\"}"
```

</details>

### Before (7c7e02b06f)

The two Nano Banana rows and the two aliases do not exist at this commit, so the config above only names them.

#### Nano Banana 2.1 generation

1. `gen21` returns HTTP 404, `litellm.NotFoundError: Fal_aiException - {"detail":"Application \"google\" not found"}`
2. `genlatest` returns the same HTTP 404

#### Nano Banana latest edit

1. `editlatest` returns HTTP 404, `{"detail":"Application \"nano-banana-latest\" not found"}`, with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0`

#### Deployment with its own unit price

1. `editcustomunit` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL and `llm_provider-x-fal-billable-units: 0.045824696`
2. The response has no `x-litellm-response-cost` header and the proxy log shows `response_cost: 0.0`, so the call is not billed

#### `/fal_ai` passthrough

1. `ptnb21` returns HTTP 400, `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1 has no pricing entry for this request; only priced Fal requests can be submitted through /fal_ai`
2. `ptnb2` returns HTTP 200 with `"status":"IN_QUEUE"` and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.08`

#### Seedance reference-to-video with `input_reference`

1. `r2v` returns HTTP 200 with a queued video id
2. The proxy log shows the body sent to Fal carried `'image_url': 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/hub/master/images/dog.jpg'`
3. GET /v1/videos/<id> ends as `"status":"failed"` with `"message":"body: At least one reference image, video, or audio file is required."`

### After (c3aea0c64a)

Every call below ran at this commit, the tip of the branch.

#### Nano Banana 2.1 generation

1. `gen21` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.049490441`. The proxy log shows the call went to `https://fal.run/google/nano-banana-2.1`
2. `genlatest` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.045802427`, sent to the same URL
3. Both costs are the per-call amount Fal reported. The per-image fallback would have been exactly 0.04

#### Nano Banana latest edit

1. `editlatest` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL, sent to `https://fal.run/google/nano-banana-2.1/edit`
2. The response headers are `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.046751111` and `llm_provider-x-fal-billable-units: 0.046751111`

#### Deployment with its own unit price

1. `editcustomunit` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL
2. The response headers are `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.087661396` and `llm_provider-x-fal-billable-units: 0.043830698`, which is the deployment's 2.0 times the reported units

#### `/fal_ai` passthrough

1. `ptnb21` returns the same HTTP 400 as before, and the proxy log shows no request to Fal for it
2. `ptnb2` returns HTTP 200 with `"status":"IN_QUEUE"` and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.08`, unchanged
3. One commit earlier, at `52d0db20fa`, `ptnb21` returned HTTP 200 and logged the 0.04 per-image fallback for a call Fal bills by units. The last commit closes that

#### Seedance reference-to-video with `input_reference`

1. `r2v` returns HTTP 200 with a queued video id
2. The proxy log shows the body sent to Fal carried `'image_urls': ['https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/hub/master/images/dog.jpg']`
3. GET /v1/videos/<id> ends as `"status":"completed"`, and GET /v1/videos/<id>/content returns HTTP 200, `video/mp4`, 2342792 bytes

Pricing source. `GET https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing` returns `unit_price: 1`, `unit: "units"`, `currency: "USD"` for `google/nano-banana-2.1` and `google/nano-banana-2.1/edit`, so one billable unit is one dollar. The per-image fallback prices are the representative costs on https://fal.ai/models/google/nano-banana-2.1 and https://fal.ai/models/google/nano-banana-2.1/edit (read 2026-11-11).

Local checks at `c3aea0c64a`: `uv run pytest tests/unit/llms/fal_ai tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_model_latest_aliases.py tests/unit/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_llm_pass_through_endpoints.py` gives 1132 passed and `make check` ends with `check: PASS`. `cargo test --locked -p litellm-model-catalog -p litellm-cost` passes and `check-registry` exits 0 on this branch's cost map.

## Type

🆕 New Feature
🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- `cost-map-guard` stays red until #51365 merges, since it runs `main`'s registry check
- `/fal_ai` passthrough answers HTTP 400 for these rows, as on `main`, since a queue submission returns no billable units
- Fal video billing does not read the header yet, only image generation and edit do

### Low

- With no header on the response, cost falls back to Fal's representative per-image price
- The provider sync still skips Fal ids billed in "units" until its Fal rule allows the new field
- The alias test's mode assertion is the same one-line edit as in #51357
- This PR bundles three Fal fixes: the rows and billing, the URL, and the Seedance reference field

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
