title: chore(cost-map): add 7 fal_ai rows for seedream 5.5, flux virtual try-on, patina material and vidu templates (fifth fal-ai sync)
body:
Fifth fal-ai sync, covering the 18 ids the dispatcher found new on 2026-11-12: the 3 Seedream 5.5 endpoints fal listed on 2026-11-11 and the 15 ids the 2026-11-11 16:08 UTC child left unseen. The fal-ai lane is list-only, so `prices fal-ai` returns `structured: false` and every id was researched by hand on 2026-11-12: its model page `https://fal.ai/models/<id>` fetched raw with a cache buster, then the fal pricing API `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing?endpoint_id=<id>` as a unit cross-check

7 of the 18 ids get a row and 11 stay out. Ruling fal-ai-promotional-rates-apply-until-promotion-ends (Kerry, 2026-11-10) was checked against every page and none of the 18 states a time-limited promotion, so it changes nothing in this batch. Every row prices the request at the endpoint's schema defaults and names the other tiers and surcharges in `metadata`, the handling #51077 and #51193 gave `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-2-pro` (first megapixel plus extra megapixels), `fal_ai/luma/agent/uni-1/v1/edit` (per image plus a mandatory per input fee) and `fal_ai/fal-ai/vidu/image-to-video` (per second derived from a fixed 4s clip)

### New rows (kind page)

- `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.5/text-to-image`: output_cost_per_image=0.0405, output_cost_per_image_1K=0.03, output_cost_per_image_2K=0.0405. Page: "Billing is calculated per output image. Each image costs $0.03 at 1K or 1.5K, or $0.0405 at 2K. For custom dimensions, the rate is $0.03 up to and including 2,610,000 pixels, and $0.0405 above that area." The schema default is `"image_size":{"default":"auto_2K"`, so the base field takes the 2K rate. API cross-check: `{"endpoint_id":"bytedance/seedream/v5.5/text-to-image","unit_price":0.03,"unit":"units"}` (the 1K rate). Shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/nano-banana-2` (per image with 1K and 2K tier fields) on the text-to-image endpoint set of `fal_ai/fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4.5/text-to-image`

- `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.5/edit`: output_cost_per_image=0.0525, output_cost_per_image_1K=0.042, output_cost_per_image_2K=0.0525. Page: "Billing is calculated per output image, including an input-image fee for each output generated. Each output costs $0.03 at 1K or 1.5K, or $0.0405 at 2K, plus $0.012 per input image per output. For custom dimensions, the output rate is $0.03 up to and including 2,610,000 pixels, and $0.0405 above that area. For example, with 2 input images, one output costs $0.054 at 1.5K or $0.0645 at 2K". Schema default `"image_size":{"default":"auto_2K"`, so the row is one output with one input image at 2K ($0.0405 + $0.012), and the 1K field is $0.03 + $0.012. Extra input images are in `metadata` as not modeled, the handling of `fal_ai/luma/agent/uni-1/v1/edit`. API cross-check: unit_price 0.03 per units. Shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4.5/edit` (`/v1/images/edits`, `/v1/images/generations`, `supports_vision`)

- `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.5/layerize`: output_cost_per_image=0.0405, output_cost_per_image_1K=0.03, output_cost_per_image_2K=0.0405. Page: "Billing is calculated per returned output image, including the base image and every separated layer, plus $0.012 for the input image once per request. Each output costs $0.03 at 1K or 1.5K, or $0.0405 at 2K. With auto resolution, the base image determines the rate for all outputs: $0.03 each up to and including 2,610,000 pixels, or $0.0405 each above that". Schema default `"image_size":{"default":"auto"`, so the base field takes the higher auto rate, the rule the earlier fal syncs used when the default is auto. The once per request $0.012 input fee and the up to `max_images` (default 30) outputs per request are in `metadata`. API cross-check: unit_price 0.03 per units. Shape of `fal_ai/bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/layerize`

- `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/vto`: output_cost_per_image=0.0425. Page: "Billing is calculated at $0.0375 for the first input megapixel, plus $0.005 per additional input megapixel and $0.005 per output megapixel. Each input image and the output are rounded up to whole megapixels separately. For example, two 1024 × 1024 inputs and one 1024 × 1024 output cost $0.0475." The row is one 1 MP input and one 1 MP output ($0.0375 + $0.005), the handling #51193 gave `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-2-pro`. API cross-check: `{"endpoint_id":"fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/vto","unit_price":0.005,"unit":"processed megapixels"}` (the per megapixel component only). Shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-pro/v1/fill` without the per pixel field, since the page's per megapixel rate is not the whole price

- `fal_ai/fal-ai/patina/material`: output_cost_per_image=0.08. Page: "Your request will cost $0.01 plus $0.02 per megapixel plus $0.01 per megapixel per map type. When using 2x upscaling, an additional $0.004 per (pre-upscaling) megapixel per map will be charged, and when using 4x upscaling, an additional $0.016 per (pre-upscaling) megapixel per map will be charged. For example, A 1024x1024 material with all 5 maps and no upscaling (1K) will cost $0.08, and a 2048x2048 material with all 5 maps and 4x upscaling (8K) will cost $0.61." The schema defaults are `"image_size":"square_hd"` (1024x1024), `"maps":["basecolor","normal","roughness","metalness","height"]` and `"upscale_factor"` default `0`, which is the page's own $0.08 example. API cross-check: `{"endpoint_id":"fal-ai/patina/material","unit_price":0.01,"unit":"megapixels"}` (the per map component only). Shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/patina`, and the endpoint set includes `/v1/images/edits` because the schema takes an optional `image_url` ("also supports image-to-image")

- `fal_ai/fal-ai/patina/material/extract`: output_cost_per_image=0.17. Page: "Your request will cost $0.10 plus $0.02 per megapixel plus $0.01 per megapixel per map type. When using 2x upscaling, an additional $0.004 per (pre-upscaling) megapixel per map will be charged, and when using 4x upscaling, an additional $0.016 per (pre-upscaling) megapixel per map will be charged. For example, A 1024x1024 material with all 5 maps and no upscaling (1K) will cost $0.17, and a 2048x2048 material with all 5 maps and 4x upscaling (8K) will cost $0.70." Same defaults as the material endpoint, so the row is the page's $0.17 example. API cross-check: `{"endpoint_id":"fal-ai/patina/material/extract","unit_price":0.01,"unit":"megapixels"}`. Shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/patina`

- `fal_ai/fal-ai/vidu/template-to-video`: output_cost_per_second=0.05. Page: "Standard templates will cost $0.20, Premium templates will cost $0.30, and Advanced templates will cost $0.50." and the `template` parameter: "Standard templates (hug, kiss, love_pose, etc.) cost 4 credits ($0.20), Premium templates (lunar_newyear, dynasty_dress, dreamy_wedding, etc.) cost 6 credits ($0.30), and Advanced templates (live_photo) cost 10 credits ($0.50)". The page states no clip length, so the 4s clip is inherited from the sibling vidu endpoints on the same page data ("For 4s video your request will cost $0.20" for `fal-ai/vidu/image-to-video`) and the row divides the default Standard price by it, the handling #51193 gave `fal_ai/fal-ai/vidu/image-to-video`. API cross-check: `{"endpoint_id":"fal-ai/vidu/template-to-video","unit_price":0.05,"unit":""}`, which agrees with $0.20 over 4 seconds. Premium and Advanced templates are in `metadata`. Shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/vidu/image-to-video`

### Left out (11 ids)

- no model page and no pricing API entry (9): `fal-ai/luma-photon`, `fal-ai/luma-photon/flash`, `fal-ai/luma-photon/flash/modify`, `fal-ai/luma-photon/flash/reframe`, `fal-ai/luma-photon/modify`, `fal-ai/luma-photon/reframe`, `fal-ai/magi-distilled`, `fal-ai/magi-distilled/extend-video`, `fal-ai/magi-distilled/image-to-video`. `https://fal.ai/models/<id>` renders the NotFoundErrorPage shell, `/api` and `/llms.txt` are HTTP 404, `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing?endpoint_id=<id>` and `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models?endpoint_id=<id>` both answer `not_found`, and `https://fal.ai/pricing.md` does not list them. Only the paginated `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models` list returns them. A leave_out ruling was asked of Kerry on 2026-11-11 and is still open

- `fal-ai/decart/lucy-5b/image-to-video` (1): the page states "Your request will cost $0.15 per video" for "5-second I2V videos", but its page data carries `"status":"unlisted"` and `"deprecated":true`, the pricing API answers `not_found` for the `fal-ai/` prefixed id, and Kerry's open 2026-11-11 question covers it

- `google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.2/upscale` (1): "Billing is calculated per second of upscaled output video, based on the source and target resolution. Upscaling 360p to 720p or 720p to 1080p costs about $0.041 per second; 360p to 1080p costs $0.0819 per second; and 720p or 1080p to 4K costs $0.1638 per second." The 1080p rate depends on the source resolution, which no catalog field carries, and Kerry was asked on 2026-11-11 which shape to write. API: `{"endpoint_id":"google/gemini-omni-flash/v1.2/upscale","unit_price":0.0273,"unit":"seconds"}`, the 360p generation rate, which the page does not list for upscaling

No delisted ids in this diff

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7d236b5bf1aa49198a835b94e179d976
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/7d236b5bf1aa49198a835b94e179d976?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

</details>

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> JSON catalog-only additions with no runtime logic; incorrect defaults could slightly skew cost estimates for these fal.ai endpoints.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **seven new `fal_ai` catalog entries** to `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and its backup, extending cost tracking for the fifth fal-ai sync.
> 
> **Seedream v5.5** (`text-to-image`, `edit`, `layerize`) get per-image rates with **1K/2K tier fields** where applicable; edit/layerize include vision and image edit/generation endpoints, with **input-image and multi-output surcharges** called out only in `metadata`.

> **New image endpoints:** `flux-pro/v1/vto` (try-on), `patina/material` and `patina/material/extract` (default-schema example prices), each with vision and edits/generations routes.
> 
> **Video:** `vidu/template-to-video` uses **`output_cost_per_second`** (Standard template, 4s clip assumption documented in `metadata`).
> 
> Every row documents **pricing caveats** (unmodeled tiers, extra inputs, template tiers) in `metadata` comments rather than extra catalog fields.

title: fix(auth): enforce customer budget rpm/tpm limits under JWT auth
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Customer budgets with an RPM or TPM limit now get enforced when the request is authenticated with a JWT, the same way they already were for virtual keys. Before this, a JWT caller could blow past their customer's rate limits because the limits never got loaded onto the request.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/88ecb000ea5f462ba7154b4cb55785de
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/88ecb000ea5f462ba7154b4cb55785de?variant=devin
Requested by: @mateo-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer `rpm_limit` and `tpm_limit` were ignored under JWT auth
- Happened for both the JWT end-user claim and body `user`
- Virtual keys with the same customer already got 429

How it solves it:

- JWT requests now load the customer's budget limits during auth
- Reuses the same budget hydration the virtual-key path already uses

## User Flow

Before: an app authenticating with a JWT is never rate limited for its customer, even with `rpm_limit=1` and `tpm_limit=1` on the customer's budget

1. The admin creates a budget with `rpm_limit=1`, `tpm_limit=1` via POST /budget/new and a customer on it via POST /customer/new
2. The app sends POST /chat/completions three times with the JWT in `x-litellm-api-key`, customer set by the JWT claim or body `user`
3. All three come back 200 with a real completion

After: the same JWT requests are rate limited exactly like a virtual key

1. The admin creates the same budget and customer
2. The app sends the same three POST /chat/completions requests with the JWT
3. Every request comes back 429 `Rate limit exceeded for end_user`, first on tokens and then on requests

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-1799

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy, real Anthropic `claude-opus-4-8` calls, Postgres, a dedicated Redis shared by two workers per proxy, and real RS256 JWTs verified against a local JWKS served at `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL`. Each source got its own customer on a fresh budget with `rpm_limit=1` and `tpm_limit=1`. The virtual-key row is the control. The first denial is on TPM because even the prompt is over one token, the rest are on RPM

| Auth and end-user source | Before, 3 back-to-back calls | After, 3 back-to-back calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JWT, `customer_id` claim (`end_user_id_jwt_field`) | 200, 200, 200 | 429, 429, 429 |
| JWT, body `user` | 200, 200, 200 | 429, 429, 429 |
| Virtual key, body `user` | 429, 429, 429 | 429, 429, 429 |

The fixed proxy also served a JWT request for an uncapped customer with 200 and real token usage, so normal JWT traffic still goes through

Env vars used are `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_LICENSE`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`

<details>
<summary>Proxy commands</summary>

The existing DATABASE_URL points to local PostgreSQL, database litellm
Secrets used only via existing environment variables DATABASE_URL, LITELLM_LICENSE, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
The test master key below is a disposable local QA key, not an account credential
Redis binds only to localhost and is dedicated to this proof
The baseline reused the checkout's compiled native extension because a new source worktree does not contain an ignored compiled artifact
The workspace proxy-extras and enterprise source directories must be on PYTHONPATH because these packages are not installed in the snapshot venv

<details>
<summary>JWKS and token server</summary>

This local server creates the RSA signing key in memory and never writes it to disk

```python
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa
import jwt

private_key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
jwk = json.loads(jwt.algorithms.RSAAlgorithm.to_jwk(private_key.public_key()))
jwk.update(kid="lit1799", use="sig", alg="RS256")

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path == "/jwks":
            body = json.dumps({"keys": [jwk]}).encode()
        else:
            from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
            params = parse_qs(urlsplit(self.path).query)
            claims = {"sub": "lit1799-user", "team_id": "lit1799-team"}
            if params.get("customer"):
                claims["customer_id"] = params["customer"][0]
            body = jwt.encode(claims, private_key, algorithm="RS256", headers={"kid": "lit1799"}).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8899), Handler).serve_forever()
```

```python
import json
import sys
import urllib.request
import urllib.error

port, phase = sys.argv[1:]
base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"

def call(path, payload, key="sk-lit1799-local", jwt_auth=False):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "x-litellm-api-key" if jwt_auth else "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}",
    })
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=120) as response:
            return response.status, json.load(response)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, json.load(error)

for path, payload in (
    ("/team/new", {"team_id": "lit1799-team", "models": []}),
    ("/user/new", {"user_id": "lit1799-user", "teams": ["lit1799-team"]}),
):
    status, result = call(path, payload)
    print(path, status)
status, key_result = call("/key/generate", {"team_id": "lit1799-team"})
assert status == 200, (status, key_result)
virtual_key = key_result["key"]
for source in ("claim", "body", "virtual-key"):
    customer = f"lit1799-{phase}-{source}"
    status, budget = call("/budget/new", {"rpm_limit": 1, "tpm_limit": 1})
    assert status == 200, (status, budget)
    status, result = call("/customer/new", {"user_id": customer, "budget_id": budget["budget_id"]})
    assert status == 200, (status, result)
    with urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:8899/token" + (f"?customer={customer}" if source == "claim" else "")) as response:
        token = response.read().decode()
    for index in range(3):
        payload = {"model": "anthropic-opus-4-8", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply only OK"}], "max_tokens": 16}
        if source != "claim":
            payload["user"] = customer
        status, result = call("/chat/completions", payload, virtual_key if source == "virtual-key" else token, source != "virtual-key")
        print(json.dumps({"phase": phase, "source": source, "request": index + 1, "status": status,
            "model": result.get("model"), "usage": result.get("usage"), "error": result.get("error")}), flush=True)
```

title: feat(guardrails): straiker stream_mode, per-phase logging and prompt-block replies
body:
## Straiker Guardrail changes:
* Streaming mode added (along with default buffered mode).
* logging added to guardrail.
* A prompt that is blocked shows up as 2xx instead of 4xx.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A blocked prompt comes back as HTTP 400, which some clients show as a malformed request
- Straiker 408, 429 and 500 responses fail closed even with `unreachable_fallback: fail_open`
- A timed-out Straiker call is retried, multiplying the wait before a verdict
- Streamed responses are always held until the whole answer is checked
- The guardrail log reads "allow" even when the guardrail failed open
- Any `claude-cli/` User-Agent is named Claude, including clients that only share the prefix
- A blocked answer on a route with no reply to send, such as `/guardrails/apply_guardrail`, returns HTTP 500

How it solves it:

- A prompt-side block is answered as a reply: HTTP 200, `finish_reason: content_filter`
- Only on chat completions, text completions, messages and responses; other routes keep the 400
- A blocked answer on a route with no reply to send is HTTP 400, where it was a 500
- 408, 429 and 500 follow `unreachable_fallback` once retries are spent
- A timed-out attempt is not retried
- New `stream_mode` option: `buffered` (default, unchanged) or `streaming`
- Each v3 phase logs its own entry: session, action, turn id, controls
- `claude-cli/` is named Claude only for Claude Code entrypoints

Intentional product change: on chat completions, text completions, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`, a prompt that Straiker blocks now returns HTTP 200 with the block message as the assistant reply, instead of HTTP 400. Routes that cannot send a reply, such as `/v1/embeddings` and `/guardrails/apply_guardrail`, keep the HTTP 400. A Straiker outage that fails closed still returns an error, so a client can tell an outage from a verdict.

## User Flow

Before: a developer whose prompt Straiker blocks gets a request error where an answer should be

1. The proxy admin enables the Straiker guardrail with `mode: pre_call` and a Straiker v3 key
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt Straiker blocks
3. The proxy answers HTTP 400 with the block message inside an error body
4. Their client shows an error where an answer should be: Claude Code prints `API Error: 400` with the message, and some clients report a malformed request and drop the message

After: the same developer sees the block message as the assistant's answer

1. The proxy admin enables the Straiker guardrail with `mode: pre_call` and a Straiker v3 key
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a prompt Straiker blocks
3. The proxy answers HTTP 200 with the block message as the assistant reply and `finish_reason: content_filter`
4. Their client shows the block message like any other answer

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [ ] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup: a real proxy on `127.0.0.1:4300` serving `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` through Anthropic (real calls), with the Straiker guardrail pointed at a real Straiker v3 tenant. The prompt that tenant blocks uses the example keys from the AWS documentation, which its `api_key` control catches.

One image was built from this branch, the way the `image-scan` workflow builds it:

```
docker build -f litellm/deploy/docker/Dockerfile --build-arg MATURIN_PEP517_ARGS="--profile ci" -t litellm-proof .
```

The PR changes three files under `litellm/`, all in the Straiker guardrail. Each side runs that image with its own copy of those three files mounted over the installed ones: Before is the merge base `52d1c4cd80`, After is the tip `25edce3340`. Postgres 16 runs beside it for the spend logs.

```
docker run -d --name litellm-proof-proxy --network litellm-proof \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY -e STRAIKER_API_BASE -e STRAIKER_API_KEY \
  -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql://litellm:litellm@litellm-proof-pg:5432/litellm -e LITELLM_LOG=INFO \
  --mount type=bind,src=$PWD/config.yaml,dst=/app/config.yaml,readonly \
  --mount type=bind,src=$PWD/<side>/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker/__init__.py,dst=/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker/__init__.py,readonly \
  --mount type=bind,src=$PWD/<side>/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker/straiker.py,dst=/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker/straiker.py,readonly \
  --mount type=bind,src=$PWD/<side>/litellm/types/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker.py,dst=/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/types/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/straiker.py,readonly \
  -p 127.0.0.1:4300:4000 litellm-proof --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000
```

<details>
<summary>stream_timing.py, the client for the stream_mode case</summary>

```python
"""Stream a chat completion through the proxy and report when the content chunks arrive.

    LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... python3 -I stream_timing.py <guardrail name>
"""

import http.client
import json
import os
import sys
import time

guardrail = sys.argv[1]
body = json.dumps(
    {
        "model": "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001",
        "stream": True,
        "guardrails": [guardrail],
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 150, one number per line, nothing else."}],
    }
)
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['LITELLM_MASTER_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", 4300, timeout=120)
start = time.monotonic()
conn.request("POST", "/v1/chat/completions", body, headers)
resp = conn.getresponse()
arrivals = []
while line := resp.readline():
    line = line.strip()
    if not line.startswith(b"data: ") or line == b"data: [DONE]":
        continue
    choices = json.loads(line[len(b"data: ") :]).get("choices") or []
    if choices and (choices[0].get("delta") or {}).get("content"):
        arrivals.append(time.monotonic() - start)

print(f"guardrail={guardrail} HTTP {resp.status}, {len(arrivals)} content chunks")
if arrivals:
    print(f"first chunk at {arrivals[0]:.2f}s, last chunk at {arrivals[-1]:.2f}s")
```

🆕 New Feature

✅ Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Severe

- A blocked prompt returns HTTP 200 instead of 400 on chat completions, text completions, messages and responses
  - Clients that treat the 400 as the block signal must read `finish_reason: content_filter`

### Medium

- A blocked prompt answered as a reply does not reach the logging callbacks
  - Measured on this build: no callback event on `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses` or non-streamed chat
  - A streamed chat completion block does reach them
  - LiteLLM runs failure logging only for some exception types, and `ModifyResponseException` is not one
  - The spend logs still record every one, with the guardrail's entry
- Five related Straiker guardrail changes in one PR
  - Happy to split it if reviewers prefer one change per PR

### Low

- HTTP 408, 429 and 500 fail-open and the `claude-cli/` naming are covered by tests only, not live
- `stream_mode: streaming` delivers text before the check
  - A block then ends the stream with the block message, after earlier text already reached the client
- No Straiker docs page exists, so `stream_mode` is documented only in the option's description

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes guardrail enforcement semantics (HTTP status for blocks), streaming delivery before moderation, and fail-open/retry behavior on the Straiker integration path—high user-visible impact but scoped to Straiker guardrail configuration.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR overhauls the **Straiker** proxy guardrail with several behavioral and observability changes.
> 
> **Blocking UX on chat-style routes:** Prompt-side blocks on completion, messages, and responses routes now raise `ModifyResponseException` so clients get an HTTP 200 assistant reply with `finish_reason: content_filter` instead of HTTP 400. Embeddings, `/guardrails/apply_guardrail`, and similar surfaces still raise `GuardrailRaisedException` (HTTP 400).
> 
> **Streaming:** New `stream_mode` config (`buffered` default, or `streaming`) toggles whether streamed post-call responses are fully buffered until moderation or chunks are released early (still one end-of-stream check).
> 
> **v3 reliability:** HTTP 408, 429, and 5xx responses are treated as transient and honor `unreachable_fallback` after retries; per-attempt timeouts are no longer retried. v3 phases write structured spend/logging entries (session, action, controls, turn id, replay metadata) instead of generic “allow” when Straiker fails open.
> 
> **Client detection:** `claude-cli/` User-Agents are labeled Claude only when the parenthetical entrypoint matches Claude Code products, not Cowork or Agent SDK clients.
> 
> Blocked-turn memory now stores richer `_RememberedBlock` records for repeat-block logging.
>

title: fix(router): normalize request fallback lists and max_fallbacks shapes
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Normalize request fallback list and max_fallbacks shapes in `_start_fields` so non-list fallback values (`fallbacks="default"`) map to empty lists and non-count `max_fallbacks` settings leave the router limit in place, preventing router-core `ValueError` deserialization crashes (HTTP 500).

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:
- In `litellm/router_rust/core.py`, `_start_fields` passed `fallbacks`, `context_window_fallbacks`, `content_policy_fallbacks`, and `max_fallbacks` directly to the router-core request document without validation.
- When clients send non-list values (e.g. `"fallbacks": "default"`) or non-integer counts (e.g. `"max_fallbacks": "2"` or `"default"`), `RequestSpec` deserialization in router-core fails with `ValueError: the router request does not have the shape router-core reads: invalid type: string ..., expected a sequence/u32`, bubbling up to clients as HTTP 500 `api_error`.

How it solves it:
- Added `_request_fallback_fields` to normalize fallback list keys (`fallbacks`, `context_window_fallbacks`, `content_policy_fallbacks`): non-list values map to `[]` (matching the Python fallback walk's `_as_list` behavior, replacing router fallbacks with 0 targets), preserving `None` and valid sequences.
- Normalized `max_fallbacks` to `u32` counts via `_crate_count`, omitting non-count values so the router's configured limit remains in place.
- Added regression tests in `tests/unit/test_router/core/test_gaps_request_overrides.py` covering field shape normalization and router completion/fallback behavior.

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51396

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(model_prices): add Bedrock EOL dates and correct Azure Whisper retirement
body:
## Summary

Updates `deprecation_date` on existing entries in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` to match official provider retirement / EOL tables.

No new model entries, prices, or capability flags.

1. **Amazon Bedrock — missing EOL dates.** AWS's current Model lifecycle (Legacy) page lists remaining-region EOL dates that these LiteLLM keys do not have:
   - Claude 3.5 Sonnet (`anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0`), Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 (`anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`), and Claude 3.7 Sonnet (`anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0`): **2026-11-13** in the regions still listed as scheduled (3.5 Sonnet: ap-northeast-2, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1; 3.7 Sonnet: ap-south-1, eu-west-2). Some other regions already reached EOL earlier; this date is the currently announced remaining EOL. GovCloud keys are left unchanged because this table does not give them a separate remaining date.
   - TwelveLabs Marengo Embed 3.0 (`twelvelabs.marengo-embed-3-0-v1:0` and the `us.` / `eu.` prefixes already in this file): **2027-03-22** (official row lists ap-northeast-2).
   Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-lifecycle-legacy.html

2. **Azure OpenAI Whisper — wrong date.** `azure/whisper` and `azure/whisper-1` currently use `2027-02-26`, which is OpenAI's shutdown date for `whisper-1`. Azure Foundry's retirement schedule lists `whisper` version `001` as retiring on **2026-12-15**. The existing `azure_ai/whisper` entry already has `2026-12-15`. This PR aligns the `azure/` keys and points `deprecation_source` at the public schedule.
   Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirement-schedule

## Relevant issues

n/a — data correction from official lifecycle pages.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

- Add `deprecation_date` to the Bedrock keys listed in the diff.
- Change `azure/whisper` and `azure/whisper-1` from `2027-02-26` to `2026-12-15`, and update `deprecation_source` to the public retirement schedule.

## Testing

JSON-only field updates. Confirmed each key already exists on `main`. Dates transcribed from the official tables linked above (retrieved 12 Nov 2026).

— LLMIntel

title: fix(cache-memory): rebuild the in-memory cache on an exact expiry index
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description - The Rust's `cache-memory` was a port of Python's InMemoryCache, which tracks expiry in a heapq because Python has no sorted set in its standard library. A heap can only remove its top item, so deleting or re-arming a key leaves a dead record behind, and Python cleans those up later with a stale check on every pop plus a full rebuild once the heap passes twice the capacity. The Rust port copied the heap but not the rebuild, so on a busy key the bookkeeping grew with the write rate times the TTL instead of staying within the configured size. - Without this PR, a router that keeps re-arming session pins or cooldowns slowly leaks memory in every worker. A single TTL too large for Duration also panics while the cache lock is held, and after that every read and write on that cache fails until the process restarts. Two smaller races sit next to these, where a plain write can land between an increment's read and write and be lost, and where a cooldown briefly disappears from memory while it is being corrected. - This PR replaces the heap with a BTreeSet, which is sorted like a heap but can remove any record. Each entry has exactly one index record that is removed together with it, so there is nothing stale to clean up and the leak cannot happen by construction. Deadlines saturate instead of overflowing, every read-modify-write runs under one parking_lot lock that cannot poison, and re-arming a deadline is one call instead of a delete followed by a set.
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The native `InMemoryCache` copied Python's lazy expiry heap - Deleting or re-arming a key left a stale heap record - A longer-lived key at the top kept them all in memory - `now + ttl` panicked on overflow while holding the cache mutex - A poisoned mutex then failed every later call on that cache - The Redis stores wrapped the cache in a second mutex - `RouterCooldowns` panicked on a cooldown too long for `Duration` How it solves it: - One index record per entry in a `BTreeSet`, removed with the entry - Nothing to compact, so the index cannot outgrow the entries - A write picks `Expiry::KeepExisting` or `Expiry::Refresh` - `update()` reads and writes under the one state lock - The memory tier uses `update()` and drops its second mutex - Deadlines saturate, and an unmeasurable cooldown stays active - Both crates lock with `parking_lot`, which cannot poison ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix E2E exception at `d0e89915e7d`. Scope is `litellm-cache-memory` and the memory tier of `litellm-redis-store`, its only non-test user. The cache has no route of its own and what changed is its bookkeeping, so there is no request a proxy user could send that shows the index staying bounded. The missing live proxy run is listed under Caveats Run from `litellm/rust`, with Docker running for the Redis-backed tests: 1. `cargo test -p litellm-cache-memory` passes the 79 inline tests and the 8 shared contract tests 2. `cargo test -p litellm-redis-store` passes 61 lib tests and 291 integration tests against a real Redis (auth_cache 32, deployment_health 19, rate_limits 48, request 16, router_cooldowns 34, router_session_pins 22, router_usage 52, sensitive_route_pins 5, spend_counters 63) 3. `cargo test -p litellm-cache-response` passes its 118 tests, which use the cache as their backend 4. `cargo clippy -p litellm-cache-memory -p litellm-redis-store --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean 5. `cargo mutants -p litellm-cache-memory --in-place` catches all 64 viable mutants, with 15 unviable 6. `cargo mutants -p litellm-redis-store --in-place` on `memory.rs`, `RouterCooldowns::correct` and `SpendCounters::set_max` first missed 9 of 23 viable mutants. The cooldown correction and the runtime capacity change had no test of their effect on memory, and now do. The one left is `<` to `<=` in `set_max`, which rewrites an equal value under the same deadline 7. 45 more mutants written by hand, 26 in `litellm-cache-memory` and 19 in `litellm-redis-store`, all fail a test now. They cover each original bug put back (the index record left behind on delete, `<=` to `<` in the expiry rule, `saturating_add` to `+`, a lock dropped between the read and the write in `update`, both cooldown overflow lines), each write mode swapped between keeping and re-arming the deadline, a TTL ignored, and each branch of the cooldown correction ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) ### Medium - No live proxy run at this tip, crate tests only - The memory tier's lock and two cache rules changed - Two deliberate rule changes in the memory tier - An entry expires at its deadline, no longer just after it - Writing a held key at capacity no longer evicts another entry - `len` and `expires_at` report live entries only ### Low - Split out of #50870, now merged. Its session pin replace was a delete then a set, and is one `Memory::refresh` here - Removed `expiration_heap_len`, `evict_cache`, `evict_element_if_expired`, `allow_ttl_override` and `max_entry_bytes` - None had a caller outside the crate's own tests - Read methods still return `Result` though they can no longer fail ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
---

title: fix(otel): send the Langfuse environment, release and version on OTel v2
body:
## Relevant issues Fixes LIT-10174. Fixes #47898. ## Problem With `LITELLM_OTEL_V2` on, `langfuse_otel` traces land in Langfuse environment `default` with no release or version: - `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT` is ignored on the proxy's own Langfuse export. - A key's or team's `langfuse_environment` is ignored on its own Langfuse destination when the proxy also has `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` / `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`. - `trace_release` / `trace_version` on the request are dropped. ## Fix | What | Where | How | |---|---|---| | Proxy environment | `presets/langfuse.py`, `plumbing/providers.py` | the proxy's Langfuse exporter adds resource attribute `langfuse.environment` from `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT` to its own copy of each span (new `ExporterSpec.resource_attributes`) | | Key / team environment | `presets/destinations.py` | the destination's resource attribute no longer depends on whether the proxy has Langfuse keys | | Release, version | `model/trace_controls.py`, `mappers/langfuse.py` | `langfuse.release` / `langfuse.version` on the root and model spans, next to name, user, session and tags | The environment is set per exporter, so a generic OTLP collector, the OTel metrics resource and a key's or team's non-Langfuse destination never see it. A key's or team's environment labels only that key's or team's Langfuse destination; the proxy's own export always carries the proxy's environment. ## Not in this PR - `langfuse_environment` in a request body stays rejected. - A key or team that sets `langfuse_environment` without Langfuse credentials of its own does not relabel the proxy's traces. - On a proxy with no Langfuse keys of its own, a key's or team's Langfuse destination gets `langfuse.release` / `langfuse.version` on the model span only, as it gets name, user, session and tags on main. Langfuse fills the trace's own Release / Version from a non-root span only when that span also updates the trace (name, user, session, tags or metadata), so a request that sends release or version alone shows the version on the generation and not on the trace. ## Behavior changes All with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2` on. Nothing changes with it off. - Proxy with Langfuse keys and `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT` set: its Langfuse traces move to that environment. They came from `default`, or from the `OTEL_ENVIRONMENT_NAME` / `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` value when one of those was also set, since `langfuse.environment` wins over `deployment.environment` in Langfuse. - Key / team Langfuse destination on a proxy with Langfuse keys: traces move from `default` to the key's or team's `langfuse_environment`, else `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT`. - Requests carrying `trace_release`, `trace_version` or `version` metadata, or the `langfuse_trace_release` / `langfuse_trace_version` / `langfuse_version` headers, now set `langfuse.release` / `langfuse.version`. `trace_version` from either place wins over `version`. - The request's root span carries `langfuse.release` / `langfuse.version` to every exporter that shares the `langfuse_otel` logger (a generic OTLP collector, Arize), the same way it already carries `langfuse.trace.name`, `langfuse.trace.tags`, `user.id` and `session.id` on main. The model span carries them to Langfuse only. - `ExporterSpec` accepts a new optional `resource_attributes` field. Every spec that parsed before still parses. - At a span attribute limit, release and version never push out another attribute: the model span sheds them first, and the root span takes them only when they fit. - A `langfuse.environment` already in the proxy's resource (`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`) keeps winning over `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT`. - An export routed to a key's own Langfuse credentials without a destination (a failure-only `langfuse_otel` entry, or per-request credentials in the SDK) carries no `langfuse.environment`, as on main. No migration needed. ## Proof Real self-hosted Langfuse, same request on base and head, proxy with `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT=aud-proxy` and `trace_release` / `trace_version` metadata. | Base: `default`, no release or version | Head: `aud-proxy`, `rel-body`, `ver-body` | |---|---| | ![base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51385/evidence/lit10174/base-proxy.png) | ![head](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51385/evidence/lit10174/head-proxy.png) | A key with its own Langfuse keys and `langfuse_environment=aud-key`, on the same proxy: ![key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr51385/evidence/lit10174/head-key.png)
Rerun: same request on base 52d1c4cd801 and head 6efa17798e3, real Langfuse v3.225.15 `config.yaml` (the model upstream was a local OpenAI-compatible stub; any model works): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-fin litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_base: http://127.0.0.1:26701/v1 api_key: sk-stub litellm_settings: callbacks: ["langfuse_otel"] ``` Env: `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `LITELLM_SALT_KEY`, `LITELLM_LICENSE`, `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=500`, `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:13398`, `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT=fin-proxy`. ```bash litellm --config config.yaml --port 26710 --num_workers 2 KEY=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:26710/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' | jq -r .key) curl -s http://127.0.0.1:26710/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "gpt-fin", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "metadata": {"trace_release": "rel-950038", "trace_version": "ver-950038"}}' curl -s -u "$LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY:$LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY" "$LANGFUSE_HOST/api/public/traces?name=litellm-acompletion&limit=1" \ | jq '.data[0] | {id, name, environment, release, version}' ``` Base `52d1c4cd801` (release / version sent as `rel-5fa0a0` / `ver-5fa0a0`): ```json {"id": "dcbddee3ebacb8d63a6cf62252cdd240", "name": "litellm-acompletion", "environment": "default", "release": null, "version": null} ``` Head `6efa17798e3`: ```json {"id": "a7bff3aef07b7b8aaa8f65cd33a6e339", "name": "litellm-acompletion", "environment": "fin-proxy", "release": "rel-950038", "version": "ver-950038"} ``` Head `6efa17798e3`, 20 requests (chat and streaming) across the three setups, read back from Langfuse. The key or team destination has its own Langfuse keys and project: | Setup | Proxy's Langfuse project | Key's / team's Langfuse project | |---|---|---| | `langfuse_otel` in `callbacks`, proxy has Langfuse keys, plain key | `fin-proxy`, release, version | no trace | | same proxy, key with `langfuse_environment=fin-key` | request not exported, as on main | `fin-key`, release, version | | same proxy, key with no `langfuse_environment` | request not exported | `fin-proxy`, release, version | | same proxy, team with `langfuse_environment=fin-team` | request not exported | `fin-team`, release, version | | proxy without Langfuse keys (`callbacks: ["langfuse_otel"]` and `callbacks: []`), key with `langfuse_environment=fin-key` | no trace | `fin-key`, version on the generation | | same, key with no `langfuse_environment` | no trace | `fin-proxy`, version on the generation | | same, team with `langfuse_environment=fin-team` | no trace | `fin-team`, release, version | | same, plain key | no trace | no trace |
## Tests - `tests/integration/observability/test_langfuse_otel_v2_environment.py`: live proxy, every span of a request names the environment on chat, responses and messages, streaming and failed calls; key and team destinations; release and version from metadata and headers. - `tests/unit/integrations/otel/`: only the proxy's Langfuse exporter gets the environment (a collector beside it does not), destination resource with and without proxy keys, trace controls, mapper. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes span export plumbing, per-tenant routing, and Langfuse attribute stamping on hot paths, which can relabel traces in Langfuse but is mostly additive and gated on OTel v2. > > **Overview** > **OTel v2 Langfuse traces** now carry the correct **environment** on exports, plus **release** and **version** from request metadata/headers. > > **`langfuse.environment`** is applied **per exporter** via a new **`ExporterSpec.resource_attributes`** field and an **`_ExporterResource`** span processor that merges those attributes onto each exporter’s copy of a span. The proxy’s Langfuse exporter sets it from **`LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENVIRONMENT`** (or key/team **`langfuse_environment`** on their destination), without the old behavior that skipped this when the proxy had its own Langfuse keys. Tenant credential routing **clears** operator **`resource_attributes`** so environments do not leak across accounts. > > **`langfuse.release`** and **`langfuse.version`** are parsed in **`TraceControls`** (`trace_release`, `trace_version`, with headers winning over body), mapped by **`LangfuseMapper`**, and stamped on the request root in **`LangfuseOpenTelemetryV2`**. When the root span is at its attribute limit, **release/version are dropped first** so name, user, session, and tags are not displaced. > > Coverage is extended with **integration tests** for proxy/key/team environments and release/version, plus **unit tests** for mapping, destinations, routing, and attribute limits. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6efa17798e3f125b12c0f794e0ec80cc1a9f72a3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

title: fix(proxy): preserve team aliases in Responses WebSockets
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Responses WebSockets can discard a team's model alias.
- Duplicate provider models can then select another deployment.

How it solves it:

- Preserve the model already rewritten by common preprocessing.
- Cover both query models and first-frame models.

## User Flow

Before, a developer's team alias can reach a shared deployment.

1. Their administrator maps a model name to a restricted deployment.
2. They open ws://127.0.0.1:40873/v1/responses and send a response.create frame for that alias.
3. The request completes, but Logs shows qa-shared-deployment outside the team's permitted model group.

After, the same alias stays on its intended deployment.

1. Their administrator maps a model name to a restricted deployment.
2. They open ws://127.0.0.1:40873/v1/responses and send a response.create frame for that alias.
3. The request completes and Logs shows qa-restricted-deployment. The alias no longer reaches the shared deployment.

## Relevant issues

Fixes #51379.

## Affected release

Observed in v1.110.0-rc.1 and main at db8ad3b13e7320bf835205cae58be5a58e0ff366. The first affected release has not been established.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests.
- [x] The test files covering this change pass locally, with 378 tests passing.
- [ ] All required CI checks have completed on the submitted PR.
- [x] This change addresses one specific problem.
- [ ] Automated PR reviews have finished and their findings have been addressed.

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The live checks used a real restricted virtual key, two local proxy workers, a dedicated Redis and Postgres, and real provider calls through an existing gateway. The same configuration and client were used before and after. No live deployment was modified. Upstream addresses and credentials are omitted.

The existing gateway accepts model names such as openai/gpt-6.1-sol. The outer openai prefix in the local provider model selects the OpenAI-compatible adapter. Both local deployments deliberately share that provider model. The request's alias points only to the restricted deployment.

The launcher supplied QA_UPSTREAM_BASE and QA_UPSTREAM_KEY internally. To repeat this run, set them for your own compatible gateway. Set QA_MASTER_KEY, QA_REDIS_PORT and DATABASE_URL for the local proxy. Only environment variable names are included here.

<details>
<summary>Exact local configuration</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: shared/gpt-6.1-sol
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_base: os.environ/QA_UPSTREAM_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/QA_UPSTREAM_KEY
      order: 0
    model_info:
      id: qa-shared-deployment
  - model_name: restricted/gpt-6.1-sol
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/openai/gpt-6.1-sol
      api_base: os.environ/QA_UPSTREAM_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/QA_UPSTREAM_KEY
      order: 1
    model_info:
      id: qa-restricted-deployment
      access_groups:
        - Restricted
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/QA_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: os.environ/QA_REDIS_PORT
router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: os.environ/QA_REDIS_PORT
  num_retries: 0
  timeout: 90
```

</details>

The proxy command in each checkout was:

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py \
  --config /tmp/litellm-ws-alias-qa/config.yaml \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 40873 --num_workers 2 \
  --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Both runs logged two serving worker PIDs. The migration flag is now a deprecated no-op, but was retained in both runs to match the repository's QA command.

<details>
<summary>Exact client used for both runs</summary>

Save this as /tmp/litellm-ws-alias-qa/exercise.py. It creates an isolated test team and key, exercises WebSockets with and without a query model, checks the adjacent HTTP route, and verifies direct access to the shared model is denied. Because the upstream gateway already encodes response IDs, it reads the local spend log to identify the local deployment.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Final
from urllib.parse import urlencode
from uuid import uuid4

import httpx2
from websockets.sync.client import connect

def recorded_deployment(base: str, request_id: str, key_alias: str) -> str:
    started: Final = datetime.now(UTC)
    deadline: Final = time.monotonic() + 60
    with httpx2.Client(
        base_url=base,
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk-local-websocket-alias-qa-only"},
        timeout=15,
        limits=httpx2.Limits(max_connections=2, max_keepalive_connections=1),
    ) as admin:
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            response = admin.get(
                "/spend/logs/v2",
                params={
                    "start_date": (started - timedelta(minutes=5)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                    "end_date": (started + timedelta(minutes=5)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                    "key_alias": key_alias,
                    "page_size": 20,
                    "sort_order": "desc",
                },
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            for row in response.json()["data"]:
                if row["request_id"] == request_id:
                    model_id = row["model_id"]
                    assert isinstance(model_id, str) and model_id.startswith("qa-")
                    return model_id
            time.sleep(0.2)
    raise TimeoutError("The local proxy did not flush the QA spend log within 60 seconds")


def main() -> None:
    phase, port = sys.argv[1:]
    base: Final = f"http://127.0.0.1:{int(port)}"
    raw_model: Final = "openai/openai/gpt-6.1-sol"
    restricted_model: Final = "restricted/gpt-6.1-sol"
    expected: Final = "qa-shared-deployment" if phase == "before" else "qa-restricted-deployment"
    suffix: Final = phase + "-" + uuid4().hex[:8]
    team_id: Final = "qa-alias-team-" + suffix
    user_id: Final = "qa-alias-user-" + suffix
    key_alias: Final = "qa-alias-key-" + suffix
    master_headers: Final = {"Authorization": "Bearer sk-local-websocket-alias-qa-only"}
    with httpx2.Client(
        base_url=base,
        headers=master_headers,
        timeout=100,
        limits=httpx2.Limits(max_connections=4, max_keepalive_connections=2),
    ) as admin:
        for path, body in (
            (
                "/team/new",
                {
                    "team_id": team_id,
                    "team_alias": "Alias routing QA " + phase,
                    "models": ["Restricted"],
                    "model_aliases": {raw_model: restricted_model},
                },
            ),
            (
                "/user/new",
                {
                    "user_id": user_id,
                    "user_role": "internal_user",
                    "teams": [team_id],
                    "auto_create_key": False,
                },
            ),
        ):
            result = admin.post(path, json=body)
            print(f"SETUP {path} status={result.status_code}", flush=True)
            result.raise_for_status()
        generated: Final = admin.post(
            "/key/generate",
            json={
                "team_id": team_id,
                "user_id": user_id,
                "key_alias": key_alias,
                "models": ["all-team-models"],
                "duration": "1h",
            },
        )
        print(f"SETUP /key/generate status={generated.status_code}", flush=True)
        generated.raise_for_status()
        key: Final = generated.json()["key"]

    headers: Final = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}
    for query, nested in ((False, False), (True, False)):
        endpoint = (
            f"ws://127.0.0.1:{int(port)}/v1/responses"
            + ("?" + urlencode({"model": raw_model}) if query else "")
        )
        payload = {
            "model": raw_model,
            "input": "Reply with OK.",
            "stream": True,
            "max_output_tokens": 32,
        }
        frame = (
            {"type": "response.create", "response": payload}
            if nested
            else {"type": "response.create", **payload}
        )
        with connect(endpoint, additional_headers=headers, open_timeout=10, close_timeout=5) as websocket:
            websocket.send(json.dumps(frame))
            while True:
                event = json.loads(websocket.recv(timeout=100))
                kind = event.get("type")
                if kind == "error" or kind == "response.failed":
                    error = event.get("error") or event.get("response", {}).get("error") or {}
                    print(
                        f"WS_ERROR phase={phase} query={query} nested={nested} "
                        f"type={error.get('type')} code={error.get('code')}",
                        flush=True,
                    )
                    raise RuntimeError("The live provider refused the QA request")
                if kind in ("response.completed", "response.incomplete"):
                    response = event["response"]
                    selected = recorded_deployment(base, response["id"], key_alias)
                    print(
                        f"WS_RESULT phase={phase} query={query} nested={nested} "
                        f"event={kind} deployment={selected} usage={json.dumps(response.get('usage'))}",
                        flush=True,
                    )
                    assert selected == expected, (selected, expected)
                    break

    with httpx2.Client(
        base_url=base,
        headers=headers,
        timeout=100,
        limits=httpx2.Limits(max_connections=4, max_keepalive_connections=2),
    ) as client:
        http_response: Final = client.post(
            "/v1/responses",
            json={"model": raw_model, "input": "Reply with OK.", "max_output_tokens": 32},
        )
        print(f"HTTP_RESULT phase={phase} status={http_response.status_code}", flush=True)
        http_response.raise_for_status()
        http_selected: Final = recorded_deployment(base, http_response.json()["id"], key_alias)
        print(f"HTTP_DEPLOYMENT phase={phase} deployment={http_selected}", flush=True)
        assert http_selected == "qa-restricted-deployment"
        denied: Final = client.post(
            "/v1/responses",
            json={"model": "shared/gpt-6.1-sol", "input": "Reply with OK.", "max_output_tokens": 32},
        )
        print(f"DENIED_RESULT phase={phase} status={denied.status_code}", flush=True)
        assert denied.status_code == 403
    print(f"QA_PASS phase={phase}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

### Before (db8ad3b13e7320bf835205cae58be5a58e0ff366)

1. Start the unmodified proxy with the shared configuration.
2. Run python /tmp/litellm-ws-alias-qa/exercise.py before 40873.
3. Observe both WebSocket calls selecting the shared deployment while HTTP routing and direct-access denial remain correct.

```text
WS_RESULT phase=before query=False nested=False event=response.completed deployment=qa-shared-deployment
WS_RESULT phase=before query=True nested=False event=response.completed deployment=qa-shared-deployment
HTTP_RESULT phase=before status=200
HTTP_DEPLOYMENT phase=before deployment=qa-restricted-deployment
DENIED_RESULT phase=before status=403
QA_PASS phase=before
```

### After (48138d6f514bc158af6f60d419cc13fdcabbd4e4)

1. Start the patched proxy with the same shared configuration.
2. Run python /tmp/litellm-ws-alias-qa/exercise.py after 40873.
3. Observe both WebSocket calls selecting the restricted deployment. The adjacent HTTP call and direct-access denial are unchanged.

```text
WS_RESULT phase=after query=False nested=False event=response.completed deployment=qa-restricted-deployment
WS_RESULT phase=after query=True nested=False event=response.completed deployment=qa-restricted-deployment
HTTP_RESULT phase=after status=200
HTTP_DEPLOYMENT phase=after deployment=qa-restricted-deployment
DENIED_RESULT phase=after status=403
QA_PASS phase=after
```

Each successful WebSocket response reported 10 input tokens and 5 output tokens in both runs. The production diff is one removed argument. Later test-only assertion and formatting adjustments did not change the live-tested production source.

The regression was first run against the original endpoint and failed with shared-deployment instead of restricted-deployment. The final related test command and result were:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/response_api_endpoints/test_endpoints.py tests/unit/test_assert_ci_coverage.py -q --timeout=45 --maxfail=3
# 378 passed, 84 warnings
make lint LINT_JOBS=4
# Exit 0, all repository lint and baseline type gates passed
```

Warnings came from existing schema definitions and test deprecations and were not suppressed. The large existing test file also has accumulated standalone type and formatting diagnostics. The new regression method had zero standalone type diagnostics, and unrelated formatting was left unchanged.

## Type

Bug Fix, Test

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Live provider checks used standard flat Responses frames.
- Nested-frame alias selection is covered by the unit regression.
- CI and automated PR reviews remain pending submission.

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests cover the reported failure and its query/frame entry variants, and the live comparison confirms the intended deployment is used.

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes WebSocket model resolution and team alias routing; risk is mis-routing to the wrong deployment if preprocessing assumptions differ from HTTP /v1/responses.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes team model aliases being dropped on the Responses WebSocket path** so multi-deployment routers pick the team's restricted deployment instead of a shared one with the same provider model.
> 
> The WebSocket session handler **stops passing `model=resolved_model` into `common_processing_pre_call_logic`**. That explicit override was re-applying the raw first-frame/query model and undoing alias rewriting done elsewhere in preprocessing, which let the router fall through to another deployment.
> 
> A **parametrized regression test** exercises team `model_aliases` for WebSocket turns (optional `?model=`, flat vs nested `response.create` frames) and asserts the response is tied to the authorized deployment id.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c7f0d3038486b9bf3136389118c46a117f7b6c6d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(proxy): fetch blog posts without blocking the event loop
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/35a7f0e9fbf94f4391800c4d61131e5d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/35a7f0e9fbf94f4391800c4d61131e5d?variant=devin
Requested by: @yassin-berriai

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `/public/litellm_blog_posts` did a blocking 5 s RSS fetch inside an async route
- When docs.litellm.ai is unreachable the whole worker froze for 5 s
- Failures were not cached, so every Admin UI load froze it again

How it solves it:

- The route now awaits the existing pooled async HTTP client (same 5 s timeout)
- The local fallback is cached for the existing 1 hour TTL, same as a success
- Concurrent misses share one refresh per worker

## User Flow

Before: an admin on a proxy that cannot reach docs.litellm.ai sees every Admin UI page stall for about 5 s

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the UI calls GET /public/litellm_blog_posts
2. That request waits 5 s for the RSS fetch to time out, then returns the bundled posts
3. Every other request in flight on that worker (GET /team/list, /v2/user/info, /health/liveliness) also waits the same 5 s
4. On the next page load the same 5 s stall happens again

After: only the blog widget waits, once per hour, and the rest of the UI stays fast

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the UI calls GET /public/litellm_blog_posts
2. That request still waits up to 5 s once, then returns the bundled posts
3. Other requests on the worker return right away, around 1 ms for /health/liveliness
4. Later page loads get the cached posts in about 1 ms with no network attempt

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. A local TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:18443 accepts connections and never answers, which reproduces the TLS handshake timeout seen in production. The proxy runs with one worker on purpose so the blocking call is not hidden by a second worker, and without Redis or Postgres since neither is involved.

```yaml
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/BLOG_QA_MASTER_KEY
```

```sh
LITELLM_BLOG_POSTS_URL=https://127.0.0.1:18443/rss.xml \
  python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config blog_proxy.yaml --port 18400 --num_workers 1

curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'blog %{time_total} HTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18400/public/litellm_blog_posts &
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'liveliness %{time_total} HTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18400/health/liveliness
wait
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'repeat blog %{time_total} HTTP %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18400/public/litellm_blog_posts
```

### Before (3d389262a4fc)

1. The blog request and the unrelated liveliness probe both take about 5 s, and the repeat request stalls again

```text
blog 5.054404 HTTP 200
liveliness 5.019989 HTTP 200
repeat blog 5.057138 HTTP 200
```

The proxy log shows `_ssl.c:994: The handshake operation timed out` on both blog requests.

### After, with concurrent refresh coalescing

1. The liveliness probe returns in about 1 ms while the blog fetch is still waiting, and the repeat blog request is served from cache

```text
liveliness 0.002604 HTTP 200
blog 5.007880 HTTP 200
repeat blog 0.001293 HTTP 200
```

Regression tests in `tests/unit/proxy/public_endpoints/test_blog_posts_endpoint.py` were run against the original code and all of them failed. The concurrency test fails because the other coroutine never runs. The failure-caching cases (timeout, invalid XML, empty feed) fail with two network attempts instead of one.

### Concurrent refresh proof

The same fixture now counts accepted TLS connections and can start 20 parallel curl requests against a fresh proxy. The old async implementation at ff1e758 opens 20 connections. The coalescing implementation opens one. All 20 calls return HTTP 200 in both runs, with bundled posts after the timeout.

```sh
BURST_ONLY=true BLOG_QA_MASTER_KEY=<local-fixture-key> .venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/blog_live.py burst_before
BURST_ONLY=true BLOG_QA_MASTER_KEY=<local-fixture-key> .venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/blog_live.py burst_after
```

The before run restores the utility from ff1e758 and verifies it with cmp. The after run restores the final utility and verifies it with cmp. The new gated-fetch test runs 32 simultaneous callers against cold and expired cache, covering success and failure. Mutation against ff1e758 produces

```text
E           AssertionError: assert 32 == 1
FAILED test_concurrent_blog_refresh_is_shared[False-False]
FAILED test_concurrent_blog_refresh_is_shared[False-True]
FAILED test_concurrent_blog_refresh_is_shared[True-False]
FAILED test_concurrent_blog_refresh_is_shared[True-True]
4 failed, 9 deselected in 0.84s
```

A separate test cancels the refresh owner and proves a queued caller can recover. Async-with holds the lock through cache publication and releases it on cancellation or error.

### Admin UI

The UI check uses local Postgres, the same hanging listener on 127.0.0.1:18444, and a one-worker proxy serving its bundled UI on 18401. The before proxy uses the original utility and endpoint from merge-base 3d389262a4fc on 18402. Both original files matched their git blob hashes. The baseline process imports those modules before the source files are restored to the final code.

```yaml
model_list: []
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/BLOG_QA_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

```sh
.venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/blog_ui_listener.py
BLOG_QA_MASTER_KEY=<local-fixture-key> LITELLM_BLOG_POSTS_URL=https://127.0.0.1:18444/rss.xml LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONPATH=/home/ubuntu/repos/litellm .venv/bin/python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config /home/ubuntu/blog_ui_proxy.yaml --port 18401 --num_workers 1
```

Open http://localhost:18401/ui/ in Chrome, enter admin and the local master key, then open Blog in the header. The fixed dashboard displays bundled posts. Open DevTools Network and reload for the cached timings. The baseline uses the same browser login, DB, UI and listener on http://localhost:18402/ui/.

Before, blog takes 5.09 s, list calls take 5.17 and 5.18 s, and info takes 5.16 s.

![Baseline dashboard requests stalled behind the blog fetch](https://app.devin.ai/attachments/4a1316fe-492d-4889-bc19-318535fa89f3/dashboard_before_network.png)

After, the loaded dashboard shows bundled posts in the blog dropdown.

![Fixed dashboard with bundled blog posts](https://app.devin.ai/attachments/52cca9b0-f60e-46b8-82eb-fe2cb44fcc72/dashboard_bundled_posts.png)

After a reload, cached blog takes 13 ms, list calls take 45 and 93 ms, and info takes 69 ms.

![Fixed dashboard and fast cached blog and admin requests](https://app.devin.ai/attachments/c8111577-a68a-4446-ad28-069f5d84ecd3/dashboard_cached_network.png)

Some unrelated unchanged dashboard requests return 404, including available_users. The measured blog, list and info calls return HTTP 200. Those unrelated UI states were not changed.

### Final checks, 30f1294b534ffd1569456af1bbb48332c5d3000d

```sh
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/test_get_blog_posts.py tests/unit/proxy/public_endpoints/test_blog_posts_endpoint.py -q
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/test_assert_ci_coverage.py -q
.venv/bin/ruff check litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_blog_posts.py litellm/proxy/public_endpoints/public_endpoints.py tests/unit/proxy/public_endpoints/test_blog_posts_endpoint.py
uv run --no-sync python litellm/scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --base origin/main
uv run --no-sync python litellm/scripts/type_discipline_gate.py --base origin/main
uv run --no-sync python litellm/scripts/type_check_gate.py --base origin/main
```

```text
31 passed in 1.09s
53 passed in 4.52s
All checks passed!
OK: no strict rule grew past its merge-base count (base origin/main)
OK: no LIT rule grew past its merge-base count (base origin/main)
OK: every basedpyright rule is within its ceiling (95287 errors total, base 3d389262a4fc)
```

The endpoint tests also no longer patch a class method. They exercise the real utility with a seeded cache or inject the module fetcher. The client fixture clears cache in teardown. This addresses the old-commit Greptile testing-rule finding along with the concurrent refresh finding.

The full A-BB taxonomy audit lists every applicable item with its changed lines and the relevant not-applicable blocks, [audit](https://app.devin.ai/attachments/cc582949-132d-4569-b23a-f7526bbe9725/blog_taxonomy_audit.md).

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Refresh coalescing and caching are local to each worker
- The sync `get_blog_posts` stays blocking, but no proxy route calls it anymore
- An outage now shows bundled posts for up to 1 hour after the feed recovers

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to a public read-only blog widget fetch with offline/local fallback; main caveat is worker-local caching may delay showing a recovered feed for up to an hour.
> 
> **Overview**
> The `/public/litellm_blog_posts` route no longer calls the blocking sync RSS helper; it **awaits** `GetBlogPosts.aget_blog_posts` with the pooled async `_fetch_remote_bytes` client so a 5 s timeout does not stall the whole worker.
> 
> `GetBlogPosts` gains an async fetch path with **per-loop refresh locking** so concurrent cache misses share one network attempt, and a shared `_cache_posts` path so **successful and fallback (local backup) results** are written to the same 1-hour in-process cache—preventing repeated stalls when the feed is down. RSS parsing now accepts `bytes` as well as `str`.
> 
> Unit tests were expanded to cover non-blocking behavior, failure/success caching, concurrent refresh coalescing, and recovery when a refresh task is cancelled.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 30f1294b534ffd1569456af1bbb48332c5d3000d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: fix(gemini): add batch and priority image output token prices to gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image
body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- The Gemini API pricing page states Batch and Priority per image output prices for Gemini 2.5 Flash Image that the catalog row lacks
- The row already carries Batch, Flex and Priority text prices, so image generation under those tiers is tracked at the Standard image rate

How it solves it:

- Adds `output_cost_per_image_token_batches` and `output_cost_per_image_token_priority` to `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image`, the same fields its siblings `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-image` and `gemini/gemini-3-pro-image` already use
- Same edit in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`

## Rows changed

Source for every value: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (now served from https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing, fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-12), section "Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana)". The footnote in that section reads "Image output is priced at $30 per 1,000,000 tokens. Output images up to 1024x1024px consume 1290 tokens and are equivalent to $0.039 per image", which is how the existing `output_cost_per_image_token: 3e-05` on this row maps $0.039 per image to a per token price. The tier values below use the same 1290 token image

| Row | Field | Evidence | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image` | `output_cost_per_image_token_batches: 1.5e-05` | Batch table, "Output price ... $0.0195 per image" (half of Standard, $15 per 1M image tokens) | page |
| `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image` | `output_cost_per_image_token_priority: 5.4e-05` | Priority table, "Output price ... $0.0702 per image" (1.8x Standard, $54 per 1M image tokens) | page |

The Flex table also states "$0.0195 per image", but the catalog has no `output_cost_per_image_token_flex` field (no row carries one and the cost calculator does not read it), so the Flex image price stays out until such a field exists. The Standard, Batch, Flex and Priority text input and output prices on this row already match the page

The `prices gemini` command reports no structured price API for this provider, so every value comes from the page. The rest of the pricing page (287 price cells across the Gemini 4, 3.x, 2.5, Omni, Live, TTS, Decision, Embedding and Robotics sections, Standard, Batch, Flex and Priority tiers) matches the catalog's `gemini/` rows

Rulings applied: `gemini-price-change-2027-keep-current` and `gemini-4-argon-dec-2026-price-change-keep-current` (the page's December 2026 and January 2027 prices are not pre-staged), `gemini-robotics-er-2-keep-current-rate`, `gemini-unrepresentable-modality-prices-leave-out` and `gemini-nano-banana-pro-tier-image-prices-leave-out` (Embedding 2 image input and per tier image input prices left out), `gemini-contributor-tier-prices-leave-out`, `gemini-image-tier-prices-stay-after-page-drop`, `gemini-delisted-no-date-keep`

## Delisted by the provider

No deprecation date is published for these ids, so their rows are kept unchanged per ruling `gemini-delisted-no-date-keep`: gemini-exp-1206, gemini/gemini-exp-1114, gemini/gemini-gemma-2-27b-it, gemini/gemini-gemma-2-9b-it, gemini/gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview-native-audio-09-2025, gemini/gemma-3-27b-it, gemini/imagen-3.0-fast-generate-001, gemini/imagen-3.0-generate-001, gemini/learnlm-1.5-pro-experimental, gemini/lyria-3.5-clip-preview, gemini/lyria-3.5-pro-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-fast-generate-001, gemini/veo-3.1-generate-001. The three Veo 3.1 preview ids (gemini/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-generate-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview) already carry `deprecation_date: 2026-10-22` from the deprecations page
