title: fix(rate-limit): hold router fallbacks, nested calls, WebSocket turns and oversized prompts to a borrowing team's model share
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Six review findings on #51328 were left open after it merged
- Router fallbacks to a model skipped the team's borrowed share on it
- Nested calls (LLM judges, silent experiments) charged the parent request's team share
- Native Responses WebSocket turns were never settled against the team share
- A saturated team could send one prompt larger than its whole share
- A Redis read failure on a WebSocket turn surfaced as a 500

How it solves it:

- `RouterFallbackRateLimitCheck` also asks the dynamic limiter before a fallback target
- Settlement reads the stash of the call it settles, never a nested call's
- Settlement reads `combined_usage_object` and WebSocket event lists like the regular limiter
- At saturation the team counter holds the estimated tokens and settles to actual usage, refunded on failure
- An unreadable counter on a WebSocket turn raises the regular limiter's retryable 503
- The reservation remembers its rate-limit window, so a settlement or refund never lands on a newer window, and a committed fallback attempt raises the target's saturation count
- A saturated fallback target holds the prompt's estimated tokens on the team's share before dispatch, settles them to actual usage and gives them back when the attempt fails. The target's model-wide count rises on every admitted attempt, on its own, so an exhausted team share cannot cancel it
- A prompt the token estimator cannot read holds the minimum and still goes through admission instead of skipping the limiter
- The fallback hold is estimated for the request's own call type, read from the per-request stash the pre-call hook fills, so a Responses fallback holds `max_output_tokens` as well as its input instead of being read as an embedding
- The hold follows `token_rate_limit_type`, so an output-only limit holds the prompt's output budget and an input-only limit its input, as settlement already did. A direct request without an explicit output cap is estimated as the regular limiter would cap it, and a successful admission writes that cap onto the request, so an unbounded answer cannot run past the share before settlement. A refused admission, or an input-only limit, leaves the request untouched. A fallback attempt is dispatched from the router's own copy of the request, so its hold is the same bounded estimate but the dispatched request stays uncapped until settlement, a router follow-up
- A failed attempt that recorded usage (an interrupted stream, a post-call rejection) is charged that usage, a full refund only when it recorded none

## User Flow

Before: with borrowing on and `sol` falling back to `luna`, a team with `model_rpm_limit: {luna: 1}` keeps getting served by luna after its share is gone

1. The admin sets `team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams: true` and `fallbacks: [{sol: [luna]}]`, and sol's upstream is down
2. A key on the team sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "sol"` three times
3. All three return 200 with `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 1`, served by luna, while a direct `"model": "luna"` call is held with 429 `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated`

After: the fallback is held to the same share as a direct call

1. Same admin settings and the same down upstream
2. The same key sends the same POST three times
3. The first returns 200 via luna, the second and third return the fallback error, "Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it"

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10560

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, `uv run pytest tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_fallback_rate_limit.py tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_parallel_request_limiter_v3.py tests/unit/test_assert_ci_coverage.py` (699 passed)
- [x] `make check` passes at 9289b0e0eb, main merged in for #51350's steering path, which now carries the request body and call type into the team hold
- [x] Integration test red on main, green at the fix

## Testing

Unit, in `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py`. Twenty-five new tests: a nested call's tokens are not charged to the request's team share while the owning call's are, a WebSocket turn's `combined_usage_object` counts against the share, an unreadable counter on a WebSocket turn gives a 503, a prompt larger than the share is refused before the call once the model saturates, the reservation settles to actual usage, the reservation is refunded when the call fails, a fallback target is refused once it saturates and the share on it is used, a fallback target still borrows while idle with its tokens charged to that share, a committed fallback attempt counts toward the target's saturation, a read-only fallback check (the one that runs before the v3 gate) uses none of the team's share, a success without a model group still releases its reservation, idle fallbacks past the team's RPM share still count toward the target's saturation, a saturated fallback target refuses a prompt larger than the team's remaining tokens and holds then settles a smaller one, a fallback attempt that fails gives back the tokens it held, a prompt the token estimator cannot read is still held to the team's share, a saturated Responses fallback holds the output budget as well as the input, an output-only token limit holds only the prompt's output budget, a request without `max_tokens` leaves admission capped to the team's share, a refused admission and an input-only limit leave the request's output uncapped, a prompt that fits only once its output is capped is admitted, a late failure from a fallback that did not serve is charged to that target rather than the admitting model, a served fallback's hold is not refunded again under the alias the request used, a steered request's images are counted for the model that serves it, and a failed attempt that recorded usage is charged that usage instead of refunded. Mutation checks, each one red: dropping the call id check in `request_stash_for_callback`, returning `None` for `combined_usage_object` in `_usage_of`, removing the `RateLimitUnverifiableError` handler, passing `tokens: 0` for the team descriptor at saturation, skipping the `-reserved` settlement delta, skipping the refund, returning `True` unconditionally from `async_fallback_target_allowed`, dropping the window guard on the refund, dropping the model-wide increment in the fallback commit, keeping the early `model_group` return ahead of settlement, putting the team share back into the model-wide atomic batch, passing `tokens: 0` on the fallback hold, skipping the hold refund in `async_log_failure_event`, letting the estimator's error reach the fail-open handler, estimating the fallback hold with no call type, estimating the hold as total under an output-only limit, dropping the output cap, capping before admission, capping under an input-only limit, estimating the uncapped request, refunding the whole hold on a failure that recorded usage.

Integration, in `tests/integration/routing/test_team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity.py`, `test_a_fallback_target_is_held_to_the_teams_share_on_it_once_it_saturates`. Red on main (`assert 200 != 200`, the second fallback was served), green at the fix, the other six cases still pass (7 passed).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Two-worker proxy, shared Redis, `--num_workers 2`, both runs checked for two `Application startup complete` lines. Config `luna` has `tpm: 400, rpm: 100` and `mock_response`, `sol` points at a closed port so it always fails, `router_settings.fallbacks: [{sol: [luna]}]`, `num_retries: 0`, `saturation_threshold: 0.0` so luna counts as saturated from the first call, borrowing on. Team A has `model_rpm_limit: {luna: 1}`. Team D is created without limits, its key is generated, then `/team/update` adds the same limit, so the key carries no inherited copy.

<summary>Before, main at 7c7e02b06f</summary>

```
call 2 to sol HTTP 200  x-litellm-model-group: luna x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks: 1   ok model=gpt-4o-mini

```
</details>

<details>

```
call 2 to sol HTTP 500    litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.

LiteLLM: model group 'sol' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate li
```

Token hold on the fallback target. Team E has `model_tpm_limit: {luna: 60}`, same config, `max_tokens: 5`. The first call to sol carries a 300 word prompt, the next two carry three words. The Redis line is the team's luna token counter after each call.

Proxy command, run from the checkout under test, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... DATABASE_URL=... python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config10.yaml --port 4028 --num_workers 2 --use_prisma_db_push`. Client, `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4028/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"sol","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'` three times per team. The nested call, WebSocket usage, reservation and 503 paths are proven by the unit tests above, they need an LLM judge guardrail, a native Responses WebSocket client or a Redis outage to drive live.

## Caveats

A hold on a fallback target is given back by that attempt's failure event or by the serving call's settlement. If neither fires, the hold expires with the rate-limit window.

title: feat(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): priority_class_share_splits_equally_among_active_teams splits a priority class share among the teams active on a model
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- One team can empty its whole priority class pool, teammates get 429 at zero usage
- An idle class's reserved share sits unused while another class is throttled

How it solves it:

- New `priority_reservation_settings.priority_class_share_splits_equally_among_active_teams` (default false)
- Tracks which teams used each model this window (one Redis sorted set per model)
- Renormalizes class weights over classes with an active team, splits each class equally among its active teams
- At saturation each team is held to its own share, 429 `rate_limited_by: priority_class_share_saturated`
- Off, or a key with no team, keeps today's shared class pool

## User Flow

Before: team B (interactive) is refused on a model it has not touched because team A (also interactive) used up the interactive share, while the batch share sits idle

1. Admin sets `priority_reservation: {interactive: 0.6, batch: 0.4}` on a `tpm: 1000` model and gives teams A and B `metadata.priority: interactive`
2. Team A sends 20 POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions of 30 tokens, every one returns 200 and the remaining-tokens header walks 600 to 30
3. Team B sends its first POST to the same URL and gets 429 "Priority-based rate limit exceeded ... Remaining: 0" with the model at 60% usage
4. A batch team sends and gets 200 with 400 tokens still remaining, so 400 of the model stayed unused while B was refused

After: the same request from team B succeeds, team A is the one held back, and interactive gets the whole model while batch is idle

1. Admin adds `priority_class_share_splits_equally_among_active_teams: true` under `priority_reservation_settings` and restarts the proxy
2. Team A sends the same 20 POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, every one returns 200 and the remaining-tokens header walks 1000 to 430 (interactive is the only active class)
3. Team B sends its first POST and gets 200 with 500 remaining (two active interactive teams, 500 each), then A's next POST gets 429 with `rate_limited_by: priority_class_share_saturated` and "Active teams in class: 2, Team share: 500"
4. A batch team sends and gets 200 with 400 remaining, B's next POST gets 200 with 240 remaining (interactive back to 600, 300 per team)

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10559

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup for both legs. Two uvicorn workers (two `Started server process` PIDs in the log) sharing one local Redis for router state, coordination and rate-limit counters, Postgres for teams and keys, `mock_response` on the model so no provider is called. Env vars set: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`.

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4031 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>config.yaml (Before leg). The After leg adds one line, `priority_class_share_splits_equally_among_active_teams: true`, under `priority_reservation_settings`</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"
      tpm: 1000
      rpm: 1000

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379
  num_retries: 0

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"]
  priority_reservation:
    interactive: 0.6
    batch: 0.4
  priority_reservation_settings:
    default_priority: 1.0
    saturation_threshold: 0.0
    saturation_check_cache_ttl: 5

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>leg.sh, the client script (creates three teams and keys, sends the calls, prints status, rate limit headers and the error text)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: leg.sh <port>   (needs LITELLM_MASTER_KEY)
set -u
P=http://127.0.0.1:$1; MK=$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
redis-cli --scan --pattern '*luna*' | xargs -r redis-cli del >/dev/null
redis-cli --scan --pattern '*priority_model*' | xargs -r redis-cli del >/dev/null
mk_team() { curl -s $P/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"team_alias\":\"$1\",\"metadata\":{\"priority\":\"$2\"}}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["team_id"])'; }
mk_key() { curl -s $P/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MK" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "{\"team_id\":\"$1\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])'; }
call() { # name key
  out=$(curl -s -D - -o /tmp/body.$$ $P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $2" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"model":"luna","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}')
  code=$(echo "$out" | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')
  hdr=$(echo "$out" | grep -iE '^(rate_limited_by|x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens|x-ratelimit-priority_class_share_saturated-remaining-tokens|x-litellm-saturation):' | tr -d '\r' | tr '\n' ' ')
  if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then printf "%-8s HTTP %s  %s ok usage=%s\n" "$1" "$code" "$hdr" "$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.load(open("/tmp/body.'$$'"))["usage"]["total_tokens"])')"; else printf "%-8s HTTP %s  %s %s\n" "$1" "$code" "$hdr" "$(python3 -c 'import json;print(json.load(open("/tmp/body.'$$'"))["error"]["message"][:400])')"; fi
}
A=$(mk_team teamA interactive); B=$(mk_team teamB interactive); C=$(mk_team teamC batch)
KA=$(mk_key $A); KB=$(mk_key $B); KC=$(mk_key $C)
echo "## luna tpm 1000, interactive 0.6 / batch 0.4, saturation_threshold 0.0 (shares enforced from the first call). Team A (interactive) sends 20 calls of 30 tokens, teams B (interactive) and C (batch) idle"
for i in $(seq 1 20); do call "A $i" $KA; sleep 0.3; done
echo "## team A at 600 tokens. Team B (interactive, used nothing) sends its first call, then A sends one more"
call "B 1" $KB
sleep 6
call "A 21" $KA
call "B 2" $KB
echo "## team C (batch) wakes up, then A and B send one more each"
call "C 1" $KC
sleep 6
call "A 22" $KA
call "B 3" $KB
call "C 2" $KC
```

</details>

### Before (6a98d09261, main before #51328 landed. #51328 only adds an opt-in team model limit path, the shared class pool path exercised here is identical at the merge base 19ffe3a5f2)

1. `bash leg.sh 4031` against the proxy started with the Before config

<details>
<summary>Output: A alone burns the 600 interactive pool, B (interactive, zero usage) is refused, batch has 400 unused</summary>

```text
## luna tpm 1000, interactive 0.6 / batch 0.4, saturation_threshold 0.0 (shares enforced from the first call). Team A (interactive) sends 20 calls of 30 tokens, teams B (interactive) and C (batch) idle
A 1      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 600  ok usage=30
A 2      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 570  ok usage=30
A 3      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 540  ok usage=30
A 4      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 510  ok usage=30
A 5      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 480  ok usage=30
A 6      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 450  ok usage=30
A 7      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 420  ok usage=30
A 8      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 390  ok usage=30
A 9      HTTP 200  x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 360  ok usage=30
```

- The remaining-tokens header for a team share is `x-ratelimit-priority_class_share_saturated-remaining-tokens`, following the `priority_model` naming
- When `team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams` is also on, the tighter of the two shares wins
- A team's counter is keyed by model and team, so a team whose keys carry different priorities spends one share, computed from the class its current request carries, whatever class another worker's clock last recorded it in
- Responses WebSocket turns are held to the class share once the model saturates, the same way they are held to the borrowing team model limit. A frame check that computed a share writes it into the connection stash, and a frame whose registry call failed leaves the stash alone, so settlement charges the counter the connection was last checked against even when the registry was down at connect and recovered later
- The per-team counter value is `{len(model)}:{model}:{team_id}`, so a model name with a colon cannot collide with another model and team pair. Settlement rebuilds that value from the served model group and the settled team id, so tokens a router fallback served on model B land on the team's counter for B, not for the model the request named
- Without Redis, the active-team list is kept in process memory and pruned by each team's last-seen time
- Real teams are stored in the registry under a team prefix, so a team id cannot spell a pool marker
- Below saturation a team's share counter is bumped through the atomic increment at the model-wide limit, so every accepted request counts and the counter is complete when the share later grows

body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add fal nano banana 2.1

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Fal's Nano Banana 2.1 has no cost map row, so it bills $0
- `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` is sent to `fal-ai/google/...` and Fal answers 404
- Fal bills it by tokens but returns no usage, only an `x-fal-billable-units` header
- Seedance reference-to-video drops `input_reference`, and Fal fails the job

How it solves it:

- Adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` and `/edit` rows to both cost maps
- Adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest` and `/edit` aliases pointing at them
- Keeps owner-qualified ids like `google/...` as they are in the Fal URL
- Adds `output_cost_per_billable_unit`, billed as the header value times that price
- Lets a deployment's own `output_cost_per_billable_unit` replace the catalog price
- Teaches the Rust registry check the new field, the same two commits as #51365
- Falls back to Fal's per-image price by resolution when the header is missing
- Sends `input_reference` as `image_urls` on Seedance reference-to-video
- Keeps `/fal_ai` passthrough closed to rows billed by reported units

## User Flow

Before: a developer who wants Fal's Nano Banana 2.1 cannot generate an image through the proxy

1. The proxy admin adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` to `model_list` as `fal-nano-banana-2.1` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `"model": "fal-nano-banana-2.1"`
3. They get HTTP 404, `Application "google" not found`

After: the same request returns an image and is billed what Fal charged for it

1. The proxy admin adds `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-2.1` to `model_list` as `fal-nano-banana-2.1` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `"model": "fal-nano-banana-2.1"`
3. They get HTTP 200 with one image URL and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.049490441`, the dollar amount Fal reported for that call
4. `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest` and POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits with `fal_ai/google/nano-banana-latest/edit` behave the same way

1. `gen21` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.049490441`. The proxy log shows the call went to `https://fal.run/google/nano-banana-2.1`
2. `genlatest` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.045802427`, sent to the same URL
3. Both costs are the per-call amount Fal reported. The per-image fallback would have been exactly 0.04

#### Nano Banana latest edit

1. `editlatest` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL, sent to `https://fal.run/google/nano-banana-2.1/edit`
2. The response headers are `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.046751111` and `llm_provider-x-fal-billable-units: 0.046751111`

#### Deployment with its own unit price

1. `editcustomunit` returns HTTP 200 with one image URL
2. The response headers are `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.087661396` and `llm_provider-x-fal-billable-units: 0.043830698`, which is the deployment's 2.0 times the reported units

#### `/fal_ai` passthrough

1. `ptnb21` returns the same HTTP 400 as before, and the proxy log shows no request to Fal for it
2. `ptnb2` returns HTTP 200 with `"status":"IN_QUEUE"` and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.08`, unchanged
3. One commit earlier, at `52d0db20fa`, `ptnb21` returned HTTP 200 and logged the 0.04 per-image fallback for a call Fal bills by units. The last commit closes that

#### Seedance reference-to-video with `input_reference`

Pricing source. `GET https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing` returns `unit_price: 1`, `unit: "units"`, `currency: "USD"` for `google/nano-banana-2.1` and `google/nano-banana-2.1/edit`, so one billable unit is one dollar. The per-image fallback prices are the representative costs on https://fal.ai/models/google/nano-banana-2.1 and https://fal.ai/models/google/nano-banana-2.1/edit (read 2026-11-11).

Local checks at `c3aea0c64a`: `uv run pytest tests/unit/llms/fal_ai tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_model_latest_aliases.py tests/unit/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_llm_pass_through_endpoints.py` gives 1132 passed and `make check` ends with `check: PASS`. `cargo test --locked -p litellm-model-catalog -p litellm-cost` passes and `check-registry` exits 0 on this branch's cost map.

## Type

🆕 New Feature
🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- `cost-map-guard` stays red until #51365 merges, since it runs `main`'s registry check
- `/fal_ai` passthrough answers HTTP 400 for these rows, as on `main`, since a queue submission returns no billable units

title: feat(replicate): add video generation, image generation and text to speech through the predictions API
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add replicate video, image, and text to speech

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `replicate/...` models only worked for chat
- `/v1/videos` with a Replicate model returned 400 "not supported"
- `/v1/images/generations` returned 200 with an empty `data` list
- `/v1/audio/speech` returned a 500 "Unable to map the custom llm provider"
- the cost map already has 67 video, 145 image and 23 speech Replicate rows nobody could use

How it solves it:

- `ReplicateVideoConfig` creates a prediction, polls `GET /v1/predictions/{id}`, downloads the output file
- `ReplicateImageGenerationConfig` and `ReplicateTextToSpeechConfig` use `Prefer: wait` and poll if needed
- shared prediction URL, auth, output URL and polling helpers in `litellm/llms/replicate/common_utils.py`
- registered in `ProviderConfigManager`, `images/main.py` dispatch and the `speech()` dispatch
- video usage carries `duration_seconds` and `video_resolution` so tiered per-second pricing applies
- new `BaseImageGenerationConfig.async_transform_image_generation_response` hook so the async handler does not block the event loop while a provider polls or downloads
- a poll response with HTTP status 400 or higher raises `ReplicateError` with that status instead of counting as pending
- image and speech polls and downloads honor the deployment `ssl_verify`, video content downloads reuse the handler client
- `extra_body` on speech requests is forwarded as native Replicate input
- `replicate_model_owner` picks the model family for `deployments/...` and `owner/name:version` strings too
- `GET /v1/videos/{id}` keeps the create-time `id` and `model` (the encoded model rides in the status URL fragment, which httpx never sends)
- status and content lookups reject a prediction whose `model` or pinned `version` differs from the encoded one (404), so a caller cannot read another model group's prediction through a shared Replicate credential
- output downloads go through `safe_get` / `async_safe_get` (SSRF validation on every hop) and a response-supplied poll URL must share the API origin
- image `extra_body` is flattened into the prediction input, the audited video and image `prompt` and speech `input` always win over `extra_body`
- `image_generation` passes `_is_async` for Replicate so `aimage_generation` and the proxy run the async transform
- native `width` and `height` in the prediction input become the image response `size`, so per-pixel rows (`input_cost_per_pixel`, for example `replicate/black-forest-labs/flux-2-flex`) price the real dimensions instead of the `1024x1024` fallback
- Replicate prediction `metrics` token counts (`token_input_count`/`token_output_count`, or the `input_token_count`/`output_token_count` spelling) become speech `usage`, so token-priced TTS rows bill generated audio tokens. `HttpxBinaryResponseContent` now takes `usage` in its constructor
- model and deployment paths reject empty, `.` and `..` segments with a 400 and URL encode each segment, so `owner/../other/model` cannot reach a model outside a wildcard grant
- output downloads stream under `REPLICATE_MAX_OUTPUT_DOWNLOAD_BYTES` (env, default 512 MiB) in both sync and async paths and fail with a 502 `ReplicateError` when exceeded. The sync `HTTPHandler.get` gained the `max_response_bytes` option the async handler already had, and `safe_get` forwards it

Model string forms accepted: `replicate/owner/name` (official model endpoint), `replicate/owner/name:version` (`POST /v1/models/{owner}/{name}/versions/{version}/predictions`, so a pinned version cannot leave the authorized model path) and `replicate/deployments/owner/name`.

OpenAI param mapping:

- video: `seconds` -> `duration` (int when whole), `size` as `480p`/`720p`/`1080p`/`4k` or `WxH` -> `resolution` plus `aspect_ratio` (minimax models get `480P`/`768P`/`2K`/`4K` and `ratio`), `input_reference` URL -> `image` (`first_frame_image` for minimax), unknown keys pass through as native input
- image: `n` -> `num_outputs`, `size` `WxH` -> `aspect_ratio`, `response_format: b64_json` downloads the outputs
- speech: `voice` -> `voice` (`voice_id` for minimax and inworld, `speaker` for qwen), `speed` passes through, `response_format` and `instructions` are dropped

## User Flow

Before: a developer who put `replicate/minimax/h3-lite`, `replicate/black-forest-labs/flux-schnell` and `replicate/xai/grok-text-to-speech` in their config cannot use any of them

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos with `{"model": "replicate-video", "prompt": "...", "seconds": "4", "size": "480p"}` and get 400 `video generation is not supported for replicate`
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `{"model": "replicate-image", "prompt": "..."}` and get 200 with `"data": []`, no image
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "replicate-speech", "input": "...", "voice": "ara"}` and get 500 `Unable to map the custom llm provider=replicate`

After: the same three requests work and are priced from the existing cost map rows

1. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos returns 200 with a `video_...` id, `status: queued` and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.05` (4 seconds at the 480p rate)
2. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/videos/{id} moves through `in_progress` to `completed`, then GET https://litellm-domain/v1/videos/{id}/content returns the mp4 bytes
3. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations returns 200 with `data[0].url` pointing at the generated image and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.003`
4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech returns 200 `audio/mpeg` bytes with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00048`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, identical for Before and After. Redis at 127.0.0.1:6379 is wired into both `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`. Two worker processes started in both runs (two `Started server process` lines in the log), so the two-worker check was kept. The proxy ran without a database (`DATABASE_URL` unset), so cost shows up in the `x-litellm-response-cost` header rather than spend logs. Env vars: `REPLICATE_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (random `sk-` value).

Proxy command (Before from the merge base on port 4100, After from the tip on port 4000):

```
uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config ~/qa/replicate_qa_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4000
```

<details>
<summary>replicate_qa_config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: replicate-video
    litellm_params:
      model: replicate/minimax/h3-lite
      api_key: os.environ/REPLICATE_API_KEY
  - model_name: replicate-image
    litellm_params:
      model: replicate/black-forest-labs/flux-schnell
      api_key: os.environ/REPLICATE_API_KEY
  - model_name: replicate-speech
    litellm_params:
      model: replicate/xai/grok-text-to-speech
      api_key: os.environ/REPLICATE_API_KEY

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379

litellm_settings:
  drop_params: True
```

</details>

Client commands (`$B` is the proxy base URL, `$K` is `Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`):

```
curl -s -w "\nhttp %{http_code}\n" -X POST $B/v1/videos -H "$K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"replicate-video","prompt":"a paper boat drifting on a pond at dawn","seconds":"4","size":"480p"}'
curl -s $B/v1/videos/$VID -H "$K"
curl -s -D - -o video.mp4 $B/v1/videos/$VID/content -H "$K"
curl -s -D - -X POST $B/v1/images/generations -H "$K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"replicate-image","prompt":"a red paper boat on a pond, watercolor","n":1,"size":"1024x1024"}'
curl -s -D - -o speech.mp3 -X POST $B/v1/audio/speech -H "$K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"replicate-speech","input":"LiteLLM now routes Replicate speech.","voice":"ara"}'
```

### Before (a3c52e69d30c)

#### video

1. POST /v1/videos -> `http 400`
2. `{"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: video generation is not supported for replicate\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'replicate-video' failed with the error above. No fallback was attempted.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"400"}}`

#### image

1. POST /v1/images/generations -> `http 200` but no image
2. `{"created":1794461912,"background":null,"data":[],"output_format":null,"quality":null,"size":null,"usage":{"total_tokens":0,"input_tokens":0,"input_tokens_details":{"image_tokens":0,"text_tokens":0},"output_tokens":0}}`

#### speech

1. POST /v1/audio/speech -> `http 500`
2. `{"error":{"message":"litellm.APIError: ReplicateException - Unable to map the custom llm provider=replicate to a known provider=[...]"}}`

### After (e6540ca944, final tip 1b0f4d7e9d)

#### video

1. POST /v1/videos -> `http 200 in 9.17s` at this tip (`0.53s` at 217587d9de), cost `0.05`. With `"extra_body": {"prompt": "unaudited"}` at 217587d9de, the Replicate request body logged by the proxy carries only the audited prompt (`'input': {'duration': 4, 'resolution': '480P', 'prompt': 'a paper boat drifting on a pond at dawn'}`), header `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.05`, body `{"id": "video_bGl0...", "status": "queued", "seconds": "4", "size": "480P", "model": "replicate-video", "usage": {"duration_seconds": 4.0, "video_resolution": "480P"}}`
2. GET /v1/videos/{id} every 6s: `in_progress` at 6s through 24s, `completed` at 30s, final body `{"status": "completed", "seconds": "4", "size": "480P", "model": "replicate-video", "usage": {"duration_seconds": 4.0, "video_resolution": "480P"}}`, and its `id` equals the create-time `id`
3. GET /v1/videos/{id}/content -> `http 200 in 0.36s`, `content-type: video/mp4`, 257222 bytes through the bounded download, `file` reports `ISO Media, MP4 Base Media v1`, ffprobe duration 4.459s

#### image

1. POST /v1/images/generations -> `http 200 in 3.94s`, header `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.003`, `size` null (per-image row), `data[0].url` is an `https://ai-gateway-outputs...r2.cloudflarestorage.com/...` link and `b64_json` is null
2. same request with `"response_format": "b64_json"` and `"extra_body": {"seed": 7, "prompt": "ignored"}` -> `http 200 in 3.07s`, cost `0.003`, `data[0].url` null, `b64_json` 155604 chars that decode to 116702 bytes starting with `RIFF` (webp)
3. failure path, `"size": "700x300"` (aspect ratio `7:3`, which flux-schnell rejects inside the model) -> `http 500 in 192s`, body `litellm.APIError: ReplicateException - Model execution failed (User Input Error): Invalid value at aspect_ratio: Invalid option: expected one of "1:1"|"16:9"|...`. The 192s is three router attempts at the 60s `Prefer: wait` ceiling each, see Caveats

4. per-pixel row `replicate-image-pixels` (`replicate/black-forest-labs/flux-2-flex`, `input_cost_per_pixel` 6e-8) with `"response_format": "b64_json"` and `"extra_body": {"aspect_ratio": "custom", "width": 768, "height": 512}` -> `http 200 in 15.8s`, response `size: "768x512"`, `b64_json` decodes to 9296 bytes starting with `RIFF`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.02359296` which is exactly 768 x 512 x 6e-8. The same row without native dimensions at de6cb908ae (then pointed at `flux-2-klein-4b`, 1e-9 per pixel) billed `0.001048576` = 1024 x 1024 x 1e-9, the documented fallback

#### speech

1. POST /v1/audio/speech -> `http 200 in 10.3s`, headers `content-type: audio/mpeg`, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000615` (character priced, 48 characters), 41856 bytes `MPEG ADTS, layer III, v2, 128 kbps, 24 kHz, Monaural`
3. token-priced row `replicate-speech-tokens` (`replicate/google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts`, 2e-6 in and 4e-5 out per token), `"input": "Hello there."`, `"voice": "Kore"` -> `http 200 in 3.06s`, `content-type: audio/wav`, 63404 bytes, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.001336` = 8 input tokens x 2e-6 + 33 output tokens x 4e-5 from the prediction `metrics`. Before de6cb908ae the same call billed `0.000048` (a 24-token tiktoken estimate of the input, zero output)
2. failure path, `"voice": "not-a-voice"` -> `http 422 in 9.8s`, body `litellm.UnprocessableEntityError: ReplicateException - {"detail":"- input.voice: voice must be one of the following: \"eve\", \"ara\", \"rex\", \"sal\", \"leo\"", "status":422, "title":"Input validation failed", ...}`

Earlier tips: the same legs also passed at aca818a813, ea5a6f0c0c, aaf2913872, 8bcc2e9e78, f2a72cc7eb, b508b1c4dc, cbd6b5fd44, 217587d9de and de6cb908ae with identical costs. Every leg above except the two failure paths and the video `extra_body.prompt` check was re-run at e6540ca944 on the same two-worker proxy. The commits after e6540ca944 (d00b7a356f, a8323a6c35, b9553ea3de, b7a13805c9, 1b0f4d7e9d) only change the sync redirect walk inside the bounded download, lint suppressions, and add the model path segment validation and the pinned-version endpoint change covered by unit tests (the versions endpoint was checked live at 1b0f4d7e9d with the real key: `POST /v1/models/black-forest-labs/flux-schnell/versions/<latest>/predictions` created a prediction for that model and `GET /v1/models/xai/grok-imagine-image/versions/<that id>` returned 404, so a version cannot be used under another owner's path), so the e6540ca944 legs stand for the tip.

Unit tests: `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/llms/replicate -q` -> 170 passed, plus 3 new sync `max_response_bytes` tests in `tests/unit/llms/custom_httpx/test_http_handler.py`. `make lint` green locally (ruff strict, type discipline, basedpyright, test quality and openapi gates all within their merge-base ceilings).

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- a prediction that fails inside the model (a bad `aspect_ratio` the model schema does not catch) comes back with HTTP 201 and `status: failed`, so LiteLLM raises `APIError` (500) and the router retries it, three attempts took 192s in the proof. Replicate schema failures are plain 422s and are not retried
- `deployments/owner/name` predictions skip the model binding check on status and content, Replicate's prediction object names the underlying model, not the deployment, so there is nothing to compare against
- a native `video` input (edit mode on models like `xai/grok-imagine-video`) passes through and usage still mirrors the requested `seconds`, Replicate reports no billed duration
- a token-priced speech row whose prediction `metrics` carry no token counts has no `usage`, so it bills the tiktoken input estimate and zero output like before. Only a model that reports the counts (gemini TTS does) bills output tokens
- image `size` is set only when the prediction input carries integer `width` and `height`. Models that take `aspect_ratio` plus `megapixels` (the flux-2-klein family) still price at the `1024x1024` fallback
- video cost only when the request sets `seconds`: usage echoes the prediction input, Replicate does not report the rendered duration, so a request without `seconds` has no `duration_seconds` and prices at 0

- speech `response_format` is dropped, Replicate TTS models name that field differently (`output_format`, `audio_format`), pass it through `extra_body` instead, the output file's own `content-type` is returned

### Low

- `GET /v1/videos/{id}` reports `created_at: 0` like the fal.ai config, Replicate's `created_at` is an ISO string and is not parsed
- polling for slow image and speech predictions is bounded by `DEFAULT_REPLICATE_SYNC_POLLING_RETRIES` (120 polls, 1s apart) after the 60s `Prefer: wait` window
- `BaseImageGenerationConfig.transform_image_generation_request` now declares `dict[str, object]` as its return type, every override returning a plain `dict` still type checks

title: feat(rate-limit): team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple caps how far a team borrows idle model capacity
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- With `team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams` on, a team can borrow up to the model's whole `tpm`/`rpm`
- One team can take most of the idle capacity, there is no per-team ceiling

How it solves it:

- New team metadata key `team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple`, next to `model_tpm_limit`
- Team's usage on a model is capped at share x multiple, TPM and RPM alike, even while idle
- Past the cap the request gets a 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple`
- At saturation the team is still held to its plain share, as before
- Unset keeps today's behavior. Values below 1, above 1,000,000, infinite or non-numeric are logged and ignored
- The key is proxy-controlled team metadata, so a team admin cannot lift their own cap through `/team/update`

## User Flow

Before: a team with `model_tpm_limit: {"luna": 60}` runs to 240 tokens a minute on an idle model, four times its share, and nothing in team metadata can stop it short of the model limit

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/team/new with `"metadata": {"model_tpm_limit": {"luna": 60}, "team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple": 2}` and a key for that team
2. Developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "luna"` eight times, 30 tokens each, all return 200
3. The ninth call returns 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated`, only because the model itself crossed `saturation_threshold`

After: the same team is refused once it reaches twice its share, while the model is still idle

1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/team/new with `"team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple": 2` and a key for that team
2. Developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "luna"`, calls one to four return 200 (120 tokens, two times the share)
3. The fifth call returns 429 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple` and the message "Team model_tpm_limit borrow cap reached for luna: the team may use at most 2.0x its model_tpm_limit while borrowing idle capacity"
4. Once the model saturates, the team is held to its plain 60 with `rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated`, same as before this PR

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10561

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, same for both legs: two uvicorn workers, one local Redis for router state and coordination, local Postgres, and the model answers with `mock_response` so no provider is called. Before ran from a checkout of `main` at 19ffe3a5f2, After from this branch at 1087de7068, with the same config, command and client. The two commits since (e35edc4208, d75b6d0773) only tighten the value validation and add the key to the proxy-controlled team metadata list, neither touches the admitted or refused path walked below, and both are covered by the unit tests named under Tests.

Proxy command (env vars: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`):

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4031 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY   # never called, mock_response answers
      mock_response: "hello from luna"
      tpm: 400
      rpm: 100

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379
  num_retries: 0

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"]
  priority_reservation:
    interactive: 0.6
    batch: 0.4
  priority_reservation_settings:
    default_priority: 1.0
    saturation_threshold: 0.4
    saturation_check_cache_ttl: 5
    team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity_from_other_teams: true

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Client: leg.sh (one team at model_tpm_limit 60 on luna with team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple 2, one key, ten chat calls one second apart)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
PORT=${PORT:-4031}
H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
redis-cli --scan --pattern '*luna*' | xargs -r redis-cli del >/dev/null
redis-cli --scan --pattern '*model_per_team*' | xargs -r redis-cli del >/dev/null
META='{"model_tpm_limit": {"luna": 60}, "team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple": 2}'
TEAM=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:$PORT/team/new -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"metadata\": $META}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["team_id"])')
KEY=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:$PORT/key/generate -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"team_id\": \"$TEAM\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "team metadata: $META"
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  OUT=$(curl -s -D - -o /tmp/body.$$ -X POST localhost:$PORT/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model": "luna", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}')
  CODE=$(echo "$OUT" | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')
  RLB=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -i '^rate_limited_by' | tr -d '\r')
  SAT=$(echo "$OUT" | grep -i '^x-litellm-saturation' | tr -d '\r')
  if [ "$CODE" = "200" ]; then USAGE=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("/tmp/body.'$$'"))["usage"]["total_tokens"])'); echo "call $i HTTP $CODE   ok usage=$USAGE"; else echo "call $i HTTP $CODE  $RLB $SAT   $(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("/tmp/body.'$$'"))["error"]["message"][:170])')"; fi
  sleep 1
done
```

</details>

### Before (19ffe3a5f2)

The metadata key is unknown, so the team borrows to the model limit. Eight calls land (240 tokens, four times the 60 share) and the team is only stopped when the model itself saturates.

```text
team metadata: {"model_tpm_limit": {"luna": 60}, "team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple": 2}
call 1 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 2 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 3 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 4 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 5 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 6 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 7 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 8 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 9 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_saturated x-litellm-saturation: 60.00%   Team model_tpm_limit reached for luna and the model is saturated, so there is no idle capacity to borrow. Team: 3104a122-..., Rate limit type: tokens, ...
call 10 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
```

### After (1087de7068)

Four calls land (120 tokens, exactly two times the share) and the fifth is refused while the model is at 7.5% saturation.

```text
team metadata: {"model_tpm_limit": {"luna": 60}, "team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple": 2}
call 1 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 2 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 3 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 4 HTTP 200   ok usage=30
call 5 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple x-litellm-saturation: 7.50%   Team model_tpm_limit borrow cap reached for luna: the team may use at most 2.0x its model_tpm_limit while borrowing idle capacity. Team: 89aa7190-...
call 6 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple x-litellm-saturation: 15.00%   Team model_tpm_limit borrow cap reached for luna: the team may use at most 2.0x its model_tpm_limit while borrowing idle capacity. Team: 89aa7190-...
call 7 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple x-litellm-saturation: 15.00%   ...
call 8 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple x-litellm-saturation: 30.00%   ...
call 9 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple x-litellm-saturation: 30.00%   ...
call 10 HTTP 429  rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple x-litellm-saturation: 30.00%   ...
```

Tests: `tests/integration/routing/test_team_model_limit_borrows_idle_capacity.py::test_team_borrowing_stops_at_its_max_borrow_multiple_while_the_model_is_idle[tpm|rpm]` is new in this PR. Run locally through the providers harness (own Postgres, Redis, scripted upstream, owned proxy) it fails on `main` at 19ffe3a5f2 with `assert blocked` -> `assert ()` for both tpm and rpm (no call is ever refused) and passes at the tip together with the four existing borrowing tests (6 passed). The 15 new unit tests in `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py` pass with the 20 existing borrowing tests, `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_admin_field_permissions.py` covers the proxy-controlled key, and a hand-rolled mutation sweep over the new code (19 mutants: cap formula, TPM/RPM swap, idle vs saturated descriptor choice, the `>=` threshold, header name, tracking branch, settle wiring, validation bound) is killed 19/19.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Tokens settle after the response, so the cap trips on the first call that starts at or past share x multiple, same as the share at saturation today
- Saturation is cached for `saturation_check_cache_ttl`, so which 429 a borderline call gets can lag by that many seconds
- The new integration test first runs on main after merge, `run-ci` was not added

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7e50755abf444e5e9886bbb506240a4d
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/7e50755abf444e5e9886bbb506240a4d?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes production rate-limit enforcement paths in dynamic_rate_limiter_v3, but behavior is opt-in via team metadata and preserves prior semantics when unset.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`team_model_limit_max_borrow_multiple`** in team metadata so idle-capacity borrowing is capped at **share × multiple** for TPM and RPM, instead of letting a team consume up to the model’s full limits.
> 
> The dynamic rate limiter v3 now tracks team usage with a **`_BorrowingTeamShare`** that picks the **borrow ceiling** while the model is below saturation and the **plain team share** once saturated. Over the cap it returns **429** with **`rate_limited_by: model_per_team_max_borrow_multiple`**; invalid or missing values keep the old “borrow up to model limit” behavior after a warning. The field is **team-admin editable**, with new **unit and integration tests** covering caps, saturation handoff, WebSocket turns, and bad metadata.

title: feat(cost-map): add seedance and nano banana -latest aliases
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

title

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Seedance and Nano Banana had no `-latest` name on any provider
- Callers had to pin `seedance2_5` or `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` and edit config on each release

How it solves it:

- Adds 7 `alias_of` rows to both cost maps, next to their targets
- `runwayml/seedance-latest` and three `fal_ai/bytedance/seedance-latest/<task>` rows point at Seedance 2.5
- `nano-banana-latest` on `gemini/`, `vertex_ai/` and `replicate/google/` points at Nano Banana 2.1
- The alias test now accepts `video_generation` and `image_generation` targets

## User Flow

Before: a developer who wants the newest Nano Banana or Seedance without pinning a version gets a provider error

1. The proxy admin adds `gemini/nano-banana-latest` and `runwayml/seedance-latest` to `model_list` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `"model": "nano-banana-latest"`
3. They get HTTP 404, `models/nano-banana-latest is not found for API version v1beta`
4. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/videos with `"model": "seedance-latest"` and get HTTP 400, `Validation of body failed`, listing Runway's real model ids

After: the same two requests return an image and a video job, billed at the target model's price

1. The proxy admin adds `gemini/nano-banana-latest` and `runwayml/seedance-latest` to `model_list` and starts the proxy
2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `"model": "nano-banana-latest"`
3. They get HTTP 200 with one image and an `x-litellm-response-cost` header of about $0.04
4. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/videos with `"model": "seedance-latest"` and get HTTP 200 with a queued video id, which later downloads as an MP4

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, identical for both legs. Two workers served in each leg (two `Started server process` lines in the log), sharing one local Redis. Env vars set: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `RUNWAYML_API_KEY`, `FAL_AI_API_KEY`, `REPLICATE_API_KEY`, `VERTEXAI_PROJECT`, `VERTEX_AI_DEVIN_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. The fal rows ran in a second proxy session with the same command and settings

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: nano-banana-latest
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/nano-banana-latest
```

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Responses streams could omit the first answer fragment when it arrived together with reasoning. This backport preserves that fragment so streamed text matches the completed response

## TLDR

Problem this solves

- Mixed reasoning chunks discard the first answer fragment

How it solves it

- Emit reasoning first, then retain the answer for streaming

## User Flow

Before, a streamed answer can differ from its completed response

1. Send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with reasoning enabled and `stream=true`
2. A provider sends reasoning and the first answer fragment together
3. The stream omits that fragment, while the completed response retains it

After, both answer representations contain the same text

1. Send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses request
2. A provider sends reasoning and the first answer fragment together
3. The stream and completed response both retain the entire answer

## Source and scope

Partial backport of https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/46754 to `lts/1.108.x`

Main merged on 2026-10-21T08:50:20Z at `a8113b0dd721804c752a6f1952367fb642205224`. The two copied helper bodies match that merge commit exactly. Both sync and async iterators apply the split before processing the chunk

This carries only mixed reasoning/answer preservation. The Anthropic compaction feature from the source PR is excluded. This backport is separate from #50478, which remains held for #51329. #36329 is unchanged

## Validation

All four new sync/async and existing/new reasoning variants failed on unchanged LTS with streamed `9 × 29 = **551**` instead of `19 × 29 = **551**`. After the patch, the complete existing Responses iterator test file passes all 78 cases

An additional network-blocked probe covers terminal mixed chunks, reasoning transitions, exact usage, contiguous sequence numbers and unchanged caller-owned chunks. All eight combinations pass, retaining 3 input and 5 output tokens

Both changed-file Ruff configurations pass. All five differential lint/type gates and API-schema synchronization pass. Full `make check` remains red on an inherited Ruff import-order error in unchanged `litellm/main.py` at line 1091, reproduced against clean base `773b783555eb8aa770288a816f7941cc82ec9597` with the same Ruff binary

Gauntlet-mini survived in degraded mode. Five lenses ran sequentially in this session because independent agent execution is unavailable. A test comprehension issue was corrected and the mapped tests and Ruff checks were repeated

Grype 0.120.1 found 86 existing LTS advisories and 85 on main. All 85 shared findings remain present on main. The only LTS-only finding has no published fix, so no lockfile or dependency changes qualify for this backport

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

The unchanged LTS merge base now reproduces the real missing first digit. Native Mistral reasoning is enabled through `extra_body`, an existing passthrough supported on the base, rather than the legacy prompt shim. This needs no code from held #50478. Before is exactly `773b783555eb8aa770288a816f7941cc82ec9597`, and After is this PR's unchanged product tip `dafe96c05a5153706670893ca5afbb47e85ae700`

Both requests use the real Mistral API, local PostgreSQL, Redis 6394, two workers, separate Redis namespaces and disabled response caching. Reload is omitted because it disables multiple workers on these checkouts. Both proxies were healthy before the requests

<details>
<summary>Exact proxy setup</summary>

`MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `DATABRICKS_API_KEY` and `DATABRICKS_API_BASE` are environment variables. This is the Before configuration. After is identical except for Redis namespace `magistral-pair-4112`

### Before (773b783555eb8aa770288a816f7941cc82ec9597)

Give only the answer.","stream":true,"extra_body":{"reasoning_effort":"high"},"max_output_tokens":2048}'

2. Reassembling all answer deltas returns `51`, while the completed message contains `551`. The first digit is lost

```json

  "i": 1,
  "prompt": "Calculate 19 times 29. Give only the answer.",
  "text": "51",
  "completed": "551",
  "equal": false,
  "has_completed": true,
  "reasoning_chars": 1270
}
```

### After (dafe96c05a5153706670893ca5afbb47e85ae700)

1. Send the same request to the current-tip proxy

```sh
curl -sS -N --max-time 180 http://127.0.0.1:4112/v1/responses -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-magistral-local-qa' -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"magistral","input":"Calculate 19 times 29. Give only the answer.","stream":true,"extra_body":{"reasoning_effort":"high"},"max_output_tokens":2048}'
```

2. Reassembling all answer deltas and reading the completed message both return `551`. The first digit is preserved

```json
{
  "port": 4112,
  "i": 1,
  "prompt": "Calculate 19 times 29. Give only the answer.",
  "text": "551",
  "completed": "551",
  "equal": true,
  "has_completed": true,
  "reasoning_chars": 920
}
```

<details>
<summary>Exact client request and SSE comparison</summary>

```python
import json
import subprocess

def compare(port):
    payload = {
        'model': 'magistral', 'input': 'Calculate 19 times 29. Give only the answer.',
        'stream': True, 'extra_body': {'reasoning_effort': 'high'}, 'max_output_tokens': 2048,
    }
    raw = subprocess.check_output([
        'curl', '-sS', '-N', '--max-time', '180', f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/responses',
        '-H', 'Authorization: Bearer sk-magistral-local-qa', '-H', 'Cache-Control: no-cache',
        '-H', 'Content-Type: application/json', '-d', json.dumps(payload),
    ], text=True)
    events = [json.loads(line[6:]) for line in raw.splitlines()
              if line.startswith('data: ') and line[6:] != '[DONE]']
    streamed = ''.join(event.get('delta', '') for event in events
                       if event.get('type') == 'response.output_text.delta')
    completed = next(event['response'] for event in events if event.get('type') == 'response.completed')
    final = ''.join(part.get('text', '') for item in completed['output']
                    if item.get('type') == 'message' for part in item.get('content', [])
                    if part.get('type') == 'output_text')
    return {'streamed': streamed, 'completed': final, 'equal': streamed == final}
```
</details>

Packet boundaries vary. In this three-prompt run, one unchanged-base request lost a digit and all three patched-tip requests preserved their complete answers. Earlier base runs using the prompt shim passed with literal thinking tags. Those tags belong to the separate Magistral change, not this backport

### Live Mistral activation proof

The qualifying baseline proof above needs no held adapter changes. Earlier interaction checks on held #50478 also reproduced three missing fragments and passed when only this patch was added. #50478 stays held until main #51329 and this separate prerequisite merge

## Type

Bug Fix

## Caveats

### Medium

- Existing base import ordering prevents a clean full lint run
- Live requests did not produce a mixed reasoning/answer chunk
- Existing dependency advisories remain inherited from the release lines

## Final Attestation

- [x] Deterministic tests reproduce and prevent the lost-answer-fragment defect

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core streaming translation for reasoning-enabled Responses streams; scope is narrow but regressions could affect event ordering or text assembly.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Responses API streaming when a provider sends **reasoning and the first answer fragment in the same chunk**. `LiteLLMCompletionStreamingIterator` now detects mixed deltas via `_delta_carries_reasoning_and_answer` and **`_reasoning_part_first`** splits them: emit reasoning-only first, **re-buffer** an answer-only chunk for the next iteration. Wired through **sync and async** chunk paths.
> 
> New parametrized tests assert streamed text deltas, reasoning deltas, and completed message text stay aligned (e.g. preserving leading digits like `19 × 29 = **551**`).

title: fix(messages): hand rust only the anthropic metadata user_id
body:
_Requested by **Nate** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK?thread=cmsg_012GpiSrjzBrfDdFUq1gGbWK18DNcRohWoS1jD9M1jE3Cr)_ ## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description Under certain circumstances, the pillar hook would set metadata to a large object, and rust would freak out. This converts the metadata to just the 'user_id' within it, which is what it should be.
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - With a Pillar guardrail on `pre_call`, Anthropic `/v1/messages` returns 500 `litellm.APIConnectionError: unsupported type UserAPIKeyAuth` since #51119 - Pillar aliases `metadata` to the `litellm_metadata` dict when the request uses `litellm_metadata`, and that dict holds the caller's `UserAPIKeyAuth`. The Rust host converts the whole `metadata` field to JSON before the Rust `validate_anthropic_api_metadata` keeps only `user_id`, and the conversion fails on the model object - Scheduled run 43133054587 fails `test_messages_bridge_hook_sees_the_definition_the_request_served` on this How it solves it: - `body_params` hands Rust only `metadata.user_id`, the one key both the Rust validator and Python's `AnthropicMetadata` forward. A non-object `metadata` still goes through untouched so Rust raises the same validation error - Unit cases in `tests/unit/rust_bridge/host/routes/test_messages.py` (two fail without the fix) ## Type Bug fix ## Caveats (if any) Verified locally: the failing integration test passes with the fix (fails on main with the same 500), and `test_messages.py` passes (178). Integration suite not run in CI on this branch (`run-ci` not posted). Pillar writing into the caller's `metadata` is left as is

auto_merge.commit_message:
A guardrail such as Pillar aliases the request's metadata to litellm_metadata,
which holds the caller's UserAPIKeyAuth. Since #51119 the Rust host converts
the whole metadata field to JSON before its own user_id filter runs, so the call
failed with "unsupported type UserAPIKeyAuth". The host now passes only
user_id, the one key the Rust validator and Python's AnthropicMetadata keep.
