title: feat(dynamic_rate_limiter_v3): steer flexible teams to a permitted alternate when their preferred model is saturated
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Lets a team opt in to being moved off a busy model. With `metadata.model_preferences: [{"model": "luna", "alternates": ["opus"]}]` on the team, a `luna` request that arrives while `luna` is at or above the dynamic rate limiter's `saturation_threshold` is served by the first listed alternate the team may call that is below it, with `x-litellm-model-steered-from: luna` on the response and spend and rate limits charged to the model that served. Teams without preferences see no change.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A busy model 429s teams that would happily take another permitted model
- Teams have no way to say "I prefer luna but opus is fine"
- Falling back by hand means clients retry and pay the 429 anyway

How it solves it:

- Teams opt in with `metadata.model_preferences: [{"model": "luna", "alternates": ["opus"]}]`
- Before routing, the preferred model's saturation is read from the dynamic rate limiter's cache
- At or above `saturation_threshold` the request is rewritten to the first alternate below it that passes every check a budget fallback passes (key, team, member, project and customer allowlists, every model budget layer and the budgets of the access groups that grant it)
- Response carries `x-litellm-model-steered-from: luna`
- Spend and rate limits are charged to the model that served, including the access groups that granted it
- Teams without `model_preferences` keep today's behavior

## User Flow

Before: a team that lists `opus` as an acceptable alternate still gets throttled on `luna` once `luna` is busy

1. The admin creates the team with POST /team/new, `models: ["luna", "opus"]` and `metadata.model_preferences: [{"model": "luna", "alternates": ["opus"]}]`
2. Another team's request fills `luna` to 50% of its `rpm: 2`
3. The flexible team sends POST /v1/chat/completions with `"model": "luna"` and is served by `luna` from OpenAI, no steering header
4. The next `luna` request from any team gets 429 `Model capacity reached for luna ... Remaining: 0`

After: the same flexible team is quietly moved to `opus` and `luna` capacity is left for teams that only want `luna`

1. The admin creates the same team with the same `model_preferences`
2. Another team's request fills `luna` to 50% of its `rpm: 2`
3. The flexible team sends POST /v1/chat/completions with `"model": "luna"` and gets 200 with `x-litellm-model-steered-from: luna`, answered by `opus` from Anthropic
4. The spend log for that request shows `model_group=opus model=anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`, and the rigid team's next `luna` request is still a 200

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10564

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, identical for both legs. A dedicated Redis on port 6390 (`redis-server --port 6390 --daemonize yes`, flushed before each leg) is shared by both uvicorn workers through `router_settings` and `general_settings.coordination_redis`. Env vars set: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Real provider calls, no mocks.

Proxy start command (two worker PIDs confirmed in the log by two `Started server process` lines, 20402 and 20403 before, 22326 and 22327 after):

```bash
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 4123 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

<details>
<summary>qa_config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.6
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
      rpm: 2
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-opus-4-8
      api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
      rpm: 100

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  proxy_batch_write_at: 1
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6390

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6390
  disable_cooldowns: true

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"]
  priority_reservation_settings:
    saturation_threshold: 0.5
    saturation_check_cache_ttl: 1
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>proof.sh, the client script run against each leg (creates a flexible and a rigid team, warms luna to 50%, then sends one luna request per team and reads the spend log)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... DATABASE_URL=... proof.sh
set -u
P=http://127.0.0.1:4123
H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
J="Content-Type: application/json"
suffix=$(date +%s)
flex_team=$(curl -s -X POST $P/team/new -H "$H" -H "$J" -d "{\"team_alias\":\"flexible-$suffix\",\"models\":[\"luna\",\"opus\"],\"metadata\":{\"model_preferences\":[{\"model\":\"luna\",\"alternates\":[\"opus\"]}]}}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["team_id"])')
rigid_team=$(curl -s -X POST $P/team/new -H "$H" -H "$J" -d "{\"team_alias\":\"rigid-$suffix\",\"models\":[\"luna\",\"opus\"]}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["team_id"])')
flex_key=$(curl -s -X POST $P/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$J" -d "{\"team_id\":\"$flex_team\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
rigid_key=$(curl -s -X POST $P/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$J" -d "{\"team_id\":\"$rigid_team\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "flexible team $flex_team (metadata.model_preferences luna -> opus), rigid team $rigid_team (no preferences); luna rpm=2, saturation_threshold=0.5"
call() { # call <label> <key>
  curl -s -D /tmp/h.$$ -o /tmp/b.$$ -X POST $P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $2" -H "$J" \
    -d '{"model":"luna","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hi"}],"max_tokens":5}'
  status=$(head -1 /tmp/h.$$ | awk '{print $2}')
  steered=$(grep -i '^x-litellm-model-steered-from:' /tmp/h.$$ | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')
  base=$(grep -i '^x-litellm-model-api-base:' /tmp/h.$$ | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')
  id=$(python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]));print(d.get("id") or d["error"]["message"][:110])' /tmp/b.$$)
  echo "$1: HTTP $status  x-litellm-model-steered-from=${steered:-<absent>}  api_base=${base:-<absent>}  $id"
  LAST_ID=$id
}
call "warm-up, rigid key, model=luna" "$rigid_key"
sleep 2
call "flexible key, model=luna      " "$flex_key"; steered_id=$LAST_ID
call "rigid key, model=luna         " "$rigid_key"
sleep 6
echo "spend log for the flexible request:"
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -At -c "SELECT 'model_group='||model_group||' model='||model||' spend='||spend FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" WHERE request_id='$steered_id'"
echo "worker pids: $(pgrep -f 'proxy_cli.py --config.*qa_config' | wc -l) processes matching proxy_cli, uvicorn workers: $(pgrep -f 'multiprocessing.spawn|uvicorn' | wc -l)"
```

</details>

### Before (2d8fd9b384, merge base on main)

1. `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... DATABASE_URL=... ./proof.sh`
2. Observed output:

```text
flexible team f14fdefd-03d6-472d-ae79-15b1bc53d238 (metadata.model_preferences luna -> opus), rigid team 0f7d13af-ef0a-49a1-b40f-854b1e0b9d8a (no preferences); luna rpm=2, saturation_threshold=0.5
warm-up, rigid key, model=luna: HTTP 200  x-litellm-model-steered-from=<absent>  api_base=https://api.openai.com  chatcmpl-EjGQ4GU3Kbpxccuxuqnnix4sULTgI
flexible key, model=luna      : HTTP 200  x-litellm-model-steered-from=<absent>  api_base=https://api.openai.com  chatcmpl-EjGQ7lWdARLDJaAFLnqALjx33qGCg
rigid key, model=luna         : HTTP 429  x-litellm-model-steered-from=<absent>  api_base=<absent>  Model capacity reached for luna. Priority: None, Rate limit type: requests, Model TPM: not configured, Model R
spend log for the flexible request:
model_group=luna model=openai/gpt-5.6 spend=0.000132
worker pids: 1 processes matching proxy_cli, uvicorn workers: 3
```

The flexible team's `luna` request is served by `luna` (OpenAI api_base, spend logged under `model_group=luna`), there is no `x-litellm-model-steered-from` header, and the rigid team's following `luna` request is a 429.

### After (62a9e81a76, proof recorded at 68d8786f2b; later commits type the hook `data` parameters, check each alternate against the key, team member, project and customer allowlists, every model budget layer and the access group budgets, stamp the alternate's access groups on the token and request metadata, refuse free-to-priced steering and alternates that add model-level guardrails, fall back to the preferred model's own check when the alternate refuses, move the header to the response headers hook so streams get it too, skip the header for non Latin-1 names, and merge main)

1. Same `./proof.sh`
2. Observed output:

```text
flexible team 05d5decb-23f5-43d9-9aba-c1d4097440f6 (metadata.model_preferences luna -> opus), rigid team 0fc3b92a-4d5b-4b2b-9742-742b9db5a28b (no preferences); luna rpm=2, saturation_threshold=0.5
warm-up, rigid key, model=luna: HTTP 200  x-litellm-model-steered-from=<absent>  api_base=https://api.openai.com  chatcmpl-EjGRIcRB1NmUe27qWCBbQF2ky1Ne3
flexible key, model=luna      : HTTP 200  x-litellm-model-steered-from=luna  api_base=<absent>  chatcmpl-d64ebeb0-6198-4d69-8d2f-1bc3095f546b
rigid key, model=luna         : HTTP 200  x-litellm-model-steered-from=<absent>  api_base=https://api.openai.com  chatcmpl-EjGRMrSu5GcPoBNXxKKXRrsXYAjtQ
spend log for the flexible request:
model_group=opus model=anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 spend=0.000175
worker pids: 1 processes matching proxy_cli, uvicorn workers: 3
```

The flexible team's `luna` request comes back 200 with `x-litellm-model-steered-from: luna`, its spend log row is `model_group=opus model=anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` at `opus` pricing, and the rigid team's following `luna` request is still a 200 because the flexible request did not consume `luna` capacity.

Integration test `tests/integration/routing/test_team_model_preference_steering.py` (real two worker proxy, Postgres, Redis, scripted upstream) fails on main at the steering step with `429 Model capacity reached for <luna>` and passes at this tip. Unit tests in `tests/unit/proxy/hooks/test_dynamic_rate_limiter_v3.py` cover the permitted, forbidden, unknown, malformed and both-saturated cases, and the `x-litellm-model-steered-from` header coming from `async_post_call_response_headers_hook` for a `stream=true` request.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Saturation is read from the `saturation_check_cache_ttl` cache, so a sudden burst can be steered up to that many seconds late
- An alternate is used only when the key, the team, the team member, the project and the customer may call it (`_is_fallback_model_authorized` with the team, membership and project loaded, plus `can_customer_access_model`, the same checks budget fallbacks pass), every `model_max_budget` layer for it has room (`_is_within_every_model_budget`) and the model access groups that grant it are under budget (`collect_matched_model_access_groups` + `_model_access_group_max_budget_check`); otherwise it is skipped, never granted. The granting groups replace `matched_model_access_groups` on the token, in every request metadata bucket and on the `user_api_key_auth` copy inside it, even when the preferred model had none, so spend charges them and nothing else
- Agent keys are never steered (`refuse_agent_keys=True`), matching the router fallback path
- If the chosen alternate's own rate limit check still refuses the request (a stale saturation read), the hook falls back to the preferred model's check, so the worst case is today's behavior
- An alternate whose deployments add model-level guardrails, or guardrail settings, the request did not already carry is skipped (entries compared with their settings), since guardrails may already have run before the limiter in callback order and would not be revisited
- A preferred model priced at zero waived the aggregate budget checks at auth (`request_skips_budget_checks`), so it is never steered to a priced alternate
- While the request holds a budget reservation sized for the preferred model, an alternate priced above it per token is skipped, so fail-closed budget enforcement never admits a call the reservation does not cover
- With `block_requests_for_models_without_pricing` on, an unpriced alternate is skipped (`_unpriced_models_in_request`), as the fallback path does
- An alternate that does not serve the request's endpoint is skipped (`endpoint_unsupported_by_model`, the same probe the rate limit fallback uses)
- When the request already reserved budget against a model access group (`budget_reservation.entries`), an alternate granted by a different group is skipped, so settlement never charges a group that did not serve
- A failing alternate check (authorization, budgets, guardrail probe) is logged and leaves the request on the preferred model, and an alternate whose own admission errors falls back to the preferred model's check, so steering never fails a request that could stay put
- Steering only runs when `dynamic_rate_limiter_v3` is enabled, since that is where the saturation number comes from

### Low

- Malformed `model_preferences` is logged and ignored rather than rejected at `/team/new`

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

title: fix(fal_ai): give MiniMax H3 Max video endpoints their own resolution profile
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add MiniMax H3 Max profile

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `fal_ai/minimax/h3-max/*` and `h3-max-turbo/*` used the Seedance resolution profile
- a `size` of `768P` was dropped, a WxH size became `1080p`, which fal rejects
- usage recorded `720p`, a tier none of the H3 Max rows have

How it solves it:

- new `_H3_MAX_PROFILE` with fal's `480P`, `768P`, `1080P` enum and `image_url` reference key
- no requested size leaves `video_resolution` out of usage, so cost uses the row's base rate

## User Flow

Before: a developer asking for a 1280x768 H3 Max Turbo video gets a failed job billed at the 1080p rate

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos with `"model": "fal-h3-max-turbo"`, `"size": "1280x768"`, `"seconds": "5"`
2. The 200 response is queued with `"size": "1080p"` and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header reads 0.28
3. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/videos/{id} ends at `"status": "failed"` with `body.resolution: Input should be '480P', '768P' or '1080P'`
4. They paid the 1080p rate for a video that never rendered

After: the same request renders at 768P and is billed at the 768p rate

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos with `"size": "1280x768"`, `"seconds": "5"`
2. The 200 response is queued with `"size": "768P"` and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header reads 0.14
3. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/videos/{id} ends at `"status": "completed"`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, identical for both legs. Redis on `127.0.0.1:6379`. `FAL_AI_API_KEY` exported from the QA vault and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` exported as a random `sk-qa-...` value. Proxy started from the repo root with `uv run --no-sync python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/fal_proxy.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver --port 4010`, two worker PIDs logged `Started server process`. Before ran on `main` at `a3c52e69d3`, After on this branch at `f1e74c6100`. The tip `507682644c` only merges `main` back in, so the proof still holds.

<details>
<summary>/tmp/fal_proxy.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: fal-h3-max-turbo
    litellm_params:
      model: fal_ai/minimax/h3-max-turbo/text-to-video
      api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

litellm_settings:
  drop_params: True
```

</details>

Client calls, run with the same master key, the GET repeated every 5 seconds until the status left `queued`/`in_progress`:

```bash
curl -sS -D - -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4010/v1/videos -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fal-h3-max-turbo","prompt":"a red kite over a green field","size":"1280x768","seconds":"5"}'
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:4010/v1/videos/<id> -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"
```

### Before (a3c52e69d3)

title: chore(cost-map): bill retired xai grok-imagine-image-quality and -pro slugs at the grok-imagine-image-2.0 low rate
body:
## Summary

Nov 12 sync for the `xai` provider. `list xai` (43 ids from GET /v1/language-models) and `prices xai` (43 records) both match the catalog row for row, so no text row changes. The docs.x.ai release-notes page gained a November entry that changes how four retired image slugs are billed, and this PR updates those rows.

Changed rows, kind page, all four already carry their `deprecation_date` and `successor_model: xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0` from earlier syncs. Each gets `input_cost_per_image: 0.04`, `output_cost_per_image_1K: 0.04`, `output_cost_per_image_2K: 0.06` and `source` set to the migration guide.

| key | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xai/grok-imagine-image-quality` | `input_cost_per_image: 0.05` | `0.04`, plus `_1K: 0.04`, `_2K: 0.06` |
| `xai/grok-imagine-image-quality-20260403` | `input_cost_per_image: 0.05` | same |
| `xai/grok-imagine-image-quality-latest` | `input_cost_per_image: 0.05` | same |
| `xai/grok-imagine-image-pro` | `input_cost_per_image: 0.05` | same |

Evidence, fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-12.

https://docs.x.ai/docs/release-notes (November entry): "Requests to `grok-imagine-image-quality` and `grok-imagine-image-pro` are now served by `grok-imagine-image-2.0-low`: `grok-imagine-image-2.0` with `quality` set to `low`, at a lower per-image price. No request changes are needed. `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks` on each response reflects the lower price"

https://docs.x.ai/developers/migration/imagine-image-quality-nov-2: "It reflects the `grok-imagine-image-2.0` low price: $0.04 per 1K image and $0.06 per 2K image, plus $0.01 per input image on edits." and "`grok-imagine-image-2.0` at `low` quality is $0.01 per image cheaper than `grok-imagine-image-quality` at every resolution. If you keep sending requests to the retired slug after November 2, you are billed at the `grok-imagine-image-2.0` `low` rate." and "Requests to `grok-imagine-image-pro`, which already redirect to `grok-imagine-image-quality`, follow it to `grok-imagine-image-2.0` at `low`."

https://docs.x.ai/docs/models Imagine Pricing table: "| grok-imagine-image-2.0 | $0.04 / image |"

The flat `input_cost_per_image` stays the 1K price, as it was on these rows before (0.05 was the 1K price of grok-imagine-image-quality, 0.01 above the new 0.04). The resolution fields follow the shape of `xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0` per ruling xai-image-provider-billed-cost-and-resolution-prices-20261107, and `litellm/llms/xai/image_generation/cost_calculator.py` on main reads `output_cost_per_image_1K` / `_2K` for low-quality calls when `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks` is absent. `successor_model` stays `xai/grok-imagine-image-2.0`, the catalog key of the redirect target (xAI's gRPC responses report it as `grok-imagine-image-2.0-low`).

Pages checked with no pricing difference: https://docs.x.ai/docs/models Text API Pricing (grok-4.7, 4.6, 4.5, 4.3, 4.20-0309 reasoning and non-reasoning, grok-build-0.1, 4.20-multi-agent-0309, with their >= 200k tiers), Imagine Pricing (grok-imagine-image 0.02, video-1.5-lite 0.020/sec, video 0.050/sec, video-1.5 0.080/sec) and Voice Pricing (0.08/min and 0.004 per text input on grok-voice-2.0 and 3.0, speech to text 0.10/hr REST) all match the existing rows.

Delisted by the provider: none. The dispatcher flagged xai/grok-imagine-image, grok-imagine-image-2.0, grok-imagine-image-pro, grok-imagine-image-quality, grok-imagine-image-quality-latest, grok-imagine-video, grok-imagine-video-1.5, grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite, grok-imagine-video-1.5-preview, grok-voice-2.0, grok-voice-3.0, grok-voice-latest, grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 and grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 as absent from GET /v1/language-models, which only lists text models, so these are a coverage gap and not delistings. xai/grok-voice-2.0 stays undated per ruling xai-grok-voice-2-0-deprecated-no-date-stay-undated (release notes still give no end of life date).

Rulings applied: xai-image-provider-billed-cost-and-resolution-prices-20261107, xai-grok-voice-2-0-deprecated-no-date-stay-undated, xai-grok-voice-text-input-charge-per-message (voice rows unchanged).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Pricing metadata only in JSON cost maps; no runtime logic changes, with minor impact on reported costs for legacy xAI image model IDs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates the **xAI cost map** for four **retired image slugs** (`grok-imagine-image-quality`, `grok-imagine-image-quality-20260403`, `grok-imagine-image-quality-latest`, and `grok-imagine-image-pro`) in both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the LiteLLM backup.
> 
> Each row now reflects **grok-imagine-image-2.0 low** pricing after xAI’s Nov 2 migration: **`input_cost_per_image`** drops from **0.05 → 0.04**, and new **`output_cost_per_image_1K`** (**0.04**) / **`output_cost_per_image_2K`** (**0.06**) fields are added so resolution-aware billing in `litellm/llms/xai/image_generation/cost_calculator.py` can apply when `usage.cost_in_usd_ticks` is missing. The **`source`** link is pointed at the imagine-image-quality migration doc.

title: ci: stop PR runs from thrashing the Actions cache and stop smoke compiling from source
body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- PR runs save private cache copies and evict main's
- sccache makes 700 to 2000 cache requests per Rust build
- GitHub answers cache restores with 429, so jobs rebuild
- Smoke compiles Rust and numpy from source on every run

How it solves it:

- Only main saves caches, every other ref restores
- sccache's GitHub cache backend is removed
- Smoke installs the Rust bridge that unit already builds
- Smoke runs on main so source-built wheels get cached

## User Flow

Before: a contributor waits about 18 minutes for required checks because CI rebuilds what it used to restore

1. They push a commit to a pull request against `main`
2. `unit` waits on its `rust-bridge` job, which misses its cache on about 2 of 3 runs and compiles Rust for about 5 minutes before any test shard starts
3. `smoke` compiles the Rust bridge in 8 jobs, and its `py3.15` job spends about 12 minutes compiling numpy
4. `unit passed` and `smoke passed` turn green after about 18 and 14 minutes at the median

After: the same push restores those builds, so the wait is set by the tests themselves

1. They push a commit to a pull request against `main`
2. `rust-bridge` restores the prebuilt bridge in under a minute and the test shards start
3. `smoke` installs that same prebuilt bridge, and `py3.14` and `py3.15` reuse wheels built once on `main`
4. `unit passed` turns green after about 12 to 13 minutes, which is an estimate from step timings until main has run with this change

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [ ] I have added meaningful tests
- [ ] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

This PR only changes CI, so the proof is the workflows themselves running on this branch.

### Before (`main`, sampled 2026-11-11, 10 to 12 PR runs per workflow)

1. `unit` took 18.4 minutes at the median and 33 at p90. On 2026-10-21 it took 12.1
2. The `rust-bridge` job missed its cache on 14 of 21 sampled runs, and a miss cost 4.8 minutes at the median
3. Cache restores failed with `Failed to GetCacheEntryDownloadURL: Rate limited: Failed request: (429) Too Many Requests` in 9 of 16 `rust-bridge` jobs and 16 of 18 lint `python` jobs. On 2026-10-28 none did
4. The repository held 1,053 cache entries, 989 of them sccache objects, and the least recently used entry was 11 minutes old
5. sccache on PR runs logged between 13 and 458 hits out of about 690 requests per build
6. `smoke` took 13.8 minutes at the median. Its `py3.15` job spent 683 seconds in "Install dependencies", and `Built numpy==2.4.4` landed 12 minutes after the build started

### After (`85a74bf771`, the tip before `main` was merged in)

Shared setup for every case below is nothing more than dispatching the workflows on a branch, for example `gh workflow run test-merge-smoke.yml --ref <branch>`.

#### The Rust bridge is restored instead of compiled

1. `unit`'s `rust-bridge` job restored the bridge and finished in 30 seconds, with no 429 in its log
2. In [smoke run 43146261126](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43146261126) the `py3.10` to `py3.13` jobs took 0.9 to 1.4 minutes, down from 5.0 to 5.7, and "Install dependencies" took 5 seconds, down from 274
3. `all-extras-py3.12` and `all-extras-py3.13` took 1.1 and 1.4 minutes, down from 5.0

#### A changed Rust input still builds, without sccache

A throwaway branch added one comment line to the Rust workspace `Cargo.toml` so the bridge key missed. The branch is deleted.

1. In [unit run 43146318355](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43146318355) `rust-bridge` restored the Cargo cache in 37 seconds, built the bridge in 76 and the gateway wheel in 37, about 2.5 minutes in total against 4.8 with sccache
2. In [smoke run 43146314686](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43146314686) every Linux job fell back to the Cargo cache and compiled, and all of them passed

#### Wheels built from source are saved once and reused

The same throwaway branch let setup-uv save from that branch, because the real save only happens on `main`.

1. The first run saved pruned uv caches of 82 MB for 3.15, 65 MB for 3.14 and under 1 MB for every other version
2. In the [second run 43148120931](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43148120931) `py3.15` spent 184 seconds in "Install dependencies", down from 635, and `py3.14` spent 126, down from 482. Both still compiled Rust in that run because of the forced bridge miss
3. Without a saved cache, as on this PR until `main` has run once, `py3.15` still takes about 11.8 minutes

#### Rust CI is no slower without sccache

1. Three runs without sccache took 3.6 to 4.0 minutes for `rust-lint`, 16.0 to 22.3 for `rust-wheel` and 21.8 to 26.5 for `rust-test`
2. The last 12 green PR runs with sccache had medians of 4.0, 21.9 and 23.5 minutes

#### Lint, Rust DB and Terraform

1. Lint's `python` job restored the uv cache that `main` saves and logged `Uninstalled 146 packages` and `Installed 22 packages` to reach its own dependency set. Every cache restore in that job hit, none returned 429
2. `db-queries` passed in 4 minutes 40 seconds and the Terraform provider job passed in 1 minute 9 seconds with the new Go cache action

#### What was red

1. `unit`'s `root` shard failed on `test_price_map_has_no_duplicate_keys`. `main` failed the same test at `7461a996cc`, the commit this branch was based on, and has since fixed it

### After (`344748fa38`, the current tip with `main` merged in)

The merge also moved the Rust, packaging and Terraform paths this PR references, so the checks ran again on the PR itself.

1. All 106 checks pass, including `unit passed`, `lint passed`, `smoke passed` and `zizmor`
2. [unit run 43170813164](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43170813164) took 13.0 minutes, and its `rust-bridge` job restored the bridge in 39 seconds
3. [smoke run 43170812876](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43170812876) took 12.1 minutes. `py3.10` to `py3.13` took 1.1 to 1.5 minutes. `py3.15` took 11.9 and `windows-sdk` 10.5, because the source-built wheel cache does not exist until `main` has run once and Windows still compiles Rust
4. [lint run 43170813157](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/43170813157) took 10.2 minutes

## Type

🚄 Infrastructure

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- sccache as the cause of the 429s is inferred from request counts
- Saves from `main` can only be confirmed after merge
- The cache limit is admin-only, so 10 GB is assumed

### Low

- A PR that changes a lockfile or Rust input still rebuilds
- `windows-sdk` still compiles Rust, about 10 minutes
- `smoke` now also runs on every push to `main`
- #46442 and #51069 touch the same workflow files

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
